example title: Genome-wide association study identifies host genetic variants influencing oral microbiota diversity and metabolic health.

definition: A population-based longitudinal cohort of 2,082 Danish adults at different levels of diabetes risk, sampled from the 16,136 high-risk individuals identified by the 2001–2006 stepwise diabetes screening programme in Danish general practice of the Danish arm of ADDITION-Europe, examined in 2009–2011 with detailed cardiometabolic phenotyping and followed for cardiovascular disease and death.
location quote: 16,136 eligible individuals were identified at high risk following participation in a stepwise screening programme in Danish general practice between 2001 and 2006.
parent quote: The ADDITION-PRO study is nested within the Danish arm (ADDITION-DK) of the ADDITION-Europe study [3,8].
note: 44 GWAS Catalog studies, 1 PMID (PMID:38926497, oral microbiota GWAS in 610 participants). Grepped coho-edit.owl, coho_list and review_names for ADDITION: no term. No expansion of the name was found (protocol paper PMID:23241242); label 'ADDITION-PRO Study' as in the titles of PMID:28509724 and PMID:40635178 (Europe PMC search), so that the acronym ADDITION-PRO differs from the label. The protocol full text says ADDITION-PRO invited 'individuals at different levels of diabetes risk identified from the stepwise screening programme of the Danish arm of the ADDITION-Europe study', i.e. mostly screened people without diabetes who were not in the ADDITION-Denmark treatment trial itself; PMID:38926497 calls it 'a subsidiary study of the Danish arm of the ADDITION trial'. isSubCohortOf follows the protocol's 'nested within' wording - curator to confirm. Example quote from the PMID:38926497 abstract, location quote from the PMID:23241242 abstract, parent quote from the PMID:23241242 full text (Methods).

input name: Arthroplasty and the Genetics of Osteoarthritis
label: Arthroplasty and the Genetics of Osteoarthritis
other synonyms: ARGO study
example title: Deciphering osteoarthritis genetics across 826,690 individuals from 9 populations.
example quote: The ARGO study, was set up to investigate the genetic architecture of hip and knee OA in a Greek population.
definition: A Greek collection of more than 1,500 well-phenotyped patients with severe hip or knee osteoarthritis undergoing total joint replacement, recruited in hospitals of Athens (2015-2017) and Larissa together with healthy controls, set up to study the genetic architecture of osteoarthritis.
location quote: More than 1,500 patients with severe OA, undergoing hip and/or knee total joint replacement were recruited from the cities of Athens and Larissa.
note: 43 GWAS Catalog studies over 2 PMIDs (40205036x22, 34450027x21). No match for argo, arthroplasty or larissa in coho-edit.owl, coho_list.txt, the review file or the curation tables. The label is the PGS name; its expansion of ARGO could not be verified in any fetched text (Europe PMC finds no 'arthroplasty and genetics' phrase; the papers, EGA study EGAS00001000917 'ARGO_GWAS' and PMC6251918 use only 'ARGO'/'the ARGO study'), so a curator should confirm it or relabel the term 'ARGO study'. PMID:34450027 (PMC8459317) analyses two sub-collections, ARGO-Larissa (knee OA cases undergoing total knee arthroplasty, city of Larissa; raw data in EGA EGAS00001000917) and ARGO-Athens (four Athens hospitals, February 2015-March 2017), described under one ARGO study; they are not tagged separately, so one cohort is proposed. Example and location quotes from the PMC8459317 cohort descriptions; definition also from the EGA study description ('The ARGO study is an ongoing collection of well-phenotyped OA patients undergoing total joint replacement and is based in Greece.') and PMC6251918 (PMID:30470734: 'ARGO comprises osteoarthritis cases and healthy controls from Larisa, Greece.').

example title: The Pharmacogenetics of Statin Therapy on Clinical Events: No Evidence that Genetic Variation Affects Statin Response on Myocardial Infarction.
example quote: The Prospective Study of Pravastatin in the Elderly at Risk (PROSPER) trial was supported by an investigator-initiated grant from Bristol-Myers Squibb, USA.
definition: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial population of 5,804 men and women aged 70 to 82 with pre-existing vascular disease or risk factors for it, screened in Scotland, Ireland and the Netherlands and randomised to pravastatin 40 mg/day or placebo for about 3.2 years to test whether statin treatment reduces coronary and cerebrovascular events in the elderly.
location quote: In Scotland, Ireland, and the Netherlands, 23,770 individuals were screened, and 5,804 subjects (2,804 men and 3,000 women), aged 70 to 82 years (average 75 years) and with baseline cholesterol 4.0-9.0 mmol/l, were randomised.
note: 38 GWAS Catalog studies over 8 PMIDs (36050321x18, 36918541x8, 34732054x6, 40038546x2, 35069183x1, 35551307x1, 38652672x1, 40050429x1). No match for prosper or pravastatin in coho-edit.owl, coho_list.txt or the review file. Typed as cohort: it is a trial population, like other trial cohorts in COHO. Example quote from the acknowledgements of PMID:35069183 (statin pharmacogenetics GWAS, PMC8769168), whose methods list PROSPER among two randomized controlled trials in stage one; its GWAS was done within the PHASE project (PHArmacogenetic Study of Statins in the Elderly at Risk), which a curator may want as a synonym or separate term. Definition and location quote from the abstracts of PMID:12097148 (baseline paper, open access) and PMID:12457784 (main results). Scotland mapped to United_Kingdom; the Irish centre was the University of Cork (author affiliations in PMC134480), hence Republic_of_Ireland.

note: 74 GWAS Catalog studies over 8 PMIDs, under four case variants of one tag: GenSalt 37 (6 PMIDs), GENSALT 23 (PMID:40181193), GENSalt 8 (PMID:36477530), GenSALT 6 (PMID:38162683); one acronym (GenSalt, the study's own spelling) kept, as tier A did. No match in COHO (coho_list.txt, coho-edit.owl and components grep for GenSalt, Salt 2026-09-23) or the review file; no acronym clash. Label from the design paper abstract (PMID:17443206, J Hum Hypertens 2007; Europe PMC full text PMC2377400 returned HTTP 500), which is the source of the definition and location quote; PGS name (hyphenated, with 'Study') kept as other synonym. NHLBI funding (U01HL072507) per PMC10755672 acknowledgements.

label: Mass General Brigham Biobank
example title: Global multi-ancestry genome-wide analyses identify genes and biological pathways associated with thyroid cancer and benign thyroid diseases.
example quote: Y.W. contributed data and analyses from the Mass General Brigham Biobank.

label: Kaiser Permanente Research Bank
other synonyms: KP Research Bank|Kaiser Permanente
example title: Three genes associated with anterior and posterior cruciate ligament injury : a genome-wide association analysis.
example quote: Genome-wide association (GWA) analyses were performed using data from the Kaiser Permanente Research Board (KPRB) and the UK Biobank.
definition: A research resource of Kaiser Permanente, launched in May 2016 and built on the Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health, that collects biospecimens and surveys linked to electronic health records from consenting adult members across Kaiser Permanente's eight US regions (about 396,000 consented by July 2021), with general, pregnancy and cancer cohorts.
location quote: The KP Research Bank (KPRB), a research resource within KP, is seeking to collect biospecimens and surveys from at least 400,000 adult members across the U.S. and linking that information to the EHR.
note: The GWAS tag KP (36 studies, 6 PMIDs) means more than one Kaiser Permanente resource, so it gets two rows (this one and the next, an existing-term row for GERA) with KP as a shared acronym. (1) KPRB: PMIDs 34169730 (ACL/PCL injury, OA PMC8244791), 34081057 (patellar tendinopathy) and 36068934 (chondromalacia), 1 study each, all say "Kaiser Permanente Research Board (KPRB)" (sic, for Research Bank) and use KP Northern California health records; PMC8244791: "Our analysis cohort included 83,414 individuals of European ancestry who were genotyped at 670,572 SNPs" (probably the GERA genotypes held by KPRB; not stated). (2) GERA: PMID:36929174 (3 studies) used Rashkin et al. 2020 summary statistics from the "Kaiser Permanente cohort", which the Rashkin abstract (PMID:32887889) names as "the Kaiser Permanente Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging cohorts"; PMID:39406924 (gout, 24 studies, the largest group; not OA) is probably GERA too: its medRxiv preprint (10.1101/2022.11.26.22281768, PDF fetched) says "Institutional Review Board of the Kaiser Foundation Research Institute provided ethical approval for the Kaiser Permanente sample set" and the only reference in it naming a Kaiser cohort is Kvale et al. 2015 "Genotyping informatics and quality control for 100,000 subjects in the Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging (GERA) cohort" - not stated outright, curator to check. (3) PMID:37196047 (diverticular disease, 6 studies, OA PMC10191288) is an eMERGE study whose per-site tags include KP for the eMERGE site "Kaiser Permanente Washington/University of Washington" (formerly Group Health Cooperative/UW), which is neither KPRB nor GERA; no named cohort for it (it may be the ACT study, tier-B row ACT, unverified), so no row; curator may re-tag those 6 GCSTs to eMERGE. The review row RPGEH (COHO:0000473) deliberately did not take KPRB as a synonym because KPRB contains RPGEH; this row mints KPRB as its own term, and RPGEH should get isSubCohortOf KPRB with the quote "Launched in May 2016, the KPRB is built on an existing repository (Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health, or RPGEH) of approximately 220,000 KP members with data and biospecimens collected primarily between 2007 and 2011 from members of KP Northern California, and to a smaller extent, Southern California [6]." (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC8876075/fullTextXML) - not entered as a parent here because the parent column is for this term's own parent. PGS name "Kaiser Permanente" is the organisation; kept as other synonym only because PGS uses it. Clash: KP also proposed for COHO:0000431 (next row). Location quote ends "across the U.S." inside a longer sentence; PMC8876075 also lists the regions "Colorado, Georgia, Hawai’i, Mid-Atlantic, Northern California, Northwest, Southern California, and Washington". COHO/review grep for KP/KPRB/Research Bank: KP only as substring (IMPACT_KPNC); no clash beyond the GERA row.

label: Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging
example title: GWAS meta-analyses clarify the genetics of cervical phenotypes and inform risk stratification for cervical cancer.
example quote: 565 cases and 29 801 controls from Kaiser Permanente cohort
note: Second meaning of the GWAS tag KP (see row KP, which mints the Kaiser Permanente Research Bank and carries the PGS id): 27 of the 36 KP studies mean the GERA cohort. PMID:36929174 (3 studies; cervical phenotypes, OA PMC10244231) took its Kaiser data from Rashkin et al. 2020 ("565 cases and 29 801 controls from Kaiser Permanente cohort", quote, thin spaces as in the XML), and the Rashkin abstract (PMID:32887889, fetched) says the two cohorts were "the UK Biobank (408,786 European ancestry individuals; 48,961 cancer cases) and the Kaiser Permanente Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging cohorts". PMID:39406924 (gout, 24 studies) is probably GERA (see row KP note), unverified. Add KP as an acronym of existing COHO:0000431; it clashes with row KP (KPRB), so both terms need editor notes. PGS id left empty because the PGS cohort KP ("Kaiser Permanente") is assigned to row KP.

input name: Cancer Prevention Study II (including the Nutrition cohort)
label: Cancer Prevention Study
other synonyms: Cancer Prevention Study II|Cancer Prevention Study-II|Cancer Prevention Study II (including the Nutrition cohort)
example title: Genome-wide association study identifies tumor anatomical site-specific risk variants for colorectal cancer survival.
example quote: The following 15 ISACC studies were included: the Cancer Prevention Study-II (CPS-II)35
parent: Genetics and Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer Consortium
parent quote: Cancer Prevention Study II (CPSII)
note: Existing COHO:0000024 Cancer Prevention Study (synonym CPS): its definition ("A cohort of adult men and women across all United States states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, enrolled by the American Cancer Society in 1982 ...", source cancer.org cps-2 page) and its example (PMID:37783704, quote "Cancer Prevention Study II (CPSII)") are already CPS-II, so this is the same cohort, not a sub-cohort; add CPSII and CPS-II as acronyms and the long forms as synonyms. The PGS name adds "(including the Nutrition cohort)": the CPS-II Nutrition Cohort is a subset of CPS-II "established in 1992" with over 84,000 men and 97,000 women who completed a mailed questionnaire (PMID:12015775 abstract); the genotyped colorectal sets are described only as "American Cancer Society Cancer Prevention Study II nested case-control study" (Supplemental table 1 of PMC11112268), not as the Nutrition Cohort; a curator may mint it later as isSubCohortOf COHO:0000024, but the tag does not distinguish it. Curator may consider relabelling COHO:0000024 to "Cancer Prevention Study II" since CPS-I and CPS-3 are distinct cohorts. 35 GWAS Catalog studies over 8 PMIDs, all GECCO colorectal or bladder cancer consortium analyses (PMID:37210288, bladder). No clash (CPS is only on COHO:0000024; KCPS is the Korean Cancer Prevention Study, tier-B row KCPS, a different string). Membership of COHO:0000020 BCAC is already recorded (aggregation_members_evidence.tsv); parent here is the new GECCO row (end of this batch), quote from the GECCO member list on the Fred Hutch page."

label: All of Us Research Program
note: GWAS-only tag, already an acronym synonym of COHO:0000423 All of Us Research Program (review row AllofUs; coho-edit.owl grep 2026-09-23). Tag AoU: 35 GWAS Catalog studies over 3 PMIDs (41882355 x20, 40902600 x13, 40823170 x2); the abstracts of PMID:41882355 and PMID:40902600 (Europe PMC, fetched 2026-09-23) name "All of Us" and "the All of Us Research Program". label: Estonian Biobank
example title: Leveraging Northern European population history: novel low-frequency variants for polycystic ovary syndrome.
example quote: For validation, we used an independent dataset from the Estonian Biobank, including 2812 cases and 89 230 controls.
note: GWAS-only tag: 61 studies, 3 PMIDs. PMID:34791234 (PCOS, 2 GCSTs, tagged FINNGEN + Estonia) validates in 'an independent dataset from the Estonian Biobank' and abbreviates it EstBB ('76% for EstBB', abstract); PMID:35922517 (COVID-19 HGI update, 5 GCSTs) lists the Estonian Biobank analysis and data collection teams among its contributors (full text PMC9352569, e.g. 'Estonian Biobank analysis team lead'); PMID:32888493 (blood-cell traits, 54 GCSTs) is not OA (Europe PMC full text, PMC and Cell supplements refused), but Supplementary Table 1 of its bioRxiv preprint (doi:10.1101/2020.01.17.910497, media-2.xlsx) lists 'Estonia_chip' ('Estonia SNP Chip') and 'Estonia_WGS' ('Estonia Whole Genome Sequencing'), both population-based and referenced to PMID:28031487, whose abstract describes 'the population-based Estonian Biobank' - so the tag there also means the Estonian Biobank (two genotyping subsets). So the tag means COHO:0000064 Estonian Biobank (synonyms EB, EGCUT, 'Estonian Genome Center of the University of Tartu'; review row EGCUT). Decision: the tag is only a country name, but CLAUDE.md says every GWAS Catalog tag for a cohort is kept as an acronym however ugly, so Estonia is proposed as an acronym synonym - curator may prefer to leave a bare country name out. EstBB (verified in the PMID:34791234 abstract) also proposed. No clash: no other COHO term, review row or tier-B row uses Estonia or EstBB (COHO:0000251 Estonian Microbiome Cohort is a sub-cohort of COHO:0000064 with different names).

input name: Minnesota Center for Twin and Family Research
label: Minnesota Center for Twin and Family Research
example title: Genome-wide association study meta-analysis of dizygotic twinning illuminates genetic regulation of female fecundity.
example quote: The Minnesota Center for Twin and Family Research (MCTFR) was supported in part by USPHS Grants from the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (AA09367 and AA11886) and the National Institute on Drug Abuse (DA05147, DA13240, and DA024417).
definition: A collection of longitudinal, community-representative twin and adoptive family studies in Minnesota, including the Minnesota Twin Registry, the Minnesota Twin Family Study, the Enrichment Study, the Adolescent Brain study and the Sibling Interaction and Behavior Study, focusing on psychological adjustment, personality, cognitive ability and brain function with an emphasis on substance use and related psychopathology.
location quote: Lykken and his colleagues developed protocols that allowed for the successful ascertainment of large, representative samples of twins from birth records, which can be accessed for research purposes in Minnesota State.
note: 34 GWAS Catalog studies over 6 PMIDs (PMID:25387710 x17 whole-genome sequencing of psychophysiological endophenotypes, PMID:36477530 x8, PMID:39875632 x5, PMID:40962958 x2, PMID:36376304, PMID:38052102). Typed as an aggregation because the 2019 overview says the MCTFR 'comprises multiple longitudinal, community-representative investigations of twin and adoptive families' (PMID:31796137 abstract) and 'now includes five established twin cohorts and one adoption cohort' (BioC text of PMC7056536); its GWAS sample (8,405 genotyped participants clustered in four-member families, PMID:23363460) pools member studies. Members (MTR, MTFS, ES, AdBrain, SIBS) are not in COHO; the same overview lists the ABCD study (row ABCD) among new MCTFR investigations. No COHO or review-file match for MCTFR/Minnesota (grep 2026-09-23). Location quote names Minnesota only (country inferred); from the NCBI BioC text of the author manuscript PMC7056536. Example quote from the PMC10767824 acknowledgements (dizygotic twinning GWAS); the WGS paper PMID:25387710 is not open access.

input name: Relationship between Insulin Sensitivity and Cardiovascular disease
label: Relationship between Insulin Sensitivity and Cardiovascular disease

note: 34 GWAS Catalog studies over 3 PMIDs (32917775x24, 37291194x8, 34059833x2). No match for risc, egir or 'insulin sensitivity' in coho-edit.owl, coho_list.txt or the review file. Label is the PGS name, which matches the design paper (Hills et al. 2004, PMID:14968294: 'The RISC (Relationship between Insulin Sensitivity and Cardiovascular disease) Study'); the paper title calls it the EGIR-RISC Study (European group for the study of insulin resistance), so EGIR-RISC is added as acronym. Example quote from the full text of PMID:37291194 (insulin-stimulated glucose uptake GWAS, PMC7614755), which also points to http://www.egir.org/egirrisc/ (not fetched). Definition from the PMID:14968294 abstract and PMC2709880 (PMID:19455304). Left unlocated: the sources only count the countries without naming them (PMID:14968294 abstract: 'to study insulin resistance and CVD risk in 1500 healthy people aged 30 to 60 years from 20 centres in 13 countries'; PMC2709880: 'healthy men and women of European ancestry, aged between 30 and 60 years, were recruited from 19 centres in 14 European countries').

example quote: We used data from the Rotterdam Study (RSI, RSII and RSIII) to create three hand OA phenotypes

location quote: The first cohort (RS-I) started in 1990 and included 7,983 inhabitants, aged ≥55 years from Ommoord, a suburb of Rotterdam in the Netherlands.
parent quote: The Rotterdam Study (RS) is a prospective, population-based cohort study of determinants of chronic diseases in older adults (7). The first cohort (RS-I) started in 1990 and included 7,983 inhabitants, aged ≥55 years from Ommoord, a suburb of Rotterdam in the Netherlands.
note: GWAS-only tag, no PGS row. 34 GWAS Catalog studies over 4 PMIDs (32888493x24, 33510174x6, 33055079x3, 33717105x1). RSI is the first cohort (RS-I) of the Rotterdam Study (COHO:0000148, whose only synonym is RS): PMID:33055079 (abstract) and PMID:33717105 (PMC7944992, which spells it RS-I) say so explicitly; in PMID:33510174 (muscle weakness, PMC7844411) the main text names only Rotterdam affiliations, and PMID:32888493 (blood-cell traits) is not open access and its PMC BioC text does not contain RSI, so those two are assumed to be the same Rotterdam sub-cohort (co-tagged with Airwave and InCHIANTI; a curator may check their supplements). No match for RSI or RS-I in coho-edit.owl, coho_list.txt, the review file or the tier-B list. Label 'Rotterdam Study I' follows usage such as 'the Rotterdam Study I–IV' (PMC12481288); the tag RSI and the spelling RS-I are acronyms. The GWAS Catalog also tags 6 studies RSII (the second cohort, not in the tier-B list); RS-III is a third. Example quote from the PMID:33055079 abstract (hand osteoarthritis GWAS, GCST90010716); definition, location and parent quotes from PMC7944992 (PMID:33717105).

input name: The Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans
label: Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans
other synonyms: The Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans
example title: Genome-wide association analysis identifies ancestry-specific genetic variation associated with acute response to metformin and glipizide in SUGAR-MGH.
example quote: The Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans (SUGAR-MGH) examined the acute response to metformin and glipizide in order to identify new pharmacogenetic associations for the response to common glucose-lowering medications in individuals at risk of type 2 diabetes.
definition: A pharmacogenetic study established in 2007 at Massachusetts General Hospital, which from 2008 enrolled about 1,000 adults of diverse ancestry enriched for risk of type 2 diabetes and challenged them with glipizide and metformin at clinical research centres in Boston, Massachusetts, to identify genetic variants influencing the acute response to glucose-lowering drugs.
location quote: All CRC visits took place at an academic medical center (Massachusetts General Hospital, Brigham and Women’s Hospital, or the Joslin Diabetes Center, all in Boston, MA).
note: 33 GWAS Catalog studies, all from PMID:37233759 (the SUGAR-MGH GWAS; its Europe PMC full text PMC10790310 returned HTTP 500, so example quote is from the abstract). No match in COHO (coho_list.txt, coho-edit.owl and components grep for SUGAR, Metformin 2026-09-23) or the review file; no acronym clash. Label drops the leading 'The' of the PGS name (kept as other synonym). Definition from the design paper PMC4374872 (PMID:25812009, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01762046: established 2007, first participant enrolled 14 February 2008, planned 1,000 participants 'enriched for individuals at risk of requiring anti-diabetic therapy in the future', recruitment of non-White groups, visits at MGH, Brigham and Women's and Joslin clinical research centres) and the PMID:37233759 abstract ('One thousand participants at risk for type 2 diabetes from diverse ancestries underwent sequential glipizide and metformin challenges'). Location quote names Boston, MA, not the country. Not a sub-cohort of the Mass General Brigham Biobank (COHO:0000383): a separately recruited study.

label: Colon Cancer Family Registry
other synonyms: Colon Cancer Family Registry Cohort
example title: Genome-wide association studies and Mendelian randomization analyses provide insights into the causes of early-onset colorectal cancer.
example quote: We conducted a GWAS meta-analysis of 6176 EOCRC cases and 65 829 controls from the Genetics and Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer Consortium (GECCO), the Colorectal Transdisciplinary Study (CORECT), the Colon Cancer Family Registry (CCFR), and the UK Biobank.
definition: An international registry and cohort, funded by the US National Cancer Institute and begun in 1997, of colorectal cancer cases, their unaffected relatives and population-based controls recruited through six centres in Australasia and North America (the Australasian, Mayo Clinic, Ontario, Seattle, University of Hawaii and USC Consortium registries), as a resource for research on familial and sporadic colorectal cancer.
location quote: Support for case ascertainment was provided in part from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program and the following U.S. state cancer registries: AZ, CO, MN, NC, NH; and by the Victoria Cancer Registry (Australia) and Ontario Cancer Registry (Canada).
note: 32 GWAS Catalog studies over 9 PMIDs, all pooled colorectal cancer analyses of GECCO/CORECT/CCFR (in PMID:38408508 and PMID:38809988 the tag stands beside GECCO and CORECT tags as a consortium-level label). No COHO or review-file match for CCFR / Colon Cancer Family / Colon CFR (grep 2026-09-23); no acronym clash. Typed as a cohort because its own literature calls it the "Colon Cancer Family Registry Cohort" (cohort profile PMID:29490034, not open access; PMC4762074, PMC5706810); a curator may prefer an aggregation of its six site registries (e.g. the Ontario Familial Colorectal Cancer Registry, Seattle Colorectal Cancer Family Registry), which are not in COHO. No parent: the Fred Hutch GECCO page says "Additionally, the Colon Cancer Family Registry (CCFR) and the Colorectal Transdisciplinary study (CORECT) are collaborating with GECCO on many analyses", i.e. CCFR is a partner consortium, not a GECCO member. The Newfoundland registry (NFCCR, row below) is not one of the six CCFR centres named in the funding statement of PMC4762074. Definition from PMC3616155 ("a National Cancer Institute (NCI)–funded registry of CRC cases, unaffected family members, and population-based controls"; "an international collaborative study initiated in 1997") and PMC4762074 (recruitment 1997-2012 "in Australasia and North America"; the six centres). Location quote from the CCFR funding acknowledgement in PMC11112268; the Australasian registry may also have recruited in New Zealand, which I did not verify, so New Zealand is not asserted.

note: 32 GWAS Catalog studies, 1 PMID (PMID:40181193, CHARGE gene-sleep interaction meta-analysis for blood pressure; Europe PMC full text and supplementary files unavailable, so the example quote comes from Supplementary file 2 (cohort descriptions, docx) downloaded from the publisher's article page). location quote: All analyses were conducted within the Gene-Lifestyle Interactions and Dental Endpoints (GLIDE) Consortium in 13 studies from Europe and the USA || The contributing studies were (1) Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC); (2) The Center for Oral Health in Appalachia cohort 1 (COHRA1), which is part of the GENEVA caries consortium; (3) the Dental Registry and DNA Repository of the University of Pittsburgh School of Dental Medicine, (DRDR), also part of the GENEVA caries consortium; (4) the Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos (HCHS/SOL); (5) the Malmö Diet and Cancer Study (MDC); 6) the Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966 (NFBC 1966); (7) the Study of Health in Pomerania (SHIP), (8) the Study of Health in Pomerania Trend (SHIP Trend); (9) TWINGENE, which is a genotyped epidemiological study recruited from the Swedish Twin Registry (TWINGENE); (10) the Women’s Genome Health Study (WGHS); (11) Biobank Japan (BBJ) and (12) Tokyo Medical and Dental University Aggressive Periodontitis Study (TMDUAGP).
note: Tier D (D028), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the GLIDE consortium, whose periodontitis/loose-teeth GWAS was combined with UK Biobank (UKBB/GLIDE summary statistics); P2: the GLIDE consortium's dental caries and periodontal disease GWAS data from an earlier study, meta-analysed with UKB and BBJ. Both GWAS papers, and P3 and P6-P8, mean the consortium. P4 and P5 use GLIDE for its Swedish arm, a population-based cohort of Swedish adults, which may deserve its own term as a member of this consortium. Sweden comes from 'the Swedish arm of the ... GLIDE Study' (D028.63). The consortium's own 2015 paper writes 'and Dental Endpoints', while the PGS Catalog and later papers write 'in Dental Endpoints'. The 'Study' synonym comes from P4, which calls the whole 'the GLIDE Study'. No unit names the member studies. Checked 2026-09-23: Both rightly draft the GLIDE consortium as an aggregation (both tagged GWAS papers use its 2019 summary statistics), but both confine it to 'Europe and the United States', which is true only of the 2015 Mendelian randomization analysis: the first wave behind the tagged data had 12 member studies on three continents, including Biobank Japan and a Tokyo periodontitis study. So both definitions and both country lists miss Japan. Both drafts' Sweden quote describes the separate Swedish GLIDE cohort, not the consortium. X's definition describes the consortium by how later papers used it. Y's calls the members 'dental and periodontal-disease cohort studies', but they are general epidemiological cohorts (ARIC, WGHS, MDC, SHIP and others) with dental data, and its purpose ('gene-lifestyle interactions') is read off the name. X's synonym 'Gene-Lifestyle Interactions and Dental Endpoints Study' comes from a paper about the Swedish GLIDE cohort and is dropped. A second, different sample is also called GLIDE: the Swedish population-based GLIDE cohort (dental records from 1999 to 2015 in Västerbotten, linked to the Västerbotten Intervention Programme; PMID:33919427, PMID:29956852). It is not one of the 12 first-wave member studies, and neither tagged GWAS paper means it. It could get its own term, related to NSHDS (COHO:0000927). GLIDE2 (PMID:36000800) is the consortium's second wave (21 studies on several continents) and is left out of the synonyms as a phase name. First-wave members already in COHO could be linked with hasCohort from the same member-list sentence: ARIC COHO:0000011, HCHS/SOL COHO:0000388, MDC COHO:0000296, SHIP COHO:0000202, SHIP-TREND COHO:0000410, TwinGene COHO:0000193, WGHS COHO:0000516 and BBJ COHO:0000377 (NFBC1966, COHRA1, DRDR and TMDUAGP need checking). The consortium uses both 'in Dental Endpoints' (2019, GLIDE2) and 'and Dental Endpoints' (2015).

note: Tier D (D032), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the Harvard Aging Brain Study, one of the cohorts with raw amyloid PET and genotype data in the multi-ethnic amyloid imaging GWAS. P3's age range (65-90) and the dataset sizes describe subsets, so they are left out. The dataset paper (P4, PMID:25843019) would be the best definition source. None of the candidate COHO terms is HABS. The lower-case synonym is P1's own abbreviation expansion (D032.13). Checked 2026-09-23: Both identify the Harvard Aging Brain Study correctly. X's 'aged 65–90' comes from one 2016 analysis of 186 participants: the study's entry criterion was 65 or older, with a few enrolled from age 62, and no upper limit is stated. (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC6547132/fullTextXML). Not in COHO under any name; the GWAS tag 'Harvard' belongs to other cohorts.

P1: the Hong Kong Osteoporosis Study, whose genotyped participants were followed for dementia through CDARS. Recruitment ages differ between sources (P4 says aged 50 or above, while P5 analyses participants aged 40 or over), so no age is given. The cohort profile cited in P1's supplement (PMID:29024957, D034.11) would be the best definition source. COHO:0000559 (the Hong Kong disc degeneration cohort) is a different cohort. Checked 2026-09-23: Both identify the Hong Kong Osteoporosis Study correctly. Y's 'aged 50 or above' is wrong: it was the entry criterion of one 2012 vertebral-fracture analysis (P4), while the cohort took Southern Chinese residents aged 12–105 (PMID:41735671). The cohort profile (Int J Epidemiol 2018;47:397, PMID:29024957, doi 10.1093/ije/dyx172) could not be fetched (the publisher's bot check blocks it from both networks, and it is not in PMC), so its entry criteria were checked in two open-access HKOS papers instead. A country quote closer to recruitment, if preferred: '9,449 Southern Chinese community-dwelling participants were recruited from public road shows and health fairs in Hong Kong from 1995 to 2010' (P1 supplement, ALZ-20-5973-s003.docx). P1: not named in any unit (abstract only), presumably the same study, as an African American cohort in the African-ancestry height GWAS; P2: SAPPHIRE, the Henry Ford Health System study, as an African American cohort in the atopic dermatitis meta-analysis. P5 describes a subset with physician-diagnosed asthma. P7 adjusts for asthma status, which suggests the cohort also includes people without asthma, but no unit says so, so the definition does not say whether all participants have asthma. definition: A prospective birth cohort of pregnant South Asian women aged 18–40 and their offspring, recruited in urban Bangalore and rural Solur in Karnataka, India, and in the Peel region of Ontario, Canada, with questionnaires, anthropometry, a glucose tolerance test, and blood and DNA samples in pregnancy, newborn measurements and follow-up of the children to age 3, to study the environmental and genetic determinants of adiposity among South Asians.

P1: START as one of many cohorts in a multi-ancestry gestational-diabetes/glycaemic-traits GWAS meta-analysis; P2: the full Canada-India cohort (its own design paper); P3: its Canadian arm ('START-Canada') within the 'NutriGen Alliance'; P4-P7: its Ontario, Canada arm specifically. P3 groups a Canadian arm ('START (SouTh Asian birth cohoRT)-Canada') into something called the 'NutriGen Alliance' with CHILD and FAMILY; NutriGen Alliance is not a candidate COHO term or a batch row, so parent is left null — a researcher should check whether it needs its own COHO term as START's aggregation parent. Most single-study papers (P4-P7) describe only the Ontario, Canada recruitment; the India arm is documented only in the cohort's own design paper (P2). PGS Catalog's 'SouTh Asian BiRth CohorT' and the evidence's 'SouTh Asian biRth cohorT' (D060.29/33) are stylised case variants of the label, kept as synonyms. Checked 2026-09-23: Both identify START correctly. X doubted that the Indian arm was recruited, so it asserts only Canada and calls the Indian sites 'planned'. The Indian arm was recruited: a 2018 START paper reports women enrolled in early pregnancy at an urban and a rural health centre in Karnataka (PMID:29400265). The design paper names the sites: St John's Medical College Hospital in Bangalore, Snehalaya Hospital in Solur, and hospitals in the Peel region of Ontario. Y has both countries right, but it misses the stylised variant 'SouTh Asian birth cohoRT' that PMID:27708121 uses (X has it), and it quotes only the design paper's plan for India. P1 used START's Canadian participants only (country 'Canada' in its cohort table), so the tag denotes the cohort through its Canadian arm (called START-Canada in PMID:27708121). The Canadian arm recruited women from July 2011 to November 2015 (PMID:28800568); the design paper gives no dates. START-Canada is one of the four birth cohorts of the NutriGen Alliance (with CHILD COHO:0000234, FAMILY COHO:0000680 and the Aboriginal Birth Cohort), which is not in COHO; if the Alliance gets a term, the membership quote would come from PMID:27708121. The Finnish name means roughly 'people who have developed type 1 diabetes, with their family members' (my gloss, not a source quote). IDDMGEN is not T1DGEN (tier-D D306, 'Tyypin 1 Diabeteksen Genetiikka'), a separate Finnish collection of cases only. Nor is it part of the Type 1 Diabetes Genetics Consortium (COHO:0000174): every paper lists it separately from T1DGC, although PMID:28983737 says its genotyping was paid for through the T1DGC grant. For both IDDMGEN and T1DGEN, PMID:28983737 cites Qiao et al. 2007 (PMID:18093291), a genome scan of Finnish multiplex families from the National Public Health Institute, Helsinki, and Karolinska Institute. That paper never uses either name, so the recruiting institution and dates remain unverified; a curator with access could ask the T1DGC/Cambridge authors. The PGS Catalog id IDDMGEN has no scores.

Tier D (D252), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: genotype data/samples generated on the Immunochip array for a previously published SLE case-control study (reference [5] in the paper), used for replication and local genetic-correlation analysis with severe COVID-19; not itself a defined, named cohort. Immunochip is Illumina's custom genotyping array for autoimmune/inflammatory disease loci. The paper repeatedly uses 'Immunochip data'/'the Immunochip study [5]' to mean data from an unnamed prior SLE case-control sample genotyped on that array (D252.1, D252.4, D252.7, D252.8, D252.13, D252.16, D252.22, D252.25, D252.34), never as the name of a defined group of people recruited by this study. Checked 2026-09-23: None. Both drafts rightly call it not a cohort. In the tagged paper, 'Immunochip' means the SLE case-control genotype data of reference [5], a study named after Illumina's Immunochip array. The PGS Catalog id 'Immunochip' (PGS000194/PGS000195) points at yet another Immunochip-genotyped dataset (source PMID:26053495, an autoimmune-disease colocalization study). So in both catalogues the tag names a genotyping array or dataset, not a group of people. If COHO ever wants the SLE collection behind reference [5], the candidate is the multi-study SLE case-control collection of Langefeld et al. 2017 (funding includes SLEGEN, the International Consortium on the Genetics of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus), not 'Immunochip'. No COHO term covers lupus.

AASC is the anti-aging study cohort of Ehime University: the MAGIC cohort table gives it as Japanese, Japan, population-based, with the J-SHIPP paper PMID:23020117 as its reference; the DIAMANTE supplement's ethics statement for 'Anti-aging study cohort (AASC)' names the Ehime University Graduate School of Medicine; and P3 (PMID:29491417) calls the same sample 'the anti-aging study cohort' in its abstract and 'J-SHIPP' in its title. Its participants are community residents who attend the Anti-aging Center health check-up at Ehime University Hospital (from February 2006) and who consent to follow-up in the Japan Shimanami Health Promoting Program (J-SHIPP) (PMID:38280978, PMID:28371474). The draft's label, acronym and example were right; it lacked the definition and country, which the J-SHIPP papers give. The Japan Shimanami Health Promoting Program (J-SHIPP) of Ehime University is broader than the anti-aging check-up cohort: its papers go back to 2002 (community residents) and include a longitudinal study of 2,037 community residents with local-government health records (PMID:21550079). The anti-aging check-up participants are one of its samples, so a J-SHIPP term, if minted, would be this cohort's isSubCohortOf parent ('Participants who gave informed consent for using their clinical information obtained at the health check-up program for a longitudinal study were enrolled in the Shimanami Health Promoting Program (the J-SHIPP study)', PMC10821963). J-SHIPP is not in COHO or this review. The lower-case synonym is the running-text form of P3's abstract, kept under the case-variant rule. Not related to the Nagahama Study (COHO:0000531) beyond being analysed alongside it.

label: Department of Defense Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
other synonyms: ADNI Department of Defense studies
example title: Large multi-ethnic genetic analyses of amyloid imaging identify new genes for Alzheimer disease.
example quote: These subjects were recruited from the Memory and Aging Project (MAP) at the Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center (Knight-ADRC) [16, 17], Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) [18], the Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network (DIAN) [19], Anti-Amyloid Treatment in Asymptomatic Alzheimer's Disease (A4) [20], ADNI Department of Defense (ADNIDOD) studies, Australian Imaging, Biomarkers and Lifestyle (AIBL) [21], The Harvard Aging Brain Study (HABS) [22], and University of Pittsburgh (UPitt) [23].
definition: A multi-site extension of the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, funded by the US Department of Defense, that enrolled Vietnam War veterans with a history of traumatic brain injury and/or ongoing post-traumatic stress disorder, with or without mild cognitive impairment, and veteran controls without either, identified mainly through Veterans Affairs records, and studies them with ADNI's clinical, cognitive, imaging and fluid biomarker methods to find whether these conditions contribute to the development of Alzheimer's disease.
location quote: This study examined how traumatic brain injury and post-traumatic stress disorder relate to cognitive function and neuroimaging markers in U.S. veterans from the Department of Defense Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI-DOD).
parent quote: The DoD-ADNI is a multi-site extension of ADNI designed to investigate the effects of TBI and PTSD on AD-related pathology in Vietnam-era Veterans (Weiner et al., 2014, 2017).
note: Tier D (D004), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ADNI-DOD/ADNIDOD as one of many contributing cohorts (Knight-ADRC, A4, DIAN, ADNI, AIBL, HABS, Memento, MCSA, WRAP, Berkeley, Korean study, MISSION-AD, UPitt) in a multi-ethnic amyloid-PET GWAS; the paper expands the name (D004.7, D004.10) but gives no design, recruitment or purpose for ADNI-DOD itself. P2-P7 (papers cited for the cohort): design/profile papers for OTHER cohorts in the same meta-analysis (AIBL, an endophenotype GWAS, APOE/PiB-PET findings, the DIAN cohort, the A4 study) -- none concern ADNI-DOD. D004.7 and D004.10 confirm the label ('ADNI Department of Defense studies', matching the PGS Catalog name) and both acronym forms, but no unit describes ADNI-DOD's own population, recruitment sites, dates or purpose beyond co-listing as a contributing cohort. D004.12's 'nearly all the samples in the ADNI-DOD cohort were males' describes only this one meta-analysis's included sample, not stated as a general cohort characteristic, so not used. The name, and its listing directly after ADNI in D004.7, suggest ADNI-DOD may be a Department of Defense-linked extension of ADNI (COHO:0000367), but no unit states this relationship explicitly, so parent is left null; a researcher should check ADNI's own documentation for the 'ADNI-DOD' study and confirm its population (military veterans?), sites, and any formal relationship to ADNI. Checked 2026-09-23: Deferred for want of a profile; research settles it. ADNI-DOD is DOD ADNI, the Department of Defense-funded extension of ADNI for Vietnam War veterans: 'These studies are collectively termed "DOD ADNI," and aim to enroll approximately 400 elderly Veterans who served in Vietnam' (PMID:28758146), 'a multi-site extension of ADNI designed to investigate the effects of TBI and PTSD on AD-related pathology in Vietnam-era Veterans' (PMID:42316769). Its own name, used as its group authorship, is 'Department of Defense Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative'; the draft's label 'ADNI Department of Defense studies' is only the GWAS paper's gloss of its abbreviation (kept as a synonym). The parent is ADNI (COHO:0000367), which the draft suspected but left out. The draft's acronyms and example are right. Not an institution: 'institution?' in the triage flag is wrong. The protocol (adni.loni.usc.edu DOD-ADNI protocol, 2012) and the award W81XWH-12-2-0012 suggest enrolment began around 2012, but no text read states a start date, so none is given. ADNI's own participants and DOD ADNI's veterans are distinct samples sharing ADNI's methods, sites and database (LONI IDA project ADNIDOD), which is why isSubCohortOf ADNI is used rather than identity. Not related to D316 VETSA (Vietnam Era Twin Study of Aging), a separate twin study.

label: Anorexia Nervosa Genetics Initiative
example title: Genome-wide association study of school grades identifies genetic overlap between language ability, psychopathology and creativity.
example quote: ANGI is an international collaboration established between scientists in the United States, Australia/New Zealand, Sweden and Denmark to establish a cohort of individuals with and without AN.
definition: An international collaboration, sponsored by the Klarman Family Foundation and the US National Institute of Mental Health, that recruited individuals with a lifetime history of anorexia nervosa and controls in the United States, Australia, New Zealand, Sweden and Denmark, through treatment centres, national registers and traditional and social media, with blood samples and an online eating-disorder questionnaire, to rapidly expand the samples available for genome-wide association studies of anorexia nervosa.
location quote: ANGI recruited from the United States (US), Australia/New Zealand (ANZ), Sweden (SE), and Denmark (DK).
note: Tier D (D005), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the Danish arm of ANGI, processed together with iPSYCH; P2 (ANGI's own overview/methods paper), P5 (the Australia/New Zealand arm's own paper), P6-P9 (found by name): the full international ANGI collaboration (US, Australia/New Zealand, Sweden, Denmark), which most of the evidence describes and which this term drafts. Well evidenced by ANGI's own overview/methods paper (P2) and its ANZ-arm paper (P5). P1 (the row's only GWAS Catalog paper) specifically used ANGI's Danish arm only, processed together with iPSYCH (D005.9, D005.11) -- drafted the full international ANGI since that is what most of the evidence (P2, P5-P9) describes. iPSYCH and the Skane University Hospital memory-clinic cohort in the candidate list are not ANGI itself: iPSYCH is a related but distinct Danish case-cohort sharing infrastructure with ANGI's Danish arm; Skane appears to be an unrelated match, probably via the word 'Sweden'. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, countries and example are right. The definition is accurate but thin: it gives only the collaboration and its funder, not how ANGI was built. Its overview paper (PMID:30287268, author manuscript PMC6338222) describes the design: four hubs (UNC Chapel Hill, QIMR Berghofer with the University of Otago, Karolinska Institutet, Aarhus University); cases with a lifetime AN diagnosis recruited through treatment centres, the Swedish and Danish registers and traditional and social media; an online questionnaire (ED100K-v1) and blood samples; and the goal 'to rapidly expand available samples for genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of AN'. The sponsors were the Klarman Family Foundation and NIMH, not the foundation alone. Kept as a cohort, not an aggregation, although the 'aggregation?' flag has some basis: besides its own recruits, ANGI took controls from existing studies (QSkin in Australia, the Christchurch Health and Development Study in New Zealand, LifeGene in Sweden, the Price Foundation study in the US) and in Denmark identified cases and controls from the national registers and neonatal blood spots, as iPSYCH does. It was built as one initiative with a common protocol, and its papers call it 'a cohort of individuals with and without AN'. Its samples augmented the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium's AN collection ('ANGI has substantially augmented Psychiatric Genomics Consortium AN sample collection', PMID:30287268), but the 2019 GWAS treats ANGI and PGC-ED as separate data sources, so no memberOf PGC (COHO:0000146) is proposed. Not a member of GCAN (COHO:0000077), which predates it. Registered as NCT01916538.

label: Ashford study
other synonyms: Asthma in Ashford study|Asthma in Ashford|Ashford cohort
example title: A meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies of childhood wheezing phenotypes identifies ANXA1 as a susceptibility locus for persistent wheezing.
example quote: The Ashford study is an unselected birth cohort study established in 1991 in Ashford, UK (Atkinson et al., 1999).
definition: An unselected birth cohort of children born in 1992–1993 in Ashford, Kent, England, whose mothers were recruited in pregnancy from 1991 as the UK cohort of the Asthma Multicentre Infant Cohort Study, with house-dust allergen measured in infancy and follow-up by questionnaire, lung function and skin prick tests to age 14 years and a questionnaire at about age 20, to study how early-life allergen exposure and other factors relate to the development of atopy, wheeze and asthma.
location quote: The Ashford study is an unselected birth cohort study established in 1991 in Ashford, UK (Atkinson et al., 1999).
note: Tier D (D006), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: Ashford as one of five UK birth cohorts (with ALSPAC, IOW, MAAS, SEATON) in the STELAR consortium's childhood-wheezing GWAS meta-analysis. P2-P3 (papers cited for the cohort): early allergen-exposure studies of the Ashford, Kent birth cohort itself. P4-P7 concern the other STELAR cohorts (the STELAR e-Lab, ALSPAC, MAAS), not Ashford specifically. D006.13 (the STELAR paper's own cohort-description appendix) gives a clean, complete profile. D006.16 suggests a possible later rebranding/follow-up as 'the Asthma in Ashford study' (ethics re-review in 2014-15); treated as the same cohort and kept as a synonym, but a checker should confirm this is not a separate follow-up wave. STELAR itself (which defines Ashford's membership alongside ALSPAC, IOW, MAAS and SEATON) is not a candidate COHO term or a row in this batch, so no memberOf parent is asserted; STELAR may need its own aggregation term. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, country and example are right. The definition gives the cohort's STELAR membership as if it were its purpose and stops at age 14. The cohort was set up as the first (UK) cohort of a three-centre European study, the Asthma Multicentre Infant Cohort Study, whose 'purpose ... is the examination of factors which modify the relationship between allergen exposure in infant life and subsequent atopy and asthma' (PMID:10232430; 'Three cohorts (Ashford in the United Kingdom and Menorca and Barcelona in Spain) followed the same research protocol', PMID:16950296). STELAR is a later data-sharing network of five birth cohorts. The STELAR paper's appendix adds a questionnaire at age 20 in 2015, which is when the name 'Asthma in Ashford study' appears (Imperial College ethics review, 2014). Two possible parents, neither in COHO nor in this review: the Asthma Multicentre Infant Cohort Study (AMICS: Ashford, Menorca and Barcelona; its Menorca arm later became part of INMA, COHO:0000100) and the STELAR consortium (ALSPAC COHO:0000016, IOW COHO:0000605, MAAS COHO:0000656, SEATON D059 and Ashford), which would be a cohort aggregation. If STELAR is minted, Ashford gets hasCohort from it with the quote 'The Study Team for Early Life Asthma Research (STELAR) consortium (Custovic et al., 2015) brings together five UK population-based birth cohorts' from PMC10292845. 'ASHFORD' is the capitalised short name used in STELAR tables, kept as a case variant of the tag. The draft's worry that 'Asthma in Ashford study' might be a separate follow-up is unfounded: the 2019 paper uses 'Asthma in Ashford cohort' for the age-5 data of the same children.

input name: Serial Biomarker Measurements and New Echocardiographic Techniques in chronic Heart Failure Patients Result in Tailored Prediction of Prognosis
label: Serial Biomarker Measurements and New Echocardiographic Techniques in Chronic Heart Failure Patients Result in Tailored Prediction of Prognosis
other synonyms: Serial Biomarker Measurements and New Echocardiographic Techniques in chronic Heart Failure Patients Result in Tailored Prediction of Prognosis
example title: Genome-wide association study meta-analysis provides insights into the etiology of heart failure and its subtypes.
example quote: Bio-SHiFT (Serial Biomarker Measurements and New Echocardiographic Techniques in chronic Heart Failure Patients Result in Tailored Prediction of Prognosis) is a prospective, observational study of stable patients with chronic heart failure (CHF).
definition: A prospective multicentre cohort of clinically stable adult outpatients with chronic heart failure, enrolled from 2011 at Erasmus MC, Rotterdam, and Northwest Clinics, Alkmaar, the Netherlands, and seen every three months for blood sampling and clinical assessment, with echocardiography in a subset, to assess whether serial measurements of biomarkers can track disease progression and predict prognosis in individual patients.
location quote: The study was conducted in Erasmus MC, Rotterdam, the Netherlands, and Noordwest Ziekenhuisgroep, Alkmaar, the Netherlands.
note: Tier D (D008), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: Bio-SHiFT grouped with TRIUMPH and Doetinchem as three separately acknowledged Dutch heart-failure cohorts in a heart-failure GWAS meta-analysis. P2-P3 (found by name): the Bio-SHiFT chronic-heart-failure biomarker cohort itself. Well evidenced by the GWAS paper's own supplement (D008.4-6), which gives a complete profile (design, sites, recruitment). D008.1 lists Bio-SHiFT alongside TRIUMPH (COHO:0000952) and Doetinchem (COHO:0000906) as three separate acknowledged cohorts, not a hierarchical relationship, so no parent is asserted. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, country, acronym, example and the absence of a parent are right. The definition is sound but leaves out when (enrolment from October 2011; registry start August 2011) and the design that gives the study its name: visits every three months with blood sampling, echocardiography in a subset, and the aim 'to investigate whether disease progression in individual patients with chronic heart failure (CHF) can be accurately assessed by serial measurements of disease-related (novel) biomarkers' (NCT01851538). The label is the PGS Catalog's spelling with 'chronic' in lower case; the registered official title (NCT01851538) and the cohort's own papers (PMID:30760105) capitalise 'Chronic', so that is the label and the PGS form is kept as a synonym. 'Bio-SHIFT' is the capitalisation in the HERMES cohort-table heading, kept as a case variant of the acronym. Northwest Clinics (Noordwest Ziekenhuisgroep) is the Alkmaar hospital that ClinicalTrials.gov lists as 'Medical Center Alkmaar'. In HERMES the three Dutch studies form one case-control dataset (Bio-SHiFT and TRIUMPH cases, Doetinchem controls), but none is part of another, so no parent is right.

label: Bonn Study of COVID Genetics
other synonyms: Bonn study of COVID genetics|Bonn Study of COVID19 genetics
example title: Genome-wide association study of long COVID.
example quote: For the initial discovery analysis, we used data from the following 24 studies: Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), Bonn Study of COVID Genetics (BoSCO), Banque québécoise de la COVID-19 (BQC19), Danish Blood Donor Study (DBDS), Extended Cohort for E-health, Environment and DNA (EXCEED), FinnGen, GCAT | Genomes for life, Genetic Bases of COVID-19 Clinical Variability (GEN-COVID), Genotek, Genetics of Long COVID (GOLD), Helix Exome+ and Healthy Nevada Project COVID-19 Phenotypes (Helix), MexGen-COVID Initiative, COVID-19 Ioannina Biobank (Ioannina), Genome-wide assessment of the gene variants associated with severe COVID-19 phenotype in Iran (IrCovid), Japan COVID-19
definition: A study run by the Institute of Human Genetics, University of Bonn, Germany, that continuously recruits adults with SARS-CoV-2 infection confirmed by PCR or antibody testing from the general population through public announcements, collecting questionnaires on demographics, pre-existing conditions and the course of infection (and, from September 2021, on long COVID) and DNA for genotyping, to study host genetic factors in COVID-19.
location quote: Bonn Study of COVID Genetics Germany The BoSCO study continuously recruits individuals from the general population through public announcements.
parent quote: Data for initial discovery GWASs (Long COVID HGI data freeze 4) was collected by DBDS, EstBB, FinnGen, GEN-COVID, GENCOV, MexGen-COVID (Supplementary Tables 1, 3–8 and 12), ALSPAC, BoSCO, BQC19, EXCEED, GCAT (COVICAT), Genotek, GOLD, Helix, Ioannina, IrCovid, JapanTaskForce, Lifelines, MoBa, MSCIC, PMBB, SweCovid, COMRI, TiKoCo, TwinsUK, UKB and Understanding Society (Supplementary Tables 11 and 12).
note: Tier D (D009), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: BoSCO as one of the discovery-cohort contributors to the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative's long-COVID GWAS meta-analysis (data freeze 4); the paper's supplement separately describes BoSCO's own recruitment and design. Well evidenced by the GWAS paper's own supplement, including the ethics-registered official title (D009.25, lower-case variant kept as synonym). The candidate list's COHO:0000094 'Human Genetics Initiative' (HGI) is the NIMH psychiatric-genetics repository, an unrelated project that only shares the acronym HGI with the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative this paper's meta-analysis actually belongs to; not used as a parent. Same false match appears for D010 (BQC19). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, country and example are right. The draft missed the parent: the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative is already COHO:0000238 (not only the unrelated NIMH 'Human Genetics Initiative', COHO:0000094, that the draft rightly rejected), and BoSCO contributed to the Long COVID HGI data freeze; COHO:0000238 already has hasCohort to the Tirschenreuth cohort (COHO:0000970) with the same sentence. The definition calls it a prospective cohort 'based at' the institute from an affiliation line and omits that participants are genotyped for a study of COVID-19 host genetics; its country quote was also an author affiliation, replaced by the cohort table's own row ('Bonn Study of COVID Genetics Germany ...'). The PGS Catalog name 'Bonn Study of COVID19 genetics' is kept as a synonym because the Catalog tags it. BoSCO has no design paper that I found; the supplement of PMID:40399555 is its fullest description. Not related to D093 Bonn-OMNI (an Alzheimer's disease GWAS dataset of PMID:42237039) or E129 BOMA (a bipolar disorder study of Bonn and Mannheim).

label: Biobanque québécoise de la COVID-19
other synonyms: Biobanque Québécoise de la COVID-19|Banque québécoise de la COVID-19|Biobanque Quebec COVID19|Biobanque Québécoise de la Covid-19
example title: Genome-wide association study of long COVID.
example quote: For the initial discovery analysis, we used data from the following 24 studies: Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), Bonn Study of COVID Genetics (BoSCO), Banque québécoise de la COVID-19 (BQC19), Danish Blood Donor Study (DBDS), Extended Cohort for E-health, Environment and DNA (EXCEED), FinnGen, GCAT | Genomes for life, Genetic Bases of COVID-19 Clinical Variability (GEN-COVID), Genotek, Genetics of Long COVID (GOLD), Helix Exome+ and Healthy Nevada Project COVID-19 Phenotypes (Helix), MexGen-COVID Initiative, COVID-19 Ioannina Biobank (Ioannina), Genome-wide assessment of the gene variants associated with severe COVID-19 phenotype in Iran (IrCovid), Japan COVID-19
definition: A province-wide biobank and prospective cohort in Québec, Canada, launched in March 2020 by the Fonds de recherche du Québec–Santé and Génome Québec, which recruits through a network of Québec hospitals adults and children with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, both hospitalised and non-hospitalised, and PCR-negative controls, with longitudinal biosamples and clinical data, to study the clinical and biological determinants of COVID-19 clinical trajectories.
location quote: Participants were recruited from eight academic hospitals in the province of Quebec, Canada.
parent quote: Data for initial discovery GWASs (Long COVID HGI data freeze 4) was collected by DBDS, EstBB, FinnGen, GEN-COVID, GENCOV, MexGen-COVID (Supplementary Tables 1, 3–8 and 12), ALSPAC, BoSCO, BQC19, EXCEED, GCAT (COVICAT), Genotek, GOLD, Helix, Ioannina, IrCovid, JapanTaskForce, Lifelines, MoBa, MSCIC, PMBB, SweCovid, COMRI, TiKoCo, TwinsUK, UKB and Understanding Society (Supplementary Tables 11 and 12).
note: Tier D (D010), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: BQC19 as one of the discovery-cohort contributors to the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative's long-COVID GWAS meta-analysis (data freeze 4); the paper's supplement separately describes BQC19's own recruitment, design and location. Well evidenced by the GWAS paper's own supplement. Two name forms appear: 'Biobanque quebecoise de la COVID-19' (D010.10, matching the PGS Catalog's 'Biobanque' spelling) and 'Banque quebecoise de la COVID-19' (D010.16, without 'Bio'); used the former as label, kept the latter as a synonym. Same false-match caveat as D009: candidate COHO:0000094 'Human Genetics Initiative' is the unrelated NIMH repository, not the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative this paper belongs to. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, country and example are right. The definition took one paper's description (hospital presenters with and without infection) for the whole: BQC19's own design paper (PMID:34010280) describes a province-wide biobank launched in March 2020 by the FRQS and Génome Québec that recruits confirmed COVID-19 adults and children in hospital (hospitalized cohort), 'asymptomatic, mild and moderate ambulatory cases who are recruited one-month post-infection (non-hospitalized cohort)', and PCR-negative controls for both, with longitudinal sampling, 'to prospectively study the clinical and biological determinants of COVID-19 clinical trajectories'. The draft missed the parent: BQC19 contributed to the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative, which is COHO:0000238 (not the NIMH HGI, COHO:0000094). Review row D090 (tag BCQ19, PGS name 'Biobanque Québécoise de la Covid-19', GCST90132193–95, PMID:36327219) is this biobank under a transposed acronym and should be 'same as D010'; its tag and PGS name are included above. 'Banque québécoise de la COVID-19' is the long COVID paper's slip for the name but is kept because that paper, the example, uses it. The design paper itself also once writes 'BCQ19' ('The BCQ19 governance is summarized in Fig 1').

label: Childhood Asthma Management Program
example title: Zinc finger protein 33B demonstrates sex interaction with atopy-related markers in childhood asthma.
example quote: We performed a genome-wide gene-by-sex interaction analysis for atopy-related markers using whole-genome sequencing data based on 889 trios from the Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica Study (GACRS) and 284 trios from the Childhood Asthma Management Program (CAMP).
definition: A multicentre, randomized, double-masked clinical trial of long-term inhaled treatment for mild to moderate asthma (budesonide, nedocromil or placebo, each with albuterol as needed) in children aged 5–12 years, who were enrolled in 1993–1995 at eight clinical centres in the United States and Canada and followed after the trial into adulthood, with a genetic ancillary study of the children and their parents.
location quote: Subjects were recruited from 8 different North American cities: Albuquerque, Baltimore, Boston, Denver, San Diego, Seattle, St. Louis, and Toronto.
parent quote: This study is part of the NHLBI Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) Whole Genome Sequencing Program.
note: Tier D (D011), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CAMP as one of two family-based trio cohorts (with GACRS) in a gene-by-sex atopy-marker interaction GWAS; the same paper's methods describe this study's own trio-based genetic-ancillary subset, not CAMP's overall multicentre trial design. P2: CAMP as one of many European-ancestry cohorts (with ALSPAC, BAMSE, CATSS, RAINE and others) in an atopic-dermatitis GWAS meta-analysis, restricted there to non-Hispanic white genotyped participants (D011.30) -- a subset, not CAMP's whole population (32% ethnic minority per D011.57). P3-P5, P7-P8 (found by name): the Childhood Asthma Management Program clinical trial and its genetic ancillary study. P6 (found by name): an apparently unrelated, more recent 'Childhood Asthma Management Program' behavioural-intervention pilot abbreviated CHAMP/mCHAMP -- not the same cohort. CAMP's own design/rationale paper (P4) is the authoritative source for the definition; avoided D011.13's 'family-based design focused on trios' and D011.30's 'non-Hispanic white subjects', both of which describe only the genetic-ancillary/GWAS-specific subsets used in P1 and P2 respectively (CAMP's own paper states 32% of participants were from ethnic minority groups, D011.57). D011.18 ties CAMP's genetic data to a TOPMed-branded dbGaP accession ('NHLBI TOPMed Childhood Asthma Management Program'), drafted as memberOf COHO:0000985 (TOPMed). No unit gives a recruitment country/location beyond the Brigham and Women's Hospital-coordinated genetic ancillary study and NHLBI funding, both excluded per the funder/affiliation rule, so countries is left empty. P6 ('mCHAMP'/'CHAMP') coincidentally expands to the same words but is a distinct, apparently unrelated program -- flagged in tag_meaning, not added as a synonym. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, parent and example are right, and the draft rightly kept the trios and the non-Hispanic white subset out of the definition. The definition leaves out when and where: children were enrolled in 1993–1995 at eight North American centres (Albuquerque, Baltimore, Boston, Denver, San Diego, Seattle, St. Louis and Toronto) and followed to 2012, into adulthood (PMID:34212545). The draft gave no country because it found only funder and affiliation text; the recruitment cities give the United States and Canada. The parent is right but its quote was a data-availability sentence; replaced by the TOPMed dbGaP study's own statement, as used for COHO:0000985's other members. Countries could also be quoted from PMID:21244681 only as 'North American'; the eight cities give the countries. The mobile 'Childhood Asthma Management Program' app study (mCHAMP, PMID:41860588) is unrelated, as the draft said. GACRS (D023), CAMP's partner in PMID:35953101, may be COHO:0000078 (Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica); not checked here.

input name: Better Outcomes for Children (Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center)
note: Tier D (D012), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (EoE GWAS, PMID 36400179): CCHMC = the local case/control sample assembled at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center from the Cincinnati Center for Eosinophilic Disorders plus the Cincinnati Genomic Control Cohort (GCC) (D012.1-2, D012.8). P2 (ITP GWAS, PMID 39189922): abstract does not name the cohort, no full text available. P3 (atopic dermatitis GWAS, PMID 39245941): CCHMC = a different local composite, the Greater Cincinnati Pediatric Clinical Repository (GCPCR) plus the Cincinnati Genomic Control Cohort (GCC) (D012.17). CCHMC = Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center, the institution where locally recruited samples were assembled; the tag denotes a different composite sample in each study (CCED+GCC in P1 per D012.1-2/.8; GCPCR+GCC in P3 per D012.17), not one fixed named cohort. The underlying named repositories (Greater Cincinnati Pediatric Clinic(al) Repository/GCPCR, Cincinnati Center for Eosinophilic Disorders, and the Cincinnati Genomic Control Cohort/Greater Cincinnati Childhood Cohort, GCC, described in D012.35-56) are candidates for their own separate cohort terms but are not this row's tag, and are not tracked elsewhere in this review. The PGS Catalog name 'Better Outcomes for Children' is not attested by any unit; P6-P11 (found by searching that phrase) are all unrelated generic pediatric-research papers, confirming it is not this cohort's real name. Candidate COHO:0000122 (MEGA, a Dutch venous-thrombosis cohort) is a false match: D012.22/.30's 'MEGA' is the Multi-Ethnic Genotyping Array, not that cohort. Checked 2026-09-23: None in the verdict. One gap in the reasoning: P2 (PMID:39189922) is open access and does say what CCHMC is there. Cincinnati Children's Hospital was one of eight centres that contributed samples to the Pediatric ITP Consortium of North America's biorepository, so the tag means yet another sample, a site subset of that biorepository. An institution tag, handled like the review's rows Columbia and UCSF. The PGS Catalog name 'Better Outcomes for Children' is the title of Cincinnati Children's eMERGE III site grant U01HG008666 ('Better Outcomes for Children: Promoting Excellence in Healthcare Genomics to Inform Policy', grantome.com/grant/NIH/U01-HG008666-03), not the name of a sample. The hospital's biobank is now called the Discover Together Biobank. The named local collections, GCPCR (PMID:22768387) and the Greater Cincinnati Childhood Cohort / Cincinnati Genomic Control Cohort (GCC, PMID:33520904), could have terms of their own, but neither is a GWAS Catalog tag or PGS id, and neither is in COHO or in this review.

label: Chinese National Twin Registry
note: Tier D (D013), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1, P5, P6, P7 (D013.1, .15, .18, .21): CNTR = the Chinese National Twin Registry throughout, used for heritability/twin analyses of BMI, lipids, DNA methylation, blood pressure and cardiometabolic traits. P3, P4 (D013.7, .10-11): the registry's own founding/status papers (established 2000/2001). Exact match: label 'Chinese National Twin Registry' and acronym 'CNTR' (both the GWAS tag and the PGS id) are already on COHO:0000933; nothing in the evidence to add. Checked 2026-09-23: None. COHO:0000933 is the registry itself, not a parent or an arm. It already carries the acronym CNTR, which is both the GWAS tag and the PGS id, and it already uses GCST90270288 (PMID:36606461) as its example.
