input name: Continental Origins and Genetic Epidemiology Network
label: Continental Origins and Genetic Epidemiology Network
example title: Genome-wide association study of white blood cell count in 16,388 African Americans: the continental origins and genetic epidemiology network (COGENT).
example quote: The subjects participating in the GWAS consisted of a total of 16,388 self-identified African-American individuals from 7 population-based cohorts (ARIC, CARDIA, JHS, WHI, HANDLS, Health ABC, and GeneSTAR) that belong to the Continental Origins and Genetic Epidemiology Network (COGENT).
definition: A network of cohorts of African ancestry and of other populations under-represented in genome-wide association studies, whose consortia meta-analyse the cohorts' genome-wide data to find genetic variants for complex traits, such as white blood cell count, blood pressure and hypertension in African-ancestry cohorts (COGENT-BP) and kidney traits across diverse ancestries (COGENT-Kidney, established in 2014).
note: Tier D (D014), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (ADHD/ASD/intelligence GWAS) and P2 (colorectal-cancer multi-omic GWAS) abstracts do not name COGENT, and no full text or supplement is available for either, so no quotable unit ties COGENT to these two specific studies or explains its role in them. P3 (D014.1, .4): COGENT as the network of population-based African-American cohorts for a white-blood-cell-count GWAS. P4 (D014.7): the 'Continental Origins and Genetic Epidemiology Network' consortium contributing to a resting-heart-rate GWAS. P5 (D014.10): COGENT of African Americans, for a blood-pressure variant replication. Identity and definition rest on P3-P5 (papers found by name search), which consistently describe COGENT as a network of African-American cohorts for blood-cell, heart-rate and blood-pressure genetics; but neither P1 nor P2 (the row's own tagged GWAS papers, for ADHD/ASD/IQ and colorectal cancer) has any quotable unit naming COGENT or showing its role there, so the link between the tag on these 4 GCST studies and the network described in P3-P5 is not directly confirmed (example given with ev null accordingly). Candidate COHO terms YRI/HapMap/CEU (COHO:0000638/0000284/0000637) are reference panels mentioned only incidentally (D014.7: imputation using 'HapMap YRI and CEU panels'), not COGENT itself. Checked 2026-09-23: The tag COGENT names three different consortia, and neither of the row's GWAS papers means this network. GCST90134330 (PMID:35764056) re-analysed the 269,867-person intelligence meta-analysis, whose cohorts the GWAS Catalog lists as UKB, COGENT, RS, Generation_R and so on; there COGENT is the Cognitive Genomics Consortium. GCST90129505, GCST90255675 and GCST90255676 (PMID:36539618, colorectal cancer, co-tagged ACCC, CCFR, CORECT, GECCO) mean the COlorectal cancer GENeTics consortium. The draft's example GCST90129505 is therefore a different COGENT, which is why no quote could be found. The definition also misstates the network: it does not pool genotype data but meta-analyses cohort results; it is not limited to African Americans (COGENT-BP covers African-ancestry populations, and COGENT-Kidney does trans-ethnic meta-analysis in diverse populations); and its traits include kidney traits, not only haematological and cardiometabolic ones. Following the review's practice for tags with several meanings (compare TMM and EAGLE), this row stays the network that the PGS id names. It gets a paper example with no GCST: it must not be put in the GWAS subset, and the tag's four GWAS Catalog studies must not be linked to it. Two further aggregations would need their own ('b') rows, each carrying the acronym COGENT with clash notes. (1) Cognitive Genomics Consortium, for GCST90134330: 'The meta-analysis included new and previously reported GWAS summary statistics from 14 cohorts: UK Biobank (UKB), Cognitive Genomics Consortium (COGENT), Rotterdam Study (RS)' (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/bionlp/RESTful/pmcoa.cgi/BioC_xml/PMC6411041/unicode). No quote can be taken from PMID:35764056 itself, which is closed, and its abstract does not name COGENT. (2) COlorectal cancer GENeTics consortium, for GCST90129505, GCST90255675 and GCST90255676: 'The COGENT (COlorectal cancer GENeTics) consortium includes 20 research groups in Europe, Australia, the Americas, China and Japan.' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=EXT_ID%3A19920828+AND+SRC%3AMED&format=json&resultType=core). No prose sentence in PMID:36539618 names it. Countries are left empty on purpose: COGENT-Kidney recruited GWAS of African, Hispanic/Latino, European and East Asian ancestry, and the source texts name no countries.

input name: Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia
label: Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia
example title: Genetic Analyses of Enamel Hypoplasia in Multiethnic Cohorts.
example quote: Our second cohort (n = 1,837) comes from the Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia (COHRA), which was designed to address oral health disparities in the Appalachian region in the USA.
definition: The cohort studies of the Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia, established in 2000 by the University of Pittsburgh in partnership with West Virginia University to find the factors behind poor oral health in northern Appalachia. They are a family-based etiology study (COHRA1), which recruited households in West Virginia and western Pennsylvania, and a longitudinal cohort (COHRA2), which since 2011 has recruited pregnant women in Pennsylvania and West Virginia and followed them and their children.
location quote: Our second cohort (n = 1,837) comes from the Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia (COHRA), which was designed to address oral health disparities in the Appalachian region in the USA.
note: Tier D (D015), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (D015.1, .4, .6): COHRA/COHRA1 (its 'second cohort') is one of four studies pooled for an enamel-hypoplasia GWAS, household-recruited from rural Appalachia in West Virginia and western Pennsylvania. P2 (D015.13, .16): COHRA1 and COHRA2 are analysed as two separate cohorts in a dental-caries vQTL scan. P3 (D015.37-40): a supplementary results table has a plain 'COHRA' column, not distinguishing 1 vs 2. The plain tag 'COHRA' shifts across the row's 4 studies between COHRA1 alone (P1, matching its stated cohort size), COHRA1 and COHRA2 kept separate (P2), and an undifferentiated combined column (P3). COHRA1 and COHRA2 are themselves separate tier-D keys elsewhere in this review (D566, D578, both tagged to GCST90255389, not in this batch) and are deliberately left out of this term's acronyms/synonyms to avoid conflating them with it. D015.58 (P9, not a GWAS paper) describes COHRA2 specifically enrolling pregnant women in West Virginia/Pittsburgh, a different design from COHRA1's household/child recruitment (D015.6); this definition covers the umbrella project only as far as D015.1/.4/.6/.46 describe it, not COHRA2's specific design. Checked 2026-09-23: COHRA is the research centre's umbrella over two distinct cohorts, COHRA1 (families, household recruitment) and COHRA2 (pregnant women and their children, from 2011), so it is an aggregation, not a cohort. The draft's definition describes only COHRA1's design. The tag meanings were also misread. In P1 (PMID:35172313) the tag covers both cohorts, 'the Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia (COHRA1, n = 1,837; COHRA2, n = 1,195)', and not COHRA1 alone. P2 (PMID:36981009) scans COHRA1 and COHRA2 separately. In P3 (PMID:40071514) the only COHRA cohort is COHRA2 ('The first cohort was recruited as part of the COHRA2 study between 2011 and 2022.'). Model it like Tohoku Medical Megabank (COHO:0000533), with COHRA1 (review key D566) and COHRA2 (D578) as members linked by hasCohort from this term. A quote for both links: 'We conducted individual genome-wide vQTL scans on three cohorts: the Iowa Fluoride Study (IFS, n = 396), the Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia, cohort 1 (COHRA1, n = 328), and cohort 2 (COHRA2, n = 773).' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC10048401/fullTextXML). COHRA1 is also a first-wave member of GLIDE (COHO:0000947; the GLIDE row's member-list quote names 'The Center for Oral Health in Appalachia cohort 1 (COHRA1), which is part of the GENEVA caries consortium'); that link belongs on D566, not here. The GENEVA Dental Caries Study (tier E key E403) may be a further parent for D566. The draft's example and country quote describe COHRA1's subsection of P1 but name COHRA, so they stand.

input name: Diabetes Genetics Initiative of Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT, Lund University, and Novartis Institutes of BioMedical Research
label: Diabetes Genetics Initiative
other synonyms: Diabetes Genetics Initiative of Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT, Lund University, and Novartis Institutes of BioMedical Research
example title: Multi-ancestry genetic study of type 2 diabetes highlights the power of diverse populations for discovery and translation.
example quote: Diabetes Genetics Initiative (DGI) was supported by the Novartis Institute for BioMedical Research with additional support from The Richard and Susan Smith Family Foundation and American Diabetes Association Pinnacle Program Project Award.
definition: A genome-wide association study of type 2 diabetes and related quantitative traits by the Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT, Lund University and the Novartis Institutes for BioMedical Research. Its participants were patients with type 2 diabetes and matched non-diabetic controls from Finland and Sweden, genotyped and characterised for glucose metabolism, lipids, obesity and blood pressure.
location quote: The DGI Study material consisting of 2,931 individuals from Finland and Sweden (1,464 patients with type 2 diabetes and 1,467 nondiabetic control subjects) was ascertained as previously described (1,11,12).
note: Tier D (D016), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (D016.7-12, trans-ancestral glycaemic-traits GWAS supplement): DGI listed among contributing cohorts; D016.7 names DGI alongside DIAGEN/EGCUT in a funding-acknowledgement table entry, D016.10 gives 'Diabetes Genetics (DGI)' with lab-method details (European ancestry). P2 (D016.13, .16, .19-24, multi-ancestry T2D GWAS supplements): DGI listed among European-ancestry contributing GWAS (D016.13); named with Novartis Institute for BioMedical Research support (D016.16); its own ethics approvals (Helsinki University Hospital, Finland; Lund University, Sweden, D016.20) and T2D case-ascertainment criteria (D016.24) given in a supplementary table. All evidence comes from supplementary acknowledgement/methods tables of two large meta-analyses rather than a dedicated DGI design paper, but two independent supplements (P1's and P2's) agree on the name and funder. Recruitment sites and case definition are given only in P2's supplement (GCST90132184), so those specific facts are confirmed there rather than for P1's studies directly, though the same acronym and Novartis funding recur in P1's supplement too (D016.7). The PGS Catalog name adds 'of Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT, Lund University, and Novartis Institutes of BioMedical Research'; no unit shows the cohort itself called that, so only 'Diabetes Genetics Initiative' is used as label and the fuller PGS form is left out of synonyms. D016.17-18 (Botnia Study, Malmo) and D016.9/.21 (EGCUT) are other cohorts in the same funding list, not DGI, and are not used as its evidence. Checked 2026-09-23: The identity is right, but the definition was built from an ethics-approval line, a supplementary case-definition cell and a funding line. It never says that DGI is a genome-wide association study with matched controls characterised for many metabolic traits. The draft's 'run through the Helsinki University Hospital in Finland and Lund University in Sweden' comes from an ethics approval, which does not say where the study was run, and the funder is not a defining fact. The countries are right, but their only quote was the ethics approval; an open text states that the participants came from Finland and Sweden. The PGS name, which the draft dropped as unattested, is the study's own group-author name on its 2007 Science paper (Europe PMC author list of PMID:17463246), so it is a synonym. The DGI GWAS drew in part on the Botnia Study family sample (COHO:0000703; its review note says so), so neither is a sub-cohort of the other. Taking part in the DIAGRAM and MAGIC meta-analyses is not membership, which matches how the review handled FUSION, so there is no parent. P1's supplementary table writes 'Diabetes Genetics (DGI)'. The shortened form 'Diabetes Genetics' is a synonym of COHO:0000705 (DIAGEN Study, taken from the PGS name there), so it is not added here; a curator may want to review that DIAGEN synonym.

label: DIAbetes Meta-ANalysis of Trans-Ethnic association studies
other synonyms: Diabetes Meta-Analysis of Trans-Ethnic association studies|DIAbetes Meta-ANalysis Trans-Ethnic association studies|DIAMANTE Consortium
example title: Multi-ancestry genetic study of type 2 diabetes highlights the power of diverse populations for discovery and translation.
example quote: We assembled an ancestrally diverse collection of genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of type 2 diabetes (T2D) in 180,834 cases and 1,159,055 controls (48.9% non-European descent) through the DIAMANTE (DIAbetes Meta-ANalysis of Trans-Ethnic association studies) Consortium.
definition: A consortium established to assemble genome-wide association studies of type 2 diabetes across diverse ancestry groups. It meta-analyses them within its European and East Asian ancestry components and, together with African, Hispanic and South Asian ancestry studies, in a multi-ancestry meta-regression, to discover and fine-map type 2 diabetes loci.
note: Tier D (D017), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (D017.1, atherosclerosis multi-trait GWAS supplement): DIAMANTE listed among contributing cohorts alongside MVP, Biobank Japan, PMBB etc. P2 (D017.4, .10-.28, multi-ancestry T2D GWAS): DIAMANTE is the consortium itself, its own dedicated study. P3 (D017.29-.54, T2D pathophysiology-heterogeneity GWAS): the DIAMANTE Consortium as a prior, previously published component contributing to the larger T2D Global Genomics Initiative (T2DGGI) meta-analysis. Well supported by open-access full text of the consortium's own paper (P2, D017.4/.10/.13/.23-26), consistently distinguished from FinnGen (D017.20: 'Because FinnGen was not part of DIAMANTE...') and from the Million Veteran Program and T2DGGI (D017.47-54), which are separate but related efforts. Full-text units stylise the expansion with capitals spelling the acronym ('DIAbetes Meta-ANalysis of Trans-Ethnic association studies', D017.10/.13); the same paper's EuropePMC-sourced abstract instead gives plain title case (D017.4) - kept as a case-variant synonym per the capitalisation-significant rule. The PGS Catalog's own name field omits 'of'; no unit attests that exact string, so it is not used. No unit ties DIAMANTE to specific recruitment countries, only ancestry groups, so left without countries per the multinational-consortium rule. Checked 2026-09-23: The identity, label, type and example are right. The definition presents the 2022 paper's multi-ancestry meta-regression as what the consortium does. The consortium has ancestry-specific European and East Asian components, reported earlier (PMID:30297969, PMID:32499647), and the 2022 paper expands on them. The PGS Catalog name (without 'of') was left out; the review keeps PGS names as synonyms when they name the cohort, as it did for DIAGRAM. No parent. The T2D Global Genomics Initiative (tier E key E1082) re-used DIAMANTE's studies: its supplement says part of its sample contributed to earlier multi-ancestry analyses by the Million Veteran Program and the DIAMANTE Consortium. That is re-use of data, and no source calls DIAMANTE a member of it. No countries: a multinational consortium defined by ancestry groups.

input name: Discovery, Biology and Risk of Inherited Variants in Breast Cancer Consortium
label: Discovery, Biology, and Risk of Inherited Variants in Breast Cancer
other synonyms: Discovery, Biology and Risk of Inherited Variants in Breast Cancer Consortium
example title: Investigating the shared genetic architecture of uterine leiomyoma and breast cancer: A genome-wide cross-trait analysis.
example quote: This GWAS meta-analyzed data from BCAC and DRIVE (Discovery, Biology and Risk of Inherited Variants in Breast Cancer Consortium), combining 11.8 million variants in 122,977 BC-affected women (of which 69,501 were ER+ cases and 21,468 were ER–) and 105,974 female control subjects (all of European ancestry).
definition: A breast cancer genetics consortium, one of the five projects funded in 2010 under the NCI's Genetic Associations and Mechanisms in Oncology (GAME-ON) post-GWAS initiative. It meta-analysed genome-wide summary data shared by existing breast cancer GWAS and genotyped breast cancer cases and controls on the OncoArray, to replicate known and find new breast cancer susceptibility loci.
parent quote: GAME-ON is network of genetic epidemiology consortia that contains GWAS data from the Colorectal Transdisciplinary Study (CORECT); Discovery, Biology, and Risk of Inherited Variants in Breast Cancer (DRIVE); Elucidating Loci Involved in Prostate Cancer Susceptibility (ELLIPSE); Follow-up of Ovarian Cancer Genetic Association and Interaction Studies (FOCI); and Transdisciplinary Research in Cancer of the Lung (TRICL).
note: Tier D (D018), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (D018.1, uterine leiomyoma/breast cancer cross-trait GWAS): DRIVE named in full and meta-analysed together with BCAC for the source breast-cancer GWAS used. P2 (chronotype/breast cancer GWAS): abstract does not name DRIVE; only BCAC appears in the tagged-cohorts list. P3 (D018.4, breast cancer/meningioma Mendelian randomization, found by name): DRIVE named in full again, listed alongside BCAC and iCOGS as a distinct source of breast-cancer genetic instrumental variables. Only two quotable units (D018.1, D018.4), from two independent papers, but both consistently give the same full name and both clearly distinguish DRIVE from BCAC and iCOGS (COHO:0000020, COHO:0000731 in the candidate list), so it is drafted as its own aggregation rather than 'same as' either. No unit describes DRIVE's own founding, composition or recruitment beyond its subject (breast-cancer GWAS) and its co-analysis with BCAC. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft missed the parent. DRIVE is one of the five NCI GAME-ON post-GWAS projects, and GAME-ON is already COHO:0000774, whose sibling consortia CORECT, ELLIPSE and TRICL are linked to it with the same sentence. The definition only restates how one paper used DRIVE's data; the consortium's own dbGaP record and the GAME-ON paper describe what it did: a meta-analysis of summary data shared by existing breast cancer GWAS, and OncoArray genotyping. The label is the PGS form. DRIVE's own name, in dbGaP and in GAME-ON papers, is 'Discovery, Biology, and Risk of Inherited Variants in Breast Cancer', without 'Consortium'; the PGS form is kept as a synonym. The example is right; the quote is swapped for the same sentence from the cleaner PMC HTML text, without the PDF's broken characters. The GWAS that shared summary data with DRIVE's meta-analysis were ABCFS, BBCS, BPC3, BCFR, DFBBCS, GC-HBOC, HEBCS, MARIE, SardiNIA, SASBAC (COHO:0000935) and UK2 (PMC5012582 acknowledgements). This is a data-sharing list, so no hasCohort links are proposed from it. No countries: its studies come from many countries. Not the same as BCAC (COHO:0000020) or iCOGS (COHO:0000731): papers list DRIVE alongside both.

label: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition–Cardiovascular Disease Study
other synonyms: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition – Cardiovascular Disease|EPIC-CVD case-cohort study
example title: Discovery and systematic characterization of risk variants and genes for coronary artery disease in over a million participants.
example quote: EPIC-CVD is a case-cohort study nested within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC) cohort (1).
definition: A case-cohort study nested within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition, designed to investigate the determinants of cardiovascular disease. EPIC participants with incident coronary heart disease or stroke, identified from 1991 to 2010, are compared with a centre-stratified random subcohort of EPIC participants with stored blood samples, in which molecular factors, including genotypes, are measured.
location quote: The EPIC cohort consists of 366,521 women and 153,457 men, aged between 35 and 70years at baseline, recruited from the population at 23 centres across 10 European countries (Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, The Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden and the UK) between 1992 and 2000.
parent quote: EPIC-CVD is a case-cohort study nested within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC) cohort (1).
note: Tier D (D019), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: Settled: EPIC_CAD (PGS name 'EPIC CAD') is the two catalogs' tag for EPIC-CVD, the cardiovascular case-cohort study nested in EPIC. It is the same cohort in both tagged GWAS papers, so the draft's guess was right. It is not in COHO or in the review, and its natural parent is EPIC (COHO:0000065), as for EPIC-InterAct (COHO:0000587). The label follows PMC9662821 ('EPIC-CVD (European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition–Cardiovascular Disease Study) was funded by the European Research Council (268834) and the European Commission Framework Programme 7 (HEALTH-F2-2012-279233).'); the literature more often writes just 'EPIC-CVD'. It shares its random subcohort with EPIC-InterAct (COHO:0000587) but is a separate case-cohort study (CHD and stroke cases rather than diabetes cases). The 'EPIC-CVD Consortium' is among the 'Consortia providing stroke data' to MEGASTROKE (COHO:0000784); the review used that sentence for memberOf links, so a second parent link is possible. label: International FTLD-TDP Whole-Genome Sequencing Consortium

example title: Deciphering distinct genetic risk factors for FTLD-TDP pathological subtypes via whole-genome sequencing.

No duplicate in COHO or the review.

P2's reference 6 (Prokopenko 2021) cites Blacker 1997 for it, and P2's supplement repeats the Initiative's standard acknowledgement (NIMH DCTR/DESR staff, 'all three sites', SRA Technologies). In P1, NIMH is 1,656 US controls supplied by the NIMH repository, an institution tag like UCSF and MCW in the same paper. In P3, NIMH is 'NIMH Schizophrenia Controls': the controls of the GAIN schizophrenia GWAS (dbGaP phs000021) from the Molecular Genetics of Schizophrenia Collaboration (COHO:0000116). The Alzheimer's disease family study is the commonest meaning of the tag and id (P2, GERAD1 PMID:19734902 and its PRS evaluation PMID:30911569; the id's autism use, PMID:30804558, is NIMH-repository autism trios). It is also the only one with a name and design of its own, so it is the cohort to mint. The draft also missed COHO:0000094 as its parent. The tag is ambiguous, so the new term needs an editor note saying that the GWAS Catalog also uses NIMH for other NIMH-repository samples: control sets in GCST90013445/6 (PMID:34127860) and GCST90824163 (PMID:42062540). Those studies must not be used as this term's example. If the curator wants P3's use resolvable, it belongs with MGS (COHO:0000116). P1's use has no name (treat like UCSF and MCW, not a cohort). The label follows the Initiative's usual name. Its acknowledgements use 'National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) Alzheimer Disease Genetic Initiative', and the families are usually called the 'NIMH Genetics Initiative AD Study Sample' (437 multiplex families in later analyses; no sizes in the definition). The Initiative's families were later whole-genome sequenced (PMID:33797837). No COHO term covers this sample. COHO:0000094's evidence names no member cohorts, so this would be its first hasCohort link.

input name: North Shore University Health systems Genomic Health Initiative
label: Genomic Health Initiative
other synonyms: Genomic Health Initiative at NorthShore University HealthSystem|Genomic Health Initiative of Endeavor Health|North Shore University Health systems Genomic Health Initiative
example title: Cross-definition GWAS of IBS in 2.8 million individuals reveals cardiometabolic and triglyceride-linked mechanisms.
example quote: The Genomic Health Initiative (GHI) is a community-based healthcare biobank established at Endeavor Health (Evanston, Illinois, USA), designed to integrate genomic data with comprehensive EHR.
definition: A healthcare-system-based research biobank of NorthShore University HealthSystem (now Endeavor Health) in Illinois, United States, started in 2014, which enrols patients of the health system who consent to give a blood sample for DNA and to linkage of their electronic health records, for translational and discovery research combining genomic and clinical data.
location quote: The GHI is a US health care-based biobank at Endeavor Health in Illinois.
note: Tier D (D046), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred, which was right on its evidence (P1's abstract only). The research settles it. NSGHI is the Genomic Health Initiative (GHI), the research biobank of NorthShore University HealthSystem in Evanston, Illinois (now part of Endeavor Health). It started in 2014 and links patients' DNA to their electronic health records. It is one defined, named cohort, not the institution: P1's online supplemental methods describe it as a biobank, and the paper that coined the acronym writes 'NorthShore University HealthSystem's Genomic Health Initiative (NSGHI: 384 controls)'. The PGS Catalog name ('North Shore University Health systems ...') is a garbled rendering of that phrase, kept as a synonym. The label is the programme's own name. Other programmes use similar names, for example the Alabama Genomic Health Initiative (AGHI), which is a different programme. If the curator prefers a label naming the host, 'Genomic Health Initiative at NorthShore University HealthSystem' is attested. PMC10713750 says enrolment and DNA collection ran 'since 2014', matching the 2014 start. Duplicates: nothing in COHO. Tier-E row E824 'NSUHS' (North Shore University Health System) is the host institution's name as the PGS Catalog records it for BCAC/CIMBA breast-cancer and prostate-cancer PRS papers. Whether that sample comes from GHI was not checked, so settle it when E824 is reviewed. GHI contributes to Global Biobank Meta-analysis Initiative projects (tier-D row D226), but no source read says it is a GBMI member, so the parent is left null.

input name: MRC National Survey of Health and Development
label: MRC National Survey of Health and Development
other synonyms: 1946 National Birth Cohort|National Survey of Health and Development
example title: Genome-wide association meta-analysis of age at onset of walking in over 70,000 infants of European ancestry.
example quote: We conducted a GWAS meta-analysis of AOW in 70,560 children including data from four European-ancestry cohorts: the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study20,21 (MoBa, N = 58,302), the Netherlands Twin Register22 (NTR, N = 6,251), the Lifelines multigenerational prospective population-based birth cohort study23 from the North of the Netherlands (N = 3,415) and the United Kingdom Medical Research Council National Study for Health and Development24 (NSHD, N = 2,592).
definition: A birth cohort of people born in one week in March 1946 in England, Scotland and Wales, selected as a social-class-stratified sample of the singleton births to married mothers that week and followed up repeatedly from birth into old age through home visits, questionnaires and clinic assessments. The oldest of the British national birth cohort studies, it is core-funded by the UK Medical Research Council and has been developed since 2008 by the MRC Unit for Lifelong Health and Ageing at UCL into an interdisciplinary study of ageing.
location quote: NSHD is a population-based prospective birth cohort study whose participants were infants from single births born in England, Scotland and Wales during 1 week in March 1946 (N = 5,362) to women with husbands24.
note: Tier D (D047), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: NSHD, one of several UK cohorts in a glycemic-traits GWAS; P2: NSHD, one of four cohorts (with MoBa, NTR, Lifelines) meta-analysed for age at onset of walking. Some of the same paper's own text renders the name as "National Study of/for Health and Development" rather than "Survey" (D047.26, D047.34); not added as a synonym since it looks like inconsistent phrasing rather than a deliberate alternate name. "England, Wales and Scotland" mapped to gazetteer United_Kingdom (no separate constituent-country entries). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country and example are right. The definition leaves out the sampling design and adds a claim the sources do not make. It was not all births of that week but a social-class-stratified sample of the singleton births within marriage (PMC3637651). 'Established by the Medical Research Council as the National Survey of Health and Development' is not supported: the cohort's papers say the MRC provides core funding and that its Unit for Lifelong Health and Ageing (set up in 2008) develops the study. The definition also rested on one GWAS paper's summary, not on the cohort's own profile papers, and did not say that the cohort has been followed from birth into old age. The draft missed the name 'National Survey of Health and Development' (without 'MRC'), which the cohort's own papers use, and the acronym 'MRC NSHD'. No COHO term covers the NSHD. NSHDS (COHO:0000927, Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study) is a different cohort with a different acronym, so there is no clash. Insight 46 (PMID:41107421) is a neuroimaging sub-study of the NSHD, if a sub-cohort is ever wanted. The draft's example sentence is fine. P2's own description ('NSHD is a population-based prospective birth cohort study whose participants were infants from single births ...') would make an equally good example.

label: Oxford Down Syndrome Cohort Study
other synonyms: Oxford DS Cohort Study
example title: Genome-wide association study of somatic GATA1s mutations in newborns with Down syndrome.
example quote: To address the question of why only a subset of DS newborns develop transient leukemia, we performed a comprehensive genetic epidemiology study of GATA1s mutations via whole-genome sequencing (WGS) plus targeted GATA1 sequencing of 434 children with DS in the Oxford Down Syndrome Cohort Study (ODSCS).
definition: A prospective cohort of newborns with Down syndrome enrolled at birth in 18 hospitals in the United Kingdom from 2006 to 2017, screened for GATA1 mutations and followed with serial clinical and haematological data from birth to 4 years of age, to study transient abnormal myelopoiesis, preleukaemic GATA1 mutations and the risk of myeloid leukaemia in children with Down syndrome.
location quote: The study comprised 434 newborns with DS from the ODSCS, a prospective cohort that enrolled children with DS between 2006 to 2017 from 18 hospitals in the United Kingdom.
note: Tier D (D048), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ODSCS, the Oxford Down Syndrome Cohort Study, the study population for a GWAS of somatic GATA1 mutations in Down syndrome newborns. Definition rests on the GWAS paper's own description (no separate cohort-profile paper in the evidence). A related but distinct earlier pilot, the "Oxford Imperial DS Cohort Study" (partly overlapping participants, D048.6), is not treated as a synonym. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, country and example are right. The definition is close but vague about what the cohort is. Participants were newborns, enrolled at birth in 18 UK hospitals and screened for GATA1 mutations with haematological follow-up. The cohort's purpose covers myeloid leukaemia of Down syndrome, not only transient leukaemia. 'Used to study' also describes a use, not the design. The draft missed the short form 'Oxford DS Cohort Study' that P1's abstract uses. Two points for the curator. (1) Enrolment end: P1 says 2006-2017, but PMID:40407036 says 'between 2006 and 2012', citing a 2017 ASH abstract. The pilot, the Oxford-Imperial Down Syndrome Cohort Study (OIDSCS), enrolled neonates at the same 18 UK hospitals from October 2006 to March 2012. The 2017 end date is kept because P1 comes from the ODSCS investigators and the larger ODSCS numbers need the longer period. (2) The OIDSCS looks like the first recruitment phase of the ODSCS: same hospitals, same start, and P1 says 172 ODSCS newborns were in it. P1 still calls it a 'related pilot study', so it is not added as a synonym, as the draft decided. A 2025 Blood paper by the same group (PMID:40561204, 'prospective study of newborns with DS ... follow-up for the window of ML-DS risk') is probably the ODSCS's main report. Its abstract does not name the cohort and the full text is closed, so it was not used. No COHO term or other review row covers either study.

input name: Pharmacogenetics of Opioid Substitution Treatment Response
label: Pharmacogenetics of Opioid Substitution Treatment Response
example title: A genome-wide association, polygenic risk score and sex study on opioid use disorder treatment outcomes.
example quote: Data were collected as part of the GENetics of Opioid Addiction (GENOA) and Pharmacogenetics of Opioid Substitution Treatment Response (POST) programs.
definition: A prospective cohort of patients aged 16 or older receiving methadone or buprenorphine–naloxone treatment for opioid use disorder at outpatient clinics of the Canadian Addiction Treatment Centres across Ontario, Canada, recruited by McMaster University researchers from May 2018 to January 2023 as an extension of the Genetics of Opioid Addiction study with a similar protocol. Participants were interviewed at entry, gave a saliva sample for DNA and were followed for up to 12 months through their medical records and urine drug screens, to study biopsychosocial and genetic factors in treatment outcomes.
location quote: Briefly, participants (nGENOA = 1536, nPOST = 3319) were recruited from 76 CATC sites across Ontario, Canada (GENOA, 2013–2016, POST, 2018–present).
note: Tier D (D049), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: POST, the Pharmacogenetics of Opioid Substitution Treatment Response cohort, alongside its companion GENOA cohort, in a GWAS/PRS study of OUD treatment outcomes. GENOA (candidate COHO terms COHO:0000434/0000466/0000467) is POST's companion program, sharing sites and design, but is a distinct, separately recruited cohort (GENOA 2013-2016, blood DNA; POST 2018-present, saliva DNA); not treated as a synonym or parent here. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, country and the decision not to link GENOA are right. The example quote came from PMID:42135448, not from the paper of GCST90454192 (PMID:38102185). It is replaced with P1's own sentence naming POST. The definition is right as far as it goes, but it gives only the start year and leaves out the eligibility (aged 16 or older, on methadone or buprenorphine–naloxone) and the recruitment period (May 2018 to January 2023). It also omits the 12-month follow-up through medical records and urine drug screens, and that POST was set up in 2018 as an extension of the Canadian GENOA study with a similar protocol. POST is a separately recruited cohort (new participants; duplicates of GENOA participants were dropped when the two were merged). It is not a sub-cohort of the Canadian Genetics of Opioid Addiction Study (COHO:0000467), so no parent. The curator may still want a note linking the two. The US Genetics of Opioid Addiction Consortium (COHO:0000466) is unrelated. Papers give different numbers of sites (31, 45 or 54 for POST, 76 for GENOA and POST together), so the definition gives no count.

input name: Prostate Cancer Association Group to Investigate Cancer-Associated Alterations
label: Prostate Cancer Association Group to Investigate Cancer-Associated Alterations in the Genome
note: Tier D (D050), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: PRACTICAL, prostate-cancer summary statistics used with BCAC and FinnGen in a pan-cancer meta-analysis; P2: PRACTICAL prostate-cancer data in a multiple-myeloma predisposition GWAS; P3: PRACTICAL tagged on a sub-Saharan-Africa prostate-cancer GWAS but not separately described. Matches the existing aggregation: same acronym (PRACTICAL) and same full name apart from a hyphen (evidence spells "Cancer Associated", COHO:0000611 uses "Cancer-Associated"). No new acronym, PGS id or synonym to add; already flagged in the batch as matching the earlier review's row 287. Checked 2026-09-23: None. The tag is the PRACTICAL consortium, COHO:0000611, an aggregation that already carries the acronym PRACTICAL and the PGS Catalog's truncated name ('Prostate Cancer Association Group to Investigate Cancer-Associated Alterations'), and the unhyphenated 'Cancer Associated' form as synonyms. Nothing needs adding. COHO:0000611 already has a GWAS Catalog example, so none of these GCSTs needs adding. In PMID:39103364 only PRACTICAL's controls were used; the consortium is still the right term.

label: PROCAM-2 Study
example title: A meta-analysis of genome-wide studies of resilience in the German population.
example quote: Briefly, this study included participants with available genotype data and the relevant phenotypic information from the BiDirect Study (N = 1453) [7], the FOR2107 consortium (N = 1789) [8], the PROCAM-2 Study (N = 3879) [9, 10], both SHIP cohorts (SHIP-START/-LEGEND, N = 2230; SHIP-TREND, N = 2330) [11, 12], and the LIFE-Adult-Study (N = 4141) [13, 14].
definition: An occupational cohort of employees of regional companies and government authorities in and around Münster, Germany, who volunteered and underwent a cardiovascular examination in 2000–2007, forming the second part of the Prospective Cardiovascular Münster (PROCAM) Study of cardiovascular risk factors and disease, initiated and conducted by the Leibniz Institute for Arteriosclerosis Research at the University of Münster. Follow-up lapsed until 2018, when the cohort was revived for genotyping, followed by a postal follow-up questionnaire in 2021.
location quote: The independent studies recruited participants of European descent from the population living in and around the cities of Münster, Marburg, Greifswald and Leipzig, Germany.
note: Tier D (D051), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: PROCAM-2, one of five German cohorts (with BiDirect, FOR2107, both SHIP waves, LIFE-Adult) in a resilience GWAS meta-analysis; P2: PROCAM-2, one of several German control biobanks in an aortic-stenosis GWAS. The row's tag is "PROCAM" but every GWAS paper's own text names the cohort actually used as "PROCAM-2", the study's second, genotyped phase (D051.31). The original first-phase Prospective Cardiovascular Münster (PROCAM) Study that D051.29 describes as the whole programme has no COHO term or tier-D row in this batch, so no parent is asserted - a researcher should consider minting a base PROCAM term and linking PROCAM-2 to it with isSubCohortOf, on the SHIP/SHIP-START/SHIP-TREND pattern. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronyms, country and example are right. The tag PROCAM denotes PROCAM-2 in both GWAS papers. PROCAM-2 is a separately recruited second sample of employees (2000-2007) and the only genotyped part, so the draft rightly mints PROCAM-2 rather than the whole study. The definition omits what the cohort is for and its baseline examination: PROCAM is a study of cardiovascular risk factors and disease in an occupational cohort, and every PROCAM-2 participant had a cardiovascular examination at baseline. As the draft says, the original Prospective Cardiovascular Münster (PROCAM) Study has no COHO term. Its earlier sample was 'men and women at work in northern Germany' (PMID:12540731) and is the basis of the PROCAM risk score (PMID:11804985). If it is minted, PROCAM-2 should be isSubCohortOf it, and both terms would carry the acronym PROCAM with editor notes. The PGS Catalog name 'The Prospective Cardiovascular Münster Study' names that whole study, so it is rightly not a synonym of PROCAM-2. Europe PMC also finds PROCAM-2 in PMID:38839884 (restless legs) and PMID:39504041 (aortic stenosis versus CAD), as a German population/control sample.

label: PsyCourse Study
other synonyms: PsyCourse study
example title: A genome-wide association study of the longitudinal course of executive functions.
example quote: In the transdiagnostic PsyCourse Study, comprising patients of the affective-to-psychotic spectrum and controls, we investigated the genetic basis of the time course of two core executive subfunctions: set-shifting (Trail Making Test, part B (TMT-B)) and updating (Verbal Digit Span backwards) in 1338 genotyped individuals.
definition: A multicentre, naturalistic longitudinal study of adults with schizophrenia-spectrum, bipolar or recurrent depressive disorders and of healthy controls, recruited at clinical centres in Germany and Austria from 2011 to 2019 and assessed four times at six-month intervals over 18 months with deep phenotyping, dimensional ratings of psychopathology, cognitive tests and blood sampling, to identify clinical, neurobiological and genetic signatures of the course of major psychiatric disorders across the affective-to-psychotic continuum.
location quote: We included 1338 genotyped individuals (dataset version 3.0) recruited in different centers in Germany and Austria, comprising patients from the affective-to-psychotic spectrum (377 bipolar I disorder, 100 bipolar II disorder, 420 schizophrenia, 95 schizoaffective disorder, 6 brief psychotic disorder, 9 schizophreniform disorder, and 73 with recurrent depression) and 258 psychiatrically healthy controls.
note: Tier D (D052), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the whole PsyCourse Study, discovery sample for a GWAS of the longitudinal course of executive function. Design and identity are corroborated by both the GWAS paper (P1) and its own design/profile paper found by name (P2, PMID:30070057), consistently. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, countries and example are right. The definition is accurate but gives no dates or schedule. The study ran from 2011 to 2019, and participants were assessed four times at six-month intervals over 18 months. It also does not say which disorders were included: schizophrenia-spectrum, bipolar and recurrent depressive disorders. The draft missed the lower-case form 'PsyCourse study' that the design paper's title uses (capitalisation variants are kept). No COHO term or other review row covers PsyCourse. The FOR2107 cohort (tier-D row D421) was P1's replication sample. It is a separate study and not a parent. PsyCourse was funded within the DFG clinical research group KFO241 (P1 acknowledgements), but KFO241 is a funding framework, not a cohort.

Tier D (D053), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred; research settles it as not a cohort. The tag is an institution label for whichever QIMR Berghofer samples a paper used, as the earlier review found for the tag QIMR. In the only GWAS paper (P1, a meta-analysis of published SUD summary statistics), 'QIMR' is glossed 'QIMR Berghofer cohorts'. It is the QIMR component of Zhou et al. 2023's problematic-alcohol-use GWAS (PMID:38062264), which names three separate cohorts: the Australian Genetics of Depression Study, the Australian twin family study of alcohol use disorder (including the Australian Alcohol and Nicotine Studies) and the Australian Genetics of Bipolar Disorder Study. The PGS id comes from the GIANT BMI paper (PMID:40691366). Its supplement lists 'QIMR Berghofer Genetic Epidemiology Cohort (QIMR)', a GIANT label for the Genetic Epidemiology group's samples with no design paper or membership. The two uses cover different sets of people, and no source defines a single sample or umbrella under this name. The P1 samples already have COHO terms or review rows: Australian Genetics of Depression Study (COHO:0000672), Australian Alcohol and Nicotine Studies (COHO:0000841; see also tier-D row D152 OZALC), and the Australian Genetics of Bipolar Disorder Study (tier-E row E375 GBP). Tier-E row E076 AUSTWIN ('Australian Twin-Family Studies') may be the PGS Catalog's name for the QIMR twin-family samples that GIANT means (not checked). If the curator prefers a term, it would be an aggregation named after the institute, as the earlier review noted for QIMR, but no source defines its membership.

input name: Queensland study of Melanoma: Environment and Genetic Associations
label: Queensland Study of Melanoma: Environmental and Genetic Associations
other synonyms: Queensland study of Melanoma: Environment and Genetic Associations|Queensland study of Melanoma: Environmental and Genetic Associations|Queensland Study of Melanoma: environmental and genetic associations|Queensland study of Melanoma: Environmental and Genetics Associations
example title: Exploring the Germline Genetics of In Situ and Invasive Cutaneous Melanoma: A Genome-Wide Association Study Meta-Analysis.
example quote: Three genome-wide association study meta-analyses were conducted of in situ melanoma vs controls, invasive melanoma vs controls, and in situ vs invasive melanoma (case-case) using 4 population-based genetic cohorts: the UK Biobank, the FinnGen cohort, the QSkin Sun and Health Study, and the Queensland Study of Melanoma: Environmental and Genetic Associations (Q-MEGA).
definition: A population-based study of cutaneous melanoma in Queensland, Australia, that brings together four earlier population-based studies of melanoma patients conducted in 1987–1995: the Queensland Familial Melanoma Project of adult cases and their families, including twins, and studies of melanoma in children, in adolescents and in men over 50. Their participants and some relatives were re-contacted in 2002–2005 for telephone interviews on sun exposure and phenotype and for blood samples, to investigate genetic and environmental factors, and their interaction, in the aetiology of melanoma.
location quote: Q-MEGA brings together four population-based studies of CMM that were conducted in Queensland, Australia between 1987 and 1995 (Figure 1).
note: Tier D (D054), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: Q-MEGA tagged on an autoimmune-melanoma GWAS but not further described (abstract does not name it); P2: Q-MEGA, one of four population-based genetic cohorts (with UK Biobank, FinnGen, QSkin) meta-analysed for in-situ vs invasive melanoma. Definition rests on a single paper (no independent profile paper in the evidence). Singletons from the Brisbane Adolescent Twin Study (D054.13) match existing COHO:0000744 "Brisbane Longitudinal Twin Study"; this is a contributing-sample relationship, not sub-cohort/membership, so no parent is asserted. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym and example are right. The definition describes P2's analysis set, not Q-MEGA. Case ascertainment through registry codes, Digestive Health Study participants and singletons of the Brisbane Adolescent Twin Study are how that GWAS assembled its cases and controls. Q-MEGA's design paper (PMID:18361720), which the draft did not have, describes a follow-up study that 'brings together four population-based studies' of melanoma patients conducted in Queensland in 1987-1995. Those are the Queensland Familial Melanoma Project (adult cases and their families, including twins), the Queensland Study of Childhood Melanoma, the Study of Melanoma in Adolescents and the Study of Men Over 50. Their participants were re-contacted in 2002-2005 by telephone interview, with blood collection. An umbrella over distinct named studies is an aggregation, like STRRIDE and THRV in the pilot, so the type changes. The country can be quoted instead of taken from the name. The draft also missed spelling and capitalisation variants of the name used in the design paper. Tier-E row E944 'QFMP' (Queensland Familial Melanoma Project) is one of Q-MEGA's four member studies. If it is minted, link it here with hasCohort, using the design paper's figure legend, which lists the four studies. The other three studies have no COHO terms or review rows. BATS (COHO:0000744) and the Digestive Health Study contributed controls to one GWAS; they are not members. Tier-E row E947 'QLD' is a Queensland prostate cancer study in PRACTICAL, unrelated. If the curator prefers to keep Q-MEGA as a cohort, because the 2002-2005 follow-up was one data collection under one protocol, the rest of this record still holds.

input name: Royal Brompton & Harefield Hospitals NHS Trust Cardiovascular Research Biobank
label: Royal Brompton & Harefield Cardiovascular Research Centre Biobank
other synonyms: Royal Brompton & Harefield Hospitals NHS Trust Cardiovascular Research Biobank|Cardiovascular Research Centre Biobank, Royal Brompton & Harefield NHS Foundation Trust|Royal Brompton & Harefield Hospital Cardiovascular Research Centre Biobank|Royal Brompton and Harefield Hospital Cardiovascular Research Centre Biobank|Royal Brompton Hospital Cardiovascular Research Centre Biobank
example title: Large-scale genome-wide association analyses identify novel genetic loci and mechanisms in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
example quote: Unrelated British HCM cases from the Royal Brompton & Harefield Hospitals NHS Trust Cardiovascular Research Biobank, and healthy controls from the UK Digital Heart Project15 were included.
definition: A research biobank of the Royal Brompton and Harefield hospitals in London, United Kingdom, which since 2009 has collected blood and other samples, including cardiac tissue, with clinical, imaging and follow-up data from adult and paediatric patients attending the hospitals for the investigation or treatment of cardiovascular conditions, and from their relatives, to find genes and biomarkers for the diagnosis and prognosis of cardiovascular disease.
location quote: Human tissue samples were provided by the Cardiovascular Research Centre Biobank at the Royal Brompton and Harefield NHS Foundation Trust, UK (NRES ethics number for biobank samples: 09/H0504/104 + 5; Biobank approval number: NP001-06-2015 and MED_CT_17_079).
note: Tier D (D055), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the Royal Brompton & Harefield Hospitals NHS Trust Cardiovascular Research Biobank, source of the paper's British HCM cases. Only prose evidence is D055.1, duplicated verbatim as D055.4 from a second copy of the same supplement; no dedicated profile paper. D055.7 ('Royal Brompton Hospital (RBH)') is a thin fragment from a site-list spreadsheet and not used, so 'RBH' alone is not added as an acronym. The candidate COHO:0000456 Nurses' Health Study match is a coincidental NHS-substring hit, unrelated. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity is right: RBH-CRB is the Royal Brompton & Harefield hospitals' Cardiovascular Research Centre (CRC) Biobank, source of the 'Royal Brompton HCM cohort' cases in the HCM GWAS. But the drafted label is the PGS Catalog/2025-supplement wording ('...Hospitals NHS Trust Cardiovascular Research Biobank'); the biobank's own name, in its HRA research summary and in its own team's papers, is the Cardiovascular Research Centre Biobank of Royal Brompton & Harefield (HRA page title 'Royal Brompton & Harefield Cardiovascular Research Centre Biobank'; 'RBHH CRC Biobank'). The PGS name is kept as a synonym. The definition described only how one GWAS used the biobank (British HCM cases); the biobank itself prospectively enrols adult and paediatric patients with cardiovascular conditions (and relatives) at the two hospitals, since 2009, storing blood, serum, plasma and cardiac tissue with clinical, imaging and questionnaire follow-up data, for gene and biomarker research. The United Kingdom is right, but the drafted quote only says the cases were British; replaced by a sentence placing the biobank in the UK. The biobank's ethics approvals are REC 09/H0504/104+5 and 19/SC/0257 (South Central - Hampshire B); the HRA summary says over 6000 patients and family members have joined. 'RBH' alone is the GWAS stratum/hospital abbreviation (Royal Brompton Hospital) and is left out as an acronym; 'RBH Biobank' (PMID:39966645) and 'RBHH CRC Biobank' (PMID:35086919) are kept. The trust is now the Royal Brompton and Harefield Clinical Group of Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust. No duplicate in COHO or this review (the Nurses' Health Study hit was an 'NHS' substring). The UK Digital Heart Project (D064) supplied the controls of the same GWAS stratum but is a separate healthy-volunteer cohort.

input name: Genome-Wide Association Study of Breast Cancer in the African Diaspora
label: Genome-Wide Association Study of Breast Cancer in the African Diaspora
other synonyms: ROOT consortium|The Root consortium|GWAS of Breast Cancer in the African Diaspora|GWAS in Breast Cancer in the African Diaspora|The GWAS of Breast Cancer in the African Diaspora consortium
example title: Polygenic risk scores for prediction of breast cancer risk in women of African ancestry: a cross-ancestry approach.
example quote: We used data in women of AA from four breast cancer GWAS consortia and the Ghana Breast Health Study (GBHS); the four consortia were: ROOT (The GWAS of Breast Cancer in the African Diaspora consortium), the African American Breast Cancer Epidemiology and Risk (AMBER) consortium, Breast Cancer Association Consortium (BCAC) and African American Breast Cancer consortium (AABC) (see Supplementary Material, Table S1).
definition: A consortium for a genome-wide association study of breast cancer in women of African ancestry in Nigeria, Barbados and the United States, pooling the cases and controls of six epidemiological studies (the Nigerian Breast Cancer Study, the Barbados National Cancer Study, the Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study, the Chicago Cancer Prone Study, the Baltimore Breast Cancer Study and the Southern Community Cohort Study), genotyped together on the Illumina HumanOmni2.5 array.
location quote: We used data from the genome-wide association study (GWAS) of breast cancer in the African diaspora (The Root consortium), which included 3686 participants of African ancestry from Nigeria, USA, and Barbados.
note: Tier D (D056), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Candidate hasCohort members, the E2C2 GWAS stage-1 studies named in PMID:24096698 ('Seven participating studies, including four cohort [California Teacher’s Study (CTS), Nurses’ Health Study (NHS), Multiethnic Cohort (MEC), Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial (PLCO)] and three case–control studies [Connecticut Endometrial Cancer (CONN), Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center (FHCRC), Polish Endometrial Cancer Study (PECS)], were genotyped in Stage 1 (2,695 cases, 2,777 controls).', PMC3898362 fullTextXML), are NHS COHO:0000456, MEC COHO:0000121, PLCO COHO:0000485, and tier-E rows CECS (E178, Connecticut Endometrial Cancer Study) and PECS (E886, Polish Endometrial Cancer Study). The sentence itself does not name E2C2; the one before it does ('studies that are part of the Epidemiology of Endometrial Cancer Consortium'). Replication studies included CPS-II (COHO:0000024), AHS (Alberta, Canada), EDGE, Turin and WISE. ECAC (tier-D D405, Endometrial Cancer Association Consortium) is a separate consortium, not E2C2's parent. For countries: NCI's page counts 25 member studies in North America; United_States is asserted from O'Mara's sentence, and North America is not mapped to Northern_America. location quote: This work was based on two French GWAS on VT, the Early-Onset Venous Thrombosis (EOVT) and the Marseille Thrombosis Association (MARTHA) studies.
parent quote: Because 865 MARTHA/EOVT participants examined in the current study also took part in the INVENT study, we were able to calculate the Spearman correlation between the true rs121918472 genotype as provided by Illumina Exome array results, and the imputed dose-derived from GWAS arrays.

Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred, correctly given its evidence: P1's abstract and main text never name EOVT, and the name-search papers are about the disease. Research settles it. EOVT is the Early-Onset Venous Thrombosis study, a French case-control GWAS sample from the Trégouët/Morange group, the partner of MARTHA (COHO:0000113). Its cases had idiopathic DVT or PE before age 50, came from four French centres, and were selected like MARTHA's patients; its controls came from SU.VI.MAX. Its participants took part in the INVENT consortium's GWAS (COHO:0000829; PMC5379621), whose 2015 discovery stage included two French case-control studies (PMC4385184; names only in its Table S1). Parent: the quote shows EOVT participants took part in INVENT's GWAS rather than stating formal membership; COHO:0000829 has no hasCohort links yet. Case numbers vary between papers (411, 419, 339 cases), so none are in the definition. SU.VI.MAX (tier-E E1070) supplied only the controls, so it is not EOVT's parent. The lower-case heading 'The early onset venous thrombosis (EOVT) study' (PMC8263618) is not added, as it reads as the disease name. Not the same study as MARTHA, EDITH (COHO:0000822) or FARIVE (D414).

P1: FHRisk (FHRISK), a breast-cancer family-history-clinic cohort recruited in Manchester from 2010, distinct from but co-funded with PROCAS (D114.4, D114.7). PGS Catalog's row name 'Family History Clinic in Manchester' is the recruiting institution, not the study's own name; the GWAS paper's own supplement (D114.2) calls it 'The FHRisk study'. The study's own name is the Family History Risk Study (FH-Risk), UKCRN-ID 8611, one of the two cohorts of the NIHR programme grant PGfAR 0707-10031 with PROCAS. The definition described the GWAS sample ('oversampling of previous breast cancers') and left out the ages and the purpose. example quote: GoKinD The Genetics of Kidneys in Diabetes (GoKinD) Study was conducted by the GoKinD Investigators and supported by the Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation, the CDC, and the Special Statutory Funding Program for Type 1 Diabetes Research administered by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK).

Participants aged 18–59 with type 1 diabetes diagnosed before age 31 were enrolled as cases with diabetic nephropathy (persistent proteinuria or end-stage renal disease) or as controls with normoalbuminuria after at least 15 years of diabetes, with both parents enrolled where possible to form family trios.

note: Tier D (D120), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting.
