definition: A hospital-based series of patients with ischaemic stroke admitted to the stroke unit of the Department of Neurology of the Medical University of Graz, Austria, investigated with brain imaging and a standardised diagnostic protocol and subtyped by stroke neurologists, whose cases are compared in genetic studies of ischaemic stroke with participants of the Austrian Stroke Prevention Study from the same catchment area as controls.
location quote: Of those sites, 7 are European centers (BASICMAR—Spain, BRAINS—United Kingdom, GRAZ—Austria, KRAKOW—Poland, LEUVEN—Belgium, LUND STROKE REGISTER—Sweden, and SAHLSIS—Sweden) and 5 are based in the United States (GASROS, GCNKSS, GEOS, ISGS, and MIAMISR).
parent quote: These include previously genotyped control groups from Sweden, Spain, the UK, and Austria to be paired with the cases to be genotyped from the two GRCs from Sweden (LUND and SAHLSIS), and from the GRCs from Spain (BASICMAR), the UK (BRAINS), and Austria (GRAZ).
note: Tier D (D121), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft makes GRAZ the Austrian Stroke Prevention Study (COHO:0000857), reading the funding line 'GRAZ: The Austrian Stroke Prevention Study was supported by...'. But P1 is a case-only GWAS of age at ischaemic stroke onset in SiGN cases, and SiGN's GRAZ genetic research centre is a hospital-based stroke case series in Graz (listed as 'Hospital-based 1992–2011' in the SiGN design paper): the Graz Stroke Study, patients admitted to the stroke unit of the Medical University of Graz Department of Neurology. ASPS, a population study of stroke-free older people, only supplied the controls that SiGN and METASTROKE paired with these cases. So the tag denotes a cohort not yet in COHO, and ASPS should not get the GRAZ acronym. The draft also missed that GRAZ is a SiGN centre (COHO:0000651). Recruitment years differ by phase (2002–2007 in METASTROKE's description, 1992–2011 in SiGN's), so none is in the definition. In SiGN and MEGASTROKE the GRAZ case-control set used ASPS participants (COHO:0000857) as controls, so PGS scores built on MEGASTROKE include ASPS controls under this tag, while the tagged GWAS Catalog studies (case-only) do not; the curator may add an editor note to that effect. METASTROKE (COHO:0000688) also used this case series as its replication cohort 'Graz'. The Austrian Stroke Prevention Family Study (COHO:0000858) is unrelated to this tag.

label: Head and Neck 5000
other synonyms: Head and neck 5000|Head and Neck 5000 study
example title: Germline determinants of humoral immune response to HPV-16 protect against oropharyngeal cancer.
example quote: This publication presents data from the Head and Neck 5000 study.
definition: A prospective clinical cohort of people newly diagnosed with head and neck cancer, recruited before treatment at NHS centres across the United Kingdom and coordinated from Bristol, with health, lifestyle, quality-of-life and sexual-history questionnaires, clinical data, blood, saliva and tumour tissue samples and follow-up, set up to evaluate the centralisation of head and neck cancer care and as a biomedical resource for translational and prognostic research.
location quote: Head and Neck 5000 is an observational study that recruited people with head and neck cancer from across the United Kingdom.
note: Tier D (D122), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Parent left for later: memberOf review name E547 (International Head and Neck Cancer Epidemiology Consortium), not minted in this run; quote: "The pooled cohort of the INHANCE Consortium studies comprised 10 042 participants with head and neck cancer from 10 INHANCE case-control studies conducted in North America (Seattle, Washington, USA; Los Angeles, California, USA; HOTSPOT, CHANCE/North Carolina, USA), South America (Sao Paulo 1, Sao Paulo 2, Latin America), and Europe (Central Europe, Western Europe, Head and Neck 5000 [HN5000])." (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC10777670/fullTextXML). P1: HN5000, a UK head-and-neck-cancer study listed alongside CHANCE, ARCAGE and others in a contributing-studies table (D122.1, D122.2); P2-P4: unrelated papers matched only via the PGS Catalog's generic descriptive name 'United Kingdom case-series', not about this cohort. PGS Catalog name 'United Kingdom case-series' is a generic description, not a real name, so left out of synonyms. The only identifying evidence is one garbled supplementary-table line (D122.1); the 'hospital-based case-control' design wording sits just before the cohort's name in that line but column alignment is not fully certain. PMID:24519853, cited next to the name in D122.1, is a plausible lead to the cohort's own profile paper for a researcher to check. No existing COHO term found (checked coho_names.tsv, triage_D/E.tsv). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity is right, but the definition rests on a misread table line. In P1's Supplementary Table 1 (columns Study, Location, PI, Design, PMID, controls, OPC, OCC) 'Hospital-based case-control 24519853' belongs to the Toronto study; HN5000's own row reads 'Head and neck 5000 (HN5000) | UK | A. Ness | Multicenter clinical cohort | 25519023' with no controls. HN5000 is a prospective clinical cohort of newly diagnosed head and neck cancer patients across the UK, described in its protocol paper (PMID:25519023), not a hospital-based case-control study. The study calls itself 'Head and Neck 5000' (capital N); P1's 'Head and neck 5000' becomes a synonym. The garbled table line used as country and example quote is replaced by prose sentences (country: the protocol paper; example: P1's acknowledgement). Missed parent: HN5000 is one of the INHANCE consortium's studies (tier-E row E547). The PGS Catalog name 'United Kingdom case-series' (HN5000 in scores PGS000081, PGS000792 and PGS012586–8, from the OncoArray GWAS PMID:27749845) is a description and stays out. The parent link needs E547 (INHANCE) minted as an aggregation; the same sentence also names the IARC Central Europe study (D123) and CHANCE (COHO:0000030). Recruitment dates are not stated in the protocol paper, which was written during recruitment.

input name: International Agency for Research on Cancer Central Europe Study
label: International Agency for Research on Cancer Central Europe Study
other synonyms: IARC Central Europe study|Central Europe study
example title: Germline determinants of humoral immune response to HPV-16 protect against oropharyngeal cancer.
example quote: The IARC Central Europe study was supported by the European Commission’s INCO-COPERNICUS Program (IC15-CT98-0332), US NIH/National Cancer Institute grant CA92039 and World Cancer Research Foundation grant WCRF 99A28.
definition: A multicentre hospital-based case–control study of cancers of the upper aerodigestive tract (oral cavity, pharynx, larynx and oesophagus), coordinated by the International Agency for Research on Cancer in Bucharest (Romania), Lodz (Poland), Moscow (Russia), Banská Bystrica (Slovakia), and Olomouc and Prague (Czech Republic) to investigate genetic susceptibility to these cancers and its interaction with alcohol and tobacco use. It is the upper aerodigestive tract arm of IARC's central European multicentre case–control study of lung, head and neck and kidney cancers, and part of its controls are shared with the lung cancer arm.
location quote: For the central European lung cancer study, the controls overlapped with the central European UADT cancer study for Bucharest (Romania), Lodz (Poland), Moscow (Russia), Banska Bystrika (Slovakia), and Olomouc and Prague (Czech Republic).
note: Tier D (D123), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Parent left for later: memberOf review name E547 (International Head and Neck Cancer Epidemiology Consortium), not minted in this run; quote: "The pooled cohort of the INHANCE Consortium studies comprised 10 042 participants with head and neck cancer from 10 INHANCE case-control studies conducted in North America (Seattle, Washington, USA; Los Angeles, California, USA; HOTSPOT, CHANCE/North Carolina, USA), South America (Sao Paulo 1, Sao Paulo 2, Latin America), and Europe (Central Europe, Western Europe, Head and Neck 5000 [HN5000])." (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC10777670/fullTextXML). Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred, having only P1's abstract. P1's full text and supplement settle it: IARCCES is the IARC Central Europe study, whose row in Supplementary Table 1 reads 'IARC Central Europe | Poland, Romania, Russia, Slovakia | P. Brennan | Multicenter Hospital-based case-control | 16614111', and whose funding P1 acknowledges ('The IARC Central Europe study was supported by...'). It is the upper aerodigestive tract (head and neck) arm of IARC's central European multicentre case-control study, with centres in Romania, Poland, Russia, Slovakia and the Czech Republic. It is not COHO:0000870: that term is defined as the lung cancer arm, a different case series, although the two arms share part of their controls. The study belongs to the INHANCE consortium (tier-E row E547). Recruitment is dated 2000–2002 in the GWAS papers and 1998–2003 in the INHANCE pooled analyses, so no dates are in the definition. If the curator prefers to model IARC's whole central European multicentre study (lung, head and neck and kidney cancers) as one cohort, COHO:0000870 would need broadening and this term could become its sub-cohort; as defined now, COHO:0000870 is the lung study and this is a sibling. E852 (ORC, 'IARC oral cancer') is a different IARC study, the one INHANCE papers call 'IARC Multicenter'. 'CE' is the study's own abbreviation in PMID:29540730 and PMID:22662130; no COHO term uses it.

label: Institute for Behavioral Genetics
example title: Genome-wide Association Meta-analysis of Childhood and Adolescent Internalizing Symptoms.
example quote: Two cohort studies from the Institute for Behavioral Genetics (IBG) supplied information for this project: The Colorado Adoption Project (http://ibgwww.colorado.edu/cap/) and the Colorado Twin Registry (https://www.colorado.edu/ibg/research/human-research-studies/colorado-twin-registry)
definition: A combined sample of two longitudinal family studies of the Institute for Behavioral Genetics at the University of Colorado Boulder, United States: the Colorado Adoption Project, a prospective adoption study of behavioural development begun in 1975, and the Colorado Twin Registry, a population-based registry of twins born since 1968 that has recruited since 1982. Their genotyped participants are analysed together in genome-wide association meta-analyses of childhood and adolescent psychiatric traits.
location quote: The Colorado Twin Registry (CTR) is a population-based registry housed at the Institute for Behavioral Genetics at the University of Colorado.
note: Tier D (D124), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because no unit described the sample. P1's Supplement 1 (Elsevier's supplementary file) and P2's Supplementary Note describe it: 'Two cohort studies from the Institute for Behavioral Genetics (IBG) supplied information for this project: The Colorado Adoption Project ... and the Colorado Twin Registry'. Both papers' cohort tables give the full name 'Institute for Behavioral Genetics' (USA; 'population-based (twin families) and clinically ascertained'). The tag therefore denotes one pooled sample of two distinct IBG cohorts, the same in both GWAS papers, which makes it an aggregation named after its institute, like the Minnesota Center for Twin and Family Research (COHO:0000542). The draft's lead, the Colorado Twin Registry, was half right: it is one of the two members. Neither member is in COHO. Tier-D row D102 (COL_Twin, Colorado Longitudinal Twin Study) is one of the Colorado Twin Registry's samples and could become a member. The genotyping (Axiom PMRA, supported by the CADD centre grant P60 DA011015) overlaps COHO:0000033 (Center on Antisocial Drug Dependence), whose tagged GWAS sample is the Registry's LTS and CTS twins (PMID:35534559), and an EAGLE GWAS calls the Colorado sample CADD (PMID:35994476); the 'clinically ascertained' part of IBG is probably CADD's clinical families, which P1 does not name. The curator may want to relate IBG and CADD. If an aggregation named after an institute is not wanted, the fallback is 'not a cohort', with IBG added as an acronym to terms for the Colorado Adoption Project and the Colorado Twin Registry. No EAGLE (COHO:0000750) membership: P1 says its sample includes EAGLE cohorts and additional cohorts without saying which.

input name: International Collaboration for the Genomics of HIV
label: International Collaboration for the Genomics of HIV
other synonyms: International Consortium for the Genomics of HIV
example title: Multiancestry sex-stratified genomic associations with HIV viral load and controller status from the ICGH.
example quote: To address this, we performed a sex-stratified genome-wide association study using data from the ICGH.
definition: An international collaboration of the HIV host genetics community, established to combine all available genome-wide SNP data sets on people living with HIV-1 worldwide, which pools genotype and clinical data from HIV cohorts and studies in North America, Europe, Australia and Africa, many of them natural-history cohorts, to study host genetic influences on HIV-1 acquisition, viral load and spontaneous control.
location quote: The International Collaboration for the Genomics of HIV was established as a platform to combine all available genome-wide SNP data sets obtained on HIV-1 infected individuals worldwide. Patient material was collected at multiple clinical centers across North America, Europe, Australia and Africa (a list of contributing cohort studies and centers is given at the end of the paper).
note: Tier D (D125), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (2023): the International Collaboration for the Genomics of HIV (ICGH), a consortium combining data from independent HIV natural-history cohorts/studies, used for a sex-stratified GWAS of HIV viral load and control; P2 (2013, cited for the cohort): the same consortium, combining SNP data from cohorts/studies/institutions for a GWAS of HIV-1 acquisition. Identity, scope and purpose are well supported by open-access units from P1 (2023) and P2 (2013, cited for the cohort). COHO:0000917 'International HIV Controllers Study' is a contributing member cohort (D125.31), not ICGH itself. No countries: the consortium is multinational and units give ancestry groups, not recruitment countries. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type and example are right. The definition leaves out what the collaboration was set up for and where its cohorts are, and the draft gave no countries, although P2's methods say the collaboration 'was established as a platform to combine all available genome-wide SNP data sets obtained on HIV-1 infected individuals worldwide' and that 'Patient material was collected at multiple clinical centers across North America, Europe, Australia and Africa', and end with a list of participating cohorts by country. P2's supplementary Text S1 calls it the 'International Consortium for the Genomics of HIV', added as a synonym. Many ICGH member cohorts are rows of this review or COHO terms and could be linked with hasCohort from P2's list of participating cohorts: D080 ACTG, D359 ALIVE, D444 GRIV, D447 HGDS, D466 MACS, D473 MHCS, D507 SFCCC, D302 SHCS, D390 CHAVI, E263 DHIVCS, E426 GISHEAL, E516 ICFA, E525 IDIBAPS, E528 IFS_b (Icona Foundation Study), E708 Modena, E940 PSWC (Pumwani), E1182 US-HIV-NHS, E1209 WAHCS, COHO:0000917 (International HIV Controllers Study) and COHO:0000971 (Amsterdam Cohort Studies). That list runs item after item under a heading, so each link needs its own quotable span. The Gambia (the WTCCC3 HIV study) is not in the gazetteer; the continents given cover it.

label: International Endometriosis Genetics Consortium
example title: Multi-ancestry genome-wide association and integrated multi-omics analyses of endometriosis and its clinical manifestations.
example quote: The IEGC is a collaborative effort that aggregates data from multiple international studies to investigate the genetic factors of endometriosis4.
definition: An international consortium of research groups studying the genetics of endometriosis, which pools genome-wide association data from studies in Europe, the United States, Australia and Japan, with cases identified by surgical confirmation, medical records or self-report, in meta-analyses of endometriosis risk.
location quote: We conducted a meta-analysis of 24 GWAS with a total effective sample size of 206,106 (60,674 cases and 701,926 controls) of European (98%: Europe, USA, Australia), and East Asian (2%: Japan) ancestry.
note: Tier D (D126), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: IEGC, one of eight cohorts/data sources in a multi-ancestry endometriosis GWAS meta-analysis, itself an aggregation of many international cohorts/studies; P2 (2020, found by name): describes IEGC's formation and growth as an international consortium. UKB, BBJ, MVP, FinnGen, EstBB, AllOfUs and 23andMe are IEGC's own contributing data sources per P1 (D126.1), not IEGC itself; COHO:0000681 FUSION in the candidate list is unrelated (a Finnish type-2-diabetes study). No countries: IEGC is described as international with groups worldwide, none named. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type and parent (none) are right. The definition's case-definition clause describes the 2023 meta-analysis rather than the consortium, and it says nothing of where the studies are. The draft gave no countries, although the consortium's meta-analysis, which P1 cites as its IEGC source (ref. 4, Rahmioglu et al. 2023), pools 24 GWAS from Europe, the USA, Australia and Japan. The drafted example quote began with the section heading 'METHODS Study populations'; it is replaced by P1's sentence saying what the IEGC is, from the same paper and study. Neither IEGC meta-analysis names the consortium in its own text; the attribution comes from P1 and later IEGC-authored papers, so the country quote comes from the meta-analysis itself. Member studies include the QIMR/HCS and Oxford studies, Leuven, NHS2, WGHS (COHO:0000516), BioBank Japan (COHO:0000377), 23andMe (COHO:0000449), deCODE and iPSYCH (2017), with UK Biobank (COHO:0000176) and FinnGen (COHO:0000403) added in 2023. Tier-E row E864 (OXEGENE, Oxford Endometriosis Gene) is probably the Oxford study and a member. In P1 the other seven data sources are listed beside IEGC, not inside it, though the IEGC meta-analysis itself includes UK Biobank.

Tier D (D127), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: Illumina iControlDB, a company-maintained database supplying healthy Caucasian control genotypes used as external controls in a sarcoidosis GWAS, alongside two dbGaP studies used the same way. D127.1 ('matched part of the tag') concerns the unrelated Illumina Omni1-Quad genotyping array, not iControlDB - disregarded. D127.4/D127.7 (open access) show iControlDB is a company-maintained database of healthy-control genotypes used as external controls; no recruitment purpose, place or date is evidenced beyond that, so it reads as a genotyping-company resource rather than a defined, recruited cohort. Checked 2026-09-23: None. The verdict is right: Illumina's purpose document for iControlDB (the Illumina Genotyping Control Database) describes an online data repository to which researchers submit, and from which others download, genotypic and phenotypic data from individuals usable as controls. It is a data resource of donated control genotypes, not a defined group of people. Part of the iControlDB data P1 used are HapMap samples (COHO:0000284, International HapMap Project). The PGS Catalog id Illumina_iControlDB has the same meaning in the source GWAS checked (PMID:24740154).

input name: Italian Network on Genetic Isolates-Val Borbera
label: INGI-Val Borbera
other synonyms: Val Borbera|Val Borbera study|Val Borbera cohort|Italian Network on Genetic Isolates-Val Borbera
example title: Novel loci and biomedical consequences of iron homoeostasis variation.
example quote: The INGI‐Val Borbera (INGI-VB) study comprises 1,785 healthy participants enrolled in the Val Borbera Valley, a geographically isolated region located within the Apennine Mountains in Northwest Italy.
definition: A population-based cohort of adults descended from the inhabitants of the upper Val Borbera, a genetically isolated valley in the Apennine mountains of Piedmont, north-west Italy, recruited on the basis of their ancestry in the valley's villages and nearby areas, with clinical and anthropometric data collected by physicians of San Raffaele Hospital, Milan, to identify genes and variants underlying common disorders and quantitative traits; one of the isolated populations of the Italian Network of Genetic Isolates.
location quote: The aim of the present study is to characterize the population isolate of the upper Val Borbera, a large valley localized within the Apennine mountains of Piedmont, in the Northwest of Italy, geographically secluded from the surrounding areas.
parent quote: All three populations belong to the Italian Network of Genetic Isolates (INGI), a project aimed at studying the genetic basis of complex diseases and phenotypes (including eating habits) [41].
note: Tier D (D128), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. GWAS tag(s) INGI-Val Borbera not carried: they denote another cohort. P1: no quotable unit names INGI-Val Borbera (abstract only); P2: one of several cohorts (including sibling INGI-Carlantino) studied for urinary uromodulin excretion; P3: the Val Borbera (VBI) discovery cohort for a sweet-taste-liking GWAS; P4: the INGI-Val Borbera (INGI-VB) study, described in the supplement as healthy participants from the Val Borbera Valley. P1's abstract doesn't name the cohort and no full text was available here, so the example is drawn from P4 instead. Parent set to COHO:0000105 (INGI aggregation) per D128.21, matching how sibling cohorts INGI-Carlantino (COHO:0000586) and INGI-FVG (COHO:0000593) are already modelled. No existing COHO term found for Val Borbera (checked coho_names.tsv, triage_D/E.tsv). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, country, parent and example study are right. The definition calls the members 'healthy participants', which is how one iron-status GWAS supplement (P4) describes its subset; the design paper (PMID:19847309) describes adults aged 18 or over descended from the valley's population, recruited by ancestry in the seven main villages of the upper Val Borbera and nearby areas, with clinical data collected by San Raffaele Hospital physicians, to find genes and variants for common disorders and quantitative traits. The drafted country and example quote ran on into about 600 characters of base64 EndNote field code: the example quote is cut at its sentence end and the country quote replaced by the design paper's. The PGS Catalog name, the study's own names 'Val Borbera study' and 'Val Borbera cohort', and its acronym VB are added. The sibling terms are labelled 'Italian Network of Genetic Isolates - Carlantino' (COHO:0000586) and 'Italian Network of Genetic Isolates - Friuli Venezia Giulia' (COHO:0000593). For consistency the curator may prefer 'Italian Network of Genetic Isolates - Val Borbera', though that exact string was not seen in any source, whereas the draft's 'INGI-Val Borbera' is what the cohort's investigators and the GWAS Catalog use. The design paper states no recruitment dates. The parent quote is the one already used for the two sibling memberships. E546 (INGI-Cilento) is another INGI population.

label: Ischemic Stroke Genetics Study
other synonyms: Ischemic Stroke Genetic Study
example title: Evidence of survival bias in the association between APOE-Є4 and age at ischemic stroke onset.
example quote: ISGS and SWISS: The Ischemic Stroke Genetics Study (ISGS) was supported by the NINDS (R01 NS42733; PI Dr Meschia).
definition: A prospective multicentre case–control study, funded by the US National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, of adults with a first-ever ischaemic stroke confirmed by CT or MRI and enrolled within 30 days of onset at five academic medical centres in the United States, with centrally adjudicated stroke subtypes, and of stroke-free controls matched by age and sex and recruited mainly among the patients' spouses and unrelated friends, to investigate genetic risk factors for ischaemic stroke and its subtypes.
location quote: The ISGS is a prospective case-control genetic association study of patients with first-ever ischemic stroke at 5 US tertiary stroke centers.
parent quote: A total of 4,253 additional CCS-phenotyped cases from 10 GRCs across Europe and the US have been previously genotyped prior to initiating SiGN (BRAINS, EDIN, GASROS, GEOS, ISGS, NHS, MUNICH, OXVASC, ST GEORGE’S, and SWISS).
note: Tier D (D129), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ISGS, one of many ischemic-stroke GWAS cohorts (age-at-onset survival-bias study); P2-P7: papers about or using ISGS directly (protocol paper, family history, sex differences in evaluation, gene-variant associations) - the same US multi-center study throughout. Well supported by six independent open-access sources (P1-P7), including a dedicated protocol paper (P2). Controls for ISGS (and the related SWISS study) are drawn from HANDLS and BLSA per the P1 supplement - separate existing COHO cohorts, not parents or members of ISGS. COHO:0000753 'Helsinki 2000 Ischemic Stroke Genetics Study' has a similar-looking label but is a distinct Finland-based study (its own acronyms are FINLAND/Finland, not ISGS); this US, five-center, NINDS/Meschia-led study is not that term. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country and example are right. The definition draws 'assessing family history of stroke' from one analysis paper and leaves out the design in the protocol paper: cases enrolled within 30 days of a first-ever, imaging-confirmed ischaemic stroke at five US academic centres, subtypes centrally adjudicated, and age- and sex-matched stroke-free controls recruited mainly among spouses and unrelated friends. It also missed that ISGS is one of SiGN's genetic research centres (COHO:0000651), which is how P1 used it. The protocol abstract and METASTROKE's appendix also call it the 'Ischemic Stroke Genetic Study', added as a synonym. In SiGN, ISGS and SWISS cases were paired with stroke-free participants of BLSA (COHO:0000195) and HANDLS (COHO:0000438) as controls (P1 supplement). ISGS was also a METASTROKE discovery cohort (COHO:0000688), combined with SWISS as 'ISGS/SWISS'. SWISS, the sibling-pair study run in parallel, is tier-D row D167. COHO:0000753 (Helsinki 2000 Ischemic Stroke Genetics Study) is a different study.

input name: Karolinska Mammography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer – Cohort Study
label: Karolinska Mammography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer
other synonyms: Karolinska Mammography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer – Cohort Study|KARolinska MAmmography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer|KARMA study
example title: A Swedish Genome-Wide Haplotype Association Analysis Identifies a Novel Breast Cancer Susceptibility Locus in 8p21.2 and Characterizes Three Loci on Chromosomes 10, 11 and 16.
example quote: Briefly, the KARMA Cohort consists of 70,877 women performing a screening or clinical mammogram at 4 hospitals in Sweden during the period October 2010–March 2013 [20].
definition: A prospective cohort of women recruited in 2011–2013 when attending mammography screening or clinical mammography at four hospitals in Sweden (in Stockholm, Helsingborg, Lund and Landskrona), with questionnaires, mammograms, blood samples and linkage to Swedish health registers, established to determine how mammographic density, genetic factors and lifestyle influence breast cancer risk and to build risk prediction models for individualised prevention and screening.
location quote: Briefly, the KARMA Cohort consists of 70,877 women performing a screening or clinical mammogram at 4 hospitals in Sweden during the period October 2010–March 2013 [20].
parent quote: KARMA is part of the Breast Cancer Association Consortium.
note: Tier D (D130), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: KARMA, a Swedish breast-cancer cohort reanalyzed together with the sibling cohort KARBAC; P2: KARMA among many breast-cancer studies in a menopausal-hormone-therapy interaction meta-analysis (a related but distinct tag, pKARMA, is also used on the same two studies). Well supported, including a direct 'Cohort Profile' citation (D130.20). Tag 'pKARMA' (tier-D key D286, a different batch) shares the same base PGS name without the 'Cohort Study' suffix and is tagged on the same two studies (GCST90129576/7) - a researcher should reconcile it with this row when D286 is drafted. No existing COHO term found for KARMA. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country and example are right. The definition takes its dates from P1 (October 2010 to March 2013) rather than the cohort profile, which says women were invited from January 2011 to March 2013; 'assembled by the Karolinska Mammography Project' restates the name; and it leaves out the data collected (questionnaire, mammograms, blood, register linkage) and the aims the profile states. Missed parent: the profile says 'KARMA is part of the Breast Cancer Association Consortium' (COHO:0000020). The profile's acronym-forming spelling 'KARolinska MAmmography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer' and 'KARMA study' are added as synonyms. pKARMA (tier-D row D286), also tagged on GCST90129576/7, is not this cohort. It is a case-control set of invasive breast cancer patients diagnosed 2001–2008 in Stockholm, with breast-cancer-free controls taken from KARMA (PMID:38366028: 'pKARMA is a cohort of 5002 invasive breast cancer patients diagnosed between 2001 and 2008 in Stockholm and 5433 breast cancer-free women from KARMA'; PMID:28725034: cases from the LIBRO-1 study). Its controls are a KARMA subset, so D286 needs its own term, not a merge with this one. KARBAC (D460) is a separate Stockholm breast cancer case series.

input name: Kathleen Cuningham Foundation Consortium for Research into Familial Breast Cancer
label: Kathleen Cuningham Foundation Consortium for Research into Familial Breast Cancer
other synonyms: Kathleen Cuningham Foundation Consortium for Research into Familial Aspects of Breast Cancer|Kathleen Cuningham Consortium for Research into Familial Breast Cancer
example title: Genome-wide and transcriptome-wide association studies of mammographic density phenotypes reveal novel loci.
example quote: kConFab was initiated in 1997, and with the help of the Family Cancer Centres in Australia and New Zealand began enrolling families with a strong history of breast and breast/ovarian cancer.
definition: A research resource of epidemiological, family-history, lifestyle and clinical data and biospecimens collected since 1997 from affected and unaffected members of families with multiple cases of breast and/or ovarian cancer, recruited by research nurses through family cancer clinics in Australia and New Zealand, and made available to researchers anywhere in the world for studies of familial breast cancer.
location quote: These families were ascertained in Australia through the Kathleen Cuningham Foundation Consortium for Research into Familial Breast Cancer. || kConFab was initiated in 1997, and with the help of the Family Cancer Centres in Australia and New Zealand began enrolling families with a strong history of breast and breast/ovarian cancer.
parent quote: A number of large studies and consortia have been established that aim to identify genetic modifiers of cancer risk in BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutation carriers, including Modifiers and Genetics in Cancer (MAGIC), Epidemiological study of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutation carriers (EMBRACE), Genetic Modifiers of cancer risk in BRCA1/2 mutation carriers (GEMO), the Kathleen Cuningham Consortium for Research into Familial Breast Cancer (kConFab), the German Consortium for Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer (GCHBOC) and the Breast Cooperative Family Registry (Breast-CFR). However, with current sample sizes of less than 1,500 carriers, none of these groups have adequate power to identify genetic modifiers with confidence. To address this problem, a 'consortium of consortia', the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 (CIMBA), was established in 2005 (see Additional file 1 for a list of current contributors).
note: Tier D (D131), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: kConFab, the Kathleen Cuningham Foundation Consortium for Research into Familial Breast Cancer. Despite 'Consortium' in the name and the automatic 'aggregation?' hint, evidence treats kConFab as a single cohort directly enrolling families since 1997, and P7 calls it a 'cohort study' (D131.27); kept as cohort. A related but distinct follow-up sub-study 'kConFab-FUS' appears in D131.19, not covered here. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, countries and example are right. The definition gave the resource's purpose as characterising germline mutations (one use of its biospecimens, from the website blurb), described the consortium as enrolling itself, and left out ovarian-cancer families, the research-nurse recruitment through family cancer clinics and the fact that kConFab is a resource made available to outside researchers (its papers: 'kConFab itself is not a research organisation in the usual sense, but rather provides a resource upon which researchers can draw', kconfab.org). No parent was given, although kConFab is one of the groups the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 (COHO:0000901) was formed from and is listed among the CIMBA studies in PGS Catalog sample sets (e.g., PSS000521). Two forms of the name used by kConFab itself were missing as synonyms: the website's 'Kathleen Cuningham Foundation Consortium for Research into Familial Aspects of Breast Cancer' and 'Kathleen Cuningham Consortium for Research into Familial Breast Cancer' (resource paper PMID:16507150, CIMBA design paper). E587 (PGS id KCONFAB/AOCS, 'Kathleen Cuningham Foundation Consortium for research into Familial Breast Cancer/Australian Ovarian Cancer Study') is the joint kConFab/AOCS study used in BCAC and OCAC analyses, not this term; AOCS is already COHO:0000014. kConFab also contributes to BCAC (COHO:0000020, through kConFab/AOCS) and OCAC; only CIMBA is given as parent. The kConFab Follow-Up Study (kConFab-FUS, P5; 'Clinical Follow Up Study' in P1's acknowledgements) is kConFab's own prospective follow-up of its participants, not a separate cohort. Some papers misspell the name 'Kathleen Cunningham'; not added.

label: Krakow stroke genetics study
example title: Evidence of survival bias in the association between APOE-Є4 and age at ischemic stroke onset.
example quote: KRAKOW: Phenotypic data and genetic specimens collection were funded by the grant from the Polish Ministry of Science and Higher Education for Leading National Research Centers (KNOW) and by the grants from the Jagiellonian University Medical College in Krakow, Poland: K/ZDS/002848, K/ZDS/003844.
definition: An ongoing, prospective, single-centre, hospital-based study of consecutive consenting patients of European origin with first-ever or recurrent ischaemic stroke admitted since 2002 to the Stroke Unit of the Jagiellonian University in Krakow, Poland, with stroke subtypes assigned by TOAST and CCS criteria, together with unrelated stroke-free controls from the population of southern Poland; one of the genetic research centres of the Stroke Genetics Network.
location quote: All consecutive subjects with ischemic stroke (fulfilling WHO criteria12 (3)) who were admitted to the Stroke Unit at the Jagiellonian University (Krakow, Poland) and who provided informed consent were included in the study.
parent quote: Because suitable control groups with available GWAS genotyping could not be identified from Poland and Belgium, controls from the KRAKOW and LEUVEN GRCs will also be genotyped as part of SiGN.
note: Tier D (D132), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: Draft deferred for want of a description; research settles it. KRAKOW is the ischaemic stroke case-control sample of the Department of Neurology, Jagiellonian University, Krakow, one of the genetic research centres (GRCs) of the Stroke Genetics Network (SiGN): the SiGN design paper lists it as 'KRAKOW Krakow, Poland Hospital-based' and genotyped both its cases and its controls because no previously genotyped Polish controls existed. The MEGASTROKE Supplementary Note describes it: consecutive consenting patients with ischaemic stroke admitted to the Stroke Unit at the Jagiellonian University (an on-going, prospective single-centre, hospital-based study; first-ever or recurrent strokes, recruited 2002-2010 for that analysis; all of European origin; TOAST and CCS subtypes), and controls 'taken from the population of southern Poland'. The draft's reading of the tag was right. No fuller name exists in any source read: SiGN, MEGASTROKE and P1 call the sample only KRAKOW, and the PGS Catalog name 'Krakow stroke genetics study' has no hit in Europe PMC. The label follows the review's precedent for MUNICH (D144): the PGS Catalog name when the sample has no name of its own. Not in COHO or the review under another name. Distinct from the Jagiellonian University Hemorrhagic Stroke Study (intracerebral haemorrhage cases in MEGASTROKE) and from the epidemiological Krakow Stroke Registry/Database. Besides SiGN it is a member of MEGASTROKE (COHO:0000784); only SiGN is given as parent.

label: Leuven Stroke Genetics Study
other synonyms: Leuven Stroke genetics study

example quote: LEUVEN: The Leuven Stroke genetics study was supported by personal research funds from the Department of Neurology of the University Hospitals Leuven.
definition: A prospective hospital-based study of patients of European descent with cerebral ischaemia (a clinical stroke with imaging confirmation, or a transient ischaemic attack with a new ischaemic lesion on diffusion-weighted imaging) admitted to the Stroke Unit of the University Hospitals Leuven, Belgium, from 2005 to 2009, with standardised diagnostic work-up and TOAST subtyping, together with controls recruited from the same population; one of the genetic research centres of the Stroke Genetics Network.
location quote: Cases of European descent with cerebral ischemia, defined as a clinical stroke with imaging confirmation or a TIA with a new ischemic lesion on diffusion-weighted imaging, who were admitted to the Stroke Unit of the University Hospitals (Leuven, Belgium) were enrolled in the LSGS between 2005 and 2009.
parent quote: Because suitable control groups with available GWAS genotyping could not be identified from Poland and Belgium, controls from the KRAKOW and LEUVEN GRCs will also be genotyped as part of SiGN.
note: Tier D (D133), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: LSGS = Leuven Stroke Genetics Study; P2, P3: same, stroke/CVD patients from the Leuven Stroke Genetics Study. Definition assembled from a funding note (D133.1), a subset description in P2 naming it alongside the Belgian Stroke Study (D133.4), and inclusion criteria from P3 (D133.7); no dedicated profile paper found. 'LEUVEN' is a heading used for this cohort's funding note in P1's supplement (D133.1), not a formal GWAS/PGS tag for this row, added as an acronym. Country Belgium inferred from University Hospitals Leuven, not stated verbatim as a country name. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronyms (LSGS; LEUVEN is SiGN's name for this genetic research centre, expanded as 'LEUVEN, Leuven Stroke Genetics Study' in the SiGN GWAS table) and example are right. The definition was assembled from a funding line and said only 'stroke patients ... assembled for genetic studies'; the MEGASTROKE Supplementary Note describes the study: cases of European descent with cerebral ischaemia (stroke with imaging confirmation or TIA with a new DWI lesion) admitted to the Stroke Unit of the University Hospitals Leuven and enrolled 2005-2009, TOAST-subtyped, with controls from the same population (healthy individuals, spouses of patients with neurological diseases, and the Leuven University Gerontology Database); the outcome paper calls it 'the prospective Leuven Stroke Genetics Study'. Belgium was right, but its quote named only the hospital; the new quote names Belgium. No parent was given, although LEUVEN is one of SiGN's genetic research centres (COHO:0000651), whose controls SiGN genotyped. Not in COHO. Tier-E rows KULEUVEN (E611, an institution id from cancer PRS papers), LES (E626, Leuven Endometrial Cancer Study) and LMBC (E639, Leuven Multidisciplinary Breast Centre) are other Leuven samples. The Belgian Stroke Study (BSS), paired with LSGS in PMID:19319159, is a separate study and not tagged. Besides SiGN, LSGS is a member of MEGASTROKE (COHO:0000784); only SiGN is given as parent.

input name: Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate
label: Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate
other synonyms: Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate Network|Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate Consortium
example title: Genome-wide association study of prostate-specific antigen levels in 392,522 men identifies new loci and improves prediction across ancestry groups.
example quote: Local and national IRBs approved Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate (MADCaP).
definition: A multicentre, clinic-based case-control study of prostate cancer run since 2016 by the Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate (MADCaP) Network at seven accrual centres in Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal and South Africa, with partner institutions in the United States, which under common eligibility criteria, instruments and biosample protocols enrols men over 30 who self-identify as black African: incident, histologically confirmed prostate cancer cases from urology and oncology clinics, and cancer-free controls frequency-matched by age from other clinics in the same catchment areas, to study the genetics and epidemiology of prostate cancer in sub-Saharan Africa.
location quote: Figure 1 depicts the MADCaP Network’s organizational structure, which has seven participant accrual centers in Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, and South Africa with several SSA and US centers partnered to enhance capacity building and offer mentorship.
note: Tier D (D134), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: MADCaP (no naming unit available from P1's own text in this batch); P2: MADCaP, the Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate Network/Consortium. Typed as aggregation on the strength of its own repeated self-description 'MADCaP is a consortium of epidemiologic studies' (D134.4/D134.23, fulltext+supplement); however D134.46-48 describe a unified multi-site design (common data elements, instruments and protocols, direct recruitment of patients and controls at the seven SSA centres), which reads more like a single multi-site cohort — a checker should weigh this. Country evidence (D134.106) also names Senegal, not in the gazetteer. Case variant 'MADCap' seen in an abbreviations list (D134.35/38). Checked 2026-09-23: Typed and defined as a consortium of studies, from P2's one-line gloss and the network's own blurb. That describes the MADCaP Consortium formed in 2007 ('Formed in 2007, the consortium includes investigators from the United States, United Kingdom, Africa, and the Caribbean, who have cohort or case-control studies on prostate cancer among men of African ancestry.', madcapnetwork.org/about-us), but every GWAS Catalog study and PGS Catalog sample set tagged MADCaP uses the MADCaP Network's own study in sub-Saharan Africa: MADCaP Array data from cases and controls in Senegal, Ghana, Nigeria and South Africa (P1 figure legend; PGS sample sets PSS009959, PSS010182, PSS011031, all 'Senegal, Ghana, Nigeria, South Africa'). The design paper (PMID:30260755) describes that sample as one 'clinic-based case-control study' with common data elements, instruments and biosample protocols at seven accrual centres; the centres are recruitment sites, not named cohorts. It is therefore a cohort (as the review treated the ASGC case-control sample), and the definition must describe the case-control study. The countries were right; the quote now comes from the design paper rather than a later array paper. Senegal, the fourth country, is not in gaz_xrefs.tsv. The name MADCaP covers both the consortium of investigators formed in 2007 (an umbrella of their own cohort and case-control studies, which pooled data in the 2011 and 2013 papers) and the network's common case-control study begun in 2016 (the website's 'MADCaP Africa' project); the tags denote the latter, so the term is that study and keeps the consortium's name as its label, as the tagged papers do ('Local and national IRBs approved Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate (MADCaP).'). If the curator later wants the 2007 consortium as an aggregation, it needs its own term. Senegal cannot be asserted: it is missing from gaz_xrefs.tsv. No parent: nothing names MADCaP as a member of AAPC (COHO:0000768) or PRACTICAL.

label: Maywood Cohort
other synonyms: Maywood cohort|Maywood cohort study|Loyola Maywood Study
example quote: Maywood cohort study was supported by the NIH grant numbers R37-HL045508, R01-HL074166, R01-HL086718, and R01-HG003054.
definition: A cohort of African-American families in Maywood, Illinois, United States, recruited from 1995 by Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine from a representative random sample of residents aged 18 to 74 for its family studies of blood pressure and the genetics of hypertension in populations of West African origin, in which Maywood was the United States site alongside Nigeria and Jamaica.
location quote: The Maywood cohort consisted of African Americans from Maywood, IL, who were enrolled in studies of blood pressure at the Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine, Maywood, IL, USA
parent quote: The Maywood cohort consisted of African Americans from Maywood, IL, who were enrolled in studies of blood pressure at the Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine, Maywood, IL, USA
note: Tier D (D135), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: Draft deferred: its only unit was an author affiliation. The draft's guess was right. Maywood is Loyola University Chicago's African American sample from Maywood, Illinois, a study of the African Ancestry Anthropometry Genetics Consortium (AAAGC, COHO:0000893), whose height meta-analysis is P1. The AAAGC supplements (BMI 2013, PMID:23583978; adiposity 2017, PMID:28430825) describe it: 'The Maywood cohort consisted of African Americans from Maywood, IL, who were enrolled in studies of blood pressure at the Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine, Maywood, IL, USA'. Kang et al. 2010 (PMID:20400458), its first GWAS, say the genotyped panel came 'from a larger cohort of families enrolled in the studies of blood pressure at Loyola University in Maywood, IL' that enrolled 'a representative random sample of the population between the ages of 18 and 74'. Loyola's 2008 paper dates the US recruitment: 'Participants from the US were recruited into the Genetic Study of Hypertension in Blacks between 1995–1999 and the Fat Reduction Intervention Trial in African-Americans (FRITAA) between 1995–1998.' The genotyped panel of about 750 unrelated people, sampled at both ends of the BMI range, is why AAAGC papers call it a 'case-control study of obesity'; the cohort itself is the family sample. Maywood and D148 'Nigeria' are the US and Nigerian site samples of Loyola University Chicago's NIH-funded family study 'Genetics of Hypertension in Blacks' (R01 HL053353 from 1995; NIH RePORTER abstract: 'The study sites include Ibadan, Nigeria, Kingston, Jamaica, and Maywood, IL.'). The AAAGC BMI table gives that project name as the full name of both samples. The D148 check made it the label of the Nigerian sample. If that stays, this term must keep a label of its own (the PGS Catalog and AAAGC supplement name 'Maywood Cohort'), and the curator may want a parent term for the three-site project; tier-E row E524 (ICSHIB, International Collaborative Study on Hypertension in Blacks) is Loyola's related multi-country survey, but no source read ties the Maywood genetic sample to it. Other Loyola studies of Maywood residents, the Maywood Cardiovascular Survey and the Fat Reduction Intervention Trial in African-Americans (FRITAA), are not this sample. The parent is AAAGC, as for the other AAAGC studies in COHO, whose membership quotes come from the same PMC5419579 supplement. Not in COHO or elsewhere in the review.

label: Minnesota Breast Cancer Family Study
example title: Genome-wide and transcriptome-wide association studies of mammographic density phenotypes reveal novel loci.
example quote: The families included in Minnesota Breast Cancer Family Study have been described earlier (Sellers et al., 1999, Vachon et al., 2007).
definition: A historical cohort of multigenerational families in Minnesota, United States, ascertained through a consecutive, family-history-unselected series of breast cancer probands diagnosed from 1944 to 1952 at the University of Minnesota, followed up by telephone interview and mailed questionnaire to measure cancer incidence and risk factors in their relatives (sisters, daughters, granddaughters, nieces and marry-ins).
location quote: In total, 426 multigenerational families were ascertained through a breast cancer proband diagnosed from 1944 to 1952 at the University of Minnesota.
note: Tier D (D136), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: MBCFS = Minnesota Breast Cancer Family Study, distinct from ABCFS (Australian Breast Cancer Family Study), a separate tag on the same paper. PGS Catalog's bare name 'Breast Cancer Family Study' omits 'Minnesota' and is ambiguous with the Australian Breast Cancer Family Study (ABCFS, tagged separately as D078 in another batch) described in the same P1 supplement passage; left out of synonyms. Identity confirmed independently by dedicated profile paper P4 (PMID:10613336, D136.20-22). Checked 2026-09-23: None. The tag is the Minnesota Breast Cancer Family Study in P1's supplement, a study separate from ABCFS. The definition matches the design paper (PMID:10613336: 'a historical cohort study of relatives of a consecutive series of 426 breast cancer cases (probands) identified between 1944 and 1952', relatives followed up by telephone interview and mailed questionnaire) and P1's description ('Probands were consecutive cases, unselected for family history.'; 'Almost all (99%) women in the 426 families were Caucasian and from Minnesota.'). No parent: the Markers of Density consortium, through which P1 used it, is not in COHO, and it is not a BCAC study. The PGS Catalog name 'Breast Cancer Family Study' drops 'Minnesota'. That leaves a generic name that would equally fit the Australian Breast Cancer Family Study (tagged ABCFS on the same studies), so the draft was right to leave it out. Relatives and spouses were interviewed in 1990-1996, and the study was run from Mayo Clinic (P1: 'The protocol was approved by the Mayo Clinic Institutional Review Board.'). Neither detail is needed in the definition. Not in COHO. Tier-E row UMN ('University of Minnesota study', a PGS id from systemic lupus erythematosus scores) is unrelated.

Tier D (D137), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the McGill University PD dataset, including samples from 'the Quebec Parkinson Network' (D137.1); P2 and P3: 'McGill' glossed directly as 'McGill University, Canada' (D137.24, D137.36), the recruiting/genotyping institution. In all three GWAS papers 'McGill'/'MCGILL' is used as a site label for McGill University rather than a named, defined sample: P2's own abbreviation list states 'McGill: McGill University, Canada' (D137.24) and P3's states 'McGill McGill University' (D137.36). P1 (D137.1) notes the McGill dataset 'includ[es] samples from the Quebec Parkinson Network' — the real cohort name, if any, which is not itself tagged in this row's evidence and has no COHO match. Checked 2026-09-23: The verdict is right, but the draft read only the GWAS papers. The PGS Catalog id MCGILL ('McGill University') denotes a different sample: McGill University's contribution of BRCA1/2 pathogenic-variant carriers to the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 (COHO:0000901). It is listed among the CIMBA studies in the CIMBA retrospective-cohort sample sets PSS000521-PSS000532 (PMID:32665703), beside EMBRACE, GEMO, HEBON and kConFab, and among the studies of the OCAC/CIMBA and BCAC/CIMBA source GWAS of PGS000082, PGS000351/352, PGS000724, PGS000773-775 and PGS000793. So the tag stands for different samples in different catalogues, both named after the institution, like the review's Columbia and UCSF rows. The draft also missed that in P2 the McGill cohort is one of the International Parkinson Disease Genomics Consortium's cohorts. Neither meaning has a name of its own beyond the institution. The Parkinson's dataset includes, but is not the same as, the Quebec Parkinson Network (Gan-Or et al., J Parkinsons Dis 2020, PMID:31868683), which is not in COHO and is not tagged here; it could get a term if a tag ever uses it. The McGill Parkinson's cohort is an IPDGC (COHO:0000919) cohort. Nothing to mint.

label: Middlesex County Ischemic Stroke Study
example title: Evidence of survival bias in the association between APOE-Є4 and age at ischemic stroke onset.
example quote: MCISS: The Middlesex County Ischemic Stroke Study (MCISS) was supported by intramural funding from the New Jersey Neuroscience Institute/JFK Medical Center, Edison, NJ, and The Neurogenetics Foundation, Cranbury, NJ.
definition: A prospective hospital-based registry of adults with ischaemic stroke, of any ethnic or racial group, admitted through the emergency room to the dedicated stroke unit of the New Jersey Neuroscience Institute at JFK Medical Center in Edison, New Jersey, United States, which enrolled first-ever and recurrent strokes of any severity from 2000 to 2009 with standardised investigations and TOAST subtyping; one of the genetic research centres of the Stroke Genetics Network.
location quote: The MCISS was initiated as a prospective hospital based stroke registry at the New Jersey Neuroscience Institute (Edison, NJ, U.S.A.).
parent quote: CASES GENOTYPED THROUGH SiGN (US SITES)GASROSBoston, USAIllumina HumanOmni 5M Exome470GCNKSSGreater Cincinnati region, USAIllumina HumanOmni 5M Exome499ISGSMulti-center, USAIllumina HumanOmni 5M Exome187MCISSNew Jersey, USA
note: Tier D (D138), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: MCISS = the Middlesex County Ischemic Stroke Study, New Jersey. Only evidence is a single funding acknowledgement (D138.1) that expands the acronym and ties it to two New Jersey institutions; no profile paper, dates, recruitment design or population detail beyond 'ischemic stroke' (from the name) was found in this batch. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym and example are right. The definition was built from a funding line: it named the funders and placed the study vaguely in Middlesex County. The MEGASTROKE Supplementary Note describes it as 'a prospective hospital based stroke registry at the New Jersey Neuroscience Institute (Edison, NJ, U.S.A.)': adults over 18 of any ethnic group, admitted through the emergency room to a dedicated stroke unit, first-ever and recurrent strokes of any severity, enrolled 2000-2009, with standardised investigations and TOAST subtyping. The country was right; the new quote names it rather than only Edison and Cranbury, NJ. No parent was given, although MCISS is one of the Stroke Genetics Network's genetic research centres (COHO:0000651): the SiGN design paper lists 'MCISS New Jersey, USA Hospital-based 1999–2009', and SiGN genotyped its cases. Recruitment years differ slightly between sources: 1999-2009 in the SiGN design paper's table, 2000 to 2009 in the MEGASTROKE description, which the definition follows. Earlier genetic association papers from the same stroke unit (for example PMC2225392, patients 'admitted to the stroke unit at New Jersey Neuroscience Institute/John F. Kennedy Hospital, Edison, New Jersey') do not use the MCISS name and were not treated as defining it. The parent quote is a table row as rendered in Europe PMC's text, with no spaces between cells, and names SiGN. Besides SiGN, MCISS is a MEGASTROKE (COHO:0000784) study; only SiGN is given as parent. Not in COHO.

label: HARMONISATION study
other synonyms: Harmonization study|Harmonization Study|Memory Clinic in Singapore Study|Memory Clinic in Singapore study|Memory Clinic in Singapore
example title: Chromosome 10q24.32 Variants Associate With Brain Arterial Diameters in Diverse Populations: A Genome-Wide Association Study.
example quote: The MCS (Memory Clinic in Singapore) study included patients attending the National University Hospital and St Luke's Hospital memory clinics between 2009 and 2015.
definition: A prospective observational cohort of older multi-ethnic Asian patients aged 50 or over with no cognitive impairment, mild cognitive impairment or dementia due to Alzheimer's disease and/or cerebrovascular disease, recruited from 2010 at the memory clinics of the National University Hospital and St Luke's Hospital in Singapore and assessed by the Memory Aging and Cognition Centre, National University of Singapore, with annual clinical and neuropsychological follow-up for up to five years and brain MRI, retinal and blood biomarker data, to study vascular cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease.
location quote: The Harmonization study is an ongoing prospective study which recruited patients from memory clinics of the National University Hospital and St. Luke’s Hospital in Singapore, aiming to examine cognitive deterioration and associated biomarkers in older Asian individuals with cognitive impairment and dementia due to AD and/or cerebrovascular disease (CeVD).
note: Tier D (D139), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: MCS = Memory Clinic in Singapore (study), a memory-clinic patient cohort in Singapore. Acronym MCS clashes with existing COHO:0000801 'UK Millennium Cohort Study' (also acronym MCS; noted in batch as row 507 of the earlier review) — an unrelated UK birth cohort, not the same cohort as this Singapore memory-clinic sample. Both terms should carry the shared-acronym editor note per COHO convention. Checked 2026-09-23: The identity is right, but 'Memory Clinic in Singapore Study' is P1's descriptive name. The sample is the Memory Aging and Cognition Centre's memory-clinic cohort, which calls itself HARMONISATION (the Harmonization study). Its cohort profile (PMID:41160443) calls it 'the HARMONISATION study, a prospective observational study of VCI and AD in multi-ethnic Asians' ('HARMONIZATION recruited and deeply phenotyped 700 older multi-ethnic Asians with no cognitive impairment, mild cognitive impairment, and dementia for up to 5 years of follow-up'), and its papers say it 'recruited patients from memory clinics of the National University Hospital and St. Luke’s Hospital in Singapore' (PMC12588707): the same two clinics, run by the same Memory Aging and Cognition Centre, as P1's MCS. The brain arterial diameter group that wrote P1 lists the same sample, in its 2024 pooled analysis of the same MRA measure (PMID:38148489), as 'The Harmonization Study Consecutive ﬁrst-visit patients ≥50 years old attending an academic memory clinic Singapore, Singapore 2009–2015', the same 2009-2015 window P1 gives for MCS, and on the same 3T Siemens scanner. The definition described P1's analysis window only. The cohort's own papers give recruitment from 2010 ('Patient recruitment started in 2010', PMC13279181; August 2010 to February 2020, PMC12588707), eligibility from age 50, and annual follow-up for up to five years. The country was right; the new quote comes from the cohort's own paper. The acronym MCS is shared with the UK Millennium Cohort Study (COHO:0000801, acronym MCS; tier-C row C202). Both terms keep it and both need the editor note ('The acronym MCS also denotes ...'). HARMONISATION and HARMONIZATION are the study's own capitalised short names (cohort profile title and abstract); they are listed as acronyms, as the review did for MEMENTO, and could equally be plain synonyms. The Harmonization study is one of the Meta VCI Map consortium's memory-clinic cohorts (PMC11032573), which is not in COHO, so there is no parent. The other Singapore sample in P1, EDIS (Epidemiology of Dementia in Singapore), is a separate population-based study. Not in COHO under another name.

definition: A hospital-based study at the Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, United States, that from 2003 enrolled adults with acute ischaemic stroke (consecutive patients admitted to its stroke unit through the emergency department, or seen in its neurology clinics or on other inpatient services), with stroke-free controls from the hospital's outpatient clinics matched on age, sex and ancestry, to study genetic influences on the risk and outcome of ischaemic stroke; one of the genetic research centres of the Stroke Genetics Network.
location quote: Of those sites, 7 are European centers (BASICMAR—Spain, BRAINS—United Kingdom, GRAZ—Austria, KRAKOW—Poland, LEUVEN—Belgium, LUND STROKE REGISTER—Sweden, and SAHLSIS—Sweden) and 5 are based in the United States (GASROS, GCNKSS, GEOS, ISGS, and MIAMISR).

note: Tier D (D140), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: MGH-GASROS = Genes Affecting Stroke Risk and Outcome Study (GASROS), a Massachusetts General Hospital stroke genetics study; P2: GASROS, same study, used as a data source for stroke outcome prediction. Definition inferred from a funding acknowledgement (D140.1, naming the 'Massachusetts General Hospital Stroke Genetics Group' and the GASROS grant) and a separate paper using 'GASROS' data for stroke risk/outcome prediction (D140.4); no dedicated profile paper with population, recruitment dates or design was found in this batch. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronyms and example are right. The definition only restated the name and the funding line. The MEGASTROKE Supplementary Note describes MGH-GASROS: 'Cases were all consecutive patients aged 18 years presenting with ischemic stroke and admitted to the Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH) Stroke Unit through the Emergency Department, or evaluated in the MGH Neurology outpatient clinics, as well as on the inpatient Medical and Vascular Surgical services from January 2003 to July 2008.' Controls were 'recruited among the stroke-free adults presenting to the MGH outpatient clinics and matched with the stroke cases on the basis of age, sex and ancestry'. Later GASROS papers describe enrolment of emergency-department patients from 2003 to 2011. The United States was right, but its quote named only the hospital and the NIH; the new quote names the country. No parent was given, although GASROS is one of the Stroke Genetics Network's genetic research centres (COHO:0000651), with cases genotyped before SiGN began. The cohort's other names were missing as synonyms: 'MGH Genes Affecting Stroke Risk and Outcome Study' (METASTROKE, MEGASTROKE), 'Massachusetts General Hospital – Genes Affecting Stroke Risk and Outcome Study' (SiGN GWAS), 'Genes Affecting Stroke Risks and Outcomes Study' (P1's funding line), 'Genes Affecting Stroke Risk and Outcomes Study' and 'Genes Associated with Stroke Risk and Outcomes Study' (the MGH group's imaging papers). Enrolment windows differ between reports (January 2003 to July 2008 in MEGASTROKE's description of the genotyped cases, 2003-2009 in SiGN's table, 2003-2011 in the imaging papers), so the definition gives only the start year. Besides SiGN, MGH-GASROS is a METASTROKE (COHO:0000688) and MEGASTROKE (COHO:0000784) study; only SiGN is given as parent. Tier-E row E695 (PGS id MGH-stroke, 'Massachusetts General Hospital Stroke Study', in the GIANT BMI 2025 scores beside MGH-AF and MGH-CNC) may overlap this sample; it was not read. Not in COHO.

label: Melanoma Institute Australia cohort

definition: A cohort of patients with histopathologically confirmed cutaneous melanoma managed at Melanoma Institute Australia in Sydney, Australia, identified with written informed consent from the institute's Biospecimen Bank and Research Database, whose germline DNA was genotyped genome-wide in phases from 2014 and who are followed prospectively for outcomes including death from melanoma, ascertained from clinical records and linkage to Australian cancer registries.
location quote: With written, informed consent, patients with histo-pathological confirmed CM cases managed at MIA, Sydney, Australia were identified from this Biospecimen Bank and Database.
note: Tier D (D141), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: MIA as one of two independent replication cohorts (with 23andMe) in a multi-trait autoimmune-loci cutaneous-melanoma GWAS; P2: the MIA cohort (Melanoma Institute Australia), a high-UV-setting discovery cohort combined with UK Biobank and validated against the Leeds Melanoma Cohort in a melanoma-survival PRS study. Named after the treating institution but is a defined, consented patient sample (Biospecimen Bank plus Research Database under two named ethics protocols, HREC/10/RPAH/530 and HREC/11/RPAH/444), not a bare institution reference. Not already in COHO and no duplicate elsewhere in this review (checked coho_names.tsv, triage_D.tsv, triage_E.tsv). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, country, acronym and example are right. The label is the institute's name; the sample's own paper names it the 'Melanoma Institute Australia cohort' (table legends in PMC9446843: 'MIA Melanoma Institute Australia cohort'; supplement heading 'Melanoma Institute Australia Cohort'), so that is the label and the institute's name (the PGS Catalog name) becomes a synonym. The definition follows P2 but leaves out what makes it a GWAS cohort: the patients' germline DNA from the MIA Biospecimen Bank was genotyped (OncoArray in 2014 and 2016, Global Screening Array in 2018), and melanoma deaths are ascertained from MIA clinical records and linkage to cancer registries. All uses of the tag are the same MIA patient sample; only the P1 replication set adds controls from an unstated source, which does not change this term. Not in COHO and no other review row for it (AMFS D360, Q-MEGA D054, WAMHS D545 and COHO:0000875 MDACC are other melanoma samples; the 'MIA' listed among ADSP's source cohorts in the review's ADSP row is an Alzheimer's disease sample, not this one).

label: Montrachet Study
other synonyms: Maculopathy Optic Nerve nuTRition neurovAsCular and HEarT diseases|Montrachet Study Cohort

example quote: Secondly, the EUGENDA cohort enrolled individuals from 55 years of age, while some other cohorts enrolled older individuals only (e.g. Montrachet ≥75 years, Alienor ≥77 years).
definition: A population-based study of people aged 75 years or older in Dijon, France, recruited from 2009 to 2013 among participants of the Three-City (3C) Study, who had eye examinations, including photographs and optical coherence tomography of the macula and optic disc, at Dijon University Hospital, designed to find associations between age-related eye diseases and neurologic and heart diseases in the elderly.

note: Tier D (D142), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: Draft deferred. The study's open-access design paper (Creuzot-Garcher et al. 2016, PMID:26466845) settles it: Montrachet stands for 'Maculopathy Optic Nerve nuTRition neurovAsCular and HEarT diseases'; it is a population-based eye study of people aged 75 and over in Dijon, France, recruited 22 October 2009 to 31 March 2013 from the Dijon participants of the Three-City (3C) Study (COHO:0000812), with eye examinations at the University Hospital Dijon, aimed at links between age-related eye disease and neurologic and heart disease. Sibling: ALIENOR (tier-D row D083) is the Bordeaux eye study of 3C participants ('Eye examinations were proposed to 3C participants from 2006 in Bordeaux (Alienor Study) (Delcourt et al. 2010) and from 2009 in Dijon (Montrachet Study).', same design paper), so it should get the same isSubCohortOf 3C link. The upper-case form MONTRACHET is the study's own, in the titles of PMID:31067319 and PMID:32282647. Not in COHO or elsewhere in the review.

note: Tier D (D143), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. 'WTCCC2-Munich' in METASTROKE is the case-control set, these cases plus 797 KORA controls; drop it from the synonyms if the curator wants only case-collection names. label: Murcia Twin Registry
example title: Genetics of monozygotic twins reveals the impact of environmental sensitivity on psychiatric and neurodevelopmental phenotypes.
example quote: The Murcia Twin Registry is funded by the Spanish Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades (RTI2018-095185-B-I00), co-funded by the European Regional Development Fund.
definition: A population-based register of adult twins and other multiples from the region of Murcia, southeast Spain, created in 2006 through an agreement between the University of Murcia and the Murcia Health Council, which identifies twins in the computerised databases of the regional health system and collects interview, questionnaire and anthropometric data in successive waves, with a biobank, for research on genetic and environmental influences on health and health-related behaviours; it began with female twins born 1940-1966 and later added male and opposite-sex twins.
location quote: MTR is a population-based register of adult twins in the region of Murcia, located in southeast Spain.
note: Tier D (D145), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the Murcia Twin Registry (MurciaTR/MTR), one of several twin registries (with CATSS, DTR, FTC, NTR, OATS, QIMR, STR, TEDS, TwinsUK) in a monozygotic-twin environmental-sensitivity GWAS. Multiple consistent, open-access sources (P1 full text/supplement; P2-P7, all found by name search) confirm identity, location, founding, purpose and evolution. Acronym 'MTR' is shared with the distinct Minnesota Twin Family Registry, tier-E row E732 (flagged there as related to D145) -- both cohorts should carry an IAO:0000116 clash note per the acronym rule once E732 is minted. Not already in COHO (checked coho_names.tsv, triage_D.tsv, triage_E.tsv). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronyms, country and example are right. The definition is accurate in outline but garbles the purpose ('genetic and health-related behaviour factors' for 'the analysis of genetic factors related to health and health-related behaviors') and says nothing of how the register works: twins are found in the regional health system's computerised databases (people born on the same day who share surnames), data are gathered in waves by interview, questionnaire and anthropometry, and there is a biobank. The 2013 profile (PMID:23046559, free PDF at Cambridge Core) gives these; the 2026 abstract gives the current scope (twins born 1940-1999). MTR is also the PGS id of tier-E row E732 (Minnesota Twin Family Registry); when E732 is minted, both terms carry MTR and the IAO:0000116 clash note, as the draft says. Not in COHO; E830 ('The Neocodex–Murcia study') is a different study.

input name: Norwegian, Exeter and King's College Consortium for Genetics of Neuropsychiatric Symptoms in Dementia
label: Norwegian, Exeter and King's College Consortium for Genetics of Neuropsychiatric Symptoms in Dementia
example title: Genetic associations with psychosis and affective disturbance in Alzheimer's disease.
example quote: testing, and in some cases neuropathologic assessment, conducted during participation in one of the following six source programs (see Supplemental Material for details for each source program), as previously described 15 : the Fundació ACE Barcelona Alzheimer Treatment and Research Center (ACE/GR@ACE), a Consortium of National Institute on Aging Alzheimer Disease Centers (ADC), Eli Lilly and Company (LILLY), the Norwegian, Exeter and King's College Consortium for Genetics of Neuropsychiatric Symptoms in Dementia (NEXGENS), the National Institute on Aging's Late Onset Alzheimer's Disease Family Study (NIA‐LOAD), and the University of Pittsburgh Alzheimer Disease Research Center (PITT ADRC).
definition: A collaboration of the University of Exeter, King's College London, Innlandet Hospital Trust, the University of Oslo and Stavanger University Hospital that undertakes secondary analysis of data on patients with Alzheimer's disease from cohort studies and patient registries, to study the genetics of neuropsychiatric symptoms such as psychosis in dementia. Its sources are the Norwegian registry of persons assessed for cognitive symptoms (NorCog) with the affiliated Progression of Alzheimer's Disease and Resource Use study, the REDIC-NH and Health and Memory Study nursing-home cohorts in Norway, AddNeuroMed, and hospital outpatient clinics in Italy and Greece.
location quote: NorCog is a national quality- and research registry collecting extensive clinical data and biobank material at outpatient clinics across Norway. || and from the following outpatient clinics in Italy and Greece (Italian and Greek Hospital Outpatients): Centre for Neurodegenerative Disorders, University of Brescia; IRCCS Casa Sollievo della Sofferenza, Neuropsychiatry Clinic of the Eginition Hospital, Athens. || The AddNeuroMed study involves six cross-European collection study sites; London (United Kingdom), Toulouse (France), Perugia (Italy), Kuopio (Finland), Lodz (Poland), and Thessaloniki (Greece)
note: Tier D (D146), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: NEXGENS as one of six source programs (with ACE/GR@ACE, ADC, LILLY, NIA-LOAD, PITT ADRC) contributing GWAS summary statistics to a study of psychosis and affective disturbance in Alzheimer's disease. Combines Norwegian (REDIC-NH; Health and Memory Study, Nord-Trøndelag), AddNeuroMed (already COHO:0000003) and an Italian/Greek hospital outpatient sample under one consortium name (D146.19-31); only summary statistics were shared for this GWAS (D146.10), consistent with an aggregation rather than a single cohort. AddNeuroMed likely needs a hasCohort link from NEXGENS once both exist in COHO. Not already in COHO and no duplicate elsewhere in this review (checked coho_names.tsv, triage_D.tsv, triage_E.tsv). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type (aggregation), acronym and example are right. P1's supplement has a section on NEXGENS that the draft did not use: 'NEXGENS is a collaboration between the following 5 institutions: University of Exeter, King’s College London, Innlandet Hospital Trust, University of Oslo, and Stavanger University Hospital which undertakes secondary analysis of data from Alzheimer’s disease patients from cohort studies and patient registries.' Its five program sources include NorCog/PADR, which the draft's definition leaves out, and the definition describes NEXGENS by what it supplied to one GWAS rather than by who runs it and what it pools. Countries: Norway, Italy and Greece are right, but the Norway quote (a table legend) does not say Norway except inside the consortium's name, and AddNeuroMed's sites add the United Kingdom, France, Finland and Poland (AddNeuroMed is one of NEXGENS's sources). Member for a hasCohort link from NEXGENS: AddNeuroMed (COHO:0000003), quote 'Data for this study came from the following five program sources: AddNeuroMed study' (same supplement URL). The other sources (NorCog, PADR, REDIC-NH, the Health and Memory Study in Nord-Trøndelag, which its cohort profile ties to HUNT, COHO:0000395, and the Italian and Greek outpatients) are not in COHO and have no GWAS or PGS tags. The United Kingdom, France, Finland and Poland come only through AddNeuroMed; drop them if aggregation countries should list only a consortium's own recruitment.
