example title: Common X-Chromosome Variants Are Associated with Parkinson Disease Risk.
example quote: The PD cohorts include the International PD Genomics Consortium (IPDGC) NeuroX dataset, the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) PD dataset, the Autopsy-Confirmed PD GWAS Consortium (APDGC) dataset genotyped by the Center for Inherited Disease Research, the NeuroGenetics Research Consortium (NGRC) dataset, the UK PD Consortium, and the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium 2, referred to here as EBI MERGE.
definition: A case-control sample of people with Parkinson's disease, diagnosed by modified UK Brain Bank criteria, and neurologically healthy controls (community volunteers and patients' spouses), recruited by the NeuroGenetics Research Consortium at affiliated neurology and movement disorder clinics in Oregon, Washington, Georgia and New York, United States, with uniform, standardised methods for diagnosis, subject selection, data collection and DNA preparation, for genetic and gene-environment studies of Parkinson's disease, and genotyped genome-wide.
location quote: Subjects were enrolled by NGRC investigators, using standardized methods, at four NGRC-affiliated movement disorder clinics in the United States.
note: Tier D (D147), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the NGRC dataset, one of several independently recruited PD case-control datasets (with IPDGC, NINDS, APDGC, EBI MERGE, AMP PD, UK Biobank) pooled in an X-chromosome PD-risk GWAS. NGRC recruits its own PD patients/controls directly under uniform, standardized protocols (D147.21, D147.24) rather than pooling pre-existing named cohorts, so drafted as a cohort, not an aggregation, despite the triage 'aggregation?' hint and the word 'Consortium' in its name; a checker should confirm. No unit gives a recruitment location/country. Not already in COHO; triage_D.tsv's only other 'neurogenetics' hit (D361, ANGST) and triage_E.tsv's E272 (Duke Neurogenetics Study) are unrelated cohorts. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym and example are right, and so is the type: the NGRC recruits its own cases and controls under one protocol rather than pooling named cohorts. The draft found no place and gave no country; the NGRC GWAS paper (Hamza et al. 2010, PMID:20711177, open access) says 'Patients and control subjects were recruited from eight NGRC-affiliated neurology clinics in Oregon, Washington, Georgia and New York.', with uniform criteria, modified UK Brain Bank diagnoses and controls who were community volunteers and patients' spouses. The definition therefore lacked where, who and how; 'used in candidate-gene and genome-wide studies' only restates the evidence. The country quote comes from the NGRC's gut microbiome study (Wallen et al. 2020, PMC7293233), a later enrolment at NGRC clinics, and the definition covers all NGRC participants. No parent: in Nalls et al. 2014 the NGRC is a separate group, not an IPDGC member. Not in COHO or elsewhere in the review.

label: Genetics of Hypertension in Blacks
example quote: The meta-analysis included results from nine studies: four population-based African-American studies (ARIC (N = 2,740), CARDIA (N = 699), JHS (N = 2,119), and MESA (N = 1,646)), one family-based African-American study (CFS (N = 386)), African-American GWA study consortia of breast (AABC (N = 5,380)) and prostate cancer (AAPC (N = 5,526)) and two case-control studies of obesity (Maywood (N = 743)) and hypertension (Nigeria (N = 1,188)) (Materials and Methods, Text S1 and Table S1).
definition: A Loyola University Chicago project on the genetics of hypertension in people of West African origin, whose genome-wide association sample consists of unrelated Yoruba-speaking adults with normal or raised blood pressure from Igbo-Ora, a rural town, and Idikan, a low-income neighbourhood of Ibadan, in southwest Nigeria, recruited as part of a long-term study of the environmental and genetic factors underlying hypertension; the Idikan participants were controls of the Africa America Diabetes Mellitus study.
location quote: Study participants were recruited from Yoruba-speaking communities in southwest Nigeria as part of a long-term study on the environmental and genetic factors underlying hypertension [10].
note: Tier D (D148), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: Draft deferred, and its example has no quote. 'Nigeria' is the Nigerian genome-wide sample of Loyola University Chicago's hypertension studies: unrelated Yoruba-speaking adults with normal or raised blood pressure from Igbo-Ora and from Idikan in Ibadan (PMID:22615923: 'The resulting quality controlled clean dataset consisted of 1,188 subjects with genotypes on 759,215 SNPs.'), first analysed by Kang et al. 2010 (PMID:20400458 abstract: '1188 Nigerians from Igbo-Ora and Ibadan, Nigeria') and used as the case-control study 'Nigeria (hypertension, N = 1,188)' in the African Ancestry Anthropometry Genetics Consortium's height and BMI meta-analyses, of which P1 is the latest. The PGS name is the title of Loyola's NHLBI grant R01 HL053353, 'Genetics of Hypertension in Blacks' (NIH RePORTER, 1995-2015), which funded the Nigerian sample ('The Nigerian cohort study was supported by NIH grant numbers R37-HL045508, R01-HL053353, R01-DK075787 and U01-HL054512.', PMID:21998595) and is the project in which the Ibadan participants took part ('the participants from Ibadan, Nigeria for their willing participation in the “Genetics of Hypertension in Blacks” project.', PMID:21573225). The GWAS Catalog studies tagged Nigeria (P1) do not describe it in open text, so the example is the earlier AAAGC height GWAS, GCST001263, which used the same 1,188 Nigerians. Scope: R01 HL053353 (read through the NIH RePORTER API, projects 1R01HL053353-01A1 and 2R01HL053353-12A1) began in 1995 as a family study at three sites ('The study sites include Ibadan, Nigeria, Kingston, Jamaica, and Maywood, IL.'); its later aim was 'a genome-wide association study of blood pressure/hypertension in 2,000 Nigerians of Yoruban ethnicity'. The tag, and this definition, are the Nigerian genome-wide sample; the curator may prefer a label naming only that sample. Decide it together with sibling D135 'Maywood', Loyola's African American sample from Maywood, Illinois, which the same consortia use beside Nigeria (N'Diaye Text S1: 'DNA samples were obtained from African Americans enrolled in studies of blood pressure at Loyola University in Maywood, IL, USA.'). Tier-E row E524 (ICSHIB, International Collaborative Study on Hypertension in Blacks) is a likely parent (Reder's 'long-term study' cites Cooper et al. 1997, 'The prevalence of hypertension in seven populations of west african origin.'), but no source read names ICSHIB for this sample, so no parent is given. Tier-E row E789 ('Nigerian cohort', PGS id Nigerian) may be this sample. The Idikan participants overlap COHO:0000474 (AADM). Not in COHO.

The project's own GWAS paper (Dai et al. 2019, PMID:31326317; read as the Europe PMC author manuscript, PMC7015703) says NJMU genotyped it on the Illumina Global Screening Array and that it 'included three studies (Nanjing GSA study: 4,149 cases and 3,198 controls from Nanjing and Shanghai; Beijing GSA study: 2,155 cases and 2,035 controls from Beijing and Tianjin; and Guangzhou GSA study: 3,944 cases and 4,065 controls from Guangdong).' The draft also took P2 for a loose later use of the name; P2 is the project's founding paper. The acronyms miss the paper's own 'NJMU GSA project' and 'NJMU GSA'. label: Oxford Parkinson's Disease Centre Discovery Cohort

example quote: The Sisters in Breast Screening Study (SIBS) was designed to study the genetic basis of quantitative phenotypes related to breast cancer, in particular breast density and sex-hormone levels [Varghese et al., 2012; Kataoka et al., 2009].

note: Tier D (D163), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: SIBS, the Sisters in Breast Screening Study, analysed alongside EPIC, UKBGS, NHS and other breast-cancer cohorts. PGS Catalog's name 'Sisters in Breast Screening' omits 'Study'; every evidence unit that spells out the name includes 'study'/'Study', so not added as a separate synonym. iCOGS array genotyping (D163.6) and the EPIC/UKBGS co-mentions are shared-resource/acknowledgement context, not a stated parent relation. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronym, country and example are right. The definition calls a family study 'a cohort of women', leaves out when recruitment began (October 2002, per P1's supplement and Varghese et al. 2012) and that families were also ascertained through newspaper and radio advertisements, and drops the second target phenotype, sex steroid hormone levels, that the study's own description names ('Its aim is the mapping of genes underlying these quantitative traits, specifically mammographic density and sex steroid hormone levels', PMID:20570912). label: St. Jude Lifetime Cohort Study
other synonyms: St Jude Lifetime Cohort Study|St. Jude Lifetime Cohort|St. Jude Lifetime Cohort study
example title: Trans-Ancestral Genetic Risk Factors for Treatment-Related Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Survivors of Childhood Cancer.
example quote: Leveraging whole-genome sequencing data from the St Jude Lifetime Cohort (N = 3,676, 304 clinically ascertained cases), we conducted ancestry-specific genome-wide association studies among survivors of African and European genetic ancestry (AFR and EUR, respectively) followed by trans-ancestry meta-analysis.
definition: A retrospective cohort with prospective follow-up, established in 2007 by St. Jude Children's Research Hospital in Memphis, Tennessee, of survivors of paediatric cancer diagnosed and treated there between 1962 and 2012 who have survived at least five years from diagnosis (until 2015, only adults who had survived ten years), with frequency-matched community controls, who are invited back to the hospital at least every five years for protocol-based medical assessments, patient-reported outcomes and biospecimen collection, to study late health outcomes of childhood cancer and its treatment.
location quote: Childhood cancer survivors were recruited from 8192 survivors diagnosed between 1962 and 2012 with paediatric cancer and treated at St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital in Memphis, TN.
note: Tier D (D164), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: SJLIFE, the St Jude Lifetime Cohort Study, analysed alongside the CCSS Original and Expansion Cohorts for trans-ancestral replication. No non-affiliation unit ties the cohort to a country (the Memphis/Tennessee text, D164.1-2, is the corresponding author's affiliation footnote, excluded by the funder/affiliation rule), so countries is left empty despite SJCRH's evident US location. Several units truncate 'St.' to 'Jude...' (D164.1, D164.4, D164.7, D164.25, D164.35); label instead taken from an intact reference-list quote (D164.16). D164.32 (not cited) gives a narrower 1962-1999 treatment-year range specific to the childhood-ALL sub-study in P3; the broader 1962-2012 range (D164.8-9) is used as it describes the cohort generally. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, acronym and example are right. Label: the cohort's own name has the full stop, 'The St. Jude Lifetime Cohort Study (SJLIFE)' (cohort profile, PMID:33374007; design paper title, PMID:21370418); the PGS/GWAS Catalog spelling 'St Jude Lifetime Cohort Study' becomes a synonym. Definition: 'adult survivors' is out of date (since 2015 survivors of any age five years from diagnosis are eligible; the adult, ten-year rule was the 2007 original), and it leaves out who set the cohort up and where (St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, Memphis), when (2007), the design (retrospective cohort with prospective follow-up, return visits at least every five years, biospecimens) and the community controls; the three participation levels are the 2011 design paper's baseline scheme. Countries: the United States is stated in free text of the cohort profile ('treated at St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital in Memphis, TN'), not only in an affiliation. Example kept (GCST90319324), with the open-access abstract sentence that names the cohort in full instead of the free PDF's replication sentence. No parent: SJLIFE is a single-institution cohort; the Childhood Cancer Survivor Study (D208 CCSS) is a separate multi-institution cohort used alongside it for replication. Tier-E row E1032 'SJCRH' (St. Jude Children's Research Hospital) is not SJLIFE: its PGS source GWAS (GCST000464, PMID:19684603) is a childhood acute lymphoblastic leukaemia susceptibility study of St. Jude patients.

input name: Swedish Low-Risk Colorectal Cancer Study Group

example title: Colorectal cancer risk susceptibility loci in a Swedish population.
definition: A multicentre study in central Sweden of consecutive patients newly diagnosed with colorectal cancer of any stage, recruited between 2004 and 2009 at 14 hospitals by the Swedish Low-Risk Colorectal Cancer Study Group and interviewed on their family history of cancer, with a lifestyle questionnaire for those recruited in 2004–2006 and cancer-free spouses of participants serving as controls; its cases and controls are used in genetic studies of colorectal cancer risk.
note: Tier D (D165), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: not stated in the evidence (its abstract does not name the cohort and no fuller text of P1 was provided). Only one citable unit exists for this name (D165.1), from P2 (PMID:37458848, a 2023 microsatellite-instability prognosis paper), not from P1 (the GWAS paper, PMID:34758156, whose abstract doesn't name the cohort). The GCST example has no quotable unit from a P1-associated source, so ev is null. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity and type are right. The draft's definition is the eligibility rule of one paper's subset (P2, PMID:37458848: stage I–III patients operated on curatively in the Stockholm area in 2002–2006, for a microsatellite-instability prognosis study), not the cohort: the study recruited consecutive, newly diagnosed patients with colorectal cancer of all stages from 14 hospitals in central Sweden in 2004–2009, interviewed them on family history of cancer, gave those recruited in 2004–2006 a lifestyle questionnaire, and used cancer-free spouses as controls (PMID:39543761, PMID:39665592, PMID:39796643, PMID:20648012). Newcomb, and the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences at the National Institutes of Health (grant KL2 TR000421 to A.N. Burnett-Hartman)

note: Tier D (D166), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: Deferred for want of text; research settles it. The Genetics and Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer study descriptions in the supplement of Huyghe et al. 2019 (PMID:30510241, the PGS Catalog's source GWAS for SMS_AD) describe 'Screening Markers for Colorectal Cancer Study (advanced adenomas) (SMS_AD)': enrollees of Group Health Cooperative (now Kaiser Permanente Washington), western Washington State, aged 24–79, who had an index colonoscopy for any indication in 1998–2007, recruited in two phases (1998–2003 and 2004–2007), with adenoma or serrated-polyp cases and polyp-free controls; its advanced-adenoma cases and matched controls were genotyped on the OncoArray. label: Siblings With Ischemic Stroke Study
other synonyms: Siblings with Ischemic Stroke Study|Sibling with Ischemic Stroke Study
example title: Evidence of survival bias in the association between APOE-Є4 and age at ischemic stroke onset.
example quote: The Sibling with Ischemic Stroke Study (SWISS) was supported by the NINDS (R01 NS39987; PI Dr Meschia).
definition: A family-based study of ischaemic stroke that from 1999 to 2011 enrolled, at clinical centres in the United States and Canada, adult probands with radiographically confirmed ischaemic stroke who had at least one living full sibling with stroke, together with their stroke-affected siblings, confirmed by central review of medical records, and where possible a stroke-free sibling, confirmed by structured telephone interview, all contacted through the proband, to search the genome for genetic risk factors for ischaemic stroke by linkage and family-based association analysis.
location quote: The Siblings With Ischemic Stroke Study enrolled 312 probands with ischemic stroke from 70 US and Canadian centers.
parent quote: A total of 4,253 additional CCS-phenotyped cases from 10 GRCs across Europe and the US have been previously genotyped prior to initiating SiGN (BRAINS, EDIN, GASROS, GEOS, ISGS, NHS, MUNICH, OXVASC, ST GEORGE’S, and SWISS).
note: Tier D (D167), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: SWISS, the Siblings With Ischemic Stroke Study, alongside its companion study ISGS (Ischemic Stroke Genetics Study). Evidence spells the name both 'With' (D167.11/14/30, the SWISS papers themselves) and 'with' (PGS Catalog; D167.36/39, a different paper); label follows the SWISS papers' own capitalisation. SWISS used stroke-free participants from BLSA (D167.5) and, for African-ancestry cases, from HANDLS (D167.8) as external controls - a resource relationship, not a parent/membership one, so parent is left null. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronym, countries and example are right. The definition lacks the recruitment years (1999–2011 in the Stroke Genetics Network design paper's table of its centres, PMID:24021684) and describes enrolment loosely: probands were adults with a study-neurologist-confirmed ischaemic stroke; stroke-affected siblings were confirmed by central record review and unaffected siblings by structured telephone interview, all through proband-initiated contact (PMID:11882254, PMID:21940970); the scan finally done was a family-based association analysis as well as linkage. Parent missed: SWISS is one of the genetic research centres of the NINDS Stroke Genetics Network (COHO:0000651), whose design paper lists it among the 24 contributing sites ('SWISS Multi-center, USA Cases with affected siblings 1999–2011'), which is also how P1 (a SiGN analysis) came to use it. Case variants of the name used by the PGS Catalog ('Siblings with Ischemic Stroke Study') and P1's supplement ('Sibling with Ischemic Stroke Study') are added as synonyms. The draft rightly did not treat BLSA (COHO:0000195) or HANDLS (COHO:0000438), which supplied external stroke-free controls, as parents. ISGS (D129) is a separate hospital-based case-control study run by the same investigators and contributes to SiGN alongside SWISS; neither is part of the other.

label: Saguenay Youth Study
example title: Genome-wide analyses of individual differences in quantitatively assessed reading- and language-related skills in up to 34,000 people.
example quote: The Saguenay Youth Study is supported by the CIHR, the Heart and Stroke Foundation of Quebec, and the Canadian Foundation for Innovation.

note: Tier D (D168), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: SYS, the Saguenay Youth Study, one of about twenty cohorts in this multi-cohort reading- and language-skills GWAS. D168.4, a reference-list citation naming an 'SYS Consortium' alongside CHARGE, IMAGEN, ENIGMA and others as contributors to an unrelated cerebral-cortex GWAS paper, does not itself state that the Saguenay Youth Study is a member of ENIGMA or any other umbrella, so no parent is drafted from it. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronym, country, parent (none) and example are right. The definition follows the 2007 design paper only: it omits the recruitment years (2003–2012), recruitment through high schools, the French-Canadian founder-population requirement and the matching of exposed and non-exposed adolescents, and it leaves out the second generation: the cohort profile (PMID:27018016) describes SYS as 'a two-generational study of adolescents and their parents' aimed at 'the aetiology, early stages and trans-generational trajectories of common cardiometabolic and brain diseases', with parents assessed fully in 2012–2015. The country quote is replaced by a sentence of the profile's abstract instead of a structured-abstract 'Setting' line. No parent: the 'SYS Consortium' in the author list of an ENIGMA/CHARGE cortex paper (D168.4) is a contributing-study credit, not membership; ENIGMA (COHO:0000969) and CHARGE (COHO:0000444) are not parents on that evidence. The PGS Catalog has no cohort record for SYS (REST returns none). Not the same as COHO:0000149 'Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean asthma study', a different study in the same region.

label: Translational Genomics Research Institute series 2
note: Tier D (D169), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: TGEN2, the Translational Genomics Research Institute series 2, one of many Alzheimer's disease cohorts in this consensus meta-analysis. Exact match to existing COHO:0000799, which already carries both the GWAS tag/PGS id 'TGEN2' and 'TGEN' as acronyms, and 'TGen series'/'Translational Genomics Research Institute' as synonyms; nothing new to add. TGEN2 in PMID:42237039 is the ADGC dataset already in COHO as COHO:0000799, which carries TGEN2 and TGEN as acronyms and the full name as its label: P1's supplement describes it in the same words as the X-chromosome study that COHO:0000799 was minted from ('TGEN2: Among the TGEN2 data analyzed were 668 clinically- and neuropathologically-characterized brain donors, and 365 CNEs without dementia or significant Alzheimer’s disease pathology.') and lists 'the Translational Genomics Research Institute series 2 (TGEN2) dataset' among the ADGC datasets. The draft's example is valid but should not be added: COHO:0000799 already has a GWAS Catalog example (GCST90449045, PMID:39633006), and COHO allows at most one example per resource. Nothing to add to COHO:0000799: no new acronym or name. The PGS Catalog has no cohort record for TGEN2 (REST returns none).

label: ThyroidOmics Consortium
other synonyms: The ThyroidOmics Consortium
example title: Genome-wide association study and polygenic risk prediction of hypothyroidism.
example quote: The SumHer heritability estimates seem to be quite heterogeneous, e.g., the heritability of TSH in the ThyroidOmics meta-analysis is less than the TSH variance explained by the independent index SNPs in that study.
definition: An international consortium of large, well-phenotyped cohort studies, mostly population-based, formed to study the determinants and effects of thyroid diseases and thyroid function with genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic data, which meta-analyses genome-wide association data from its member cohorts on thyroid-stimulating hormone, free thyroxine, triiodothyronine, thyroid dysfunction and related traits and makes the summary statistics available.
note: Tier D (D170), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ThyroidOmics Consortium as the source cohort/dataset for a thyroid-disorder and reproductive-health shared-genetics study; P2: ThyroidOmics as one of the datasets meta-analysed for a hypothyroidism GWAS and polygenic risk study. Identity and general purpose (a thyroid-trait GWAS meta-analysis consortium, per D170.1's 'ThyroidOmics meta-analysis') are well supported across eight papers, matching the triage 'aggregation?' hint, but no unit lists its member cohorts, founding, governance or location, so drafted as an aggregation without countries or parent. A researcher could confirm composition from P1/P2 full text (not provided here, only abstracts/supplement excerpts). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type (aggregation), label, acronym and example are right, and leaving countries empty is right for a consortium whose collaborating cohorts span Europe, North America, Australia and Japan (its cohort list). The definition was assembled from Mendelian randomization papers that used the consortium's summary statistics: it says what the consortium's meta-analyses cover but not what the consortium is. Its own description: 'The ThyroidOmics Consortium was formed to study the determinants and effects of thyroid diseases and thyroid function, using various omics technologies in multiple large and well-phenotyped cohort studies' (website), and its GWAS meta-analyses pool 'predominantly population-based cohorts from the ThyroidOmics Consortium' (PMID:38291025). The PGS Catalog name 'The ThyroidOmics Consortium' is added as a synonym. The PGS Catalog has no cohort record for ThyroidOmics (REST returns none). The website's 'Collaborating Cohorts, Studies, and Consortia' list (about 60 entries, including SHIP, the Rotterdam Study, HUNT, MGI, FHS, ARIC, TwinsUK, LifeLines, BioBank Japan, the Copenhagen Hospital Biobank and the Danish Blood Donor Study) could supply hasCohort links; many are already in COHO. The example quote is a reviewer's comment in P2's peer-review file, the only text of either GWAS paper that could be read and that names the consortium.

input name: Treatment Options for Type 2 Diabetes in Adolescents and Youth
label: Treatment Options for Type 2 Diabetes in Adolescents and Youth
other synonyms: Treatment Options for type 2 Diabetes in Adolescents and Youth
example title: Genome-wide Association Study of Lipid Traits in Youth With Type 2 Diabetes.
example quote: We genotyped 206 928 variants and imputed 17 642 824 variants in 1076 youth (mean age 15.0 ± 2.48 years) with T2D from the Treatment Options for Type 2 Diabetes in Adolescents and Youth (TODAY) and SEARCH for Diabetes in Youth (SEARCH) studies as part of the Progress in Diabetes Genetics in Youth (ProDiGY) consortium.
definition: A multicentre randomized clinical trial funded by the US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases that from 2004 to 2009 enrolled children and adolescents aged 10–17 years with type 2 diabetes of less than two years' duration, a body-mass index at or above the 85th percentile and no diabetes autoantibodies at 15 clinical centres in the United States, and compared metformin alone with metformin plus rosiglitazone or plus an intensive lifestyle intervention for durable glycaemic control until 2011; its participants were then followed into adulthood in the observational TODAY2 study (2011–2020).
location quote: Briefly, 699 participants, 10 to 17 years old, diagnosed with type 2 diabetes by American Diabetes Association criteria, with duration 2 years or less, body mass index (BMI) ≥ 85th percentile for age and sex, were enrolled across 15 clinical centers in the United States
note: Tier D (D171), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: TODAY, the Treatment Options for Type 2 Diabetes in Adolescents and Youth trial, analysed alongside SEARCH for Diabetes in Youth as the ProDiGY consortium. NIH sponsorship (D171.30) is a funder mention, not used to assert a country per the funder-exclusion rule, and no unit otherwise states where TODAY recruited, so countries is left empty. TODAY and SEARCH are described as combined 'as part of' the ProDiGY consortium (D171.1) for this genetic sub-study, but ProDiGY is neither a candidate COHO term nor a tier-D row in this batch, so no parent is drafted; a researcher could check whether ProDiGY itself warrants a term. P8's abstract (D171.101) renders the name/acronym as 'TOD2AY', an apparent typo, not added as a synonym or acronym. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type and example are right. The definition is the 2007 design paper's plan ('recruited over a four-year period', 'followed for two to six years') rather than what the study became: enrolment ran from July 2004 to February 2009 and the trial ended in February 2011 (PMID:22540912), at 15 clinical centres in the United States, after which the same participants were followed in the observational TODAY2 study in 2011–2020 (PMID:38815053); it also leaves out the eligibility criteria that define the cohort (BMI at or above the 85th percentile, negative diabetes autoantibodies). Countries: the United States was missed; an open-access TODAY paper states it ('enrolled across 15 clinical centers in the United States'). TODAY2, the name of the cohort's follow-up phase, is added as an acronym, and the lower-case 'type 2' spelling of the name (PMID:40566988) as a synonym. No parent in COHO: the Progress in Diabetes Genetics in Youth (ProDiGY) consortium, in which TODAY and SEARCH for Diabetes in Youth (COHO:0000882) were genotyped together ('composed of participants originally enrolled in 2 different pediatric studies: the TODAY study and the SEARCH study', PMID:34568709), is neither in COHO nor a row of this review; if ProDiGY is minted as an aggregation, TODAY and COHO:0000882 are its members. 'TOD2AY' (PMID:19244566 abstract) is a typographical variant and is not added.

label: Tracking Parkinson's
other synonyms: Parkinson's repository of biosamples and networked datasets
example title: Genome-wide determinants of mortality and motor progression in Parkinson's disease.
example quote: Tracking Parkinson’s is a longitudinal, prospective, multi-centre observational study in the UK51.
definition: A prospective, multicentre, longitudinal epidemiological and biomarker study of Parkinson's disease in the United Kingdom, funded by Parkinson's UK, that recruited patients aged 18–90 with a clinical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease of recent onset (diagnosed within the preceding 3.5 years) or young onset (diagnosed at or before age 50) at 72 National Health Service secondary-care sites, together with unaffected siblings of patients, and follows them with repeated motor, non-motor and quality-of-life assessments, genotyping and biosamples, to explain variation in the clinical phenotype of Parkinson's disease, including its relation to genetic variation.
location quote: Patients were recruited at 72 secondary healthcare centres that are part of the UK National Health Service.

P1 (Sub-Saharan-African kidney-disease GWAS, PMID 38812969): ARK = the African Research on/Kidney Disease study, a South African population cohort from Agincourt, one of two Sub-Saharan-African cohorts (with AWI-Gen) contributing urinary albumin-creatinine-ratio GWAS data alongside UK Biobank and CKDGen. Two name forms appear: 'African Research on Kidney Disease' (with 'on': D192.10, D192.31, likely the study's own original name per its design-paper citation Kalyesubula et al. 2020) versus 'African Research Kidney Disease study' (no 'on': D192.13, matching the PGS Catalog's stored name exactly) - used the 'on' form as label since it recurs independently in two sources including a clean, self-contained definitional sentence (D192.31), and kept the other as a synonym. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym and example are right, but the definition described only the South African arm that P1 used ('ARK-Agincourt'). The design paper (PMID:31941441) says 'The African Research on Kidney Disease (ARK) study is a three-country study embedded within existing cohorts': Uganda's General Population Cohort, the MEIRU sites in Karonga and Lilongwe in Malawi, and the Agincourt HDSS in South Africa. So the countries are incomplete: Uganda and Malawi were missing. Malawi has no entry in gaz_xrefs.tsv, so it cannot be asserted until one is added. The design paper's title spells the name 'African Research into Kidney Diseases (ARK) study', and I added that form. No single parent: ARK sampled from three host cohorts. Two are COHO terms: the Agincourt HDSS (COHO:0000912; the South African arm is 'an age and gender stratified random sample of 2250 members of the rural Agincourt HDSS') and the Uganda General Population Cohort (COHO:0000345). MEIRU (Malawi) is not in COHO. To assert Malawi, add dbpedia:Malawi to gaz_xrefs.tsv; quote: the PMID:35839814 abstract sentence above. note: Tier D (D194), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P8-P10 (found by name): BACS's own amyloid-PET/cognition sub-studies (D194.86-92), the source of the longitudinal design details used in the definition. The United States was withheld because 'Berkeley' seemed ambiguous, but a BACS description places its participants in the San Francisco Bay Area. example quote: Here, we aimed to identify genetic variants associated with host susceptibility to Campylobacter infection using two well-characterized birth cohorts: the Performance of Rotavirus and Oral Polio Vaccines in Developing Countries (PROVIDE) Study (19) and the Cryptosporidiosis Birth Cohort (CBC) (20).
definition: A prospective birth cohort of children enrolled within a week of birth between June 2014 and March 2016 in Mirpur, an urban neighbourhood of Dhaka, and Mirzapur, a rural subdistrict north-west of Dhaka, Bangladesh, whose mothers were identified in the second trimester of pregnancy. The children were followed with twice-weekly home visits for diarrhoea, monthly stool samples and three-monthly growth measurements, to study the incidence of cryptosporidiosis, the immune response to it, host genetic susceptibility and its effect on child growth.
location quote: To identify host genetic risk factors associated with astrovirus disease susceptibility that may explain disease mechanism and vaccine targets, we performed genome-wide association studies in children enrolled in 2 birth cohorts, the Performance of Rotavirus and Oral Polio Vaccines in Developing Countries (PROVIDE) study and the Cryptosporidiosis and Enteropathogens in Bangladesh Birth Cohort (CBC) study in Dhaka, Bangladesh [15, 16].
note: Tier D (D206), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CBC (given as 'Cryptosporidiosis Birth Cohort'), used alongside PROVIDE for a Campylobacter GWAS; P2: CBC (fuller form 'Cryptosporidiosis and Enteropathogens in Bangladesh Birth Cohort', matching the PGS Catalog name), used for an astrovirus GWAS. Same cohort. Two name forms for the same cohort: P1 uses the shorter 'Cryptosporidiosis Birth Cohort', P2 and the PGS Catalog use the fuller name. Both describe the same Mirpur/Mirzapur, Bangladesh birth cohort recruited alongside PROVIDE. Checked 2026-09-23: The definition says the children were enrolled from 2014 to 2018, but 2014-2018 is P2's period of home visits. The children were enrolled within a week of birth between June 2014 and March 2016, and follow-up in Mirpur was later extended to age 5. The definition also leaves out that the mothers were identified in pregnancy, and it gives only one of the study's aims. The other aims were the acquired immune response and host genetic susceptibility. The synonyms lack the study's own registered name, 'Cryptosporidiosis and Enteropathogens in Bangladesh' (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02764918), which the design paper also uses. CBC is not in COHO. PROVIDE (D289) and the Dhaka Birth Cohort are separate birth cohorts from the same Mirpur area. The ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT02764918 has since been updated for a new enrolment starting in October 2024 (an estimated 150 mother-child pairs from Mirpur), so its current dates and size are not those of the 2014-2016 cohort.

Tier D (D207), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: cases from the Cleveland Clinic Foundation (CCF), combined with University of Michigan/MGI patients as the joint 'UM/CCF' or 'UM-MGI/CCF' fibromuscular-dysplasia case-control study; P2: cases and controls contributed by Cleveland Clinic Foundation alongside National Jewish Health and the GRADS consortium for a sarcoidosis GWAS. CCF = Cleveland Clinic Foundation, the hospital. P1 and P2 use it only as part of joint study names ('UM/CCF', 'UM-MGI/CCF') or as one of several contributing institutions, never as a standalone named cohort/sample collection. P9-P14 (found by name) are about the institution generally (a 1953 staff radiation survey, a case series, bibliometric analyses naming it a leading institution), confirming it denotes the hospital, not a defined sample. Checked 2026-09-23: Nothing wrong with the verdict; one detail to add. In P1 the tag means the Cleveland Clinic cases of the 'University of Michigan/Cleveland Clinic Foundation (UM/CCF) study'. These fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) patients were enrolled consecutively at the Cleveland Clinic's FMD referral clinic; the paper's funding note names the Cleveland Clinic FMD Biorepository, and the study's controls came from MGI. The CCF tag does not name one cohort. Two named samples lie behind it: the UM/CCF FMD case-control study (P1) and the Cleveland Clinic FMD Biorepository. Either could get a term of its own if a tag ever names it. CCF is none of the review's other Cleveland Clinic rows: D097 CCAF (Cleveland Clinic AF Study) and E172/E173 CCGB (Cleveland Clinic GeneBank). Checked 2026-09-23: The definition takes one paper's recruitment window (October 2000 to October 2006, from the 2008 JAMA abstract) and omits what the study is: twins and siblings who all have CF, with their parents, recruited by Johns Hopkins to find genetic and environmental modifiers of CF outcomes. It also leaves out a design feature the CHAP design paper stresses: successive age cohorts of residents were entered as they turned 65. P1 is an Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Consortium (COHO:0000518) analysis, but no source read here says CHAP is a member of ADGC, so no parent is given. definition: A multicentre, population-based cohort of adults aged 20 to 44 years who were selected at random from population registers in 1990-1994 in centres mainly in Western Europe, and also in Australia, New Zealand, the United States and elsewhere, and surveyed with a standardised protocol (a screening questionnaire, then a clinical examination of a random subsample and of those reporting asthma symptoms) to compare the prevalence of asthma and allergic disease, their risk factors and their treatment across countries. Those examined were followed up in ECRHS II (1998-2002), ECRHS III (2008-2014) and ECRHS IV (from 2021) to study the incidence and prognosis of asthma and allergy, lung function decline and COPD.
location quote: This investigation included 24 centres from 11 countries: Iceland (Reykjavik), Norway (Bergen), Sweden (Gothenburg, Umeå and Uppsala), Estonia (Tartu), Germany (Erfurt and Hamburg), UK (Ipswich and Norwich), Belgium (Antwerp), France (Bordeaux, Grenoble, Montpellier and Paris), Spain (Albacete, Barcelona, Galdakao, Huelva and Oviedo), Italy (Pavia, Torino and Verona) and Australia (Melbourne). || We gathered data from the 30 centres within regions: United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland), northern Europe (Iceland, Norway, Sweden), central Europe (Belgium, France, the Netherlands), southern Europe (Italy and Spain), Australia and New Zealand, and United States (Portland was the only area in the United States). || No estimate for Melbourne, Australia or Basel, Switzerland, as information on asthma medication use was not recorded during postal survey. || Until now (December 2025) data for ECRHS IV has been collected in 7 countries with clinical investigations (Denmark, Norway, Estonia, Sweden, Iceland, Spain, Australia) and one country with questionnaire data only (United kingdom).
note: Tier D (D218), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ECRHS, tagged among many other cohorts (ALSPAC, B58C, BAMSE, CATSS, CHOP, DNBC, FINNGEN, etc.) in a multi-ancestry atopic dermatitis meta-analysis. D218.5 describes eligibility for this GWAS's own genotyped subset (selected via GABRIEL centres), so it was left out of definition_ev to avoid describing one paper's subset. No unit gives ECRHS's recruiting countries or a founding date despite it being a European multicentre survey, so countries is empty. Checked 2026-09-23: The definition restates one abstract's phrasing and leaves out who was sampled (adults aged 20-44 selected at random from population registers), when (1990-1994), where (centres mainly in Western Europe, also in Australia, New Zealand and the United States), the two-stage design and the survey's purpose (comparing asthma and allergy prevalence, risk factors and treatment across countries with a standardised protocol). It also says the cohort was followed up twice, but a fourth wave, ECRHS IV, began in 2021. Countries were left empty although the survey's own papers and website name them. The example quote begins with the DNBC genotyping acknowledgement and runs across the page number and the heading 'ECHRS Recruitment'; it is replaced by the supplement's ECRHS eligibility sentence from the same paper. ECRHS I had centres in 25 countries (website), and other countries whose centres took part only in ECRHS I (for example Greece, Portugal, Austria and India, which appear in the funding and centre lists of PMC6355980 and PMC119432) are not given here because no open-access sentence found states recruitment there. In the colorectal cancer GWAS of GECCO, 'EDRN' is the set of colorectal cancer cases and age- and sex-matched controls from the University of Pittsburgh's EDRN Colorectal and Pancreatic Neoplasm Virtual Biorepository. example title: Genetic modifiers of body mass index in individuals with cystic fibrosis.
example quote: The Cystic Fibrosis Genome Project (CFGP) is comprised of individuals with CF recruited by the CF Twin and Sibling Study (TSS)15 and Cystic Fibrosis-Related Diabetes (CFRD) Study16 (Johns Hopkins University), Genetic Modifier Study (GMS)17,18,19 and GMS of Severe CF Liver Disease (GMS CFLD)20,21 (University of North Carolina), and Early Pseudomonas Infection Control Observational (EPIC Obs) Study22 (University of Washington and Seattle Children’s Hospital).
definition: A prospective, multicentre observational cohort of children with cystic fibrosis aged 12 years or younger who were free of Pseudomonas aeruginosa at enrolment (no earlier positive respiratory culture, or at least two years of negative cultures) or were taking part in the companion Early Pseudomonas Infection Control clinical trial, enrolled in 2004-2006 at 59 cystic fibrosis care centres in the United States and led from the University of Washington and Seattle Children's Hospital. Participants were followed through encounter-based data collection built on the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation Patient Registry, annual family surveys, respiratory cultures and banked serum, bacterial isolates and DNA, to identify risk factors for early acquisition of P. aeruginosa and to describe its clinical consequences.
location quote: To identify novel risk factors and corroborate previously identified risk factors for mean annual decline in FEV1% predicted in a large, contemporary, United States cohort of young cystic fibrosis (CF) patients.
note: Tier D (D221), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: EPIC_Obs, one of the constituent CF studies comprising the Cystic Fibrosis Genome Project (CFGP), tagged alongside CFRD, CF_TSS, GMS, GMS_CFLD. D221.1 (P1 full text, free access) names EPIC_Obs as one of CFGP's constituent studies, run by University of Washington/Seattle Children's Hospital; no unit states a country/place name directly, so (consistent with how the CFRD entry elsewhere in this review left countries empty despite naming Johns Hopkins University) countries is left empty here too. CFGP itself is not among this batch's candidate COHO terms or rows, so parent is left null. Candidate COHO:0000627 'Trinity Student Study' (acronym TSS) is unrelated: a false match on the different 'CF Twin and Sibling Study (TSS)' named in the same sentence. Checked 2026-09-23: The definition says the children were enrolled by the University of Washington and Seattle Children's Hospital, which led the study, but they were enrolled at 59 CF care centres across the United States. It gives neither the age limit (12 or younger), the entry criterion (free of P. aeruginosa, or in the companion EPIC trial), the enrolment years (2004-2006) nor the purpose (risk factors for, and outcomes of, early P. aeruginosa acquisition); 'followed over at least four years' is one paper's analysis window, and membership of the Cystic Fibrosis Genome Project is a later use of its DNA, not what the study is. The country was left empty although EPIC papers call it a 'United States cohort' and the 'U.S. EPIC Observational Study'. The design paper's acronym 'EPIC-OBS' was missing. The example quote was taken from the PDF, with hyphenation breaks, and ran across the headings 'Subjects and methods' and 'Study cohorts'; it is replaced by the same sentence from P1's PMC page, as for D211 and D212. Not in COHO. The EPIC Observational Study and the EPIC clinical trial (EPIC-CT) were companion studies of the Early Pseudomonas Infection Control programme; trial participants could also be enrolled in the observational study. 'EPIC' alone is not given as an acronym: it names the whole programme (and P1 uses it only in its IRB list), and it is also the acronym of the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer (COHO:0000065). As for D211 and D212, the Cystic Fibrosis Genome Project would be an aggregation of TSS (D212), CFRD (D211), GMS (D236), GMS_CFLD (D237) and EPIC_Obs; it is neither in COHO nor in this review, so the parent is left null.

example quote: Participants were members of E-Risk, which tracks the development of a 1994-95 birth cohort of
definition: A nationally representative birth cohort of same-sex twins born in England and Wales in 1994-1995, drawn from a birth register of twins and recruited to represent UK families with newborns in the 1990s (ensuring enough children in disadvantaged homes and avoiding an excess of twins born to well-educated women after assisted reproduction). Proposed in 1997, funded by the Medical Research Council from 1998 and based at King's College London, it assessed the families at home when the twins were 5 (1999-2000), 7, 10, 12 and 18 years old, surveyed them online in their mid-twenties and planned a further assessment at age 30 for 2024-2025, to study how environmental and genetic factors contribute to behaviour, health and mental health problems from childhood into adulthood.
location quote: The Environmental Risk Longitudinal Twin Study (E-Risk) comprised 2163 twin children from England and Wales (49.1% male) identified at birth in 1994 and 1995 and included administration of the Test of Word Reading Efficiency at age 7 years and the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence-Revised as a test of IQ at age 5 years.
note: Tier D (D222), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: E-Risk, tagged in a childhood ADHD GWAS meta-analysis; the abstract does not describe the cohort. P1 abstract doesn't name the cohort and no P1 supplement/fulltext was given, so example ev is null; identity and definition rest on P2-P7, which consistently describe the same nationally representative 1994-1995 England-and-Wales twin birth cohort followed to age 18. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym and country are right. The definition leaves out that the twins are same-sex pairs drawn from a birth register and recruited to represent UK families with newborns in the 1990s, that the cohort was constructed and first assessed at age 5 (1999-2000), the MRC funding and home base, the later assessments (an online survey at 24-26 and a planned assessment at 30, so not only 'to age 18') and the study's aim. The draft said P1 does not name the cohort and gave no example quote, but P1's free Supplementary Information has an E-Risk paragraph; its first sentence gives the example quote, cut before the PDF's margin line number. Not in COHO. The 'larger birth register of twins born in England and Wales in 1994–1995' from which E-Risk drew its families is cited to the design paper of the Twins Early Development Study (COHO:0000173) (PMC12220285, reference 39, PMID:12537874), but E-Risk is a separately recruited and separately followed sample, so no parent is given. The draft's country quote (from P3's abstract, naming England and Wales) is kept; the website's sentence would serve equally.

The preprint of P1 (medRxiv 10.1101/2023.06.18.23291407) says the controls were 'ancestry-matched controls with available WGS data ... selected from the GenomeAsia, Phase 2 (GAsPh2) reference cohort', citing the GenomeAsia 100K pilot paper and the GAsP2 paper (PMID:37291107). If the curator keeps GAsP2 on it, the definition could add Phase 2, and South Asian countries could be added: 'Here we describe whole genome sequence (WGS) data from 4806 individuals recruited from the healthcare delivery systems of Pakistan, India and Bangladesh, combined with WGS from 927 individuals from isolated South Asian populations.' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC10250394/fullTextXML). example title: Multi-ancestry meta-analysis identifies 5 novel loci for ischemic stroke and reveals heterogeneity of effects between sexes and ancestries.
example quote: We performed a genome-wide meta-analysis of 16 biobanks across multiple ancestries to study the genetics of ischemic stroke (60,176 cases, 1,310,725 controls) as part of the Global Biobank Meta-analysis Initiative (GBMI) and further combined the results with previously published MegaStroke.
definition: A collaborative network of biobanks and genomics initiatives, formed in 2019 by 23 biobanks from four continents (North America, Europe, East and West Asia, and Australia) and since joined by others, whose participants have genotypes linked to electronic health records or other health data. Member biobanks run genome-wide association studies with harmonised phenotype definitions and methods, stratified by ancestry and sex, and GBMI meta-analyses the summary statistics across biobanks and ancestries, beginning with 14 diseases and endpoints, and releases them publicly, to increase the power and ancestral diversity of genetic studies of human disease.

Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, example and the empty country list (a network of biobanks on several continents; countries belong to its members) are right. The definition is generic: it leaves out that GBMI is a standing network of member biobanks (formed in 2019 by 23 biobanks on four continents, now 31 biobanks and initiatives), that each member runs ancestry- and sex-stratified GWAS with harmonised phenotype definitions whose summary statistics GBMI meta-analyses and releases, and its first set of 14 endpoints. definition: Patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) enrolled in the LNH03 (LNH 2003) programme of treatment trials of the Groupe d'Etude des Lymphomes de l'Adulte (GELA, later the Lymphoma Study Association, LYSA), who consented to DNA analysis. The patients' germline DNA was genotyped as the case series of GELA's genome-wide association study of DLBCL, with controls drawn from the French component of EPIC.
location quote: Patients were included from 38 centres in France and Belgium.
note: Tier D (D227), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft makes the cooperative group itself (GELA, the French adult lymphoma trials group, now LYSA) an aggregation. The tag names a patient sample: the DLBCL patients of GELA's LNH03 trial programme who consented to DNA analysis, genotyped as cases (with French EPIC participants as controls) in the GELA/EPIC GWAS. Cerhan et al. 2014 (PMID:25261932), the source GWAS of the PGS Catalog's GELA scores, names the study 'Treatment program of DLBCL patients from the Groupe d'Etude des Lymphomes de l'Adulte (GELA) consisting in LNH03-1B, 2B, 3B, 39B, 6B and 7B' and says 'The GELA study was conducted on cases only'. That study name, which the PGS Catalog took over, becomes the label, and the type is cohort. The draft said it was not stated which trials contributed the cases; Cerhan et al.'s table lists them (LNH03-1B, 2B, 3B, 39B, 6B and 7B), and P1 cites their trial reports as the sample's references. Countries were left empty although the trials recruited in France and Belgium. Not in COHO. The PGS Catalog's name drops the apostrophes ('Groupe dEtude des Lymphomes de lAdulte'); that exact string is kept as a synonym for matching, and the label uses the source paper's spelling. ClinicalTrials.gov also lists Swiss sites for LNH03-6B, but no open-access sentence found names Switzerland, so it is not given. The cooperative group (GELA/LYSA) runs trials rather than collecting cohorts, so no parent is given. EPIC (COHO:0000065) supplied the controls and is not a parent. ENGELA (review key E302) is a separate French hospital-based case-control study.

example quote: The Genetic and Environmental Risk Factors for Alzheimer’s Disease Among African Americans (GenerAAtions) Study.
definition: A case-control study of Alzheimer's disease in community-dwelling African Americans aged 65 or older, led from Johns Hopkins University, whose participants were identified through the electronic claims database of the Henry Ford Health System in Detroit, Michigan, and had a proxy informant; cases met NINCDS-ADRDA criteria for possible or probable Alzheimer's disease at a consensus conference, and controls were cognitively normal.
note: Tier D (D228), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the GenerAAtions cohort, community-dwelling African Americans recruited via the Henry Ford Health System for the study of genetic and environmental risk factors for Alzheimer's disease. The definition restated the eligibility sentence but left out that GenerAAtions is a case-control study (cases and cognitively normal controls), that it was led from Johns Hopkins University, and that participants were found through the Henry Ford Health System's electronic claims database in Detroit. Country from the name (African Americans); the only place quote is PMID:20697030's 'Populations not of Caucasian descent included African American subjects from several ADCs, a community-based (Detroit) study of AD, and the MIRAGE study' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3048805/), which does not name GenerAAtions but refers to it.
