input name: Gene Environment Interaction and Breast Cancer in Germany
label: Gene Environment Interaction and Breast Cancer in Germany
other synonyms: Gene-ENvironment Interaction and breast CAncer|gene environment interaction and breast cancer|Gene Environment Interactions and Breast Cancer study
example title: Genome-wide interaction analysis of menopausal hormone therapy use and breast cancer risk among 62,370 women.
example quote: The GENICA was funded by the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) Germany grants 01KW9975/5, 01KW9976/8, 01KW9977/0 and 01KW0114, the Robert Bosch Foundation, Stuttgart, Deutsches Krebsforschungszentrum (DKFZ), Heidelberg, the Institute for Prevention and Occupational Medicine of the German Social Accident Insurance, Institute of the Ruhr University Bochum (IPA), Bochum, as well as the Department of Internal Medicine, Evangelische Kliniken Bonn gGmbH, Johanniter Krankenhaus, Bonn, Germany.
definition: A population-based case-control study of breast cancer in women of the Greater Bonn region, Germany, run by the GENICA network of German research institutions, in which incident cases, enrolled from all hospitals of the region in 2000–2004 within six months of diagnosis, and controls drawn from the population registries of 31 communities of the region and matched in five-year age classes were interviewed and gave blood, to study how genes and environmental exposures interact in breast cancer.
location quote: Three studies were from Germany: the Bavarian Breast Cancer Cases and Controls Collection (BBCC), the Gene Environment Interactions and Breast Cancer study (GENICA), and the Mammary Carcinoma Risk Factor Investigation (MARIE).
parent quote: BCAC DACC approval is required to access data from studies ABCFS, ABCS, ABCTB, BBCC, BBCS, BCEES, BCFR-NY, BCFR-PA, BCFR-UT, BCINIS, BSUCH, CBCS, CECILE, CGPS, CTS, DIETCOMPLYF, ESTHER, GC-HBOC, GENICA, GEPARSIXTO, GESBC, HABCS, HCSC, HEBCS, HMBCS, HUBCS, KARBAC, KBCP, LMBC, MABCS, MARIE, MBCSG, MCBCS, MISS, MMHS, MTLGEBCS, NC-BCFR, OFBCR, ORIGO, pKARMA, POSH, PREFACE, RBCS, SKKDKFZS, SUCCESSB, SUCCESSC, SZBCS, TNBCC, UCIBCS, UKBGS and UKOPS (see Supplementary Table 1).
note: Tier D (D229), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred for want of a design description; research settles it. GENICA is a population-based case-control study of breast cancer in the Greater Bonn region, Germany: incident cases enrolled from all hospitals of the region in 2000–2004 and population-registry controls from 31 communities (PMID:23781229 Table 1; PMID:25229211; PMID:23543199; PMID:20039012). Its name, 'Gene Environment Interaction and Breast Cancer in Germany', is the PGS Catalog name and is used by BCAC papers (PMID:23781229, PMID:24887515). It is a BCAC study (COHO:0000020). The draft's example GCST90129576 had no quote, though the GWAS paper's funding sentence names GENICA (D229.4). The design papers cited for GENICA (Pesch et al. 2005; Justenhoven et al. 2008) are closed and were not read; the definition rests on the open BCAC table and GENICA abstracts. A different, cardiological 'GENICA study' of coronary heart disease patients exists in the literature (PMID:12651036, PMID:14508233); it is not in COHO and no catalog tag uses it, so no editor note is needed. MARIE (D264), the other German population-based case-control study, is a separate review name.

label: Genizon GWAS
other synonyms: Genizon BioSciences
example title: Multi-ancestry genome-wide meta-analysis with 472,819 individuals identifies 32 novel risk loci for psoriasis.
example quote: Currently published GWASs include eight Europe-originated psoriasis-associated GWAS cohorts, including CASP [7], Kiel [8], Genizon [8], PsA GWAS [9], WTCCC2 [10], Exomechip [11], PAGE [12], and GAPC [12], two South Asia-originated psoriasis-associated GWAS cohort including three batches [13], and one East Asia-originated psoriasis-associated GWAS cohort [14].
definition: A case-control sample of people with psoriasis, ascertained through dermatologists or other secondary-care specialists, and controls, all drawn from the Québec founder population (people whose four grandparents had French-Canadian family names and were born in Québec or neighbouring areas), assembled by Genizon BioSciences of Saint-Laurent, Québec, and genotyped genome-wide on the Illumina Human 1M BeadChip; it is one of the European-ancestry GWAS datasets of the international psoriasis genetics meta-analyses.
location quote: The Kiel sample included 471 cases and 1,129 controls, and the Genizon data from Canada included 1,755 samples.
note: Tier D (D230), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred; research settles it. The tag is not the company but its psoriasis GWAS dataset: in the paper both GWAS studies cite for it (PMID:20953188, PMC3136364), replication panel D is 'Genizon', and 'The Canadian population sample used for panel D consisted of 762 psoriasis patients and 994 controls, sampled from the Québec founder population (QFP)', genotyped on the Illumina Human 1M BeadChip by Genizon BioSciences authors. Later meta-analyses call it 'Genizon GWAS' (PMID:25939698, 28537254, 34927100) or 'the Genizon data from Canada' (PMID:25903422). It is a defined, named case-control sample, so a cohort. The draft's example quote was the bare table cell 'Genizon'; the same paper's full text names it in a sentence. No own name beyond 'Genizon'; 'Genizon GWAS' is the fullest verbatim form, used by three meta-analyses. The PGS Catalog name 'Genizon BioSciences' is the company (Saint-Laurent, Québec) and is kept as a synonym only because the Catalog tags it; drop it if company names are not wanted as synonyms. Related to but not the same people as COHO:0000979 'Quebec Founder Population cohort', which is defined as Genizon's Alzheimer's disease case-control sample from the same founder population; a curator could broaden COHO:0000979 into Genizon's Québec founder population collection and make this a sub-cohort, but as the two terms are now defined neither contains the other, so no parent is given. Sibling datasets in the same meta-analyses: CASP (D204), KIEL (D258), BSTOP (D201), GAPC (D425).

input name: Genetic Studies in Nuclear Families with Atopic Dermatitis
label: GEnetic analysis of NUclear Families with Atopic Dermatitis
other synonyms: GEnetic studies in NUclear Families with Atopic Dermatitis|Genetic Analysis of Nuclear Families with Atopic Dermatitis|Genetic Studies in Nuclear Families with Atopic Dermatitis|GENUFAD study
example title: European and multi-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of atopic dermatitis highlights importance of systemic immune regulation.
example quote: Children of the extended GENUFAD study were unrelated individuals recruited based on moderate to severe atopic dermatitis and an age of onset below two years.
definition: A family-based genetic study of atopic dermatitis run from Charité Universitätsmedizin Berlin, which recruited complete nuclear families, mostly German and a few Swedish, through at least two children with physician-diagnosed, moderate to severe atopic dermatitis that began before the age of two, and in its extended phase also unrelated children with such early-onset disease, recording asthma and hay fever at recruitment, for genetic studies of atopic dermatitis and allergic disease.
location quote: The GENUFAD study contributed 522 complete German nuclear families to the Central European study and 32 Swedish families to the Northern European data set.
note: Tier D (D232), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the GENUFAD family cohort recruited at Charité Universitätsmedizin Berlin, analysed here as two batches ('GENUFADext' and 'GENUFAD (SHIP2)') against two different SHIP control tranches; P2: the same GENUFAD cohort, used as an independent replication sample for an eczema-associated variant. The PGS Catalog name 'Genetic Studies in Nuclear Families with Atopic Dermatitis' is close to but not an exact match of either evidenced expansion (D232.7's 'analysis of', D232.13's 'studies in'); used the closer, standalone D232.7 form as label. 'GENUFADext'/'(SHIP2)' are internal QC/control-set batch labels within one paper, not separate cohort names, so not added as acronyms. Controls for the SHIP2 batch come from the existing SHIP cohort (COHO:0000202), not from GENUFAD itself. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym and example study are right. The definition described only the 2009 GWAS family set (families ascertained through two affected siblings) and restated the name as its purpose; GENUFAD also has an extended phase of unrelated children with early-onset moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (the 'GENUFADext' set of the same GWAS), physician diagnosis, and asthma and hay fever recorded at recruitment (PMID:29083406, PMID:37794016). The countries missed Sweden: 'The GENUFAD study contributed 522 complete German nuclear families to the Central European study and 32 Swedish families to the Northern European data set' (PMID:25757221). The example quote is replaced by a cleaner sentence from the same supplement; the draft's was verbatim but run together. Label kept in its acronym-forming capitals, as COHO does for other such names; the plain-case form is a synonym. The batch labels GENUFADext, GENUFAD (SHIP1), GENUFAD (SHIP2) and GENUFAD-SHIP-1/-2 are analysis sets (GENUFAD cases with SHIP controls, COHO:0000202), not names of the cohort, so they are not added. The 2000 linkage study's co-authors include Rome clinicians, so early families may also have come from Italy, but no text read says so. No clash in COHO or the review.

label: German Myocardial Infarction Family Study
other synonyms: German MI Family Study|German Myocardial Infarction Family Studies|German MI Family Studies
example title: Discovery and systematic characterization of risk variants and genes for coronary artery disease in over a million participants.
example quote: The GerMIFS V cases consist of patients referred for coronary angiography, classified as MI cases, from Germany (5).
definition: A series of German case collections for genetic studies of myocardial infarction and coronary artery disease, numbered GerMIFS I to VII, that began as a family study recruiting, from all parts of Germany, people with myocardial infarction before the age of 60 and relatives with premature coronary artery disease. Later collections added patients with early-onset myocardial infarction, non-fatal myocardial infarction cases from the KORA registry of the Augsburg region, and patients with coronary artery disease or myocardial infarction referred for coronary angiography, mostly compared with population controls from other German studies.
location quote: The GerMIFS V cases consist of patients referred for coronary angiography, classified as MI cases, from Germany (5).
parent quote: CARDIoGRAM combines data from all published and several unpublished GWAS in individuals with European ancestry; includes >22 000 cases with CAD, MI, or both and >60 000 controls; and unifies samples from the Atherosclerotic Disease VAscular functioN and genetiC Epidemiology study, CADomics, Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology, deCODE, the German Myocardial Infarction Family Studies I, II, and III, Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Heath Study/AtheroRemo, MedStar, Myocardial Infarction Genetics Consortium, Ottawa Heart Genomics Study, PennCath, and the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium.
note: Tier D (D233), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity and label are right, but the draft defined GerMIFS by its later angiography collections only (V–VII, plus IV). GerMIFS is a numbered series of separately recruited case collections, 'the German Myocardial Infarction Family Studies I, II, and III' (PMID:20923989) and later IV–VII, each analysed as its own study (GerMIFS5, GerMIFS6 and GerMIFS7 in the GWAS paper's direction column). It began as a family study of people with myocardial infarction before 60 and affected first-degree relatives, recruited from all parts of Germany (PMID:17634449, PMID:18398472); GerMIFS II took early-onset MI patients, GerMIFS III non-fatal MI cases from the KORA registry (PMID:26343387). As an umbrella of distinct samples it is better typed an aggregation. It is a member of CARDIoGRAM (COHO:0000745), which the draft missed. The draft's example quote began with the supplement heading 'GerMIFS 8'; it is trimmed to the sentence. If the curator prefers to keep GerMIFS a cohort (one programme run by the same German groups, first from Regensburg and Lübeck), the definition still stands; the individual collections GerMIFS I–VII are not in COHO. GerMIFS III's cases come from the KORA myocardial infarction registry, and most GerMIFS controls come from KORA (COHO:0000045) or, for GerMIFS VII, the Heinz Nixdorf Recall Study (COHO:0000756); these are not GerMIFS members. 'GerMIFs' is verbatim in the GWAS paper's acknowledgements. CARDIoGRAM is itself part of CARDIoGRAMplusC4D (COHO:0000029).

input name: Gene-Lifestyle interactions And Complex traits Involved in Elevated disease Risk Study
label: Gene-Lifestyle Interactions and Complex Traits Involved in Elevated Disease Risk Study
other synonyms: Gene-Lifestyle interactions And Complex traits Involved in Elevated disease Risk Study|Gene x Lifestyle interactions And Complex traits Involved in Elevated disease Risk Study|GLACIER Study
example title: The trans-ancestral genomic architecture of glycemic traits.
example quote: GLACIER
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of adults from the county of Västerbotten in northern Sweden, nested within the Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study, whose members had baseline health and lifestyle examinations in the Västerbotten Intervention Programme between 1985 and 2004, in the years of their 40th, 50th or 60th birthdays, with a repeat examination about ten years later. It was established in 2008 to study the genetics of cardiometabolic traits and interactions between genes and lifestyle.
location quote: Sixteen fasting glucose-raising loci were genotyped in middle-aged adults from the Gene x Lifestyle interactions And Complex traits Involved in Elevated disease Risk (GLACIER) Study, a population-based prospective cohort study from northern Sweden.
parent quote: The GLACIER Study is a prospective, population-based cohort study comprising 19,547 adults from the northern Swedish county of Västerbotten, nested within the Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study (20).
note: Tier D (D234), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred; research settles it. GLACIER is a prospective population-based cohort of adults of Västerbotten county, Sweden, nested within the Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study (COHO:0000927): its members were examined in the Västerbotten Intervention Programme (Västerbotten Health Survey) at ages 40, 50 or 60 between 1985 and 2004, with ten-year follow-up, and the study was set up in 2008 for gene–lifestyle interaction research (PMID:20870969, PMID:25396097, PMID:26625858). The GWAS paper names GLACIER only as an entry in its supplementary acknowledgements ('GLACIER None'), so the example quote is the bare name; there is no sentence to quote. Parent is the Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study (COHO:0000927), as for the Umeå Fracture and Osteoporosis Study (COHO:0000986); the immediate frame is the Västerbotten Intervention Programme, which is not a COHO term (tier-E row E1203 'VIP study' may or may not be it). The en-dash spelling 'Gene–Lifestyle Interactions and Complex Traits Involved in Elevated Disease Risk' (PMID:26625858) differs from the label only in the dash and is not added. An unrelated multiple sclerosis trial of glatiramer acetate is also called GLACIER (PMID:26195058); it is not in COHO and no catalog tag uses it.

label: German Multicenter Allergy Study
other synonyms: German Multicentre Allergy Study|Multicentre Allergy Study|Multicenter Allergy Study|German multicentre atopy study
example title: European and multi-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of atopic dermatitis highlights importance of systemic immune regulation.
example quote: The Multicentre Allergy Study (MAS) is a German birth cohort which has been described in detail previously71,72 .
definition: A birth cohort of children born in 1990 and recruited in the maternity wards of university hospitals in five German cities (Berlin, Düsseldorf, Freiburg, Mainz and Munich), enriched for newborns at high risk of allergy, with two allergic immediate family members or raised cord-blood IgE, alongside a random sample of low-risk newborns, and followed with repeated examinations and questionnaires from infancy into adulthood to study the course of asthma, allergic rhinitis, eczema and allergic sensitisation.
location quote: The German Multicentre Allergy Study began with the recruitment of 1314 newborns between January and December 1990 in maternity wards from university hospitals in 5 German cities – Berlin, Düsseldorf, Freiburg, Mainz and Munich
parent quote: This study is based on data from five ongoing European birth cohorts in three different countries participating in MeDALL. Of the cohorts included, we selected those with a) relevant information on maternal smoking during pregnancy or SHS exposure during the first year of life; b) follow-up between 14 and 16 y of age; and c) suitable outcome assessments from three predefined age intervals (4–6, 8–10, and 14–16 y).The following five cohorts were included: Children, Allergy, Milieu, Stockholm, Epidemiology (BAMSE) (single-center, Sweden) (Wickman et al. 2002), German Infant Nutritional Intervention (GINIplus) (multicenter, Germany) (Berg et al. 2010), Influences of Lifestyle-Related Factors on the Immune System and the Development of Allergies in Childhood (LISAplus) (multicenter, Germany) (Zutavern et al. 2008), Multicentre Allergy Study (MAS) (multicenter, Germany) (Bergmann et al. 1994), and Prevention and Incidence of Asthma and Mite Allergy (PIAMA) (multicenter, the Netherlands) (Wijga et al. 2014).
note: Tier D (D235), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: presumably the G.MAS/German Multicenter Allergy Study cohort (co-tagged alongside GENUFAD on this atopic-dermatitis GWAS), though no retrieved unit from P1 itself names it; P2-P7: the German Multicenter Allergy Study, a German birth cohort (also called MAS, MAS-90) studied across allergy/atopy genetics papers from 1997-2022. P1 (the GWAS Catalog paper) does not name G.MAS in any retrieved unit; identity, name variants (MAS, MAS-90) and definition rest entirely on the six papers found by searching Europe PMC for the name. No COHO term currently matches this name. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronyms and country are right. The definition lacks the design that defines MAS: newborns recruited through the maternity wards of university hospitals in five named German cities, risk-enriched (children with two allergic immediate relatives or raised cord-blood IgE over-represented beside a random low-risk sample), and followed into adulthood (PMID:26011739). The draft's country quote describes one paper's selected subset without naming MAS; it is replaced. The draft missed that MAS is one of the MeDALL birth cohorts (COHO:0000297). The draft's example had no quote, but the GWAS paper's supplement describes the cohort ('The Multicentre Allergy Study (MAS) is a German birth cohort ...'). The MeDALL quote spans three sentences of one section (two paragraphs); the first says the five cohorts participate in MeDALL and the third names MAS among them. The Heinz Nixdorf Recall controls of the GWAS (COHO:0000756) are not part of MAS. The acronym MAS is also carried by tier-E row E663 (Sydney Memory and Ageing Study); if E663 is minted, both terms need the shared-acronym editor note. The 1994 design paper's title calls it 'The German multicentre atopy study (MAS-90)', hence that synonym.

label: Genetic Modifier Study
other synonyms: Gene Modifier Study|University of North Carolina/Case Western Reserve University Case-Control Study|GMS Lung Study|US extremes of phenotype study
example title: Genetic modifiers of body mass index in individuals with cystic fibrosis.
example quote: The Cystic Fibrosis Genome Project (CFGP) is comprised of individuals with CF recruited by the CF Twin and Sibling Study (TSS)15 and Cystic Fibrosis-Related Diabetes (CFRD) Study16 (Johns Hopkins University), Genetic Modifier Study (GMS)17,18,19 and GMS of Severe CF Liver Disease (GMS CFLD)20,21 (University of North Carolina), and Early Pseudomonas Infection Control Observational (EPIC Obs) Study22 (University of Washington and Seattle Children’s Hospital).
definition: A case-control study of genetic modifiers of cystic fibrosis lung disease, led by the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and Case Western Reserve University, that enrolled unrelated patients homozygous for F508del whose lung function for age was at either extreme (severe or mild disease) from cystic fibrosis centres across the United States, together with a smaller population-based sample from children's hospitals in Denver, Wisconsin and Boston.
location quote: (II) the University of North Carolina/Case Western Reserve University Case-Control Study, a sample ascertained on the phenotype of extremes of lung disease (7) (US extremes of phenotype study)
note: Tier D (D236), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the Genetic Modifier Study (GMS), one of the cystic fibrosis cohorts making up the Cystic Fibrosis Genome Project, run by the University of North Carolina. GMS is one of several studies comprising the Cystic Fibrosis Genome Project (CFGP: TSS/D212, CFRD/D211, GMS, GMS_CFLD/D237, EPIC_Obs/D221, spread across other batches); CFGP itself is not a candidate term or a row in this batch, so no parent is recorded. The 'Northern_America' country rests on D236.8's 'North American CF Genetic Modifier Study Consortium', taken to be the same initiative as GMS; flagged as a cross-paper inference. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label and type are right. The definition gives no design and wrongly equates GMS with the 'North American CF Genetic Modifier Study Consortium', which is the collaboration of three studies (GMS, the Canadian CGS and the Johns Hopkins TSS; PMID:21602797 Table 1, PMID:20681990). GMS is the UNC/Case Western Reserve case-control study of F508del homozygotes at the extremes of lung function (PMID:16207846, PMID:21602797), with a population-based subset from Denver, Wisconsin and Boston (PMID:26417704). 'Northern_America' is a region inferred from the consortium's name; GMS recruited in the United States ('US extremes of phenotype study', PMID:20681990). The GWAS Catalog tag UNC on GCST90271928 (PMID:36921087, 'the Gene Modifier Study at the University of North Carolina (UNC)', 'UNC=University of North Carolina (extremes of phenotype)') also denotes this study, so UNC is added. The example quote is trimmed to the one sentence; the draft's began mid-sentence before a heading. No parent: the Cystic Fibrosis Genome Project (the five studies of PMID:39260370) and the North American CF Modifier Gene Consortium (GMS, CGS D389, TSS D212) would be cohort aggregations but neither is in COHO or this review; as for D211, D212 and D221, both should get hasCohort links to GMS if minted. 'UNC' is proposed here because the review's UNC row (D539) is the University of North Carolina site tag, like JHU (D459) whose tag went to CF_TSS; drop it here if D539 is settled otherwise. GMS CFLD (D237) is a separate UNC-coordinated study (its own IRB number) whose controls were largely drawn from GMS participants. No acronym clash in COHO or the review.

input name: Genetic Modifier Study of Severe Cystic Fibrosis Liver Disease
label: Genetic Modifier Study of Severe CF Liver Disease
other synonyms: Genetic Modifier Study of Severe Cystic Fibrosis Liver Disease|Genetic Modifier Study of Severe Liver Disease in Cystic Fibrosis|GMS of Severe CF Liver Disease
example title: Genetic modifiers of body mass index in individuals with cystic fibrosis.
example quote: The Cystic Fibrosis Genome Project (CFGP) is comprised of individuals with CF recruited by the CF Twin and Sibling Study (TSS)15 and Cystic Fibrosis-Related Diabetes (CFRD) Study16 (Johns Hopkins University), Genetic Modifier Study (GMS)17,18,19 and GMS of Severe CF Liver Disease (GMS CFLD)20,21 (University of North Carolina), and Early Pseudomonas Infection Control Observational (EPIC Obs) Study22 (University of Washington and Seattle Children’s Hospital).
definition: A two-stage case-control study of genetic modifiers of severe liver disease in cystic fibrosis, coordinated by the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, which from January 1999 enrolled people with cystic fibrosis and cirrhosis with portal hypertension from cystic fibrosis centres in the United States, Canada and other countries of Europe, Australia, South America and the Middle East, and compared them with people with cystic fibrosis aged 15 or over without liver disease, many of them from the Genetic Modifier Study of lung disease.
location quote: Severe CFLD subjects described in this analysis were enrolled in the Genetic Modifier Study of Severe CF Liver Disease from 34 North American CF Centers from the United States (n = 145 CFLD patients) and Canada (n = 34 CFLD patients), with a coordinating center at The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill as previously described [7]. || Of the 158 CF patients evaluated for severe liver disease (CFLD; portal hypertension; enrolled 1/1999–12/2004), there were 128 patients who fulfilled criteria from 22 CF Centers in 10 countries (Australia, 8; Canada, 17; Czech Republic, 17; Germany, 3; Italy, 28; Netherlands, 1; Scotland, 2; Slovakia, 4; Turkey, 4; and U.S., 44). || Of the 191 CF patients evaluated for CFLD (portal hypertension; enrolled 1/2005–2/2007), there were 139 CF patients who fulfilled criteria from 35 CF Centers in 10 countries (Argentina, 5; Australia, 5; Canada, 24; Chile, 1; France, 9; Ireland, 8; Israel, 7; Italy, 14; United Kingdom, 4; and U.S., 62).
note: Tier D (D237), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the Genetic Modifier Study of Severe CF Liver Disease (GMS_CFLD), one of the cystic fibrosis cohorts making up the Cystic Fibrosis Genome Project, run by the University of North Carolina. The clearest description of this cohort (76 international centers, January 1999-July 2013) is unit D236.11, filed under the sibling name GMS (D236) in the batch file but explicitly about 'the Genetic Modifier Study of Severe CF Liver Disease'; cited here as a unit about this cohort, as permitted. The tag denotes the General Population Trial: in the GWAS it comes from the NCI GWAS of Abnet et al. (PMID:20729852), whose NIT samples came from 'a prospective cohort' and which a later paper on the same data describes as 'The Linxian General Population Nutrition Intervention Trial was a large-scale, randomized, double-blind, primary prevention trial in Linxian, China' (PMC8141232). No COHO term or other review name covers either Linxian trial; D301 (Shanxi, the Shanxi Upper Gastrointestinal Cancer Genetics Project) is the other study of the same NCI GWAS. label: Pancreatic Cancer Cohort Consortium
example title: Identification of Recessively Inherited Genetic Variants Potentially Linked to Pancreatic Cancer Risk.
example quote: To discover recessively inherited pancreatic cancer risk loci, we performed a re-analysis of the largest pancreatic cancer GWAS, the Pancreatic Cancer Cohort Consortium (PanScan) and the Pancreatic Cancer Case-Control Consortium (PanC4), including 8,769 cases and 7,055 controls of European ancestry.
definition: A consortium formed in 2006 within the US National Cancer Institute's Cohort Consortium by investigators of 12 prospective cohort studies to run PanScan, a multi-stage genome-wide association study of pancreatic cancer funded by the NCI. PanScan I genotyped cases and controls from the cohorts and one case-control study, PanScan II (from 2007) those of eight case-control studies, and PanScan III new incident cases from 14 cohorts and from case series and case-control studies, mostly people of European ancestry from the United States and Europe.
location quote: Geographic region was defined as REGION_US (United States): AgHealth, CPS-II, DFCI, HPFS, MEC, NHS, NYU-WHS, PHS, PLCO, SELECT, VITAL, WHI; REGION_CNE (Central and Northern Europe): ATBC, EPIC, PANDoRA-Heidelberg, MCCS (Melbourne); and REGION_SE (Southern Europe): SBCS (Spain controls), PANKRAS-II (cases). || In addition to the cases from cohorts, we also included cases from the Gastrointestinal Cancer Clinic of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Study (DFCI-GCC); from the University Hospital in Heidelberg, Germany, which is part of a larger European clinical case-control study (PANDoRA); and from clinic-based cases from eastern Spain (PANKRAS-II). || Also included are 61 pancreatic cancer cases and 67 control subjects from PanScan I as well as 173 pancreatic cancer cases from PanScan III of Asian ancestry from the Shanghai Men's and Women's Health Study (Supplemental Table 10, Wolpin et al. (Nat Genet, 2014)).
note: Tier D (D281), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: abstract doesn't name it; P2: PanScan = Pancreatic Cancer Cohort Consortium, paired with PanC4, reanalysed for recessive risk loci; P3: abstract doesn't name it; P4: PanScan I is the cohort-study arm vs PanC4's case-control arm in an alcohol-interaction analysis. Verdict is aggregation: PanScan pools ~27 distinct cohort/case-control studies across 3 phases (D281.38), paired with PanC4 (a separate consortium, not this batch's D489). No countries stated beyond 'European ancestry', so left blank. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type and acronyms are right: dbGaP's PanScan study reads 'Within the framework of the NCI-sponsored Cohort Consortium, investigators from 12 prospective epidemiologic cohorts formed the Pancreatic Cancer Cohort Consortium in 2006. This study, also known as "PanScan", ...', and PMID:29422604 writes 'the Pancreatic Cancer Cohort Consortium (PanScan: https://epi.grants.cancer.gov/PanScan/ )'. The definition lacked the origin (2006, NCI Cohort Consortium, NCI-funded) and what each phase added (PanScan I cohorts plus one case-control study, PanScan II eight case-control studies, PanScan III new cases from 14 cohorts, case series and case-control studies); 'run alongside PanC4' describes later joint analyses, not the consortium. Countries were left empty although the PanScan papers and dbGaP name them; added the United States, Europe, Australia (Melbourne), Germany (Heidelberg), Spain and China (Shanghai), each quoted. Tier-E row E880 (PGS id PCCC, 'Pancreatic Cancer Cohort Consortium') names the same consortium and should be 'same as' D281 (PCCC then joins the acronyms). D489 (PanC4, the Pancreatic Cancer Case-Control Consortium) and E869 (PANDoRA) are separate consortia; the phrase 'Pancreatic Cancer Cohort Consortium and Pancreatic Cancer Case-Control Consortium' in dbGaP's study title probably reflects the eight case-control studies added in 2007 and a study team that 'includes scientists from the cohorts comprising the Consortium, the NCI and the Pancreatic Cancer Case Control Consortium (PanC4)'. Candidate hasCohort members already in COHO, all named in one dbGaP sentence ('The nine cohort studies that participated in PanScan I and had new genotyping of cases in PanScan III include ATBC, CPS-II, EPIC, HPFS, NHS, PHS, PLCO, SMWHS, and WHI; the five newly joined cohort studies include the Agricultural Health Study (AHS), the Multiethnic Cohort Study (MEC), the Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study (MCCS), the Vitamins and Lifestyle Study (VITAL), and Selenium and Vitamin E Cancer Prevention Trial (SELECT).', https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/projects/gap/cgi-bin/study.cgi?study_id=phs000206.v5.p3): ATBC COHO:0000598, CPS-II COHO:0000024, EPIC COHO:0000065, HPFS COHO:0000527, NHS COHO:0000456, PHS COHO:0000626, PLCO COHO:0000485, SMWHS as SMHS COHO:0000578 and SWHS COHO:0000553, WHI COHO:0000409, AHS COHO:0000740, MEC COHO:0000121, MCCS COHO:0000523, VITAL COHO:0000579, SELECT COHO:0000693. PanScan II's case-control studies (not listed in any text read) may add further countries.

note: Tier D (D282), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred for want of a description; the sources settle it. The GWAS paper's Supplementary Table 1 (MOESM4) gives 'ProstatE cancer Genetic Association Study of Uncommon Susceptibility loci', abbreviation Pegasus, design 'Nested case-control in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial, US'. PLCO men outside PEGASUS also appear in the same GWAS under the separate tag PLCO ('Men with a confirmed diagnosis of prostate cancer from PLCO and not included in PEGASUS or PRACTICAL Oncoarray analysis'), which belongs to COHO:0000485 itself. input name: Polygenic and Environmental Risk for Alzheimer's Disease
label: Genetic and Environmental Risk in Alzheimer's Disease Consortium

note: Tier D (D284), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (GCST90012877), P2 (GCST90027158): PERADES tagged alongside GERAD on both AD meta-analysis studies; D284.4 describes "the GERAD/PERADES sample" as one combined case-control set, i.e. the Cardiff-led GERAD consortium continued under the JPND-funded PERADES name. GERAD/PERADES tagged as combined sample (D284.4); PERADES is the JPND-funded successor name for the same Cardiff-led AD consortium already at COHO:0000646. Both P1 and P2 tag GERAD and PERADES separately on the same GCST studies, so a checker should confirm they denote the identical sample rather than an extended/updated one. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity is right: PERADES is not a sample of its own but the second name of the Cardiff-led GERAD consortium, which the IGAP papers call 'Genetic and Environmental Risk in AD/Defining Genetic, Polygenic and Environmental Risk for Alzheimer's Disease Consortium (GERAD/PERADES)' (Kunkle et al. 2019); the GWAS Catalog splits that joint name into two tags, GERAD and PERADES, on both studies, and the PGS Catalog lists GERAD beside PERADES on every one of its seven PERADES scores. In both tagged papers the dataset is the GERAD GWAS sample: 'The GERAD/PERADES sample comprises 3,177 Alzheimer's disease cases and 7,277 controls', and 'Genotypes from all cases and 4617 controls were previously included in the AD GWAS by Harold and colleagues', the other 2,660 population controls coming from WTCCC2 (Bellenguez 2022 supplement; Kunkle 2019 Supplementary Note). PERADES itself is a JPND research programme ('Defining Genetic, Polygenic and Environmental Risk for Alzheimer's Disease using multiple powerful cohorts, focussed Epigenetics and Stem cell metabolomics', started January 2014, coordinated at Cardiff with partners in the Netherlands and France), which funded the consortium's later work; it defines no sample of its own, so it gets no term. The draft's example quote ran the supplement's section heading into the first sentence; replaced by the main text's sample list. The joint tag GERAD/PERADES and the expansions are added. COHO:0000646 already has a GWAS Catalog example (GCST90162599); the example above is only a replacement if the curator prefers a PERADES-tagged study, not a second one. The review row for GERAD (catalog_cohorts_review.tsv line 332) calls the PERADES sample 'the extended GERAD/PERADES sample'; the extension is only 2,660 extra WTCCC2 population controls, so it is the same consortium's dataset. The PGS Catalog name 'Polygenic and Environmental Risk for Alzheimer's Disease' drops 'Defining Genetic,' from the programme's name; kept as a synonym only because the Catalog uses it. For COHO:0000646's countries: the same recruitment sentence also names Trinity College Dublin ('Cases and elderly screened controls were recruited by the Medical Research Council (MRC) Genetic Resource for Alzheimer's disease (Cardiff University; Institute of Psychiatry, London; Cambridge University; Trinity College Dublin), ...', PMC9005347 supplementary files), so Ireland may be missing from COHO:0000646's United Kingdom, United States and Germany.

definition: A multi-site cross-sectional study of typically developing children, adolescents and young adults aged 3 to 20 years, recruited through local postings and outreach in eight metropolitan areas of the United States and assessed at ten US sites, with its coordinating centre at the University of California, San Diego, that collected developmental histories, cognitive assessments, multimodal brain imaging and genome-wide genotypes to create a shared repository for studying brain and cognitive development.

No PING design/profile paper is in the evidence (only papers that used it, plus NIH acknowledgment and PING Coordinating Center references); definition limited to what D285.1/.22/.25 state. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, country and example are right, but the definition was built from a funding line, a data-dissemination line and a consent sentence rather than the study's own description. 'Children and adolescents under 18' is wrong: PING screened participants 'between the ages of 3 and 20 years' and obtained consent directly from those aged 18 or over. The draft also missed the design: a multi-site, cross-sectional study of typically developing children recruited in eight US metropolitan areas and assessed at 10 US sites with imaging, the NIH Toolbox cognition battery and genome-wide genotyping, built as a shared data repository (the PING Data Repository paper, PMID:25937488, which the GWAS paper cites for the cohort). The draft described KARMA, the prospective mammography-screening cohort of 2011-2013 (tier-D row D130), and proposed merging the two rows. pKARMA is a different sample: 'prevalent KARMA', a case-control set in which 'pKARMA is made up of 5,002 invasive breast cancer cases (from the Linne-Brost 1 (Libro1) study) and 5,433 controls (from the Karolinska Mammography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer (KARMA 60 ))', the cases being women with primary breast cancer 'diagnosed in Stockholm between January 2001 and December 2008 identified via the Regional Cancer register' (PMID:28725034); BCAC papers put it as 'pKARMA is a combination of the KARMA and LIBRO-1 studies' (PMID:24943594). The tagged paper itself keeps them apart: its study table has 'KARMA Prospective cohort' and a separate 'PKARMA Mixed' row, with the legend 'PKARMA: Karolinska Mammography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer - Case-Control Study' (PMID:35418701 supplement). The country, Sweden, is right. Missed parent: pKARMA is a BCAC study (COHO:0000020). Keep D286 and D130 as two terms; the D130 check (d12.jsonl) reached the same conclusion. pKARMA is not isSubCohortOf KARMA: only its controls are KARMA women, its cases come from LIBRO-1 (Linné-Bröst 1), which is not in COHO or this review. The PGS Catalog's name for pKARMA, 'Karolinska Mammography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer', is KARMA's own name and D130's label, so it is left out of the synonyms to avoid a label clash. input name: Parkinson Research Examination of CEP-1347 Trial
label: Parkinson Research Examination of CEP-1347 Trial
other synonyms: Parkinson Research Examination of CEP-1347 Trial/A Longitudinal Follow-up of the PRECEPT Study Cohort
example title: Dopamine Pathway and Parkinson's Risk Variants Are Associated with Levodopa-Induced Dyskinesia.
example quote: PreCEPT: Parkinson Research Examination of CEP-1347 Trial
definition: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial run by the Parkinson Study Group, which enrolled people with early Parkinson's disease not yet requiring dopaminergic therapy at 65 sites in the United States and Canada between April 2002 and April 2004 to test whether the mixed lineage kinase inhibitor CEP-1347 could slow disease progression; the trial was stopped early for futility in 2005, and its participants were then followed in the observational PostCEPT study.
location quote: The participants (n=806) were enrolled between April 2002 and April 2004 at 65 sites across the United States and Canada.
note: Tier D (D287), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (GCST90281037, GCST90281038): PreCEPT listed among several PD trial/cohort tags in a glossary (D287.4); P2-P7: the trial's own primary and secondary publications, consistently spelling it all-caps PRECEPT. No unit states a recruitment country for PRECEPT; left blank. D287.1 also names a related but distinct follow-on study "PostCEPT", not treated as a synonym here. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronyms and type are right. The definition's 'enrolled ... between April 2002 and August 2005' is wrong: the trial ran from April 2002 to August 2005, but 'The participants (n=806) were enrolled between April 2002 and April 2004 at 65 sites across the United States and Canada' (PMID:18413464 full text). The definition also missed who ran it (the Parkinson Study Group) and the follow-up of the same participants in the observational PostCEPT study, which is how the genetic cohort is known ('Parkinson Research Examination of CEP-1347 Trial/A Longitudinal Follow-up of the PRECEPT Study Cohort [PreCEPT/PostCEPT]', PMID:27717005); the LID GWAS thanks the funders of 'PreCEPT and PostCEPT'. The draft left countries blank; the same full text gives the United States and Canada. The example quote ran on into the author manuscript's running header ('Tartu: University of Tartu Sosero et al.'); replaced by the legend entry itself. PostCEPT is the observational follow-up of the same participants, not a separate cohort, so no second term is needed; 'PreCEPT/PostCEPT' is added as an acronym because PD genetics papers name the cohort that way. DATATOP (E242, a tier-E row) is the other Parkinson Study Group trial often analysed with it; not related as parent or member. The Parkinson Study Group is a trial network, not a COHO aggregation, so no parent.

label: Predictors For ECT
other synonyms: Predictors for ECT|PREFECT study
example title: Genome-wide association analyses identify distinct genetic architectures for early-onset and late-onset depression.
example quote: The PREFECT sample constituted N=1,796 cases who had a clinical diagnosis of MDD and were treated for a major depressive episode with electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)6 .
definition: A Swedish study that between 2013 and 2017 recruited adults who had received electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) recorded in the Swedish National Quality Register for ECT, inviting registered patients by letter to a telephone interview and blood sampling and recruiting others at Swedish psychiatric hospitals before an ECT series, and that links their DNA, stored at the Karolinska Institutet Biobank, to the register's data on each treatment series, to study predictors of ECT outcome, including genetic ones, and the genetics of severe depressive episodes.
location quote: Cohort and country: iPSYCH2012, iPSYCH2015 - Denmark; MoBa - Norway; PREFECT, STAGE - Sweden; FinnGen - Finland.
note: Tier D (D288), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because no unit expanded the acronym; research settles it. The study's own papers name it: 'Participants were selected from the Predictors For ECT (PREFECT) study. PREFECT enrolled people from the Swedish National Quality Register for ECT between 2013 and 2017 (Q-ECT)' (PMID:33483693), and 'The study population was derived from the Predictors for ECT (PREFECT) study, conducted in Sweden' (PMID:36069021). Recruitment was retrospective (a letter to patients aged 18 or over in Q-ECT, a telephone interview and a blood sample sent to Karolinska Institutet Biobank) and prospective (patients recruited before an ECT series at Swedish psychiatric hospitals); it was funded by the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research. The draft's country, acronym and example study were right; its example quote is trimmed to drop the lead-in label 'PREFECT vs ANGI:'. The two papers disagree on the number of hospitals of the prospective arm (seven named: Danderyd, Huddinge, Hudiksvall, Sahlgrenska, Umeå, Uppsala and Örebro, in PMID:33483693; eight in PMID:36069021), so the definition gives no number. The label keeps the PGS Catalog's and the first paper's capitalisation 'Predictors For ECT'; the lower-case form is a synonym under the case rule. In the tagged GWAS, PREFECT's controls come from LifeGene, a different study, which is not part of PREFECT. PREFECT clashes with no COHO acronym.

input name: Performance of Rotavirus and Oral Polio Vaccines in Developing Countries
label: Performance of Rotavirus and Oral Polio Vaccines in Developing Countries
other synonyms: PROVIDE study|PROVIDE Study
example title: Genome-Wide Association Study of Campylobacter-Positive Diarrhea Identifies Genes Involved in Toxin Processing and Inflammatory Response.
example quote: Here, we aimed to identify genetic variants associated with host susceptibility to Campylobacter infection using two well-characterized birth cohorts: the Performance of Rotavirus and Oral Polio Vaccines in Developing Countries (PROVIDE) Study (19) and the Cryptosporidiosis Birth Cohort (CBC) (20).
definition: A birth cohort of children enrolled with their mothers within seven days of birth in low-income wards of Mirpur, Dhaka, Bangladesh, from May 2011, into a randomized controlled trial with a two-by-two factorial design, conducted by the International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh (icddr,b) with the University of Vermont and the University of Virginia, that tested a delayed-dose oral rotavirus vaccine and the replacement of one oral polio vaccine dose by an injectable polio vaccine, and followed the children through their first two years of life to study why oral vaccines underperform in children living with poverty, poor sanitation and overcrowding.
location quote: A birth cohort of 700 infants from the Mirpur area of Dhaka, Bangladesh was established, following infants for the first 2 years of life.
note: Tier D (D289), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (GCST90129578) and P2 (GCST90446496): PROVIDE names the same Dhaka, Bangladesh birth-cohort vaccine trial throughout, alongside its sibling the Cryptosporidiosis Birth Cohort (CBC), a separate cohort not this row. Well supported by the cohort's own methods paper (P3/D289.55-65) and both GWAS papers. CBC, co-analysed throughout, is a distinct sibling cohort, not PROVIDE itself, and not confused here. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, country and example are right, and the definition's claims hold. It lacked who ran the study and how children entered it: the methods paper (PMID:25711607) says 'This study was performed with experienced senior investigators at the International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh (icddr,b)' (its authors are from icddr,b and the Universities of Vermont and Virginia, whose review boards approved the protocol), that families came from three low-income northern wards of Mirpur, that consent and enrolment took place within 7 days after birth, that the trial 'had a 2 × 2 factorial design', and that 'The on-study phase spanned May 2011–November 2014.' Definition rewritten to include these. The methods paper mentions 'A parallel trial with a modified study design' at the National Institute of Cholera and Enteric Diseases in Kolkata, India; that trial is not this cohort and neither GWAS paper uses it. The Cryptosporidiosis and Enteropathogens in Bangladesh Birth Cohort, co-analysed in both GWAS papers, is a separate cohort (tier-D row D206), as is the Dhaka Birth Cohort of PMID:32019797; neither is a parent. No COHO term shares the name or acronym.

label: Queensland Twin Registry
other synonyms: Queensland Twin Registry Study|Queensland Twin Register|Queensland Twin and Family Registry
example title: Genome-wide association study meta-analysis of dizygotic twinning illuminates genetic regulation of female fecundity.
example quote: Queensland Twin Registry
definition: A population-based registry of identical and non-identical twins and triplets of all ages living in Australia, established in 2006 at the QIMR Berghofer Medical Research Institute in Brisbane, whose members are invited into twin research projects on health and disease; genetic studies drawing on QIMR Berghofer's genotyped twin and family samples report them under the registry's name.
location quote: Queensland Twin Registry (QTwin) Study is a population-based registry of identical and non-identical twins and triplets of all ages, living in Australia.
note: Tier D (D290), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred with no text; research settles it. The GWAS tag QTR means two different registries. In PMID:35907915 (GCST90134646) it is the Chinese one: 'the participants were adult twins from the Qingdao Twins Registry, China', i.e. COHO:0000932, which already carries the acronym QTR; so the draft's example study, GCST90134646, is a Qingdao study and wrong for this row. In PMID:38052102 (GCST90244755, the DZ-twinning meta-analysis) it is the Australian sample, which the supplement's analysis plan lists as 'Queensland Twin Registry' among the collaborating cohorts and the main text describes as samples 'collected by the Queensland Institute of Medical Research (QIMR Berghofer; QIMR), from a number of studies which collected DNA in twin families since around 1990'. The PGS Catalog id QTR ('Queensland Twin and Family Registry', no scores) also means the Queensland registry. QIMR Berghofer's own page describes it: a population-based registry of twins and triplets of all ages living in Australia, established in 2006. Other genetic papers name QIMR's twin samples after it ('The target sample consisted of individuals from two cohorts of the Queensland Twin Registry.', PMID:32546850; 'Queensland Twin Registry (QTR610)' and other genotyping batches, PMID:26242864). Shared acronym: QTR is already an acronym of COHO:0000932 (Qingdao Twin Registry), so both terms need the editor note, e.g. 'The acronym QTR also denotes the Queensland Twin Registry (COHO:new); this term is the Qingdao Twin Registry.' and 'The acronym QTR also denotes the Qingdao Twin Registry (COHO:0000932); this term is the Queensland Twin Registry.' The GWAS Catalog's QTR tag on GCST90134646 belongs to COHO:0000932, which needs no change. The name is used loosely: some papers treat the Queensland Twin Registry as separate from the Australian Twin Registry (COHO:0000015), both at QIMR (PMID:33955455, 40956885); CODATwins says 'Queensland Twin registry is part of Twins Research Australia' (PMID:42286115), and if Twins Research Australia is the Australian Twin Registry under a later name (my understanding, not verified from a fetched source), an isSubCohortOf COHO:0000015 is possible; not asserted. The EGG/EAGLE consortium lists 'Qtwin Queensland Twin Registry' with the Brisbane adolescent twin study paper as its reference (PMID:30887376), and PMID:29845340 describes 'Qtwin' as twins recruited from schools in south-east Queensland since 1992, which is the Brisbane Longitudinal Twin Study (COHO:0000744); in those consortia the name means that study. The example quote is the only place the tagged paper names the registry, its supplement's list of collaborating cohorts (the rest of that line is investigators' names, left out). If a quote with context is preferred over the GWAS example, PMID:23756378 gives 'Participants were drawn from the Queensland Twin Registry and comprised 12 MZT pairs discordant for MDD and 12 MZT pairs concordant for no MDD and low neuroticism.' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC3693404/fullTextXML). Tier-D row D053 (QIMR-BGE) was checked as not a cohort; QIMR itself was 'not a cohort' in the earlier review.

input name: The Research in African American Alzheimer Disease Initiative
label: Research in African American Alzheimer Disease Initiative
other synonyms: The Research in African American Alzheimer Disease Initiative|Research in African American Alzheimer's Disease Initiative
example title: Extended genome-wide association study employing the African genome resources panel identifies novel susceptibility loci for Alzheimer's disease in individuals of African ancestry.
example quote: Study participants for the REAAADI were ascertained as part of a family-based study of Alzheimer’s Disease through the John P. Hussman Institute for Human Genomics Outreach and Diversity Core at the University of Miami, Columbia University Alzheimer Disease Research Center, Case Western Reserve University, and Maya Angelou Center for Health Equity at Wake Forest School of Medicine.
definition: A multi-site US study of African Americans, a sub-study of the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project run by investigators at North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University, Wake Forest School of Medicine, the University of Miami, Columbia University and Case Western Reserve University, that ascertains African American families affected by Alzheimer's disease through community outreach and collects blood or saliva samples, medical and family histories and cognitive assessments, to identify rare variants, genes and pathways associated with Alzheimer's disease in African Americans.
parent quote: REAAADI, a sub-study of the Alzheimer’s Disease Sequencing Project (ADSP), is a multi-site study bringing together investigators at NC Agricultural and Technical State University, Wake Forest School of Medicine, University of Miami, Columbia University, and Case Western Reserve University.
note: Tier D (D291), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (both GCSTs): REAAADI named directly (D291.4) among several individually-listed AD cohorts (ACT, ADGC, CHAP, Indianapolis, MIRAGE, NIA-AD FBS, WHICAP); described as a family-based African-American AD study, not an aggregation despite the automated hint. Automated "aggregation?" hint looks wrong: D291.1 calls REAAADI a "cohort" among other individually named cohorts, and D291.5/.17 describe one family-ascertainment design, not a collection of member cohorts. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type (a single multi-site study, not an aggregation), acronym and country are right. The label carried the PGS Catalog's leading article; the study's own papers call it 'Research in African American Alzheimer Disease Initiative (REAAADI)' (PMID:37952397) or 'Research in African American Alzheimer’s Disease Initiative (REAAADI)' (PMID:37212603), so the article is dropped and both forms kept as synonyms. The definition missed the study's own description: 'REAAADI, a sub-study of the Alzheimer’s Disease Sequencing Project (ADSP), is a multi-site study bringing together investigators at NC Agricultural and Technical State University, Wake Forest School of Medicine, University of Miami, Columbia University, and Case Western Reserve University. REAAADI was designed to identify rare variant enriched genes and genetic pathways associated with AD among AAs.' (PMID:37212603). It named the Miami, Columbia, Case Western and Wake Forest recruitment centres but left out NC A&T, the purpose and the data collected (blood or saliva, medical and family history interviews, cognitive tests; families eligible when a member aged 50 or over has at least two relatives with memory or cognitive problems). Missed parent: the ADSP (COHO:0000561). The country quote was a list of institutions naming no country; the name gives it instead. The example quote was a bare heading; replaced by the sentence under it. Country from the name: 'African American' denotes the US population, and all the named sites are in the United States (North Carolina, Miami, New York, Cleveland). Not the same as the NIA-LOAD Family Study (COHO:0000669), which PMID:37952397 analyses alongside it, nor MIRAGE (COHO:0000115) or GenerAAtions, which the GWAS lists separately. ADSP (COHO:0000561) should get a hasCohort link to it with the quote above. REAAADI clashes with no COHO acronym. No start date is given in the papers read, so the definition gives none.

input name: The Roskilde cohort of pregnant women
label: The Roskilde cohort of pregnant women

example title: Multi-ancestry, trans-generational GWAS meta-analysis of gestational diabetes and glycaemic traits during pregnancy reveals limited evidence of pregnancy-specific genetic effects.

definition: A prospective cohort of unselected pregnant women enrolled from 2009 at the nuchal translucency scan in the obstetrics and gynaecology department of Roskilde Hospital, Region Zealand, Denmark, with ultrasound, uterine artery Doppler and blood samples at about 12, 20, 25 and 32 weeks of gestation and outcomes taken from medical records, set up to study whether serum YKL-40 predicts preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction, and later used in genetic studies of gestational diabetes and glucose levels in pregnancy.
location quote: Roskilde The Roskilde cohort of pregnant women Fetal - GDM and 2hG Denmark
note: Tier D (D292), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (both GCSTs): Roskilde named directly (D292.1-2) as "The Roskilde cohort of pregnant women", a Danish pregnancy cohort recruited via Roskilde Hospital's obstetrics department (D292.7). No COHO candidate existed for this name. Danish Diabetes Academy funding (D292.5) used only for the research-topic detail, not as country evidence; country instead rests on the Roskilde Hospital obstetrics site (D292.7). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, country and example are right, but the definition gave the cohort a purpose it did not have: the Danish Diabetes Academy grant funded its use in the gestational diabetes GWAS, while the cohort itself is the one registered as NCT00836524, which the tagged paper cites ('registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT00836524)'). That registration, 'Is Serum YKL-40 Capable of Predicting Intrauterine Growth Restriction (IUGR) and Preeclampsia?', a prospective observational cohort started in January 2009 at the obstetrics and gynaecology department in Roskilde, enrolled 'Pregnant women attending nuchal transcluency examination at Gynækologisk-Obstetrisk dept. Roskilde University Hospital', with blood samples and uterine artery Doppler at 12, 20, 25 and 32 weeks. Its paper (PMID:24861484) describes 'unselected pregnant women enrolled at nuchal translucency examination between 11(+3) and 13(+6) weeks of gestation'. The country quote was an acknowledgement naming two people and no country; replaced by the study table row that gives Denmark. The registration gives a start in January 2009 and an estimated end of recruitment in 2011-2012; the definition says only 'from 2009'. The GWAS table analyses fetal (offspring) genotypes against the mothers' gestational diabetes and 2-hour glucose, measured from 14 to 38 weeks. 'Roskilde Cohort' is the name used in the paper's acknowledgements. No COHO term or review row matches.

Tier D (D293), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (idiopathic multifocal choroiditis GWAS) and P2 (sunitinib pharmacogenetics GWAS): RUNMC denotes Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Centre, the Dutch hospital/institution that contributed each study's own distinct patient sample, not one defined named cohort; P4's "Nijmegen inception cohort of early RA" is a different, unrelated named cohort also based there. RUNMC = Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Centre (institution), tagged on two unrelated disease studies (choroiditis, sunitinib response) with no shared named sample. P3, P5, P6, P8 are unrelated institutional papers (training, curriculum, prosthetics, care protocol); none names a cohort called RUNMC. Checked 2026-09-23: None in the verdict: RUNMC (the PGS Catalog's 'Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Centre') is an institution label for different sample sets, not one named sample. In the two GWAS Catalog papers it is Radboudumc's share of a multi-centre case series of idiopathic multifocal choroiditis ('Patients were recruited from the following centers in the Netherlands: University Medical Center Utrecht, Radboud University Medical Center, ...', PMID:37410486) and sunitinib-treated patients found through routine drug monitoring ('Cases were identified during routine therapeutic drug monitoring in standard patient care in the Radboud University Medical Centre (Radboudumc, Nijmegen, the Netherlands) and The Netherlands Cancer Institute (Amsterdam, the Netherlands) between December 2013 and December 2019.', PMID:39107874). The draft's reasoning did not cover the PGS Catalog's uses, which also differ (see note). No term. The named samples behind the label are already in COHO: the Nijmegen Biomedical Study (COHO:0000128, acronym NBS) and the Nijmegen Bladder Cancer Study (COHO:0000572, acronym NBCS), which GIANT pooled as 'RUNMC'. The Radboudumc thyroid cancer cases of PMID:28195142 may be the tier-E row E826 NTCC ('Nijmegen Thyroid Cancer Cohort'); not checked. Adding RUNMC as an acronym of COHO:0000128 and COHO:0000572 because of the GIANT usage is not recommended: the same label means unrelated Radboud patient series elsewhere. The Nijmegen inception cohort of early rheumatoid arthritis (P4 of the drafter's evidence) is unrelated to the tag.

label: Epidemiologische Studie zu Chancen der Verhütung, Früherkennung und optimierten Therapie chronischer Erkrankungen in der älteren Bevölkerung
note: Tier D (D294), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: SAAR = ESTHER, the Saarland, Germany cohort (COHO:0000665); GWAS Catalog's tag for it in this mitochondrial-copy-number GWAS (alongside UKB). SAAR is the GWAS Catalog tag for ESTHER (COHO:0000665), already fully described there; P1's abstract doesn't name the cohort so example ev is null. Add SAAR as an acronym; no new synonyms. But the draft's claim that PMID:34964454's abstract does not name the cohort is wrong: the abstract says the GWAS was done in subjects 'from the ESTHER prospective cohort', so the example has a quote. The ESTHER-only study is GCST90019040 (6,836 Germans, tagged SAAR alone); GCST012656 is its meta-analysis with UK Biobank (tagged SAAR|UKB). Add SAAR as an acronym of COHO:0000665; no new synonyms. label: Shanghai Breast Cancer Genetics Study

example title: Identification of novel breast cancer susceptibility loci in meta-analyses conducted among Asian and European descendants.
example quote: The Chinese participants were drawn from Shanghai Breast Cancer Genetics Study 4 (SBCGS), which consists of the Shanghai Breast Cancer Study (SBCS), Shanghai 5 Breast Cancer Survival Study (SBCSS), Shanghai Endometrial Cancer Study 6 (SECS, contributed control data only), and the Shanghai Women’s Health Study 7 (SWHS), four large population-based studies in urban Shanghai.

The definition called SBCGS a consortium 'combining their genotype data' and gave the Shanghai Endometrial Cancer Study as a full member; SBCGS is one case-control genetics study (dbGaP phs000799, design Case-Control) that genotyped cases and controls drawn from the four studies, the endometrial cancer study contributing controls only. Tier D (D298), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: 'Steno Diabetes Center' (Copenhagen), one of several institutions listed as contributing sample 'collections' (D298.4, D298.13-14) to this type-1-diabetes fine-mapping GWAS, alongside NIHR Cambridge BioResource, UKBS, BRI etc. 'Steno Diabetes Center' appears only as one of several institutions contributing samples (D298.4), with generic labels 'collection 1'/'collection 2' (D298.13-14), not a named, defined cohort. Checked 2026-09-23: The verdict is right for the GWAS tag: in PMID:34127860 'Steno Diabetes Center' is the institution, standing for two Danish type 1 diabetes collections that the paper calls only 'Steno Diabetes Center, collection 1' (cases and controls) and 'collection 2' (cases), with no name, design or source beyond the institution (Supplementary Tables 1 and 4; the 2015 ImmunoChip paper, PMID:25751624, does not describe them either). label: Sequenced Treatment Alternatives to Relieve Depression

note: Tier D (D305), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: STAR*D itself, the antidepressant-treatment trial cohort. Full expansion of STAR*D appears only once, in a sentence about GSRD's similarly designed criteria; label taken from that parenthetical. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type and country are right. The definition restated the GWAS supplement's one-line description and left out the design (multisite, prospective, randomised, multistep trial), its purpose (sequential treatment options for patients without a satisfactory response to citalopram), the funder and lead centre (NIMH award N01MH90003 to UT Southwestern Medical Center at Dallas) and the start (July 2001); all taken from the design paper's abstract (PMID:15061154), ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00021528 (sponsor NIMH, start 2001-07, completion 2006-09, 41 sites, all in the United States) and the PGC-MDD age-at-onset paper's acknowledgements (PMID:27519822). The example quote began with the supplement's heading ('STAR*D The STAR*D study ...'); it is replaced by a main-text sentence that expands the acronym and names STAR*D among the study's antidepressant response cohorts. STAR*D's genotyped participants were also one of the nine discovery samples of the PGC major depressive disorder mega-analysis (PMID:22472876 Table 1; PMID:27519822 Table 1: 'STAR*D United States') and of PGC29, so a hasCohort link from the Psychiatric GWAS Consortium (COHO:0000146) would also be true; I found no open text naming STAR*D as a PGC sample outside table rows and an author-contribution footnote, so only the NIMH Human Genetics Initiative link is proposed. No duplicate in COHO or this review.

example title: Fine-mapping, trans-ancestral and genomic analyses identify causal variants, cells, genes and drug targets for type 1 diabetes.
example quote: These studies include the Type 1 Diabetes Genetics Consortium (T1DGC), British 1958 Birth Cohort, Genetic Resource Investigating Diabetes (GRID), Consortium for the Longitudinal Evaluation of African-Americans with Early Rheumatoid Arthritis (CLEAR), Epidemiology of Diabetes Interventions and Complications (EDIC), Genetics of Kidneys and Diabetes Study (GoKinD), New York Cancer Project (NYCP), SEARCH for Diabetes in Youth study (SEARCH), Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet study (TrialNet), Tyypin 1 Diabetekseen Sairastuneita Perheenjäsenineen (IDDMGEN), Tyypin 1 Diabeteksen Genetiikka (T1DGEN), Northern Ireland GRID Collection, Northern Ireland Young Hearts Project, Hvidoere Study Group on Childhood Diabetes (HSG), and International HapMap Project.

note: Tier D (D306), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: one of several named collections (with IDDMGEN, HapMap, EDIC, etc.) contributing type 1 diabetes samples/data; no description of its own population or design given. Only appears in consortium acknowledgement lists; no unit describes T1DGEN's population, design or dates. Name is Finnish ('Type 1 Diabetes Genetics'), suggesting Finland; check Finnish paediatric diabetes registries. Checked 2026-09-23: Deferred for want of a description; the research gives a thin but usable record, like that of its sister collection IDDMGEN (COHO:0000963). T1DGEN is a named Finnish type 1 diabetes collection of cases only: Supplementary Table 1 of the GWAS paper lists it with country Finland and only cases (no controls, no parents), almost all in the Finnish ancestry cluster; Inshaw et al. 2018 (PMID:28983737, open access) analyse 'the Finnish IDDMGEN ... and T1DGEN (Tyypin 1 Diabeteksen Genetiikka) cohorts' as independent cases (Table 1: T1DGEN, Finland, Independent), and its ESM lists no controls from T1DGEN (IDDMGEN's controls are parents and siblings of its cases). The draft's example quote began mid-sentence ('Consortium (T1DGC), ...'); the full sentence is given. No open source found says who recruited T1DGEN, where in Finland or when; the Finnish name means roughly 'type 1 diabetes genetics' (my gloss, not a source quote). Kept separate from IDDMGEN (COHO:0000963, a family collection) and from the Type 1 Diabetes Genetics Consortium (COHO:0000174): every paper lists T1DGEN apart from both, although its genotyping was paid for through the T1DGC grant. No duplicate in COHO or this review.

input name: Swedisch Twin study of CHild and Adolescent Development
label: Swedish Twin study of CHild and Adolescent Development
