example quote: The Swedish Twin study of Child and Adolescent Development (TCHAD) was supported by the 658 Swedish Council for Working Life and the Swedish Research Council (Medicine and SIMSAM).
definition: A population-based longitudinal study, run from Karolinska Institutet, of all twins born in Sweden between May 1985 and December 1986, identified through the Swedish Twin Registry, in which the twins and their parents completed questionnaires in four waves from 1994 to 2005, when the twins were aged 8–9, 13–14, 16–17 and 19–20, with a further follow-up at age 26, to study how genes and environments contribute to the development of health and behavioural problems from childhood to adulthood.
location quote: Six large population-based cohorts (NTR and GenR from the Netherlands, TEDS from the UK, CATSS and TCHAD from Sweden and FinnTwin12 from Finland) analysed the co-occurrence of aggression measures with other psychopathologies.
parent quote: A population-based prospective cohort study including all twins from the Swedish Twin Registry who were born in Sweden 1985–1986 (N = 2960) [19] was conducted. These twins were invited to participate in a longitudinal Twin study of CHild and Adolescent Development (TCHAD), see [20].
note: Tier D (D307), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: TCHAD itself, given its own acknowledgement paragraph separate from CATSS in the same supplement. No unit gives TCHAD's population, recruitment or dates - only its name, funders, and a joint 'CATSS/TCHAD' heading whose text then describes only CATSS. Possible link to CATSS (COHO:0000633) unconfirmed; check the 2007 TCHAD-Study profile paper (Twin Research and Human Genetics 10:67-73). Checked 2026-09-23: Deferred for want of a profile; the design paper's abstract (PMID:17539366) and open-access papers settle it. TCHAD is the Karolinska Institutet twin study of all twins born in Sweden from May 1985 to December 1986, drawn from the Swedish Twin Registry and followed with parent and twin questionnaires at ages 8-9 (1994), 13-14, 16-17 and 19-20 (2005), later to age 26. It is a separate study from CATSS (COHO:0000633, twins born since July 1992); the GWAS supplement's 'CATSS/TCHAD' heading describes only CATSS, but the paper gives TCHAD its own acknowledgement, its own row in the cohort table and its own forest-plot estimates. The draft label began with 'The' and used the lower-case 'Child'; the design paper's own form is 'Swedish Twin study of CHild and Adolescent Development' (the capitals spell the acronym), and the lower-case variant, the PGS Catalog's misspelt 'Swedisch' name and the Karolinska Institutet form 'Twin Study of Child and Adolescent Development' are kept as synonyms. Like CATSS and SATSA in this review, TCHAD is a sub-cohort of the Swedish Twin Registry (COHO:0000160). The draft's example quote ran from an Australian acknowledgement across the 'TCHAD' heading; it is cut to the TCHAD sentence. The design paper gives the last of the four waves as 2005, PMID:29845340 as 2006; the definition follows the design paper. No duplicate in COHO or this review.

input name: Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in TBI
label: Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in Traumatic Brain Injury
other synonyms: Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in TBI
example title: A genome-wide association study of outcome from traumatic brain injury.
example quote: The majority of patients in the US cohort were recruited between 2014 and 2018 to TRACK-TBI, a NIH-NINDS funded prospective multicenter study aimed at improving the characterization of TBI through the collection of clinical and genetic data, plasma biomarkers, as well as neuroimaging and other multidimensional outcomes.
definition: A prospective, multicentre, longitudinal observational cohort study, led from the University of California, San Francisco, with funding from the US National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, that from February 2014 to July 2018 enrolled patients presenting within 24 hours of a traumatic brain injury who received a clinically indicated head CT scan, together with orthopaedic trauma controls, at 18 level I trauma centres in the United States, and collected clinical, neuroimaging, blood biomarker, genetic and outcome data to improve the characterisation, diagnosis and prognosis of traumatic brain injury.
location quote: Individuals included were recruited between 2000 and 2018 at 78 centres in Europe (CENTER-TBI, Cambridge, and Turku) and the US (TRACK-TBI and MGB) (Supplementary Methods).
note: Tier D (D308), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: TRACK-TBI, the main US arm of the GAIN Consortium's TBI genetics study (distinct from the earlier 'TRACK-TBI Pilot' study named in P4-P6). TRACK-TBI helped form the Genetic Associations in Neurotrauma (GAIN) Consortium with CENTER-TBI, MGB, CABI and TBIcare (D308.11/16); GAIN has no COHO candidate or batch row, so parent is left null. Distinguish from the earlier 'TRACK-TBI Pilot' study named in P4-P6. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, acronym, type, country and example are right. The label used the contraction 'TBI'; the study's own registration (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02119182, sponsor UCSF) gives the full name 'Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in Traumatic Brain Injury', so that is the label and the PGS Catalog form is a synonym. The definition misread the GWAS supplement: 'The majority of patients in the US cohort were recruited between 2014 and 2018 to TRACK-TBI' means most of the GWAS's US patients came from TRACK-TBI (the rest from the MGB Biobank), not that TRACK-TBI recruited most of its own patients then; TRACK-TBI enrolled from 26 February 2014 to 27 July 2018 at 18 US level I trauma centres (PMID:36939699). The definition also lacked the lead institution, the entry criteria (within 24 hours of injury, head CT) and the orthopaedic trauma controls. Distinct from the earlier TRACK-TBI Pilot study (NCT01565551; three level I trauma centres and one rehabilitation centre), which the main study built on and which P3-P5 describe; the GWAS used the main study. TRACK-TBI is an InTBIR study and a founding member of the Genetic Associations in Neurotrauma (GAIN) Consortium with CENTER-TBI (this review's D210), but neither InTBIR nor GAIN is in COHO or this review, so no parent. The Cloudflare-protected study website (tracktbi.ucsf.edu) could not be read. No duplicate in COHO or this review.

label: Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet
other synonyms: Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet Study Group|Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet Research Group|Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet study
example title: Fine-mapping, trans-ancestral and genomic analyses identify causal variants, cells, genes and drug targets for type 1 diabetes.
example quote: We acknowledge the support of the Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet Study Group (https://www.trialnet.org), which identified study participants and provided samples and follow-up data for this study.
definition: A cohort of people with or at risk of type 1 diabetes recruited since 2001 by Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet, an international network of clinical research centres established by the US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases: chiefly relatives of people with type 1 diabetes who are screened for islet autoantibodies and followed for progression in its Pathway to Prevention natural-history study, and people at risk of or newly diagnosed with type 1 diabetes enrolled in its trials aimed at delaying or preventing the disease.
location quote: Currently, TrialNet includes 17 clinical centers located in the U.S., Canada, and Australia.
note: Tier D (D309), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet itself, which supplied participants and samples for this GWAS. Definition from P6, a TrialNet overview paper, not the GWAS paper. Evidence calls it international but names no specific countries, and NIDDK/NIH is only the funder, so no country is asserted. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type and example are right, and the synonyms need only the tagged paper's own form, 'Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet study': TrialNet in the GWAS is the NIDDK type 1 diabetes network, which 'identified study participants and provided samples and follow-up data' (Supplementary Table 1: United States, with cases and controls). The definition described the organisation (a consortium of clinical centres) rather than the people who make up the cohort; the TrialNet overview (PMID:40272284, PMC12178618) says who they are: relatives of people with type 1 diabetes screened for islet autoantibodies and followed in the Pathway to Prevention study (TN01, formerly the Natural History Study, 2001-ongoing), and participants of its prevention and new-onset trials. The draft asserted no country, but the same overview's full text names them: 'Currently, TrialNet includes 17 clinical centers located in the U.S., Canada, and Australia.'. Typed as a cohort, not an aggregation: TrialNet recruits its own participants under common protocols rather than pooling pre-existing cohorts, and its Pathway to Prevention study is described as 'the largest long-running cohort study' of people at risk. Clinical centres in other countries (the overview says only 'Clinical centers in other countries have been engaged over TrialNet's history', without naming them) are not asserted. The PGS Catalog name 'Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet (www.trialnet.org)' carries the website address and is not proposed as a synonym. Separate from the Type 1 Diabetes Genetics Consortium (COHO:0000174). No duplicate in COHO or this review.

Tier D (D310), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: 'UC' = University of Colorado, one of several institutions contributing samples to T1DGC (D310.1), not a named defined sample; the same string elsewhere in the paper means 'ulcerative colitis' (D310.7-9), an unrelated disease label. PGS Catalog gives 'University of Chicago' but the paper's own supplement expands UC as University of Colorado; no unit names any specific UC-recruited sample or cohort. Checked 2026-09-23: None in the verdict. In PMID:34127860 'UC' is the University of Colorado, one of the 'Additional institutions contributing samples' (with BDA, BRI, NIMH, UAB, UCSF, MCW and Steno). Supplementary Table 1 shows what it contributed: a small United States set of type 1 diabetes cases and controls, almost all of African ancestry, with no study name or description anywhere in the paper, so the tag names an institution, like the paper's other institution tags (UAB, UCSF, MCW, BRI, NIMH), which this review also treats as not cohorts. The PGS Catalog's 'University of Chicago' is a different institution: the PGS id UC comes from the CIMBA/OCAC/BCAC source GWAS, where it is one of the CIMBA contributing centres of BRCA1/2 mutation carriers, again not a named cohort. Neither meaning is a defined, named sample, so no term and no extra record. The string UC also means ulcerative colitis in the paper's review file (MOESM3); irrelevant. If the University of Colorado samples are ever identified (for example as Barbara Davis Center collections), reconsider; the review already treats BDC as not a cohort.

example title: Genome-wide interaction analysis of menopausal hormone therapy use and breast cancer risk among 62,370 women.
example quote: The UCIBCS component of this research was supported by the NIH [CA58860, CA92044] and the Lon V Smith Foundation [LVS39420].

location quote: All cases diagnosed in Orange County, California from 1994-1995; ascertained through the population-based Cancer Surveillance Program of Orange County California (CSPOC)
parent quote: BCAC DACC approval is required to access data from the ABCFS, ABCS, ABCTB, BBCC, BBCS, BCEES, BCFR-NY, BCFR-PA, BCFR-UT, BCINIS, BSUCH, CBCS, CECILE, CGPS, CTS, DIETCOMPLYF, ESTHER, GC-HBOC, GENICA, GEPARSIXTO, GESBC, HABCS, HCSC, HEBCS, HMBCS, HUBCS, KARBAC, KBCP, LMBC, MABCS, MARIE, MBCSG, MCBCS, MISS, MMHS, MTLGEBCS, NC-BCFR, OFBCR, ORIGO, pKARMA, POSH, PREFACE, RBCS, SKKDKFZS, SUCCESSB, SUCCESSC, SZBCS, TNBCC, UCIBCS, UKBGS and UKOPS studies (Supplementary Table 1).
note: Tier D (D311), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: UCIBCS itself, one of several breast-cancer cohorts contributing to this menopausal-hormone-therapy GWAS; a garbled table cell reads 'UCIBCS Mixed' for design (D311.7, not quotable). No unit spells out UCIBCS's full name or describes its population, design or dates; only acknowledgements naming it. PGS Catalog expands it to 'UCI Breast Cancer Study' but no evidence unit confirms this; a researcher should verify and find a design paper. Checked 2026-09-23: Deferred for want of a description; BCAC sources settle it. UCIBCS is the Breast Cancer Association Consortium's 'UCI Breast Cancer Study' (University of California, Irvine), the name the PGS Catalog gives. The BCAC supplement of PMID:22267197 describes it: cases were all breast cancers diagnosed in Orange County, California, in 1994-1995, ascertained through the Cancer Surveillance Program of Orange County, and controls were Orange County residents recruited in 1998-2003 by random digit dialling, matched on age and race/ethnicity; its design reference (Ziogas et al. 2000, PMID:10667470) is the UCI population-based breast and ovarian cancer family registry, and Anton-Culver et al. 2000 (PMID:10882857) gives the case period as the year from 1 March 1994. PMID:21194473 marks it as a population-based case-control study. It is a BCAC member (COHO:0000020), named in BCAC's data-access statement like the other BCAC studies this review has linked. PMID:35418701's supplement calls UCIBCS's design 'Mixed', while PMID:21194473 marks it population-based case-control; the definition follows the design descriptions. The UC Irvine Ovarian Cancer Study (tier-E row E1132, PGS id UCIOCS) is a separate study; I did not check whether it shares the registry. The country quote is the cases cell of the BCAC study table (it names Orange County, California; the table's country cell reads 'U.S.A.'). No duplicate in COHO or this review.

example quote: The USRT Study was funded by Intramural Research Funds of the National Cancer Institute, Department of Health and Human Services, USA.
definition: A cohort of current and former radiologic technologists in the United States, women and men certified by the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists for at least two years between 1926 and 1982, assembled in 1982 by the US National Cancer Institute with the University of Minnesota and the Registry and followed through four mailed questionnaires (1983–1989, 1994–1998, 2003–2005 and 2012–2014), to assess risks of cancer and other diseases from protracted low-dose occupational and personal medical ionising radiation and other exposures.

note: Tier D (D314), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: USRT itself, one of several cohorts in this menopausal-hormone-therapy/breast-cancer meta-analysis; classified 'Mixed' design in the paper's characteristics table (not quotable). Name expansion and purpose come from P2 (a 2016 USRT-specific paper), not P1 itself. No unit states an enrolment date; P2's numbers describe a 1983-2008 outcomes-ascertainment window, not necessarily when the cohort was established. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, acronym, type, country (from the name) and example are right. The label copied the PGS Catalog's singular 'US Radiologic Technologist Study'; the study's own name, on the NCI page, is 'U.S. Radiologic Technologists (USRT) Study' (also 'the Rad Tech Study'), and BCAC papers write 'US Radiologic Technologists Study'. label: Vanderbilt Atrial Fibrillation Ablation Registry
other synonyms: Vanderbilt AF Ablation Registry
example title: Whole genome sequencing analysis of body mass index identifies novel African ancestry-specific risk allele.
example quote: NHLBI TOPMed: Vanderbilt Atrial Fibrillation Ablation Registry (VAFAR)
definition: A prospective clinical and genetic biorepository at Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, Tennessee, founded in 2011, that enrols adults scheduled for catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation, recording their medical history, pre-ablation imaging and procedure details, collecting blood for DNA at the time of ablation and following them for arrhythmia recurrence at 3, 6 and 12 months, to identify predictors of response to ablation and to support research on the mechanisms of atrial fibrillation.
location quote: Vanderbilt University, Nashville, TN,USA.
parent quote: This study is part of the NHLBI Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) Whole Genome Sequencing Program.
note: Tier D (D315), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: VAFAR itself, one of many TOPMed-affiliated cohorts contributing WGS/phenotype data to this BMI GWAS. Design/purpose taken from P2 (a 2017 sub-phenotype paper on VAFAR subjects), not from P1. No unit gives a location beyond the name 'Vanderbilt' or an enrolment date, so no country is asserted. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, acronym, type, parent (TOPMed, COHO:0000985) and example study are right. The label used the contraction 'AF'; the registry's own registration (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02404415, acronym VAFAR) and P1 spell it 'Vanderbilt Atrial Fibrillation Ablation Registry', so that is the label and the PGS Catalog form a synonym. The definition was built from one sub-phenotype paper and misplaced the registry's purpose; the registration and dbGaP phs000997 describe it: founded in 2011 at Vanderbilt, prospectively enrolling adults scheduled for AF ablation, with blood for DNA at ablation, procedure details and follow-up at 3, 6 and 12 months, to find predictors of response to ablation. The draft asserted no country, but dbGaP and the registration place it at Vanderbilt University (Medical Center), Nashville, Tennessee, USA. The parent and example quotes ran across acknowledgement headings into the next study's heading and 'We thank Dr.'; the parent quote is replaced by dbGaP's TOPMed statement and the example by the VAFAR heading alone, the only place P1 names it. Separate from the other Vanderbilt atrial fibrillation study in TOPMed, VU_AF ('Vanderbilt Genetic Basis of Atrial Fibrillation', this review's D319), and from BioVU (COHO:0000417). The country quote is dbGaP's attribution line for the study (the investigator's institution); the ClinicalTrials.gov record lists the one site, Vanderbilt University Medical Center, Nashville, Tennessee, United States, but only as structured data. PMID:28880943 includes ablations from 2003, before the 2011 founding date given by dbGaP and ClinicalTrials.gov; the definition follows the registry's own records. No duplicate in COHO or this review.

input name: The Vietnam Era Twin Study of Aging
label: Vietnam Era Twin Study of Aging
other synonyms: The Vietnam Era Twin Study of Aging
example title: Genome-wide association study meta-analysis of neurofilament light (NfL) levels in blood reveals novel loci related to neurodegeneration.
example quote: In short, genotypes for VETSA participants were generated using the Illumina HumanOmniExpress-24 v1.0A BeadChip.
definition: A longitudinal behavioural genetic study of cognitive and brain aging in men, and later of early risk of mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease, whose participants are twins randomly selected from the Vietnam Era Twin Registry of male twin pairs who both served in the US military between 1965 and 1975, recruited in their 50s and assessed at two sites, San Diego and Boston, from 2003, with follow-up waves every 5 to 6 years.
location quote: VETSA participants live throughout the US.
parent quote: seven cohorts from the Cohorts for heart and aging research in genomic epidemiology (CHARGE) consortium (the Framingham Heart Study (FHS), the Rotterdam Study (RSI and RSII), the MEMENTO Study, the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) Study, the Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS), the Vietnam Era Twin Study of Aging (VETSA) Study
note: Tier D (D316), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: VETSA, the Vietnam Era Twin Study of Aging, for both studies. P1 misspells the acronym as VESTA twice (D316.1, D316.10); confirmed as VETSA by P2-P7. Not to be confused with the Vietnam Era Twin Registry (VETR), the source registry VETSA samples from. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, acronym, country and example study are right. The label carried the PGS Catalog's leading article; the study's own papers title it 'VETSA: The Vietnam Era Twin Study of Aging' and 'Current Status of the Vietnam Era Twin Study of Aging (VETSA)', so the article goes and the PGS form is kept as a synonym. The definition's 'assessed together from midlife onward' was vague and missed when (wave 1 from 2003), where (two sites, San Diego and Boston), how participants were chosen (random selection from the Registry's prior study, in their 50s) and the later focus on early risk of MCI and Alzheimer's disease. The parent was missing: two CHARGE GWAS name VETSA as one of the CHARGE consortium's cohorts, the total-tau GWAS explicitly ('seven cohorts from the ... (CHARGE) consortium (... the Vietnam Era Twin Study of Aging (VETSA) Study ...), and the ADNI Study'). The example quote began with the previous cohort's imputation line and a section number; replaced by a clean sentence from the same supplement. VETSA samples the Vietnam Era Twin Registry (VETR, housed at the VA Puget Sound Health Care System, Seattle), which is not in COHO; if the registry is ever minted, VETSA becomes isSubCohortOf it. 'VESTA' in PMID:39251807 is a misspelling in that paper, not a database tag, so it is not added. The CHARGE link matches COHO's existing link for the Rhineland Study (COHO:0000386) and the check of D091 (BiDirect), both from the NfL GWAS.

label: VHIR-FMT-Barcelona
other synonyms: Barcelona GWAs Study
example title: Multi-trait association analysis reveals shared genetic loci between Alzheimer's disease and cardiovascular traits.
example quote: Stroke Malik et al., 2018 Nature Genetics METASTROKE, NINDS-SIGN, CHARGE, EPIC, AIDHS/SDS, VHIR-FMT-Barcelona, Biobank Japan
definition: A case-control collection from Barcelona, Spain, of European-ancestry patients with non-lacunar ischaemic stroke confirmed by neuroimaging within 7 days, a subset of those enrolled in the Genetic contribution to functional Outcome and Disability after Stroke (GODS) project, and of controls over 40 years old without ischaemic stroke, collected in Barcelona primary care centres and Spanish network hospitals for the ISSYS and GRECOS studies, genotyped together and used as a case-control set in ischaemic stroke genome-wide association studies.
location quote: VHIR-FMT-BARCELONA Spain HumanCore ExomeChip EUR 545 320
note: Tier D (D317), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: Deferred; research settles it. In the tagged paper VHIR-FMT-Barcelona is one of the MEGASTROKE contributing studies (Malik et al. 2018) whose stroke summary statistics the AD-cardiovascular multi-trait analysis reused. MEGASTROKE's Supplementary Note describes it: 'The Barcelona cohort is a subset of Caucasian Ischemic stroke subjects that were enrolled as a part of the Genetic contribution to functional Outcome and Disability after Stroke (GODs) project', non-lacunar cases confirmed by neuroimaging in the first 7 days, with controls over 40 without ischaemic stroke 'collected in primary care centers from Barcelona city and some hospital in the Spanish Network' for ISSYS and GRECOS, all genotyped on the Illumina Human Core Exome chip; its acknowledgement calls it 'The Barcelona GWAs Study'. SiGN (PMID:26708676) used it as a stage II case-control set ('VHIR-FMT-BARCELONA Spain HumanCore ExomeChip'). No fuller name exists, so the label is the name MEGASTROKE, SiGN and both catalogues use. The example quote is shortened to the span naming the study. Parent: none. It was a SiGN stage II look-up set, not a SiGN (COHO:0000651) member, and MEGASTROKE is not in COHO. VHIR is the Vall d'Hebron Institut de Recerca (MEGASTROKE: 'The Vall d'Hebron Research Institute (VHIR) cohort'); FMT is presumably the Fundació Docència i Recerca Mútua Terrassa, whose Stroke Pharmacogenomics and Genetics group shares the investigators (MEGASTROKE and SiGN affiliations), but no source expands it, so it stays out of the definition. Not the same as Barcelona-1 (COHO:0000369, a Mútua Terrassa memory clinic cohort), the ADHD-VHIR blood-donor controls in MEGASTROKE, or E502 HUVH (a Hospital Universitari Vall d'Hebron sample in the PGS Catalog's ovarian and breast cancer score records). The synonym 'Barcelona GWAs Study' keeps the source's capitalisation; drop it if acknowledgement names are not wanted.

input name: GEDI Virginia Twin Study on Adolescent Behavioral Development
label: Virginia Twin Study of Adolescent Behavioral Development
other synonyms: Virginia Twin Study on Adolescent Behavioral Development|GEDI Virginia Twin Study on Adolescent Behavioral Development
example title: Genome-wide association meta-analysis of childhood ADHD symptoms and diagnosis identifies new loci and potential effector genes.
example quote: Virginia Twin Study of Adolescent Behavioral Development VTSABD
definition: A population-based, cohort-sequential longitudinal study of European-ancestry twin pairs born in 1974-1983, ascertained at ages 8 to 16 through the state and participating private schools of Virginia, United States, who with their parents were assessed by psychiatric interviews and questionnaires in four waves about 18 months apart and again in their mid-20s, to study genetic and environmental influences on the development of child and adolescent psychopathology and substance use.
location quote: The VTSABD is a cohort-longitudinal study of twins born between 1974 and 1983 ascertained primarily through the state school system and participating private schools in Virginia.
note: Tier D (D318), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Parent left for later: memberOf review name E384 (Gene-Environment Development Initiative), not minted in this run; quote: "Gene-Environment-Development Initiative -GEDI – Virginia Commonwealth University (VTSABD; dbGAP in progress) was supported by the National Institute on Drug Abuse (U01DA024413, R01DA025109)" (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC6430207/fullTextXML). P1: VTSABD, also headed 'VTSABD (GEDI)', the Virginia twin study whose existing data were genotyped via the GEDI initiative's VCU arm. PGS Catalog name 'GEDI Virginia Twin Study...' combines the GEDI genotyping initiative with VTSABD's own name. GEDI is tracked separately as tier-E row E384 (possible aggregation) and may become VTSABD's memberOf parent once minted. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type and country are right. The definition restated the ADHD paper's one-sentence description and left out who (European-ancestry twin pairs born 1974-1983, aged 8-16, with their parents), how they were found (through Virginia's state and private schools) and the design (four waves about 18 months apart, then a fifth in the mid-20s). The parent was left open: the NIDA Gene-Environment-Development Initiative (GEDI, tier-E row E384) is a consortium of four longitudinal data sets (VTSABD, the Great Smoky Mountains Study, Caring for Children in the Community and the Christchurch Health and Development Study; PMID:23461817), and VTSABD is its Virginia Commonwealth University component. note: Tier D (D337), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ALEXANDROS, the Chilean series in this Argentinian-and-Chilean Alzheimer's GWAS (FONDECYT-funded); P2: 'the ALEXANDROS cohorts', followed up from a 2000 baseline for dementia risk. Definition rests on P2's abstract (a leptin/dementia follow-up of 'the ALEXANDROS cohorts', D337.8), not a dedicated profile paper; plural 'cohorts' wording is a small doubt. Argentinian samples in P1 are a separate tag, not ALEXANDROS. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity and type are right: in PMID:37985413 the tag is the Alexandros longitudinal study of INTA, University of Chile, which supplied the Chilean controls. The label was only the acronym, although the study's papers expand it: 'Active Life Expectancy, Ageing, and Disability Related to Obesity Study' (PMC5549118, 2013), with later variants 'Active Life Expectancy, Aging and Disability Related to Obesity Study' (PMC11264702) and 'Active Life Expectancy, Aging and Disorders Related to Obesity Study' (PMC9319397), which become synonyms. The definition was built from one leptin paper's abstract: a 2000 baseline holds only for the SABE participants; the study was designed to study disability associated with obesity (later also dementia), not dementia as such; the place is Santiago, not Chile at large; and the three constituent cohorts were missing. Fixed from the study's descriptions: SABE Santiago participants born before 1940 (recruited 1999–2000), the ALEXANDROS cohort of people born 1940–1948 from public primary health care centre registries (2005–2008), and the ISAPRES cohort of high socioeconomic status from private health insurance registries (recruitment given as 2005 in PMC8055355 and 2007 in PMC9319397, so no year is stated). The example quote was a funding sentence; replaced by the Methods sentence showing the controls came from the study. Treated as one cohort, not an aggregation: a single INTA study with one protocol that recruited three samples and follows them together; the papers call the pooled sample 'the ALEXANDROS cohorts' or 'the Alexandros cohort' interchangeably. The name ALEXANDROS also denotes the second of its three cohorts (the 1940–1948 primary care sample), which is not separately tagged anywhere. Host, not in the definition because no source states it outright: every paper is from the Institute of Nutrition and Food Technology (INTA), University of Chile, whose ethics board approved the study, with FONDECYT grants 1080589 and 1130947. P1: GGLAD (n=2,952), one of three African-ancestry case-control datasets (with ADAGES, POAAGG) combined in a discovery mega-analysis. P2: GGLAD again as a summary-stats dataset in further GBMI-IGGC-GGLAD meta-analyses; same cohort throughout. The draft gave no countries; eleven are added (Morocco and Mali are not in gaz_xrefs.tsv). The example stays on GCST90455614, but the quote is now the mega-analysis sentence, which shows the data being used, rather than the data-availability line. Member cohorts for hasCohort links from this aggregation, all named in the JAMA Table ('First Validation Women’s Health Initiative 23.1 20.8 1720 6067 Kaiser Permanente GERA 23.3 18.4 300 2700 ADAGES 24.3 21.4 1890 2205', https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6865235/): Women's Health Initiative (COHO:0000409), GERA (COHO:0000431) and ADAGES (review row D355). The JAMA Table names neither: its first-validation 'United States' collection may be BioMe, since the consortium includes Mount Sinai investigators, but without the eAppendix this cannot be confirmed, so no link is proposed. note: Tier D (D340), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ICON7, one of four Phase III trials (with CALGB 80303, 40503, 80405) pooled in this bevacizumab-survival GWAS meta-analysis; consistent meaning throughout. CALGB (COHO:0000022) is a co-tagged sibling trial group in P1, not ICON7's parent - the Gynecologic Cancer InterGroup/ICON series isn't a listed candidate or batch row, so parent is left null. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, verdict and type are right: ICON7 is the Gynecologic Cancer InterGroup phase 3 trial NCT00483782 / ISRCTN91273375, and it is the tag's meaning in PMID:34528705. The label was only the acronym; the trial team's papers expand it as 'The International Collaboration on Ovarian Neoplasms 7 (ICON7) trial' (PMC3596061), so the label follows COHO's pattern for named trials. note: Tier D (D342), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because the abstract never names the cohort; the paper settles it. P1's medRxiv preprint (same title and authors, collective author 'Parkinson Research Alliance of India (PRAI)') profiles '674 PD subjects predominantly with earlier onset PD from the Parkinson’s Research Alliance of India (PRAI) cohort' and refers to 'the previous clinical characterization of this cohort', its ref. 36, PMID:33685545 ('Clinical Study of 668 Indian Subjects with Juvenile, Young, and Early Onset Parkinson's Disease', same investigators, collective author PRAI). The investigators name this study 'Genetics Of Parkinson’s in India - Young Onset Parkinson’s Disease (GOPI-YOPD)', 'a prospective multicenter, collaborative study to analyze clinical and genetic patterns of JOPD, YOPD, and EOPD' with 'a cohort of 668' (MDS 2022 abstract). The Parkinson Research Alliance of India itself is not a cohort: it is a society of movement disorder clinicians, registered in Hyderabad in May 2015 (prai.in/about-us). So the term is the cohort, named by its project name, with PRAI (the GWAS tag) and GOPI-YOPD as acronyms. In P1 the tag PRAI denotes the cases and GAsP2 (GenomeAsia Phase 2) the controls (GWAS Catalog: 515 cases, 1,363 controls). The example quote comes from the medRxiv preprint of PMID:38014556, because the published version cannot be fetched; replace it with the published sentence if someone reads it. The tag PRAI is the society's acronym. PRAI also runs the Pan India Registry for Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PAIR-PSP; 1,035 PSP patients enrolled April 2021 to July 2025, PMC13339298), a different sample that is not in COHO. If PAIR-PSP is ever added, do not give it this term's PRAI acronym without an editor note. Recruitment dates for GOPI-YOPD are not given in any source I could read, beyond 'a 2-year' study published in 2021; the preprint says recruitment of more PD and control samples 'for the PRAI cohort is in progress'. example quote: Follow-UP study of patients with critical COVID-19/COVID-19 Cohort Study of the University Hospital of the Technical University Munich (SweCovid/COMRI)
definition: A study of patients with critical COVID-19 admitted from March 2020 to the intensive care unit of Uppsala University Hospital, Sweden, who were enrolled in the prospective observational PronMed cohort and invited to follow-up three to six months after discharge, in which researchers at Uppsala University and Karolinska Institutet investigate the mechanisms of acute and long-term organ dysfunction in critical COVID-19, including its host genetics.
location quote: The discovery set was taken from the Pronmed cohort that consists of 374 critically ill COVID-19 patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) at Uppsala University Hospital, in Uppsala, Sweden between March 13, 2020 and June 30, 2021 (Fig. 2A).
parent quote: Data for initial discovery GWASs (Long COVID HGI data freeze 4) was collected by DBDS, EstBB, FinnGen, GEN-COVID, GENCOV, MexGen-COVID (Supplementary Tables 1, 3–8 and 12), ALSPAC, BoSCO, BQC19, EXCEED, GCAT (COVICAT), Genotek, GOLD, Helix, Ioannina, IrCovid, JapanTaskForce, Lifelines, MoBa, MSCIC, PMBB, SweCovid, COMRI, TiKoCo, TwinsUK, UKB and Understanding Society (Supplementary Tables 11 and 12).
note: Tier D (D344), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred, and its reading of the tag was right: SweCovid-COMRI is one pooled long-COVID dataset from two unrelated hospital cohorts, listed in PMID:40399555 as 'Follow-UP study of patients with critical COVID-19/COVID-19 Cohort Study of the University Hospital of the Technical University Munich (SweCovid/COMRI)'. The main text also lists 'SweCovid, COMRI' as separate contributors. Research settles each cohort. SweCovid is the Uppsala University and Karolinska Institutet study ('The study SweCovid, received funding from the National SciLifeLab-KAW COVID-19 Research Program in both 2020 and 2021 to investigate the mechanisms of acute and long-term organ dysfunction in critical COVID-19.', SciLifeLab) of critically ill COVID-19 patients in the Uppsala University Hospital ICU. Its patients are those of the PronMed study: both carry the same ethics approval ('SweCovid was approved by the National Ethical Review Agency (EPM; 2020-01623).', PMC8631592; 'included in the PronMed-study, approved by the National Ethical Review Agency (EPM; No. 2020–01623).', PMC8773415), and the long-COVID supplement describes SweCovid's data as 'Pronmed/FUP-COVID', the acute study and its follow-up. COMRI is the prospective COVID-19 cohort and registry of the TUM university hospital in Munich (see extra). So the tag becomes an acronym of two new terms, each with an editor note naming the other. The draft's countries (Sweden and Germany, quoting only the table cell 'Sweden/Germany') split one per term. Both terms get memberOf COHO:0000238 (COVID-19 HGI), as the checks of this paper's other contributors did. The example quote is now the open-access main-text name list; the supplement quote ended in a person's initial. Review row E1076 (PGS Catalog id SweCovid, 'The genetic predisposition to severe COVID-19') is this SweCovid study and should become 'same as D344'. The PGS REST API has no scores for it, and I could not find where the name comes from, so it is not used as a label here. The Uppsala team writes 'The SweCOVID study' (long-COVID supplement acknowledgements), and SciLifeLab writes 'The study SweCovid'. The label 'SweCovid study' follows COHO's pattern for acronym-named studies (e.g. 'BELLINI trial'); the plain acronym SweCovid is kept as an acronym. PronMed's ethics approval is Dnr 2017-043, with 2020-01623 among its later amendments (long-COVID supplement), which suggests PronMed began before COVID-19 as a general ICU study; the COVID-19 papers use 'Pronmed cohort' only for its COVID-19 patients, which is what the synonyms mean. PMID:36514076 adds Sahlgrenska University Hospital patients to one PronMed-based analysis, but SweCovid itself is described as 'data from COVID-19 patients at Uppsala University Hospital' (SciLifeLab), so only Sweden and Uppsala are stated. The long-COVID dataset's controls came from PsyCourse (review row D052), which is not given this tag.

label: Placental Abruption Genetic Epidemiology study
other synonyms: Placental Abruption Genetic Epidemiology
example title: Genetic association study of preterm birth and gestational age in a population-based case-control study in Peru.
example quote: This study was conducted among participants of the Placental Abruption Genetic Epidemiology
definition: A population-based case-control study of women admitted for obstetric care at seven hospitals in Lima, Peru, between March 2013 and December 2015, with cases of placental abruption and of preterm birth and controls selected at random from women delivering at the same hospitals, designed to investigate the genetic and environmental determinants of placental abruption and other adverse pregnancy outcomes.
location quote: Participants of the Placental Abruption Genetic Epidemiology (PAGE) study, a population based case-control study of PA conducted in Lima, Peru, were genotyped using the Illumina HumanCore-24 BeadChip platform.
note: Tier D (D346), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because the abstract never names the cohort; the paper settles it. P1's medRxiv preprint (same title and authors; the journal version is closed) says in its Methods that the study was conducted among participants of the Placental Abruption Genetic Epidemiology study (PAGE), a case-control study from Lima, Peru, designed to investigate the genetic and environmental determinants of placental abruption and other adverse pregnancy outcomes such as preterm birth. This is paraphrased, because the PDF text has line numbers inside the sentence; the example quote stops before the first of them. Its GWAS used 2,212 PAGE women (933 preterm cases, 1,279 term controls), exactly the GWAS Catalog sample of GCST90271572/3 (cohort field 'PAGEPI', country of recruitment Peru). So PAGEPI is the GWAS Catalog's tag for PAGE (Placental Abruption Genetic EPIdemiology). Design from PMID:29884306 (PMC5995331): 'a population based case-control study of PA conducted in Lima, Peru', recruiting 'between March 2013 and December 2015' at seven hospitals (Instituto Nacional Materno Perinatal and the Rebagliati, San Bartolome, Hipolito Unanue, Arzobispo Loayza, Dos de Mayo and Maria Auxiliadora hospitals), with 'Controls were randomly selected from eligible pregnant women who delivered at participating hospitals'. The draft's acronym list lacked the study's own acronym PAGE. As the draft said, the triage candidate COHO:0000145 (Psoriasis Association Genetics Extension) is unrelated. The acronym PAGE is already on COHO:0000145 (Psoriasis Association Genetics Extension). Under the acronym rule both terms keep it, and both need an editor note of the usual form, one naming this Peruvian study on COHO:0000145 and one naming the Psoriasis Association Genetics Extension (COHO:0000145) on this term. PAGE is distinct from the earlier Peruvian Abruptio Placentae Epidemiology (PAPE) study in Lima ('Both PAGE and PAPE studies were independently recruited, had similar study objectives and study designs.', PMC5995331), which is not in COHO. The preprint says the study 'was administratively based' at the Swedish Medical Center, Seattle, WA, and its investigators are from Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, Universidad de San Martín de Porres and Asociación Civil PROESA (Lima). No sources state who runs it outright, so the definition leaves that out. The example quote comes from the preprint because the journal version cannot be read.

label: STORK Groruddalen
other synonyms: STORK Groruddalen study|STORK Groruddalen research programme
example title: Multi-ancestry, trans-generational GWAS meta-analysis of gestational diabetes and glycaemic traits during pregnancy reveals limited evidence of pregnancy-specific genetic effects.
example quote: Data collection for the Stork Groruddalen study was funded by The Research Council of Norway, The South-Eastern Norway Regional Health Authority and the public Child Health Clinics in Stovner, Grorud and Bjerke districts in Oslo.
definition: A population-based cohort of pregnant women of diverse ethnic origin attending three public Child Health Clinics for antenatal care in Groruddalen, a multi-ethnic area of Oslo, Norway, recruited in 2008–2010 and followed with their offspring through pregnancy and after birth, to study gestational diabetes, physical activity and obesity in pregnancy and to identify predictors of gestational diabetes and fetal growth.
location quote: This population-based cohort study was conducted at three public Child Health Clinics in Groruddalen, Oslo, Norway (12).
note: Tier D (D348), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred for want of a profile; the cohort's own papers settle it. STORK-G is STORK Groruddalen, a population-based cohort of pregnant women recruited in 2008–2010 at three public Child Health Clinics (Stovner, Grorud and Bjerke) in Groruddalen, Oslo, Norway, with a universal 75 g OGTT at week 28, run as a research programme on gestational diabetes, physical activity and obesity in pregnancy. Its own acronym 'STORK G' (used throughout the EPIPREG cohort profile) was missing, and the country Norway was not asserted. The draft's example quote was the bare tag 'STORK-G' from a table cell; replaced by a sentence of the same supplement that names the study. Not the same cohort as D329 STORK: in PMID:42225636 the tag STORK is the 'STORK Project' (pregnancies 2001-2008, OGTT at weeks 14-16 and 30-32), a separate Oslo University Hospital pregnancy cohort; both tags sit on GCST90861010 and GCST90861011. EPIPREG (the epigenome-wide DNA-methylation sub-study of European and South Asian STORK G women) is not in COHO. The paper's supplement also writes the study as 'STORKG' in effect-allele footnotes; not added as it is neither a catalogue tag nor the cohort's own form.

definition: A research biobank of patients hospitalised with COVID-19 in the Mount Sinai Health System in New York City, enrolled from April to June 2020 through daily review of new admissions together with a smaller group of healthy and hospitalised controls, whose blood was sampled repeatedly alongside routine clinical draws during their hospital stay for multi-omic study of the host response to SARS-CoV-2, and whose survivors were later surveyed for post-acute sequelae of COVID-19.
location quote: In this Correspondence, we provide an account of a 49-day period during which we built a COVID-19 research biobank with samples from patients hospitalized in a large New York City health system.
parent quote: Data for initial discovery GWASs (Long COVID HGI data freeze 4) was collected by DBDS, EstBB, FinnGen, GEN-COVID, GENCOV, MexGen-COVID (Supplementary Tables 1, 3–8 and 12), ALSPAC, BoSCO, BQC19, EXCEED, GCAT (COVICAT), Genotek, GOLD, Helix, Ioannina, IrCovid, JapanTaskForce, Lifelines, MoBa, MSCIC, PMBB, SweCovid, COMRI, TiKoCo, TwinsUK, UKB and Understanding Society (Supplementary Tables 11 and 12).
note: Tier D (D350), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: MSCIC = Mount Sinai COVID Biobank, one of many cohorts in the Long COVID HGI discovery meta-analysis (freeze 4); consistent throughout. MSCIC = 'Mount Sinai COVID Biobank' is solid (2 units); D350.9's institute line may be an author affiliation, so no country asserted. It fed the Long COVID Host Genetics Initiative's discovery meta-analysis (not in COHO, so no parent) but no population/date criteria are given. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity right, but the label is the GWAS paper's shortening: the biobank's own papers call it the 'Mount Sinai COVID-19 Biobank' (PMID:32719485, PMID:36482101), so that is the label and 'Mount Sinai COVID Biobank' a synonym. MSCIC is the Mount Sinai Clinical Intelligence Center (also written Mount Sinai COVID-19 Informatics Center), the Icahn School of Medicine group that built the biobank; the long COVID paper's supplementary study table gives the Mount Sinai COVID Biobank the IRB protocol STUDY-20-00341, the same as in PMID:36482101 and in the COVID-19 HGI exome paper's 'MSCIC' ethics section. The draft's definition restated the name plus an author affiliation and its use in host-genetics studies; the biobank is a spring-2020 collection of serial blood samples from patients hospitalised with COVID-19 across the Mount Sinai Health System, with controls and later PASC surveys. The country (United States, New York City) is stated in the biobank's own paper. The draft left out a parent, but the Long COVID HGI data freeze that used MSCIC is the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative (COHO:0000238), to which the Tirschenreuth Study was already linked with the same quote. Not BioMe (COHO:0000424, whose acronyms include 'Mount Sinai' and 'MSH'). E725 MSHS-CGI 'Mount Sinai Health System COVID-19 Genomics Initiative' is the name under which Mount Sinai's COVID-19 data entered the COVID-19 HGI papers of 2021-2022 (PMC8674144, PMC9352569), with team members who also built this biobank; it may be this biobank, or include it and BioMe COVID-19 cases, so settle it when E725 is checked.

label: Die Deutsche Diabetes Dialyse Studie
other synonyms: 4D Study|German Diabetes and Dialysis Study
example title: Lowering of Circulating Sclerostin May Increase Risk of Atherosclerosis and Its Risk Factors: Evidence From a Genome-Wide Association Meta-Analysis Followed by Mendelian Randomization.
example quote: We found that this variant showed a robust negative effect on sclerostin in all cohorts; however, the genetic effect estimate was particularly large in the 4D cohort, comprising individuals with end‐stage chronic kidney disease (CKD) (Supplementary Table 5B).
definition: A multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, begun in 1998 at dialysis centres throughout Germany, of adults aged 18–80 with type 2 diabetes who had been on maintenance haemodialysis for less than two years, which tested whether atorvastatin lowers the risk of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction and stroke, and followed its participants for a median of four years.
location quote: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, aged 18–80 years, who had received maintenance hemodialysis for less than 2 years were included by 178 dialysis centers in Germany into the 4 D study (Die Deutsche Diabetes Dialyse Studie/German Diabetes and Dialysis Study).
note: Tier D (D353), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: '4D' = the 4D cohort / Die Deutsche Diabetes Dialyse Studie, a German end-stage-CKD dialysis trial population, one of several cohorts (ALSPAC, Fenland, GOOD, HUNT, INTERVAL, LURIC, MANOLIS, OAI) in this sclerostin/atherosclerosis GWAS meta-analysis. Well documented across P2-P7 (the trial's own papers) as a German RCT of atorvastatin in diabetic haemodialysis patients; country from the cohort's own German name ('Deutsche'). PGS Catalog's other name 'DDDD' isn't seen in any evidence unit, so left out. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label and example right. The definition missed who exactly was eligible (aged 18–80, on maintenance haemodialysis for less than two years, not just 'established on haemodialysis'), that the trial was multicentre and double-blind, and when it began (1998), and it gave the design paper's planned endpoint rather than the composite that was analysed (cardiac death, stroke and non-fatal myocardial infarction). The PGS Catalog's other name DDDD is left out, but acronyms are always kept when a catalogue uses them. The country follows from the name, and an open-access quote now backs it. DDDD appears only as the PGS Catalog's other name for the cohort; it is kept as an acronym under the rule, and no COHO term or review name uses it. Not related to D189 4D-SZ.

input name: African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study
label: African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study
example title: A multi-cohort genome-wide association study in African ancestry individuals reveals risk loci for primary open-angle glaucoma.
example quote: This study included three African ancestry datasets in the discovery analyses (n=11,275): (1) African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study study (n=1,999), (2) Genetics of Glaucoma in People of African Descent consortium (n=2,952), and (3) Primary Open-Angle African American Glaucoma Genetics study (n=6,324).
definition: A multicentre prospective observational cohort study, which from 2003 enrolled people of African descent and of European descent without glaucoma, with suspected glaucoma or with glaucoma at the University of California San Diego, the New York Eye and Ear Infirmary and the University of Alabama at Birmingham, United States, and followed them with repeated visual function testing and optic nerve imaging to identify why glaucoma onset and progression differ between people of African and European descent. Its third phase (ADAGES III) recruited, in 2014–2016 at five US centres, patients with primary open-angle glaucoma and controls of African or European descent, with DNA, to study the genetics of the disease in people of African descent.
location quote: There were 3266 glaucoma patients and controls without glaucoma of African or European descent recruited from five study centers in different regions of the United States.
note: Tier D (D355), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ADAGES = African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study, one of three African-ancestry discovery datasets (with GGLAD, POAAGG) meta-analysed for primary open-angle glaucoma; consistent throughout. Definition drawn from P4, ADAGES' own 'design and baseline data' paper; sizes and comparator DIGS cohort omitted per the no-numbers rule. No location stated in any open unit, so no country asserted despite 'African descent' in the name (ancestry, not a place). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity and label right. The definition wrongly made ADAGES a cohort of glaucoma patients of African descent: it enrolled people of African and of European descent who were healthy, glaucoma suspects or glaucoma patients (January 2003 to July 2006) at three named US centres, and its genetic third phase (ADAGES III, 2014–2016, five US centres), whose design and genetics papers the tagged GWAS cites for its ADAGES dataset, was left out. The United States is stated in open text (the draft asserted no country). The example quote described an earlier ADAGES GWAS finding; replaced by the tagged paper's statement that ADAGES was one of its three discovery datasets. Not the same as the Diagnostic Innovations in Glaucoma Study (DIGS), UCSD's European-descent comparison cohort combined with ADAGES, nor as D494 POAAGG or the GGLAD consortium, its co-datasets in the tagged GWAS; none is a parent.

input name: Admixture and Risk of Acute Leukemia
label: ADMIxture and Risk of Acute Leukemia Study
other synonyms: Admixture and Risk of Acute Leukemia|ADMIRAL Study
example title: Genome-wide association study of childhood B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia reveals novel African ancestry-specific susceptibility loci.
example quote: In this study, we show differences in the genetic architecture of childhood B-ALL risk in African ancestral populations with an analysis of 4200 African American children, including 840 B-ALL cases, as a part of the ADMIxture and Risk of Acute Leukemia (ADMIRAL) Study.
definition: A case-control study of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia in Black or African American children and young adults diagnosed at ages 0–25 in the United States, run from the University of Minnesota, which gathered germline DNA of cases from Children's Oncology Group frontline trials, from newborn dried blood spots held by the Michigan BioTrust for Health and linked to the state cancer registry, and from hospital leukaemia biobanks, with controls matched on sex and ancestry from Michigan newborn blood spots and paediatric well-child visits. It investigates African ancestry-specific genetic susceptibility to B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia and its relation to disease subtype and survival.
location quote: Archived newborn dried blood spots (DBS) with matching birth certificate information held by the Michigan BioTrust for Health were obtained for cases and calendar birth year-, sex-, and race/ethnicity-matched (based on mother’s race/ethnicity) controls with no cancer history were obtained as a part of a larger population-based case-control study with linked cancer registry information through the Michigan Cancer Surveillance Program
note: Tier D (D356), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ADMIRAL = ADMIxture and Risk of Acute Leukemia Study, an African-ancestry childhood B-ALL case-control study; the row's only paper, consistent throughout (with an external control set 'ZOE2.0'). Cases are drawn partly from COG frontline ALL trials (D356.5, D356.22) but no unit calls ADMIRAL a member/part of COG, so no parent set. All size/count figures omitted per the no-numbers rule; only the 0-25 age range is kept. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym and example right; the definition was close but missed where (the United States: Michigan's newborn blood-spot and cancer-registry linkage, hospital biobanks at CHOP, MSKCC, UT Southwestern, UAB and Baylor), who runs it (University of Minnesota, NCI grant R01 CA239701) and that controls come from Michigan newborn blood spots and Baylor well-child visits, not only 'ancestry- and sex-matched controls'. No country was asserted although every source and site is in the US. The PGS Catalog name 'Admixture and Risk of Acute Leukemia' differs from the label only in capitalisation and the missing 'Study', and is kept as a synonym. Not a sub-cohort of the Children's Oncology Group (COHO:0000771): ADMIRAL takes cases from COG trials but also from Michigan and five hospital biobanks, and no source calls it part of COG. A 2026 profile of the Childhood Cancer and Leukemia International Consortium (PMID:42628293, closed) matches the name in Europe PMC and may list ADMIRAL as a member; CLIC is not in COHO. The external ZOE 2.0 controls tagged on the same study are a separate North Carolina dental caries cohort.

label: Amish Family Osteoporosis Study
example title: WNT16 influences bone mineral density, cortical bone thickness, bone strength, and osteoporotic fracture risk.
example quote: The Amish Family Osteoporosis Study (AFOS) study was designed to identify genetic determinants of osteoporosis in the Old Order Amish (OOA) population from Lancaster County, PA USA [49], [50].
definition: A family study of the Old Order Amish of Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, United States, begun by the University of Maryland in 1997, which identified Amish adults with osteoporosis by bone mineral density screening and recruited their first-degree relatives aged 20 and over and their spouses, measuring bone density by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, to find genetic and clinical determinants of osteoporosis and bone health in large multigenerational families.
location quote: The Amish Family Osteoporosis Study (AFOS) study was designed to identify genetic determinants of osteoporosis in the Old Order Amish (OOA) population from Lancaster County, PA USA [49], [50].
parent quote: To date, we have screened ∼6500 Amish adults for a variety of risk factors related to cardiovascular disease (Mitchell et al. 2008), diabetes (Hsueh et al. 2000), and osteoporosis (Streeten et al. 2006) as part of the Amish Complex Disease Research Program (ACDRP).
note: Tier D (D357), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: AFOS = Amish Family Osteoporosis Study, one of several skeletal-phenotype cohorts (with AOGC, CAMOS, GOOD, TwinsUK, UFO) in this WNT16/bone-density GWAS meta-analysis; consistent throughout. Tier D (D366), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. location quote: We establish the German AugUR study (Age-related diseases: understanding genetic and non-genetic influences - a study at the University of Regensburg), a prospective study in the mobile elderly general population in and around Regensburg in eastern Bavaria.
note: Tier D (D368), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: AugUR = one of ten population-based cohorts (with ARIC, CHS, GHS-I/II, IAMDGC, KORA, LIFE-Adult, NICOLA, UKB, WHI) meta-analysed for early age-related macular degeneration; P2: AugUR's own dedicated protocol paper, consistent. The automatic 'institution?' hint is wrong: AugUR is a named prospective cohort/research platform based at, not simply named for, the University of Regensburg (D368.39, D368.42). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country and example study right. The definition followed the 2015 protocol's plans (3,000 people via registration offices) and missed what happened: recruitment in two independent baseline surveys, AugUR1 in 2013-2015 and AugUR2 in 2017-2019, from random samples of the city and county registries, examined at the University Hospital Regensburg, with follow-up (PMID:37721739). The study also uses a German expansion of its acronym, 'Altersbezogene Untersuchungen zur Gesundheit der Universität Regensburg' (PMID:37721739), added as a synonym. The example quote was about an earlier AugUR finding cited in the discussion; replaced with the methods sentence saying AugUR baseline data were used in this analysis. AugUR contributes to several genetics consortia (e.g. the early AMD meta-analysis here); no single consortium membership is asserted as a parent. AugUR1 and AugUR2 are its two baseline surveys, not separate cohorts.

location quote: The study took place in Bambuí, Brazil.
parent quote: We performed admixture mapping (followed by fine-mapping) of BMI using data of ~2.3 million SNPs for three Brazilian population-based cohorts, from Northeast (Salvador), Southeast (Bambuí), and South (Pelotas), with distinct admixture and socio-demographic backgrounds, studied by the EPIGEN-Brazil Initiative (https://epigen.grude.ufmg.br,).
note: Tier D (D369), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: BAMBUI = the Bambuí (Brazil) Cohort Study of Ageing itself, one of eight ancestry-diverse 'test GWAS' cohorts (with AADM, REGARDS, WHI-AA, BIOME-AA/HA, HCHS/SOL, SHS) used to validate a multi-ancestry kidney-function polygenic score; matches its own profile papers (P2-P7). Consistent across P1 and six independent profile/analysis papers naming the same Bambuí, Brazil, elderly cohort; accent/spelling varies (Bambui/Bambuí/Bambuì) across sources, kept as the same name, not separate synonyms. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country (with its quote) and example right. The parent was missing: Bambuí is one of the three population-based cohorts of the EPIGEN-Brazil Initiative (COHO:0000062, whose other cohort Pelotas, COHO:0000739, is already linked with the same quote), and the example paper's BAMBUI data are the EPIGEN-Brazil genotypes ('the EPIGEN-Brazil Initiative is funded by...'). The definition's 'established in 1997 and followed for about a decade' was one paper's 10-year analysis window; the design is a census of all residents aged 60 and over on 1 January 1997, a February-May 1997 baseline, and annual follow-up (PMID:23251690). The cohort's other name and acronym, Bambuí Health and Aging Study (BHAS), used in many of its papers, was missing. The name BHAS (Bambuí Health and Aging Study) appears in the titles of several cohort papers (e.g. PMID:25931817, PMID:17934638) and as '(BHAS)' after 'Bambuí (Brazil) Cohort Study of Aging' in PMID:23251690. Accent variants (Bambui, Bambuí, Bambuì) are all in use; the main ones are kept as synonyms.

label: Berlin Aging Study II
note: Tier D (D370), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred for want of text; research settles it: both the GWAS tag and the PGS Catalog id BASE denote the Berlin Aging Study II (COHO:0000887), not the original 1990s Berlin Aging Study that the PGS Catalog's name suggests. input name: The Biology, Affect, Stress, Imaging and Cognition Study
label: Biology, Affect, Stress, Imaging and Cognition study
other synonyms: The Biology, Affect, Stress, Imaging and Cognition Study
example title: Genome-wide association analyses identify distinct genetic architectures for early-onset and late-onset depression.
example quote: BASIC: The Biology, Affect, Stress, Imaging and Cognition (BASIC) study recruited 5,492 pregnant women from the Uppsala Hospital University (Uppsala, Sweden) and followed them and their children from pregnancy to one year postpartum between 2012 and 201911 .
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of pregnant women in Uppsala County, Sweden, invited at their routine ultrasound examination at gestational week 16–18 at Uppsala University Hospital from September 2009 to November 2018 and followed to one year postpartum with web surveys, biological samples and medical-record data, to study the biopsychosocial causes and predictors of perinatal depression.
location quote: From September 2009 to November 2018, the BASIC study at Uppsala University Hospital, Sweden, has enrolled 5492 women, in 6478 pregnancies, of which 46.3% first-time pregnancies and with an average age of 31.5 years.
note: Tier D (D371), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: BASIC, the Swedish BASIC pregnancy/perinatal-depression cohort, included as one input group in the depression GWAS meta-analysis. P1 itself doesnt name BASIC; definition rests on P1s supplement (D371.8), which cites the 2019 BMJ Open cohort-profile paper. P2s abstract gives a differing 2010-2015 participation window; not used. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity is right. The definition took its dates from the GWAS supplement's one-line note ('between 2012 and 2019'), but the cohort profile says enrolment ran from September 2009 to November 2018, with the last follow-up in November 2019. The note also said mothers were followed 'with their children'. In fact BASIC follows the women from gestational week 16–18 to one year postpartum; the children are followed in a separate study, U-BIRTH. The definition now gives the recruitment route (all pregnant women in Uppsala County invited at the routine ultrasound at Uppsala University Hospital), the data collected and the purpose, from the profile. The label began with the article 'The', which is not part of the name. The profile calls it 'the Biology, Affect, Stress, Imaging and Cognition (BASIC) study'. The PGS Catalog's form of the name is kept as a synonym. I replaced the country quote with the profile's sentence; the old one was also acceptable. No duplicate in COHO or in this review. BASICMAR (D087) is an unrelated Barcelona stroke database. No parent: the GWAS pools BASIC with PREFECT, iCBT and STAGE for its analysis, but no named aggregation.

label: Baltimore Breast Cancer Study
example title: Associations between age of menarche and genetic variation in women of African descent: genome-wide association study and polygenic score analysis.
example quote: The Root consortium is comprised of six epidemiologic studies of breast cancer in women of African ancestry: the Nigerian Breast Cancer Study (Ibadan, Nigeria); the Barbados National Cancer Study (Barbados); the Southern Community Cohort (southern United States); the Baltimore Breast Cancer Study (Baltimore, United States); the Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study (Detroit and Pennsylvania, United States); and the Chicago Cancer Prone Study (Chicago, United States).
definition: A case-control study of breast cancer in the greater Baltimore area, Maryland, United States, in which incident breast cancer cases and controls frequency-matched to them on race and age were recruited from February 1993 to August 2003 at six hospitals, including the University of Maryland Medical Center and the Baltimore Veterans Affairs Medical Center, to identify and characterise markers of disease aggressiveness and poor outcome.
location quote: The Root consortium is comprised of six epidemiologic studies of breast cancer in women of African ancestry: the Nigerian Breast Cancer Study (Ibadan, Nigeria); the Barbados National Cancer Study (Barbados); the Southern Community Cohort (southern United States); the Baltimore Breast Cancer Study (Baltimore, United States); the Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study (Detroit and Pennsylvania, United States); and the Chicago Cancer Prone Study (Chicago, United States).
parent quote: The Root consortium is comprised of six epidemiologic studies of breast cancer in women of African ancestry: the Nigerian Breast Cancer Study (Ibadan, Nigeria); the Barbados National Cancer Study (Barbados); the Southern Community Cohort (southern United States); the Baltimore Breast Cancer Study (Baltimore, United States); the Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study (Detroit and Pennsylvania, United States); and the Chicago Cancer Prone Study (Chicago, United States).
note: Tier D (D372), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: BBCS_c denotes the Baltimore Breast Cancer Study, one of six African-ancestry breast-cancer studies pooled in the Root consortium for this menarche-age GWAS. Member of the Root consortium (D372.1), a defined 6-study umbrella; Root/ROOT is tier-D row D056, not in this batch, so parent left null. Little detail on BBCS_c itself beyond location and disease focus; only P1 evidence available. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronyms, country and example are right. The definition only said the study is a member of the Root consortium and is based in Baltimore. BBCS has its own descriptions (Huo et al., Carcinogenesis 2012, and the AABCG supplementary note): a case-control study designed to find markers of breast cancer aggressiveness and poor outcome, with incident cases and race- and age-matched controls recruited from February 1993 to August 2003 at six Baltimore-area hospitals. The definition now says so. It no longer describes the study as African-ancestry only: only its African American participants went into Root. The parent was left null because Root (D056) is not in this batch. D056 has been checked as a new aggregation, so the membership is now set, with the P1 sentence naming both. Shared acronym: BBCS is also an acronym of the Brescia Bladder Cancer Study (COHO:0000815, acronyms BBCS_b and BBCS). Both terms need the editor note 'The acronym BBCS also denotes …'. PGS-only name E082 (BBCS = British Breast Cancer Study) is a third cohort with this acronym. BBCS is very probably the early (1993–2003) recruitment of the NCI Laboratory of Human Carcinogenesis's 'NCI-Maryland Breast Cancer Study'. That study used the same hospitals, the same years and the same intramural funding, and continued recruiting in 2012–2019 (PMC10628736, PMC11851241). No source says outright that the two are the same, so I did not add it as a synonym. It is unrelated to the NCI-Maryland prostate cancer study (D273). PGS Catalog caution for E082: sample set PSS000995 (Du et al. 2021, PMID:33769540, the African-ancestry breast cancer PRS evaluation) lists PGS id 'BBCS', named 'British Breast Cancer Study', next to exactly the other Root members (BNCS, NigBCS, CCPS, RVGBC, SCCS). The paper pools Root (dbGaP phs000383). In that sample set the id therefore almost certainly means this Baltimore study, not the British Breast Cancer Study. The paper's main text does not list the member studies, and its supplement was not read.

label: Beaver Dam Eye Study
example title: Rare variant analyses across multiethnic cohorts identify novel genes for refractive error.
example quote: These 14 cohorts were: Singapore Chinese Eye Study (SCES), Singapore Malay Eye Study (SiMES), Singapore Indian Eye Study (SINDI), Age Related Eye Study (AREDS), Rotterdam Study I (RSI), Erasmus Rucphen Family (ERF), Raine Eye Health Study (REHS) of the Raine Study, Beaver Dam Eye Study (BDES), Estonian Genome Center for the University of Tartu (EGCUT), Finnish Twin Study on Aging (FITSA), Ogliastra, Croatia-Korcula, TwinsUK, and EPIC-Norfolk.
definition: A population-based cohort of the residents of the city and township of Beaver Dam, Wisconsin, United States, aged 43 to 84 years at a private census begun in 1987. They were examined at baseline in 1988–1990 and re-examined about every five years (up to a 25-year follow-up in 2014–2016) by the University of Wisconsin-Madison, to study the prevalence, incidence and risk factors of age-related eye diseases, such as age-related macular degeneration and cataract, and of visual impairment.
location quote: The recruitment population consisted of European ancestry individuals ages 43-84 from the town of Beaver Dam, Wisconsin, United States. 4,926 individuals were recruited into the study from 1988- 1990.
parent quote: Fourteen population-based CREAM cohorts that had exome chip genotypes on individuals with refractive error measurements were used in this study. These 14 cohorts were: Singapore Chinese Eye Study (SCES), Singapore Malay Eye Study (SiMES), Singapore Indian Eye Study (SINDI), Age Related Eye Study (AREDS), Rotterdam Study I (RSI), Erasmus Rucphen Family (ERF), Raine Eye Health Study (REHS) of the Raine Study, Beaver Dam Eye Study (BDES), Estonian Genome Center for the University of Tartu (EGCUT), Finnish Twin Study on Aging (FITSA), Ogliastra, Croatia-Korcula, TwinsUK, and EPIC-Norfolk.
note: Tier D (D373), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: BDES is the Beaver Dam Eye Study, one of the discrete input cohorts in both the multiethnic and Indo-European refractive-error meta-analyses. Detail (place, ages, recruitment years, follow-up interval) drawn from P1s supplement (D373.23-25), a brief cohort profile. Multiple by-name papers (P2-P7) confirm consistent identity across studies of cataract, acuity, maculopathy and refraction. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym and country are right. The definition followed the GWAS supplement's one-paragraph summary. That summary makes 'European ancestry' sound like an entry criterion and speaks of the 'town' of Beaver Dam. The cohort's own papers say everyone aged 43–84 in the city and township of Beaver Dam was identified by a private census begun in 1987. Of these, 4,926 were examined in 1988–1990 and re-examined in 1993–95, 1998–2000, 2003–05, 2008–10 and 2014–16 by the University of Wisconsin. The definition now says this. The parent was missing: P1 itself calls BDES one of the 'population-based CREAM cohorts', and the Consortium for Refractive Error and Myopia is COHO:0000905. The example quote started with the last sentence of another cohort's section ('a total of 1,105 individuals ...') and ran across the heading '1.15 Beaver Dam eye study (BDES)'. It is replaced by the main-text sentence listing the 14 CREAM cohorts. BDES is also a member of the International AMD Genomics Consortium (D036, checked as a new aggregation). Its checker found BDES in the IAMDGC supplementary Table 1, which I could not open. If that table is quoted, a hasCohort link from D036 can be added. The Epidemiology of Hearing Loss Study and the Beaver Dam Offspring Study are separate studies of this cohort and of its participants' children; neither is in COHO or in this review. No duplicate.
