input name: BioImage Study: A Clinical Study of Burden of Atherosclerotic Disease in an At-Risk Population
label: BioImage Study: A Clinical Study of Burden of Atherosclerotic Disease in an At-Risk Population
other synonyms: BioImage Study|High Risk Plaque BioImage study
example title: Genetic and clinical determinants of abdominal aortic diameter: genome-wide association studies, exome array data and Mendelian randomization study.
example quote: The BioImage study (NCT00738725) is a multi-ethnic, observational study aimed at characterizing subclinical atherosclerosis in 6,699 US adults (55-80 years at baseline, 2008- 2009) at risk for, but without, clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
definition: A prospective observational cohort of asymptomatic adults at risk of, but without, clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (men aged 55–80 and women aged 60–80). They were recruited in 2008–2009 by the High-Risk Plaque Initiative from members of the Humana health plan in Chicago, Illinois, and Fort Lauderdale, Florida, United States, and examined with vascular imaging and blood sampling, to identify imaging and circulating biomarkers that predict near-term atherothrombotic events.
location quote: The BioImage study (NCT00738725) is a multi-ethnic, observational study aimed at characterizing subclinical atherosclerosis in 6,699 US adults (55-80 years at baseline, 2008- 2009) at risk for, but without, clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
note: Tier D (D375), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: BioImage/BIOIMAGE denotes the NCT00738725 BioImage Study cohort, one exome-array discovery panel among several in the abdominal aortic diameter GWAS. P2 calls it the High Risk Plaque BioImage study; D375.12 suggests HRP Initiative is a funding collaboration encompassing BioImage rather than a membership aggregation, so not used as parent. Full text renders the tag all-caps BIOIMAGE; same acronym. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, country, example and the absence of a parent are right. The definition was accurate but left out who and where. The High-Risk Plaque Initiative's own description (Falk et al. 2011, open access) says participants were recruited among Humana health-plan members, men over 55 and women over 60, and that 'enrollment occurred in two cities: Chicago, IL and Fort Lauderdale, FL'. Enrolment ended in June 2009 after 18 months. The study measured circulating biomarkers as well as imaging. I added these. The GWAS paper writes the name all in capitals (BIOIMAGE). Case variants are kept, so it is added as an acronym. The study's usual short name, 'BioImage Study', is added as a synonym next to the long registered title used as the label. The High-Risk Plaque Initiative is the industry collaboration that funded and ran the study. It is not an aggregation of cohorts, so no parent. Not to be confused with the Swedish CArdioPulmonary bioImage Study (SCAPIS, COHO:0000391). No duplicate in COHO or this review.

label: Barbados National Cancer Study
example title: Associations between age of menarche and genetic variation in women of African descent: genome-wide association study and polygenic score analysis.
example quote: The Root consortium is comprised of six epidemiologic studies of breast cancer in women of African ancestry: the Nigerian Breast Cancer Study (Ibadan, Nigeria); the Barbados National Cancer Study (Barbados); the Southern Community Cohort (southern United States); the Baltimore Breast Cancer Study (Baltimore, United States); the Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study (Detroit and Pennsylvania, United States); and the Chicago Cancer Prone Study (Chicago, United States).
definition: A nationwide population-based case-control study of breast and prostate cancer in Barbados-born residents of Barbados. It was run by Stony Brook University with the Barbados Ministry of Health and the University of the West Indies and funded by the US National Human Genome Research Institute. Its breast cancer arm enrolled every histologically confirmed incident breast cancer identified by the island's only pathology department, at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital, from July 2002 to March 2006, with controls randomly selected from a national database and frequency-matched by age. The aim was to study environmental and genetic risk factors in this predominantly African-origin population.
location quote: BNCS is a case-control study of environmental risk factors for breast and prostate cancer in a predominantly African-origin population in Barbados.
parent quote: The Root consortium is comprised of six epidemiologic studies of breast cancer in women of African ancestry: the Nigerian Breast Cancer Study (Ibadan, Nigeria); the Barbados National Cancer Study (Barbados); the Southern Community Cohort (southern United States); the Baltimore Breast Cancer Study (Baltimore, United States); the Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study (Detroit and Pennsylvania, United States); and the Chicago Cancer Prone Study (Chicago, United States).
note: Tier D (D376), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: BNCS denotes the Barbados National Cancer Study, one of six African-ancestry breast-cancer studies pooled in the Root consortium for this menarche-age GWAS. Member of the Root consortium (D376.1), a defined 6-study umbrella; Root/ROOT is tier-D row D056, not in this batch, so parent left null. P3/P4 give BNCS its own profile sentences, unlike sibling BBCS_c (D372). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, country and example are right. The definition was accurate but gave no who, when or how. The study's methods paper (Nemesure et al., Int J Cancer 2009, free PMC text) says it is a population-based case-control study in Barbados-born residents. Stony Brook coordinated it with a clinical centre at the Ministry of Health and the University of the West Indies, under NHGRI funding. Breast cancer cases were all histologically confirmed incident cases from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital pathology department between July 2002 and March 2006, and controls were drawn at random from a national database and age-frequency-matched. The definition now says this. The parent was left null because Root (D056) was not in this batch. D056 has been checked as a new aggregation, so the membership is set with the P1 sentence. The prostate arm: the BNCS papers describe a breast and prostate study (the FFQ validation drew controls 'frequency-matched on sex and age group to breast and prostate cancer cases'). BNCS-group papers on prostate cancer call their study the 'Prostate Cancer in a Black Population (PCBP) study'. It was a nationwide case-control study of Barbadian men with prostate cancer, July 2002 to January 2011, funded by NHGRI and the Office of Minority Health, with controls drawn at random from a national database (PMC4322001, PMC3596924). That is tier-E name E879 (PCBP). PCBP is very probably the prostate arm of BNCS and could be linked with isSubCohortOf, but I found no single sentence that says so. The PGS Catalog lists PGS id 'BBCS', named 'British Breast Cancer Study', in the same sample set PSS000995. There it most likely means the Baltimore Breast Cancer Study (see D372). Not to be confused with the Barbados Asthma Genetics Study (COHO:0000959).

label: Brigham and Women's Rheumatoid Arthritis Sequential Study
other synonyms: Brigham Rheumatoid Arthritis Sequential Study|Brigham and Women's Hospital Rheumatoid Arthritis Sequential Study
example title: Genome-wide association study meta-analysis identifies seven new rheumatoid arthritis risk loci.
example quote: This study expands upon our previous GWAS meta-analysis of 3,393 cases and 12,462 controls by (a) adding a new GWAS dataset of 483 RA cases recruited from the Boston area (Brigham Rheumatoid Arthritis Sequential Study, BRASS) and 1,449 shared controls, (b) adding 513 cases and 431 controls recruited from Sweden (Epidemiological Investigation of Rheumatoid Arthritis, EIRA), (c) incorporating a recently published GWAS of 2,418 cases and 4,504 controls recruited from North America (Canada and North American Rheumatoid Arthritis Consortium-III, NARAC-III), and (d) adding additional shared controls to the NARAC-III dataset.
definition: A single-centre prospective observational registry cohort of adults with rheumatoid arthritis diagnosed by a rheumatologist, enrolled from March 2003 at the Brigham and Women's Hospital Arthritis Center in Boston, Massachusetts, United States. Participants are followed with annual visits, semi-annual questionnaires and stored blood samples, to find biomarkers that predict drug response, toxicity, disease activity and prognosis and to describe the natural history of treated rheumatoid arthritis.
location quote: Enrollment for the registry began in March of 2003 in the Brigham and Women’s Hospital Arthritis Center in the United States.
note: Tier D (D377), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: BRASS denotes the Brigham Rheumatoid Arthritis Sequential Study, a Boston-area RA case collection with shared controls, one of six GWAS collections meta-analysed for RA risk. Only P1 evidence available (no other papers found by name); definition/place come from D377.1s recruitment sentence, not genotyping-site units. No named aggregation states BRASS as a member; co-participation in the meta-analysis isnt stated as membership. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity is right, but the definition described one GWAS's collection, 'RA patients recruited from the Boston area with shared or matched controls, genotyped for GWAS'. BRASS itself is a different kind of thing. It is a single-centre prospective observational registry of adults with rheumatoid arthritis at the Brigham and Women's Hospital Arthritis Center in Boston. Enrolment began in March 2003, with annual visits, semi-annual questionnaires and banked blood and DNA. Its registered aims are biomarkers of drug response, toxicity, disease activity and prognosis, and the natural history of treated RA. The controls in the GWAS collection came from other studies (NIMH, and multiple sclerosis, macular degeneration and myocardial infarction GWAS), not from BRASS. The draft's note said only P1 was available, but dozens of BRASS papers exist. The label was a shortened form. The registry's own ClinicalTrials.gov record (NCT01793103) and its 2021 registry paper use 'Brigham and Women's Rheumatoid Arthritis Sequential Study', so that is now the label and the short form is kept as a synonym. The country quote now says 'United States' explicitly; the old one gave only 'Boston area'. No parent: the GWAS meta-analysis pools BRASS with other collections but names no aggregation. No duplicate in COHO or this review. E141 'Brigham and Womens Hospital' is an institution name, and COHO:0000383 Mass General Brigham Biobank is a different, hospital-wide biobank.

Only P1 evidence available; name itself states the sponsoring society and disease focus. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym and example are right. The definition called BSSH-GODD a 'case-control cohort of people with Dupuytren's disease and controls'. BSSH-GODD holds cases only: adults in the UK who had surgery for the disease, who gave saliva for DNA and whose excised diseased fascia was also collected. In both GWAS that use it, the UK controls come from the UK Household Longitudinal Study (UKHLS). P1's Supplementary Data 1 lists 'BSSH-GODD (5,408)' as the case cohort and 'UK Household Longitudinal Study (9,961)' as the control cohort. The definition now says this. The draft's note said only P1 was available, but the 2017 GWAS (Ng et al., AJHG) and the collection's EGA study describe it. The country quote now comes from the 2017 paper's methods rather than P1's ethics list; the old quote was also acceptable. The collection has its own EGA study, EGAS00001001206 (released 2015), which is not in COHO. If the term should join the EGA subset, that study is the EGA example; its description is quoted above. No parent and no duplicate. GODDAF (D438) is the Dutch and the German Dupuytren Study (COHO:0000976) the German counterpart case collection. The controls belong to UKHLS (COHO:0000179), not to this term.

input name: Cambridgeshire Parkinson's Incidence from GP to Neurologist

definition: An observational, longitudinal, population-representative incident cohort of people newly diagnosed with parkinsonism or Parkinson's disease in the county of Cambridgeshire, United Kingdom, between December 2000 and December 2002. location quote: The Cambridgeshire Parkinson’s Incidence from GP to Neurologist (CamPaIGN) study is an observational, longitudinal study of incident PD patients in the county of Cambridgeshire, UK55,56.
note: Tier D (D381), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CamPaIGN denotes the Cambridgeshire Parkinson's Incidence from GP to Neurologist cohort, one of 12 PD cohorts analysed for the mortality/motor-progression GWAS; distinct from the separately listed Cambridge PD Research Clinic cohort. CamPaIGN is distinct from the separately-listed Cambridge PD Research Clinic cohort (D381.8) - same geography, different cohort, not conflated. Supplement (D381.26) spells the acronym CamPaiGN (lowercase i); kept as a separate case-variant acronym. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft is essentially right. The definition needed three small corrections. The recruitment window is December 2000 to December 2002; the draft had 'December 2000 and 2002', copied from a truncated abstract sentence. The study is run and sponsored by the University of Cambridge. Genetic testing is part of the follow-up. The cohort's own 13-year follow-up paper (open access) states the window and says the study 'was established to provide comprehensive and true‐to‐life data on the natural history of idiopathic PD'. Tier D (D382), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CANADA denotes the Toronto-based Canadian RA case-control collection (Illumina 370K) in the primary meta-analysis; CANADA-II is a later Halifax+Toronto replication update of it. The tag is literally the country name in every unit (D382.1, D382.4, D382.6); unlike sibling collections BRASS/EIRA/NARAC in the same study, no proper name is ever given for this Toronto (later CANADA-II) rheumatoid-arthritis case-control collection. Checked 2026-09-23: None in the verdict. The draft only had P1, so here is the source it lacked. The collection behind the tag comes from P1's reference 13, the REL GWAS (Gregersen et al. 2009). That paper describes it only as 'Canadian cohorts'. It had unrelated RA probands recruited in the Toronto area under 1987 ACR criteria, with European-origin controls from the Toronto area, genotyped on the Illumina HapMap370. It has no study name, design paper or identity beyond the country and the laboratory. This fits how other unnamed place and institution collections have been handled in this review (for example D065 'Umea'), so it is not a cohort. The Toronto RA collection was assembled by the University of Toronto / Mount Sinai Hospital and University Health Network group that genotyped it. input name: Canadian spontaneous coronary artery dissection study

definition: A multicentre, prospective, observational cohort of patients presenting with acute non-atherosclerotic spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD), run from the University of British Columbia and enrolled at cardiac centres in Canada and the United States since June 2014, whose precipitating stressors, predisposing conditions and core-laboratory-reviewed angiograms are recorded and who are followed for cardiovascular events, to establish the natural history of SCAD and the outcomes of its treatment. note: Tier D (D383), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: canSCAD tag = 'CanSCAD/MGI' sub-study: SCAD cases from the Canadian SCAD Cohort Study (plus some from NACAD Study) meta-analysed with population controls from Michigan Genomics Initiative (COHO:0000442). Modelled as the case cohort (Canadian SCAD Cohort Study) only; MGI controls are the existing COHO:0000442 term, out of scope here. The label 'Canadian SCAD Cohort Study' abbreviates the name and names only the first phase: the study registered its first phase as the 'Canadian Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection (SCAD) Cohort Study' (NCT02188069, 750 patients enrolled June 2014 to June 2018 at 22 North American centres, three-year follow-up) and extended it from December 2018 as the 'Canadian SCAD Study' (NCT04906356: 'This current study will be an extension of that study, now named the "Canadian SCAD Study."'), with international enrolment, a genetic sub-study and ten-year follow-up. The tagged GWAS samples span both phases (PMID:32887874: cases enrolled 2017-2018 and 2018-2019), so the label is the study's current full name, with the phase names as synonyms. definition: A prospective cardiovascular population study of an age-stratified random sample of adults aged 20 years or older living in the Østerbro district and part of Nørrebro around Rigshospitalet in Copenhagen, Denmark, launched in 1975 with a first examination in 1976–1978 and re-examinations in 1981–1983, 1991–1994, 2001–2003 and 2011–2013, whose participants are followed through the Danish national registers. note: Tier D (D384), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CCHS = Copenhagen City Heart Study, one of the stage I meta-analysis case-control datasets. Well documented by its own design description (D384.7-9); no candidate COHO term denotes it. Other candidates listed (EADB, GR@ACE, etc.) are sibling datasets in the same Alzheimer meta-analysis, not this cohort. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, country, parent (none) and example are right. The definition copied a GWAS supplement's boilerplate: 'selected randomly based on the national Danish Civil Registration System to reflect the adult Danish population aged 20-100' blurs the sampling, which was an age-stratified random sample, drawn through the civil registration number, of residents aged 20 and over of ten wards around Rigshospitalet (all of Østerbro and a third of Nørrebro) in Copenhagen (PMID:26779513). It also lacked the purpose (prevention of coronary heart disease and stroke) and the start (launched 1975). The Danish name Østerbroundersøgelsen, which the study itself uses, was missing as a synonym. Not in COHO. Tier-E rows E185 (CGPS, Copenhagen General Population Study), E193 (CIHDS, Copenhagen Ischaemic Heart Disease Study) and E204 (COGEN, Copenhagen Cardiovascular Genetic study, a hospital cohort of cardiology patients admitted 2010-2017, PMID:34143812) are separate Copenhagen studies, not parents or arms of this one. C-Data is one NHLBI-sponsored observational study with a single protocol, not an aggregation: the Comprehensive Sickle Cell Centers Collaborative Data Project (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00529061, acronym C-Data; BioLINCC 'Study Period March 2005 – September 2008') built a database of children and adults with sickle cell disease seen at the Comprehensive Sickle Cell Centers ('Nine CSCC centers, representing 19 clinical sites, participated in the C-Data Project', PMID:20658620), with medical-record abstraction, interviews and quality-of-life questionnaires, and was extended in 2007 to collect blood and DNA from its participants (NCT00528203, 'Gen/Phen'; PMID:19902523). example title: Deciphering the genetics and mechanisms of predisposition to multiple myeloma.

definition: A three-year initiative of the US National Cancer Institute, begun in 2006, that ran multi-stage genome-wide association studies of prostate and breast cancer in case-control sets drawn from existing studies (for prostate cancer, men from the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial, the American Cancer Society Cancer Prevention Study II, the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study and the French Prostate Case-Control Study; for breast cancer, postmenopausal women from the Nurses' Health Study, with replication in further cohorts), and shared its genotype data and results with the research community.
location quote: The cohort studies were: the Prostate, Lung Colorectal and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial (PLCO, subjects from continental USA) (Gohagan et al. 2000); the American Cancer Society Cancer Prevention Study II (CPS-II, from continental USA) (Calle et al. 2002) and the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study (ATBC, from Finland) (1994). || The case–control study was the French Prostate Case–Control Study (CeRePP, Centre de Recherche pour les Pathologies Prostatiques, from France) (Valeri et al. 2003).
note: Tier D (D388), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred; research settles it. CGEMS is not one cohort but the NCI's Cancer Genetic Markers of Susceptibility initiative ('A new NCI initiative, Cancer Genetic Markers of Susceptibility (CGEMS), is a three-year study designed to identify common genetic variations associated with risk for prostate and breast cancer', PMC2291937), whose genotyped sets were case-control samples nested in existing studies: PLCO for the first prostate scan and the Nurses' Health Study for the first breast scan (PMID:21573004, 17529973), with CPS-II, ATBC and the French CeRePP study in later prostate stages (PMID:22271044). These named, shared datasets (dbGaP phs000207 prostate, phs000147 breast) are what the GWAS tag and PGS id denote, so it is typed as an aggregation, like the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (COHO:0000182). The drafted label carries the institute's name as a prefix; the initiative's own name is 'Cancer Genetic Markers of Susceptibility', and the PGS Catalog form is kept as a synonym. The drafted example had no quote: P1 names CGEMS only in its Supplementary Data 1, as the control set of the USA dataset. The aggregation's members are all COHO terms and should get hasCohort links: PLCO (COHO:0000485) and the Nurses' Health Study (COHO:0000456), quoting PMID:21573004's abstract ('genome-wide genotyping data on 3,554 individuals from the Nurses' Health Study and the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial that took part in the National Cancer Institute Cancer Genetic Markers of Susceptibility initiative for breast and prostate cancer'); and CPS-II (COHO:0000024), ATBC (COHO:0000598) and the French Prostate Case-Control Study (CeRePP, COHO:0000818), quoting PMC3374121 ('Stage I of this study included 3,995 men diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the prostate and 3,815 control subjects from three case–control studies nested within cohorts and one hospital based case–control study, previously analyzed in stages I and II of the Cancer Genetics Markers of Susceptibility study (CGEMS).', followed by the list of studies used for the country quotes). The breast replication cohorts NHS II (COHO:0000619), PLCO and CPS-II were genotyped for a few SNPs only, so they are left out of the definition's member list. The example quote is a single cell of P1's Supplementary Data 1 table ('Data sets used in the MM meta-analysis'), the only place P1 names CGEMS. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, country, parent (none) and example are right. definition: A prospective cohort of whole-blood donors aged 18–70 recruited by the Finnish Red Cross Blood Service alongside standard donation at three fixed donation sites in the Helsinki metropolitan area of Finland (Kivihaka, Sanomatalo and Espoo) from May 2015 to December 2017, with blood samples taken at their donation visits during the study for blood counts, CRP, ferritin and soluble transferrin receptor and for DNA, and health and lifestyle questionnaires at enrolment and again in 2018, to study iron status and the genetic and lifestyle factors affecting iron stores in blood donors.
location quote: A total of 2584 blood donors (N = 8003 samples) were recruited into the study alongside standard donation at three donation sites in the capital region of Finland between 5/2015 and 12/2017.
note: Tier D (D416), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: FinDonor (processed as FinDonor_1/FinDonor_2 genotyping batches of one cohort) as a contributing cohort in an iron-homeostasis GWAS meta-analysis with CROATIA-VIS, INTERVAL, InCHIANTI, KORA, deCODE; P2 is FinDonor's own design/profile paper. FinDonor_1/FinDonor_2 in P1 are genotyping-batch labels for one cohort (D416.10), not separate cohorts or synonyms. deCODE, Helsinki 2000 and FinnGen among candidates are other cohorts in the same multi-cohort meta-analysis, not FinDonor itself. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, country, parent (none) and example are right. The definition restated one sentence of the GWAS supplement and said nothing of who ran it, where, when or how: the design paper (PMID:31657023, open access PMC7004091) gives the Finnish Red Cross Blood Service, three fixed donation sites in the Helsinki metropolitan area, 18 May 2015 to 8 December 2017, donors aged 18–70, samples at donation visits for blood count, CRP, ferritin and sTfR and DNA, and enrolment and 2018 follow-up questionnaires. The country quote is replaced by the abstract sentence that names Finland rather than 'Finnish blood donors'. Not in COHO or this review under another name; the Danish Blood Donor Study (COHO:0000475) and other donor cohorts are unrelated. FinDonor_1 and FinDonor_2 are genotyping batches of this one cohort, not tags or synonyms. No parent.

label: National FinHealth 2017 Study
other synonyms: national FinHealth 2017 study|FinHealth 2017 Study|FinHealth 2017 Survey|FinHealth Study
example title: Nightmares share genetic risk factors with sleep and psychiatric traits.
example quote: The national FinHealth 2017 study comprises a random sample of adults in Finland, and it focuses on objective and perceived health, quality of life, lifestyle, prevalence, and risk factors for common health problems including sleep, insomnia, and alcohol consumption.
definition: A national health examination survey of adults aged 18 or older living in mainland Finland, run by the Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL) at 50 study locations between January and May 2017 in a representative sample drawn from the Population Register by one- and two-stage stratified random sampling, in which participants answered questionnaires on sociodemographic factors, health, quality of life, lifestyle, diseases and medication and attended a health examination with physical measurements and blood sampling, to monitor the health, functional capacity and welfare of the Finnish population and the prevalence and risk factors of common health problems. It combined the protocols of the FINRISK surveys and the Health 2000 and 2011 surveys.
location quote: The national FinHealth 2017 study comprises a random sample of adults in Finland, and it focuses on objective and perceived health, quality of life, lifestyle, prevalence, and risk factors for common health problems including sleep, insomnia, and alcohol consumption.
note: Tier D (D417), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: FinHealth as one of five distinct Finnish cohorts (with FINRISK, Finnish Twin Cohort Study, GeneRISK, Genes for Good) analysed for nightmares; P2-P4 are FinHealth's own profile/analysis papers (physical activity, diet). FINRISK's own COHO definition ends its five-yearly survey series in 2012; FinHealth 2017 is evidently a later wave of the same national health-survey programme but no unit states this relationship explicitly, so no parent is asserted. Casing varies across papers; two variants kept as synonyms. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, country, parent (none) and example are right. The definition restated the GWAS paper's one-sentence description and lacked who (THL), when (January to May 2017), where (50 study locations in mainland Finland), how (Population Register sample, questionnaires and a health examination with blood samples) and its place among the Finnish national surveys; open papers give these (PMC9002951: 'the FinHealth 2017 Study, a national health examination survey, was carried out in 50 study locations in mainland Finland between January and May 2017'; PMC9578096: 'The FinHealth 2017 combined the protocols from the FINRISK Study and Health 2000 and 2011 surveys'). The synonym 'The FinHealth 2017 Study' carried a leading article from a paper title; replaced by 'FinHealth 2017 Study', with 'FinHealth 2017 Survey' and 'FinHealth Study' added. Parent: none asserted. PMC7272447 treats FinHealth 2017 as the renamed continuation of the FINRISK series ('In 2017, the sampling was modified somewhat, and the name of the study was changed to the FinHealth 2017 Survey'), but COHO's FINRISK (COHO:0000071) is defined as the 1972–2012 surveys and FinHealth 2017 also continued the Health 2000/2011 surveys (Health 2000 is COHO:0000090), so a hasCohort from FINRISK would need its definition widened first; the curator may prefer to do that. Its successor, the Healthy Finland Survey (2023), is not in COHO. No other COHO term or review row denotes it.

label: FinnTwin12 Cohort

example title: Genome-wide Association Meta-analysis of Childhood and Adolescent Internalizing Symptoms.
example quote: FinnTwin12 is a population-based cohort of Finnish twins born 1983–1987 that was established to follow health and behavioural habits
definition: A population-based longitudinal cohort of the twins born in Finland in 1983–1987, the youngest of the three Finnish Twin Cohorts, identified through Finland's Central Population Registry and enrolled with their biological parents in the year they reached age 11, with twin, parent and teacher questionnaires and ratings at baseline and follow-up surveys at ages 14, 17, about 22 and about 37; a subset was studied intensively with in-school assessments and peer nominations at age 12, psychiatric interviews at ages 14 and 22, and neurocognitive tests and DNA collection in early adulthood. It was designed to identify individual, familial and school and neighbourhood risks for substance use before its onset and to follow trajectories of use, abuse and their consequences into adulthood.
location quote: In the first stage, we conducted multiwave questionnaire research enrolling all eligible twins born in Finland during 1983–1987 along with their biological parents.
parent quote: This review offers an update on research conducted with FinnTwin12 (FT12), the youngest of the three Finnish Twin Cohorts.
note: Tier D (D418), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: Deferred; research settles it. The tag is the FinnTwin12 cohort, the youngest of the three Finnish Twin Cohorts, not the Finnish Twin Cohort Study itself: the tagged paper's Table S1 (Elsevier supplement mmc1.pdf) lists 'Finnish Twin Cohort / FinnTwin12 / Finland / population-based (twin families)', and its Supplement 1 (mmc2.docx) describes it: 'FinnTwin12 is a population-based cohort of Finnish twins born 1983–1987', enrolled at ages 11–12 through the Central Population Registry, with depressiveness and social anxiety rated by the twins at 14 and 17, parents at 12 and teachers at 12 and 14. So it is a new cohort, a member of the Finnish Twin Cohort Study aggregation (COHO:0000070), whose definition already names FinnTwin12 as one of its cohorts; the draft left the parent out. Design from the cohort's own review (PMID:31640839, PMC7108792) and its age-37 follow-up (PMID:39920525). The draft's GCST was right but had no quote; Supplement 1 supplies one. FT12, the cohort's own abbreviation, is added. Sibling names in this review: E343 FinnTwin16, E344 FinnTwinOld ('The Older Finnish Twin Cohort'), E361 FSCD and E362 FTC/NAG-FIN; FinnTwin12 and FinnTwin16 are both 'younger' Finnish twin cohorts, so the PGS Catalog's name 'The Younger Finnish Twin Cohort' is ambiguous and is kept only as the Catalog's synonym for this id. Label 'FinnTwin12 Cohort' (title of the cohort's review) rather than 'FinnTwin12', so that the GWAS tag can stay an acronym without duplicating the label. The example quote stops before the author-year citations, which the docx stores as field codes.

label: Finnish Twin Study on Aging
example title: Rare variant analyses across multiethnic cohorts identify novel genes for refractive error.
example quote: Finnish Twin Study on Aging (FITSA) is a study of genetic and environmental effects on the disablement process in older female twins.
definition: A study of the genetic and environmental effects on the disablement process in older women, in which female twin pairs aged 63–76, recruited from the Older Finnish Twin Cohort, took part in laboratory examinations of physical functioning, muscle strength and power, hearing and other health measures, with blood sampling, in Jyväskylä, Finland, in 2000–2001 and again at a 3-year follow-up, and have since been followed for mortality, by researchers of the Gerontology Research Center of the University of Jyväskylä.
location quote: Altogether 103 MZ and 114 DZ twin pairs (424 individuals, all women of European ancestry) aged 63-76 years living in Finland took part in multiple laboratory examinations in 2000 and 2003, and responded in 13 questionnaires in 2011.
note: Tier D (D419), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Parent left for later: isSubCohortOf review name E344 (The Older Finnish Twin Cohort), not minted in this run; quote: "The participants in the FITSA were recruited from the Older Finnish Twin Cohort, which is comprised of all same-sex twin pairs born before 1958 with both co-twins alive in 1975 (24)." (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC10395559/fullTextXML). P1: FITSA as one of 14 cohorts (with the Singapore Chinese/Malay/Indian Eye Studies, AREDS, Rotterdam Study I, ERF, Raine/REHS, BDES, EGCUT, Ogliastra, Croatia-Korcula, TwinsUK, EPIC-Norfolk) in a multiethnic refractive-error GWAS; P2-P7 are FITSA's own analyses (muscle strength, hearing, epigenetic ageing, grip-strength PRS). D419.11's '13,888 adult twin pairs started in 1975' likely names a larger parent Finnish twin registry FITSA sampled from, not FITSA's own size; excluded per the no-numbers rule, and not asserted as parent since no candidate COHO term for it appears here. All ten other candidates are co-listed cohorts in P1's meta-analysis, not FITSA. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, country and example study are right. The parent was missing: FITSA is a subsample of the Older Finnish Twin Cohort ('The participants in the FITSA were recruited from the Older Finnish Twin Cohort, which is comprised of all same-sex twin pairs born before 1958 with both co-twins alive in 1975', PMC10395559; the draft's '13 888 adult twin pairs started in 1975' is that cohort), which is E344 of this review. The definition described the GWAS supplement's subset wording and left out the source cohort, the University of Jyväskylä examinations (PMC2265555: 'laboratory investigations performed in Jyväskylä during 2000–2001'), the 3-year follow-up and the mortality follow-up. The example quote began with a stray acknowledgement name and section number ('Tammesoo. 1.10 FITSA') and ran into the parent cohort's size; shortened to the span naming the study. Parent is E344 ('The Older Finnish Twin Cohort', PGS id FinnTwinOld) of this review. If E344 is not minted, the Older Finnish Twin Cohort is covered only by the Finnish Twin Cohort Study aggregation (COHO:0000070), which could then take hasCohort FITSA with PMC8201844's 'a subcohort of twin sisters belonging to the Finnish Twin Cohort'. Not the SAWEs twin study, a separate Jyväskylä study of hormone-therapy-discordant twin sisters mentioned alongside FITSA in PMC5883300. No other COHO term or review row denotes it.

input name: Follow-up of Ovarian Cancer Genetic Association and Interaction Studies
label: Follow-up of Ovarian Cancer Genetic Association and Interaction Studies
other synonyms: The Follow-up of Ovarian Cancer Genetic Association and Interaction Studies|Follow-up of Ovarian Cancer Genetic Association and Interaction Studies of the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium
example title: Boosting the Power of Rare Variant Association Studies by Imputation Using Large-scale Sequencing Population.
example quote: For EOC, three SNP array datasets were collected from the Follow-up of Ovarian Cancer Genetic Association and Interaction Studies (FOCI)-OncoArray [64], the FOCI-Exome Chip [65], and the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1/2 (CIMBA) [66] (Table S26).
definition: A post-GWAS research programme on epithelial ovarian cancer, funded by the US National Cancer Institute (U19-CA148112) as the ovarian cancer consortium of the Genetic Associations and Mechanisms in Oncology (GAME-ON) initiative, led from Moffitt Cancer Center and built on the collaboration of the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium, that pools genome-wide and further genotyping data (including exome-chip and OncoArray genotyping) from the case-control studies of that consortium, to discover and replicate susceptibility variants, including histotype-specific variants and variants associated with survival, to study their biological mechanisms, and to investigate gene–gene and gene–environment interactions and risk prediction.
parent quote: GAME-ON is network of genetic epidemiology consortia that contains GWAS data from the Colorectal Transdisciplinary Study (CORECT); Discovery, Biology, and Risk of Inherited Variants in Breast Cancer (DRIVE); Elucidating Loci Involved in Prostate Cancer Susceptibility (ELLIPSE); Follow-up of Ovarian Cancer Genetic Association and Interaction Studies (FOCI); and Transdisciplinary Research in Cancer of the Lung (TRICL).
note: Tier D (D420), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: FOCI (its OncoArray and Exome-chip components) as one of the SNP-array datasets, with CIMBA, used for rare-variant imputation in ovarian cancer; P2-P4 are papers P1 cites for the cohort but which describe OCAC's own studies or CIMBA, not FOCI by name; P5 (2012) is FOCI's own post-GWAS collaboration paper. FOCI's exome-array cases/controls originate from OCAC's member studies (D420.27, from P3, an OCAC exome paper P1 cites as the FOCI-Exome-chip source without ever using 'FOCI'); P2 and P4 likewise never say FOCI. Relationship to OCAC (COHO:0000134, in candidates) is unclear -- not asserted as parent; a researcher should check if FOCI is an OCAC sub-project. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronym and example are right. The parent was missing: FOCI is one of the five consortia of GAME-ON (COHO:0000774), whose existing hasCohort assertions for CORECT, ELLIPSE and TRICL use the same quote that names FOCI. The definition described what one 2025 paper took from FOCI (OncoArray and exome-chip datasets) instead of FOCI itself: its dbGaP top-level study (phs001133, 'Follow-up of Ovarian Cancer Genetic Association and Interaction Studies (FOCI)', case-control, U19-CA148112 at Moffitt Cancer Center) says it pools GWAS for discovery, replication, histotype-specific risk and survival (Project 1), biological follow-up (Project 2) and gene–gene, gene–environment interaction and risk prediction (Project 3), building 'upon the strengths and history of collaboration inherent in the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium (OCAC)'. GAME-ON papers call it 'FOCI-OCAC (Follow-up of Ovarian Cancer Genetic Association and Interaction Studies of the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium)' (PMC5666592), so that name and tag are added. FOCI's samples are those of OCAC member studies (COHO:0000134); FOCI is OCAC's GAME-ON project rather than a member study of OCAC, so it is placed under GAME-ON only; the curator may add an OCAC link if COHO allows two parents. Countries left empty: an international pool of OCAC case-control studies whose countries are not listed in any FOCI source read. Not the same as OCAC itself or the OncoArray Consortium.

label: Marburg-Münster Affective Disorders Cohort Study
other synonyms: The FOR2107 consortium|FOR2107 consortium|FOR2107 Marburg-Münster Affective Disorders Cohort Study|Marburg Münster Affective Disorders Cohort Study
example title: A meta-analysis of genome-wide studies of resilience in the German population.
example quote: The FOR2107 consortium was established to investigate the neurobiology of affective disorders.
definition: The human cohort of the German Research Foundation (DFG) research unit FOR2107 on the neurobiology of the major psychoses, recruited between 2014 and 2018 at the Universities of Marburg and Münster, Germany, through local psychiatric hospitals and newspaper advertisements: adults aged 18–65 with major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, schizoaffective disorder or schizophrenia, healthy people at genetic and/or environmental risk, and healthy controls, deeply phenotyped with MRI, clinical course, neuropsychology, personality, risk and protective factors and biomaterials (blood, stool, urine, hair, saliva) at baseline and again at a 2-year follow-up, to identify how genetic and environmental factors shape brain structure and function and the course of these disorders.
location quote: Briefly, participants aged 18−65 years were recruited at Marburg and Münster Universities in Germany through advertisements and in psychiatric hospitals.
note: Tier D (D421), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: FOR2107 as one of five independent German cohorts (with BiDirect, PROCAM-2, SHIP-START/TREND, LIFE-Adult) analysed together for a resilience GWAS meta-analysis; P2 is FOR2107's own consortium profile paper; P3-P7 are profile papers for the other four co-listed cohorts, not FOR2107; P8 is an independent FOR2107 executive-function GWAS. Triage flagged 'aggregation?' but both P1 (D421.24) and P2 (D421.38) call FOR2107 'a cohort'/'a human cohort' of patients, at-risk individuals and controls, not an umbrella of separately named member studies; drafted as cohort. FOR2107 also has an unmodelled animal-model arm (D421.37), outside COHO's scope. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, parent (none), country and example are right. FOR2107 is the DFG research unit (Forschungsgruppe) 'Neurobiology of Affective Disorders', which also has an animal-model arm; its human sample, the one the GWAS genotyped, has its own name, the Marburg-Münster Affective Disorders Cohort Study (MACS): 'the FOR2107 Marburg-Münster Affective Disorders Cohort Study (MACS)' (PMC13471357), 'Work Package WP1, FOR2107/MACS cohort and brainimaging' (PMC10005934). So the label is that name, MACS is added as the cohort's own acronym, and the consortium names become synonyms (the lower-case 'the FOR2107 consortium' was running text with an article and is dropped). The definition limited the patients to MDD and bipolar disorder (the cohort takes all major psychoses, including schizoaffective disorder and schizophrenia, PMID:30267149) and lacked the DFG unit, ages, recruitment years and routes. The country quote did not name Germany; replaced. The acronym MACS also denotes the Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study (D466 of this review); if both are minted, both terms carry MACS with the editor note 'The acronym MACS also denotes …'. The BiDirect Study (D091) and the Münster Neuroimaging Cohort (MNC), often analysed together with MACS, are separate cohorts, not parts of it. Recruitment years: MACS controls were scanned from 2014 (PMID:29410079) and one analysis gives enrolment from January 2015 to May 2018 (PMC13471357), so the definition says 2014 to 2018. Not in COHO under any name.

label: Genes and Blood Clotting Study
example title: Genome-Wide Scan of Fifth Finger Clinodactyly.
example quote: The third cohort included participants recruited as part of the GABC study between 2006 and 2009 (Desch et al. 2013).
definition: A family-based study of healthy young people aged 14–35, recruited at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, United States, between June 2006 and January 2009 from the university's undergraduate and graduate students together with their biological siblings, with blood samples for measuring plasma haemostatic proteins (such as von Willebrand factor and plasminogen), genome-wide genotyping and a survey of common morphological traits, to identify the genetic factors behind variation in blood clotting in healthy people, using its sibling structure for linkage as well as association analysis.
location quote: A total of 1189 healthy individuals (ages 14-35) representing 507 sibships (with 2-6 siblings per family) from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, were recruited between June 26, 2006, and January 30, 2009.
note: Tier D (D423), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: GABC as one of the cohorts (alongside COHRA2 and OFC2) reused for a fifth-finger-clinodactyly GWAS, drawing on its existing blood-clotting genotypes; P2 is GABC's own original design paper (with TSS) on plasma plasminogen genetics. Michigan Genomics Initiative (MGI) and GENESIS among candidates are unrelated: MGI is a much larger, separate University of Michigan EHR biobank with no unit tying it to GABC; 'GENESIS' is the R software package used for GABC's GWAS (D423.18), not the cohort GENESIS. TSS (Trinity Student Study) is GABC's distinct co-analysed sibling cohort, not the same cohort. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, country, parent (none) and example are right. The definition was accurate but thin: it lacked the sibship (family) design used for linkage analysis, the age range, the city and exact period ('A total of 1189 healthy individuals (ages 14-35) representing 507 sibships (with 2-6 siblings per family) from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, were recruited between June 26, 2006, and January 30, 2009', PMC12314372) and what was collected (plasma haemostatic protein levels such as VWF, plasminogen and histidine-rich glycoprotein, genome-wide genotypes, an online survey of morphological traits). The country quote named only the university; replaced by one naming Ann Arbor. Not in COHO or this review under another name. The Trinity Student Study (COHO:0000627) is the Irish cohort analysed alongside it, not part of it; the Michigan Genomics Initiative (COHO:0000442) is unrelated; 'GENESIS' in the tagged paper is the R package. Genotypes and phenotypes are in dbGaP (phs000304).

input name: GABRIEL (a multidisciplinary study to identify the genetic and environmental causes of asthma in the European Community) Advanced studies
label: Gabriel Advanced Survey
other synonyms: GABRIEL Advanced Studies|GABRIEL Advanced Surveys|GABRIEL Advanced Survey|GABRIEL (a multidisciplinary study to identify the genetic and environmental causes of asthma in the European Community) Advanced studies
note: Tier D (D424), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: GABRIELA as a contributing cohort (with ALSPAC, EGEA, SLSJ) in an asthma-plus-eczema comorbidity GWAS; abstract does not name it. P2-P4 (found by name): 'The GABRIEL Advanced Studies', a cross-sectional, multiphase, population-based farm-environment asthma/allergy survey in children aged 6-12, matching existing COHO:0000073. Not in D424's auto-candidate list; found by grepping coho_names.tsv. COHO:0000073 'Gabriel Advanced Survey' (acronym GAS) closely matches this row's 'GABRIEL Advanced Studies' (D424.4) in theme, differing only in Survey/Studies and case. Checker should confirm against COHO:0000073's own definition before finalising as existing. Checked 2026-09-23: Verdict right: GABRIELA is the GABRIEL Advanced Surveys, which COHO already has as COHO:0000073 'Gabriel Advanced Survey' (its EGA example is 'Gabriel samples from the German Gabriel Advanced Survey' and its GWAS example 'GABRIEL-AS (GABRIEL Advanced Surveys)'). The survey's design paper (PMID:21819425) says 'The GABRIEL Advanced Surveys (GABRIELA) were conducted to determine factors in farming environments which are fundamental to protecting against asthma and atopic disease', and the tagged paper's supplement describes GABRIELA as cross-sectional population-based surveys in rural areas of Austria, Germany and Switzerland. The draft's additions (acronym GABRIELA, synonym GABRIEL Advanced Studies) are right; GABRIEL-AS, the survey's other names and the PGS Catalog name are added, and so are the countries COHO:0000073 lacks (it has only Germany, from the Bavarian phase 3): the surveys ran in rural Austria, Germany and Switzerland (PMID:22534534) and Poland (PMID:23621318). Existing-term suggestion for COHO:0000073: its definition ('children living on farms and reference children examined cross-sectionally for asthma, atopy and household microbial exposures in the GABRIEL Advanced Study', from the NEJM 2011 paper) describes the Bavarian phase-3 subsample; the term's label and examples are the whole survey, which could be defined as 'A multi-phase, stratified, cross-sectional population-based survey of school-aged children in rural regions of southern Germany, Austria and Switzerland and in Poland, run from 2006 within the EU-funded GABRIEL project: a screening questionnaire (phase I), a stratified random subsample with detailed farm-exposure questionnaires and blood, genetic and environmental samples (phase II), and in Bavaria an in-depth respiratory and environmental assessment (phase III), to determine the factors in farming environments that protect against asthma and atopic disease' (sources PMID:21819425, PMID:22534534, PMID:23621318, and the PMID:34155719 supplement: phase 1 in fall/winter 2006, phase 2 in spring/summer 2007). No new example: COHO:0000073 already has a GWAS Catalog example (GCST003682); GCST012462 (PMID:34155719) is an alternative. The PGS Catalog's GAS and GABRIELA ids both denote this term.

label: Genetic Analysis of Psoriasis Consortium
other synonyms: GAP consortium
example title: Multi-ancestry genome-wide meta-analysis with 472,819 individuals identifies 32 novel risk loci for psoriasis.
example quote: Samples of the Genetic Analysis of Psoriasis Consortium (GAPC) datasets were collected from subjects of European Caucasian descent at the participating institutions after obtaining informed consent in adherence with the Declaration of Helsinki Principles.
definition: An international consortium of psoriasis genetics research groups in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Austria, Finland, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain and Sweden, with a management committee chaired from King's College London, that pools its members' collections of people of European descent with psoriasis vulgaris, together with controls from national control collections, for genetic association studies of psoriasis, including a genome-wide association study with the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium 2 and an Immunochip case–control study.
countries: United_Kingdom || Republic_of_Ireland || Austria|Sweden|Netherlands || Germany || Finland || Spain || Italy
location quote: The UK controls were the WTCCC common controls that did not overlap with samples included in the original GWA studies (the dataset consisted of 6,740 1958 British Birth cohort and 2,900 UK Blood Service samples genotyped at the WTSI and the University of Virginia). || The Irish controls were provided by the Irish Blood Transfusion Service / TCD Biobank and the Irish cases collected with the aid of the Dublin Centre for Clinical Research. || We did not include specific controls from Austria or Sweden, but PCA analysis suggested that the cases from these cohorts were well matched to the controls from the Netherlands and Germany. || The German controls were obtained from the PopGen biobank and genotyped at the Institute of Clinical Molecular Biology, Christian-Albrechts-University of Kiel. || The Finland control data were from the DILGOM (Dietary, Lifestyle, and Genetic determinants of Obesity and Metabolic syndrome) collection || The GAPC cases and the Irish and Spanish controls were genotyped at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute (WTSI) || Groningen group (Italian and Dutch controls)
note: Tier D (D425), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: GAPC = the Genetic Analysis of Psoriasis Consortium's own Immunochip-genotyped case collection, one of several psoriasis GWAS cohorts (with PAGE, WTCCC2, FinnGen) combined in this meta-analysis. Typed as cohort like paired dataset PAGE (D425.4), not aggregation; no member cohorts named. Controls genotyped alongside GAPC (Irish/Spanish D425.12, UK-WTCCC D425.13, German-PopGen D425.14) are external, not GAPC's own, so no countries asserted. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym and example are right. GAPC is a consortium, not one sample: the Immunochip paper the tag's study cites (Tsoi et al. 2012, PMID:23143594) lists its management committee (chaired from King's College London) and member groups in London, Glasgow, Manchester, Sheffield, Graz, Helsinki, Erlangen, Nijmegen, Dublin, Rome, Barcelona, Gothenburg and Stockholm, and its Supplementary Table 2 shows the GAPC Immunochip dataset pooling the cases of those groups in nine countries with controls from other collections (WTCCC common controls from the 1958 British Birth Cohort and UK Blood Service, PopGen, DILGOM, the Irish Blood Transfusion Service/TCD Biobank, Groningen for the Italian and Dutch controls). Ellinghaus et al. 2016 (PMC4848113) names GAPC among 'the main disease consortia' whose management committees grant data access. So it is an aggregation, like WTCCC (COHO:0000182), not a cohort. The definition described only cases and the Immunochip dataset, called Immunochip genotyping genome-wide, and gave no where or who; the consortium also ran the 2010 psoriasis GWAS with WTCCC2 (PMID:20953190, authored as 'Genetic Analysis of Psoriasis Consortium & the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium 2'). Countries were missing although the source names them. If the curator links members with hasCohort: the 1958 British Birth Cohort (COHO:0000207) and UK Blood Service Control Group (COHO:0000347) as the WTCCC common controls, and PopGen (COHO:0000406), each backed by the quotes under United_Kingdom and Germany (PMC3510312); DILGOM is tier-D row D107, backed by the Finland quote. The case collections of the member groups have no names of their own. PAGE (COHO:0000145) is built the same way (a consortium's Immunochip dataset pooling groups' cases from the USA, Canada, Estonia and Germany with controls from EGCUT, KORA and HNR, same paper) but is typed cohort; the curator may want the two typed alike. Not the same as CASP (D204), NPF (D485) or WTCCC (COHO:0000182). 'GAP consortium' is the paper's own short form ('listed in the GAP consortium members list', PMC3510312 and P1's supplement).

label: Ghana Breast Health Study
other synonyms: Ghana breast health study
example title: Polygenic risk scores for prediction of breast cancer risk in women of African ancestry: a cross-ancestry approach.
example quote: We used data in women of AA from four breast cancer GWAS consortia and the Ghana Breast Health Study (GBHS)
definition: A population-based case–control study of breast cancer, a collaboration of the US National Cancer Institute with three major hospitals in Accra and Kumasi, Ghana (Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital and Peace and Love Hospital), that in 2013–2015 enrolled women aged 18–74 recommended for biopsy of a breast lesion suspicious for malignancy, or treated for breast cancer, at these hospitals, and population controls sampled by household enumeration of the surrounding districts and frequency-matched on age and district, collecting interviews and tumour tissue, blood, saliva and faecal samples to study breast cancer risk factors in a West African population.
