The study is a Dutch case series: surgically treated or surgeon-diagnosed Dupuytren patients recruited through plastic and hand surgery clinics from 2007, with blood DNA and surgeon-recorded clinical data. Its controls come from Lifelines, which is a separate cohort. The country quote now says where cases were recruited, not only which body gave ethics approval. PMID:28886342 gives 'EGA: EGAS00000000043 for GODDAF'. COHO's EGA curation (ega_study_cohorts.tsv) maps that study, 'WNT-signaling and Dupuytren's Disease' (856 Dupuytren patients and 2,836 LifeLines controls), only to LifeLines (COHO:0000108). Its cases are GODDAF cases, but the EGA record does not name GODDAF, so it gives no quotable EGA example. The authors of the NEJM 2011 pilot GWAS include a 'Dutch Dupuytren Study Group'; this looks like the recruiting group, not another name for the cohort, so it is not proposed as a synonym. Not a duplicate: COHO has the German Dupuytren Study (COHO:0000976), and BSSH-GODD (D379) is the UK case series.

label: Genetics of Impulsivity project
example title: Polygenic contributions to performance on the Balloon Analogue Risk Task.
example quote: Genetic, cognitive and behavioral data were similarly collected in the Genetics of Impulsivity (GOI) project, performed at the University of Georgia and the University of Chicago.
definition: A study of healthy young adults aged 18–30 of self-reported Caucasian, non-Hispanic ancestry with low levels of alcohol and drug use, recruited from the community at the University of Chicago and the University of Georgia in the United States, and from the Georgia site's undergraduate research pool, who completed a laboratory battery of impulsivity measures (delay discounting, response inhibition, risk-taking and impulsive personality traits) and gave saliva DNA for genotyping, to study the genetic basis of impulsivity.
location quote: A total of 934 Caucasian-ancestry participants 18–30 years of age were tested at two sites (40% at Athens, GA and 60% Chicago, IL).
note: Tier D (D439), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the GOI project sample (Georgia/Chicago), analysed alongside the CNP and MEGA samples in this paper. Only source is this GWAS paper's own methods section (no separate design paper); age/ancestry/site details read as the project's general eligibility criteria, not a further subset. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country and example are right. The definition was taken from the BART paper alone: it made the Balloon Analogue Risk Task the defining measure and ended by restating the name. It left out that the sample was screened to low substance use (AUDIT/DUDIT cut-offs, breath and urine tests) and for no recent psychiatric treatment, that participants came from the community and the University of Georgia's undergraduate research pool, and that the study's core is a battery of impulsivity measures with saliva DNA. The GWAS paper's references 15 and 58 (PMID:27449350 and PMID:29120849) describe this; the definition is rewritten from them. 'Genetics of Impulsivity (GOI) project' appears only in the BART paper and the PGS Catalog; the design papers describe the same sample without naming it. The GWAS Catalog study co-tags CNP (the UCLA Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics sample), which is a different cohort. Not a duplicate of COHO:0000657 (PATH, a Hamilton, Ontario community sample from an overlapping research group).

label: Genetics of Latinos Diabetic Retinopathy
other synonyms: Genetics of Latinos Diabetic Retinopathy Study
example title: Genome-wide study investigating effector genes and polygenic prediction for kidney function in persons with ancestry from Africa and the Americas.
example quote: Genetics of Latinos Diabetic Retinopathy (GOLDR): GOLDR was supported in part by the Genetics of Latinos Diabetic Retinopathy (GOLDR) Study grant EY14684.
definition: A family-based study of Latinos of Mexican or Central American origin in the Los Angeles area, run jointly by Cedars-Sinai Medical Center and the Los Angeles Biomedical Research Institute at Harbor-UCLA Medical Center, which from 2007 recruited probands with type 2 diabetes and either diabetic retinopathy or diabetes of at least ten years' duration together with their siblings and parents, with retinopathy graded from fundus photographs, to study the genetics of diabetic retinopathy and other complications of diabetes.
location quote: Large family-based cohort of Latinos with type 2 diabetes recruited exclusively in the Los Angeles area.
note: Tier D (D440), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the GOLDR cohort, one of many ancestry-specific cohorts in this multi-cohort kidney-function GWAS. Only acknowledgment/supplement text available, no design paper found. Southern California appears only in a genotyping-funding sentence, not recruitment, so no country asserted. Design and recruitment dates unknown. Checked 2026-09-23: The drafter had only the kidney GWAS's acknowledgement sentence. The definition therefore gave the grant number and nothing about design or place, and no country was asserted. The study's own papers settle both. PMID:25452868 says 'The GOLDR study is a family-based study assessing diabetes and diabetic complications in families (siblings and/or parents) of a proband, defined as having type 2 diabetes and either known DR or a diabetes duration of ≥10 years'. It also says participants are 'all Latinos of Mexican or Central American origin' recruited and studied at the Los Angeles BioMedical Research Institute at Harbor-UCLA Medical Center, and that the cohort was 'recruited exclusively in the Los Angeles area'. PMID:22330960, which that paper cites for GOLDR, gives recruitment from October 2007 as a joint study of Cedars-Sinai Medical Center and Harbor-UCLA. United States is added. The example is only an acknowledgement sentence, but it names the cohort in the example paper; the paper has no descriptive sentence about GOLDR. Not a duplicate of the Mexican-American Coronary Artery Disease Study (COHO:0000686), the Los Angeles Latino Eye Study (COHO:0000733) or the Mexican American Hypertension and Insulin Resistance study, which the same GWAS lists separately.

label: Global Parkinson's Genetics Program
other synonyms: Global Parkinson's Disease Genetics Program
example title: Identification of genetic risk loci and causal insights associated with Parkinson's disease in African and African admixed populations: a genome-wide association study.
example quote: Individuals were included from several cohorts that were available as a part of the Global Parkinson's Genetics Program, the International Parkinson's Disease Genomics Consortium Africa, and 23andMe.
definition: A worldwide programme, the first resource project of the Aligning Science Across Parkinson's initiative, that genotypes and sequences people with Parkinson's disease, and some controls, from existing and newly collected patient and cohort collections, working with established Parkinson's disease consortia and focusing on populations under-represented in genetic research, and shares the harmonised data to find genetic causes of and risk factors for typical and monogenic Parkinson's disease.
note: Tier D (D441), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the GP2 program, a source of several contributing PD cohorts, alongside IPDGC-Africa and 23andMe. Aggregation, not a single cohort: D441.17 and D441.25 show GP2 recruits and hosts many named contributing cohorts (e.g. PPMI, BioFIND, Coriell). Distinct from IPDGC (COHO:0000919), named separately in the same sentences. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, label and example are right. The definition was assembled from one consent sentence and one abstract phrase. It said GP2 'aggregates genetic and clinical data from numerous contributing Parkinson's disease cohorts and studies worldwide'; the design paper (PMID:33513272) says what the programme itself does. It generates genotype data on a purpose-built array and whole-genome and long-read sequence data. For the most part it uses existing or ongoing patient and cohort collections and established consortia, and in some cases supports new collection, especially in under-served communities. It has two arms, complex (typical) and monogenic Parkinson's disease, and it shares its data openly. Rewritten from that; funder names are replaced by its place as the first resource project of the Aligning Science Across Parkinson's initiative. Countries are left empty on purpose. GP2 is worldwide, and the design paper names countries only as planned partner efforts (IPDGC Africa, IPDGC East Asia, GEoPD, Lux-GIANT, LARGE-PD), not as recruitment. No parent: the Aligning Science Across Parkinson's initiative is a funding initiative, not a cohort aggregation, and AMP-PD (COHO:0000894) only hosts GP2's data. Possible hasCohort members for the curator, from the GWAS paper's list of 'GP2 cohorts with predicted African ancestry': PPMI (COHO:0000200) and BioFIND, BLAAC PD, Coriell, MDGAP-KINGS, University of Maryland, Baylor College of Medicine and IPDGCAF-NG. Caution: the 'PAGE' in that list is the PAGE study at pagestudy.org (Population Architecture using Genomics and Epidemiology), not COHO:0000145 (Psoriasis Association Genetics Extension), which the drafter's COHO match surfaced.

input name: Genomic Research on Asthma in the African Diaspora
label: Genomic Research on Asthma in the African Diaspora
other synonyms: Genomic Research on Asthma in the African Diaspora study
example title: Multiethnic genome-wide and HLA association study of total serum IgE level.
example quote: the Genomic Research on Asthma in the African Diaspora (GRAAD) consortium that recruited African American children and adults from the Baltimore-Washington DC metropolitan area [10]
definition: A case-control collection of self-reported African American children and adults with physician-diagnosed asthma and non-asthmatic controls from the Baltimore–Washington, DC metropolitan area, brought together by the Genomic Research on Asthma in the African Diaspora consortium from eight NIH-funded asthma studies and one study of healthy African Americans, to study genetic contributions to asthma and its disparities in people of African descent.
location quote: We note that the Amish, FHS, CAG and GRAAD are US-based studies; the Amish is a European descent population isolate [1], the FHS study recruited participants of European descent [5], and the CAG and GRAAD studies recruited African American individuals [2].
parent quote: Genomic Research on Asthma in the African Diaspora GRAAD
note: Tier D (D442), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: presumably the GRAAD cohort, though its abstract does not name it; P2 (an unrelated 2010 paper) names GRAAD as a replication cohort. Very thin: only a 2010 replication-cohort mention (D442.1) describes GRAAD. P1's abstract doesn't name it and no fuller P1 text was available, so example ev is null. 'African-American' is an ethnicity, not a place. Checked 2026-09-23: The drafter had only a 2010 replication mention, so the definition restated the name, there was no country, and the example had no quote. The GWAS paper's online supplement (Elsevier mmc1 of PMID:34536413) names GRAAD as one of five CAAPA studies in the IgE GWAS: 'the Genomic Research on Asthma in the African Diaspora (GRAAD) consortium that recruited African American children and adults from the Baltimore-Washington DC metropolitan area'. The same supplement says GRAAD is a 'US-based' study. The design paper (PMID:19910028) says the GRAAD subjects 'represent eight separate, NIH-funded studies of asthma in pediatric and adult African American populations, plus one study on healthy African Americans', with cases defined by reported and physician-diagnosed asthma. GRAAD is also one of the studies of the Trans-National Asthma Genetic Consortium (review key D527), listed in its Supplementary Table 1 under the EVE consortium, so a memberOf link to D527 is added. Type: the sources call GRAAD a 'consortium' that represents eight asthma studies and one healthy-control study. It is kept as a cohort, not an aggregation: those studies are never named, GRAAD recruited and genotyped as one Baltimore–Washington case-control sample, and it kept recruiting after its first GWAS (GRAAD(2)). Compare D001 (AABC), made an aggregation because its nine studies are named cohorts. The 2010 design paper's introduction also counts the Barbados families as a GRAAD population. Later papers (CAAPA, TAGC, the IgE GWAS) treat those as the separate Barbados Asthma Genetics Study (COHO:0000959), so no link to BAGS is proposed. Other aggregations naming GRAAD as a member are the Consortium on Asthma among African-ancestry Populations in the Americas (CAAPA) and the EVE asthma consortium; neither is in COHO or this review. If EVE is ever minted, TAGC should link to EVE and EVE to GRAAD. The parent quote is a row of TAGC's Supplementary Table 1 ('Description of TAGC studies included in the meta-analysis'), so it names GRAAD but not TAGC. A CAAPA quote for a future CAAPA term: 'Association statistics were generated by means of inverse-variance meta-analysis of CAAPA studies with mean African ancestry percentage > 75% (BASS, CAG, SAPPHIRE, HONDAS, JHS, JAAS, GRAAD, BAGS, SAGE II, HUFS, SARP).' (https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41467-019-08469-7/MediaObjects/41467_2019_8469_MOESM1_ESM.pdf).

input name: Genomic Research in Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency and Sarcoidosis study
label: Genomic Research in Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency and Sarcoidosis Study
other synonyms: Genomic Research in Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency and Sarcoidosis study
example title: Genome-wide association study identifies multiple HLA loci for sarcoidosis susceptibility.
example quote: DNA samples from sarcoidosis cases and controls were obtained from National Jewish Health (NJH), University of California, San Francisco, Genomic Research in Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency and Sarcoidosis (GRADS) consortium (17) and Cleveland Clinic Foundation.
definition: A multicentre observational study in the United States, solicited by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute and run by a genomics and informatics centre with several clinical centres, that enrolled adults with sarcoidosis across defined clinical phenotypes and adults over 35 with the PiZZ or PiMZ alpha-1 antitrypsin genotypes, with questionnaires, chest CT, lung function tests, bronchoalveolar lavage and blood samples, to study the role of the lung microbiome and genome-wide gene expression in the two diseases.
location quote: GRADS recruited 368 patients with sarcoidosis from 9 sarcoidosis centers across the United States [27].
note: Tier D (D443), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: GRADS as one external consortium source of sarcoidosis cases/controls, alongside NJH, UCSF and Cleveland Clinic Foundation. GRADS's own participating centres/dates aren't stated (NJH/UCSF/CCF in D443.4 are P1's OTHER, separate sources, not GRADS's own sites); NIH-sponsorship (D443.21) is a funder, so no country is asserted. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity and label are right. The definition was built from single-paper subsets: the PI*MZ/PI*ZZ subgroup of a 2025 paper and the PBMC/BAL RNA-seq subset of the GWAS. It missed the study's design, which the two 2015 protocol papers give. GRADS is an NHLBI-solicited multicentre observational study run by a genomics and informatics centre and clinical centres. It has an Alpha-1 protocol (adults over 35 with PiZZ or PiMZ genotypes, recruited mainly through the Alpha-1 Foundation Research Registry) and a Sarcoidosis protocol (confirmed sarcoidosis across nine clinical phenotype groups). Both protocols collect CT, lung function, BAL and blood to study the lung microbiome and genome expression. The drafter asserted no country, but the centres are in the United States (PMID:35806883: '9 sarcoidosis centers across the United States'). The draft's example quote runs across the section headings 'Materials and Methods' and 'Study design and population'. It is replaced by the same sentence from the PMC page, which starts after the headings and has no line-break hyphen. The protocol papers give seven clinical centres; later papers give nine. The definition therefore gives no number. The Alpha-1 protocol's PiMM comparison group was drawn from SPIROMICS (COHO:0000652), whose BAL samples were shared with GRADS. That is sample sharing, not membership, so no parent. The sarcoidosis GWAS calls GRADS a 'consortium', but it is one study with two protocols, so it is typed as a cohort.

input name: Genomics of Resistance to Immunodeficiency Virus
label: Genomics of Resistance to Immunodeficiency Virus
other synonyms: Genetics of Resistance to Immunodeficiency Virus
example title: Multiancestry Genome-Wide Association Study Identifies Variants in a Zinc Finger Gene Cluster as Novel Regulators of HIV Control.
definition: A collection of DNA samples, established in France in 1995, from HIV-1-infected people of European descent living in France with extreme courses of infection: long-term non-progressors (infected for more than eight years with CD4 T-cell counts above 500/mm3 and no symptoms) and rapid progressors. It is used to identify host genes associated with slow and rapid progression to AIDS, with genetic analyses comparing its members with seronegative French controls from another study.
location quote: However, three independent SNPs in the top ten associations between SNP genotypes and time between seroconversion and AIDS-diagnosis, and one from the top ten associations between SNP genotypes and time between seroconversion and AIDS-related death, had P-values smaller than 0.05 in the French Genomics of Resistance to Immunodeficiency Virus cohort on disease progression.
parent quote: The GRIV cohort, which includes Long-Term Non-Progressors (LTNP) and Elite Controllers (ECs), is part of the ICGH consortium (9).
note: Tier D (D444), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: presumably the GRIV cohort via the GWAS Catalog tag, though P1's abstract doesn't name it; P2-P5 consistently describe the French LTNP/RP/control GRIV cohort. P1's abstract doesn't name GRIV, so example ev is null; identity and definition instead rest on P2-P5 (2010-2014), which consistently describe the same French cohort. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country and example accession are right. The definition counted 'a healthy uninfected control group' as part of the cohort. The GRIV analyses compare cases with French seronegative controls from the D.E.S.I.R. programme ('The control group used for comparison with GRIV subjects [22], [23] comprised 697 French HIV-1 seronegative individuals of Caucasian descent from the D.E.S.I.R. program [49].', PMID:21750674), so the controls are not GRIV members. The definition also framed the cohort as being about 'resistance to HIV infection' when it studies progression. It left out that GRIV was established in 1995, that it enrolled only white people of European descent living in France, and how long-term non-progression was defined (PMID:26367535, PMID:38146367). The draft had no parent, but GRIV is a participating cohort of the International Collaboration for the Genomics of HIV (review key D125): 'The GRIV cohort, which includes Long-Term Non-Progressors (LTNP) and Elite Controllers (ECs), is part of the ICGH consortium'. PMID:23935489 also lists 'The GRIV Cohort in France' among ICGH's participating cohorts. The example stays GCST90824165 without a quote until the paper can be read (the D390 check did the same for CHAVI in this study). The D125 check reports that ICGH's sex-stratified GWAS (PMID:37097752, Supplementary Table S1) lists GRIV together with ANRS PRIMO. I could not re-read it: the JCI Insight supplement is behind reCAPTCHA. If the tag in the spVL GWAS denotes a pooled French dataset, the curator should say so. PMID:23935489 says 'Genotypes for uninfected control individuals were obtained directly from three of the participating centers (GRIV, ACS, CHAVI)'. GRIV's own papers take their seronegative controls from the D.E.S.I.R. programme, so these were probably D.E.S.I.R. genotypes supplied through GRIV (an inference, not stated), not GRIV members.

label: Guangzhou Twin Eye Study
other synonyms: Guangzhou twin eye study|Guangzhou Twins Eye Study
example title: Novel loci for ocular axial length identified through extreme-phenotype genome-wide association study in Chinese populations.
example quote: A genome-wide association study meta-analysis was conducted in totalling 2644 Chinese individuals from 3 cohorts: the Guangzhou cohort (GZ, 537 high myopes and 151 hyperopes), Wenzhou cohort (334 high myopes and 6 hyperopes) and Guangzhou Twin Eye Study (1051 participants with normally distributed AL).
definition: A longitudinal twin study in Guangzhou, China, that from 2006 enrolled twin pairs aged 7 to 15 years from the population-based Guangzhou Twin Registry, living near the Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center, together with some of their parents or siblings. It collected DNA and baseline eye measurements, then examined the twins annually until 2018 for progressive traits such as cycloplegic refraction, axial length, height and weight, to study the genetic and environmental causes of common eye diseases, particularly myopia.
location quote: The Guangzhou Twins Eye Study (GTES) is a longitudinal study including over 1200 pairs of twins and their parents or siblings living in Guangzhou, China
note: Tier D (D445), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the Guangzhou Twin Eye Study, one of 3 distinct Chinese cohorts (with GZ and Wenzhou) meta-analysed for ocular axial length. Distinct from the 'Guangzhou cohort (GZ)' (see D446, this batch) and Wenzhou cohort, both named separately in the same paper. Two title casings appear (Title Case and lower-case 'twin eye study'); both kept. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label and example are right. The definition described the study through three 2008 heritability papers (anterior chamber depth, angle width, optic disc) as a 'classic twin study' of ocular measurements. That is a set of early analyses, not the cohort. The study's own profiles (PMID:17254403, PMID:23186635, PMID:32014069) describe a longitudinal cohort: from 2006, about 1,300 twin pairs aged 7-15 from the population-based Guangzhou Twin Registry, with parents or siblings, DNA at baseline and annual examinations of refraction, axial length, height and weight, mainly to study myopia. The draft's China quote rested on 'Chinese children' in a paper title; it is replaced by a sentence that places the twins in Guangzhou, China. GTES is the eye cohort of the Guangzhou Twin Project, which is built on the Guangzhou Twin Registry (initiated 2005, about 9,700 twin pairs born 1987-2000, from Guangzhou's household registry) and also planned an arm of adult twins aged 50 and over. COHO has no term for the registry or project, so no parent. 'Guangzhou Twin Project' is not proposed as a synonym because it is the broader project. The draft's case variant 'Guangzhou twin eye study' is kept, and the variant 'Guangzhou Twins Eye Study' (PMC5118713) is added. Not the same as the Born in Guangzhou Cohort Study (COHO:0000624), the Guangzhou Nutrition and Health Study (E436) or the Guangzhou myopia case series of D446.

label: Guangzhou cohort
example title: Novel loci for ocular axial length identified through extreme-phenotype genome-wide association study in Chinese populations.
example quote: A genome-wide association study meta-analysis was conducted in totalling 2644 Chinese individuals from 3 cohorts: the Guangzhou cohort (GZ, 537 high myopes and 151 hyperopes), Wenzhou cohort (334 high myopes and 6 hyperopes) and Guangzhou Twin Eye Study (1051 participants with normally distributed AL).
definition: A cohort of high myopes and hyperopes recruited in Guangzhou, China, one of three Chinese cohorts combined in a genome-wide association meta-analysis of ocular axial length.
location quote: A genome-wide association study meta-analysis was conducted in totalling 2644 Chinese individuals from 3 cohorts: the Guangzhou cohort (GZ, 537 high myopes and 151 hyperopes), Wenzhou cohort (334 high myopes and 6 hyperopes) and Guangzhou Twin Eye Study (1051 participants with normally distributed AL).
note: Tier D (D446), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the 'Guangzhou cohort' (GZ), a case series of high myopes and hyperopes, distinct from the Guangzhou Twin Eye Study and Wenzhou cohort in the same paper. PGS Catalog name ('Asian Consortium, Colorectal Cancer Guangzhou') names an unrelated study, not used. Evidence is entirely from one ophthalmology paper (shared with D445), which also names GTES and Wenzhou as distinct cohorts; no dedicated design paper for GZ. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft is right for the GWAS tag: in GCST90319888 (PMID:37524447) 'Guangzhou' is 'the Guangzhou cohort (GZ, 537 high myopes and 151 hyperopes)', an extreme-refraction sample. It is one of three Chinese cohorts in the axial-length GWAS, distinct from the Guangzhou Twin Eye Study (D445) and the Wenzhou cohort. It is not an aggregation, despite the triage hint. The PGS Catalog id 'Guangzhou' denotes a different cohort that COHO lacks: the Guangzhou colorectal cancer case-control study of the Asia Colorectal Cancer Consortium. The drafter set it aside as 'an unrelated study'; it is given in full under extra. The GZ cohort is known only from the abstract and contributor statement of its one paper, so the definition cannot say more (recruitment site, dates, criteria). Its acronym 'GZ' clashes with nothing in COHO. Its acronym 'Guangzhou' (the GWAS tag) is shared with the extra Guangzhou Colorectal Cancer Study (the PGS id); if both are minted, both need an IAO:0000116 note, e.g. 'The acronym Guangzhou also denotes the Guangzhou Colorectal Cancer Study (COHO:nnnnnnn); this term is the Guangzhou myopia and hyperopia cohort of the axial-length GWAS.' The D079 check already names D446 as an ACCC member study by its PGS name; that membership belongs to the extra record, not to this ophthalmic cohort.

label: Guangzhou Colorectal Cancer Study
other synonyms: Guangzhou CRC Study|Asian Consortium, Colorectal Cancer Guangzhou
example title: Large-scale genetic study in East Asians identifies six new loci associated with colorectal cancer risk.
example quote: Specifically, stage 1 (GWAS discovery) consisted of five studies: Shanghai CRC Study 1 (Shanghai-1, n = 3,102), Shanghai CRC Study 2 (Shanghai-2, n = 908), Guangzhou CRC Study 1 (Guangzhou-1, n = 1,603), Aichi CRC Study 1 (Aichi-1, n =1,346), and Korean Cancer Prevention Study-II CRC (KCPS-II, n = 1,301).
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of colorectal cancer in Guangzhou, China. Its cases are patients with histopathologically confirmed colorectal cancer recruited at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center between 2002 and 2012, and its controls are cancer-free men and women recruited in the same period from the physical examination centres of several large hospitals in Guangdong. Its four case-control collections (Guangzhou-1 to Guangzhou-4) were genotyped for genome-wide association studies of colorectal cancer in East Asians.
location quote: Cases were histopathologically confirmed patients with CRC recruited from Sun Yat-Sen University Cancer Center between January 2002 and January 2012 and controls were cancer-free men and women recruited from the physical examination centers of several large hospitals in Guangdong during the same time period.
parent quote: Studies (listed with grant support) participating in the Asia Colorectal Cancer Consortium include the Shanghai Women's Health Study (US NIH, R37CA070867, UM1CA182910), the Shanghai Men's Health Study (US NIH, R01CA082729, UM1CA173640), the Shanghai Breast and Endometrial Cancer Studies (US NIH, R01CA064277 and R01CA092585; contributing only controls), the Shanghai Colorectal Cancer Study 3 (US NIH, R37CA070867, R01CA188214 and Anne Potter Wilson Chair funds), the Guangzhou Colorectal Cancer Study
note: Tier D (D446x), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. This is what the PGS Catalog cohort id 'Guangzhou' ('Asian Consortium, Colorectal Cancer Guangzhou') denotes: its scores PGS000801, PGS000802, PGS001776, PGS002252 and PGS002742-4 were developed from the Asia Colorectal Cancer Consortium GWAS (GCST001792/PMID:23263487, GCST002454/PMID:24836286, GCST003799/PMID:26965516, GCST007552/PMID:30529582). The 2014 supplement describes 'The Guangzhou CRC Study' as 'four case-control collections, Guangzhou- 1, Guangzhou-2, Guangzhou-3 and Guangzhou-4'. The label is the spelled-out name used in the ACCC member list of the PMID:36539618 supplement. The PGS Catalog's constructed name is kept as a synonym only because the Catalog uses it. None of these GWAS Catalog studies carries a cohort tag in gwas_catalog_cohorts.tsv.gz, so the example GCST002454 comes from the PGS Catalog's source-GWAS link, not a GWAS Catalog tag; the curator may prefer a paper example without GCST. Acronym clash: 'Guangzhou' is also the GWAS Catalog tag of the Guangzhou myopia/hyperopia cohort (the D446 term), so both terms need an IAO:0000116 clash note. Not in COHO: the only Guangzhou term is the Born in Guangzhou Cohort Study (COHO:0000624). Added by the check as another cohort that D446's tag or PGS id denotes.

label: Hemophilia Growth and Development Study
example title: Africa-specific human genetic variation near CHD1L associates with HIV-1 load.
example quote: The HGDS is a multicenter study of hemophilia and its complications that was established in 1988.
definition: A multicentre longitudinal study, established in 1988 at 14 hemophilia treatment centres in the United States, of boys and young men aged 6 to 19 years with moderate to severe hemophilia, HIV-infected through clotting factor concentrates or HIV-uninfected, with their non-hemophiliac, HIV-uninfected male siblings as a comparison group, followed until 1996/97 to study the impact of HIV on physical growth and sexual maturation, immune function, and neurological and neuropsychological functioning.
location quote: Data were prospectively collected in 14 U.S. hemophilia treatment centers through 1996/97.
parent quote: The Hemophilia Growth and Development Study (HGDS) in the USA
note: Tier D (D447), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: one of several North American hemophilia/HIV cohorts pooled for genotyping in a multi-cohort HIV-1 host-genetics study; not described beyond being listed in a supplementary table. P1 (the tagged GWAS paper) only lists HGDS in a flattened supplementary table, not a naming sentence, so example ev is null; identity and definition come from HGDS's own design/profile papers (P2, P4, P7). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronym and country are right. The definition called it a natural history study of hemophilia; its design paper (PMID:8498644) describes a multicentre longitudinal study of the impact of HIV infection on males aged 6 to 19 with moderate to severe hemophilia (growth and sexual maturation, immune function, neurological and neuropsychological functioning), with non-hemophiliac, HIV-uninfected male siblings as comparison (PMID:11075607); the age range and the end of follow-up (1996/97) were missing. The example had no quote: the tagged paper's Supplementary Note 2 describes the HGDS among the cohorts contributing to the International Collaboration for the Genomics of HIV, and its first descriptive sentence is now the quote. Missing parent: the HGDS is listed among the 'Cohorts, studies, and centers participating in the International Collaboration for the Genomics of HIV' (PMID:23935489), review name D125. The parent D125 holds only if ICGH is minted as an aggregation, as the checks of D080, D354 and D359 also assume. HGDS is distinct from the Multicenter Hemophilia Cohort Studies (D473), which sits in the same genotyping group.

label: Hordaland Health Study
other synonyms: Hordaland Health Studies|Helseundersøkelsen i Hordaland|Helseundersøkelsene i Hordaland

Checked 2026-09-23: The draft called IUPUI an institutional label for an unnamed pool with 'no recruitment dates, design or eligibility'. That is not so: the tag denotes one standing research collection, 'the IUPUI sample', which the paper's cited source describes. White et al. 2021 (PMID:33288918, Supplementary Methods; repeated in open access in PMID:33692830): 'The IUPUI sample includes 3D images and genotypic data from individuals recruited in Indianapolis, IN and Twinsburg, OH (IUPUI IRB 1409306349).' Participants self-reported age, height, weight and ancestry; minors were included with a parent's or guardian's signature; no restrictions were placed on recruitment; it was genotyped on the Illumina Multi-Ethnic Global array; and 'IUPUI personnel, data collection, and analyses were supported by the National Institute of Justice'. The same protocol (1409306349) appears in at least 15 papers (Europe PMC full-text search), among them facial-shape GWAS, facial asymmetry studies and the 2018 head-hair-shape GWAS (PMID:29220522, 'US study'). They call it the IUPUI sample, IUPUI dataset, 'Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis (IUPUI) cohort' (PMID:36539420) and 'US Indiana Study' (PMID:40670343). Unlike the review's Karolinska, TUM, UAB and Steno rows, where an institution tag stands for different or undescribed samples, this tag means one defined, recurring sample. It has no name of its own beyond the institution's, so the label uses the expanded form the literature uses. Borderline by the review's own precedents. If the curator does not want institution-named collections minted even when they are defined (as the Karolinska row was not), the verdict can stay 'not a cohort'. What sets this row apart is that the tag and the literature consistently mean one collection under one ethics protocol, as with the minted OHSU row. The sample is distinct from 3D Facial Norms (D188) and from the Penn State sample, which has no tag or row of its own. 'US-I' is a paper-local abbreviation (PMID:40670343), so it is not added as an acronym. No COHO or review-row clash for IUPUI; E543 'Indiana cohort' has no PGS use and nothing links it to this sample. Recruitment years are not stated in any text read. The IRB number suggests a 2014 protocol, but that is not asserted.

example title: A Swedish Genome-Wide Haplotype Association Analysis Identifies a Novel Breast Cancer Susceptibility Locus in 8p21.2 and Characterizes Three Loci on Chromosomes 10, 11 and 16.
example quote: We included 3215 invasive breast cancer cases from two Swedish cohorts, KARMA (n = 2712) and KARBAC (n = 503), and controls without family history of breast cancer from KARMA (n = 5032) in the analysis.
definition: A breast cancer case-control study in Stockholm, Sweden, whose cases are consecutive breast cancer patients treated at the oncology departments of Huddinge and Söder hospitals from 1998 to 2000 and women with familial breast cancer without BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations seen at the Department of Clinical Genetics of Karolinska University Hospital from 2000, and whose controls are blood donors from the same region, used to study inherited susceptibility to breast cancer.
location quote: We included 3215 invasive breast cancer cases from two Swedish cohorts, KARMA (n = 2712) and KARBAC (n = 503), and controls without family history of breast cancer from KARMA (n = 5032) in the analysis.
parent quote: Therefore, we were prompted to reanalyze two Swedish breast cancer cohorts—KARMA and KARBAC—consisting of 3200 invasive breast cancer cases and 5021 controls previously analyzed within the BCAC consortium [8,9,10,16,17,18,19].
note: Tier D (D460), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred only for want of a quotable full name, and it is quotable. 'Financial support for the Karolinska Breast Cancer Study (KARBAC) was provided through the regional agreement on medical training and clinical research (ALF) between Stockholm County Council and Karolinska Institutet' (PMID:27711073, PMC5382131), and BCAC's study tables use the same name. The BCAC study-description table (PMID:24943594, supplementary Table 1, open access) gives the design: '1. Familial cases from Department of Clinical Genetics, Karolinska University Hospital, Stockholm. 2. Consecutive cases from Department of Oncology, Huddinge & Söder Hospital, Stockholm 1998-2000. Blood donors of mixed gender from same geographical region.' The controls were sampled from blood donors in 2004. So KARBAC is a case-control study, not only the two case series the tagged GWAS used, which took its controls from KARMA. The consecutive cases are the population-based Stockholm series of Margolin et al. 2004 (PMID:15345109): all incident surgically treated breast cancer in a 19-month period. The familial cases are BRCA1/2-negative, recruited through genetic counselling from February 2000 to January 2012 (PMID:35267517; family series in PMID:26082817). Distinct from KARMA (D130), pKARMA (D286) and the Singapore and Sweden Breast Cancer Study (COHO:0000935, SASBAC). In the tagged GWAS, KARBAC supplies only cases; its own blood-donor controls appear in BCAC/iCOGS analyses (PMID:24943594 Table 1 lists KARBAC controls). The BCAC table's parent quote comes from the tagged paper; the BCAC DACC list sentence (e.g. PMC7808397) is an alternative. No COHO or review-row clash for KARBAC.

label: Korea National Cancer Center gastric cancer case-control study
example title: Functional Annotation and Gene Set Analysis of Gastric Cancer Risk Loci in a Korean Population.
example quote: For GWAS analysis, genotypes from the National Cancer Center (NCC) and an urban community of the Korean Genome Epidemiology Study (KoGES) were used.
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of gastric cancer at the National Cancer Center in Goyang, South Korea, that from March 2011 to December 2014 recruited patients recently diagnosed with gastric cancer at its Center for Gastric Cancer as cases and cancer-free people attending health-screening check-ups at its Center for Cancer Prevention and Detection as controls, with lifestyle and food-frequency questionnaires and blood DNA genotyped on an exome array, to study dietary and genetic risk factors for gastric cancer.
location quote: This case-control study was conducted at the Center for Gastric Cancer (CGC) and the Center for Cancer Prevention & Detection (CCPD) of the National Cancer Center (NCC) in Korea between March 2011 and December 2014.
note: Tier D (D461), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred; research settles it, and the GWAS tag and the PGS id mean two different National Cancer Center (Korea) studies. The only GWAS Catalog study with the tag, GCST90319844 (PMID:37340842), is a gastric cancer GWAS whose 'NCC' samples are '450 GC cases and 1,134 healthy controls' genotyped on the Axiom Exome 319 chip, under IRB NCC2021-0181. That is the NCC hospital-based gastric cancer case-control study, described in its own papers (PMID:33634021, PMID:38810984; same exome array, same IRB number in the latter). It 'was conducted at the Center for Gastric Cancer (CGC) and the Center for Cancer Prevention & Detection (CCPD) of the National Cancer Center (NCC) in Korea between March 2011 and December 2014'. Its cases are recently diagnosed gastric cancer patients and its controls health-screening examinees confirmed cancer-free through the Korea Central Cancer Registry. The PGS Catalog id Korea-NCC ('Korean-National Cancer Center Study') is used only in colorectal cancer work of the Asia Colorectal Cancer Consortium. There it is the 'Korea-NCC (National Cancer Center) Colorectal Cancer Study', a separate case-control study (MEGA array), given below under extra. The gastric study has no name of its own, so the label is constructed. The PGS name is kept off this term because it belongs to the colorectal study. Both terms would carry the acronym Korea-NCC: the gastric study because the GWAS Catalog tags it, the colorectal study because the PGS Catalog id and the ACCC papers use it. Each needs an IAO:0000116 editor note naming the other. The two studies draw controls from the same pool, health-screening examinees at the NCC Center for Cancer Prevention and Detection, so their control sets may overlap. Their case series, dates and genotyping differ, so they are two terms. An umbrella term is not proposed, because no source names one. Not the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (COHO:0000411), whose urban-community samples the gastric GWAS also used (tag KoGES). No COHO or review-row clash beyond this row.

input name: Low Concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression Study
label: Low Concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression Study
other synonyms: Low-Concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression Study|LAMP Study
example title: Genome-wide association study identified novel loci and gene-environment interaction for refractive error in children.
example quote: To identify novel genetic loci for children refractive error, we performed a meta-analysis of two genome-wide association studies (GWASs) of spherical equivalent (SE) in 1,237 children from the population-based Hong Kong Children Eye Study (HKCES) and the Low Concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression (LAMP) study.
definition: A randomised, double-masked, placebo-controlled trial at the Chinese University of Hong Kong Eye Centre that from 2016 to 2017 enrolled children aged 4 to 12 with myopia in both eyes, limited astigmatism and documented myopic progression in the previous year, assigned them to nightly 0.05%, 0.025% or 0.01% atropine eye drops or placebo, and followed them in later phases (placebo switched to atropine, re-randomisation to continued treatment or washout, and longer-term follow-up), to evaluate the efficacy and safety of low-concentration atropine for slowing myopia progression.
location quote: This study was conducted from January 2016 to November 2017 at the CUHK Eye Centre of the Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China.
note: Tier D (D463), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the LAMP trial cohort, one of two datasets (with HKCES) meta-analysed for a childhood refractive-error GWAS. Trial design/eligibility from the original LAMP paper (P3) and P1's meta-GWAS text agree closely. Country not asserted: CUHK sponsors the trial registry (D463.23) but no unit states where participants were recruited, though pairing with the Hong Kong-based HKCES suggests Hong Kong. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type and example are right. The definition gave no place, dates or sponsor, left out the progression criterion, described only the first year and restated the design paper's thresholds. The tagged paper's own supplement (Table S20, 'Study cohorts description') settles the missing facts: 'LAMP is a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-masked trial ... This study was conducted from January 2016 to November 2017 at the CUHK Eye Centre of the Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China.' Enrolled children also needed 'documented myopic progression of at least 0.5D in the past 1 year'. The trial continued in phases (PMID:41732593, PMC12925536): in year 2 the placebo group switched to 0.05% atropine; in year 3 the groups were re-randomised to continued treatment or washout; years 4-5 were further follow-up. The draft called the place unknown, but the country is Hong Kong. The trial's registry title (ChiCTR-TRC-13004032, WHO ICTRP record, sponsor CUHK Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences) is 'Low Concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression (LAMP-1) Study', so LAMP-1 is added as an acronym and 'LAMP Study' as a synonym. Keep apart from D449 HKCES (the population-based Hong Kong Children Eye Study, the other discovery cohort of the same GWAS) and from the later LAMP2 trial of myopia onset, which is not in COHO or this review. The GWAS's adult set 'Adult-2' is 'parents of children from LAMP' (supplement Table S22), so a later catalogue may tag LAMP parents. The trial's hyphenated spelling ('Low-Concentration ...') is the form in its phase-report titles; the unhyphenated label matches its registry title and the PGS Catalog, so either is defensible. No parent: the trial is not part of HKCES or any consortium in COHO.

label: Leipzig Childhood Obesity cohort
other synonyms: Leipzig Childhood Obesity Cohort|Leipzig childhood obesity cohort|Leipzig Childhood Obesity Study|Leipzig Obesity Childhood Cohort|LEIPZIG Kids|Extended Geno- and Phenotyping of Overweight and Obese Children and Adolescents
example title: The trans-ancestral genomic architecture of glycemic traits.
example quote: LEIPZIG-kids LEIPZIG Kids were supported by the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF), Germany, Integrated Research and Treatment Centre 60 (IFB) Adiposity Diseases FKZ: 01EO1001
definition: An obesity-enriched cohort of children and adolescents from the Leipzig area, Germany, recruited through the paediatric obesity outpatient clinic of Leipzig University Medical Center and run by its Center for Pediatric Research, with oral glucose tolerance tests, serum and DNA samples collected at clinic visits and regular follow-up, some into adulthood, to identify genetic variants and biomarkers underlying childhood obesity and its metabolic consequences.
location quote: In this study, we adopt a comprehensive approach to describe the transition of children and adolescents with overweight or obesity into adulthood from an obesity center in Germany.
note: Tier D (D464), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: LEIPZIG Kids/Leipzig Childhood Obesity cohort, one of dozens of cohorts contributing to a multi-cohort trans-ancestral glycemic-traits meta-analysis. Name draws on 3 independent papers (adulthood follow-up, ASIP mutation screen, P1's funding acknowledgment for 'LEIPZIG-kids'/'LEIPZIG Kids') that agree on identity; no single design paper with recruitment dates or eligibility was in the evidence. D464.27 (n and BMI detail) is marked not-quotable, so unused. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type and country are right, and there is no parent. The definition was built from a funding acknowledgement ('supported by' IFB and LIFE, which is funding, not design) and one follow-up paper, and it lacked who is enrolled, where, by whom and why. Those facts come from the cohort's registration (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04491344, 'Leipzig Childhood Obesity Study'): all paediatric patients of the adiposity outpatient clinic, OGTT serum and DNA samples, and an aim 'to identify polymorphisms that make children and adolescents more prone to obesity and metabolic dysfunction, as well as to identify biomarkers'. Its own papers add: 'the obesity-enriched Leipzig Childhood Obesity Cohort (recruited from the local obesity outpatient clinic, IRB-Nr: 007/04, NCT04491344)' (PMID:37465325); children 'from the area around Leipzig ... included in the study with subsequent regular follow-ups', with an adulthood follow-up in 2021-2023 (PMID:41168416). The country and example quotes were one long acknowledgement that runs into the LifeLines funding text. The country quote is replaced by a direct statement, and the example quote is cut to the LEIPZIG-kids part. The consortium abbreviations LEIPZIG_CHILDHOOD_IFB and Leipzig-childhood_IFB (MAGIC 2012, PMID:22885924) and the registered names are added. Distinct from COHO:0000588 Leipzig Adults (LEIPZIG-adults / LEIPZIG_ADULT_IFB, the adult IFB obesity cohort) and from COHO:0000487 LIFE-Heart. It is also distinct from LIFE Child, the population-based Leipzig children's cohort that the same group analyses alongside it, which is not in COHO. GWAS Catalog tagging of PMID:34059833 is incomplete: MAGIC's HbA1c analysis (GCST90002244) included LEIPZIG-adults as well, but only 'Leipzig' is tagged there, while GCST90002227/29 carry Leipzig_Adults without Leipzig. The PGS Catalog lists both cohorts for GCST90002244. The cohort's start is given as 2002 in the registry, but a 2023 paper pools paediatric data from 1999, so no start year is asserted.

label: Lung Oncology Research & Discovery
other synonyms: Lung Oncology Research and Discovery
example title: Polygenic inheritance and its interplay with smoking history in predicting lung cancer diagnosis: a French-Canadian case-control cohort.
example quote: LORD consists of a single site case-only cohort based on a 20-year data collection (1999–2021) of patients who underwent lung cancer surgery at IUCPQ-UL.
definition: An ongoing single-site, case-only cohort of patients who have undergone lung cancer surgery since 1999 at the Quebec Heart and Lung Institute (Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Québec – Université Laval) in Quebec City, Canada, with diagnoses confirmed by pathology of the resected specimens, clinical data and consent to the institute's biobank, assembled by a translational research programme towards precision medicine in lung cancer and used for germline genetic and tumour molecular studies.
location quote: Lung Oncology Research & Discovery (LORD) is an ongoing translational research program towards precision medicine in lung cancer diagnosis, management and treatment conducted at the Quebec Heart and Lung Institute (IUCPQ-UL or “Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Québec—Université Laval”), located in Quebec City, Canada.
note: Tier D (D465), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the LORD case-only surgical lung-cancer cohort, paired analytically with CARTaGENE's population controls as 'LORD/CARTaGENE' for a PRS validation study. LORD is clearly self-described in its own GWAS paper (P1); combined with CARTaGENE (COHO:0000031, already a candidate) only for case-control matching in this analysis, not membership. No parent asserted. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label (the programme's own '&' spelling; the PGS Catalog's 'and' form is a synonym), type, acronym, country and example are right, and there is no parent. The definition is accurate but fixes the programme at the 1999-2021 collection that one paper analysed ('a 20-year data collection (1999–2021)'), although LORD is described as ongoing. It also omits that patients consent to the IUCPQ-UL biobank ('All patients from the LORD cohort provided written informed consent to participate in our local biobank') and that the cohort also serves tumour profiling (PMID:40209611, 'Results from the LORD project': 50-gene panel sequencing of resected adenocarcinomas). The wording is adjusted to cover these. CARTaGENE (COHO:0000031) supplied only the matched controls; 'LORD/CARTaGENE' is an analysis dataset, not a parent or member relation. The funding statement ties the programme's name to a donation to the IUCPQ Foundation from a donor of that surname, so 'LORD' may not be an expansion acronym at heart. It is still the programme's acronym as used. No COHO or review-row clash.

label: Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study
example title: Africa-specific human genetic variation near CHD1L associates with HIV-1 load.
example quote: The Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study (MACS) DESCRIPTION: The Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study (MACS) is an ongoing prospective study of the natural and treated histories of HIV-1 infection in homosexual and bisexual men conducted by sites located in Baltimore, Chicago, Pittsburgh and Los Angeles.
definition: A prospective multicentre cohort study of gay and bisexual men with and without HIV-1 infection, first enrolled in 1984–1985 at sites in Baltimore/Washington DC, Chicago, Pittsburgh and Los Angeles in the United States, with later enrolment waves, and followed with interviews, physical examinations, laboratory testing and specimen banking every six months, to study the natural and treated history of HIV infection and AIDS and its risk factors; in 2019 it was combined with the Women's Interagency HIV Study into the MACS/WIHS Combined Cohort Study.
location quote: The MACS targeted enrollment of men who have sex with men (MSM), with initial enrollment during 1984–1985 in 4 cities across the United States (2) and additional enrollment waves in 1987–1990 and 2001–2003, and limited replenishment enrollment from 2010 to 2017.
parent quote: The Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study (MACS) DESCRIPTION: The Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study (MACS) is an ongoing prospective study of the natural and treated histories of HIV-1 infection in homosexual and bisexual men conducted by sites located in Baltimore, Chicago, Pittsburgh and Los Angeles.
note: Tier D (D466), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: MACS, one of six contributing cohort groups (Illumina 1M Duo genotyping, US African-American ancestry) in a multi-cohort GWAS meta-analysis of HIV-1 viral-load control. D466.1 is an unstructured, table-like line (not pipe-delimited so not marked ⊞) — the only P1 unit naming MACS; used as example evidence despite the awkward format. Design and setting otherwise well supported by MACS's own 1987 papers (P2-P4). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronym and country are right. The definition says 'enrolled from 1985', but the first evaluations ran April 1984 to April 1985 (PMID:3300281). It gives only the first wave; there were later waves in 1987-1990 and 2001-2003 and replenishment in 2010-2017. It does not say that HIV-seronegative men were followed too. It calls MACS ongoing without noting that 'In 2019, the National Institutes of Health combined the Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study (MACS) and the Women’s Interagency HIV Study (WIHS) into the MACS/WIHS Combined Cohort Study (MWCCS)' (PMID:33675224). The country quote named only cities; it is replaced by one naming the United States. The parent was missing. In the tagged paper MACS is listed among the 'Cohorts and Individuals contributing to the International Consortium for the Genomics of HIV' (Supplementary Note), so it is memberOf D125, as the checks of the co-listed ALIVE (D359), HGDS (D447) and MHCS (D473) also set. The example quote was a flattened table row; the supplement's MACS description sentence replaces it. Parent D125 holds only if the International Collaboration for the Genomics of HIV is minted as an aggregation, as its check (d12) proposes. The quote is MACS's item under the Supplementary Note heading, which cannot be joined to the heading in one span; the same text serves as the example quote. The MACS/WIHS Combined Cohort Study (MWCCS), into which MACS was merged in 2019, and the Women's Interagency HIV Study are not in COHO or this review. Mint MWCCS later as an aggregation with hasCohort MACS if a catalogue tags it. The same study table also groups MACS with the US military HIV Natural History Study (E1182), a separate cohort. No COHO clash for the acronym MACS.

label: Manchester Lung Health Check
other synonyms: Manchester Lung Health Check cohort
example title: Validation of lung cancer polygenic risk scores in a high-risk case-control cohort.
example quote: We validated 9 PRSs in a high-risk case-control cohort, comprising genotype data from 652 surgical patients with LC and 550 cancer-free, high-risk (PLCOM2012 score ≥ 1.51%) participants of the Manchester Lung Health Check, a community-based LC screening program (n = 550).
definition: A community-based targeted lung cancer screening programme in socioeconomically deprived areas of Manchester, England, run by Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust, which began as a pilot in 2016 and continued in later programmes. It invites ever-smokers registered with local general practices (aged 55–74 in the pilot, 55–80 later) to a nurse-led Lung Health Check on mobile units, with lung cancer risk calculation (PLCOm2012), symptom assessment, spirometry and smoking cessation advice, offers annual low-dose CT screening to those at high risk, and follows attendees for lung cancer outcomes.
location quote: Furthermore, implementation programmes are currently underway in the UK following the success of the UK Lung Cancer Screening (UKLS) trial, which included the Liverpool Health Lung Project, Manchester Lung Health Check, the Lung Screen Uptake Trial, the West London Lung Cancer Screening pilot and the Yorkshire Lung Screening trial.
note: Tier D (D467), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: Manchester Lung Health Check's high-risk attendees form the cancer-free control group (paired with separately-sourced surgical LC cases, tag MCRCB) in a lung-cancer PRS validation study. D467.4's claim that UKLS 'included' Manchester LHC is a loosely worded review sentence (P3); not used to assert a parent, since it's unclear whether it means UKLS itself or the wider post-UKLS implementation programmes. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, country and example are right, and the draft rightly asserted no parent from the review sentence about UKLS. The definition took its age range (55-80) from one later paper and left out the rest. The programme began as the Manchester 'Lung Health Check' pilot of 2016-2017. It was 'a pilot of community-based targeted lung cancer screening for ever-smokers aged 55–74 invited by letter from 14 primary care practices in socioeconomically deprived parts of Manchester, commencing in 2016' (PMID:40046247), with LHCs that were 'nurse-led' and included PLCOm2012 risk, symptom assessment, smoking cessation advice and spirometry, on mobile units (PMID:30420406). It was delivered by the Wythenshawe Hospital lung cancer team of Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust and followed by the North and East Manchester LHC programme from 2019. Attendees, screened or not, were followed for lung cancer for six years. The papers' abbreviation M-LHC is added as an acronym and 'Manchester Lung Health Check cohort' (PMID:40046247 title) as a synonym. The screening programme's attendees are the cohort. The later North and East Manchester LHC (from 2019) is treated as a continuation of the Manchester Lung Health Check, not a separate term, because papers use the one name for both (PMID:35430354 describes 'The Manchester Lung Health Check (LHC) programme' with ages 55-80). Split it if a catalogue tags the phases separately. The acronym LHC is generic (England's Targeted Lung Health Check, Ireland's Lung Health Check pilot), but no other COHO term carries it, so no editor note is needed now. Not part of UKLS; the review sentence (PMID:33046839) lists implementation programmes that followed UKLS.

label: Mayo Vascular Disease Biorepository
other synonyms: Mayo Vascular diseases Biorepository|Mayo Clinic Vascular Disease Biorepository|Vascular Disease Biorepository|Vascular Diseases Biorepository - Mayo Clinic
example title: Genome-wide association meta-analysis identifies risk loci for abdominal aortic aneurysm and highlights PCSK9 as a therapeutic target.
example quote: Mayo VDB: Mayo Vascular Disease Biorepository (VDB) at the Mayo Clinic was established to archive DNA, plasma, and serum from patients with suspected atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) referred for noninvasive vascular evaluation and exercise stress testing at the Mayo Clinic Gonda Vascular Center from January 14, 2006 to July 24, 2020.
definition: An electronic medical record-linked biorepository at Mayo Clinic, begun in 2006, that archives DNA, plasma and serum and a questionnaire from consecutive adult patients with known or suspected atherosclerotic vascular disease (such as carotid artery stenosis, abdominal aortic aneurysm or peripheral arterial disease) referred for non-invasive vascular evaluation or exercise stress testing at the Mayo Clinic Gonda Vascular Center, ascertaining disease and comorbidities with electronic phenotyping algorithms, to discover genetic and circulating biomarkers of atherosclerotic vascular disease.
location quote: All participants were U.S. residents, with 85% from the Upper Midwest.
parent quote: MAYOVDB The Mayo Clinic Vascular Disease Biorepository (MAYOVDB) was initiated in 2006 to archive DNA, plasma, and serum from patients with atherosclerotic vascular disease
note: Tier D (D468), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (GCST90026612): Mayo VDB's case-control subset for a fibromuscular-dysplasia GWAS; P2 (GCST90432152): Mayo VDB as one of 14 discovery cohorts in an abdominal aortic aneurysm meta-analysis. Same cohort as tier-D row D469 ('Vascular Diseases Biorepository - Mayo Clinic', PGS id MAYO-VDB, same GCSTs/tags per triage_D.tsv) — this entry (D468) is first in key order and carries the full record. Country not asserted: no unit ties Mayo Clinic to a country string. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type and example are right, and D468 and D469 are rightly one cohort. The definition read 'established from January 14, 2006 to July 24, 2020', which is the sampling window of one paper (the AAA meta-analysis), not the repository's founding. Its last clause restated how papers used it. The design paper (PMID:24689004, cited by the FMD GWAS for the VDB) supplies the design: 'The Vascular Disease Biorepository at Mayo Clinic was established to archive DNA, plasma, and serum from patients with suspected AVD'; consecutive adult patients referred for vascular ultrasound or lower-extremity arterial evaluation are approached; there is a questionnaire, EMR linkage and electronic phenotyping; the goal is 'facilitating discovery of biomarkers for AVD'. The country was missing, although the design paper states it: 'All participants were U.S. residents, with 85% from the Upper Midwest.' The parent was missing. The PGS id MAYO_VDB reaches the Catalog through the CARDIoGRAMplusC4D 1000 Genomes CAD meta-analysis (source GWAS of PGS004921), whose Supplementary Note cohort descriptions include 'MAYOVDB', the Mayo Clinic Vascular Disease Biorepository (initiated 2006; CHD cases and controls without atherosclerotic vascular disease). So the cohort is memberOf CARDIoGRAMplusC4D (COHO:0000029), and MAYOVDB is added as an acronym. D469 ('Vascular Diseases Biorepository - Mayo Clinic', PGS id MAYO-VDB, the same GWAS tags) should be 'same as D468'. Its PGS name is kept here as a synonym. The acronym VDB is also the PGS id of E1196 (Vejle Diabetes Biobank). If E1196 is minted with it, both terms need IAO:0000116 editor notes. The VDB overlaps with Mayo's eMERGE samples (the AAA paper excluded 'overlapping samples between Mayo VDB Dataset and eMERGE III V3 Imputed Array Dataset'), and Mayo's Phase I eMERGE PAD cohort was recruited from the same vascular laboratory. No isSubCohortOf eMERGE (COHO:0000491) or Mayo Genome Consortia (COHO:0000714) is asserted, because no source says the VDB is part of either. The CARDIoGRAMplusC4D membership rests on the consortium paper's cohort descriptions; the quoted item cannot be joined to the 'Cohort Descriptions' heading in one span. The Gonda Vascular Center's city is not stated in the texts read, so no city is given.

label: Mayo Vascular Disease Biorepository
other synonyms: Vascular Diseases Biorepository - Mayo Clinic
note: Tier D (D469), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. same cohort as review name D468. Same cohort as D468: identical GWAS studies (GCST90026612, GCST90432152) and tags; per D469.11 this is the Mayo Clinic Vascular Diseases Biorepository (VDB). Its own paper (Polderman et al. 2013) describes it as 'a general population sample (sample 1) and a genetically informative, family-based sample (sample 2)' whose aim is 'to study individual differences in cognition and cognitive-related disorders', with sample 1 recruited through media advertisements and the NEMO Science Center's Science Live programme in Amsterdam. input name: UK Nephropathy Family Study and Oxford Regional Prospective Study

The Nephropathy Family Study recruited adolescents aged 10–16 years with type 1 diabetes, and their parents, in four English regions in 2000–2005. note: Tier D (D481), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because the tagged paper never names the collection. Its four discovery studies include 'the UK Nephropathy Family Study and Oxford Regional Prospective Study (NFS-ORPS/Cambridge)', also called 'the NFS-ORPS study' and, in Table 1, 'Cambridge'. The draft's example GCST90013791 has no quotable text (neither the paper, its supplement nor its bioRxiv preprint names NFS or ORPS). It is replaced by GCST003864, the SUMMIT 'combined DKD' GWAS (GWAS Catalog sample 2,563 cases and 2,593 controls, matching Table 1's four-study totals of 2,563 and 2,595, which include Cambridge's 197 cases and 199 controls), whose free PMC text names the collection. Members, for hasCohort links from this term (quote: the example sentence above): the Oxford Regional Prospective Study is D560 ('Oxford Regional Prospective Study of Childhood Diabetes (ORPS)', batch d52, drafted as a new cohort), and the Nephropathy Family Study is given under extra. definition: A case-control study of breast cancer in women aged 18 or older, begun in 1998 in Ibadan, Nigeria. Women with invasive breast cancer are recruited at University College Hospital, Ibadan (from 2014 also at Lagos State University Teaching Hospital). Root consortium (D482.1) has no candidate COHO term or tier-D row here, so parent is left null. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type and acronyms are right. The definition had only the recruitment place and years plus the Root membership, which belongs in the parent link. It left out the design: cases at University College Hospital, Ibadan (and from 2014 Lagos State University Teaching Hospital), controls from outpatient clinics and randomly selected communities, and the 2011 extension to Cameroon and Uganda. The drafter wrongly said the tagged paper has no retrieved text naming the cohort. Its own evidence D482.1 comes from that paper's free full text (PMC9011920, P1), which lists the Nigerian Breast Cancer Study among Root's six studies, so the example has a quote. The parent is not missing: Root is review key D056, checked as a new aggregation whose members include this study. Countries: the study's 2025 paper says enrolment was extended to Cameroon and Uganda in 2011 'using the same questionnaire and protocol', so those countries are added. label: National Joint Registry

example title: Genetic study identifies novel genes in developmental dysplasia of the hip.
example quote: The DDH samples were identified from the National Joint Registry cohort, which at the time included 5 411 adult individuals living in England who had undergone a hip replacement surgery for DDH.
definition: A national registry of joint replacement surgery, set up by the Department of Health and the Welsh Government, that has recorded hip and knee replacements since April 2003 (ankle, elbow and shoulder replacements since 2010–2012) in NHS and independent hospitals in England and Wales, joined by Northern Ireland in 2013, the Isle of Man in 2015, Guernsey in 2019 and Jersey in 2025. Each procedure is recorded with the implant used and, with the patient's consent, the patient's details, to monitor the outcomes of implants, hospitals and surgeons.
location quote: NJR descriptive: The National Joint Registry for England, Wales, Northern Ireland, and the Isle of Man (NJR, http://www.njrcentre.org.uk/)
note: Tier D (D483), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the National Joint Registry, from which surgically confirmed developmental-dysplasia-of-the-hip cases were identified for this GWAS. Coverage grew over time: England and Wales only at the 2003 launch (D483.12), later Northern Ireland and the Isle of Man (D483.4, the GWAS paper's own supplement). Country given as United_Kingdom; the Isle of Man is not in the gazetteer. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronym, country and example are right. The definition gave the registry's regions as if fixed. It presented linkage to Hospital Episode Statistics, which individual studies do, as a feature of the registry, and ended by restating the one GWAS ('to identify surgically confirmed cases for genetic studies such as developmental dysplasia of the hip'). It left out what the registry records (hip, knee, ankle, elbow and shoulder replacements, with implant details), who set it up, when each region joined (Northern Ireland 2013, Isle of Man 2015, Guernsey 2019, Jersey 2025) and its purpose (monitoring implants, hospitals and surgeons). Synonyms: the leading 'The' of the second synonym is dropped, and the later official long name (with the States of Guernsey) is added, as used in PMID:37848303. The genotyped sample under this tag is a subset: NJR patients whose recorded indication for hip replacement was hip dysplasia (5,411 at the time) were invited by post, and those with self-confirmed UK European ancestry and idiopathic childhood DDH gave saliva for DNA (NRES 12/YH/0390). PMID:30273415 (Hatzikotoulas et al. 2018) used the same cases, so its GWAS Catalog studies could also carry NJR if the curator wants another example. The Isle of Man and the Channel Islands are Crown Dependencies with no gazetteer entry, so United_Kingdom stands for the registry's area. Tier D (D484), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. In the only tagged study (GCST90840647, PMID:39107874) NKI is the Netherlands Cancer Institute's share of the cases: patients with high sunitinib exposure 'identified during routine therapeutic drug monitoring in standard patient care in the Radboud University Medical Centre (Radboudumc, Nijmegen, the Netherlands) and The Netherlands Cancer Institute (Amsterdam, the Netherlands) between December 2013 and December 2019'. label: National Psoriasis Victor Henschel BioBank

example title: Multi-ancestry genome-wide meta-analysis with 472,819 individuals identifies 32 novel risk loci for psoriasis.
example quote: For the PsA GWAS, 1,526 PsA case subjects and 1,508 unaffected control subjects North American (American and Canadian population) were recruited by four collection centers—Michigan, Toronto, Newfoundland, and the National Psoriasis Foundation.
definition: A biobank of biological samples, including DNA, and clinical information from volunteers in the United States with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis and from unaffected controls. The National Psoriasis Foundation created it in 2006, with the financial backing of the Henschel family, to advance genetic research on psoriatic disease. Its samples were made available to researchers internationally for case-control and family studies until the biobank was retired in 2025.
location quote: We thank the National Psoriasis Foundation for provision of US replication samples.
note: Tier D (D485), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft took NPF only as the patient-advocacy organisation, with the Foundation merely one of four channels that recruited the pooled psoriatic arthritis (PsA) GWAS sample. But the Foundation supplied that sample from its own named, defined collection, the National Psoriasis Victor Henschel BioBank. The PsA GWAS paper (Stuart et al. 2015) lists the Foundation as a collection centre and thanks the Henschel Charitable Foundation 'for their support of the National Psoriasis Victor Henschel Biobank'. Other psoriasis GWAS thank the Foundation 'for provision of US replication samples' and acknowledge the same biobank. The Foundation's own page gives the design: created in 2006, biological samples with clinical information from patient volunteers, shared internationally, retired in 2025. So the tag denotes a biobank that deserves a term. The PsA GWAS pools the four centres (Michigan, Toronto, Newfoundland, NPF), so the tag covers only the NPF share of that pooled sample. The Foundation ran an earlier 'National Psoriasis Tissue Bank' (described in 1995; its family samples appear as the 'National Psoriasis Foundation Tissue Bank' in PMID:16642438). The Foundation's page says the Victor Henschel Biobank was created in 2006, so the older name is not added as a synonym. The curator may treat them as one resource. The PGS Catalog name 'National Psoriasis Foundation' names the organisation and is left out of the synonyms, although papers use it as a cohort label. If the curator prefers not to map the organisation's tag to its biobank, the fallback is the draft's 'not a cohort'. Not related to CASP (D204), GAPC (D425) or PAGE (COHO:0000145); the University of Michigan, Toronto and Newfoundland collections of the same PsA GWAS have no tags of their own on GCST90565134.

definition: A population-based prospective cohort of Han Chinese adults, a sub-project of China's National Science & Technology Basic Research Project, recruited as volunteers in four sub-cohorts in Taizhou (Jiangsu province; 2015 and 2019), Zhengzhou (Henan province; 2017) and Nanning (Guangxi province; 2018). P1 (hair whorl direction GWAS, GCST90671959): no text was retrieved; P2-P4 consistently use NSPT for this Chinese physical-traits cohort, presumably the same one P1 means. No unit was retrieved from P1 itself (the tagged GWAS paper); identity and definition rest entirely on three other papers (P2-P4) that reuse the same cohort name. Example ev is null accordingly. The definition restated the name ('surveyed for physical traits') and listed three papers' uses (hypertension, diabetes, solar lentigines). It gave no design: a population-based prospective cohort of Han Chinese adult volunteers, a sub-project of the National Science & Technology Basic Research Project, recruited as four sub-cohorts in Taizhou (2015, 2019), Zhengzhou (2017) and Nanning (2018), with facial, ear and fingerprint phenotyping and blood for genotyping and multi-omics. input name: The New York Genome Center's ALS Consortium

definition: A consortium formed in 2015 around the New York Genome Center, through which 41 ALS clinics and research institutions in the United States, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Greece and Israel contribute blood and post-mortem brain and spinal cord tissue from people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, other neurological diseases and non-neurological controls. note: Tier D (D487), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred on structure and countries. The consortium's 2026 resource paper (medRxiv, free full text) settles both. It was 'formed in 2015', bringing together 41 institutions. 'Blood and autopsy tissue samples were obtained from 41 ALS clinics and research institutions spanning the USA, the UK, the Netherlands, Greece, and Israel'. All samples were sequenced at the NYGC and each site's clinical data harmonised there. The paper calls the result 'the NYGC ALS Consortium cohort'. The contributors are clinics and institutions, not separately named cohorts, so it is typed as a cohort. The NYGC ALS Consortium differs: its 41 contributors send samples from their clinics and brain banks for central sequencing and harmonisation, with no member studies of their own, and its own paper calls it a cohort (as the review did for GELCC, D024). The curator may still prefer to type the two consortia alike. The resource covers WGS of about 4,700 donors and multi-region post-mortem RNA-seq of about 700; the ALS exome/WGS GWAS uses the ALS cases and controls. 'NYGC' alone, as in the supplement's PCA legends, names the New York Genome Center itself and is not added as an acronym.
