example title: Genome-wide association meta-analysis identifies risk loci for abdominal aortic aneurysm and highlights PCSK9 as a therapeutic target.
example quote: These 14 discovery cohorts are as follows: (1) Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC); (2) Copenhagen Hospital Biobank—Cardiovascular Disease Cohort and Danish Blood Donor Study (CHB-CVDC+DBDS); (3) Cardiovascular Health Improvement Project and Michigan Genomics Initiative (CHIP + MGI); (4) deCODE; (5) DiscovEHR; (6) Electronic Medical Records and Genomics (eMERGE); (7) Trøndelag Health study (HUNT), (8) Mayo Vascular Disease Biorepository (Mayo VDB); (9) MVP; (10) NZ AAA Genetics Study; (11) Penn Medicine biobank (PMBB); (12) Triple A Barcelona Study (TABS); (13) UKAGS and Viborg Vascular (UKAGS+VIVA); (14) UKBB (Supplementary Fig. 16).
definition: A case-control study of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) in New Zealand. The Vascular Research Consortium of New Zealand recruited men and women with AAA (infrarenal aortic diameter of at least 30 mm on ultrasound or CT scan, about 80% after surgical repair), nearly all of Anglo-European ancestry, and elderly Anglo-European controls in whom AAA was excluded by abdominal ultrasound and who were also screened for peripheral and carotid artery disease. Its participants were genotyped in two genome-wide case-control sets for genetic studies of AAA.
location quote: NZ AAA Genetics Study: The Vascular Research Consortium of New Zealand recruited New Zealand men and women with a proven history of AAA (infra-renal aortic diameter ≥ 30 mm proven on ultrasound or CT scan).
note: Tier D (D488), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the NZ AAA Genetics Study, one of 14 named discovery cohorts in this abdominal aortic aneurysm GWAS meta-analysis. Definition and country both from the GWAS paper's own open-access supplement (D488.10). triage_E lists a PGS-only row 'NZ-VAS' (New Zealand Vascular Genetic Study AAA GWAS dataset, E833) that may be the same cohort under a different PGS Catalog entry; worth checking. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, country and example are right. The definition described only the cases, leaving out the ultrasound-screened controls, so it read as a case series. It is a case-control study with two genotyped case-control sets. It also ended by restating its use in the GWAS meta-analysis. The draft's suspicion about tier-E row E833 is borne out. The AAA GWAS meta-analysis of Jones et al. 2017 (PMID:27899403, the source of COHO:0000167) calls the same collection the 'New Zealand (NZ) Vascular Genetics Study AAA GWAS dataset'. Its supplement describes it in the same words as the 2023 paper's 'NZ AAA Genetics Study' section, with the same two sets (608 cases and 612 controls on Affymetrix SNP6; 397 and 384 on Illumina Omni2.5). So the PGS Catalog id NZ-VAS ('New Zealand Vascular Genetic Study AAA GWAS dataset') is this cohort and joins the acronyms, with the long names as synonyms. E833 (NZ-VAS, PGS only) should become 'same as D488'. Two alternative labels would also be defensible: the review kept the PGS dataset name 'The Netherlands AAA GWAS dataset' for COHO:0000167 from the same 2017 paper, and the Otago group's 2017 supplement uses 'New Zealand (NZ) Vascular Genetics Study'. The draft's label is kept because the tagged paper and the PGS Catalog use it. The recruiting group is the Vascular Research Consortium of New Zealand. The 2017 paper's corresponding author and its New Zealand validation genotyping were at the University of Otago, Dunedin, and 'The New Zealand project' was funded by the Health Research Council of New Zealand. Not the same as E019 (Aneurysm Consortium AAA GWAS dataset: UK and Western Australian cases with WTCCC2 controls) or E832 (NZ-CAD, 'The New Zealand CAD Study', by its name a coronary artery disease study).

label: Pancreatic Cancer Case-Control Consortium

example title: Genome-Wide Analysis to Assess if Heavy Alcohol Consumption Modifies the Association between SNPs and Pancreatic Cancer Risk.
example quote: Data from study participants in three previously conducted genome-wide association studies of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in European ancestry populations, the PanScan I-II studies, and the PanC4 study (Figure 1) were used in these analyses.
definition: An international consortium that pools data from case-control studies of pancreatic cancer, conducted in North America, Europe, China and Australia, to study risk factors such as tobacco and alcohol use, diabetes and pancreatitis; cases and controls from several member studies were also genotyped together for a genome-wide association study of pancreatic cancer.

P1: PanC4 as the case-control GWAS pooled with PanScan I-II for a heavy-alcohol interaction analysis; P2-P4: PanC4 pooling case-control studies for smoking/alcohol/tobacco analyses; P5-P7: PanC4 alongside PanScan in Mendelian-randomisation analyses of pancreatic cancer. The label took the minority form: the consortium calls itself the Pancreatic Cancer Case-Control Consortium (its website panc4.org is cited under that name; dbGaP phs000648, the consortium's own GWAS paper and later PanC4 papers use it; 127 Europe PMC hits against 32 for the 'International' form used by the 2011-2017 Annals of Oncology pooled analyses), so 'International ...' becomes a synonym. The definition described the consortium through one paper (PanC4 'alongside the PanScan studies') and gave no scope; rewritten from McWilliams 2016 ('an international group of researchers organized to pool data from individual case-control studies of pancreatic cancer'), the pooled analyses (member studies in North America, Europe, China, and the IARC SEARCH study in Canada, Europe and Australia) and the PanC4 GWAS (8052 subjects from nine member studies genotyped at CIDR). input name: Primary Open-Angle African American Glaucoma Genetics Study
label: Primary Open-Angle African American Glaucoma Genetics Study

example title: A multi-cohort genome-wide association study in African ancestry individuals reveals risk loci for primary open-angle glaucoma.
example quote: In brief, the POAAGG study population consists of self-identified Blacks (African American, African descent, or African Caribbean), aged 35 years or older, recruited from the Philadelphia area.
definition: A case-control genetic study of primary open-angle glaucoma led by the University of Pennsylvania's Scheie Eye Institute, which since July 2010 has enrolled self-identified Black adults (African American, African descent or African Caribbean) aged 35 or over from the Philadelphia region, mainly from University of Pennsylvania eye clinics and also through community screenings, two other Philadelphia ophthalmology practices and the Penn Medicine Biobank, with glaucoma specialists classifying them as cases, controls or glaucoma suspects, to identify genetic and clinical risk factors for the disease.
location quote: Participants were recruited from ophthalmology clinics in Philadelphia between July 2010 and August 2024.
note: Tier D (D494), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: POAAGG as one of three African-ancestry discovery cohorts (with ADAGES, GGLAD) in a multi-cohort primary open-angle glaucoma GWAS, replicated partly in Penn Medicine BioBank, All of Us and MVP; P2-P7: POAAGG's own baseline, recruitment and clinical papers. ADAGES, GGLAD, Penn Medicine BioBank, MVP, All of Us, TOPMed and eMERGE candidates are separate cohorts combined or replicated in the same paper, not POAAGG itself. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronym, country, example and the absence of a parent are right, and the PGS Catalog id (PGS000764 evaluated in PMID:33605984) is the same study. The definition was close but described recruitment as clinics only; the study's recruitment paper says enrolment began in July 2010 at three University of Pennsylvania sites (Scheie Eye Institute, Perelman Center, Mercy Fitzgerald Hospital) and from 2014-2015 added community outreach and in-house screenings, two external Philadelphia sites (a West Philadelphia practice and Temple University's ophthalmology department) and DNA from the Penn Medicine Biobank, with glaucoma specialists classifying participants as cases, controls or suspects (suspects are followed longitudinally). Rewritten. Of the synonyms, 'Primary Open-Angle African American Glaucoma Genetics (POAAGG) study' is the label with its acronym inserted, not a name, and 'the primary open-angle ...' carried the article; replaced by the case variants the papers use. The Penn Medicine BioBank (COHO:0000457) supplied DNA samples (mostly controls) to POAAGG and is a separate replication cohort in the GWAS; this is a sample source, not a parent. ADAGES (D355) and GGLAD (D339) are sibling datasets in the same GWAS.

label: Project MinE

example quote: Case cohorts included the Project MinE ALS sequencing consortium (7,614 cases; 2,605 controls)47, the NYGC ALS Consortium (2,650 cases; 342 controls), the ALS Sequencing Consortium (2,851 cases)5, two cohorts from the FALS consortium (1,277 cases; phs001585), the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Exome Sequencing of FALS Project (194 cases; phs000101), two Australian cohorts described in ref. 48 (125 cases, 18 controls) and ref. 49 (568 cases), and a Chinese motor neurone disease (MND) cohort50 (583 cases, 182 controls).
definition: An international collaboration of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis research groups from about 16 countries, coordinated from the ALS Centre Netherlands at University Medical Center Utrecht and begun with a pilot in Dutch patients, in which people with ALS and matched controls are recruited through the groups' ALS clinics under a common protocol with a standardised core clinical data set and their whole genomes sequenced, to identify and fine-map genetic risk loci for ALS and share the data with researchers.
location quote: Samples were from the international Project MinE whole genome sequencing consortium and derived from seven countries: the USA, Ireland, Belgium, the Netherlands, Spain, Turkey, and the United Kingdom (van Rheenen et al., 2018).
note: Tier D (D495), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: Project_MinE_ALS as one of several 'case cohorts' (with NYGC ALS Consortium, ALS Sequencing Consortium, FALS consortium, a Chinese MND cohort, etc.) contributing exome data to a rare-variant ALS meta-analysis; P2 (cited for the cohort): the consortium's own design/pilot paper. Only the Netherlands pilot is confirmed by a quotable unit; the consortium's later international scope is stated (D495.37) but no other member country is named. TOPMed, UK Biobank and Netherlands-AAA candidates are unrelated false matches. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type (a consortium of national research groups pooling their case-control collections), acronym and example are right. The label took the PGS Catalog's lower-case rendering of the consortium's author name; the collaboration's own name is Project MinE (its website and design paper), with 'Project MinE ALS Sequencing Consortium' as the name it publishes under, so the label becomes 'Project MinE' and the consortium forms are synonyms. The definition was right in outline but omitted its structure: ALS research groups from 16 countries in a 'franchise' design, each ascertaining patients and controls through affiliated clinics under a shared protocol and core clinical data set, with central sequencing and storage, coordinated from UMC Utrecht; the Dutch pilot drew on the PAN registry. Countries: only the Netherlands (pilot) was given; papers using the data freezes state that the sequenced samples come from the USA, Ireland, Belgium, the Netherlands, Spain, Turkey and the United Kingdom. The design paper says 16 countries take part, and consortium affiliations include Australia, Canada, Israel, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, France and Italy, but no open text states that samples were recruited there, so only the seven quoted countries are listed. E800 (tier E, 'Project Mine (Netherlands NL4 controls)') is a subset of Project MinE's Dutch controls; if minted it would be a member. The NYGC ALS Consortium (D487) and the Australian and Chinese cohorts of the same GWAS paper are separate. COHO:0000506 ALS Utrecht is an ENIGMA MRI sample from UMC Utrecht, not linked to Project MinE by any evidence read.

example title: Integrative genomic analyses identify candidate causal genes for calcific aortic valve stenosis involving tissue-specific regulation.
example quote: The QUEBEC-CAVS study was approved by the ethics committee of the Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Québec-Université Laval.
definition: A case-control study of calcific aortic valve stenosis at the Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Québec – Université Laval, Canada, in which blood and aortic valve tissue are collected from patients undergoing aortic valve replacement for the disease and compared with controls (in its first phase, patients without valve disease undergoing cardiac surgery, mostly coronary artery bypass, at the same institute; in its second, CARTaGENE participants without valvular heart disease), to identify genetic susceptibility to the disease; its valve tissues, collected in 1998–2019, are also used for gene expression studies.
location quote: Aortic valve tissues were collected from patients undergoing cardiac surgery at the Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Québec – Université Laval between 1998 and 2019 (QUEBEC-CAVS-RNA).
note: Tier D (D499), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: QUEBEC-CAVS as the umbrella name for the Quebec case-control CAVS cohorts (QUEBEC-CAVS-1, QUEBEC-CAVS-2) and RNA dataset, one of six cohorts (with EPIC-Norfolk, EstBB, UK Biobank, FinnGen) in a CAVS GWAS; P2: QUEBEC-CAVS as the whole study, with 3 French cohorts, UK Biobank, EPIC-Norfolk, GERA. QUEBEC-CAVS-2's controls are drawn from the existing CARTaGENE cohort (COHO:0000031); a control-source relation, not membership, so no parent is set. Phases 1/2/RNA are treated as one institutional cohort, not an aggregation. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, acronym, country, example and the absence of a parent are right. The label was the catalogues' name, which the study's papers never use; the study team's own expansion of QUEBEC-CAVS is 'Genome-Wide Association Study on Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis in Quebec' (PMID:31141105), so that becomes the label and the catalogue name a synonym. The definition said the study recruits 'patients undergoing aortic valve replacement or other cardiac surgery', which is true of phase 1 only: phase 1 cases underwent valve replacement for severe tricuspid, non-rheumatic stenosis and its matched controls underwent cardiac surgery (over 98% for coronary disease), while phase 2 took cases with tricuspid or bicuspid valves and drew controls from the CARTaGENE cohort. Rewritten from the design description of the first GWAS (PMID:29511167) and the cohort notes of PMID:38494474. QUEBEC-CAVS-2's controls come from CARTaGENE (COHO:0000031), a control source rather than a parent, as the draft noted. The phase tags QUEBEC-CAVS-1 and QUEBEC-CAVS-2 name subsets and are not added as acronyms of the whole study.

input name: NHLBI Recipient Epidemiology Donor Evaluation Study
label: REDS-III Brazil Sickle Cell Disease Cohort
other synonyms: REDS-III Brazil SCD Cohort|REDS-III Brazil SCD cohort study|Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study III Brazil Cohort Study|Brazil Sickle Cell Disease Cohort Study|Brazil SCD Cohort Study
example title: Genome-wide association study of early ischaemic stroke risk in Brazilian individuals with sickle cell disease implicates ADAMTS2 and CDK18 and uncovers novel loci.
example quote: This was conducted within the Brazil Sickle Cell Disease Cohort Study as part of the Recipient Epidemiology Donor Evaluation Study III (REDS-III).
definition: A cohort of children and adults with sickle cell disease, randomly sampled from the active patients of six care sites in the Brazilian states of Minas Gerais (Belo Horizonte, Juiz de Fora and Montes Claros), Rio de Janeiro, Pernambuco (Recife) and São Paulo and enrolled in 2013–2015 as the Brazilian component of the NHLBI REDS-III programme, with clinical data, a blood biorepository and genome-wide genotyping, to characterise the clinical and transfusion outcomes of sickle cell disease in Brazil and support genotype–phenotype studies.
location quote: A total of 2795 participants at six Brazilian sites were enrolled between 2013 and 2015.
parent quote: The Brazil SCD Cohort Study is part of the National Institutes of Health, National Heart Lung and Blood Institute (NHLBI) REDS-III program.
note: Tier D (D500), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: REDS-III denotes the Brazil Sickle Cell Disease Cohort Study, the Brazilian arm of the NHLBI REDS-III program, used for a Brazilian ischaemic-stroke-in-SCD GWAS. Tag REDS-III denotes the Brazil-specific SCD cohort within the REDS-III program, not the REDS-III aggregation itself (COHO:0000472, its parent). Walk-PHaSST/PUSH in D500.11 is a different cohort in the same meta-analysis, not this one. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, parent and example are right: the GWAS tag REDS-III on GCST90270269 means the REDS-III Brazil sickle cell disease cohort, the one SCD cohort of the programme, not the REDS-III programme (COHO:0000472) itself. The label was the form one GWAS paper uses once ('Brazil Sickle Cell Disease Cohort Study'); the cohort's own design paper and later papers call it the REDS-III Brazil SCD Cohort, and one title spells it 'REDS-III Brazil Sickle Cell Disease Cohort' (PMID:32172616), which is now the label; the draft's forms are kept as synonyms. The definition said only 'people with sickle cell disease enrolled in Brazil'; the design paper (PMID:30027669) gives the design: patients randomly sampled from the active patient lists of six care sites (Hemominas in Belo Horizonte, Juiz de Fora and Montes Claros; Hemorio, Rio de Janeiro; Hemope, Recife; Instituto da Criança of HCFMUSP, São Paulo), enrolled 2013–2015 with interview, medical-record abstraction, a biorepository and Transfusion Medicine array genotyping, to characterise clinical and transfusion outcomes and support genotype–phenotype studies. The country quote was an ethics-approval sentence; replaced by the abstract's enrolment sentence. Shared acronym: REDS-III is also the acronym of the programme, COHO:0000472 (Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study-III), so both terms need the editor note, e.g. here 'The acronym REDS-III also denotes Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study-III (COHO:0000472); this term is its Brazil sickle cell disease cohort.' COHO:0000472 currently uses this same study (GCST90270269) as its example, from the earlier review; once this cohort is minted the curator may prefer to move that example here and give the programme another example, or keep both. The cohort was also whole-genome sequenced in TOPMed ('After enrolment commenced, REDS-III was selected to participate in the NHLBI-funded Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) study.', PMC8019534), so COHO:0000985 could list it with hasCohort as well. Not the Red Blood Cell-Omics Study (COHO:0000451, US blood donors of the same programme) and not the 'Brazilian Cohort' (COHO:0000019). Later papers also call it 'the REDS-III multicenter cohort study' (PMID:36884065, PMID:41692868).

label: Raine Eye Health Study
other synonyms: Raine eye health study|Western Australian Pregnancy Cohort (Raine) Eye Health Study|Western Australian Pregnancy (Raine) Cohort 20 year follow up Eye Study
example title: Rare variant analyses across multiethnic cohorts identify novel genes for refractive error.
example quote: These 14 cohorts were: Singapore Chinese Eye Study (SCES), Singapore Malay Eye Study (SiMES), Singapore Indian Eye Study (SINDI), Age Related Eye Study (AREDS), Rotterdam Study I (RSI), Erasmus Rucphen Family (ERF), Raine Eye Health Study (REHS) of the Raine Study, Beaver Dam Eye Study (BDES), Estonian Genome Center for the University of Tartu (EGCUT), Finnish Twin Study on Aging (FITSA), Ogliastra, Croatia-Korcula, TwinsUK, and EPIC-Norfolk.
definition: The eye study of the offspring (Generation 2) of the Raine Study pregnancy cohort in Western Australia, in which participants completed a comprehensive eye assessment at the cohort's 20-year follow-up, including visual acuity, orthoptic assessment, cycloplegic autorefraction, ocular biometry and anterior and posterior segment photography, to determine the prevalence of and risk factors for eye disease in young adults and characterise their ocular biometric parameters.
location quote: Subject groups were participants in (1) the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC; UK; age 15 years; N = 4401), (2) the Singapore Cohort Study of Risk Factors for Myopia (SCORM; Singapore; age 13 years; N = 1959), (3) the Raine Eye Health Study (REHS; Australia; age 20 years; N = 1344), and (4) Israeli Defense Force Pre-recruitment Candidates (IDFC; Israel; age 16-22 years; N = 888,277).
parent quote: These 14 cohorts were: Singapore Chinese Eye Study (SCES), Singapore Malay Eye Study (SiMES), Singapore Indian Eye Study (SINDI), Age Related Eye Study (AREDS), Rotterdam Study I (RSI), Erasmus Rucphen Family (ERF), Raine Eye Health Study (REHS) of the Raine Study, Beaver Dam Eye Study (BDES), Estonian Genome Center for the University of Tartu (EGCUT), Finnish Twin Study on Aging (FITSA), Ogliastra, Croatia-Korcula, TwinsUK, and EPIC-Norfolk.
note: Tier D (D501), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: REHS as one of 14 cohorts (with the Singapore Chinese/Malay/Indian Eye Studies, AREDS, RSI, ERF, BDES, EGCUT, FITSA, Ogliastra, Croatia-Korcula, TwinsUK, EPIC-Norfolk) in a multiethnic refractive-error GWAS; P2 is REHS's own design/profile paper. REHS is explicitly 'of the Raine Study' (D501.16), an eye-health wave of the young-adult offspring, not the same as Raine Study itself (COHO:0000538, its parent). P3/P4 corroborate Australia and young-adult age. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, parent, country and example are right: REHS is the Raine Eye Health Study, the eye examination of the Raine Study's offspring at the 20-year follow-up, with its own design paper (PMID:23301674) and funding, and it enters refractive-error and IOP consortia as a cohort of its own. The definition called it a 'wave' of a 'birth cohort in Australia' and left out what was done; rewritten from the design paper's abstract: offspring of the Western Australian Pregnancy Cohort (Raine) Study, comprehensive eye assessment at the 20-year follow-up (acuity, orthoptics, cycloplegic autorefraction, biometry, anterior and posterior segment photography), to find the prevalence of and risk factors for eye disease in young adults. Synonyms added: the lower-case form of the design paper's title, 'Western Australian Pregnancy Cohort (Raine) Eye Health Study' (PMID:25072831), and 'Western Australian Pregnancy (Raine) Cohort 20 year follow up Eye Study', the name the IOP GWAS behind the PGS id's score uses for it. Typed as a cohort that isSubCohortOf the Raine Study (COHO:0000538): its participants are the Raine Generation 2 offspring who had the 20-year eye examination. Examination dates (the design paper's abstract gives only 'a 24-month period' at the 20-year follow-up) were not found in open text, so the definition gives none. Not to be confused with the Raine Study as a whole, which the GWAS Catalog tags RAINE/Raine.

input name: Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study
label: Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study
example title: Associations between age of menarche and genetic variation in women of African descent: genome-wide association study and polygenic score analysis.
example quote: The Root consortium is comprised of six epidemiologic studies of breast cancer in women of African ancestry: the Nigerian Breast Cancer Study (Ibadan, Nigeria); the Barbados National Cancer Study (Barbados); the Southern Community Cohort (southern United States); the Baltimore Breast Cancer Study (Baltimore, United States); the Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study (Detroit and Pennsylvania, United States); and the Chicago Cancer Prone Study (Chicago, United States).
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of breast cancer conducted in the Philadelphia and Detroit metropolitan areas of the United States from 1999 to 2003, whose cases, diagnosed with invasive ductal breast cancer within 18 months of recruitment and over-sampled for diagnosis before age 40, were identified in the University of Pennsylvania Health System and the Karmanos Cancer Institute or recruited through local advertisement, with controls without breast cancer recruited in the same way.
location quote: The Root consortium is comprised of six epidemiologic studies of breast cancer in women of African ancestry: the Nigerian Breast Cancer Study (Ibadan, Nigeria); the Barbados National Cancer Study (Barbados); the Southern Community Cohort (southern United States); the Baltimore Breast Cancer Study (Baltimore, United States); the Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study (Detroit and Pennsylvania, United States); and the Chicago Cancer Prone Study (Chicago, United States).
parent quote: The Root consortium is comprised of six epidemiologic studies of breast cancer in women of African ancestry: the Nigerian Breast Cancer Study (Ibadan, Nigeria); the Barbados National Cancer Study (Barbados); the Southern Community Cohort (southern United States); the Baltimore Breast Cancer Study (Baltimore, United States); the Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study (Detroit and Pennsylvania, United States); and the Chicago Cancer Prone Study (Chicago, United States).
note: Tier D (D502), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: RVGBC as one of six member studies of the Root breast-cancer consortium (with the Nigerian Breast Cancer Study, Barbados National Cancer Study, Southern Community Cohort, Baltimore Breast Cancer Study, Chicago Cancer Prone Study), analysed for age at menarche. Root consortium (naming all six member studies including this one) is not among the candidate COHO terms or this batch's rows, so no parent asserted; a researcher should check if Root consortium exists in COHO under another key. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, country and example are right. The definition gave only the places and the consortium; the study's design is in the supplementary note of the African Ancestry Breast Cancer Genetic consortium paper (PMID:38741014, MOESM1, section 4.3): 'RVGBC is a hospital-based case-control study conducted in Philadelphia and Detroit metropolitan areas from 1999 to 2003', cases identified at the University of Pennsylvania Health System and Karmanos Cancer Institute or by local advertisement, diagnosed within 18 months of recruitment with invasive ductal cancer, women diagnosed under 40 over-sampled, controls recruited the same way; the definition is rewritten from it. The parent was left empty although the ROOT consortium is review row D056 (checked as a new aggregation whose members include RVGBC); it is now memberOf D056 with the tagged paper's sentence. The tagged paper's Table 1 abbreviates the study 'RVGDBCR', added as an acronym. Whether RVGBC also enrolled women of other ancestries (its name suggests a comparison across races) is not stated in the sources read; ROOT and the later consortia used only its women of African ancestry, so the definition makes no claim either way. The AABCG supplement's sentence on the numbers included says 'from BNCS' under the RVGBC heading, an evident slip. No COHO term or other review row duplicates it.

label: Genome-Wide Association Study of Adiposity in Samoans
other synonyms: Samoan Adiposity Study|Genome-wide Association Study of Adiposity in Samoans|Genome Wide Association Study of Adiposity in Samoans|Samoan Genome-Wide Association Study
example title: Whole genome sequencing analysis of body mass index identifies novel African ancestry-specific risk allele.
example quote: NHLBI TOPMed: Samoan Adiposity Study (Samoan)
definition: A population-based cross-sectional study of adults with four Samoan grandparents, recruited from February to July 2010 in 33 villages across all four census regions of the independent nation of Samoa (Apia Urban Area, Northwest Upolu, the rest of Upolu and Savai'i), with anthropometry, fasting blood biomarkers, dietary, physical activity, health and socio-demographic data and genome-wide genotyping, to identify genetic variation that increases susceptibility to obesity and cardiometabolic traits in Samoans.
parent quote: samples from the Samoan Adiposity Study have been included in the Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine program (TOPMed)
note: Tier D (D503), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: Samoan as the Samoan Adiposity Study, one of 15 population groups (with Amish, Taiwanese, Han Chinese, and others) in a multi-population BMI whole-genome-sequencing GWAS via TOPMed. OLaGA (D503.16) is acknowledged separately from the Samoan Adiposity Study; evidence doesn't state whether they're the same, so not merged. country not in the gazetteer: Samoa. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, parent, acronym and example are right: the tag Samoan on GCST90502911 is TOPMed's 'Samoan' study, whole-genome sequences of a subset of the 2010 Samoan adiposity GWAS sample. 'Samoan Adiposity Study' is TOPMed's project name (and the PGS Catalog's); the study itself is registered and described by its investigators as the 'Genome-Wide Association Study of Adiposity in Samoans' (dbGaP phs000914; TOPMed's phs000972 carries the same title, and its design paper calls it the Samoan genome-wide association study), now the label, with the TOPMed name kept as a synonym. The definition restated the name and an acknowledgement (ministry and statistics bureau support) and said nothing about who, when or how; rewritten from the design paper (PMID:24799123): a population-based sample of adults with four Samoan grandparents, recruited February–July 2010 in 33 villages in all four census regions of Samoa, with anthropometry, fasting biomarkers, questionnaires and Affymetrix 6.0 genotyping, to find genetic variants for obesity and cardiometabolic traits. The parent quote now names both the study and TOPMed in one sentence rather than a supplement heading with a page number. The example quote ran the supplement's study heading, a page number ('36') and the next sentence together; it is trimmed to the heading, the only text of the study that names the cohort. No country can be asserted: Samoa is not in gaz_xrefs.tsv (the design paper says 'Our study population is derived from the independent nation of Samoa.', PMC4292846). 'Samoan Obesity, Lifestyle and Genetic Adaptations Study (OLaGA) Group' in the acknowledgements is the investigators' research group, which also ran earlier Samoan family studies and later ones, not another name for this sample, so it is not a synonym. The dbGaP page mentions replication in 'an independent sample of 2,500 Samoans from earlier studies', which is not part of this cohort. No COHO term or other review row duplicates it.

label: Sanford Biobank
other synonyms: Sanford Health|Sanford Health Biobank|Sanford Health BioBank
example title: Time-to-Event Genome-Wide Association Study for Incident Cardiovascular Disease in People With Type 2 Diabetes.
example quote: Stroke Study; ROTTERDAM, Rotterdam Study; SANFORD, Sanford Health; UKBB, UK Biobank;
definition: A hospital-based biobank of adult patients of Sanford Health, a rural health system of the Upper Midwest of the United States based in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, who since 2011 have elected to provide specimens for research, genotyped on the Illumina Global Screening Array and linked to the health system's clinical records for genetic studies such as of cardiovascular disease.
location quote: Sanford Health is the largest rural non-profit health system in the United States, serving more than 2 million patients through 46 medical centers, more than 200 clinics and 2,500 providers.
note: Tier D (D504), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: SANFORD is not just an author affiliation: the paper's main text says 'we studied 49,230 participants with T2D from 16 cohorts', and its supplementary methods (figshare 10.2337/figshare.25444327) list Sanford Health (short name SANFORD) as one of the 16, a 'Hospital based cohort (Biobank)' of 'Patients of Sanford Health System' in the 'Upper Midwest, USA', European ancestry, genotyped on GSA Version 1 and imputed to TOPMed, with type 2 diabetes from hospital records and adjudicated cardiovascular events. The PGS Catalog's sample set for this paper (PSS012312) lists SANFORD 'Sanford Health' among its cohorts too. The drafter saw only the affiliation lines. The sample is Sanford Health's research biobank, which Sanford's genomics investigators describe as 'participants aged ≥18 years from the Sanford Health system who elected to provide a specimen to the Sanford Biobank for research purposes, starting in 2011' (PMID:41669951); a full record is given. Label: the GWAS and PGS Catalogs and the papers call the cohort 'Sanford Health', the health system's name; the tagged paper describes the sample as its biobank, whose own name is the Sanford Biobank (also written 'Sanford Health Biobank'/'Sanford Health BioBank' in other papers), so that is proposed as the label with 'Sanford Health' kept as a synonym. Caveat for the curator: Sanford's own CAD risk-score papers pool the biobank with patients genotyped clinically through the Imagenetics 'Sanford Chip' programme (from 2018) and call the pooled set 'the Sanford Health cohort' ('The Sanford Health population is a cohort of 26 291 European‐origin patients from the Sanford Biobank and the Imagenetics program', PMC13055487); the diabetes paper does not say whether its Sanford sample includes Sanford Chip patients. If the curator prefers the catalogs' name, 'Sanford Health' could be the label instead. The example quote is a table footnote of the supplement, the only text of the study that names the cohort. No COHO term or other review row covers Sanford.

input name: Social Changes, Asthma, and Allergy in Latin America cohort
label: Salvador-SCAALA study
other synonyms: Social Changes, Asthma, and Allergy in Latin America cohort|SCAALA cohort|Salvador-SCAALA|SCAALA-Salvador|Salvador-SCAALA project
example title: Genome-wide association study of Helicobacter pylori serological status in Latin American children.
example quote: The discovery study was based on the SCAALA (Social Changes, Asthma, and Allergy in Latin America) cohort, including 1161 of a total of 1445 children who comprised the original cohort
definition: A cohort of children from 24 low-income areas of Salvador, Bahia, in north-eastern Brazil, first enrolled aged 0–3 years in 1997, 2001 and 2003 to evaluate the health effects of the city's sanitation programme and followed from 2005, at ages 4–11, with further surveys (questionnaires, anthropometry, stool, blood and house-dust samples, skin prick tests and, later, genome-wide genotyping), to study social, environmental, infectious, immunological and genetic risk factors for asthma and allergic diseases; it is the Brazilian study of the Social Changes, Asthma and Allergy in Latin America (SCAALA) programme.
location quote: The Salvador-SCAALA project described here is a longitudinal study involving children aged 4–11 years living in the city of Salvador, Northeastern Brazil.
parent quote: The SCAALA composes the EPIGEN-Brazil initiative, it is based on three well-defined ongoing population-based cohorts from Brazil’s regions
note: Tier D (D505), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred for want of text; research settles it. The tagged paper (Wiley, closed, but a green open-access copy is in the Fiocruz ARCA repository) says 'The discovery study was based on the SCAALA (Social Changes, Asthma, and Allergy in Latin America) cohort, including 1161 of a total of 1445 children who comprised the original cohort, aged 4–11 years and living in outlying areas in Salvador's city, Bahia, Brazil', with data and samples collected in 2005 and genotypes in EGA (EGAS00001001245, EPIGEN's study). So the tag means the Salvador cohort of the SCAALA programme. Its design paper (PMID:16796729) describes it: children of three cohorts recruited at ages 0–3 in 1997, 2001 and 2003 from 24 'sentinel areas' of Salvador without sanitation to evaluate the Bahia Azul sanitation programme, resurveyed in 2005 at 4–11 years and again in 2008 (later also 2013), with questionnaires, stool, blood and dust samples and skin prick tests, to study risk factors and immunological pathways for asthma and allergy. The drafter's example had no quote; it now has one from the repository copy. SCAALA is also the name of the Wellcome Trust-funded research programme ('Social Changes, Asthma and Allergy in Latin America Programme') whose other study is the cross-sectional Esmeraldas-SCAALA study of Afro-Ecuadorian schoolchildren (PMID:16970809); the GWAS tag means only the Salvador cohort, so the label names Salvador and the programme is not proposed as a term. Member of EPIGEN-Brazil (COHO:0000062) with the Bambuí cohort (D369) and the 1982 Pelotas cohort (COHO:0000739). The same Salvador genotypes are EPIGEN's EGA study EGAS00001001245, already COHO:0000062's EGA example. No COHO term or other review row duplicates it.

label: San Francisco City Clinic Cohort
other synonyms: San Francisco City Clinic Cohort Study|San Francisco City Clinic cohort
example title: Africa-specific human genetic variation near CHD1L associates with HIV-1 load.
example quote: The San Francisco City Clinic Cohort (SFCCC) consists of approximately 6700 homosexual men recruited between 1978 and 1980 from a clinic for sexually transmitted diseases.
definition: A cohort of homosexual and bisexual men recruited in 1978–1980 at the San Francisco municipal sexually transmitted disease clinic for studies of sexually transmitted hepatitis B, whose stored serum specimens, follow-up examinations and questionnaires, and linkage to AIDS surveillance and death registries were later used to study the natural history, transmission and cofactors of HIV infection and AIDS.
location quote: We use data from the San Francisco City Clinic Cohort Study (SFCCC), documenting the onset of HIV in San Francisco (1978-1984).
note: Tier D (D507), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: SFCCC as a contributing cohort (with ALIVE, HGDS, IHIVCS, MACS, MHCS, SHCS) in an African-ancestry HIV-1 viral-load GWAS meta-analysis. Triage's 'institution?' hint is wrong: D507.1 defines SFCCC as a defined 1978-1980 recruitment cohort from an STD clinic, not an institution. The 'Study' suffix varies across papers and is kept as a synonym. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, country, acronym and example study are right. The definition left out what the cohort was and why it was assembled: the men were homosexual and bisexual men recruited at the city's municipal STD clinic 'for studies of sexually transmitted hepatitis B' (PMID:2261554), and the HIV work came later, from their stored sera, re-examinations and linkage to the national AIDS registry and the National Death Index (PMID:1546772); rewritten. The example quote ran a section heading and a page number into the sentence; trimmed to the sentence. 'San Francisco City Clinic cohort' (the lower-case form in two titles and abstracts) added as a synonym. No parent: the CHD1L paper pooled it with other HIV cohorts through the International Collaboration for the Genomics of HIV, which is not a COHO term or a review row. The triage hint 'institution?' is wrong. Not the San Francisco Men's Health Study, a separate population-based cohort that some SFCCC papers analyse alongside it.

label: Sea Islands Genetics Network – Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke
same as: Sea Islands Genetics Network – Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke
note: Tier D (D508), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. same cohort as review name D179. Checked 2026-09-23: The identity is right, as the draft's own note suspected: the tag SIGNET on GCST90104550 (GIGASTROKE) and the PGS id SIGNET both mean SIGNET-REGARDS, the African American REGARDS participants genotyped by the Sea Islands Genetics Network, which is review row D179 (GWAS tag SIGNET-REGARDS, checked in d17 as a new cohort that isSubCohortOf REGARDS, COHO:0000692, already carrying SIGNET as an acronym). D179 comes first and carries the record, so this row is 'same as D179'. Against D179's record the draft's label is the short form (D179 uses the full name 'Sea Islands Genetics Network – Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke'), and its definition missed the second selection group, all other REGARDS participants living in the 15-county Low Country of South Carolina and Georgia. The PGS Catalog name 'Sea Islands Genetics Network' is the funding network's name, not a name of this sample, so it is not proposed as a synonym of D179. A term for the whole network is not needed for these tags; its other member Project SuGAR is review row E930 (PGS id Project_SuGAR).

input name: Silent Cerebral Infarct Multi-Center Clinical Trial
label: Silent Cerebral Infarct Multi-Center Clinical Trial
other synonyms: Silent Infarct Transfusion trial|Silent Cerebral Infarct Transfusion Trial
example title: FLT1 and other candidate fetal haemoglobin modifying loci in sickle cell disease in African ancestries.
example quote: The cohorts included: Cooperative Study of Sickle Cell Disease (CSSCD: n = 841), Multicenter Study of Hydroxyurea (MSH: n = 178), Pulmonary Hypertension and the Hypoxic Response in Sickle Cell Disease (PUSH) study (n = 73), Comprehensive Sickle Cell Centers Collaborative Data (C-data) project (n = 127), Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Treatment (Walk-PHaSST) trial (n = 181), Duke University Outcome Modifying Genes study (n = 152), and Silent Infarct Transfusion (SIT) trial (SITT: n = 488).
definition: A multicentre, single-blind randomised clinical trial at 29 centres in the United States, Canada, France and the United Kingdom, which from December 2004 to May 2010 screened children aged 5 to 15 years with sickle cell anaemia (haemoglobin SS or Sβ0 thalassaemia) and no history of stroke by brain MRI, and randomly assigned those with silent cerebral infarcts to regular blood transfusions or standard care, to test whether transfusion therapy reduces the recurrence of cerebral infarcts.
location quote: In the multicenter, single-blind clinical trial for children with sickle cell anemia, each participant was randomly allocated to receive regular blood transfusion therapy (transfusion group) or standard care (observation group) in 29 centers in the United States, Canada, France, and the United Kingdom.
note: Tier D (D509), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: SIT as the Silent Infarct Transfusion (SIT) trial (SITT), one of seven sickle-cell cohorts (with CSSCD, MSH_CSA, PUSH, C-data, Walk-PHaSST, and Duke's Outcome Modifying Genes study) meta-analysed for fetal-haemoglobin loci; P2-P4 use the fuller name matching the PGS Catalog. Two name variants for one trial: P1 calls it 'Silent Infarct Transfusion (SIT) trial (SITT)'; P2-P4 and PGS Catalog call it 'Silent Cerebral Infarct Multi-Center Clinical Trial (SIT Trial)' (also NCT00072761, D509.18). Triage's 'institution?' hint is wrong. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronyms and example are right: the tag SIT (and the paper's 'SITT') is the Silent Cerebral Infarct Transfusion (SIT) trial, NCT00072761, registered as the 'Silent Cerebral Infarct Multi-Center Clinical Trial'. The definition described only the two arms of the randomisation (and the transfusion targets, a treatment detail); it left out the screening cohort, the ages, the sites and the dates, which the trial's main report gives (PMID:25140956: 29 clinical centres in the United States, Canada, France and the United Kingdom, recruitment December 2004 to May 2010, children aged 5-15 with HbSS or HbSβ0 thalassaemia screened by MRI, those with silent infarcts randomised to transfusion or observation, primary aim to reduce stroke and new or worsening silent infarcts); rewritten. No countries were given although open-access text names all four; added. 'Silent Cerebral Infarct Transfusion Trial', the expansion the tagged paper and later trial papers use, added as a synonym. The tagged paper's SITT sample (n = 488) is larger than the 196 randomised participants (PMC9153054), so it includes screened children who were not randomised; the definition therefore covers the screening cohort as well as the randomised trial. The triage hint 'institution?' is wrong. No parent; no COHO term or other review row duplicates it (the other sickle cell cohorts of the same meta-analysis are CSSCD D397, MSH COHO:0000987, PUSH D496, C-data D386, Walk-PHaSST COHO:0000805 and OMG-SCD COHO:0000839).

input name: Swiss Kidney Project on Genes in Hypertension
label: Swiss Kidney Project on Genes in Hypertension
other synonyms: Swiss Kidney Project On Genes in Hypertension
example title: Genetic determinants of zinc homeostasis and its role in cardiometabolic diseases.
example quote: The SKIPOGH study (Swiss Kidney Project on Genes in Hypertension) is a multicenter family-based population study aiming at exploring genetic and environmental determinants of blood pressure and renal function as well as other health-related cardiometabolic outcomes [29,30].
definition: A multicentre family- and population-based study of adults of European descent in Switzerland, in which index participants drawn at random from population samples in the city of Lausanne (the CoLaus study), the canton of Geneva (the Bus Santé study) and the canton of Bern (the cantonal phone directory) were recruited from December 2009 to April 2013 together with their first-degree relatives and re-examined about three years later, to study genetic and environmental determinants of blood pressure, kidney function and other cardiometabolic outcomes; it is the Swiss part of the European Project on Genes in Hypertension.
location quote: Epidemiology and risk factors of urolithiasis: insights from SKIPOGH, a population-based cohort study in Switzerland.
note: Tier D (D510), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: SKIPOGH as one of three prospective cohorts (with CoLaus|PsyCoLaus, GCKD) meta-analysed for a urinary/blood zinc GWAS; P2-P7 are SKIPOGH's own design and analysis papers. CoLaus, GCKD, HUNT, MoBa and PIVUS among candidates are sibling or unrelated cohorts co-analysed alongside SKIPOGH in P1 or a cited comparison meta-analysis (D510.8), not SKIPOGH itself. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, country, acronym and example are right. The definition's recruitment years (2009–2012, from one abstract) are wrong: the study's design description (PMID:24663506, open access) says 'recruitment began in December 2009 and ended in April 2012 in Lausanne, in October 2012 in Geneva, and in April 2013 in Bern', as the tagged paper's '2009 and 2013' agrees. The definition also missed how the families were found (index participants randomly selected from the CoLaus study in Lausanne, the Bus Santé study in Geneva and the cantonal phone directory in Bern, plus at least one first-degree relative, all of European descent), the follow-up visit about three years later (PMID:41695656), and that SKIPOGH is part of the European Project on Genes in Hypertension; rewritten. The capitalised variant 'Swiss Kidney Project On Genes in Hypertension' (PMID:41159936) added as a synonym. No parent: the European Project on Genes in Hypertension (EPOGH), of which 'SKIPOGH is part', is neither a COHO term nor a review row; a curator could add it as an aggregation. The Lausanne families were drawn from CoLaus (COHO:0000522), but SKIPOGH is a separate study, not a sub-cohort of CoLaus. Minor inconsistency in the sources: PMID:41939824 dates the cohort '2008-2013' and PMID:41695656 '2009-12'; the design paper's month-by-centre dates are used.

label: SLOVENIA study
other synonyms: Slovenia study
example title: Identification of ROBO2 as a Potential Locus Associated with Inhaled Corticosteroid Response in Childhood Asthma.
example quote: A genome-wide association study (GWAS) of the change in lung function after 6 weeks of ICS treatment was performed in 166 asthma patients from the SLOVENIA study.
definition: A clinical study of children and young people aged 5–18 of Slovenian origin with a physician diagnosis of mild-to-moderate persistent asthma and hospital records at tertiary health centres in Slovenia, part of them regularly treated with inhaled corticosteroids under medical supervision, with lung function measured after six weeks of inhaled corticosteroid treatment. It is one of the asthma studies enrolled in the Pharmacogenomics in Childhood Asthma (PiCA) consortium, which studies the genetics of response to asthma treatment.
note: Tier D (D511), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: SLOVENIA denotes this same asthma-ICS-response cohort throughout, in both its own design blurb and the GWAS analysis. Country 'Slovenia' is not in the gazetteer (only 'Slovakia' is listed), so no country entry is given despite D511.26 naming it explicitly. Definition rests on one paper's supplement (D511.26-27); no independent profile paper found. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, name, acronym and example are right. The definition misread the supplement: it says patients were 'recruited from hospital records', but the source describes patients with a physician diagnosis and hospital records at tertiary centres. It also said nothing about what the study is for. It now says the participants were of Slovenian origin, that lung function was measured after six weeks of inhaled corticosteroids, and that the study is a PiCA pharmacogenetic study. PMID:35754128 writes the name as 'Slovenia study', and that case variant is added as a synonym. Slovenia is not in the gazetteer. The supplement gives it: 'The SLOVENIA study recruited patients (5-18 years old) with a physician diagnosis of mild to moderate persistent asthma and hospital records at tertiary health centers in Slovenia.' SLOVENIA is one of the studies enrolled in the PiCA consortium (PMC5967359: 'Currently, 21 asthma studies from 12 different countries are enrolled in the PiCA consortium.'). PiCA is not a COHO term or a row of this review, so no parent is given. No source gives a longer name than 'SLOVENIA study'.

label: Santiago Longitudinal Study
example title: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association study of childhood body mass index identifies novel loci and age-specific effects.
example quote: To identify genetic loci associated with early-childhood body mass index (BMI), we performed GWAS of BMI Z scores in eight ancestrally diverse cohorts: ZOE 2.0 cohort, the Santiago Longitudinal Study (SLS), the Vanderbilt University BioVU biobank, the Geisinger MyCode Health Initiative biobank, Study of Latino (SOL) Youth, Pelotas (Brazil) Birth Cohort, Cameron County Hispanic Cohort (CCHC), and Viva La Familia cohort.
definition: A cohort of healthy, full-term infants from low- to middle-income neighbourhoods of Santiago, Chile, recruited through community clinics in 1991–1996 for an iron-deficiency anaemia preventive trial or a neuromaturation study, and followed up through childhood, adolescence and adulthood in studies of nutrition, development, substance use and cardiometabolic risk.
location quote: The Santiago Longitudinal Study (SLS) is a cohort of participants recruited from community clinics in Santiago, Chile, at infancy between 1991 and 1996 for participation in a randomized trial of iron supplementation to prevent iron deficiency anemia, as described previously.24 Participants were followed during infancy and at ages 5, 10, 16 or 17, and 21 or 22 years and assessed for a range of outcomes.25 Standardized BMIzs were computed using the 2000 CDC Growth Reference charts.21 A total of n = 861 SLS participants were included in the GWAS of BMIz (mean age = 5.51 years).
note: Tier D (D512), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: SLS = the Santiago Longitudinal Study, one of eight cohorts meta-analysed for childhood BMI. Well attested by the study's own paper (P1 full text, D512.8) and five independent papers found by name (P8-P12); GWAS-subset and enrollment numbers dropped from the definition per rule. Checked 2026-09-23: The definition restated the GWAS paper's summary. It left out that some of the cohort was recruited for a neuromaturation study rather than the preventive trial. It listed only the follow-up ages that paper names, although the cohort was also seen at 1, 12, 14 and 23 years and again from 2021. It also gave neither the population (healthy full-term infants from low- to middle-income neighbourhoods) nor the later aims (adolescent substance use, obesity and cardiometabolic risk). The adolescent substance-use study that also calls itself the Santiago Longitudinal Study (PMID:21152714, 24662965) followed the same cohort: 'Study participants came from a community based sample of low SES families from working-class “comunas” (municipalities) in the southern part of the city of Santiago who had earlier participated in a study of nutrition' (PMC3987043). It is not the same as COHO:0000599 (Growth and Obesity Chilean Cohort Study).

input name: Shanghai Mens and Shanghai Womens Health Studies

definition: The Shanghai Women's Health Study and the Shanghai Men's Health Study taken together: two population-based prospective cohorts of middle-aged and elderly Chinese adults in urban Shanghai, China, which recruited women in 1996–2000 and men in 2002–2006 and whose data and biospecimens are often analysed jointly, for example in nested case–control and genome-wide association studies.
location quote: The SWHS (Shanghai Women’s Health Study) and the SMHS (Shanghai Men’s Health Study) are ongoing prospective cohort studies that recruited 75 000 women and 61 500 men of Chinese ancestry, aged 35 to 75 years, from Shanghai, China.
note: Tier D (D513), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because it had no text to work from. The open-access full text settles the name: SMWHS is the Shanghai Women's Health Study (COHO:0000553) and the Shanghai Men's Health Study (COHO:0000578) analysed together as a single contributing study ('SWHS/SMHS'), not a third cohort. It is modelled like COHO:0000400 (Religious Orders Study and Rush Memory and Aging Project), as an aggregation whose two members are existing terms. hasCohort COHO:0000553 and COHO:0000578, with the quote 'We conducted this study using data from Shanghai Men's Health Study (SMHS) and Shanghai Women's Health Study (SWHS), two population-based prospective cohorts of middle-aged and elderly Chinese adults in urban Shanghai, China.' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC5328738/fullTextXML). example title: Deciphering the genetics and mechanisms of predisposition to multiple myeloma.
example quote: This project is made feasible by that fact that our constellation is closely involved in coordinating the Swedish Myeloma Biobank as well as clinical studies on MM and MGUS in Sweden and the Nordic region, providing access to samples from patient cohorts that are sufficiently large to allow a GWAS.
definition: A national biobank of samples from patients with multiple myeloma in Sweden, based at Skåne University Hospital in Lund, whose patients' germline DNA has been genotyped for genome-wide association studies of inherited susceptibility to multiple myeloma.

It is distinct from COHO:0000168 (The Norwegian Biobank for Myeloma), which supplied patients to the same Swedish–Norwegian GWAS, and from COHO:0000085 (German Multiple Myeloma Study Group). note: Tier D (D515), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred. In its only GWAS paper the tag does not denote the study that the PGS Catalog name describes. That case–control sample has no name of its own, and tier C already judged the same sample, tagged SNUH in PMID:42225636, not a cohort. parent quote: The Hispanic Community Children’s Health Study/Study of Latino Youth (SOL Youth) cohort is an ancillary study of the Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos (HCHS/SOL) that recruited n = 1,466 children aged 8–16 years between 2012 and 2014 whose parents/legal guardians participated in the HCHS/SOL at one of four field centers (Chicago, Bronx, San Diego, and Miami).33 A total of n = 1,073 children were included in GWAS analyses (mean age = 12.00 years).
note: Tier D (D516), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: SOLYouth = the SOL Youth ancillary paediatric cohort of HCHS/SOL, one of eight cohorts meta-analysed for childhood BMI. PGS Catalog's 'Study of Latino Youth Study' matches D516.31's own phrasing ('Study of Latino Youth (SOL Youth) study'), added as synonym minus the duplicated trailing 'Study'. label: Sao Paulo Heart Failure Cohort
other synonyms: Sao Paolo Heart Failure Cohort
example title: Meta-analysis of genome-wide associations and polygenic risk prediction for atrial fibrillation in more than 180,000 cases.
example quote: The following studies have previously been described: ARIC8 , BBJ9 , deCODE10 , DiscovEHR10 , FHS8 , HUNT10 , KAFN11 , MESA6 , MGI10 , MGH CAMP6 , PHB12 , SiGN13 , SPHFC6 , UKBB14 and WGHS8 .
definition: A cohort of adults with symptomatic (stage C) heart failure of different aetiologies, prospectively enrolled from the outpatient clinic of the Heart Institute of the University of São Paulo Medical School in São Paulo, Brazil. Its genotyped participants, with atrial fibrillation ascertained from electrocardiograms and medical records, have contributed to genome-wide association studies of atrial fibrillation.
location quote: SPHFC: Participants for the Sao Paolo Heart Failure Cohort (SPHFC) were prospectively enrolled from the outpatient clinic at the Heart Institute, the University of Sao Paulo Medical School, Sao Paulo, Brazil.
note: Tier D (D517), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred, and its example quote was a bare spreadsheet cell ('SPHFC') that says nothing about the study. P1's Supplementary Information lists SPHFC among previously described studies and cites the 2017 AFGen paper (PMID:28416818). That paper's Supplementary Note describes 'the Sao Paolo Heart Failure Cohort (SPHFC)', and its Supplementary Tables expand the acronym as 'SPHFC, Sao Paulo Heart Failure Cohort'. It is a Brazilian heart-failure outpatient cohort at the Heart Institute of the University of São Paulo. The label spells Paulo as the Supplementary Tables do; the Supplementary Note's spelling 'Sao Paolo' is kept as a synonym. Its eligibility and exclusion criteria match, word for word, those of the Heart Institute's prospective heart-failure cohort enrolled in 2002–2004 and followed for all-cause death until 2009 (PMID:25059829, PMC4113663: 'A prospective cohort study was conducted from 2002 to 2004 and included heart failure patients from Heart Institute of University of São Paulo Medical School, São Paulo, Brazil.'). It is almost certainly the same cohort, but the dates are left out of the definition because that paper does not call it SPHFC. SPHFC contributed to AFGen meta-analyses (AFGen is COHO:0000855), but no source I read states membership, so no parent is given.

input name: Singapore Preconception Study of Long-Term Maternal and Child Outcomes
label: Singapore Preconception Study of Long-Term Maternal and Child Outcomes
other synonyms: Singapore PREconception Study of long-Term maternal and child Outcomes
example title: Exploring multi-omics and clinical characteristics linked to accelerated biological aging in Asian women of reproductive age: insights from the S-PRESTO study.
example quote: The Singapore Preconception Study of Long-Term Maternal and Child Outcomes (S-PRESTO) longitudinal preconception cohort, a deeply-phenotyped, multi-ethnic cohort of Asian women of reproductive age, provides a promising opportunity to address these research gaps.
definition: A preconception, longitudinal cohort of Chinese, Malay or Indian women aged 18–45 who intended to conceive and deliver in Singapore, recruited in February 2015–October 2017 through a preconception clinic at KK Women's and Children's Hospital and through public outreach, and followed with their children from before conception through pregnancy into early childhood. Its aim is to study how nutrition, lifestyle and maternal mood before and during pregnancy affect the offspring's epigenome, duration of gestation, fetal growth, and metabolic and neural phenotypes.
location quote: Between February 2015 and October 2017, the S-PRESTO study recruited 1039 Chinese, Malay or Indian (or any combinations thereof) women aged 18-45 years and who intended to get pregnant and deliver in Singapore, resulting in 1032 unique participants and 373 children born in the cohort.
note: Tier D (D518), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: S-PRESTO = the paper's own preconception cohort, analysed for biological ageing in Asian women. Kept the mixed-case spelled-out variant 'Singapore PREconception Study of long-Term maternal and child Outcomes' (D518.32) as a synonym per the capitalisation rule. Recruitment counts excluded from the definition as sizes, not identity. Checked 2026-09-23: Close. The aims now follow the cohort profile's wording (outcomes in the offspring; the draft had written 'maternal and child metabolic and neural outcomes'). The definition now also says that the women's children are followed from birth, and how the women were recruited: a preconception clinic at KK Women's and Children's Hospital plus public outreach. A sister cohort of COHO:0000866 (GUSTO), not part of it: the profile presents S-PRESTO as a platform for replicating GUSTO's epigenetic findings.

label: Swiss Pediatric Sepsis Study
example title: Genome-wide association study of paediatric bacteraemia and sepsis.
example quote: Using samples and clinical data from 650 children enrolled in the Swiss Pediatric Sepsis Study, a national multicentre cohort for culture-proven bacterial sepsis, we conducted within-cohort analyses and a separate case-control analysis in 510 cases and 994 controls, testing genome-wide polymorphisms for association with sepsis susceptibility and, in cases only, with disease characteristics.
definition: A nationwide, prospective, multicentre cohort of neonates and children younger than 17 with blood culture-proven bacterial sepsis meeting criteria for systemic inflammatory response syndrome, enrolled from September 2011 to December 2015 at ten tertiary and regional paediatric hospitals in Switzerland, including all five university centres and all paediatric intensive care units, to study the incidence, clinical features and outcomes of paediatric sepsis.
location quote: The Swiss Pediatric Sepsis Study was a nationwide, prospective, multicentre cohort conducted from September 1, 2011, to December 31, 2015, across 10 tertiary and regional paediatric hospitals in Switzerland, including all five university centres and all paediatric intensive care units.
note: Tier D (D519), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: SPSS denotes the Swiss Pediatric Sepsis Study cohort itself, for both within-cohort and case-control genetic analyses. Definition combines the study's own profile from P1 (nationwide design, dates, ten hospitals, sepsis-eligibility criteria); enrollment and case-control numbers dropped per the no-sizes rule. No parent or sub-study relationship stated. Checked 2026-09-23: Close. The definition took its eligibility from P1's methods ('bacterial or fungal'), but the design paper and P1's own abstract say blood culture-proven bacterial sepsis. input name: Systematic Treatment Enhancement Program for Bipolar Disorder
label: Systematic Treatment Enhancement Program for Bipolar Disorder
example title: Body weight changes and bipolar disorder: a molecular pathway analysis.
example quote: The STEP-BD sample is analyzed through a hypothesis-free molecular pathway analysis in order to detect the molecular pathways that distinguish individuals who experience weight change during BD treatment from those who do not.
definition: A long-term, multicentre study funded by the US National Institute of Mental Health that enrolled outpatients aged 15 or older with any subtype of bipolar disorder at 22 academic medical centres in the United States and followed them over seven years. All participants entered a naturalistic standard care pathway, with randomized care pathways for acute and refractory depression, to answer questions about the effectiveness of treatments for bipolar disorder.
location quote: The study was conducted across 22 academic medical centers in the United States and was approved by the institutional review board of the participating institutions.
note: Tier D (D522), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: STEP = the STEP-BD naturalistic bipolar-disorder cohort, analysed here for weight change during BD treatment. No unit gives STEP-BD's recruitment country or enrollment dates; general knowledge suggests a US effectiveness programme, but nothing here confirms it, so no country is given. Sample-size numbers dropped per rule. Checked 2026-09-23: The definition gave the wrong purpose ('to characterise the course of illness'). STEP-BD was an NIMH-funded study of the effectiveness of treatments for bipolar disorder, with a naturalistic standard care pathway and randomized care pathways. The definition also did not say where the study ran. The draft left out the United States for want of a quote, but open-access text states it. No duplicate in COHO or this review. The tag STEP is kept as an acronym with STEP-BD.

label: Simultaneous Study of Gemcitabine-Docetaxel Combination adjuvant treatment, as well as Extended Bisphosphonate and Surveillance-Trial
other synonyms: SUCCESS-A study|SUCCESS-A trial|SUCCESS A trial|Simultaneous Study of Gemcitabine-Docetaxel Combination Adjuvant Treatment, as Well as Extended Bisphosphonate and Surveillance-Trial
example title: Identification of Two Genetic Loci Associated with Leukopenia after Chemotherapy in Patients with Breast Cancer.
example quote: The multicenter SUCCESS-A study included a prospective subprotocol concerned with the influence of germline genetic variants on side effects and efficacy of the chemotherapy.
definition: An open-label, multicentre, randomised phase III trial in Germany, sponsored by Ludwig-Maximilians-University Munich, that enrolled adult patients with invasive early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence from 2005 to 2007 and compared, in a 2×2 factorial design, adjuvant FEC–docetaxel chemotherapy with or without gemcitabine and two versus five years of zoledronic acid, with an affiliated translational research programme on circulating tumour cells, serum tumour markers and pharmacogenetics.
location quote: The SUCCESS-A study was conducted in 251 study centers in all regions of Germany.
note: Tier D (D524), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: SUCCESSA, the SUCCESS-A trial cohort itself. Multiple independent mentions (D524.1,4,7,9,10,13,16,19) consistently describe one multicentre German breast-cancer trial cohort. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, country and example are right. The label was the PGS Catalog's short name, not the trial's full name: SUCCESS stands for 'Simultaneous Study of Gemcitabine-Docetaxel Combination adjuvant treatment, as well as Extended Bisphosphonate and Surveillance-Trial' (PMID:24832787, EudraCT 2005-000490-21, which is SUCCESS-A's number), the brief title of its registration NCT02181101 (org study id SUCCESS-A). The definition leaned on one paper: it gave a centre count (251 there, 271 in PMID:26385214), made the GWAS paper's germline-variant subprotocol a defining feature, and left out the dates (2005-2007), the open-label phase III 2×2 factorial design, the sponsor and the wider translational programme. The draft also missed the acronyms 'SUCCESS A' (e.g. 'the randomized SUCCESS A trial', PMID:26385214) and 'SUCCESS' (the trial's name before SUCCESS-B and -C existed, PMID:24832787). If the curator prefers the short name as label, 'SUCCESS-A trial' is the form the trial group uses most; the expanded title is the registered name. SUCCESS-B (E1067) and SUCCESS-C (E1068) are separate, later trials, not arms of SUCCESS-A. E1067's PGS Catalog name 'Simultaneous Study of Gemcitabine-Docetaxel Combination adjuvant treatment' is in fact SUCCESS-A's name: SUCCESS-B is registered as 'Studying the Benefits of Adjuvant Sequential vs. Combined Taxane Based Chemotherapy, Followed by Different Biological Treatment Strategies in Early, HER2-positive Breast Cancer' (NCT00670878), so check that row when tier E is reviewed. The acronym 'SUCCESS' is added because the trial used it alone before B and C existed; no COHO term carries it.

input name: Seoul National University Prospectively Enrolled Registry for RCC-Nephrectomy

example title: Polygenic risk score model for renal cell carcinoma in the Korean population and relationship with lifestyle-associated factors.

definition: A prospective, biobank-linked registry at Seoul National University Hospital, South Korea, that since March 2016 has enrolled patients clinically diagnosed with renal cell carcinoma who undergo surgical treatment (ablation, or partial, radical or cytoreductive nephrectomy), collecting standardised clinical, pathological, quality-of-life and survival data and blood and tumour samples stored in the hospital's Human Biobank. It is the nephrectomy sub-cohort of the renal cell carcinoma arm (SUPER-RCC) of the Seoul National University Prospectively Enrolled Registry for Genitourinary Cancer (SUPER-GUC).
