In PMID:36780644 UoPMC is the University of Pittsburgh part of the paper's U.S. data set ('Patients constituting the U.S. cohort included those from UChicago (n = 118) and the University of Pittsburgh (n = 200) (see Figures E1 and E2).', PMC10263132), IPF patients first gathered for the 2013 IPF GWAS, which describes them only as patients 'clinically characterised at the University of Chicago and University of Pittsburgh' (PMC3894577). The PGS Catalog id denotes a different group: in PMID:26352532 (source GWAS of PGS000740), UoPMC is an unnamed clinical series of lung cancer surgery patients ('A clinical study contributed 45-85 year-old ≥10 pack-year current or former cigarette smokers who received diagnostic, staging, or therapeutic surgery after 2001 at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center for non-carcinoid lung cancer and who provided a research blood sample within 1 year of diagnosis.', PMC4636453). Neither is a named study, and the two cover different patients, so the tag gets no term. The tag denotes different people in the two catalogues: IPF patients (GWAS Catalog) and lung cancer patients (PGS Catalog). The Pittsburgh Lung Screening Study, paired with UoPMC in PGS000740's source GWAS, is its own review name (E903 PLuSS).

label: Danish T2D Case-Control Study
other synonyms: Danish T2D case-control study
example title: Multi-ancestry genetic study of type 2 diabetes highlights the power of diverse populations for discovery and translation.
example quote: Danish T2D Case-Control Study (UCPH) was undertaken by the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Basic Metabolic Research, which is an independent Research Center, based at the University of Copenhagen, Denmark and partially funded by an unconditional donation from the Novo Nordisk Foundation (www.cbmr.ku.dk, Grant number NNF18CC0034900).
definition: A type 2 diabetes case-control sample of Danish participants, undertaken by the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Basic Metabolic Research at the University of Copenhagen, that brings together people from several Danish studies, among them the Vejle Diabetes Biobank, Inter99, Health2006, Health2008 and DanFunD: cases with type 2 diabetes by self-report, anti-diabetic treatment or fasting or 2-hour plasma glucose, and controls with normal fasting and, where measured, 2-hour plasma glucose, genotyped genome-wide for genetic studies of type 2 diabetes.
location quote: The studies included in the Danish T2D Case- Control Study (UCPH) were conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki II and were approved by the local Ethical Committees of Copenhagen County, the Capital Region of Denmark, or the Region of Southern Denmark.
note: Tier D (D541), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: UPCH/UCPH is one of many discovery cohorts (with UKB, deCODE, FUSION etc.) in a multi-ancestry type 2 diabetes GWAS. Row's own tag is 'UPCH' but the evidence always spells it 'UCPH' (University of Copenhagen); both kept as acronyms. Combines pre-existing named Danish studies (one, Inter99, is itself a candidate COHO:0000511) under one case-control protocol; typed as a cohort, per MEGA's precedent, not an aggregation. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type and example are right. The tag UPCH is not a mistake of the catalogues alone: the DIAMANTE European paper's Supplementary Table 1 lists the study under the acronym UPCH, with the name 'Danish T2D case-control study' and reference PMID 23160641 (static-content.springer.com, 41588_2018_241_MOESM3_ESM.xlsx), while its cohort acknowledgements head it 'DANISH-UCPH' and the 2022 paper uses UCPH; DANISH-UCPH is added. The definition gave only glucose criteria for cases (they are also defined by self-report or anti-diabetic treatment) and presented the five funded source studies as the full list, which the source does not say. The country quote now ties the included studies to Danish regions rather than naming the university's location. Typed as a cohort, as DGDG (D402), another GWAS case-control sample drawn partly from other studies, was. Its source studies include Inter99 (COHO:0000511), Health2006 (COHO:0000913), Health2008 (D242), DanFunD (E240) and the Vejle Diabetes Biobank (E1196); none is its parent or child. It contributed to the European component of DIAMANTE (D017), but no source calls it a member, so no parent is given; if the curator links DIAMANTE's studies with hasCohort, this is one. 'UCPH' is also the University of Copenhagen's abbreviation, which is an institution and so needs no editor note.

label: CoFAR Eosinophilic Esophagitis Registry
other synonyms: Eosinophilic Esophagitis Databank|Eosinophilic Esophagitis (EoE) Databank (CoFAR 5)|NIH Consortium of Food Allergy Research (CoFAR) EoE Cohort|NIH CoFAR EoE cohort|US NIH CoFAR EoE cohort
example title: Genome-wide admixture and association analysis identifies African ancestry-specific risk loci of eosinophilic esophagitis in African Americans.
example quote: The external cohorts were composed of cases from the National Institutes of Health Consortium of Food Allergy Researchers (CoFAR)13, and the Consortium of Eosinophilic Gastrointestinal Disease Researchers (CEGIR)37.
definition: A registry of children and adults aged 6 months to 65 years with biopsy-confirmed eosinophilic esophagitis, enrolled at a single visit in 2011–2016 at the five US sites of the NIAID-funded Consortium of Food Allergy Research (in New York, North Carolina, Denver, Little Rock and Baltimore), with medical history questionnaires and blood or saliva samples genotyped at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center, to characterise the disease and establish its genetic basis.
location quote: To describe the clinical, endoscopic, and histopathologic features of a large number of children and adults with EoE across the United States.
note: Tier D (D542), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: Researched. The GWAS paper's full text (PMC10164699, on disk) names the cohort: its external EoE cases came from the NIH Consortium of Food Allergy Research (CoFAR), citing ref 13, the CoFAR EoE phenotype paper (PMID:30075341). That paper describes the sample as 'a multisite single visit registry enrolling subjects aged 6 months to 65 years with EoE' (abstract), recruited 'from the 5 US sites forming CoFAR' and part of a CoFAR study 'the primary aim of which was to establish the genetic basis of EoE', with genotyping at Cincinnati Children's; '708 subjects were enrolled between May 2011 and March 2016' (PMC6132253). It is registered as NCT01323803, 'Eosinophilic Esophagitis (EoE) Databank (CoFAR 5)', acronym CoFAR5, sponsored by NIAID. CoFAR's own overview calls it the 'CoFAR Eosinophilic Esophagitis Registry' (PMC6368887 section heading), and the CCHMC genetics papers call it the 'NIH Consortium of Food Allergy Research (CoFAR) EoE Cohort' (PMC8082436), which the catalogue name 'US NIH CoFAR EoE cohort' abbreviates. Label choice: the registration title 'Eosinophilic Esophagitis Databank' is too generic to stand alone, so the label is CoFAR's own name for it and the registration titles are synonyms; a curator may prefer the registration title. CoFAR, the NIAID consortium that ran it, is a research network of trials and observational studies and is not in COHO, so there is no parent. The GWAS's other tags are CCHMC (its local cohort) and 'other' (CEGIR cases).

label: Vanderbilt Online Musicality Study
example title: Genome-wide investigation of prosody perception: Shared genetic influences between speech rhythm, musical rhythm, and reading traits.
example quote: The study population was a subset of those who participated in the Vanderbilt Online Musicality Study,47 where participants completed various internet-based tasks, including TOPsy, and submitted genetic samples.
definition: An online study of adults aged 18 or over who speak English fluently, conducted by researchers at Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, Tennessee, and recruited worldwide, mainly through ResearchMatch and also through Vanderbilt newsletters and research mailing lists, Reddit, Facebook advertising and social media sharing. Participants completed web-based questionnaires on music engagement and auditory tasks of musical rhythm and speech perception, and those with a US mailing address were invited to return mail-in saliva samples for genotyping, to study the genetics of musicality.
location quote: Saliva collection kits were sent to 2,286 of these participants meeting the following criteria: they had completed the entire survey, reported that their data was usable, and had a valid US mailing address.
note: Tier D (D543), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: Vanderbilt_OM = Vanderbilt Online Musicality Study, the parent cohort from which the prosody/speech-rhythm-perception GWAS subset was drawn. No country asserted: no quotable unit ties recruitment to a place, and 'Vanderbilt' is a university name rather than a place-name in the cohort's own title. 23andMe is co-thanked (D543.13) but no unit says the samples overlap. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym and example are right. The definition was circular ('recruited through the Vanderbilt Online Musicality Study') and said nothing of who ran it, whom it recruited or how DNA was collected. The design paper (PMID:36718543, PMC10038917 author manuscript) says 'The Vanderbilt Online Musicality Study is a worldwide sample of adults recruited from five sources: ResearchMatch.org (primary recruitment source, ...' plus Vanderbilt University Medical Center newsletters and mailing lists, Reddit, Facebook advertising and social media sharing; participants had to be at least 18 and fluent in English; the study had 'an online portion consisting of surveys and behavioral measures, and an optional DNA collection via mail-in saliva sampling', under the Vanderbilt IRB. The draft missed the country: the online part was worldwide, but saliva kits went only to participants with a valid US mailing address, so the genotyped sample the GWAS uses is from the United States. No recruitment dates are given in the sources read. The phenotypic sample was recruited worldwide online, so United_States describes where DNA was collected, not every participant. Not related to BioVU (COHO:0000417, acronym Vanderbilt) or the 23andMe research cohort (COHO:0000449), which P1 analyses separately.

label: Viva la Familia Study
other synonyms: Viva La Familia Study|Viva La Familia|VIVA LA FAMILIA Study
example title: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association study of childhood body mass index identifies novel loci and age-specific effects.
example quote: The Viva La Familia study recruited n = 1,030 children from 319 families between November 2000 and August 2004 from a Hispanic population in Houston, Texas, to assess genetic and environmental factors affecting obesity and its related comorbidities.31 A total of n = 656 participants were included in GWAS analyses (mean age = 10.7 for girls and mean age = 11.2 for boys).
definition: A family study of Hispanic children in Houston, Texas, conducted at the USDA/ARS Children's Nutrition Research Center of Baylor College of Medicine, which in 2000–2005 recruited families through a proband aged 4–19 with a BMI above the 95th percentile, together with the proband's siblings aged 4–19 and their parents. The children were phenotyped in depth (anthropometry, body composition by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, diet, physical activity, energy expenditure and metabolic risk factors) and followed up after one year, to map genetic and environmental contributions to childhood obesity and its comorbidities.
location quote: The Viva La Familia study recruited n = 1,030 children from 319 families between November 2000 and August 2004 from a Hispanic population in Houston, Texas, to assess genetic and environmental factors affecting obesity and its related comorbidities.31 A total of n = 656 participants were included in GWAS analyses (mean age = 10.7 for girls and mean age = 11.2 for boys).
note: Tier D (D544), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: VFA = Viva La Familia (Study), one of eight ancestrally diverse cohorts meta-analysed (with a further EGG/MoBa meta-analysis) for a childhood BMI GWAS. Two case variants of the label appear (Title Case 'Viva La Familia [Study]' in most sources vs 'Viva la Familia Study' in the cohort's own profile paper, D544.51/.54); both kept. No parent: VFA is meta-analysed alongside EGG/MoBa, not stated a member of them. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, country, example and no-parent are right. The definition left out who ran the study (the Children's Nutrition Research Center, where families were invited and measured), that siblings and parents were enrolled with the proband, the proband criterion (BMI above the 95th percentile at 4–19 years) and the one-year follow-up; the cohort's own GWAS paper says 'Family recruitment and phenotyping were conducted in 2000–2005 in Houston, TX.' and 'Each family was ascertained on an obese proband, defined as a BMI>95th percentile, between the ages 4–19 y.' (PMC3522587). The all-capitals form 'VIVA LA FAMILIA Study', which the cohort's own papers use, is added as a synonym. The draft's country quote names Houston, Texas, which is in the United States; the automatic check only asked for that to be confirmed. P1 gives recruitment as November 2000 to August 2004 and the 2012 paper gives recruitment and phenotyping as 2000–2005, so the definition uses the latter. Not Project Viva (D325) or Viborg Vascular (VIVA, D175).

label: Western Australian Melanoma Health Study
example title: Genome-wide association meta-analyses combining multiple risk phenotypes provide insights into the genetic architecture of cutaneous melanoma susceptibility.
example quote: The WAMHS population based study was collected from Perth, Australia based on histopathology confirmed invasive, cutaneous melanoma cases in the Western Australian Cancer Registry.
definition: A population-based collection of adult melanoma cases resident in Western Australia and diagnosed between January 2006 and September 2009, identified through the Western Australian Cancer Registry and invited by mail with their diagnosing doctor's consent, with registry pathology data, a telephone questionnaire on melanoma risk factors such as sun exposure and skin type, and blood samples for DNA, RNA and serum, established to investigate the genetic epidemiology of melanoma.
location quote: The WAMHS population based study was collected from Perth, Australia based on histopathology confirmed invasive, cutaneous melanoma cases in the Western Australian Cancer Registry.
note: Tier D (D545), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (melanoma multi-trait GWAS): abstract doesn't name WAMHS; identity and definition rest on WAMHS's own profile paper (P2) and later WAMHS papers (P3, P4). P1 doesn't name the cohort (no full text/supplement given here), so example ev is null. P4 also tags the separate 'Genes, Environment, and Melanoma Study' in the same sentence - a different cohort, not WAMHS. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, country and no-parent are right. The definition left out who was enrolled and when: 'all eligible, resident Western Australian, adult cases of melanoma diagnosed between January 2006 and September 2009, were contacted by mail and invited to participate', and what was collected (registry pathology, a telephone risk-factor questionnaire, blood for DNA, RNA and serum) (PMID:21474410 abstract); it is a case-only collection, whose GWAS used external Australian control sets. The example had no quote and none can be had from the tagged paper: PMID:34813871 (read in its accepted version, White Rose eprint 181336) names only the input meta-analysis (Landi et al. 2020), QSkin and UK Biobank in its text and leaves the cohort list to a supplement that jidonline.org blocks (403). The corrected example is that input meta-analysis, GCST010304 (PMID:32341527), whose supplementary note describes WAMHS; the country quote now names Australia. Case-only: the control sets paired with WAMHS in the melanoma GWAS (IBD programme of the Royal Brisbane & Women's Hospital and ANZRAG glaucoma cases) are not part of WAMHS. The GWAS Catalog tags WAMHS only on GCST90103971; GCST010304 carries no cohort tags but its paper describes WAMHS, so it satisfies the GWAS-subset example rule. P4's other cohort, the Genes, Environment, and Melanoma Study, is a different study.

input name: Warfarin Anticoagulation in Patients in sub-Saharan Africa
label: Warfarin Anticoagulation in Patients in sub-Saharan Africa
other synonyms: WARfarin anticoagulation in PATients in Sub-Saharan Africa|Warfarin Anticoagulation in Patients in Sub-Saharan Africa
example title: Meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies of stable warfarin dose in patients of African ancestry.
example quote: The African cohorts were obtained through the Warfarin Anticoagulation in Patients in sub-Saharan Africa (War-PATH http://warpath.info/) observational study.16, 17, 18 The War-PATH study enrolled participants receiving warfarin treatment, who were on stable dose, defined as consistent prescribed doses for 2 consecutive clinic visits in the year before recruitment.
definition: An observational study of adults taking warfarin at a stable maintenance dose for venous thromboembolism, atrial fibrillation or valvular heart disease, Black African and, in South Africa, also of mixed ancestry, recruited from June 2018 to March 2020 at outpatient clinics and hospital departments in Uganda and South Africa by the NIHR Global Health Research Group on warfarin anticoagulation in sub-Saharan Africa (the University of Liverpool, the Infectious Diseases Institute in Kampala and the University of Cape Town), with clinical data and blood samples for genotyping, to develop clinical and genetic warfarin dosing algorithms for sub-Saharan African patients.
location quote: Participants were recruited from 12 outpatient clinics and hospital departments in Uganda and South Africa between June 2018 and March 2020 (Asiimwe et al., 2020a; Asiimwe et al., 2021).
note: Tier D (D546), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: War-PATH as its own multi-wave observational study (4 internal 'cohorts') providing African-ancestry discovery samples for a warfarin-dose GWAS meta-analysis alongside IWPC and UAB. The 4 internal 'War-PATH cohorts 1-4' are recruitment waves of one study, not separate cohorts. Country not in the gazetteer: Zimbabwe (D546.3, War-PATH cohort 2 also recruited in Harare). IWPC and UAB are distinct external cohorts, not part of War-PATH. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, countries and example are right. The definition described the GWAS paper's four analysis sets ('recruited in successive waves') rather than the study, and folded in the 'bundle of care' study, which enrolled patients newly started on warfarin and so contradicts 'established on a stable warfarin dose'. It also left out who ran the study, the indications and its aim. The War-PATH observational study (NCT03512080, sponsor University of Liverpool) enrolled adults on a stable maintenance dose for venous thromboembolism, atrial fibrillation or valvular heart disease, to develop a clinical and a genetic dosing algorithm; its group is 'a study between the University of Liverpool, Infectious Diseases Institute, Uganda and University of Cape Town, South Africa' (warpath.info), funded by the NIHR; participants were recruited 'between June 2018 and March 2020' (PMC9537548). 'WarPATH', the spelling on the study website, is added as an acronym and the Sub-Saharan capitalisation of the registered title as a synonym. The country quote is replaced by one about the study's own recruitment. The tag covers more than the registered observational study: the GWAS's cohort 4 comes from the group's later 'bundle of care' implementation study (newly started patients in Kampala and Cape Town, 2021-2022), and part of cohort 2 was recruited in 2016-2017 in Cape Town and Harare, Zimbabwe, for earlier studies. Zimbabwe is left out: it is not in the gazetteer and its participants predate War-PATH. The registered official title, 'National Institute of Health Research (NIHR) Global Health Research Group on Warfarin Anticoagulation in Patients with Cardiovascular Disease in Sub-Saharan Africa', names the research group; a curator may add it as a synonym. IWPC (D458) and UAB, the GWAS's African American cohorts, are separate. No parent.

input name: Women's Environmental Cancer and Radiation Epidemiology Study
label: Women's Environmental Cancer and Radiation Epidemiology Study
other synonyms: Women's Environment, Cancer, and Radiation Epidemiology Study|WECARE Study
example title: A genome-wide association study of contralateral breast cancer in the Women's Environmental Cancer and Radiation Epidemiology Study.
example quote: We performed a genome-wide association analysis in the Women’s Environmental Cancer and Radiation Epidemiology (WECARE) Study of women with first breast cancer diagnosed at age < 55 years including 1161 with CBC who served as cases and 1668 with unilateral breast cancer (UBC) who served as controls.
definition: A population-based case-control study of contralateral breast cancer, designed to examine the joint roles of radiation exposure and genetic susceptibility, in which women diagnosed before age 55 with a first primary invasive breast cancer who later developed contralateral breast cancer were individually matched to women with unilateral breast cancer. Participants were identified through population-based cancer registries in the United States, Canada and Denmark and recruited in two phases, WECARE I (2001–2004) and WECARE II (2009–2012).
location quote: All study subjects were identified, recruited, and interviewed through five population-based cancer registries, four in the USA (three Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results registries, namely Iowa, Los Angeles County [CA], and Seattle [WA], and the Cancer Surveillance Program of Orange County [CA]) and one in Denmark (the Danish Cancer Registry). || All participants were identified through eight population-based cancer registries: six in the USA, one in Canada and one in Denmark (Table 1).
note: Tier D (D547), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: WECARE itself (combining WECARE I and II), the sole cohort behind this GWAS. WECARE I (2001-2004) and WECARE II (2009-2012) are phases of one study, not separate cohorts. Danish data were excluded from this particular GWAS for regulatory reasons (D547.39) but the cohort's design still includes Denmark. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, countries and example are right. The definition left out what the study was built for (the design paper: 'To examine the joint roles of radiation exposure and genetic susceptibility in the etiology of breast cancer, we designed a case-control study nested within five population-based cancer registries') and did not say that cases had a later contralateral cancer and controls were matched women with unilateral breast cancer; 'studied in two phases' should say recruited in two phases (WECARE I 2001–2004, WECARE II 2009–2012, per PMID:27400983). The draft's United States quote says only 'US', which the automatic check did not recognise; replaced by the design paper's registry list (Iowa, Los Angeles County, Seattle, Orange County), which also names Denmark. Canada entered only in WECARE II (the Ontario registry). Added the study's own name variant from PMID:39786405 and 'WECARE Study' as synonyms. No duplicate in COHO or this review. Some WECARE papers spell the name 'Women’s Environmental, Cancer, and Radiation Epidemiology' (PMID:27400983) or 'Women’s Environment, Cancer, and Radiation Epidemiology' (PMID:39786405); the label keeps the form of the study's titles and of the PGS Catalog.

label: Wills Eye Hospital GWAS
other synonyms: Wills Eye Hospital
example title: Meta-analysis of uveal melanoma genome-wide association studies identifies novel risk loci and population effect size heterogeneity.
example quote: We recruited 409 UM cases via the UPenn Genetic Diagnostic Laboratory from patients receiving treatment at the Wills Eye Hospital (Philadelphia, PA, USA).
definition: A case-control study of uveal melanoma run at the University of Pennsylvania for a genome-wide association study of the cancer and of differences between tumours with monosomy and disomy of chromosome 3, whose cases were patients treated at Wills Eye Hospital in Philadelphia, recruited through the UPenn Genetic Diagnostic Laboratory with blood samples and clinical and tumour data, and whose controls were selected from participants of the Penn Medicine Biobank.
location quote: We recruited 409 UM cases via the UPenn Genetic Diagnostic Laboratory from patients receiving treatment at the Wills Eye Hospital (Philadelphia, PA, USA).
note: Tier D (D548), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: the Wills Eye Hospital GWAS itself (UM cases plus PMBB-derived controls); sole paper using the WEH tag. Controls are a subset of the Penn Medicine Biobank (COHO:0000457), not modelled as parent since this is a distinct assembled case-control set, not a sub-cohort of PMBB. 'Wills Eye Hospital' also names the hospital generically in unrelated cornea/retina papers (P11-P13), not this GWAS cohort. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country, example and the decision not to make it a sub-cohort of the Penn Medicine BioBank are right. The definition called the whole sample 'a case-control cohort of uveal melanoma patients', although the controls are Penn Medicine Biobank participants selected as controls, and it did not say who ran the study or what it was for (risk loci overall and loci with different effects in monosomy-3 and disomy-3 tumours: 'we aimed to identify loci with differential effects on M3 and D3 cases'). The paper calls the sample 'Wills Eye Hospital GWAS', 'Wills Eye Hospital study' and 'the Wills cohort'; the synonym 'Wills Eye Hospital' is the PGS Catalog's name and the paper's short name in Table 1, though it is also the hospital's name. Controls come from COHO:0000457 (Penn Medicine BioBank) but the case-control set as a whole is not part of it, so no parent. No duplicate in COHO or this review.

label: WOBASZ II
other synonyms: Multi-centre National Population Health Examination Survey|Multicentre National Population Health Examination Survey|Multicenter National Health Survey II
example title: Genetic investigation of fibromuscular dysplasia identifies risk loci and shared genetics with common cardiovascular diseases.
example quote: We used 298 controls from a randomly ascertained sample from the WOBASZ II (Multicentre National Population Health Examination Survey) study, a population-based Polish cohort54.
definition: A cross-sectional national health examination survey of a random sample of residents of Poland aged over 20, drawn from the national identity card registry by three-stage sampling stratified by voivodeship, type of urbanisation and gender, and examined in 2013–2014 with face-to-face questionnaire interviews, physical examinations and blood samples to assess the prevalence, treatment and control of cardiovascular diseases and their risk factors. It continued the first WOBASZ survey of 2003–2005 with a new, independent sample and was coordinated by the Institute of Cardiology in Warsaw with medical universities in Gdansk, Katowice, Krakow, Lodz and Poznan.
location quote: The WOBASZ II study was planned as a cross-sectional survey of a random sample of Polish residents aged over 20 years.
note: Tier D (D549), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: WOBASZ II (its own text always says 'WOBASZ II'; the paper's cohort-tag list drops the 'II'), source of the study's controls. GWAS tag 'WOBASZ' (bare) but P1's own text and its table consistently name the cohort 'WOBASZ II', 2013-2014, distinct from the original WOBASZ round (2003-2005, per P8-P10, a separate earlier cohort not covered by this tag). No unit gives WOBASZ's Polish-language expansion. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity and modelling are right: the bare tag WOBASZ on GCST90026612 means WOBASZ II, the 2013–2014 survey that supplied the Polish controls, not the 2003–2005 WOBASZ, which was a separate random sample. The definition omitted what the survey is for (its design paper: 'to evaluate prevalence, control, treatment, and morbidity' of cardiovascular disease and its risk factors) and how the sample was drawn, and 'second round of the WOBASZ programme' needed to say it was a new sample. Added 'Multicenter National Health Survey II' (PMID:35807845), the one English full-name form found that carries the 'II'. The label stays 'WOBASZ II' because the English full name, 'Multi-centre National Population Health Examination Survey', is used for both rounds (e.g. PMID:28224973 uses it for WOBASZ 2003–2014 as a whole), so it cannot tell them apart; the draft's two synonyms are the forms used for WOBASZ II in its design paper and in the GWAS paper. COHO has no term for the first WOBASZ survey; if one is minted it will share the acronym WOBASZ (and those synonyms) with this term and both will need editor notes. No duplicate in COHO or this review.

Tier D (D550), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Same cohort as review name E533 (Intern Health Study), a later tier: its names are added when that tier is minted. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft read HIS as the paper's abbreviation for its Hispanic/Latin American ancestry group. It is almost certainly the Intern Health Study's acronym IHS with two letters transposed. (1) The GWAS Catalog's cohort list for GCST90328131 covers every named study in the paper's Supplementary Table 1 (CKB, CONVERGE, 23andMe, WHI, UKB, BioMe, BBJ, MVP, AGDS, GERA, JHS, BioVU as 'Vanderbilt', HCHS/SOL as 'HCHS' and 'SOL', PGC-MDD2 as 'PGC', Army STARRS, Genes & Health as 'G&H', DCHS, DNHS; Taiwan MDD, PIRC, MAMHS and PrOMIS fall under 'other') except the Intern Health Study, and HIS is the one tag that matches no study. (2) The list runs in Supplementary Table 1's row order, skipping IHS, Army STARRS, Genes & Health, DCHS and DNHS, and then appends exactly those five, with HIS in place of IHS. (3) No other ancestry abbreviation (AFR, EAS, SAS) was entered as a cohort, and the Catalog records ancestry separately. The Intern Health Study contributed East Asian, African and South Asian participants and no Hispanic ones, so HIS cannot be an IHS subset either. Merge into E533 (IHS, Intern Health Study): add HIS as an acronym, since the GWAS Catalog uses it however garbled, and use GCST90328131 with the quote above as E533's GWAS example (E533 has no GWAS study of its own). For E533's definition: a prospective cohort study, run from the University of Michigan, of physicians starting their first year of residency (interns) at many US institutions, with a parallel arm in Shanghai and Beijing, China, since 2016, who report depressive symptoms (PHQ-9) before and quarterly during internship (PMID:35581251, PMC9112267; PMID:37166801); countries United States and China. If the curator finds the transposition too uncertain, the fallback is 'not a cohort' (the ancestry-group reading), never a new cohort.

Tier D (D551), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: a generic country-based control-group label among a templated set of national case/control tags in a multinational sCJD GWAS. One of a templated set of nationality+status tags on GCST90001389 (Dutch/French/German/Italian/Spanish/UK/US controls; German/Other/UK/US sCJD cases), like the instructions' own 'UK controls' example. P1's abstract does not name it; no other evidence was gathered. Checked 2026-09-23: Verdict right, reasoning now sourced. 'US controls' is one of seven per-country control groups the GWAS Catalog made from this sporadic CJD GWAS's design: 'Control data was obtained from publicly available datasets matched for country' (PMC8220892), and the preprint says 'Control samples were chosen from genotype datasets available for biomedical research derived from countries that matched those providing case samples', with the sources only in its Supplementary Table 1. The tag names a country-matched selection of public genotype data, not a sample with a name of its own, consistent with the pilot's verdict on 'UK controls' (D579). Which US datasets were used is listed only in the unreadable Supplementary Table 1 / appendix. If it turned out to be a single named study already in COHO, the curator could put the tag on that term as an acronym; nothing readable suggests so.

Tier D (D552), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: a generic country-based case-group label ('German sCJD cases') among the same templated set of national case/control tags as D551 and D556. Cases were 'identified at national CJD referral centres' generically (D552.5); D552.27 is only a bibliography title citing an earlier 'large German case-control study', not naming a specific registry or cohort. No unit gives a named German sCJD collection. Checked 2026-09-23: Verdict right; the note's evidence was thin, and the preprint settles it. The definition described the GWAS paper's own subset ('recruited from 2013': its 1,150 participants collected in 2013-2017) and left out who runs the study, where exactly and why. The GWAS cites a Shika study paper for the cohort (its reference 25, PMID:29207502), and its 'SHIP cohort study' has the Shika study's ethics approval (GWAS: 'protocol code, 1491; date of approval, December 18, 2013'; Shika study: 'protocol code 1491 and date of approval: 18 December 2013', PMC9407879). So SHIP is Kanazawa University's Shika study, 'a longitudinal community-based observational study that has been conducted since 2011 among the residents of Shika town' (PMC9139339), of residents aged 40 and over in four model districts who answer a self-administered questionnaire and undergo a comprehensive health examination, run 'to investigate approaches that prevent lifestyle-related diseases' (PMC8336805). The definition is rewritten from those papers. The draft had no synonyms; the study's other names are added: 'Shikamachi Health Improvement Practice genome cohort' (abstract of PMID:33967275), 'SHIP genome cohort study' (the GWAS acknowledgements), 'Shika study'/'SHIKA study', and 'Shika-machi Super Preventive Health Examination', the name its gut-microbiome papers use for the same survey (PMID:36118024; the sister paper PMID:32984370 calls it the Shika study, ethics approval No. 1491). SHIP is also the acronym of the Study of Health in Pomerania (COHO:0000202, which carries SHIP): both terms need the shared-acronym editor note, e.g. 'The acronym SHIP also denotes Study of Health in Pomerania (COHO:0000202); this term is the Shikamachi Health Improvement Practice genome cohort study in Shika Town, Japan.' The Shika study name also covers a survey of Shika schoolchildren aged 6 to 15 run under a different ethics protocol ('The Shika study protocols were approved by the Kanazawa University Ethical Committee (No.1464).', PMC6081878); this term is the adult study with blood and DNA. If COHO prefers the most-used name, 'Shika study' could be the label, with the SHIP names as synonyms. No other COHO term or review name for it (searched Shika, SHIP, Kanazawa).

(https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC9516613/fullTextXML). The paper builds its controls from existing genotype datasets matched to the case countries, and neither the paper nor its preprint names a study called 'Spanish controls'; the tag is the Spanish slice of that pooled control set, not a named cohort. example title: Genome-wide association analyses of breast cancer in women of African ancestry identify new susceptibility loci and improve risk prediction.

definition: A consortium for genetic studies of breast cancer in women of African ancestry that pools whole-genome sequencing data, new Multi-Ethnic Genotyping Array genotypes and existing genotype data on breast cancer cases and controls from more than 20 studies in the United States, Africa and Barbados, among them the samples of the AMBER, ROOT, AABC and GAME-ON OncoArray consortia, for genome-wide association analyses and polygenic risk prediction.
location quote: In brief, we analyzed whole-genome sequenced and high-density genotyped data from 18,034 female cases with breast cancer and 22,104 female controls of African ancestry from 26 studies participating in the AABCG, with 85.3% of participants from the United States and 14.7% from the African continent and Barbados. || The GBHS is a population-based case-control study conducted in Accra and Kumasi, Ghana || The NBCS is an ongoing case-control study of breast cancer in Ibadan, Nigeria || The WAABCS is a hospital-based case-control study originally started in Nigeria in 1998 and was expanded to Uganda and Cameroon in 2011 with the same questionnaires and protocol || The BNCS is a population-based case-control study of incident breast and prostate cancer in the predominantly African population of Barbados, West Indies
note: Tier E (E008), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P3 (PGS Catalog papers: evaluation/score development): AABCG denotes the whole consortium/pooled dataset. P4 (found by name): a separate paper also naming the AABCG consortium directly. Name spelling varies across papers ('Genetic' vs 'Genetics', hyphenated 'African-ancestry'); synonyms capture the main variants. MEGA here means the Multi-Ethnic Genotyping Array platform, not COHO:0000122's Dutch thrombosis cohort. TCGA-BRCA and the WECARE Study are separate external validation cohorts, not part of AABCG. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type (aggregation) and example were right. The definition's last clause ('with data collection and ethical approval handled by each participating institution') is administrative. The definition also left out that AABCG is partly a consortium of consortia (its Supplementary Note describes the AMBER, ROOT, AABC and GAME-ON OncoArray consortia as data components) and what the pooled data are used for (GWAS and PRS development). Ghana (GBHS), Nigeria (NBCS and WAABCS), and Uganda and Cameroon (WAABCS) now replace it, and the Barbados quote now comes from the Barbados study itself. The same Supplementary Note calls the consortium 'The African American Breast Cancer Genetic (AABCG) consortium', and the main text calls it the 'African-ancestry Breast Cancer Genetic (AABCG) consortium'; both forms are added as synonyms. Its Supplementary Note (PMID:38741014, MOESM1) lists members that are already COHO terms, which the curator can link with hasCohort from this aggregation: the consortia AABC (COHO:0000989) and ROOT (COHO:0001033). African American Breast Cancer Epidemiology and Risk (AMBER) consortium ...'), so quotes for those links must be taken from the study paragraphs. The synonym 'African American Breast Cancer Genetic consortium' is close to, but not the same as, COHO:0000989's label 'African American Breast Cancer Consortium' (AABC, a component of AABCG); no editor note is needed because no string is shared. parent quote: Australian Asthma Genetics Consortium (AAGC) Australian Asthma Genetics Consortium AAGC European Australia Population-based and case-control studies
note: Tier E (E009), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because no gathered unit spelled out the name. The PGS Catalog's name, 'Australian Asthma Genetics Consortium', is the consortium's own: the 2011 Lancet asthma GWAS was published 'for the Australian Asthma Genetics Consortium', which was 'supported by the Australian National Health and Medical Research Council (613627)'. It is an aggregation, not one uniform sample. The 2014 asthma-with-hay-fever GWAS says the AAGC data were drawn from four studies ('Cases and control subjects were drawn from 4 studies: the Queensland Institute of Medical Research (n = 921), the Lung Institute of Western Australia (n = 475), the Busselton Health Study (n = 445), and the Tasmanian Longitudinal Health Study (n = 296).'). The 2017 PGS paper's subset came from QIMR, LIWA and TAHS, and TAGC's study table describes AAGC as 'Population-based and case-control studies'. The country was right, but its quote was an author-contribution line listing people's initials; it is replaced. The drafted example quote was two headings run together ('AAGC (n=2,435)' and 'Sample ascertainment and phenotype definition.'). It is replaced by the AAGC row of the TAGC study table (PMID:29273806, the source GWAS of PGS000799), which also supports membership of the Trans-National Asthma Genetic Consortium (COHO:0001419). The acronym is used in two scopes. In the 2011 Lancet paper, 'the Australian Asthma Genetics Consortium (AAGC) cohort (n=1,810); the Busselton Health Study cohort (n=1,230); and the Queensland Institute of Medical Research (QIMR) GWAS cohort (n=4,157).' are three separate genotyping projects of one 'Australian GWAS'. From 2014 on, 'AAGC' names that whole Australian GWAS dataset ('A total of 2,669 case subjects of European ancestry with physician-diagnosed asthma and 4,528 control subjects of European ancestry without asthma were genotyped for a recent GWAS of asthma described in detail elsewhere.'), and that is what the PGS id means in all five PGS papers. Members to link with hasCohort from this aggregation: the Busselton Health Study (COHO:0000389), and the tier-E names LIWA (E637, Lung Institute of Western Australia) and TLHS (E1113, Tasmanian Longitudinal Health Study) if minted, each from the JACI 2014 sentence above. The QIMR part is an institution's samples, which the earlier review ruled not a cohort (tag QIMR). The TAGC check already listed AAGC (E009) as a TAGC member candidate. The same TAGC table row serves as country, parent and example evidence; the curator may prefer PMID:29083406, whose AAGC funding sentence names only the acronym, as the example.

Tier E (E010), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The id does not denote a cohort. 'Aalborg University Hospital blood bank' is a hospital department's blood bank. In its only paper (PMID:36303976, an endometriosis PRS evaluation), the id labels an unnamed, ad hoc control group: 'The control group consisted of Danish blood donors from the Aalborg University Hospital blood bank, Aalborg, Denmark, and were age-matched women without a diagnose of N80 (n = 348).' and 'Control samples were anonymized prior to genotyping.' The group has no name, design or follow-up of its own, and no other paper uses it. The drafted definition, 'a blood bank ... from which population controls were drawn for a genetic association study of endometriosis', describes the institution plus one paper's use, which is the pattern the earlier review rules not a cohort (institution tags such as RUNMC, SDCC, CCF and UAB, and generic control groups such as 'UK controls'). Nothing links these donors to the Danish Blood Donor Study (COHO:0000475): the paper does not name it, and its controls were anonymized before genotyping. The paper's other samples are the Danish Twin Registry (COHO:0000490, DTR) and UK Biobank. The companion id Aarhus (E011, another batch) was checked as the PRACTICAL prostate cancer study, with this endometriosis case series noted there as an unnamed second meaning. The study's own row in Supplementary Table 1 of the OncoArray GWAS (PMID:29892016, 'Brief overview and details of studies included in the prostate cancer OncoArray project') gives its design ('Hospital-based, Retrospective, Observational'), its cases ('Patients treated for prostate adenocarcinoma at Department of Urology, Aarhus University Hospital, Skejby (Aarhus, Denmark)') and its controls ('Age-matched males treated for myocardial infarction or undergoing coronary angioplasty, but with no prostate cancer diagnosis based on information retrieved from the Danish Cancer Register and the Danish Cause of Death Register.'); the definition now says so. Tier E (E012), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. definition: A hospital-based breast cancer case-control study run from the Netherlands Cancer Institute – Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Hospital (NKI-AVL) in Amsterdam, whose cases are women diagnosed with breast cancer before age 50 (operable invasive cancers diagnosed in 1970–1994 in four Dutch hospitals and, for the iCOGS and OncoArray genotyping, patients diagnosed in 1995–2011 at the NKI-AVL) and whose controls are women recruited through the Sanquin blood bank. A familial arm, ABCS-F, adds breast cancer patients without BRCA1/2 mutations from the NKI-AVL family cancer clinic, and the study contributes to the Breast Cancer Association Consortium.

parent quote: BCAC DACC approval is required to access data from the ABCFS, ABCS, ABCTB, BBCC, BBCS, BCEES, BCFR-NY, BCFR-PA, BCFR-UT, BCINIS, BSUCH, CBCS, CECILE, CGPS, CTS, DIETCOMPLYF, ESTHER, GC-HBOC, GENICA, GEPARSIXTO, GESBC, HABCS, HCSC, HEBCS, HMBCS, HUBCS, KARBAC, KBCP, LMBC, MABCS, MARIE, MBCSG, MCBCS, MISS, MMHS, MTLGEBCS, NC-BCFR, OFBCR, ORIGO, pKARMA, POSH, PREFACE, RBCS, SKKDKFZS, SUCCESSB, SUCCESSC, SZBCS, TNBCC, UCIBCS, UKBGS and UKOPS studies (Supplementary Table 1).
note: Tier E (E013), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ABCS among many BCAC-pooled datasets/abbreviations (supplement heading list). P2: ABCS as one of the named studies requiring BCAC DACC approval, and separately credited/funded ('The ABCS study was supported by...'). P3-P6: not evidenced. Identity rests on a tag-name pair in a spreadsheet export (E013.19-20) plus 'the ABCS study' (E013.10, E013.13); no unit gives ABCS's own design, dates or recruitment, so the definition covers only country and BCAC membership. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country, BCAC membership and example were right; the definition said only that it is a Dutch breast-cancer study in BCAC because the drafter had no design text. The study's own rows in BCAC tables give it: PredictCBC-2.0 Additional file 2 (PMID:36271417): 'Pre-iCOGS: All breast cancer patients (with operable, invasive mammacarcinoma) aged <50 years and diagnosed from 1970-1994 in four Dutch hospitals.' and 'iCOGS/OncoArray: Breast cancer patients diagnosed before age 50 in 1995-2011 at the Netherlands Cancer Insitute - Antoni van Leeuwenhoek hospital (NKI-AVL).'; Mavaddat 2015 Supplementary Table 1 (PMID:25855707), whose ABCS row also covers '(ABCS-F) All non-BRCA1/2 breast cancer cases from the family cancer clinic of the NKI-AVL' and gives the controls as 'Population-based cohort of women recruited through the Sanquin blood bank, all ages.'; and Blows 2010 Table 1 (PMID:20520800), which calls its case ascertainment hospital-based. The country quote was the blood bank's acknowledgement, not recruitment; it is replaced by the recruitment row. The case series differ between sources: Blows 2010 dates the early cases 1974–1994 and adds familial non-BRCA1/2 cases under 50; Mavaddat 2015 gives the genotyped cases as diagnosed in 2003–2009 at the NKI-AVL; PredictCBC-2.0 gives 1970–1994 and 1995–2011. The definition follows the latest, most complete description (PredictCBC-2.0) and names the familial arm. ABCS-F (E014) is that familial arm and should be its sub-cohort. No COHO term or review name duplicates ABCS; D484 (NKI, the Netherlands Cancer Institute as a recruitment site) is unrelated.

label: Amsterdam Breast Cancer Study – Familial
other synonyms: Amsterdam Breast Cancer Study - Familial
example title: Genome-wide association study identifies 32 novel breast cancer susceptibility loci from overall and subtype-specific analyses.
example quote: ABCS-F Amsterdam Breast Cancer Study – Familial
definition: The familial arm of the Amsterdam Breast Cancer Study, whose cases are breast cancer patients of any age without a pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation who were counselled and tested from 1995 at the family cancer clinic of the Netherlands Cancer Institute – Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Hospital in Amsterdam, and whose controls are healthy women from the general population recruited through the blood bank. The Breast Cancer Association Consortium lists it as a study separate from the main ABCS.
location quote: The samples included in this study were from two Dutch breast cancer case-control studies: RBCS and ABCS-F.
parent quote: Breast cancer patients diagnosed before age 50 in 2003-2009 at the NKI-AVL; and (ABCS-F) All non-BRCA1/2 breast cancer cases from the family cancer clinic of the NKI-AVL tested in the period 1995-2009; all ages and diagnosed with breast cancer in 1965-2008.
note: Tier E (E014), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ABCS-F listed as its own BCAC DACC-covered study, separate from ABCS, with the tag-name pair confirming the expansion. P2: not evidenced for ABCS-F specifically. Only a tag-name mapping and a BCAC DACC listing support this row; no unit states its design, dates, or relation to the Amsterdam Breast Cancer Study (E013/ABCS) despite the name, so isSubCohortOf was not asserted -- a researcher should check. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity was right, but the draft did not know what the familial study is or how it relates to ABCS, and gave the country from the name, which names only Amsterdam. Its design is in an open-access paper that uses it (PMID:27424772, HOXB13 in Dutch breast cancer): cases are 'female breast cancer patients of all ages ... without a pathogenic BRCA1/2 mutation or unclassified variant, who were counselled in the Family Cancer Clinic and diagnosed and/or treated with cancer in the Antoni van Leeuwenhoek hospital in the period 1995–2012', and 'ABCS-F controls ... are healthy women of all ages ... from the general population and were recruited through the blood bank.' The ABCS row of Mavaddat 2015 Supplementary Table 1 (PMID:25855707) lists '(ABCS-F) All non-BRCA1/2 breast cancer cases from the family cancer clinic of the NKI-AVL' within ABCS, so it is a sub-cohort of the Amsterdam Breast Cancer Study (E013). The draft's example quote was the bare name; it now pairs the tag with the name. Keep the draft's BCAC membership too: ABCS-F is named separately in the BCAC data-access list ('BCAC DACC approval is required to access data from the 2SISTER, ABCS, ABCS-F, ABCTB, ...', https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-020-0609-2, a subscription page), so BCAC (COHO:0000020) should list it with hasCohort as well as ABCS. The label keeps the en dash of the BCAC table; the PGS Catalog's spelling with a hyphen is added as a synonym. The HOXB13 paper calls ABCS-F 'the Amsterdam Breast Cancer Study (ABCS-F)', confirming it is run as part of ABCS.

label: Australian Breast Cancer Tissue Bank
example title: Genome-wide association study identifies 32 novel breast cancer susceptibility loci from overall and subtype-specific analyses.
example quote: The Australian Breast Cancer Tissue Bank (ABCTB) was supported by the National Health and Medical Research Council of Australia, The Cancer Institute NSW and the National Breast Cancer Foundation.
definition: A breast cancer biobank, headquartered at the Westmead Institute for Medical Research of the University of Sydney, that since 2005 has collected tumour tissue, blood and linked clinical and follow-up data from consenting patients with breast cancer at collection sites across Australia and provides them for research. It contributes breast cancer cases to the Breast Cancer Association Consortium.
location quote: ABCTB collection sites where donors are identified, consent obtained, and specimens collected and processed for initial storage are located across Australia.
parent quote: BCAC DACC approval is required to access data from the ABCFS, ABCS, ABCTB, BBCC, BBCS, BCEES, BCFR-NY, BCFR-PA, BCFR-UT, BCINIS, BSUCH, CBCS, CECILE, CGPS, CTS, DIETCOMPLYF, ESTHER, GC-HBOC, GENICA, GEPARSIXTO, GESBC, HABCS, HCSC, HEBCS, HMBCS, HUBCS, KARBAC, KBCP, LMBC, MABCS, MARIE, MBCSG, MCBCS, MISS, MMHS, MTLGEBCS, NC-BCFR, OFBCR, ORIGO, pKARMA, POSH, PREFACE, RBCS, SKKDKFZS, SUCCESSB, SUCCESSC, SZBCS, TNBCC, UCIBCS, UKBGS and UKOPS studies (Supplementary Table 1).
note: Tier E (E015), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1,P2: ABCTB as a contributing/validation study in BCAC-wide breast-cancer PRS papers, its Investigators listed as a group author. P7-P11 (found by name): the biobank itself and its operations, directly described; P11 uses the variant acronym 'AUBC'. BCAC (COHO:0000020) isn't in this name's own candidate list, but E015.43 names it exactly as for ABCS/ABCS-F elsewhere in this batch, so memberOf is asserted -- flagging the source for a checker. 'AUBC' (E015.62) added as a second acronym. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country and BCAC membership were right. The definition described how the biobank is managed (hub-and-spoke model) instead of who is in it; it now says whose samples and data it holds, where it is based and its role in BCAC. 'AUBC' is not an acronym of the biobank: it is one paper's label for a triple-negative subset drawn from it ('The Australian Breast Cancer Tissue Bank (AUBC) cohort (n = 318)', PMID:36705810), neither the biobank's own acronym nor a database tag, so it is dropped. The example quote was an author affiliation, which does not show that the paper used the biobank; it is replaced by a statement from a paper that did. The BCAC row says ABCTB contributes cases without controls, but Mavaddat 2019's validation table lists 74 ABCTB controls, so the definition says only that it contributes cases. A WIMR news page names it 'the Australian Breast Cancer Tissue Bank headquartered at Westmead Millennium Institute' (the institute's former name). No COHO term or review name duplicates it.

label: Anonymous Blood Donor Cohort
other synonyms: Anonymous blood donor cohort|Anonymous Blood Donor Cohort (3D Population Controls)|3D Population Controls
example title: Polygenic prediction of body mass index and obesity through the life course and across ancestries.
example quote: DKctrl / 3D Anonymous Blood Donor Cohort (3D Population Controls)
definition: A population-based sample of anonymous Danish blood donors used as population controls in genetic studies, contributed under the abbreviation DKctrl, with self-reported anthropometry, to the GIANT consortium's genome-wide meta-analyses of height and body mass index. The study its contributors cite for it recruited its healthy controls among blood donors of the Danish Blood Donor Corps in the Copenhagen area.
location quote: The healthy controls subjects were recruited among 15,000 blood-donors from the Danish Blood Donor Corps in the Copenhagen area.
note: Tier E (E016), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because its only evidence was the name in one supplement. The GIANT height GWAS (Yengo et al. 2022, PMID:36224396) describes the same study in its Supplementary Table 1 (read from the xlsx in the Europe PMC supplement bundle of PMC9605867): study 'DKctrl', full name 'Anonymous blood donor cohort', design 'Population-based', ancestry 'European (Danish)', anthropometry 'Self-report', reference 'PMID: 17849003', ethics 'Danish Scientific Committees and the Danish Data Protection Agency'; its other tables say 'The following studies are omitted from the table as descriptive data was not made available: Wake Forest and DKctrl.' The cited paper (PMID:17849003, a Danish schizophrenia case-control study) recruited its controls among Copenhagen-area blood donors with approval from the same two bodies. The PGS paper's table gives the study's abbreviations as 'DKctrl / 3D'. The draft's label and acronym stand; the verdict and the rest of the record are new. Identity rests on the GIANT tables; no paper describes DKctrl itself (GIANT reports that its descriptive data were not made available), so the definition says only what the tables and the cited reference say. What '3D' stands for could not be found; it is kept as an acronym because the PGS paper's table lists it as the study's abbreviation, but a curator may prefer to drop it. The sample predates and differs from the Danish Blood Donor Study (COHO:0000475, recruited nationwide from 2010) and from the Aalborg University Hospital blood bank controls (E010). GIANT (COHO:0000558) has no curated members in COHO, so no parent is given. No other COHO term or review name matches.

input name: Australian Imaging, Biomarker & Lifestyle Flagship Study of Ageing
label: Australian Imaging, Biomarker & Lifestyle Flagship Study of Ageing

label: Adelaide Blood Pools
other synonyms: Adelaide Blood pool|Adelaide population-based cohort in Blood pooling design
example quote: The four cohorts in comparison are the combined Australian twin cohorts (AU), the UK twin cohort (UK), the Blue Mountains population-based cohort in DNA pooling design (DNA), and the Adelaide population-based cohort in Blood pooling design (BLOOD).
definition: A population-based sample of unrelated adults from Adelaide, Australia, with measured central corneal thickness, whose members in the thinnest and thickest fifths of the distribution had equal volumes of whole blood pooled before DNA extraction and genotyped as case and control pools in a genome-wide association study of central corneal thickness.
location quote: The second cohort, based on a blood pooling design [26] was collected from Adelaide, Australia.
note: Tier E (E018), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft had no evidence: no PGS Catalog score or GWAS Catalog study uses ABP. A Europe PMC search for the name finds one paper, the central corneal thickness (CCT) GWAS of Lu et al. 2010 (PMID:20485516, PLoS Genet, open access), whose Table 3 has an 'Adelaide Blood pool' column and whose methods say 'The second cohort, based on a blood pooling design [26] was collected from Adelaide, Australia.': 530 unrelated people, of whom the thinnest and thickest fifths for CCT were pooled ('Equal quantity (100 µL) of whole blood was aliquoted shortly after venesection from each individual.') and genotyped as case and control pools. The identification rests on the name: 'Adelaide Blood pool' occurs only in PMID:20485516, and the PGS Catalog entry has no score that would show which paper it came from. If the curator does not want a term for a sample used in one GWAS, 'not a cohort' is defensible; the draft's guess (an Adelaide blood resource) was in the right place. The other pooled cohort of that paper is the Blue Mountains Eye Study (COHO:0001061). The ethics statement names the Flinders Medical Centre committee, but the paper does not say where in Adelaide participants were recruited, so the definition does not either. No COHO term or review name matches.

label: Aneurysm Consortium
other synonyms: The Aneurysm Consortium|Aneurysm Consortium AAA GWAS dataset|Aneurysm Consortium AAA GWAS|Aneurysm Consortium GWAS|Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Consortium
example title: Genome-wide association meta-analysis identifies risk loci for abdominal aortic aneurysm and highlights PCSK9 as a therapeutic target.
example quote: These two sets of weights were then used to calculate PRS in three external validation cohorts, two with control groups representative of the general population (UK Aneurysm Growth Study-UK Biobank (UKAGS-UKB) and Aneurysm Consortium-Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (AC-WTCCC)) and one representative of populations with cardiovascular disease (Second manifestations of ARTerial disease (SMART)).
definition: A consortium of investigators in the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand formed to carry out a genome-wide association study of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Its GWAS dataset pools AAA cases with DNA from eight centres in those countries and from the UK Small Aneurysm Trial, recruited from inpatients, outpatient clinics and population screening programmes, and compares them with Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium 2 controls from the 1958 British Birth Cohort and the UK National Blood Service.
location quote: Aneurysm Consortium (AC), cases of AAA together with available DNA recruited in eight centers in the UK, Australia, and New Zealand and also samples from the United Kingdom Small Aneurysm Trial from inpatient populations, outpatient clinics, or population screening programs in the participating centers.
note: Tier E (E019), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft had no evidence. The name is the Aneurysm Consortium's GWAS dataset: the AAAgen GWAS (PMID:37845353, a PGS Catalog publication for PGS003972/PGS003973) says 'The Aneurysm Consortium AAA GWAS 33 had not met QC criteria for inclusion in the discovery analysis but was available for validation of polygenic risk scores.' and describes it as 'Aneurysm Consortium (AC), cases of AAA together with available DNA recruited in eight centers in the UK, Australia, and New Zealand and also samples from the United Kingdom Small Aneurysm Trial ...'. The consortium announced itself in 2008 ('an international group of investigators from Australia, New Zealand and the UK have formed “The Aneurysm Consortium” and recently obtained funding to carry out a GWAS of AAA', PMID:18621558) and published the GWAS in 2011 (PMID:22055160), with WTCCC2 controls: 'A genome-wide discovery study was performed by comparing data from 1866 cases with AAA and 5435 unscreened controls from the WTCCC2 study consisting of samples from the 1958 British Birth Cohort and from the UK National Blood Service.'. Typed as an aggregation because it is a consortium that pooled case collections from eight centres and a trial; if the curator prefers to treat the pooled GWAS case-control set as one sample, as the NZ AAA Genetics Study (COHO:0001386) was, the same record can be minted as a cohort. Candidate members: the UK Small Aneurysm Trial (E1167 in this review; quote above). Its GWAS controls came from the WTCCC2 1958 British Birth Cohort (COHO:0000207) and UK National Blood Service (COHO:0000347) samples, which are the dataset's controls rather than consortium members. The later International Aneurysm Consortium (PMID:27899403) and the AAAgen consortium are different, larger aggregations; neither is in COHO. The PGS Catalog's evaluation PSS011197 of PGS003972 is this dataset but is tagged WTCCC (COHO:0000182). No COHO term or review name duplicates it; the UK Aneurysm Growth Study (COHO:0001427) is a different study.

label: Autism Case-Control cohort
other synonyms: Autism CaseControl cohort|ACC cohort
example quote: We assembled an Autism Case-Control (ACC) cohort by collecting 859 ASD cases (from a total of 1,246 ACC cases, parents, and siblings) of European ancestry, and 1,409 healthy controls.
definition: A case-control collection for genome-wide studies of autism spectrum disorders assembled at the Center for Applied Genomics of the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, combining people with autism spectrum disorders from several US sites, diagnosed with the Autism Diagnostic Interview and Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule and from simplex and multiplex families (with some of their parents and siblings), with control subjects without autism spectrum disorders from the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia.
location quote: To boost power for identifying these associations, we examined an Autism Case-Control cohort (ACC cohort, Table 1), comprising 1,453 subjects with ASDs from several US sites, and 7,070 control subjects without ASDs from the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, who were also genotyped on the same platform.
note: Tier E (E020), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft had no evidence: no PGS Catalog score or GWAS Catalog study uses ACC. The name is the Autism Case-Control (ACC) cohort of the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, the case-control discovery cohort of two 2009 Nature papers from its Center for Applied Genomics: the 5p14.1 autism GWAS (PMID:19404256: 'we examined an Autism Case-Control cohort (ACC cohort, Table 1), comprising 1,453 subjects with ASDs from several US sites, and 7,070 control subjects without ASDs from the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia'; 'The subjects with ASDs in this cohort were diagnosed using the ADI and ADOS tools.') and the autism CNV study (PMID:19404257: 'We assembled an Autism Case-Control (ACC) cohort ...'; 'Fifty-four per cent were from simplex families, the rest were from multiplex families.'). Identified from the name, which matches these papers exactly ('Autism Case-Control (ACC) cohort'); the PGS Catalog entry has no score to confirm which paper it came from. Its controls came from the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, presumably through the Center for Applied Genomics Biobank (COHO:0000489), but its cases came from other US sites, so it is not asserted as a sub-cohort of that biobank. It is distinct from AGRE (E042 in this review), the family cohort analysed beside it. No COHO term or review name duplicates it.

input name: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes
label: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes
example title: Genetic Tools for Coronary Risk Assessment in Type 2 Diabetes: A Cohort Study From the ACCORD Clinical Trial.
example quote: We also evaluated the extent to which these genetic markers improve the prediction of incident MCE when added to conventional cardiovascular risk factors and assessed whether a genetic risk score (GRS) derived from these SNPs could identify subsets of patients with type 2 diabetes with different responses to intensive glucose, blood pressure, and lipid control in the Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD) trial.
definition: A randomised, multicentre, double 2×2 factorial trial cohort of middle-aged and older adults with type 2 diabetes at high risk of cardiovascular events because of existing cardiovascular disease or additional risk factors, recruited in 2001–2005 through seven clinical networks in the United States and Canada with funding from the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute. All participants were randomised to intensive or standard glycaemic control and, in two sub-trials, to intensive or standard blood-pressure control or to fenofibrate or placebo added to simvastatin, to test whether these strategies reduce major cardiovascular events.
location quote: A total of 10,251 participants with type 2 diabetes were recruited from seven clinical networks in the U.S. and Canada between 2001 and 2005 and randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive intensive glucose-lowering treatment, aiming for an HbA1c level below 6%, or to standard treatment, aiming for an HbA1c level between 7.0% and 7.9%.
note: Tier E (E021), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ACCORD and ORIGIN as two distinct trial cohorts in one GRS study. P2: ACCORD trial participants (BP PRS). P3-P4: NEJM results papers for ACCORD's blood-pressure and lipid sub-trials. P5-P6: ACCORD's own genetic-predictors and design/methods papers. P8-P10: ACCORD as one of several diabetes outcome trials. P11: pooled with SPRINT-MIND as ACCORD-MIND. P12: ACCORD and its Follow-up study. P13: ACCORD-BP arm alongside SPRINT. ACCORD-BP, ACCORD-Lipid and ACCORD-MIND are sub-trial tags, not kept as ACCORD's own acronyms. P1 also names ORIGIN, a distinct trial (COHO:0000133), not this cohort. No country given: only the NHLBI funder/repository ties it to the US, which the rules exclude. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, example and the absence of a parent are right. The definition left out where, when and by whom participants were recruited, which P1's open-access Methods state (seven clinical networks in the U.S. and Canada, 2001–2005; NHLBI contracts), and it misdescribed the lipid sub-trial as intensive lipid lowering against standard care: it compared fenofibrate with placebo on a background of simvastatin. 'Follow-up continuing to 2009' was the design paper's expected completion date written in 2007, a plan rather than a fact, and is dropped. The countries are not only implied by the funder: P1 states that participants were recruited in the U.S. and Canada, so both are asserted with that quote. ACCORD-BP, ACCORD-Lipid and ACCORD-MIND name sub-trials or sub-studies and are rightly not added as acronyms of the whole trial. No GWAS Catalog study carries an ACCORD tag. ACCORD is not in COHO or elsewhere in this review.

label: Anglo-Cardiff Collaborative Trial
other synonyms: Anglo Cardiff Collaborative Trial
example title: Normal vascular aging: differential effects on wave reflection and aortic pulse wave velocity: the Anglo-Cardiff Collaborative Trial (ACCT).
example quote: Normal vascular aging: differential effects on wave reflection and aortic pulse wave velocity: the Anglo-Cardiff Collaborative Trial (ACCT).
definition: A population of adults in East Anglia and Wales, United Kingdom, selected at random from local general practice lists and open-access cardiovascular risk assessment clinics and studied by investigators in Cambridge and Cardiff, comprising healthy people as well as people with cardiovascular risk factors or disease, whose peripheral and central blood pressure, wave reflection and aortic pulse wave velocity were measured, with questionnaires and blood samples, to study vascular ageing, arterial stiffness and central blood pressure across the adult lifespan.
location quote: Subjects were drawn from the ACCT (Anglo‐Cardiff Collaborative Trial) population, which consists of >12 000 individuals, selected at random from local general practice lists and open‐access Cardiovascular Risk Assessment Clinics across East Anglia and Wales.
note: Tier E (E022), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ACCT's own naming paper (vascular ageing, wave reflection, aortic PWV). P2: 'Anglo-Cardiff Collaborative Trial II', an expanded/later analysis under the same name family. P3, P5, P6: subjects/subsets drawn from ACCT for specific sub-analyses. P4: a cross-sectional ACCT analysis giving the 18-92 age range. 'Anglo-Cardiff Collaborative Trial II' (P2) may be a distinct second-phase cohort or an expanded continuation of the same one; evidence doesn't say, so not folded in as a synonym -- a researcher should check. Country UK from 'Cardiff' in the name only. Triage's 'aggregation?' hint isn't supported: this is one trial population, not a consortium. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, synonym, acronym, type and example are right, and so is the country. The definition described one paper's subset: 'aged 18 to 92' is the 5,371 people free of cardiovascular disease and medication selected for PMID:40879028, whereas the ACCT population (more than 12,000 people in that paper's words) also includes people with diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, smoking or cardiovascular disease, and ACCT II analysed people aged 18 to 101 (PMID:18426997). It also left out how participants were found (at random from general practice lists and open-access cardiovascular risk assessment clinics in East Anglia and Wales) and by whom (the Cambridge and Cardiff investigators). The country need not rest on the name alone: PMID:40879028 (open access) places recruitment in East Anglia and Wales, so that quote is given. 'Anglo-Cardiff Collaborative Trial II' (PMID:18426997) and 'ACCT III' (PMID:20696989) are titles of later analyses of the same, growing ACCT population rather than separate cohorts, so they are not new terms; they could be added as synonyms if paper-series names are wanted. Despite 'Trial' in the name, ACCT is an observational cross-sectional study population, not an intervention trial, and it is one study run jointly from Cambridge and Cardiff, not an aggregation. Author lists also use 'Anglo-Cardiff Collaboration Trial Investigators' for its investigator group. No GWAS Catalog study carries an ACCT tag.

label: Alcoholic Cirrhosis GWAS
example title: Association of Genetic Variation With Cirrhosis: A Multi-Trait Genome-Wide Association and Gene-Environment Interaction Study.
example quote: Individuals with cirrhosis were identified in two prospective cohorts (UK Biobank and Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study), a medical center-based cohort (Vanderbilt BioVU) and two case-control studies from previously published genome wide association studies of alcohol-related cirrhosis.
definition: A genome-wide association study of alcohol-related cirrhosis in people of European descent that meta-analysed two case–control data sets, one from Germany and one from the United Kingdom, comparing patients with alcohol-related cirrhosis with drinking controls to find genetic risk loci for the disease; its discovery results were published in 2015 and its summary statistics have been reused by later studies of cirrhosis.
location quote: Quantile-quantile plot of the primary meta-analysis of the German and UK data sets.
note: Tier E (E023), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred for want of text; research settles what the id denotes. In its only paper, PMID:33310085 (PGS000726), ACG is not a phenotype subset but the 'two case-control studies from previously published genome wide association studies of alcohol-related cirrhosis' that the paper's Table 1 heads 'Buch et al. German cohort' and 'Buch et al. UK Cohort', used as summary-level statistics; the PGS Catalog's own sample description for PGS000726 calls them the 'Alcoholic cirrhosis GWAS German Cohort' and 'Alcoholic cirrhosis GWAS UK Cohort'. They are the discovery stage of the 2015 Nature Genetics GWAS of alcohol-related cirrhosis (PMID:26482880), whose free supplement describes 'the primary meta-analysis of the German and UK data sets' ('Discovery: Germany GWAS 1, United Kingdom GWAS 2'), and whose summary statistics page (TU Dresden) describes a meta-analysis of cases with alcohol-related cirrhosis and controls across 'cohort 1, cohort 2' (Germany, UK). A later open-access paper (PMID:38727677) calls it 'Buch and colleagues' cohort', of 'ALC cases and ... drinking controls'. The draft's example paper was right but had no quote; one is given. The data set has no name of its own: the label is the PGS Catalog's, which is the only name any source gives the whole; a curator may prefer a more specific descriptive label such as 'German and UK alcohol-related cirrhosis GWAS'. Typed as an aggregation because it is a meta-analysis of two separately collected case–control data sets from two countries ('GWAS 1' and 'GWAS 2', 'cohort 1, cohort 2'); neither data set has a name, so no members are proposed. If the curator prefers to treat the pooled GWAS sample as one case–control cohort, only the type changes. Not the same as D428 GenomALC (whose base GWAS in PMID:38727677 meta-analysed GenomALC-1 with these summary statistics, a separate study) or COHO:0000419 GALAXY. The authors include Swiss and Austrian investigators, so the 'German' data set may include some patients from neighbouring countries; only Germany and the UK are asserted, as the supplement names them.
