label: University of Manchester Longitudinal Study of Cognition in Normal Healthy Old Age
other synonyms: Age and Cognitive Performance Research Cohort|University of Manchester Age and Cognitive Performance Research Cohort|Manchester and Newcastle Age and Cognitive Performance Research Cohort|Manchester and Newcastle Longitudinal Studies of Cognitive Aging|Manchester and Newcastle Longitudinal Studies of Cognitive Ageing|Manchester Longitudinal Cognitive Ageing Cohort
example title: Amyloid-β and APOE genotype predict memory decline in cognitively unimpaired older individuals independently of Alzheimer's disease polygenic risk score.
example quote: [28] The PreclinAD study recruited participants from two sites: the Manchester and Newcastle Age and Cognitive Performance Research Cohort (ACPRC) in Manchester [29] and the Netherlands Twin Register (NTR) [30] in Amsterdam.
definition: A longitudinal cohort of healthy community-dwelling volunteers in middle and old age, recruited in Greater Manchester and Newcastle upon Tyne, England, between 1983 and the early 1990s by the University of Manchester's Age and Cognitive Performance Research Centre to chart trajectories of cognitive function in normal old age; participants took alternating batteries of cognitive tests every two years until 2003, with questionnaires on health and behaviour repeated until 2017. Blood was collected for DNA extraction, a Manchester subsample was physically examined and gave saliva, serum and plasma in 2003, and some participants donated their brains to the Manchester Brain Bank.
location quote: Recruitment took place in Newcastle and Greater Manchester between 1983 and 1992.
note: Tier E (E024), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ACPRC as one of two source cohorts (with NTR) from which EMIF-AD PreclinAD drew participants; names and locates ACPRC but doesn't otherwise describe it. P2 (PreclinAD's own design paper): same framing, giving PreclinAD's enrolment dates/criteria, not ACPRC's own. P3: NTR's, not ACPRC's, profile paper. Only known via its role as a source cohort for EMIF-AD PreclinAD (with NTR); no independent ACPRC profile/design paper is in the evidence, so purpose beyond 'age and cognitive performance' and any establishment date are unstated. PreclinAD's own Dec2014-Oct2017/age-60+ criteria describe PreclinAD's enrolment, not ACPRC generally, so left out. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, country, example and the absence of a COHO parent are right. The label is the PGS Catalog's shortened name: the cohort's profile paper, which PMID:36522743 itself cites for ACPRC (ref. 29), is 'The University of Manchester Longitudinal Study of Cognition in Normal Healthy Old Age, 1983 through 2003', and its investigators use that name and its acronym UMLCHA in recent papers, while genetics papers also call it 'The University of Manchester Age and Cognitive Performance Research Cohort (ACPRC)'. The draft missed that acronym and the other names. The definition restated the name and described the cohort through one later study's use of it (a source of PreclinAD participants), when open-access papers describe it fully: volunteers recruited by local advertisement in Greater Manchester and Newcastle from 1983 (to 1992 or 1993) by the University of Manchester Age and Cognitive Performance Research Centre, tested with alternating cognitive batteries every two years until 2003, blood taken for DNA, and brains donated to the Manchester Brain Bank. Davies et al. 2011 count Manchester and Newcastle as two of the five cohorts of the CAGES project (Cognitive Ageing Genetics in England and Scotland): 'The five cohorts within the CAGES project are the Lothian Birth Cohorts of 1921 and 1936 (LBC1921, LBC1936), the Aberdeen Birth Cohort 1936 (ABC1936), and the Manchester and Newcastle Longitudinal Studies of Cognitive Aging cohorts' (PMC3182557); CAGES is not in COHO or this review, so no parent is given; if it is minted, this term is its member. The two recruitment sites are one study under one programme and one profile paper, so one term is proposed rather than separate Manchester and Newcastle cohorts. The 1993 paper names the programmes 'The University of Manchester Age and Cognitive Performance Research Centre and North East Age Research Longitudinal Programmes', and one paper abbreviates the study 'UoM', left out as too generic. The Netherlands Twin Register (COHO:0000125), the other PreclinAD source, is a separate cohort. Also in the COGENT cognitive GWAS (PMID:28093568) as 'ACPRC Age and Cognitive Performance Research Cohort', but no GWAS Catalog study carries an ACPRC tag.

P1: 'American Cancer Society Prevention Study I' (CPS-I), examined 1959-1960 -- a different, earlier ACS cohort. P2: 'American Cancer Society Prevention Study (CPS-II)', matching this term. P1 names a distinct earlier study, 'American Cancer Society Prevention Study I' (examined 1959-60), i.e. CPS-I, not this term (CPS-II, enrolled 1982). Checked 2026-09-23: The verdict, the COHO ID and the names to add (ACS_c; 'American Cancer Society Prevention Study') are the best reading, but they rest on the name alone: the PGS Catalog lists ACS_c in its cohort list yet records no score, sample set or publication for it (REST cohort/ACS_c and the website search return nothing). The example should not be added: PMID:31768169 did not analyse the cohort, it only took published relative risks 'from the American Cancer Society Prevention Study (CPS-II)', and COHO:0000024 already has a paper example (PMID:37783704) and a GWAS Catalog example (GCST90102456), so a further paper example would break the one-example-per-resource rule. ACS_c is the Catalog's third 'ACS' id (ACS is the Australia Cancer Study; ACS_b the Amsterdam Cohort Studies, COHO:0000971), so it was created for a sample some publication labelled with the American Cancer Society's name; in genetic studies that sample is the CPS-II Nutrition Cohort, which COHO:0000024 already carries ('Cancer Prevention Study II (including the Nutrition cohort)', the PGS id CPSII). If a later Catalog release shows ACS_c used for CPS-3 or CPS-I, move the id and synonym to a term for that cohort. 'American Cancer Society Prevention Study II Nutrition Cohort' (PMC3092924) could also be added to COHO:0000024 as a synonym.

input name: Affective Center at St Goran Hospital, Stockholm
label: St. Göran Bipolar Project
other synonyms: St. Göran Project
example quote: Subjects were recruited from a long-term naturalistic study of bipolar disorder, the St. Göran Bipolar Project, at the bipolar outpatient unit at the Northern Stockholm psychiatric clinic in Stockholm, Sweden.
definition: A longitudinal naturalistic cohort of outpatients with bipolar disorder, launched in 2005 by the Karolinska Institutet and the St. Göran bipolar outpatient clinic (the Affective Center) of Northern Stockholm Psychiatry in Stockholm, Sweden, with a second centre in Gothenburg from 2009, which consecutively enrols patients treated at these clinics, with age- and sex-matched population controls randomly selected by Statistics Sweden. It combines clinical ratings, cognitive testing, blood and cerebrospinal fluid sampling, brain imaging and genetics, with follow-up planned at 7 and 14 years, to identify predictors of long-term outcome in bipolar disorder.
location quote: SBP is a collaborative effort between academia and healthcare, enrolling study participants from bipolar outpatient clinics in Stockholm (SBP-S) and Gothenburg (SBP-G), Sweden.
note: Tier E (E026), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred on an empty record; research settles it. The PGS Catalog lists ACSGH but records no score, sample set or paper for it (REST cohort/ACSGH and the website search are empty), so it was identified by its name. The name is not a bare institution: in the genetics literature the 'Affective Center at St. Göran Hospital in Stockholm' is the recruitment source of the St. Göran Bipolar Project, a named longitudinal cohort. PMID:28072414 (open access) says of the Swedish Bipolar Disorder Cohort that '271 cases were recruited via physician’s referral from the Affective Center at St. Göran Hospital in Stockholm', and the SWEBIC profile (PMID:40478381) says 'SWEBIC-I included cases from the St. Göran Bipolar Project (N = 272), a longitudinal clinical cohort of individuals with bipolar disorders'; St. Göran papers place their patients at 'the outpatient clinic Affective Center at Northern Stockholm Psychiatry' (PMID:28468681). The cohort's own overview paper (PMID:39746340) gives its design. Tier-E row E1016 (PGS id SGBP, 'St G_ran Bipolar Project', a mis-encoded 'St Göran Bipolar Project') is the same cohort and should become 'same as E026', adding SGBP to the acronyms. The PGS name 'Affective Center at St Goran Hospital, Stockholm' names the clinic, so it is not kept as a synonym; strictly it points to the Stockholm arm (SBP-S), which was the whole project until the Gothenburg arm (SBP-G) began in 2009, so the tag is put on the project rather than on a separate arm term. The project's cases also went into the Swedish Bipolar Disorder Cohort (SWEBIC, COHO:0000159), but SWEBIC is a separate collection that took some St. Göran cases, not a parent; the Systematic Treatment Enhancement Program for Bipolar Disorder (COHO:0001415), whose interview the project adopted, is unrelated as a sample.

label: Adult Changes in Thought Study
note: Tier E (E027), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred for want of text; the source GWAS's supplement settles it. PGS000823's variant sample lists the cohorts ACTS, ADC, ADNI, GENADA, UM/VU/MSSM, MIRAGE, NIA-LOAD and TGEN from its source GWAS, the ADGC late-onset Alzheimer disease GWAS (PMID:21460841, GCST001026). That paper's Supplementary Note (free, Nature) lists the Stage 1 datasets as 'the Adult Changes in Thought (ACT)/Electronic Medical Records and Genetics (eMERGE) study', the NIA ADCs, ADNI, GenADA, UM/VU/MSSM, MIRAGE, OHSU, NIA-LOAD and TGEN2, and describes 'The ACT/eMERGE Studies (ACT)' as 'an urban and suburban elderly population from a stable HMO that includes 2,581 cognitively intact subjects age ≥ 65 who were enrolled between 1994 and 1998', with later and continuous enrolment. So ACTS is the PGS Catalog's id for the Adult Changes in Thought Study, already COHO:0000483 (acronym ACT). The draft's example (PMID:29555425, the Rotterdam Study paper that developed PGS000823) did not use ACT data, only the GWAS summary statistics, and an existing term needs no new example. The PGS Catalog elsewhere records the same ADGC cohort under the id ACT ('Adult Changes in Thought'), which COHO:0000483 already carries; ACTS is its second id for it. The ADGC calls the dataset 'ACT/eMERGE' because deceased ACT participants were added through the eMERGE study, but the people are ACT participants, so no separate term is needed.

input name: Amyloidosis Center at University Clinic Heidelberg
note: Tier E (E028), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred on an empty record. Research does not turn up a cohort behind the name. ACUCH is in the PGS Catalog's cohort list, but REST cohort/ACUCH and the website search return no score, sample set or publication, so nothing shows which sample the Catalog meant. The name is that of a clinical referral centre, the Amyloidosis Center of Heidelberg University Hospital (Department of Internal Medicine V), whose patients appear in many clinical studies but under no cohort name. The only genetic sample drawn from it that I found is the German patient set of the three-centre GWAS of immunoglobulin light chain (AL) amyloidosis (PMID:28025584: 'AL amyloidosis patients from Germany, UK and Italy'), which the follow-up paper calls simply the 'German cohort' among 'three patient cohorts' of 'the three centers' (PMID:28679651, Haematologica, open access); no paper names it after the centre. If a later PGS Catalog release uses ACUCH, it will most likely be for the German patients of the AL amyloidosis GWAS (PMID:28025584, and the MM/AL amyloidosis/MGUS meta-analysis PMID:31695157); the natural term would then be the three-centre AL amyloidosis GWAS sample (Heidelberg, London's National Amyloidosis Centre, Pavia) rather than the clinic. No acronym editor note is needed.

label: Alzheimer's Disease Cardiff Cohort
other synonyms: AD Cardiff Cohort
example quote: The Alzheimer’s Disease Cardiff Cohort (ADCC) was collected between 2004 and 2020 using MRC, Moondance Foundation and Health and Care Research Wales (HCRW) funding.
definition: A case–control cohort of people with sporadic early- or late-onset Alzheimer's disease and elderly controls screened for dementia, recruited from community and hospital settings in the United Kingdom between the early 2000s and 2020 with funding from the Medical Research Council, the Moondance Foundation and Health and Care Research Wales, and assessed with a standardised clinical and neuropsychological protocol. Its longitudinal clinical and cognitive data and blood samples support genome-wide genotyping, plasma biomarker and induced pluripotent stem cell studies of Alzheimer's disease.
location quote: were a subset of the AD Cardiff Cohort, collected between 2004 and 2020 from individuals recruited from UK community and hospital settings using MRC, Moondance Foundation, and Health and Care Research Wales (HCRW) funding
note: Tier E (E029), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred on an empty record; research settles it. The PGS Catalog records no score or paper for ADCC (REST cohort/ADCC and the website search are empty), but the name is a real, named cohort: open-access papers describe 'The Alzheimer’s Disease Cardiff Cohort (ADCC)' of sporadic early- and late-onset Alzheimer's disease cases and screened elderly controls, collected with MRC, Moondance Foundation and HCRW funding from UK community and hospital settings, genotyped genome-wide, and used for a plasma biomarker and polygenic risk study (PMID:35383826), a complement protein study (PMID:37480051) and an iPSC resource selected on polygenic risk (PMID:40614728). It has nothing to do with E022 (ACCT), which the draft wondered about: that is an arterial-stiffness study that shares only the city. The start of recruitment is given as 2004 in two papers and 2001 in one, so the definition says 'the early 2000s'. The PGS id most likely comes from a polygenic score evaluation in PMID:35383826 or a later Cardiff paper not yet released in the Catalog. Cardiff's older Alzheimer's collections contributed to GERAD (COHO:0000646); whether ADCC includes them is not stated, so no parent or membership is given. 'ADCC' also abbreviates antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, which is not a cohort, so no editor note is needed.

label: ADDITION-Denmark
other synonyms: ADDITION study
note: Tier E (E030), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: 'Existing' is right but the term is not: COHO:0000614 is the three-country ADDITION-Europe trial, the parent of the sample the id denotes. The only paper in which the PGS Catalog records the id is the source GWAS of PGS004864, PMID:19079260, and its Supplementary Material (free, Nature; on disk) describes the Danish follow-up samples as coming from 'two population cohorts': Inter99 and '(2) the ADDITION study group 6 , a population-based sample recruited for a high-risk screening and intervention study for type 2 diabetes in general practice and sampled through the Department of General Practice at the University of Aarhus', listed as 'Follow-up sample sets Denmark ... Addition' and 'an additional 5,450 Danish individuals from the ADDITION study'. Those are participants of the Danish ADDITION screening programme, i.e. ADDITION-Denmark, COHO:0000613, whose term covers the whole screened population of its general practices. The drafter's view that no paper mentions the cohort came from only seeing abstract matches of the word 'addition'; the review row it cited (row 291) minted COHO:0000614 as a parent, with no PGS or GWAS tag, so it does not show that the id means the European trial. Adding ADDITION to COHO:0000613 makes it an acronym shared with COHO:0000614, so both terms need the editor note: on COHO:0000613 'The acronym ADDITION also denotes the Anglo-Danish-Dutch Study of Intensive Treatment in People with Screen Detected Diabetes in Primary Care (COHO:0000614); this term is its Danish arm, ADDITION-Denmark.' and on COHO:0000614 'The acronym ADDITION also denotes ADDITION-Denmark (COHO:0000613); this term is the three-country ADDITION-Europe trial.' 'ADDITION study' is the source GWAS's own name for the Danish sample and the PGS Catalog name; the design paper the GWAS cites for it is titled 'The ADDITION study'. Not COHO:0000525 (ADDITION-PRO), which examined a sub-sample of the Danish high-risk screenees only in 2009–2011, after this GWAS was published.

label: Analyse des DEterminants génétiques et environnementaux de la Leucoaraiose dans une population de sujets Agés Hypertendus présentant des troubles cognitifs DEbutants
other synonyms: Analyse des DEterminants génétiques et environnementaux de la Leucoaraïose dans une population à sujets Agés HYpertendus présentant des troubles cognitifs DEbutants|ADELAHYDE study|ADELAHYDE-Nancy study
example quote: Samples from the Jerusalem LRC Longitudinal Study (N = 620) (68), Health ABC study (N = 337) (69), from ADELAHYDE-Nancy study and ERA-France study (N = 316) (70,71) and from a Danish collection (N = 964) (47) were included in the replication stage.
definition: A single-centre cohort study at Nancy University Hospital, France, of older treated hypertensive patients with subjective memory complaints, recruited in the early 2000s through local press advertisements and general practitioners of the Inserm clinical investigation centre network, who had cognitive testing, brain MRI for white matter hyperintensities, measurements of arterial stiffness, carotid structure and endothelial function, and DNA and serum banking, and were re-examined about eight years later (ADELAHYDE-2), to identify genetic, environmental and vascular determinants of leukoaraiosis and cognitive decline.
location quote: Patients were recruited between 2003 and 2005 by local press advertisements or referred by general practitioners from an investigator network of the Inserm Clinical Investigation Center, France[19].
note: Tier E (E031), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred on an empty record; research settles it. The PGS Catalog name 'ADELAHYDE/Nancy/ERA-France' copies a row of Table 1 of the leukocyte telomere length GWAS of PMID:23001564 ('ADELAHYDE/Nancy/ERA-France', 316 people in the replication stage), whose methods describe it as samples 'from ADELAHYDE-Nancy study and ERA-France study', i.e. two separate French cohorts of the same Nancy geriatrics group pooled for replication. The id ADELAHYDE names the first: the ADELAHYDE study (Analyse des DEterminants génétiques et environnementaux de la Leucoaraiose dans une population de sujets Agés Hypertendus présentant des troubles cognitifs DEbutants), a single-centre Nancy cohort of older treated hypertensive patients with subjective memory complaints, first examined in the early 2000s and re-examined about eight years later as ADELAHYDE-2 (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01351961). The second, the Evolution de la Rigidité Artérielle (ERA) study of a Paris cohort, is given under extra. Label: the cohort's papers spell out ADELAHYDE two ways; the NeuroImage Clin form (grammatical 'de sujets Agés Hypertendus') is taken as the label and the Sci Rep form, which capitalises 'HYpertendus' as the acronym is formed, as a synonym. Recruitment dates differ between reports (2001–2005 in the ClinicalTrials.gov record, 2003–2005 in HOMAGE, 2005 in PMID:32039844), so the definition says 'the early 2000s'. ADELAHYDE-2 (ClinicalTrials.gov acronym ADELAHYDE2) is the cohort's second visit, not a separate cohort, so it is not proposed as an acronym. The PGS name 'ADELAHYDE/Nancy/ERA-France' is not proposed as a synonym because it names the pooled sample of this cohort and ERA. ADELAHYDE is also one of the cohorts pooled in the HOMAGE (Heart 'omics' in AGEing) database, which COHO lacks. With no PGS score attached, the example is the GWAS paper whose table the Catalog's name copies.

The PGS Catalog id ADELAHYDE ('ADELAHYDE/Nancy/ERA-France') also covers this cohort, the other half of the pooled French replication sample of the telomere GWAS. The later telomere meta-analyses name it 'Evolution de la Rigidité Artérielle (ERA)', country France (PMID:31312500, PMID:31824705), citing PMID:28630210 ('This research draws on the Evolution de la Rigidité Artérielle (ERA) study, which examined determinants of arterial aging'; examinations in 1998–1999 and 2007–2008); PMID:23001564 cites the arterial-stiffness study of PMID:11889014 at the same centre (examinations in 1992–1993 and 1998–1999) for it. input name: Alcohol Dependence GWAS in European- and African Americans
label: Yale-Penn study
other synonyms: Alcohol Dependence GWAS in European- and African Americans
note: Tier E (E032), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred on an empty record; research settles it. The PGS Catalog name is, word for word, the title of dbGaP study phs000425.v1.p1, 'Alcohol Dependence GWAS in European- and African Americans' (principal investigator at Yale, co-principal investigator at the University of Pennsylvania): SSADDA-assessed African- and European-American subjects, mostly unrelated with some affected sibling pairs, collected 'in the course of three projects' on the genetics of alcohol, cocaine and opioid dependence and genotyped on the Illumina HumanOmni1-Quad. That is the first genome-wide genotyped wave of the Yale-Penn sample, which COHO already has (COHO:0000628, whose definition describes its three genotyping waves, Yale-Penn 1–3); the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium's alcohol dependence GWAS attributes the accession to Yale-Penn ('Yale-Penn: dbGAP accession phs000425.v1.p1 and phs000952.v1.p1'). So the id goes on the Yale-Penn study as an acronym, with the dbGaP title as a synonym, as for other genotyping-wave tags (e.g. IMAGE-I and IMAGE-II on COHO:0000607). COHO:0000628's example, definition and country stand. Not the Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Alcoholism (COHO:0000772), the NIAAA cohort (COHO:0000620) or SAGE, which have their own dbGaP accessions.

label: ADHD-VHIR study
example title: Multiancestry genome-wide association study of 520,000 subjects identifies 32 loci associated with stroke and stroke subtypes.
example quote: The Vall d'Hebron Research Institute (VHIR) cohort included 435 blood donors of Caucasian origin recruited from 2004 to 2008 at the Hospital Universitari Vall d'Hebron (Barcelona, Spain) to identify loci conferring susceptibility to Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder.
definition: A case–control collection of the Psychiatric Genetics Unit of the Vall d'Hebron Research Institute (VHIR) in Barcelona, Spain, of adults of European origin with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, recruited and evaluated at the Hospital Universitari Vall d'Hebron, and of unrelated blood donors screened for lifetime ADHD symptoms, genotyped genome-wide to identify loci conferring susceptibility to persistent ADHD.
location quote: All patients were adults of Caucasian origin, recruited and evaluated at the Hospital Universitari Vall d’Hebron located in Barcelona (Spain), and met Diagnostic and Statistical Manual for Mental Disorders-IV (DSM-IV) criteria for ADHD.
parent quote: BASICMAR Spain 5M EUR, HIS 890 – ADHD Spain 1M EUR – 411 INMA Spain 1M EUR – 807
note: Tier E (E033), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The id is not the disorder. Both scores the Catalog records it for (PGS000665, PGS002259) list it among the cohorts of their source GWAS, MEGASTROKE (PMID:29531354), whose Supplementary Note, in the NINDS-SiGN section under 'Controls for discovery analysis', describes 'Attention-deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)': 'The Vall d'Hebron Research Institute (VHIR) cohort included 435 blood donors of Caucasian origin recruited from 2004 to 2008 at the Hospital Universitari Vall d'Hebron (Barcelona, Spain) to identify loci conferring susceptibility to Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder', acknowledged under 'Control-only Cohorts' as 'The ADHD-VHIR study from Barcelona'. SiGN's own GWAS (PMID:26708676) lists 'ADHD Spain 1M EUR – 411' controls and glosses 'ADHD, Attention-deficit Hyperactivity Disorder', the source of the Catalog's name. The blood donors are the screened controls of VHIR's adult ADHD case–control GWAS (PMID:25284319: cases 'recruited and evaluated at the Hospital Universitari Vall d’Hebron' and 'unrelated blood donors' with lifetime ADHD symptoms excluded, on the HumanOmni1-Quad, the array MEGASTROKE gives). So the id denotes a defined, named sample; the draft's name-search papers on the disorder (P4–P9) were irrelevant and P1–P3 were not read for the cohort. The PGS Catalog name 'Attention-deficit Hyperactivity Disorder' is the disorder, not a name of the sample, so it is not proposed as a synonym; the acronym ADHD is kept because it is the Catalog's id, and CLAUDE.md asks for editor notes only for clashes with other cohorts. The label follows the cohort's own acknowledgement ('The ADHD-VHIR study from Barcelona'); no fuller name was found. The 435 MEGASTROKE controls are presumably a subset of the ADHD GWAS's 584 blood donors (same hospital, same array), though no text states the overlap. Not VHIR-FMT-Barcelona (COHO:0001247, a VHIR stroke case–control set), IMAGE (COHO:0000607) or INMA (COHO:0000100); INMA children were a second control subset of the ADHD GWAS and a separate SiGN control set. The parent could equally be MEGASTROKE (COHO:0000784), which contains SiGN; SiGN is the aggregation that lists these controls.

input name: Action in Diabetes and Vascular disease: Preterax and Diamicron-MR Controlled Evaluation
label: Action in Diabetes and Vascular disease: Preterax and Diamicron-MR Controlled Evaluation
other synonyms: Action in Diabetes and Vascular disease; preterAx and diamicroN-MR Controlled Evaluation|Action in Diabetes and Vascular Disease: Preterax and Diamicron MR Controlled Evaluation|Action in Diabetes and Vascular Disease: PreterAx and DiamicroN Modified-Release Controlled Evaluation|Action in Diabetes and Vascular disease: preterAx and diamicroN mr Controlled Evaluation
example title: Genome-wide Association Studies Identify Genetic Loci Associated With Albuminuria in Diabetes.
example quote: Our study was based on 30 discovery and replication studies mostly from the general population, with the exception of Action in Diabetes and Vascular Disease: Preterax and Diamicron MR Controlled Evaluation (ADVANCE) and Genetics of Diabetic Nephropathy (GENDIAN), which enrolled exclusively individuals with type 2 diabetes, totaling 67,452 participants of European ancestry across the different analyses (up to 7,787 with diabetes in discovery and replication).
definition: A multinational randomised controlled trial with a 2×2 factorial design, conducted from 2001 by 215 collaborating centres in 20 countries in Asia, Australasia, Europe and North America among people with type 2 diabetes diagnosed at age 30 or older, aged 55 or older and with cardiovascular disease or at least one other cardiovascular risk factor, which compared a fixed combination of perindopril and indapamide with placebo, whatever the initial blood pressure, and an intensive gliclazide modified-release-based glucose control regimen targeting an HbA1c of 6.5% or less with standard glucose control, for their effects on major macrovascular and microvascular events; surviving participants were followed after the trial in ADVANCE-ON.
location quote: As in previous analyses based on ADVANCE 15, 19, the primary comparison in the present study was between three groupings of countries based on geography and economic development: Asia, comprising China, India, Malaysia and the Philippines; Eastern Europe, comprising the Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Lithuania, Poland, Russia and Slovakia; and 'established market economies', comprising Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, New Zealand, and the UK.
note: Tier E (E034), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P10: the ADVANCE trial cohort of people with type 2 diabetes throughout. Shares the acronym ADVANCE with tier-D row D082 ("Atherosclerotic Disease, Vascular function, and Genetic Epidemiology"), an unrelated cohort -- both need the acronym-clash editor note when minted. No specific country named (only "20 countries", unnamed). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronyms, type, parent and example are right: in every paper the Catalog records the id in, ADVANCE is the diabetes trial (Teumer 2016 names it and acknowledges the 'ADVANCE Study' genetic epidemiology work; CKDGen 2019's study table gives the full name, 'factorial, multicentre, randomised controlled trial, with a 5- to 6-year follow-up' and baseline 2001-2003, and its acknowledgements the 'ADVANCE genomic sub-studies'). The definition called the blood-pressure arm 'intensive blood-pressure-lowering therapy'; the trial compared a fixed perindopril–indapamide combination with placebo regardless of initial blood pressure, and the draft left out who was eligible (type 2 diabetes, aged 55 or over, with cardiovascular disease or a risk factor), when, where and the post-trial follow-up. Countries were left out as unnamed, but an open-access ADVANCE paper names all 20. More spellings of the full name are added as synonyms. The acronym ADVANCE is already on two COHO terms: COHO:0001052 (ADVANCE trial, a South African trial of first-line antiretroviral therapy) and COHO:0001053 (Atherosclerotic Disease, Vascular Function, and Genetic Epidemiology Study). All three need editor notes, e.g. on this term: 'The acronym ADVANCE also denotes the ADVANCE trial of first-line antiretroviral therapy (COHO:0001052) and the Atherosclerotic Disease, Vascular Function, and Genetic Epidemiology Study (COHO:0001053); this term is the Action in Diabetes and Vascular disease trial of blood pressure lowering and intensive glucose control in type 2 diabetes.' 'ADVANCE trial' is not proposed as a synonym because it is COHO:0001052's label. The genotyped participants belong to the trial's genomic sub-study. ADVANCE is also a CKDGen member study (COHO:0000532 has no hasCohort links yet), so no parent is proposed.

Second link for the curator: the study is a member of the Asia Colorectal Cancer Consortium (COHO:0001049), like its sibling studies COHO:0001349 and COHO:0001364; quote: 'Studies (grant support) participating in the Asia Colorectal Cancer Consortium include: Shanghai Women’s Health Study (R37CA070867), Shanghai Men’s Health Study (R01CA082729), Shanghai Breast and Endometrial Cancer Studies (R01CA064277 and R01CA092585, contributing only controls), Shanghai Colorectal Cancer Study 3 (R37CA070867 and Ingram Professorship funds), Guangzhou Colorectal Cancer Study (National Key Scientific and Technological Project – 2011ZX09307-001-04; the National Basic Research Program – 2011CB504303, contributing only controls; Natural Science Foundation of China – 81072383, contributing only controls), Japan-BioBank Colorectal Cancer Study (grant from the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology of the Japanese government), Hwasun Cancer Epidemiology Study-Colon and Rectum Cancer (grants from the Korea Center for Disease Control and Prevention and Jeonnam Regional Cancer Center), Aichi Colorectal Cancer Study' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4068797/). Aside for COHO:0001049: its definition says the consortium was 'initiated in 2010', as PMID:30529582 has it ('In 2010, we initiated the Asia Colorectal Cancer Consortium (ACCC)'), but PMID:35765848 says 'In 2009, we established the Asia Colorectal Cancer Consortium (ACCC)'.

label: Aichi Colorectal Cancer Study
note: Tier E (E045), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. same cohort as review name E044. P1 (2014): 'Aichi CRC Study 1' (Aichi-1) in stage-1 discovery and 'Aichi CRC Study 2' (Aichi-2) in stage-4 replication; P2-P5: later PRS papers partly built on this data; P6: same pooled training-set table as E044/P3. Same PGS-Catalog-recorded sample (Aichi-1/Aichi-2 case-control waves) as E044's 'Aichi': both tags cite the identical training-set table in PMC9509464 (this row's P6 = E044's P3). 'Aichi_Con' looks like a PGS Catalog case/control sample-row split, not a different cohort. Checked 2026-09-23: None. Aichi_Con is the same study as E044's Aichi: in every paper that names it, the tag's sample is the Aichi Colorectal Cancer Study's case-control collections Aichi-1 and Aichi-2. The PGS Catalog's name 'Asian Consortium, Colorectal Cancer Aichi' follows its pattern for Asia Colorectal Cancer Consortium studies (id Guangzhou is 'Asian Consortium, Colorectal Cancer Guangzhou', already a synonym of COHO:0001349); it is not a separate consortium, so the triage hint 'aggregation?' does not apply. Merge into E044 (label Aichi Colorectal Cancer Study), which carries this id's PGS Catalog name as a synonym; keep Aichi_Con as an acronym of that term.

Tier E (E046), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft's 'not a cohort' rests on three clinical abstracts found by searching Europe PMC for 'AITD', which use it only as the abbreviation of autoimmune thyroid disease; they say nothing about the PGS Catalog id. The id is an entry of the Catalog's cohort table ('AITD Autoimmune thyroid disease', src/curation/pgs_catalog_cohorts.csv), and such entries without scores are often real samples copied from consortium study lists (in this batch, AMI and Amsterdam_UMC_COVID_study_group are exact copies of MIGen's and the COVID-19 HGI's study names). Nothing read shows which sample the Catalog meant, so the name can be settled neither as a cohort nor as not one. Most likely candidate, unconfirmed: the UK AITD National Collection, the main named AITD case collection in genetic studies (for example 'We thank nurses and doctors for recruiting AITD patients into the AITD National Collection.' and 'The British AITD cases consisted of 2374 (390 males and 1984 females) GD and 474 (69 males and 405 females) HT patients (18).', https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC3490518/fullTextXML, the ImmunoChip AITD study PMID:22922229). COHO:0000355 (WTCCC case-control study for Autoimmune Thyroid Disease) models the WTCCC's UK AITD case series. If the Catalog later attaches a score or sample set to AITD, that sample decides between COHO:0000355, a new term for the national collection, or not a cohort.

input name: The African American Breast Cancer Epidemiology and Risk consortium
label: African American Breast Cancer Epidemiology and Risk Consortium
other synonyms: African American Breast Cancer Epidemiology and Risk consortium|African American breast cancer epidemiology and risk consortium|The African American Breast Cancer Epidemiology and Risk consortium|African American Breast Cancer Epidemiology and Risk|AMBER Consortium|AMBER consortium
example title: Improved polygenic risk prediction models for breast cancer subtypes in women of African ancestry.
example quote: The genotype datasets used in this study are publicly available via dbGaP (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gap/) including AABC under accession code phs000851.v1.p1, ONCO under accession code phs001265.v1.p1, AMBER under accession code phs000669.v1.p1, ROOT under accession code phs000383.v1.p1, and GBHS under accession code phs002387.v1.p1.
definition: A consortium, funded by the US National Cancer Institute as a Program Project, that pools the questionnaire data, tumour tissue and DNA of four epidemiological studies of breast cancer in African American women in the United States (two case-control studies, the Carolina Breast Cancer Study and the Women's Circle of Health Study, and two cohorts, the Black Women's Health Study and the Multiethnic Cohort Study), with tumour subtyping, genotyping and data harmonisation done centrally in shared cores, to study the causes of breast cancer subtypes, especially oestrogen receptor-negative breast cancer, in African American women.
location quote: The study began in 1995 when 59,000 AA women 21–69 years of age from across the United States completed a 14-page postal health questionnaire.
parent quote: The AMBER is a collaboration of four studies: the Women’s Circle of Health Study (WCHS), the Black Women’s Health Study (BWHS), the Carolina Breast Cancer Study (CBCS), and the Multiethnic Cohort Study (MEC) funded by the National Cancer Institute.
note: Tier E (E047), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: no quotable evidence extracted; P2: AMBER named as one of several genotype datasets (dbGaP phs000669) pooled for a cross-ancestry PRS meta-analysis; P3-P7: the AMBER consortium itself, its design and pooled epidemiological analyses. No unit states a country; 'African American' and dbGaP (a US resource) imply the United States but that is not asserted by name or quote. A related but distinct 'African Ancestry Breast Cancer Genetics Consortium' pools AMBER with AABC/ONCO/ROOT/GBHS; not established as AMBER's parent. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type (aggregation), acronym and example paper were right. The definition left out which four studies AMBER pools and that it is a US National Cancer Institute Program Project ('The AMBER consortium is an NCI-funded Program Project consisting of four cores and four scientific projects.', PMID:24343304; 'The AMBER Consortium pools data from two large case–control studies, the Carolina Breast Cancer Study (CBCS) and the Women’s Circle of Health Study (WCHS), and two large cohort studies, the Black Women’s Health Study (BWHS) and the Multiethnic Cohort Study.', PMID:25849024), and 'centralised tumour pathology review' overstated the design paper's 'assays of molecular markers carried out at a pathology core'. Country missing: every member study recruited in the United States. Parent missing: AMBER is one of the consortia pooled in the African Ancestry Breast Cancer Genetic consortium (review key E008), whose Supplementary Note describes it among the participating studies. The example quote began with PDF watermark text and the heading 'DATA AVAILABILITY STATEMENT'; it is replaced by the same sentence from the PMC page. Members to link with hasCohort from this term: Carolina Breast Cancer Study (COHO:0001210), Black Women's Health Study (COHO:0001150), Multiethnic Cohort Study of Diet and Health (COHO:0000121, the Hawaii and Los Angeles cohort, not COHO:0000612) and Women's Circle of Health Study (review key E1210); quote: 'The AMBER Consortium pools data from two large case–control studies, the Carolina Breast Cancer Study (CBCS) and the Women’s Circle of Health Study (WCHS), and two large cohort studies, the Black Women’s Health Study (BWHS) and the Multiethnic Cohort Study.' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC4358874/fullTextXML). The parent quote is the first sentence under the Supplementary Note heading for AMBER in AABCG's 'Description of participating studies'; no single sentence there names both consortia. The country quote describes the BWHS, one of AMBER's members, in AMBER's own design paper; the other members are in North Carolina, New York City and New Jersey, and Hawaii and Los Angeles. AMBER is distinct from the African American Breast Cancer Consortium (AABC, COHO:0000989), a separate member of AABCG; the two share no name or acronym.

input name: Acute Myocardial Infarction Gene Study/Dortmund Health Study
label: Acute Myocardial Infarction Gene Study
other synonyms: AMI Gene Study|Acute Myocardial Infarction Gene Study/Dortmund Health Study|AMI Gene Study/Dortmund Health Study
example quote: The six studies were: i) Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI) Gene Study/Dortmund Health Study; ii) Verona Heart Study; iii) Mid-America Heart Institute; iv) Irish Family Study; v) German MI Family Study II; and vi) INTERHEART.
definition: A German case-control study of myocardial infarction whose cases were enrolled in 2004–2006 in a prospective multicentre registry at 4 heart centres and 6 cardiology departments in North Rhine-Westphalia, Lower Saxony and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: consecutive men younger than 65 admitted with ST- or non-ST-segment elevation acute myocardial infarction, all of whom underwent cardiac catheterisation and revascularisation. Its controls are participants of the population-based Dortmund Health Study, and the case-control sample served as a replication study for the Myocardial Infarction Genetics Consortium's genome-wide association study of early-onset myocardial infarction.
location quote: The AMI Gene Study/Dortmund Health Study13 is a prospective multi-centre registry involving 4 heart centres and 6 cardiologic departments in North-Rhine-Westphalia, Lower Saxony, and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
note: Tier E (E048), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred with no evidence; research settles it. The PGS Catalog records no score, sample set or paper for AMI, but its name is copied verbatim from the Stage 3 study list of the Myocardial Infarction Genetics Consortium GWAS (PMID:19198609), whose supplement describes the study: 'The AMI Gene Study/Dortmund Health Study13 is a prospective multi-centre registry involving 4 heart centres and 6 cardiologic departments in North-Rhine-Westphalia, Lower Saxony, and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.'; 'Between 2004 and 2006, we enrolled a cohort of 809 consecutive men younger than 65 and suffering from non-ST-segment elevation MI or ST- segment elevation MI with an onset of symptoms less than 24 hours before admission.'; 'All cases underwent cardiac catheterization and interventional or surgical revascularization.'; 'Controls came from the Dortmund Health Study13,14 , a population-based survey conducted in the city of Dortmund with the aim to determine the prevalence of headache types, cardiovascular and other chronic diseases and their risk factors in the general population.' It is not a combination of the Dortmund Health Study with an unmodelled study but one case-control sample: the AMI Gene Study's cases with Dortmund Health Study controls, which later meta-analyses call simply the 'AMI Gene Study'. Controls: the Dortmund Health Study is COHO:0000054, but the cases are recruited separately in hospitals, so no isSubCohortOf is asserted (as E074 did for its Netherlands Twin Register controls). The registry's states are German Länder; the same supplement says 'study procedures were approved by the ethics committees of the University of Witten-Herdecke and the University of Muenster, Germany, respectively.' No parent: in PMID:19198609 it is one of the six Stage 3 replication studies, not one of the six Stage 1 discovery studies that the supplement lists for the Myocardial Infarction Genetics Consortium's GWAS; whether MIGen (review key E702) should list replication partners as members is left to that record. No other COHO term uses the acronym AMI.

label: Amsterdam Dementia Cohort
note: Tier E (E049), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft judged the id an author affiliation because the drafter looked for 'University of Amsterdam' in the papers' text. The PGS Catalog does not use the id for authors: it labels a sample in each of its two papers, and neither is 'the University of Amsterdam'. In the Alzheimer's disease consensus meta-analysis (PMID:42237039; PGS005389–PGS005391 development samples, where the Catalog lists 'Amsterdam' beside 'ADC', its id for the US NIA Alzheimer Disease Centers) it is the paper's 'Amsterdam UMC' dataset: 'The Amsterdam UMC provided additional cases and controls from the Amsterdam Dementia Cohort (ADC)12 , not previously genotyped as part of EADB.' (supplementary note 1.3.5). Those are participants of the Amsterdam Dementia Cohort, COHO:0000374, which gets the acronym. The bibliometric and 1940s papers found by name search have nothing to do with the id. The id denotes two different samples. Besides the Amsterdam Dementia Cohort (PGS005389–PGS005391), it labels the evaluation samples of PGS000735–PGS000737: the Brugada syndrome ajmaline-testing series of Amsterdam UMC location AMC in PMID:31504448. That series has no name of its own (the paper calls it 'the cohort' or 'the study population'), so it is not given as an extra cohort; if the curator wants it, it would need a descriptive label. The Catalog's full name 'University of Amsterdam' fits the AMC series (the AMC is the University of Amsterdam's hospital) but not the Amsterdam Dementia Cohort (Alzheimer Center Amsterdam at location VUmc, Vrije Universiteit), so the id was probably created for the 2019 Brugada paper and reused for the 2026 paper's 'Amsterdam UMC' dataset. The institution's name is not added as a synonym of COHO:0000374, as E073 decided for 'Amsterdam UMC'. COHO:0000374 already carries the Catalog's own id for the cohort, AmDem.

label: Amsterdam UMC COVID-19 Biobank
other synonyms: Amsterdam UMC COVID study group|Amsterdam UMC Covid-19 Biobank|Amsterdam UMC COVID-19 biobank
example quote: Patients or their legal representatives received written information about the study (Amsterdam UMC Covid-19 biobank) and were asked to give written informed consent for participation.
definition: A prospective cohort and biobank, set up by the Amsterdam UMC COVID study group, of adult patients admitted with COVID-19 from 2020 to the COVID-19 wards and intensive care units of the two academic hospitals of Amsterdam UMC (locations University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam) in the Netherlands, which stores their clinical data and left-over and serially collected biological samples. Its genotyped patients, with controls, were contributed to the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative's genome-wide association meta-analyses of COVID-19.
location quote: The Amsterdam UMC COVID study group (Amsterdam UMC location University of Amsterdam and location Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Amsterdam, the Netherlands)
parent quote: Amsterdam UMC COVID study group
note: Tier E (E050), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred with no evidence; research settles it. The PGS Catalog records no score or paper for the id, but the id is the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative's site abbreviation: Supplementary Table 1 of the HGI's Nature paper (PMID:34237774, 'Information regarding studies contributing to the consortium') has the row 'Amsterdam UMC COVID study group' (country 'The Netherlands', site abbreviation 'Amsterdam_UMC_COVID_study_group', European ancestry), whose informed-consent cell names the study as the Amsterdam UMC Covid-19 biobank and whose funding row reads 'The Amsterdam UMC Covid-19 Biobank was funded by the Amsterdam UMC, The Corona Research Fund, and the Dr. C.J. Vaillantfonds' The biobank's own papers describe it: 'The Amsterdam UMC COVID-19 biobank is a prospective cohort study containing clinical data and archive material from adult patients admitted with COVID-19 in two academic hospitals of Amsterdam UMC.' (PMID:34000622), and the study group is the team 'who set up the biobank at Amsterdam UMC' (PMID:38337670). The group name is the HGI's label for the sample, so the biobank's name becomes the label and the group name a synonym. The HGI table does not say where the 1,413 controls came from, so the definition does not describe them. Papers also call the team 'the Amsterdam UMC COVID-19 biobank study group' (PMID:34713349) and the 'Amsterdam UMC COVID-19 Biobank Study Group' (PMID:37080568, PMC10151455); these name the investigators, not the sample, and are not added. Not to be confused with the other Amsterdam UMC samples of this review: E049 (Amsterdam Dementia Cohort, COHO:0000374, and an AMC ajmaline series) and E073/E074 (the Amsterdam UMC dilated cardiomyopathy GWAS cohort). The label's capitalisation follows 'were included in the Amsterdam UMC COVID-19 Biobank' (PMID:34000622); the other two capitalisations are kept as synonyms.

label: Australian National Endometrial Cancer Study
example title: Five endometrial cancer risk loci identified through genome-wide association analysis.
example quote: As described previously, cases with endometrioid histology were selected from two population studies; the UK Studies of Epidemiology and Risk factors in Cancer Heredity (SEARCH, n=681) and the Australian National Endometrial Cancer Study (ANECS, n=606), and genotypes generated using Illumina Infinium 610K arrays 10.
definition: A nationwide population-based case-control study of endometrial cancer in Australia, run by a study group at QIMR Berghofer Medical Research Institute in Brisbane, whose cases are women aged 18–79 years newly diagnosed with histologically confirmed primary endometrial cancer between July 2005 and December 2007, identified through major hospitals and state cancer registries, and whose controls are women randomly selected from the Australian Electoral Roll and frequency-matched to the cases by state of residence and five-year age group. Participants gave risk-factor information by telephone interview and blood samples, and the cases were followed for survival, to study the causes and outcomes of endometrial cancer.
location quote: Data from the Australian National Endometrial Cancer Study (ANECS) cohort was examined, which was established as a nationwide, population‐based, case–control study assessing Australian endometrial cancers.
parent quote: 606 ANECS samples all of endometrioid-only histology were used for the original endometrial cancer case-control GWAS and a further 538 were genotyped using iCOGS for the first additional genotyping phase.
note: Tier E (E051), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P4 (PGS Catalog papers): ANECS as one of the genotyping/population studies contributing endometrioid-histology cases to the EC meta-analyses; P5-P15: consistently the same Australian case-control study. Contributed iCOGS-genotyped samples (E051.57) to what E051.36 calls the Endometrial Cancer Association Consortium (ECAC), but ECAC isn't in the candidate list, so parent left null for a checker to add. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type and example are right. The definition described only the cases (and called the study a 'family study', a phrase from one supplement's Zotero-garbled paragraph); it now also says who ran it (the ANECS group at QIMR Berghofer), how the controls were chosen (random sample of the Australian Electoral Roll, frequency-matched by state and five-year age group; PMC5920223), what was collected (telephone interview, blood samples) and that the cases were followed for survival. The country is right, but its quote was a span of Zotero citation code; it is replaced by an open sentence that names ANECS as a nationwide, population-based study of Australian endometrial cancers (PMC12723092). The parent was left null although the draft's own evidence (E051.36, E051.57) places ANECS among the case studies of the Endometrial Cancer Association Consortium, this review's D405, whose checked record already lists ANECS (E051) as a candidate member: ANECS supplied 538 cases to ECAC's iCOGS genotyping phase. The parent quote is from the Supplementary Note of PMID:27135401, where the iCOGS genotyping phase is the ECAC case collection ('For the iCOGS genotyping stage, 4,330 women ... were recruited via 11 studies in Western Europe, North America and Australia, collectively called the Endometrial Cancer Association Consortium (ECAC)', PMC4907351 main text); no single open sentence names ANECS and ECAC together. ANECS is also a member study of the Epidemiology of Endometrial Cancer Consortium (E2C2, this review's D110, the one Australian study on NCI's E2C2 page): it is a row of 'Characteristics of 14 studies included in the E2C2 pooled analysis' (PMID:25688738, PMC4453954 Table 1: 'Australian National Endometrial Cancer Study (ANECS) Australia 2005–2007') and one of the nine case-control studies of the E2C2 pooled FTO/MC4R analysis (PMID:21347432, PMC3035652), so D110 could take ANECS with hasCohort too. The GWAS controls came from other cohorts, the Hunter Community Study (COHO:0000095) and the Brisbane twin studies (COHO:0000744), which are not part of ANECS; its own electoral-roll controls were used in the epidemiological analyses. Papers are authored by the 'Australian National Endometrial Cancer Study Group'.

label: Lübeck Registry of Structural Heart Disease
other synonyms: Luebeck Angiographic Study
example title: Large-scale association analysis identifies new risk loci for coronary artery disease.
example quote: Angio-Lueb/ KORA F3 Lübeck Registry of Structural Heart Disease /KORA (Kooperative Gesundheitsforschung 21378990 16648850 European Germany CAD/MI Consecutive patients referred for coronary angiography, classified as CAD/MI cases based on the coronary angiogram
definition: A registry of patients with heart disease treated at the University of Lübeck hospital (University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein, Campus Lübeck) in Germany, with blood samples and clinical data, whose angiography sample (Angio-Lueb) consists of consecutive patients referred for coronary angiography and classified from the angiogram as having coronary artery disease or myocardial infarction or not. It has provided cases for genetic association studies of coronary artery disease, with population controls from KORA, and of dilated cardiomyopathy.
location quote: additional German DCM cases (mean age 53±13 years; n = 564, n = 440 men, n = 124 women) were recruited from different German study centers: Berlin, n = 64; Lübeck, n = 96 (Angio-Lueb)
parent quote: The Lübeck Registry of Structural Heart Disease /KORA (Kooperative Gesundheitsforschung in der Region Augsburg) survey S3/F3 datasets included cases selected from consecutive patients referred for coronary angiography, which were classified as CAD/MI based on the coronary angiogram; cases were < 65 y in males or < 70 y in females.
note: Tier E (E052), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred for want of text; research settles it. None of the six PGS Catalog papers names Angio-Lueb: each built its coronary score from the CARDIoGRAMplusC4D 2013 meta-analysis (PMID:23202125), the source GWAS the Catalog records for all six, and in that paper Angio-Lueb is one of the stage-2 (Metabochip) case-control studies, 'Angio-Lueb/KORA F3': cases from 'The Lübeck Registry of Structural Heart Disease', consecutive patients referred for coronary angiography and classified as CAD/MI from the angiogram, compared with KORA S3/F3 population controls from Augsburg (Supplementary Table 1 and Supplementary Note). The PGS Catalog name 'Luebeck Angiographic Study' appears in no paper in Europe PMC and looks constructed from the tag; the study's own name in the consortium's description is the registry's, so that is the label and the Catalog name a synonym. 'Angio-Lüb' is the paper's own spelling of the tag (author contributions). No design paper or website for the registry was found, so its start date and size are not given; its angiography patients were enrolled at least from 2005 (PMID:19348677) and the ethics approval is numbered 04-041. The registry is wider than its angiography sample (it also enrolled dilated cardiomyopathy and pulmonary embolism patients); the term is labelled with the registry's name because CARDIoGRAMplusC4D gives that as Angio-Lueb's full name. The KORA controls paired with it in CARDIoGRAMplusC4D belong to KORA (COHO:0000045; tier-E rows E602 KORA F3 and E605 KORA S3), and in CARDIoGRAM 2011 its cases were paired with the Regensburg GoKard study ('Angio-Lueb/GoKard'); neither is part of this term. The Cardiogenics Study (COHO:0000028) recruited its own Lübeck cases and is separate. The parent quote is from the CARDIoGRAMplusC4D paper's Supplementary Note describing its stage-2 studies, as for other CARDIoGRAMplusC4D members; Angio-Lueb was also a replication study of CARDIoGRAM (COHO:0000745) in 2011, but not one of its discovery GWAS.

input name: The Australia and New Zealand Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Conortium
label: Australia and New Zealand Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium
other synonyms: The Australia and New Zealand Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Conortium|Australian and New Zealand Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium|ANZgene Consortium|ANZgene Study
example title: Genome-wide meta-analysis identifies novel multiple sclerosis susceptibility loci.
example quote: Analyzed in the ANZgene Study
definition: A multiple sclerosis case-control collection assembled for genome-wide association studies by the Australia and New Zealand Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium (ANZgene), a collaboration of multiple sclerosis research groups in Australia and New Zealand, whose cases are people with multiple sclerosis of European ancestry from Australia and New Zealand; its genome-wide scan compared them with shared genotype data from controls of European ancestry from Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States, and further ANZgene cases and controls were collected for replication and fine-mapping, to identify genetic variants that influence susceptibility to multiple sclerosis.
location quote: Following quality control as outlined in the ANZgene GWAS [28], this dataset consisted of 1618 MS cases of European ancestry from Australia and New Zealand, and 3413 healthy controls of European ancestry from Australia, the UK and the US.
note: Tier E (E053), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because its evidence never expanded the tag; research settles it. ANZgene is the Australia and New Zealand Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium, the author of the 2009 MS GWAS (PMID:19525955: 1,618 cases, shared data for 3,413 controls, replication in 2,256 cases and 2,310 controls). In the PGS Catalog's source GWAS (P1, Patsopoulos 2011) the tag is that GWAS dataset, the 'ANZ' stratum ('Analyzed in the ANZgene Study'); in P2 it occurs only in the reference to P1's byline. The consortium collected its own cases rather than pooling named cohorts, so the term is a cohort (the ANZgene case-control collection), labelled with the consortium's name because the sample has no other; the PGS Catalog's misspelt name is kept as a synonym only because the Catalog uses it. The draft's example is right. Countries are Australia and New Zealand, where the cases were recruited; the UK and US controls were shared genotype data from other studies, not recruited by ANZgene, and are not asserted. ANZgene is a collaborating group separate from the International Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium (COHO:0000103) in P1's byline ('ANZgene Consortium, GeneMSA, International Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium'); no sentence read makes it an IMSGC member, so no parent. Not related to PrevANZ (COHO:0000323), an Australian and New Zealand vitamin D prevention trial. 'ANZ' (P1's stratum label) is not added as an acronym. In a replication sample of the same consortium (PMID:21347448), 'Australian MS cases were volunteers recruited from Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Hobart, Melbourne, Newcastle, Perth and Sydney' and 'MS cases from New Zealand were recruited through a national prevalence survey'; the GWAS cases are likely similar but no open text says so.

input name: Australian & New Zealand Registry of Advanced Glaucoma
label: Australian & New Zealand Registry of Advanced Glaucoma
other synonyms: Australian and New Zealand Registry of Advanced Glaucoma|Australia and New Zealand Registry of Advanced Glaucoma
example title: Multitrait analysis of glaucoma identifies new risk loci and enables polygenic prediction of disease susceptibility and progression.
example quote: The Australian & New Zealand Registry of Advanced Glaucoma (ANZRAG) comprises 3,071 POAG cases of European descent, who were compared to 6,750 controls.
definition: A prospective registry, run from the Department of Ophthalmology at Flinders University in Adelaide, of people with glaucoma referred by their eye practitioners across Australia and New Zealand: mainly people with advanced glaucoma (chiefly primary open-angle glaucoma with severe visual field loss), but also with less advanced, secondary and developmental glaucomas such as Axenfeld–Rieger malformation, whose clinical information and blood or saliva samples are collected by post. It was set up to find genetic risk factors for glaucoma blindness, and relatives of participants who carry myocilin mutations are offered cascade genetic testing.
location quote: Samples are collected across Australia and New Zealand using postage kits. || For the primary analysis, we examined the glaucoma phenotype of 2154 POAG patients enrolled in the Australian and New Zealand Registry of Advanced Glaucoma, including patients recruited from the United Kingdom.
parent quote: The CREAM meta-analysis included data from 32 studies: 1958 British Birth Cohort, ALSPAC (mothers), ANZRAG, AREDS1a1b, AREDS1c, Beijing Eye Study, BMES, CROATIA-Korcula, CROATIA-Split, CROATIA-Vis, DCCT, EGCUT, ERF, FECD, FITSA, Framingham, GHS 1, GHS 2, KORA, OGP Talana, ORCADES, RS1, RS2, RS3, SCES, SIMES, SINDI, SP2, TEST/BATS, TwinsUK, WESDR, and YFS.
note: Tier E (E054), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P3-P5: ANZRAG as an independent case registry used to validate glaucoma PRS/MTAG results; P6 supplement: ANZRAG listed among CREAM's contributing refractive-error cohorts (table-style text, E054.22-24, treated cautiously). 'Advanced' names the registry's focus; sub-analyses further restrict to a stricter 'advanced POAG' subset (E054.14, not used here). Country given via from_name since the name itself states Australia and New Zealand. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type and example are right. The definition described one GWAS's analysis sample ('POAG cases ... of European descent ... compared with controls in genetic studies'); the registry's own design paper describes a prospective study that collects glaucoma cases with severe visual field loss, referred by eye practitioners across Australia and New Zealand, with clinical information and blood (or saliva) sent by post, to identify genetic risk factors for glaucoma blindness, and it also takes less advanced, secondary and developmental glaucomas; it has no controls of its own (GWAS controls came from other Australian studies). Countries: Australia and New Zealand were right (from the name), now with the design paper's sentence, and the United Kingdom is added, since patients recruited there were enrolled in the registry (PMID:32081492 abstract). The parent was missing: the draft's own evidence (E054.22) lists ANZRAG among the cohorts of the Consortium for Refractive Error and Myopia (COHO:0000905), and an open CREAM paper names it among the consortium's 32 studies. The label keeps the '&' form the registry uses in its website header and research-fund name; the design paper's title uses 'and', now a synonym. No start date is stated in the open text read. ANZRAG also contributes to the International Glaucoma Genetics Consortium (COHO:0000916): the 'ANZRAG consortium' is an author group of the IGGC open-angle glaucoma meta-analysis (PMID:33627673), but no sentence read names it as an IGGC member, so CREAM, which lists it among its studies, is given as the parent. The Southampton/Liverpool advanced glaucoma cases that PMID:31959993 used to replicate ANZRAG findings are described there as a separate UK sample. The registry also runs a relatives' screening project (TARRGET) on its website.

definition: A population-based, retrospective study of the histological types of ovarian carcinoma in the province of Alberta, Canada, whose cases are women with ovarian carcinoma identified through the Alberta Cancer Registry and sampled by histological type (endometrioid, clear cell, mucinous and high-grade serous carcinoma), with archival tumour tissue and pathology reports reviewed by a gynaecological pathologist, clinical data abstracted from medical charts and yearly updates of vital status, to study molecular and clinical differences between the types and survival.
location quote: AOV (Alberta Ovarian Tumor Types study, Canada, 1978–2010, PubMed ID: 25349970)
parent quote: OCAC (Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium).aStudy acronyms and years of interview: AOV (Alberta Ovarian Tumor Types study, Canada, 1978–2010, PubMed ID: 25349970)
note: Tier E (E055), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred for want of any paper; research settles it. The PGS Catalog lists AOTT in its cohort table but links it to no score or paper (its REST cohort endpoint returns nothing), so the tag cannot be traced to a paper there. The study is real and published under its own name, abbreviated AOV by the consortia that use it: an ovarian carcinoma histotype study of women identified through the Alberta Cancer Registry (PMID:24175302, whose first author's group describes 'an ongoing study of ovarian histological types' sampled by type), a member study of the Ovarian Tumor Tissue Analysis consortium (PMID:25349970, PMID:41922350) and one of the OCAC studies in a 2026 survival analysis. P1 (PGS Catalog evaluation paper): APCB co-listed alongside PRACTICAL, CAPS, GAME-ON/ELLIPSE and others as a separate contributing group, not stated as a member of any of them; P2-P4 (found by name): APCB as the source tissue bank for separate biomarker studies. Co-listed with PRACTICAL, CAPS and GAME-ON/ELLIPSE in P1's byline, but no unit states formal membership, so parent is left null. label: Aarhus Osteoporosis Study
example quote: We examined the effect of ALOX12 polymorphisms on BMD and the risk of fractures in two Danish cohorts: AROS, a case-control population comprising 809 individuals and DOPS, a population comprising 1,716 perimenopausal women allocated to hormone therapy or not at baseline and followed for up to 10 years.
definition: A case–control study of osteoporosis at Aarhus University Hospital, Denmark, whose cases are osteoporotic men and women with vertebral fractures and low bone mineral density and whose controls are normal individuals, assessed with dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, radiographs and bone turnover markers and genotyped for candidate-gene studies and for replication of genome-wide association findings on bone mineral density and fracture. It took part in the GENOMOS consortium and in the GEFOS meta-analysis of bone mineral density and fracture.
location quote: We examined the effect of ALOX12 polymorphisms on BMD and the risk of fractures in two Danish cohorts: AROS, a case-control population comprising 809 individuals and DOPS, a population comprising 1,716 perimenopausal women allocated to hormone therapy or not at baseline and followed for up to 10 years.
note: Tier E (E061), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred on an empty record (no papers). Research settles it: AROS is the Aarhus Osteoporosis Study, a case–control study of osteoporosis run by the Department of Endocrinology at Aarhus University Hospital. The vertebral fracture GWAS (PMID:24516880) says 'AROS (Aarhus Osteoporosis Study) is a case–control study, including 462 osteoporotic patients (vertebral fracture and T-score < −2.5) and 336 controls'; the group's own candidate-gene papers call it 'AROS, a case-control population comprising 809 individuals' in 'two Danish cohorts' (PMID:21104233, 21104228) and describe DXA and bone turnover markers in '462 osteoporotic patients and 336 normal controls' (PMID:17205326); the GEFOS 2012 supplement lists it as 'Aarhus Osteoporosis Study, Case‐control, Clinical‐based, Denmark, Aarhus' with de novo replication genotyping; the GENOMOS COLIA1 paper (PMID:16475872) counts in Aarhus 'only vertebral fractures documented radiographically at the time of enrolment'; and the GEFOS website's AROS page gives Aarhus University Hospital, case/control design, men and women aged 19–87, 'Participation in GENOMOS: Yes' and 'Participation in GEFOS (GWA): No' (no genome-wide data of its own). No parent. GENOMOS is not in COHO. GEFOS (COHO:0000826) lists AROS in its website's cohort catalogue and AROS was genotyped de novo for the GEFOS 2012 replication, but its GEFOS page says 'Participation in GEFOS (GWA): No' and no text read states membership, so no memberOf is given; the curator may add GEFOS hasCohort AROS if catalogue listing is enough. Sample counts differ between sources (462 patients and 336 controls in the Aarhus papers; 336 cases and 473 controls on the GEFOS page), so the definition gives none. DOPS (E275, Danish Osteoporosis Prevention Study) is the separate Danish cohort the Aarhus group analyses beside AROS; not a duplicate. No COHO term or review name matches.

label: Amsterdam Resuscitation Studies
other synonyms: AmsteRdam REsuscitation STudies|AmsteRdam Resuscitation Studies
example title: Association Between Delay to First Shock and Successful First-Shock Ventricular Fibrillation Termination in Patients With Witnessed Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
example quote: Patients with a witnessed out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and ventricular fibrillation (VF) as an initial rhythm were included using the prospective ARREST registry (Amsterdam Resuscitation Studies).
definition: An ongoing prospective, community-based registry, set up in June 2005 and run from the Academic Medical Center in Amsterdam, of all out-of-hospital cardiac arrests with a resuscitation attempt by emergency medical services in the province of North Holland, the Netherlands, which collects resuscitation and ECG data, outcomes, medical history from hospitals and general practitioners, medication use from community pharmacies and, since July 2007, DNA from patients with documented ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation. It studies the outcome and the clinical, pharmacological, environmental and genetic determinants of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, taking controls from pharmacy and general-practice databases for case–control analyses.
location quote: ARREST is a prospective, community-based study aimed at establishing the genetic and clinical determinants of SCA in the population of a contiguous region (urban and rural communities, ∼2.4 million inhabitants) of the Netherlands.
note: Tier E (E062), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P6 (all found by name): each refers to the same ARREST (Amsterdam Resuscitation Studies) registry; no PGS Catalog citation paper was found for this id. COHO:0000167 (Netherlands AAA GWAS dataset) is an unrelated case-control cohort, not this registry. Synonym 'AmsteRdam REsuscitation STudies' matches the PGS Catalog's own capitalisation, spelling out the acronym; most papers use plain 'Amsterdam Resuscitation Studies'. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country and example are right. The definition had the registry's purpose and dates wrong and its place vague: per the design paper (PMID:25332818, full text), 'ARREST is an ongoing, prospective observational registry of all OHCAs in the study region North Holland, a province of The Netherlands', 'setup in June 2005 to establish the determinants of outcome of OHCA', whose aims were extended only in July 2007 to genetic, clinical, pharmacological and environmental determinants, when DNA collection from patients with documented VT/VF began; it records all EMS resuscitation attempts, medical history from GPs and hospitals and medication from community pharmacies, and draws case–control controls from the PHARMO pharmacy database and a GP database (HAG-net-AMC). The draft's 'ARREST research group ... and area hospitals' is replaced by the running institution (Academic Medical Center, Amsterdam; the registry's current page is at Amsterdam UMC). The design paper's own spelling 'AmsteRdam Resuscitation Studies' is added as a synonym beside the Catalog's 'AmsteRdam REsuscitation STudies'. The name was used earlier for the 1995–1997 'Amsterdam resuscitation study (ARREST)' (PMID:9872637), whose data the 2012 Circulation paper (PMID:22869841) compares with the registry's; the design paper dates the registry itself from June 2005, so the definition does not fold the earlier study in. No consortium or parent cohort in COHO names ARREST, so no parent. COHO:0000167 (Netherlands AAA GWAS dataset) is unrelated.

label: Alzheimer's Research Trust Collaboration
other synonyms: ART Collaboration|Alzheimer's Research UK Consortium|ARUK Consortium
example title: Genome-wide association study identifies variants at CLU and PICALM associated with Alzheimer's disease.
example quote: Samples were drawn from the MRC genetic resource for AD; the ART Collaboration; Competence Network of Dementia and Department of Psychiatry, University of Bonn; Aristotle University of Thessaloniki
definition: A collaboration of United Kingdom Alzheimer's disease research groups at the Universities of Nottingham, Manchester, Southampton and Bristol, Queen's University Belfast and the Oxford Project to Investigate Memory and Ageing, funded by the Alzheimer's Research Trust (renamed Alzheimer's Research UK, after which the collaboration is called the ARUK Consortium), that pooled DNA from people with probable or post-mortem-confirmed Alzheimer's disease and from elderly controls into a DNA bank hosted at the University of Nottingham. Its cases and controls formed one of the sample collections of the GERAD genome-wide association study of Alzheimer's disease.
location quote: Human DNA samples were obtained from the Alzheimer’s Research Trust (ART) Collaboration [University of Nottingham; University of Manchester; University of Southampton; University of Bristol; Queen’s University, Belfast; the Oxford Project to Investigate Memory and Ageing (OPTIMA), Oxford University]
parent quote: The GERAD1 sample comprised up to 3941 AD cases and 7848 controls. A subset of this sample has been used in this study, comprising 3333 cases and 1225 elderly screened controls genotyped at the Sanger Institute on the Illumina 610-quad chip. These samples were recruited by the Medical Research Council (MRC) Genetic Resource for AD (Cardiff University; Kings College London; Cambridge University; Trinity College Dublin), the Alzheimer's Research Trust (ART) Collaboration (University of Nottingham; University of Manchester; University of Southampton; University of Bristol; Queen's University Belfast; the Oxford Project to Investigate Memory and Ageing (OPTIMA), Oxford University)
note: Tier E (E063), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (source GWAS of PGS000823): 'ART' denotes the Alzheimer's Research Trust Collaboration, a pooled UK multi-site AD sample; P2-P3 (PGS000823 development/evaluation): no evidence units were retrieved, so ART's usage there is unconfirmed. COHO:0000366/0000401/0000045/0000756/0000506 are other, unrelated cohorts sharing the same GWAS meta-analysis table, not ART. The plain PGS Catalog name 'Alzheimers Research Trust' denotes the funding charity (E063.4/E063.8), so left out as synonym. Two passages of the same paper give slightly different member-institution lists; a checker should verify current ART Collaboration membership. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label and type are right: the PGS id ART is the Alzheimer's Research Trust (ART) Collaboration's case–control samples in the GERAD GWAS (Harold et al. 2009), and the Catalog lists it only with the other GERAD components (MRC, WASHU, UCL-PRION, UCL-LASER, NIMH, Bonn, B58C, KORA, HNR). The definition was vague and conflated the collaboration with its funder: the draft's sentence 'ART supported sample collections at the Institute of Psychiatry, the South West Dementia Bank, Universities of Cambridge, Nottingham, Manchester and Belfast' describes the charity's grants, including MRC-resource sites (Institute of Psychiatry, Cambridge), not the collaboration, so it is also a wrong example quote; the example is now the supplementary note's list of stage-2 sample sources naming 'the ART Collaboration'. The parent was missing: the collaboration is one of the recruiting groups of the GERAD1 sample, and GERAD is COHO:0000646. The country quote was a 700-character sentence that also names Washington University, St Louis, United States; replaced by the collaboration's own member list (all UK institutions). After the charity was renamed ('Alzheimer's Research UK (formerly the Alzheimer's Research Trust)', PMID:23459933) the same groups publish as the ARUK Consortium, which hosts its DNA bank at Nottingham and whose 2018 CR1 paper takes its samples 'from the Alzheimer’s Research Trust (ART) Collaboration' (PMID:29675612); those names are added as synonyms. Diagnoses: 'definite (post mortem confirmed) or probable Alzheimer’s disease (AD)' by NINCDS-ADRDA and CERAD criteria (PMID:29675612). Kept as an aggregation: the collaboration pools sample collections from separate groups, one of them a cohort in its own right (OPTIMA, Oxford Project to Investigate Memory and Ageing, not in COHO), though GERAD analyses them as one sample. The PGS Catalog name 'Alzheimers Research Trust' is the funding charity's name, so it is not added as a synonym (the draft's choice kept). The ARUK Consortium synonyms rest on the same member groups and the charity's renaming, not on a sentence saying the collaboration was renamed; drop them if that is thought too indirect. The other GERAD components in this review: MRC (D474, judged not a cohort), UCL-LASER (E1134) and UCL-PRION (E1135).

COHO:0000024/0000818/0000870/0000598/0000485/0000183 are other, unrelated cohorts sharing the same multi-cohort supplementary table (table row, unquotable), not ASHRAM.
