The definition named only basal cell carcinoma 'such as' and left out what the study is: the BCC paper's methods (PMID:22436128, full text) say the BCC series 'was part of a larger study of skin, bladder, and kidney cancers with a common referent population', whose controls were general surgery, orthopaedic and trauma in-patients aged 30–79 recruited 'from all 24 hospitals in the study area' and 'frequency matched to all potential cancer cases by sex, 5-year age band, and residence in the same county/region'; the kidney cancer GWAS supplement (PMID:21131975) describes ASHRAM as 'a case–control study concerning cancer risks in relation to low-level arsenic exposure via drinking water in Central Europe', hospital based, 2002–2004. The name that GWAS uses, 'Arsenic Health Risk Assessment and Molecular Epidemiology study in Central Europe', is added as a synonym. No parent. In the RCC GWAS the ASHRAM cases were analysed against controls that the supplement says were originally matched to lung cancer cases and included in a previous lung cancer GWAS (its ref. 41, Hung et al. 2008); the supplement does not say which study those controls belong to, so no relation to COHO:0000870 (IARC central European lung cancer study) is asserted. The other COHO terms the draft listed (COHO:0000024, 0000818, 0000870, 0000598, 0000485, 0000183) are different cohorts in the same GWAS tables.

example quote: The aim of this study within the Athens Study of Psychosis Proneness and Incidence of Schizophrenia (ASPIS) was the examination of the latent structure of schizotypal dimensions among a large population of young male conscripts in the Greek Air Force during their first week of military training.
definition: A study of young men aged 18–24 doing compulsory military service in Greece, randomly selected in successive waves during their first two weeks at the National Basic Air Force Training Center in Tripolis, who completed self-rated questionnaires on schizotypy and psychopathology and computerised neurocognitive and eye-movement tasks and gave DNA, a subgroup being reassessed at discharge two years later. Led from the University Mental Health Research Institute in Athens, it studies psychosis proneness and its cognitive and genetic correlates in the general population.
location quote: The aim of this study within the Athens Study of Psychosis Proneness and Incidence of Schizophrenia (ASPIS) was the examination of the latent structure of schizotypal dimensions among a large population of young male conscripts in the Greek Air Force during their first week of military training.
note: Tier E (E065), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P5 (all found by name): each refers to the same ASPIS cohort of Greek Air Force conscripts; no PGS Catalog citation paper was found for this id. No COHO term or candidate was listed for this name. All five papers consistently describe the same Greek military-conscript cohort; none gives an establishment date or total sample size beyond individual sub-study subsets, so none is included. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country and example are right. The definition was close but called the study purely cross-sectional, said conscripts were 'undergoing induction to Air Force training' without place or selection, and omitted who runs it. The RGS4 paper (PMID:18834502, full text) summarises the design: ASPIS 'examined 2243 randomly selected young male conscripts aged 18 to 24 years from the Greek Air Force in their first 2 weeks of admission to the National Basic Air Force Training Center', with computerised neurocognitive and eye-movement tasks, self-rated psychometrics and DNA from mouthwash samples, approved by the University Mental Health Research Institute's committee; the ZNF804A paper (PMID:23155182) places the centre 'in Tripolis, Greece' and says '8 such consecutive separate waves of conscripts were assessed'; a subgroup was re-examined '2 years later (T(2)-second assessment), at the time of military discharge' (PMID:22503357 abstract). No parent in COHO. ASPIS is one of the cohorts of the COGENT (Cognitive Genomics Consortium) GWAS of general cognitive function (PMID:28093568), but that consortium is not in COHO; COHO:0000999's acronym COGENT denotes a different consortium (Continental Origins and Genetic Epidemiology Network), so beware the clash if the cognitive consortium is ever added. No COHO term or review name matches ASPIS.

label: Australian Twin Eye Study
other synonyms: Australian Twin Eye study
example title: Copy number variation at chromosome 5q21.2 is associated with intraocular pressure.
example quote: The Australian Twin Eye Study and BMES both replicated the 5q21.2 CNV association and direction of effect (P = 0.001 and P = 0.02, respectively).
definition: An Australian twin study of eye traits that combines twins, and some of their siblings, given an eye examination in the Twins Eye Study in Tasmania or in the Brisbane Adolescent Twin Study, with measures such as cycloplegic refraction, intraocular pressure and retinal photographs and with genome-wide genotypes, used in heritability, linkage and genome-wide association studies of ophthalmic traits. Its participants were recruited through the Australian Twin Registry, existing twin studies, schools and publicity.
note: Tier E (E066), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (ATES's own review paper, found by name): describes ATES directly alongside the unrelated 'Genes in Myopia (GEM)' study. P2 (found by name): treats ATES as one of three twin/population eye-genetics panels (with TwinsUK and BMES). COHO:0000682 (Ginkgo Evaluation of Memory Study, GEM) is an unrelated dementia trial; P1's own 'GEM' (Genes in Myopia) is a different, uncaptured study, not that COHO term. COHO:0000722 (RISK) and COHO:0000175 (TwinsUK) are also unrelated, merely co-listed panels. Checked 2026-09-23: The name is right but the draft missed what the Australian Twin Eye Study is: every paper that describes it says it is made of two other studies' participants, 'The Australian Twin Eye Study comprised participants examined as part of the Twins Eye Study in Tasmania or the Brisbane Adolescent Twins Study' (Solouki 2010, PMID:20835236; the same in PMID:23599335 and PMID:23776548). Both are distinct cohorts: the Brisbane Adolescent Twin Study is COHO:0000744 and the Twins Eye Study in Tasmania is E1102 of this review, so the name is an umbrella over them and is typed as an aggregation, not a cohort (BATS as a whole cannot be a sub-cohort of it). The definition only restated the review abstract; it now says whom it combines and what was measured (post-cycloplegic refraction in PMID:20835236, Tono-Pen IOP in PMID:23599335, retinal photography in the TEST papers), and how twins were found (the TEST methods paper, PMID:19803772: existing twin studies, the national twin registry, word-of-mouth and media, schools, other twin research groups, and a final wave 'recruited from the BATS at QIMR', plus siblings). The Catalog's own spelling 'Australian Twin Eye study' is added as a capitalisation variant. Members to record from this aggregation with hasCohort: COHO:0000744 (Brisbane Longitudinal Twin Study, acronym BATS) and E1102 (Twins Eye Study in Tasmania, when minted), both with the quote 'The Australian Twin Eye Study comprised participants examined as part of the Twins Eye Study in Tasmania or the Brisbane Adolescent Twins Study.' from https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/bionlp/RESTful/pmcoa.cgi/BioC_xml/PMC4115148/unicode. Whoever checks E1102 should note that the TEST methods paper counts the BATS eye examinations as TEST's last recruitment wave, while the GWAS papers treat TEST and BATS as the two parts of ATES. Recruitment through the Australian Twin Registry (COHO:0000015) is not a sub-cohort relation, so no parent. The draft's claim that P1's 'Genes in Myopia (GEM)' study is uncaptured is wrong: it is E425 (GIMS, 'Genes in Myopia study') of this review, unrelated to COHO:0000682 (Ginkgo Evaluation of Memory Study).

label: AtheroGene Registry

example title: Impact of C-reactive protein and fibrinogen on cardiovascular prognosis in patients with stable angina pectoris: the AtheroGene study.
example quote: In a substudy of the prospective AtheroGene registry, we assessed in 1806 patients with documented CAD and stable angina pectoris, the risk of cardiovascular death and non-fatal myocardial infarction (n=183) over a median follow-up of 3.5 (maximum 7.7) years according to baseline levels of C-reactive protein and fibrinogen.
definition: A prospective clinical cohort of patients with coronary artery disease (at least one coronary stenosis over 30% on angiography), from stable angina to acute coronary syndromes, enrolled in successive phases from November 1996 to early 2004 when they underwent coronary angiography at the Department of Medicine II of the Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz or the Bundeswehrzentralkrankenhaus Koblenz, Germany, and followed for cardiovascular death and non-fatal myocardial infarction. It studies clinical, genetic and laboratory determinants of the progression and outcome of coronary atherosclerosis, and for genetic case–control analyses also recruited healthy controls from the Rhein-Main area.
location quote: Between June 1999 and March 2004, 3800 patients who underwent coronary angiography were recruited in the AtheroGene Study at the Department of Medicine II of the Johannes Gutenberg-University Mainz and the Bundeswehr-Zentralkrankenhaus Koblenz
note: Tier E (E067), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred with a label, acronyms and an example but no definition; open-access papers of the cohort settle it. 'The AtheroGene study is a prospective, multicenter, clinical cohort study including patients with known CAD (at least one stenosis over 30%) as diagnosed by coronary angiography', covering acute coronary syndrome and stable angina, aimed 'to elucidate clinical, genetic and laboratory factors associated with progression of coronary atherosclerosis and outcome during follow-up' (PMID:26154343); patients were 'enrolled during several successive phases of recruitment between November 1996 and February 2004' at the Medical Department of the Johannes Gutenberg-University Mainz or the Bundeswehrzentralkrankenhaus Koblenz (PMID:23136988), the larger phase from June 1999 to March 2004 (PMID:32321351, 30096922); healthy controls from GP check-ups or newspaper announcements, inhabitants of the Rhein-Main area, were added for genetic comparisons (PMID:19495570). The draft's label is one the group itself uses ('the hospital-based catheter-lab AtheroGene Registry', PMID:21606135) and matches the Catalog's name, so it is kept; 'AtheroGene Study', the name in most of its paper titles, and 'Large AtheroGene Study' are added as synonyms. The country quote names the recruiting hospitals in Mainz and Koblenz, both in Germany; the same paper's ethics sentence names 'the State Rhineland-Palatinate (Germany)'. No parent: nothing read names AtheroGene as part of another cohort or consortium in COHO (the AtheroRemo tag of E068 denotes LURIC samples, not this registry), and CADomics (E144 of this review) is a case–control GWAS sample whose cases come from this registry and whose controls come from the 'Gutenberg-Heart Study (GHS)', presumably COHO:0000263 (Gutenberg Health Study); whoever checks E144 should relate it to this term rather than treat it as a duplicate.

label: Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health Study
other synonyms: LURIC/AtheroRemo
note: Tier E (E068), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. label: Australian Twin Migraine
other synonyms: Australian Twin Migraine GWA study|Australian Twin Migraine GWA Study|Australia ATM
example quote: The Australian Twin Migraine (ATM) GWA study includes data from Australian twins and their families.
definition: A genome-wide association case–control sample of unrelated Australians of European descent, one from each family, drawn from the twins and their relatives studied at the Queensland Institute of Medical Research (QIMR) who were genotyped genome-wide: migraine cases, identified in semi-structured telephone interviews based on the International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD-II) or by self-report and chosen preferentially for severity, and population controls from families with no known migraine. It is one of the studies of the International Headache Genetics Consortium.
parent quote: ATM Australian Twin Migraine 1,683 2,383
note: Tier E (E071), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred, having no evidence at all; research settles it. The PGS id ATM has no scores and no papers (the REST cohort endpoint returns nothing; it is only in the Catalog's cohort list), but its name 'Australia ATM' is copied from the study column of Supplementary Table 2 of the 2013 IHGC migraine meta-analysis (PMID:23793025), where the cell reads 'Australia' over 'ATM' with references 20303062 and 18676988. ATM is the Australian Twin Migraine GWA study: 'The Australian Twin Migraine (ATM) GWA study includes data from Australian twins and their families', with cases and population controls, one unrelated person per family, 'drawn from our QIMR GWA cohort of over 19,000 individuals genotyped using a variety of Illumina GWA arrays'. Migraine was assessed in semi-structured telephone interviews based on ICHD-II, plus self-reported migraine (PMID:24081561). It is a named, defined case-control sample contributing to the International Headache Genetics Consortium (COHO:0000102; Table 1 of the 2016 meta-analysis lists 'ATM | Australian Twin Migraine'), so a new cohort and member of IHGC. No other Australian cohort abbreviated ATM was found. Acronym ATM is used by no other COHO term. 'Australia ATM' is kept as a synonym because it is the PGS Catalog's full name for the id; it is the IHGC table cell, not a name the study uses, so the curator may drop it. One of ATM's references (PMID:18676988) describes QIMR's Brisbane migraine sample as two Australian Twin Registry cohorts interviewed by telephone in 1993-1995 (born 1902-1964) and 1996-2000 (born 1964-1975), in interviews assessing alcohol use and related disorders; these may be the interviews of the Australian alcohol studies (COHO:0000841), but no source says ATM is part of another cohort, so no isSubCohortOf is given. The cases were split into ATM1 (ICHD-II migraine without aura) and ATM2 (self-reported migraine) strata in the IHGC analyses; these are strata, not cohorts. Distinct from E076 AUSTWIN, another QIMR label.

input name: Asthma UK Genetics of Severe Asthma
label: Asthma UK Genetics of Severe Asthma
example title: A large-scale, consortium-based genomewide association study of asthma.
example quote: We did find a suggestive association with rs1837253 on chromosome 5, situated within the TSLP gene, among patients with severe asthma in the SEVERE study (P = 3×10−6; odds ratio, 0.56), but this association was not replicated among patients with severe asthma in the AUGOSA (Asthma UK Genetics of Severe Asthma) study.
definition: A genetic study of severe asthma in the United Kingdom, supported by Asthma UK, which recruited people of European ancestry with severe asthma (Global Initiative for Asthma classes 3–5) at UK centres and compared them in genome-wide association studies with controls without asthma or wheeze, to identify genetic determinants of severe asthma and whether they differ from those of mild to moderate asthma.
location quote: Only subjects in classes 3–5 were included, recruited across UK-based centres.
note: Tier E (E072), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (source GWAS of PGS000037): AUGOSA is a distinct UK severe-asthma genetics study contributing samples to this asthma GWAS meta-analysis, explicitly separate from the 'SEVERE' study; P2 (score development paper): no evidence units extracted. Listed COHO candidates (PIAMA, SAPALDIA, SLSJ, two SAGE cohorts) are unrelated cohorts sharing the same evidence table, not AUGOSA itself. Country UK inferred from 'Asthma UK' in the name; a flattened table in the full text (E072.4) also ties AUGOSA to United Kingdom. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type and example were right, but the definition only restated the name ('a cohort of people with severe asthma in the United Kingdom ... studied for the genetic basis of severe asthma'): the drafter saw only the GABRIEL paper, not AUGOSA's own GWAS. That is Wan et al. 2012 (Thorax, PMID:22561531, open access, keyword AUGOSA; 'Individuals in AUGOSA were included in the total case subjects in the GABRIEL study'): people of European ancestry with severe asthma, GINA classes 3-5, recruited across UK-based centres (eight major centres), compared with clean controls without asthma or wheeze, aiming 'first to identify genetic determinants of severe asthma, and second to evaluate whether susceptibility to severe asthma differs from that of mild to moderate asthma'; funded by Asthma UK, the Wellcome Trust and the MRC. The definition now says so. The country was asserted 'from the name', but the UK in the name is the charity Asthma UK, so a recruitment quote replaces it. AUGOSA's controls in its own GWAS were 'collected from the UK and Western Australia' (borrowed control sets such as the 1958 birth cohort), so only the UK is given as the recruitment country. Scope differs between papers: in Wan et al. 2012 the AUGOSA cases 'were selected from individuals participating in the Difficult/Severe Asthma (BTS) study (n=290), supplemented with subjects from other centres', while GABRIEL lists AUGOSA and SEVERE (290 UK severe-asthma cases, apparently the same BTS study) as separate sets; the checker of tier-E row E1012 (PGS id SEVERE, 'Severe Asthma Cohorts') should weigh this. The GABRIEL consortium has no COHO term, so no parent. The Thorax supplement with per-centre recruitment could not be fetched (rate-limited).

label: Amsterdam UMC dilated cardiomyopathy GWAS cohort
note: Tier E (E073), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. same cohort as review name E074. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft judged AUMC an author affiliation because the drafter looked for 'Amsterdam UMC' in the AF paper's text. The PGS Catalog does not use the id for the paper's own cohorts. The multi-trait AF scores PGS012532-PGS012536 combine GWAS of AF and seven correlated traits, and the Catalog lists each input GWAS as a development sample. AUMC is a cohort of one of those samples: 9,365 cases and 946,368 controls, phenotype 'I42.0' (dilated cardiomyopathy), European, source DOI 10.1038/s41588-024-01975-5, with cohorts 'AUMC' (Amsterdam UMC), 'MGBB', 'UKB' and 'FinnGen' (PGS Catalog REST, score PGS012532). That DOI is the Jurgens et al. 2024 DCM GWAS (PMID:39572784), whose clinical datasets include 'a new dataset of Dutch DCM cases from Amsterdam UMC'. The AF paper's supplementary table of training GWAS confirms 'DCM Jurgens 9,365 / 946,368 ... https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-024-01975-5'. So AUMC denotes the same Amsterdam UMC dilated cardiomyopathy dataset as AUMC_DCM (row E074), and becomes an acronym of that record. The PGS Catalog's full name for the id is just the institution, 'Amsterdam UMC'. It is not added as a synonym, because it names the hospital, not the dataset, and other Amsterdam UMC cohorts exist (COHO:0000374 Amsterdam Dementia Cohort; E050 Amsterdam UMC COVID study group). The id's Catalog cohort list omits the Garnier and Heidelberg clinical DCM sets that the DCM GWAS also used, so AUMC is the Amsterdam component only. No other COHO term uses the acronym AUMC. No separate example: the AF paper names only 'DCM Jurgens', not the Amsterdam cohort, and E074's example (PMID:39572784) serves the merged record.

input name: Amsterdam UMC dilated cardiomyopathy GWAS cohort
label: Amsterdam UMC dilated cardiomyopathy GWAS cohort
other synonyms: Amsterdam UMC cohort
example title: Genome-wide association study reveals mechanisms underlying dilated cardiomyopathy and myocardial resilience.
example quote: The Amsterdam cohort comprised DCM patients referred for genetic testing at Amsterdam UMC, who underwent chart review for DCM diagnosis and had evidence of hypocontractility on imaging; 978 DCM cases passed all genotype quality-control criteria, of which 783 homogeneous cases of patients of European ancestry were included in GWAS (Supplementary Note and Supplementary Table 3).
definition: A case–control dataset for genome-wide association studies of dilated cardiomyopathy assembled at Amsterdam UMC, the Netherlands. Its cases are adult index patients referred by secondary or tertiary cardiologists to Amsterdam UMC for genetic testing for dilated cardiomyopathy, with the diagnosis confirmed from the medical chart and a left ventricular ejection fraction below 50%, and its controls are unrelated participants of the Netherlands Twin Register.

note: Tier E (E074), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: AUMC_DCM = 'the Amsterdam cohort', one of six datasets (3 clinical DCM case-control sets, 3 biobank cohorts: FinnGen, UKB, MGB) pooled in this DCM GWAS/MTAG meta-analysis; a new clinical dataset, distinct from the other clinical DCM sets (Garnier et al., Heidelberg/Meder et al.). Label combines 'the Amsterdam cohort' (E074.21) with the institution+disease naming used throughout, paralleling PGS Catalog's 'Amsterdam UMC dilated cardiomyopathy GWAS cohort' (dropping non-name 'GWAS'). Distinct from row E073/AUMC, an unrelated AF paper's author affiliation, not a dataset. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, country and example were right. The label was a construction ('Amsterdam UMC dilated cardiomyopathy cohort') found in no source. The paper's own name is only 'the Amsterdam UMC cohort' (Supplementary Note heading 'Amsterdam UMC Cohort study description and methods'), which names the hospital, so the PGS Catalog's name, the one specific name in use, becomes the label and the paper's name a synonym. The definition left out half the dataset and gave an ethics waiver instead of the design. The Supplementary Note's section on the cohort gives the design: cases are 'index patients referred by secondary or tertiary cardiologists to the Amsterdam UMC for genetic testing for DCM', diagnosis 'confirmed for all patients by manual examination of the medical chart, with a required left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of less than 50%', age over 18, and 'The control group was sourced from the Dutch Twin Register (NTR)' (unrelated NTR participants). The acronyms missed AUMC: the PGS Catalog uses that id for this same dataset in PGS012532-PGS012536 (see E073). The controls come from the Netherlands Twin Register (COHO:0000125), but the case set is recruited separately at the hospital, so no isSubCohortOf is asserted. 'Amsterdam UMC cohort' is generic: if the curator prefers not to carry it, the paper's other wording ('a new dataset of Dutch DCM cases from Amsterdam UMC') gives no better name. Merge E073 (PGS id AUMC) into this record.

label: Austrian Diabetic Nephropathy Study
other synonyms: Austrian Diabetes Nephropathy Study
example title: Genome-Wide Association Study of Diabetic Kidney Disease Highlights Biology Involved in Glomerular Basement Membrane Collagen.
example quote: The Austrian Diabetic Nephropathy Study (AusDiane) was initiated in 2012 in the state of Salzburg in Austria, and is part of the InterDiane Consortium (please see also the InterDiane cohort description).
definition: A clinic-based cohort study of patients with type 1 diabetes in the state of Salzburg, Austria, initiated in 2012 as the Austrian study of the International Diabetic Nephropathy Consortium (InterDiane), which follows the protocol of the Finnish Diabetic Nephropathy Study to identify risk factors for diabetic nephropathy and other chronic complications of type 1 diabetes. Patients are recruited consecutively at the outpatient departments of Paracelsus Medical University Hospital Salzburg and Diakonissen-Wehrle Hospital Salzburg, with clinical data drawn mainly from the Type 1 diabetes Registry of the state of Salzburg, and are re-examined every 1 to 1.5 years.
note: Tier E (E075), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred, having seen only the acknowledgement; research settles it. The DKD GWAS (PMID:31537649) describes the cohort in its Supplementary Data (the LWW supplemental file, openly downloadable): 'The Austrian Diabetic Nephropathy Study (AusDiane) was initiated in 2012 in the state of Salzburg in Austria, and is part of the InterDiane Consortium'. Patients with type 1 diabetes are studied at two Salzburg hospitals, recruited consecutively in their outpatient departments, with clinical data 'collected mainly as part of the Type 1 diabetes Registry of the state of Salzburg', and re-studied every 1 to 1.5 years. InterDiane ('The International Diabetic Nephropathy Consortium') 'was initiated in 2010 based on the protocol of the FinnDiane Study' to identify risk factors for diabetic nephropathy and other chronic complications in T1D. Supplemental Table 1 types it a 'Clinic based cohort study'. So it is a new cohort. The draft's example quote, 'AusDiane acknowledges Dr.', was a three-word fragment of an acknowledgement and is replaced. Its sibling InterDiane cohorts are review rows E618 LatDiane, E634 LitDiane and E971 RomDiane, described in the same supplement; the InterDiane consortium itself has no COHO term or review row, so no parent is given (if the curator mints InterDiane as an aggregation, these four are its members, quote: 'InterDiane centers included in this study come from Romania, Austria, Latvia and Lithuania.'). The synonym 'Austrian Diabetes Nephropathy Study' is the name in the paper's Supplemental Table 1 ('Cohorts contributing to analyses', https://links.lww.com/JSN/C815). Distinct from the Finnish Diabetic Nephropathy Study (COHO:0000496), whose protocol it follows.

label: Australian Alcohol and Nicotine Studies
other synonyms: Australian Twin-Family Studies
note: Tier E (E076), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred, having no evidence; research settles it as COHO:0000841 (Australian Alcohol and Nicotine Studies). The PGS id has no scores or papers, but its name, 'Australian Twin-Family Studies', is the GIANT consortium's label for the QIMR twin-family sample in the smoking-adjusted obesity GWAS (Justice et al. 2017, PMID:28443625). That paper's supplementary study table reads 'AUSTWIN Australian Twin‐Family Studies Population‐based European Australia 2166 95% 1) mendelian errors 2) HWE p < 10‐6 3) sample call rate 96% Self‐reported NA NA 21529783' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC5414044/supplementaryFiles). The reference it cites, PMID:21529783 (Heath et al. 2011, the OZ-ALC alcoholism GWAS of sibships ascertained through the Australian Twin Registry), is the source of COHO:0000841's definition. Its acknowledgement thanks the QIMR Genetic Epidemiology Unit and lists the NIH alcohol and nicotine grants of those studies (AA07535, AA10248, AA11998, AA13320, AA13321, AA13326, AA14041, AA17688, DA12854). Europe PMC finds no other paper using the full name. COHO:0000841 already carries the similar synonym 'Australian Twin-Family Studies on Nicotine and Alcohol Genetics'. So AUSTWIN and 'Australian Twin-Family Studies' are added to it. The label AUSTWIN does not always cover the same people. In the PGS Catalog, PGS000809's source GWAS (Patsopoulos et al. 2011, PMID:22190364, GCST001341) lists its cohorts as IMSGC_UK, IMSGC_US, Gene_MSA_US/NL/CH, ANZgene, BWH and BayerScheringPharma, splitting that paper's 'BWH/TT' stratum ('Values are for BWH cases and TT cases separately'). The member trials (BENEFIT, BEYOND, the IFNβ-1b long-term follow-up and the CCR1-antagonist study) have no COHO terms. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, country and example were right, but the definition only listed three later nested sub-studies (placental glucocorticoid-receptor methylation, smoking metabolomics, FGF23 and gestational diabetes) instead of saying who the cohort is. The cohort's own references, cited for it by the EGG consortium papers and by its later papers, describe it: consecutive singleton deliveries at the Charité obstetrics department (PMID:19696694), mother/child pairs with maternal and fetal blood at delivery (PMID:17030683), 1023 mothers delivering at the Charité 2000-2008 with placentas collected after delivery (PMC6976643, cited as the BBC reference by PMC7820257 and PMC8081388), and the EGG maternal-GWAS study table (PMC5886200 Supplementary Table 2: 'Community-based', offspring born 2000-2004, birth weight measured 'in a single big center'). The draft missed the parent: BCINIS is a study of the Breast Cancer Association Consortium (COHO:0000020), named in BCAC's data-access statement and study tables, which is why the PGS Catalog lists it. Same centre and control-sampling scheme as the Molecular Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer study (MECC, COHO:0000618), but a separate study; no parent link between them. E785 (PGS id NICCC, 'National Israeli Cancer Control Center') is recorded by the Catalog only for the CIMBA paper PMID:32665703, i.e. that centre's BRCA1/2 carrier data, not BCINIS. PMID:37451831's label for the BCAC data set, BCAC-IL, is a one-paper tag and is not added.

label: Blood-Cell Consortium
other synonyms: Blood Cell Consortium
example title: Exome Genotyping Identifies Pleiotropic Variants Associated with Red Blood Cell Traits.
example quote: The Blood-Cell Consortium (BCX) aims to identify novel common and rare variants associated with blood-cell traits using an exome array.
definition: An international consortium of cohort studies and biobanks, organised in red blood cell, white blood cell and platelet working groups, that meta-analyses genetic associations with blood-cell counts and indices in participants of European, African, Hispanic/Latino, East Asian and South Asian ancestry, first with exome-array genotypes and later (its second phase, BCX2) with genome-wide imputed data, to identify common and rare variants that influence blood-cell traits.
note: Tier E (E101), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1/P3: BCX's RBC and PLT/MPV working groups (source consortium); P2: cites BCX-derived scores; P4-P8: BCX summary statistics used as an external GWAS source in MR studies. Sizes vary by trait/paper (130,273 RBC; 157,293 PLT) so omitted from definition. 'BCX2' (E101.25) may be an African-ancestry extension; not conflated with BCX here. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type (aggregation), acronym and example are right. The definition described only the consortium's first, exome-array phase: BCX went on to a genome-wide second phase, which papers call BCX2 ('BCX2 is a consortium comprising of trans-ethnic data of blood cell traits of 746,667 individuals from five different ancestries', PMID:34925446, PMC8674726, citing the 2020 trans-ethnic GWAS PMID:32888493, which itself says 'we followed the protocol developed by the Blood-Cell Consortium'); most papers that use 'Blood Cell Consortium' summary statistics (the draft's P5-P8 MR studies) use that second phase. The definition now covers both phases; its first-phase claims stand on PMID:27346685 ('The Blood-Cell Consortium (BCX) aims to identify novel common and rare variants associated with blood-cell traits using an exome array'; 'five ancestries: European, African American, Hispanic, East Asian, and South Asian'; 'divided into three main working groups: RBC, white blood cell (WBC), and platelet (PLT)') and PMID:27346686 ('we formed the Blood Cell Consortium (BCX) to perform a large-scale meta-analysis of Exomechip association results for PLT and MPV'). Countries left empty: an international consortium whose member cohorts (24 discovery cohorts in phase 1, listed in PMID:27346685 Table S1, which PMC would not serve) are located individually. hasCohort candidates with quotes: Framingham Heart Study (COHO:0000385), Montreal Heart Institute Biobank (COHO:0000615) and Women's Health Initiative (COHO:0000409): 'To assess whether the genetic associations with RBC traits are independent of lipid levels, we performed additional analyses in a subset of BCX participants from three of our studies (FHS, MHIBB, and WHI) ranging from ∼10,000 to 23,000 individuals.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5005438/); for BCX2's African-ancestry data, BioMe (COHO:0000424), Cardiovascular Health Study (COHO:0000384), GERA (COHO:0000431), Jackson Heart Study (COHO:0000381), MESA (COHO:0000119) and UK Biobank (COHO:0000176): 'From the BCX2, we retrieved WBC traits from individuals with African ancestry composed of data pulled from the BioMe™ BioBank Program, Cardiovascular Health Study, Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging, Jackson Heart Study, The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, and the UK Biobank African ancestry.' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC8674726/fullTextXML). BCX2 is the consortium's second phase, not another cohort; it is used by one third-party paper only, so it is not added as an acronym (add it if phase labels are wanted). No duplicate in COHO (COHO:0000451 Red Blood Cell-Omics Study is unrelated) or in tiers D/E.

Tier E (E102), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred on an empty record, and research does not identify the sample. BD ('Belgian Donors') is only in the PGS Catalog's cohort list (src/curation/pgs_catalog_cohorts.csv): https://www.pgscatalog.org/rest/cohort/BD returns no record, the score, sample-set and performance dumps never use it, the Catalog's website search for 'Belgian' finds nothing, no GWAS Catalog study carries the tag, and Europe PMC full-text searches for 'Belgian donors' (12 hits) or 'Belgian blood donors' in genetic studies find no paper that names a 'Belgian Donors' sample. Without the paper the Catalog took it from, no label, definition or example can be written. Most likely a control series of Belgian (Red Cross Flanders) blood or plasma donors genotyped for a Belgian case-control GWAS (Leuven groups used such donors as controls for breast cancer, schizophrenia and, via IMSGC, stroke and multiple sclerosis), listed in some consortium's cohort table; if the source table turns up, the term would be that control series, or no term if it is only the controls of a named case-control study. Not the same as E106 (Belgium_AD, the Antwerp Flanders-Belgian Alzheimer cohort, whose controls were patients' partners and community volunteers, not donors). No COHO term or tier D/E name is a candidate duplicate.

input name: Bavarian Endometrial Cancer Cases and Controls Study
label: Bavarian Endometrial Cancer Cases and Controls Study
other synonyms: Bavarian Endometrial Cancer Study
example quote: Replication analysis in the German population included 221 cases from the Bavarian Endometrial Cancer Study (BECS) and 251 healthy controls aged 55 years and older from the Bavarian Breast Cancer Cases and Controls (BBCC).
definition: A single-centre case-control study of endometrial cancer at the University Hospital Erlangen in Bavaria, Germany, conducted between 2002 and 2008 to investigate genetic and epidemiological risk factors for endometrial cancer, whose cases were incident cases referred to the hospital by surrounding practitioners or prevalent cases approached during follow-up care after treatment there for primary endometrial cancer, with epidemiological information from a structured interview questionnaire and clinical data from health records.
location quote: Replication analysis in the German population included 221 cases from the Bavarian Endometrial Cancer Study (BECS) and 251 healthy controls aged 55 years and older from the Bavarian Breast Cancer Cases and Controls (BBCC).
parent quote: We conducted replication analysis of the 15 loci detected in the discovery GWAS in two separate cohorts (Belgian and German), previously used within the collaboration of ECAC [5]. Replication in the Belgian population included 528 cases from the Leuven Endometrial Cancer Study (LES) and 1,266 controls from blood donors of the Leuven Multidisciplinary Breast Centre Study (LMBC). Replication analysis in the German population included 221 cases from the Bavarian Endometrial Cancer Study (BECS) and 251 healthy controls aged 55 years and older from the Bavarian Breast Cancer Cases and Controls (BBCC).
note: Tier E (E104), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred on an empty record; research settles it. The PGS Catalog records no score or paper for BECS (REST cohort/BECS empty), but the name is exactly the study's own: the Endometrial Cancer Association Consortium's 2016 GWAS describes it in its Supplementary Note ('BECS The Bavarian Endometrial Cancer Cases and Controls Study (BECS) is a single-center case-control study, conducted between 2002 and 2008, with the aim of investigating genetic and epidemiological risk factors for endometrial cancer.'; 'Cases were either incident cases referred to the University Hospital Erlangen by surrounding practitioners (66% of the case sample set), or prevalent cases that were outpatients in follow-up care approached within 6.2 (±4.6 SD) years after treatment for primary endometrial cancer in the same hospital (34% of the case sample set).', https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC4907351/supplementaryFiles). Consortium papers also call it 'The Bavarian Endometrial Cancer Study (BECS)'. Its cases were genotyped in ECAC's iCOGS and OncoArray phases (PMID:27135401 Supplementary Table 1; PMID:30093612 Supplementary Data 1) and, as a German ECAC cohort, in a 2025 Swedish replication study (PMID:40101186). In the consortium's GWAS the BECS cases were compared with German controls from breast cancer studies, mainly the Bavarian Breast Cancer Cases and Controls Study (COHO:0001058) run by the same Erlangen department, so the 'Controls' of the name are not described as a series of its own in any text read and the definition does not claim them. The ECAC tables' 'hospital-based cases, population-based cases' is shared with the Hannover-Jena study (E480) in the iCOGS row; the study's own description says single-centre. Sister studies of the Erlangen group are COHO:0001058 (BBCC) and tier-E row E127 (BOCC, Bavarian Ovarian Cancer Cases and Controls); none is a duplicate. hasCohort link from COHO:0001316 (ECAC) with the quote given as parent.

input name: Belfast Elderly Longitudinal Free-living Ageing Study
label: Belfast Elderly Longitudinal Free-living Ageing Study
other synonyms: Belfast Elderly Longitudinal Free-living Ageing STudy|Belfast Elderly Longitudinal Free-living Aging STudy|Belfast Elderly Longitudinal Free-living Aging Study|BELFAST study
example title: Apolipoprotein E alleles in nonagenarian subjects in the Belfast Elderly Longitudinal Free-living Ageing Study (BELFAST).
example quote: Apolipoprotein E alleles in nonagenarian subjects in the Belfast Elderly Longitudinal Free-living Ageing Study (BELFAST).
definition: A longitudinal study of ageing by the Belfast Longevity Group of Queen's University Belfast, Northern Ireland, of 'elite' octogenarians and nonagenarians, and some centenarians: community-living, apparently well, independently mobile and mentally competent people recruited through their general practitioners in the Greater Belfast area and seen at home by a research nurse, who took their medical history, anthropometric and blood pressure measurements and blood samples for DNA and laboratory tests, with nutrition and lifestyle questionnaires, to study the immunological, cardiovascular, nutritional and genetic factors of healthy ageing and longevity.
location quote: In the BELFAST study, 90 year old subjects, who were ‘very good’ for their age, also called ‘elite’ and met the Senieur protocol (Lightart et al. 1984), were recruited through their General Practitioners, from the Greater Belfast area.
note: Tier E (E105), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P4: all denote the same Belfast free-living ageing study of nonagenarians (and centenarians in P2). PGS tag 'BELFAS' truncates the papers' own acronym 'BELFAST' (both kept as acronyms). 'STudy' capitalisation (P2-P4) shows Belfast+ST=BELFAST; kept as synonym alongside the standard-caps label. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronyms (the study's own BELFAST and the PGS Catalog's truncated BELFAS), type, country and example are right. The definition was built from abstracts and said only 'community-living nonagenarians, and some centenarians, in Belfast': the study's methods describe octogenarians as well as nonagenarians ('Briefly, when recruited, BELFAST octo/nonagenarians were community-living, apparently well, independently mobile, mentally competent', PMID:19496022, PMC2813048, which calls it 'a longitudinal study of ageing'), selected as 'elite' and recruited through their general practitioners in the Greater Belfast area (PMID:25773008, PMC4552771), and seen at home by a research nurse who took medical history, anthropometric measurements and blood samples (PMID:19496022). The definition now says so. The US spellings used in two titles ('Belfast Elderly Longitudinal Free-living Aging STudy', PMID:19496022; 'Belfast Elderly Longitudinal Free-living Aging Study', PMID:15247052) and 'BELFAST study' are added as synonyms; the country, asserted from the name, now has a quote. The recruitment years are not stated in the texts read (the design paper the study's papers cite as Rea et al. 2000 was not read), so the definition gives no dates. The cases' comparison group in the ApoE paper (Belfast MONICA participants aged 30-65) is a separate study, not part of BELFAST. Not a subset of the Genetics of Healthy Ageing study (the 2010 review cites GEHA only as a larger study to come). No duplicate in COHO or in tiers D/E.

label: Flanders-Belgian AD cohort
other synonyms: Flanders-Belgian study cohort
example quote: The Flanders-Belgian study cohort (Belgium_AD, n = 2370), was ascertained in the frame of a prospective study of AD, as previously described in.
definition: A case-control cohort for genetic studies of Alzheimer's disease, drawn from a prospective study of Alzheimer's disease in Flanders, Belgium, whose genetic studies are run from the University of Antwerp: unrelated patients with early- or late-onset possible or probable Alzheimer's disease, diagnosed by consensus of at least two neurologists at the memory clinics of the Hospital Network Antwerp (Middelheim and Hoge Beuken) and the University Hospitals Leuven and at other neurology centres of the Belgian Neurology (BELNEU) consortium, and healthy unrelated control individuals from Belgium, patients' partners or community volunteers, with blood samples for DNA, cell lines and plasma and, for some patients, cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers.
location quote: The patients were ascertained at the memory clinic of Middelheim and Hoge Beuken (Hospital Network Antwerp, Belgium) and at the memory clinic of the University Hospitals of Leuven, Belgium.
parent quote: Belgium: The participants were part of a large prospective cohort1 of Belgian AD patients and healthy elderly control individuals.
note: Tier E (E106), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred on an empty record; research settles it. The PGS Catalog records no score or paper for Belgium_AD (REST cohort/Belgium_AD empty), but both the id and the Catalog's name are copied from the AD gene-gene interaction GWAS PMID:24958192 (Neurobiol Aging 2014, PMC4370231), which names its Belgian replication set 'The Flanders-Belgian study cohort (Belgium_AD, n = 2370)' alongside France_AD, USA_AD, USA2_AD, UK_AD and Germany_AD. It is the Antwerp group's Flanders-Belgian Alzheimer's disease case-control cohort, described in PMID:21403675 (PMC3265835: 'The Flanders–Belgian AD group consisted of 1039 patients', 'ascertained at the memory clinics of the ZNA Middelheim, Antwerpen, Belgium21, 22 and the University Hospitals Leuven', consensus NINCDS/ADRDA diagnosis by at least two neurologists, controls 'healthy, unrelated individuals from Belgium'), in the EADB Supplementary Note of PMID:35379992 (controls 'the partners of the patients or volunteers from the Belgian community', BELNEU hospitals) and, as 'the Flanders-Belgian AD cohort', in PMID:22248099 and PMID:40078479. The cohort has no formal name; its investigators call it the Flanders-Belgian AD cohort (2012-2025), hence the label; 'Flanders-Belgian Alzheimer's disease cohort' would be the expanded form if the curator prefers no abbreviation. Parent EADB (COHO:0000551): the Belgian samples are part of EADB's France node. Part of the cohort was also a replication sample of the French EADI GWAS (PMC3265835: 'Part of this cohort had been included as replication sample in the French GWA study'), which is not membership of EADI (COHO:0000643). The same Antwerp group and BELNEU consortium also collect Flanders-Belgian frontotemporal dementia, Parkinson's disease and ALS cohorts; those are separate samples, not this term. Not the same as E102 (Belgian Donors) or E350 FLEMENGHO.

label: Boston Early-Onset COPD Study
other synonyms: Boston Early-Onset COPD study|Boston Early-Onset Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease study
example title: Predictors of survival in severe, early onset COPD.
example quote: The cohort of 139 probands in the Boston Early-Onset COPD Study was recruited from lung transplant and general pulmonary clinics between September 1994 and July 2002.
definition: A family study begun in 1994 at Brigham and Women's Hospital, Boston, to find genetic determinants of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease other than alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, which enrols extended pedigrees, mainly in New England, ascertained through probands with severe COPD (FEV1 at most 40% predicted) before age 53 and without severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, recruited from lung transplant and general pulmonary clinics, together with their first- and second-degree relatives aged 10 years or older.
parent quote: This study is part of the NHLBI Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) Whole Genome Sequencing Program.
note: Tier E (E107), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P6: all denote the same Boston Early-Onset COPD family/pedigree study; P4 and P6 also mention COPDGene and the International COPD Genetics Network as separate, distinct studies. 'study' capitalisation varies (lowercase in P1/P5, capital 'Study' in P2/P3/P6); lowercase form kept as synonym. Country is from the cohort's own name (Boston); no unit states a location separately. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, country and example are right. The definition gave the recruitment window of one paper's 139 probands ('between September 1994 and July 2002', PMID:15539711) as if it bounded the study, and left out who may enrol and why. The study's dbGaP record (phs000946, NHLBI TOPMed: Boston Early-Onset COPD Study) says 'The Boston Early-Onset COPD was started in 1994 in an effort to find genetic determinants of COPD other than alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.', that 'Extended pedigrees are enrolled, primarily in New England, although some more geographically distant subjects have been included.', and gives the entry criteria: probands under 53 with pre-bronchodilator FEV1 at most 40% predicted and physician-diagnosed COPD, without severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, and first- or second-degree relatives aged 10 or over; its principal investigator is at Brigham and Women's Hospital. The parent was missing: part of the study was whole-genome sequenced in TOPMed (COHO:0000985). The spelled-out name 'Boston Early-Onset Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease study' and its acronym 'BECOPD', used once by the study's own investigators (PMID:28191685), are added. Country kept from the name (Boston); dbGaP places the pedigrees 'primarily in New England'. The International COPD Genetics Network (E520) and COPDGene (COHO:0000514) are separate studies that the exome papers analyse alongside it, not parents. 'BECOPD' is a one-off spelling in one paper; drop it if one-off variants are not wanted.

input name: Bangladesh Vitamin E and Selenium Trial
label: Bangladesh Vitamin E and Selenium Trial
example title: Genome-wide association studies and heritability estimates of body mass index related phenotypes in Bangladeshi adults.
example quote: The Bangladesh Vitamin E and Selenium Trial (BEST) [28] was established in Araihazar and surrounding areas in 2006 to determine whether 7,000 arsenic-exposed participants who supplemented their diet with vitamin E and selenium would reduce their rate of non-melanoma skin cancer.
definition: A population-based, 2×2 factorial, double-blind randomised controlled chemoprevention trial in Bangladesh that enrolled adults with manifest arsenical skin lesions from the Narayanganj, Comilla, Noakhali and Chandpur districts, through field offices in Araihazar and Matlab, between April 2006 and August 2009, and gave them vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol), selenium (L-selenomethionine), both or placebo for six years to test the prevention of non-melanoma skin cancer, with all-cause and cancer mortality, diabetes and oxidative stress biomarkers as secondary endpoints.
location quote: This study reports on the design, methods and baseline analyses from the Bangladesh Vitamin E and Selenium Trial (BEST), a population-based chemoprevention study conducted among adults in Bangladesh with visible arsenic toxicity.
note: Tier E (E108), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: BEST genotyped alongside HEALS for PGS000770's source GWAS; P2 (Quebec Family Study) has no BEST evidence, unrelated; P3: BEST's own design paper; P4-P6: BEST as a distinct Bangladeshi cohort alongside HEALS/HEALS-E. Acronym BEST is shared with E109 (Black Women: Etiology and Survival of TNBC Study) in this batch; both need the COHO shared-acronym note once minted. Distinct from HEALS (COHO:0000204): P4/P5 list them as separate cohorts, jointly genotyped in P1. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, country, example and the absence of a parent are right, and BEST is rightly kept apart from HEALS (COHO:0000204). The definition took 'established in Araihazar and surrounding areas in 2006' from a GWAS paper; the trial's own design paper (PMID:23590571, BioC text of PMC3953314) says 'Individuals were recruited from the Narayanganj, Comilla, Noakhali, and Chandpur districts of Bangladesh.', with Araihazar and Matlab as the two field-office strata, and 'Participant randomization was initiated in April 2006 and completed in August 2009.'; it also gives the placebo arm and the secondary endpoints ('Secondary endpoints include all-cause and cancer-related mortality, diabetes mellitus, and oxidative stress biomarkers.'). The definition now follows the design paper. The acronym BEST is shared with E109 (the Black Women: Etiology and Survival of Triple-Negative Breast Cancers Study); if both are minted, both need the shared-acronym editor note. Distinct from HEALS (COHO:0000204) and the HEALS Expansion (HEALS-E), which the same investigators analyse alongside it, and from the US Selenium and Vitamin E Cancer Prevention Trial (COHO:0000693).

input name: The Black Women: Etiology and Survival of Triple-Negative Breast Cancers (BEST) Study
label: Black Women with Breast Cancer: Etiology, Survival, and Treatment Outcomes Study
other synonyms: Black Women: Etiology and Survival of Triple-negative Breast Cancers Study|Black Women: Etiology and Survival of Triple-negative Breast Cancers (BEST) Study|The Black Women: Etiology and Survival of Triple-Negative Breast Cancers (BEST) Study|Black Women: Etiology and Survival of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer study|BEST study
example title: Improved polygenic risk prediction models for breast cancer subtypes in women of African ancestry.
example quote: We additionally performed external validation of PRS models for each of the four BC phenotypes in an independent combined dataset of women of African ancestry (580 cases and 3,011 controls) from three studies of women of African ancestry including The Vanderbilt Biobank (BioVU),42,43 Black Women: Etiology and Survival of Triple-negative Breast Cancers (BEST) Study,44 and the Women Firefighters Biomonitoring Collaborative (WFBC).45
definition: A population-based longitudinal cohort of self-identified Black women diagnosed with invasive breast cancer at age 50 or younger, identified through the state cancer registries of Florida and Tennessee (diagnoses from 2005 to 2018; its first phase recruited women diagnosed in Florida in 2009–2012), who completed a questionnaire on sociodemographic, reproductive, epidemiologic and lifestyle factors, released their medical records and tumour tissue and gave saliva for germline genetic testing, now based at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, to study the causes, inherited predisposition, treatment and survival of breast cancer, including triple-negative breast cancer, in young Black women.
location quote: Women were recruited through state cancer registries in Florida and Tennessee, spoke English, and were alive at the time of recruitment.
note: Tier E (E109), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: BEST as one of three distinct African-ancestry validation cohorts (with BioVU and WFBC) for breast-cancer PRS models. Only one paper (uses BEST as a validation dataset, not its own design). A same-paper subscription reference (E109.4-6, 'matched part of tag') on BRCA mutations in young Black women with breast cancer in Florida may be BEST's own profile paper; unconfirmed - a researcher should verify. Acronym BEST clashes with E108; both need the shared-acronym note. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type and acronyms are right, but the draft rested on one sentence of the PRS paper and knew nothing of the study. The study's own papers describe it: first 'a population-based case-only study conducted in Florida' of 'Black women aged 50 years or younger at diagnosis, diagnosed with primary incident breast cancer between 2009 and 2012' identified 'through the statewide cancer registry' (PMID:33947654, BioC text of PMC8254754), and now 'the Black Women with Breast Cancer: Etiology, Survival, and Treatment Outcomes (BEST) study, a population-based longitudinal cohort of self-identified Black women diagnosed with invasive breast cancer at or below age 50 between 2005 and 2018' recruited 'through state cancer registries in Florida and Tennessee' (PMID:41360000, PMC12686358), with questionnaire, medical-record and tissue release and a saliva sample for germline testing (PMID:42252839, PMC13244119, which gives the study's Vanderbilt IRB number). The draft definition ('A study of Black women with breast cancer, including triple-negative subtypes, investigating the disease's etiology and survival.') gave none of who, where, when or how, and the country was missing. The label is the study's superseded name: its current name, used in its own 2025-2026 papers and ethics statement, is taken as the label, and the older forms (including the PGS Catalog's name and the PRS paper's spelling) are kept as synonyms. The example quote is kept but trimmed: it ran on into the next heading ('Strategies for PRS development.'). The PGS id says Florida because the study began as a Florida registry study; Tennessee recruitment was added later (Tennessee Department of Health IRB 2019), so the id denotes the same cohort. The acronym BEST is shared with E108 (Bangladesh Vitamin E and Selenium Trial); if both are minted, both need the shared-acronym editor note. Not a member of a COHO aggregation: in the PRS paper it is an external validation set alongside BioVU (COHO:0000417) and the Women Firefighters Biomonitoring Collaborative (WFBC; the PGS Catalog's cohort WFBC, tier-E row E1217, is named 'Wake Forest University Breast Cancer Study', so that row should check which study the Catalog means in PMID:41629673), and in PMID:33947654 it is pooled case-only with the Southern Community Cohort Study, the Nashville Breast Health Study and the Southern Tri-State Breast Health Study, which is a joint analysis, not a consortium. No duplicate in COHO (COHO:0000235, the City of Hope triple negative breast cancer cohort, and COHO:0001150, the Black Women's Health Study, are different) or in tiers D/E (E1115 TNBCC is the Triple Negative Breast Cancer Consortium).

input name: Baltic Familial Breast and Ovarian Cancer Consortium
label: Baltic Familial Breast and Ovarian Cancer Consortium
other synonyms: Baltic Familial Breast Ovarian Cancer Consortium
example title: Polygenic risk scores and breast and epithelial ovarian cancer risks for carriers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variants.
example quote: Baltic Familial Breast and Ovarian Cancer Consortium (BFBOCC) - Centrālā medicīnas ētikas Komiteja; Lietuvos Bioetikos Komitetas;
definition: A collection of carriers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variants from families seen in clinical cancer genetics services in Lithuania and Latvia, gathered by a collaboration of Lithuanian (BFBOCC-LT) and Latvian (BFBOCC-LV) hereditary breast and ovarian cancer research groups and contributed as one study to the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2, for studies of genetic modifiers of cancer risk in carriers.
location quote: BFBOCC Latvia/Lithuania
parent quote: Male BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers were recruited through 40 studies from 19 countries participating in the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 (CIMBA) (24).
note: Tier E (E110), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1,P2,P4-P6: PGS Catalog score-development papers with no BFBOCC-naming text extracted; P3: names BFBOCC directly in ethics/funding lists, with Latvian and Lithuanian approvals. Definition rests on table-like ethics/funding entries (E110.1, E110.4), not prose describing BFBOCC's purpose or full membership; only Latvia and Lithuania are evidenced (Estonia, also Baltic, is not). 'BFBOCC-LT' suggests national sub-sites exist but none is drafted here. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym and the two countries are right, but the draft had no source describing the consortium and guessed a 'consortium of national familial breast and ovarian cancer study sites in the Baltic states'. In every paper the PGS Catalog records it in, BFBOCC is one study of the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 (CIMBA), contributing BRCA1 and BRCA2 carriers from Latvia and Lithuania, all ascertained through clinics (PMID:34320204 Supplementary Table 1: 'BFBOCC Latvia/Lithuania' with 100% clinic-based ascertainment; CIMBA carriers 'were ascertained through families attending cancer genetic clinics'); it has a Lithuanian and a Latvian section ('Lithuania (BFBOCC-LT)', 'Latvia (BFBOCC-LV)', PMID:23544012, PMC3609647; 'BFBOCC-LT (Baltic Familial Breast Ovarian Cancer Consortium Lithuanian section)', PMID:28448241). It is used as a single study, not as an umbrella of named cohorts, so it is a cohort, as COHO types the comparable kConFab (COHO:0001094) and Breast Cancer Family Registry (COHO:0000668); its CIMBA membership was missing. The country quotes are replaced by the CIMBA table's 'BFBOCC Latvia/Lithuania' (the draft's Latvia quote named only a Latvian ethics committee), and the example quote is trimmed to the span naming the study (it began mid-list at 'Review Board;'). The CIMBA quote does not name BFBOCC itself: BFBOCC is one of the 40 CIMBA studies of that paper, listed in its Supplementary Table 1 as 'BFBOCC Latvia/Lithuania' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC8755508/supplementaryFiles). The sections BFBOCC-LT and BFBOCC-LV appear only in acknowledgements and are not given terms. Estonia is not part of it. Label spelling: the PGS Catalog and PMID:32665703 write 'Baltic Familial Breast and Ovarian Cancer Consortium', most CIMBA papers 'Baltic Familial Breast Ovarian Cancer Consortium' (kept as a synonym). No duplicate in COHO or in tiers D/E (COHO:0000256, the Latvian Biobank, is unrelated).

label: Brains for Dementia Research
other synonyms: Brains for Dementia Research cohort
example title: Genetic variants in glutamate-, Aβ-, and tau-related pathways determine polygenic risk for Alzheimer's disease.
example quote: We have determined the predictive capacity of the Synaptic PRS in two datasets of cognitively normal controls (target dataset; n=137, validation dataset; n=80) and pathologically confirmed LOAD patients (target dataset; n=302, validation dataset; n=56) from the Brains for Dementia Research (BDR) resource.
definition: A longitudinal brain-donation cohort in the United Kingdom, established in 2008 with funding from Alzheimer's Research UK and the Alzheimer's Society, of volunteers with dementia and volunteers without cognitive impairment (the latter aged 65 or over, apart from spouses or partners of participants with dementia), recruited through a network of six dementia research centres (King's College London, Bristol, Manchester, Oxford, Cardiff and Newcastle) and their university brain banks, who undergo standardised clinical and psychometric assessments during life and have consented to donate their brains for dementia research after death.
location quote: The Brains for Dementia Research (BDR) cohort and program was for planned brain donation across five UK brain banks and one donation point, with standardized operating procedures, following longitudinal clinical and psychometric assessments for people with no cognitive impairment as well as those with dementia.
note: Tier E (E111), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because the PGS Catalog gives no expansion of BfDR and no text of its only paper had been gathered. The paper (PMID:33303219, closed at Elsevier) has a free accepted manuscript in the Nottingham Trent University repository (linked by Europe PMC/Unpaywall): both its target and validation data sets, autopsy-confirmed late-onset Alzheimer's disease cases and cognitively normal controls, come 'from the Brains for Dementia Research (BDR) resource', and its acknowledgements name the brain banks as 'members of the Brains for Dementia Research (BDR) Network'. So BfDR is the PGS Catalog's own abbreviation of Brains for Dementia Research, whose own acronym BDR the draft lacked. The record is built from the cohort's open-access profile paper (PMID:30452415, J Alzheimers Dis 2018). The draft's example paper was right but had no quote; one is given from the accepted manuscript. Not in COHO or elsewhere in this review (no BDR, BfDR or Brains for Dementia Research). The profile says BDR is one of the more than 35 UK cohorts brought together by Dementias Platform UK (DPUK) and that its brain banks are members of the MRC UK Brain Bank Network; neither is in COHO, so no parent is given. The cohort is 'Brains for Dementia Research'; the 'BDR Network' is the organisation of centres and brain banks that runs it. BfDR is used only by the PGS Catalog; the cohort itself writes BDR.

label: Scottish Bipolar Family Study
other synonyms: Bipolar Family Study
example title: Dysfunction of emotional brain systems in individuals at high risk of mood disorder with depression and predictive features prior to illness.
example quote: The Bipolar Family Study (BFS) is a prospective longitudinal study that has examined individuals at familial risk of mood disorder and healthy controls on three occasions, 2 years apart.
definition: A prospective longitudinal study based at the University of Edinburgh of young people aged 16–25 at entry who were well but at high familial risk of mood disorder, having at least one first-degree or two second-degree relatives with bipolar I disorder (identified through patients with bipolar I disorder referred by psychiatrists across Scotland), and of unrelated controls with no personal or family history of bipolar disorder drawn from their social networks, assessed clinically and with brain MRI on three occasions about two years apart to study changes that precede the onset of mood disorders.
location quote: Individuals with a diagnosis of bipolar I disorder were identified by psychiatrists across Scotland.
note: Tier E (E112), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: possibly a different, Maudsley-based 'Bipolar Family Study', explicitly called 'separate' -- not confirmed as this cohort. P2-P5: this cohort, named 'Bipolar Family Study (BFS)' (P2) or 'Scottish Bipolar Family Study' (P3-P5). P1's 'Maudsley Bipolar Family Study' is called a 'separate' study, likely a different, London-based cohort -- not used as evidence here. Label follows P2's 'Bipolar Family Study (BFS)'; 'Scottish Bipolar Family Study' (P3-P5) is treated as the same cohort's fuller name, given matching design and population. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, example and the absence of a parent are right. The label is the short form: the study's investigators call it the 'Scottish Bipolar Family Study' (the title of PMID:27418025 and PMID:32954013, whose authors added it to the title as 'the cohort name'), which also tells it apart from the Maudsley and Maritime bipolar family studies, so that becomes the label and 'Bipolar Family Study' a synonym. The draft missed the study's own acronym SBFS ('We used data from the Scottish Bipolar Family Study (SBFS)', PMC7479500). The definition was right but thin: open-access methods (PMC3590244, PMC4834463, PMC7479500) say how participants were found (relatives aged 16–25 of patients with bipolar I disorder identified by psychiatrists across Scotland; at least one first-degree or two second-degree affected relatives; controls with no personal or family history of bipolar disorder from the high-risk participants' social networks) and that assessments included brain MRI at Edinburgh. The country is right, but its quote only gave the name; it now cites the recruitment across Scotland. Because the PGS Catalog records no score or paper for BFS, which 'Bipolar Family Study' it means cannot be confirmed from the Catalog; the Scottish study is the one that calls itself 'Bipolar Family Study (BFS)', while the Maudsley (London) and Maritime (Canada, MBFS) family studies are always named with their qualifier. None of the three is in COHO or elsewhere in this review. Ethics approval reference 06/MRE00/9 suggests recruitment began around 2006, but no text read gives the recruitment years, so the definition gives none.

Tier E (E113), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred with no evidence at all. Research finds where the PGS Catalog's name comes from but not who the participants are. The only human study called BGWAS in Europe PMC is a stage-2 replication sample of the East Asian adult height GWAS meta-analysis (PMID:25429064, Hum Mol Genet 2015, free in PMC), whose funding section expands it exactly as the Catalog does: 'BGWAS (Beijing Genome-wide Association Studies): This work was supported by the National Basic Research Program of China (973 Plan) (2011CB503901), the High-Tech Research and Development Program of China (863 Plan) (2012AA02A516), grants (2011BAI11B03, 2011BAI09B03) from the Ministry of Science and Technology of China.' The same paper's 'WHBJ (Wuhan-Beijing GWA study)' is also in the PGS Catalog's cohort list (E1219), which confirms this paper as the Catalog's source. The main text says only that BGWAS was one of five replication GWAS and was genotyped on an Affymetrix array; the study descriptions are in the paper's Supplementary Note and Tables S1–S2, which could not be fetched (OUP answers 403; PMC's copy sits behind a proof-of-work page). So what BGWAS is, one study or several (the name is plural), cannot be settled. The grant numbers point to the Fuwai Hospital cardiovascular epidemiology group in Beijing, so BGWAS is probably that group's GWAS data (for example BAS, COHO:0000896, and/or CAS, COHO:0000187, both genotyped on Affymetrix arrays; InterASIA is E550 in this review), but no text read says which. If the supplement shows BGWAS is BAS or CAS alone, add BGWAS as an acronym of that term; if it pools several of the group's GWAS, it is an aggregation whose members are those studies. The draft's search of COHO for Beijing-named cohorts (Beijing Eye Study, Beijing Atherosclerosis Study, Han Chinese in Beijing) was right to find no name match, but BAS and CAS are the likely candidates. Not the gastric cancer 'Beijing GWAS' of the Nanjing group. The example above is offered only for when the identity is settled.

input name: British Heart Foundation Family Heart Study
label: UK BHF CAD/MI cohort
other synonyms: BHF Family Heart Study
note: Tier E (E114), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P4 (PGS Catalog papers for PGS000011/PGS000349) and P5-P7 (found by name): BHF-FHS denotes the same British Heart Foundation Family Heart Study throughout, distinct from the NHLBI Family Heart Study and Framingham Heart Study, also abbreviated FHS in these papers' legends. Distinct from candidate COHO:0000582 (NHLBI Family Heart Study, FamHS/FHS) and COHO:0000385 (Framingham Heart Study, FHS): E114.2/.14 list BHF-FHS, FHS and FOS as separate studies in the same legend. Controls partly sourced from WTCCC/UK 1958 Birth Cohort (funding/sharing only, not stated membership), so parent left null. Checked 2026-09-23: The name, acronym, country and example are right, but the cohort is already in COHO as COHO:0000346 'UK BHF CAD/MI cohort', minted from EGA study EGAS00001000079 (Cardiogenics re-sequencing), whose description reads 'The experiment will use the early onset patients from the German MI cohort and the UK BHF CAD/MI cohort both of which have strong family history and together total over 5000 cases.' That pairing is the one of the 2007 WTCCC/German coronary GWAS (PMID:17634449, PMC2719290), where 'The 1988 case subjects in the WTCCC study had a history of either myocardial infarction or coronary revascularization before the age of 66 years, as well as a strong family history of coronary artery disease', citing the BHF Family Heart Study paper; the only UK, BHF-funded collection of early-onset coronary patients with a strong family history is the BHF Family Heart Study, whose lead centre (Leicester) is a Cardiogenics partner. The definition also had the design wrong: the BHF-FHS is not a case-control study but a national collection of families with at least two siblings with premature coronary disease (PMID:16380912: 'The objective of the BHF Family Heart Study was to establish a substantial resource of families with at least two siblings affected with premature CAD'); the controls in the GWAS data sets tagged BHF-FHS come from other collections (UK Blood Service donors via the WTCCC in PMID:21966275; the 1958 Birth Cohort in PMID:28209224). Merge into COHO:0000346: add BHF-FHS as an acronym and 'British Heart Foundation Family Heart Study' and 'BHF Family Heart Study' as synonyms; the curator may relabel it with the cohort's own name 'British Heart Foundation Family Heart Study' (the draft's label) and keep the EGA's 'UK BHF CAD/MI cohort' as a synonym, and replace its thin definition with the one above. No text read names the Family Heart Study in the EGA record itself, so the merge rests on the EGA description matching the BHF-FHS exactly (UK, BHF, CAD/MI, early onset, strong family history, paired with the German MI Family Study as in the 2007 WTCCC/German GWAS). Related: COHO:0000358 'WTCCC case-control study for Coronary Artery Disease' is the WTCCC's genotyped subset of this cohort, one case per family ('Although the majority of subjects had at least one further sib also affected with premature CAD, only one subject from each family was included in the present study', WTCCC 2007, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/bionlp/RESTful/pmcoa.cgi/BioC_xml/PMC2719288/unicode), so it could get isSubCohortOf COHO:0000346. Distinct from COHO:0000582 (NHLBI Family Heart Study, FamHS/FHS) and COHO:0000385 (Framingham Heart Study, FHS). The draft's example (PMID:21966275) can be kept only as a curated second example next to COHO:0000346's EGA example (both then written in example_studies_curated.tsv).

example quote: The Brazilian Immunogenetics of Asthma and Schistosomiasis (BIAS) study is a whole-population ascertainment designed study of asthma and schistosomiasis in the rural district of Conde, Bahia, located 200 km north of Salvador, Brazil [14-16].
definition: A family-based study of asthma and schistosomiasis in five rural communities of the district of Conde, Bahia, north-eastern Brazil, an area endemic for Schistosoma mansoni about 200 km north of Salvador, in which residents aged 5 to 85, most of them members of two large pedigrees, were enrolled by whole-population ascertainment from July to September 2004 by the Federal University of Bahia and Johns Hopkins University, with later follow-up visits, to study the genetic control of total serum IgE, S. mansoni infection intensity and asthma; it is one of the studies of the Consortium on Asthma among African-ancestry Populations in the Americas (CAAPA).
location quote: By use of a whole-population ascertainment scheme, 822 individuals were enrolled from a schistosomiasis-endemic area in Conde, Bahia, in Brazil.
note: Tier E (E115), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because no paper had been gathered. The name is used by the Consortium on Asthma among African-ancestry Populations in the Americas (CAAPA): its asthma GWAS (PMID:30787307, open access) and whole-genome sequencing paper (PMID:27725671, open access) describe in their Supplementary Notes 'The Brazilian Immunogenetics of Asthma and Schistosomiasis (BIAS) study' as a whole-population, family-based study of asthma and schistosomiasis in the rural district of Conde, Bahia, recruited July–September 2004 from five communities, with follow-up visits; its own papers (PMID:18717640, PMID:22574126, open access) describe the same Conde population as schistosomiasis-endemic, enrolled by the Federal University of Bahia and Johns Hopkins University. CAAPA itself is not in COHO or this review; if it is minted as an aggregation, BIAS is a member (Supplementary Note 1 of PMID:30787307 lists it among the CAAPA studies), as are COHO:0000959 (BAGS) and COHO:0001344 (GRAAD).
