example title: Transferability of Alzheimer Disease Polygenic Risk Score Across Populations and Its Association With Alzheimer Disease-Related Phenotypes.
example quote: This was part of the ongoing BICWALZS study (Biobank Innovation for Chronic Cerebrovascular Disease With Alzheimer’s Disease Study) and data from the Center for Convergence Research of Neurological Disorders.
definition: A prospective, longitudinal, multicentre biobank cohort of older adults with cognitive complaints (subjective cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, vascular and other dementias) enrolled from October 2016 to December 2020 at five South Korean university hospitals (Ajou University Hospital, Samsung Medical Center, Inha University Hospital, Pusan National University Hospital and Chonnam National University Hospital), planned and funded by the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency for the Korea Biobank Project to bank biospecimens and data for research on Alzheimer's disease, chronic cerebrovascular disease and mixed pathology; participants have clinical and neuropsychological assessments and blood tests, subsets have brain MRI, amyloid PET, Korea Biobank Array genotyping, actigraphy and skin fibroblast sampling, and follow-up is planned annually.
location quote: Korea pheno1 and Korea pheno2 were from the Biobank Innovations for Chronic Cerebrovascular Disease with ALZheimer’s Disease Study (BICWALZS) as a Korea Biobank Project[26].
parent quote: For access and sharing, biological resources of the BICWALZS were stored in the BICWALZS consortium biobank (www.bicwalzs.com/) as well as the National Biobank of Korea (www.nih.go.kr/biobank) which is a central biobank supporting for the Korea Biobank Project.
note: Tier E (E116), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 and P2 (both PGS Catalog evaluation papers): BICWALZS denotes the same Korean biobank cohort in both; P1 (E116.1) names and expands it, P2 (E116.7, E116.12) confirms it as a Korea Biobank Project cohort. Name varies: PGS Catalog/E116.1 use singular 'Innovation', E116.4/.15's citation title uses plural 'Innovations' (kept as synonym); E116.7's 'ALZheimer's' capitalisation is likely a citation-rendering quirk. Distinct from the Japan/NCGG cohort (COHO:0000876) and INTERVAL, NHS, NIHR BioResource -- separate cohorts pooled in the same consortium paper (P2). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, acronym, country and example are right. The label is the PGS Catalog's singular 'Biobank Innovation ...'; the cohort's own design paper (PMID:35042283, open access, cited by both PGS papers) calls it 'Biobank Innovations for Chronic Cerebrovascular Disease With Alzheimer’s Disease Study' in its title and '... with ALZheimer’s Disease Study (BICWALZS)' in its text, so the plural title form becomes the label and the singular a synonym. The 'ALZheimer’s' spelling is not a citation quirk, as the draft thought: the design paper itself uses it to spell out the acronym, so it is kept as a synonym. The definition was vague ('collects baseline clinical and biomarker data') and said nothing of who, where or when; the design paper gives older adults with cognitive complaints enrolled October 2016 to December 2020 at five named university hospitals, the assessments and the planned annual follow-up. The draft missed a parent: the design paper says the BICWALZS biospecimens are stored in the National Biobank of Korea (COHO:0000926), which COHO already links to KoGES the same way. PGS papers pair it with PREMIER (E920), a separate study, and IHCC paper P2 also writes 'Biobank Innovations for Chronic cerebrovascular disease With ALZheimer’s disease Study', a capitalisation variant not added here. Distinct from COHO:0000713 (K-ROAD) and from the Korea Biobank Array project (E584), whose array BICWALZS used for genotyping.

Tier E (E117), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred and misread the table: BIDMC is not a Baltic study. The sheet that the draft's fragments come from is 'Supplementary Table 2: CIMBA studies contributing data on BRCA1 mutation carriers, by genotyping intiative' of the ER-negative breast cancer GWAS (PMID:29058716), with columns Acronym, Study Name and Country; its row reads 'BIDMC | Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center | USA' (41 unaffected and 44 affected carriers on OncoArray, 1 and 1 on iCOGS), next to the separate row 'BFBOCC | Baltic Familial Breast Ovarian Cancer Consortium | LITHUANIA/LATVIA'. So BIDMC is the Boston hospital's contribution of BRCA1 mutation carriers to CIMBA (COHO:0000901). No study name is given anywhere read: CIMBA papers name it only after the institution ('Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC) is supported by the Breast Cancer Research Foundation', PMC5408990). As with the other CIMBA site tags this review has settled (MCGILL, MSKCC, UC), it is an institution label, not a cohort. If the curator ever wants CIMBA site contributions as terms, this one is the BRCA1/2 carriers ascertained at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston (United States), memberOf COHO:0000901; but no text describes how or when they were recruited. No COHO term or other review name uses BIDMC or Beth Israel.

P1 (E118.1, supplement list) and P2 (E118.4-16): BIGGS denotes the same Irish study throughout, listed as a BCAC member study (E118.4) and expanded as 'Breast Cancer in Galway Genetic Study' (E118.14) with country 'Ireland' (E118.15). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, synonym, acronym, type, country, BCAC membership and example are right. The free Supplementary Table 2 of the BCAC iCOGS paper (PMID:23535729, 'Participating studies in BCAC contributing to the COGS replication phase') describes the design: cases 'Unselected cases recruited from University College Hospital Galway and surrounding hospitals in the West of Ireland since 2001', controls women over 60 with no personal history of any cancer and no family history of breast or ovarian cancer 'identified from retirement groups in the West of Ireland' in 2001–2008; Zhang et al. 2020 (PMID:32424353, Supplementary Table 1) types it 'Case-control study', Ireland. label: Bipolar Genome Study
example title: Accuracy of CNV Detection from GWAS Data.
example quote: The second evaluation was program performance calling rare and common CNVs in the Bipolar Genome Study (BiGS) data set (1001 bipolar cases and 1033 controls, all of European ancestry) as measured by the Affymetrix SNP 6.0 array.
definition: A case-control genetic study of bipolar disorder in the United States, initiated in 2006 as the genetic component of the NIMH-sponsored Genetics Initiative for Bipolar Disorder Consortium to carry out genome-wide association studies: cases with bipolar disorder of European and African American ancestry, collected through the consortium's eleven US collection sites (mostly from multiplex families or sibling pairs for the first, GAIN-funded genotyping; without regard to family history for the later TGen genotyping), and controls from the NIMH Genetics Initiative control sample collected for the Molecular Genetics of Schizophrenia study.
location quote: Participants in the US Bipolar Genome Study (BIGS) were assessed on six items of concerns in the Questionnaire on Genetic Risk (QGR).
note: Tier E (E119), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (E119.1/.13/.19/.25) expands BiGS = Bipolar Genome Study, case-control, European ancestry. P2 (E119.31) confirms 'US Bipolar Genome Study (BIGS)', an all-caps variant. P3-P6: each a distinct GWAS of one bipolar-related trait using the same BiGS sample. P2 uses the all-caps variant 'BIGS' (kept as a separate acronym per capitalisation rule) and is the only unit stating a country ('US'). HapMap (candidate COHO:0000284) and 'GAIN genotype data' (P6) are separate reference datasets/repositories used alongside BiGS, not a parent relationship, so parent is left null. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronyms (BiGS and the all-caps BIGS), type, country, example and the absence of a COHO parent are right. The definition described one paper's subset ('cases and controls of European ancestry'): BiGS also genotyped African American cases and controls (PMID:19488044: 'one involving a sample of individuals of African ancestry'), and it left out what BiGS is and where its samples come from. Its own papers say: 'A genetic component of the Bipolar Consortium, termed the ‘Bipolar Genome Study (BiGS),’ was initiated in 2006 to conduct a GWA study of BD' (the NIMH Genetics Initiative for Bipolar Disorder consortium, which collected bipolar patients from 1990 to 2008); 'All eleven collection sites in the BiGS Consortium received IRB approval ...'; the GAIN-genotyped cases came mainly from multiplex families or sibling pairs and the later TGEN cases were population-based (PMID:21738484); controls came from the NIMH Genetics Initiative MGS2 control sample. Relation for another name of this review: E368 GAIN-BP ('Bipolar Disorder Genetic Association Information Network') is the first, GAIN-funded genotyping of the BiGS sample ('The initial BiGS GWA study was funded through the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health Genetic Information Association Network (GAIN) initiative', PMC3035981), so if E368 is minted it is isSubCohortOf this term (or the same term, if the curator prefers). The TGEN part of BiGS is not the Alzheimer TGen series (COHO:0000799). Some EA cases and controls overlap with the NIMH/Pritzker bipolar GWAS (E793). The NIMH Bipolar Disorder Genetics Initiative itself is not in COHO. Not related to BIGGS (E118) despite the similar acronym.

input name: Biological pathways of risk and resilience in Syrian refugee children
label: Biological pathways of risk and resilience in Syrian refugee children
other synonyms: Biological Pathways of Risk and Resilience in Syrian Refugee Children
example title: Risk and resilience in Syrian refugee children: A multisystem analysis.
example quote: Participants were drawn from the biological pathways of risk and resilience in Syrian refugee children (BIOPATH) study (McEwen et al., Reference McEwen, Popham, Moghames, Smeeth, de Villiers, Saab, Karam, Fayyad, Karam and Pluess2022).
definition: A longitudinal cohort of Syrian refugee children aged 8–16 and their primary caregivers, from families who had fled the war in Syria within the previous four years and were living in informal tented settlements in the West and Central Beqaa regions of Lebanon, recruited by purposive cluster sampling from October 2017 to January 2018 and followed up once a year later, with interviews of children and caregivers and children's saliva (for genotyping and DNA methylation) and hair (for cortisol, DHEA and testosterone), to study how psychosocial and biological factors shape resilience and mental health problems; it was funded by the US National Institute of Child Health and Human Development and sponsored by Queen Mary University of London.
location quote: Based in Lebanon, a middle-income country significantly impacted by the refugee crisis, it is the first such cohort of refugees in the Middle East.
note: Tier E (E120), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (PGS Catalog evaluation paper), P2 (the cohort's own Cohort Profile paper) and P3 (found by name): BIOPATH denotes the same Lebanon-based Syrian refugee children's cohort throughout. P2 is the cohort's own Cohort Profile paper (clearest source). Title-case variant (P3, running prose) kept as synonym; the sentence-case first-letter difference between citation renderings (P1 vs P2's own title) is treated as formatting noise, not a real variant, so not added separately. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, synonym, acronym, type, country and example are right, and the definition's facts are correct, but it was built from the profile's abstract only and left out who the participants are (children aged 8–16 and their primary caregivers, from families who had left Syria because of the war within the four years before recruitment), the single one-year follow-up, the biological samples and who ran and funded the study. The cohort profile is open access in full (PMC8960581) and gives all of these; the definition now uses it. No COHO term or other review name covers it. The profile says only two waves were collected and no further follow-up is planned, because of the population's mobility. A clinical-interview subsample (2018-2019) and a linked clinical trial are part of the same cohort, not separate terms.

input name: Biological Determinants of Peritoneal Dialysis (Bio-PD) study
label: Biological Determinants of Peritoneal Dialysis
other synonyms: Biological Determinants of Peritoneal Dialysis (Bio-PD) study|Biological Determinants of PD
example quote: To bridge this gap in knowledge, we undertook the Biological Determinants of PD (Bio-PD) study to perform a GWAS to test the hypothesis that common genetic variants explain some of the inter-individual variability in PSTR in people with kidney failure treated with PD.

location quote: The Bio-PD study enrolled 3817 participants undergoing PD at 70 centers across Australia, Belgium, Canada, Hong Kong, Sweden, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
note: Tier E (E121), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Bio-PD is the University of Washington's international genetic study of people treated with peritoneal dialysis (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02694068, official title 'Biological Determinants of Peritoneal Dialysis', acronym Bio-PD, observational model 'Cohort'). Its first GWAS (PMID:34197840) describes prospective enrolment at 54 centres in Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom and the United States from September 2013 through November 2018 of everyone on PD who had a peritoneal equilibration test within six months of starting PD, plus DNA and phenotype data procured from PD-CRAFT (42 UK centres, 2012-2014), a Belgian cohort of peritoneal function (1994-2018) and a Swedish cohort of incident patients (1993-2014); the 2026 ultrafiltration GWAS (PMID:40669005) gives the study's final extent, 70 centres across Australia, Belgium, Canada, Hong Kong, Sweden, the United Kingdom and the United States. Typed as one cohort, not an aggregation: it is a single registered observational study with its own protocol and prospective enrolment, and its papers analyse all participants as 'the Bio-PD study'; part of its sample is DNA procured from earlier studies (PD-CRAFT, 'Peritoneal Dialysis Competitive Risk Analysis for Long-Term Outcomes', in the UK; unnamed Belgian, Swedish and Hong Kong cohorts), none of which is in COHO or this review. The 2021 paper gives prospective enrolment as September 2013 to November 2018, whereas ClinicalTrials.gov gives a study start of 15 September 2015; the definition follows the paper. Ten Bio-PD centres were also PDOPPS sites, but PDOPPS enrolment was not required, so PDOPPS is not a parent. example quote: The Biologics in Rheumatoid Arthritis Genetics and Genomics Study Syndicate is a nationwide observational cohort study recruiting patients from 53 centers across the United Kingdom before the initiation of biologic treatment and following them up prospectively for 12 months.
definition: A multicentre observational study of patients with rheumatoid arthritis treated with biologic drugs at rheumatology centres across the United Kingdom, which collects their blood samples for DNA, RNA and cellular studies together with clinical, laboratory and adherence data, to study genetic and other predictors of response to biologic therapy. Its first patients, starting anti-TNF therapy, were identified through the British Society for Rheumatology Biologics Register; from November 2008 patients were recruited before starting a biologic and followed up prospectively for 12 months.
location quote: The Biologics in Rheumatoid Arthritis Genetics and Genomics Study Syndicate is a nationwide observational cohort study recruiting patients from 53 centers across the United Kingdom before the initiation of biologic treatment and following them up prospectively for 12 months.
note: Tier E (E131), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P6: the BRAGGSS cohort of UK rheumatoid arthritis patients starting biologic therapy, studied for genetic predictors of treatment response, throughout. Patients are identified through the British Society for Rheumatology Biologics Register (BSRBR, E131.14-15), but no unit states BRAGGSS is formally part of BSRBR (a broader registry), so no parent is asserted. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country and example were right. The definition merged the study's two phases into one design that never existed: the BSRBR route ('Patients eligible for the BRAGGSS cohort were initially identified through the British Society for Rheumatology Biologics Register (BSRBR)', inclusion 'registration with the BSRBR; planned treatment with an anti-TNF', PMC3580526) was the first, retrospective arm, while recruitment before the start of treatment with 12-month prospective follow-up is the 'prospective arm' begun in November 2008 ('Patients attending 60 rheumatology clinics across the UK were recruited into the study between November 2008 and March 2012', PMC4334684; 'BRAGGSS recruited patients with a clinical diagnosis of RA from 53 centers across England from November 2008 to December 2019', PMC12854005). It also narrowed the treatment to anti-TNF, but the prospective arm takes any biologic (abatacept and adalimumab in PMID:40567118), and carried one paper's centre count (53; another paper says 60). The definition now says what BRAGGSS collects ('collects blood samples from biologic treated RA patients for DNA, RNA and cellular studies', PMC6150911; 'clinical, laboratory and adherence data on patients with RA who are starting treatment with biologic therapy in the UK', PMC4334684) and keeps the two arms apart. No parent: BRAGGSS draws patients from the BSRBR-RA register's centres but is a separate study, and the MATURA consortium that used its samples (PMID:30166627) is not in COHO. Neither BSRBR nor RAMS (the Rheumatoid Arthritis Medication Study, BRAGGSS's methotrexate-starter counterpart in PMID:32097471) is in COHO.

definition: A case-control study of first-onset acute myocardial infarction in Bangladesh, established in 2011 by the University of Cambridge with the International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh (icddr,b) and the National Institute of Cardiovascular Disease (NICVD) in Dhaka, whose cases are adults admitted to the NICVD's emergency rooms with a first myocardial infarction and whose controls, frequency-matched by age and sex, are hospital visitors without cardiovascular disease; with questionnaire data, electrocardiograms and stored blood samples, it was set up to study environmental, genetic, lifestyle and biochemical determinants of coronary heart disease in Bangladeshis.

Grouped with PROMIS as 'South Asian' studies (E132.1) and with TaiChi/VIRGO/MESA as ancestry cohorts (E132.31, E132.37), but no unit says BRAVE is a member of another named aggregation, so no parent given. The study's design paper (PMID:25930055, PMC4516898) gives who ran it ('established in 2011 by the Department of Public Health and Primary Care at the University of Cambridge (the study’s international coordinating centre), in collaboration with the Chronic Non-communicable Disease Unit at the International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh (icddr,b) and the National Institute of Cardiovascular Disease (NICVD) in Bangladesh'), the cases (patients aged at least 20 admitted to the NICVD emergency rooms with a first MI), the controls (visitors without cardiovascular disease identified in the same hospital, 'frequency-matched' by age and sex) and its purpose ('an epidemiological bioresource established to examine environmental, genetic, lifestyle and biochemical determinants of CHD among the Bangladeshi population'); the definition now says so. definition: A population-based case-control study of bladder cancer in the Belgian province of Limburg, whose cases are people with histologically confirmed incident transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder diagnosed between 1999 and 2004, identified through the Limburg Cancer Registry and invited by their urologists and general practitioners, and whose controls are inhabitants of the province aged 50 or over sampled at random through the Crossroads Bank of Social Security, stratified by municipality and socioeconomic status; it was used to study occupational, dietary and genetic risk factors for bladder cancer.

note: Tier E (E134), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because the evidence file held only paper titles; the abstracts of all six papers were on disk and settle it. It is a named, defined sample: 'A population-based case-control study was performed in the Belgian province of Limburg among 200 cases and 385 controls.' (PMID:16380991). The open full text of PMID:21203820 (PMC3042097, read from Europe PMC) gives the design: 'All cases included in the study were incident cases identified with histologically confirmed transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of the bladder between 1999 and 2004.', 'Cases were derived from the Limburg Cancer Registry (LIKAR) and invited to participate in the study by urologists and general practitioners.', and controls 'selected through the Belgian authority, Kruispuntbank van de Sociale Zekerheid (Crossroads Bank of Social Security)' by random sampling 'stratified by municipality and social economic status among inhabitants from the province of Limburg who were 50 years of age and older'. The BLEND design paper (PMID:27386115, PMC4933992, Table 1) lists it as 'Belgian Case–control study on bladder cancer [12] Belgium 1999–2004 Population based case–control'. The label is the study's own name as its papers use it ('the Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer risk', PMID:21203820, 21485759, 20947337, 17450546); the PGS Catalog's 'Belgian Case Control Study of Bladder Cancer' and the shorter forms in other titles are kept as synonyms. The design paper ('A Belgian case control study on bladder cancer: rationale and design', Arch Public Health 2005;63:17-34) has no PMID and was not read. The study is one of the pooled studies of the BLadder cancer Epidemiology and Nutritional Determinants (BLEND) consortium (PMID:27386115), which is neither in COHO nor in this review, so no parent. The authors are at the Department of General Practice of the Katholieke Universiteit Leuven and the study was approved by its medical school's ethics board, but no text read says the university runs it, so the definition leaves that out. The cases came from the Limburg Cancer Registry, which is review name E632 (PGS id LIKAR); whoever checks E632 should make sure it is not this same sample.

Research settles it: BSN is the table label of the Busselton Health Study (COHO:0000389) in the two GWAS the PGS Catalog took it from. In the supplement of PMID:22982992 (Nature MOESM14), Supplementary Tables 4 and 5 list BSN between B58C-T1DGC and CoLaus ('BSN Illumina Human 610‐ Quad Illuminus ≥ 1% ≥ 95% > 10 ‐6 549,294 MACH'), and every other tabled study has its own study-specific acknowledgement, while the one acknowledgement with no table row is 'BHS The Busselton Health Study (BHS) acknowledges the generous support for the 1994/5 follow‐up study from Healthway, Western Australia and the numerous Busselton community volunteers who assisted with data collection and the study participants from the Shire of Busselton.' The array also matches: the Busselton discovery set was typed 'on the Illumina Human 610 K Quad-Bead Chip (Illumina Inc., San Diego, CA, USA) at the Centre National de Genotypage in Paris, France (n = 1468)' (PMID:35668104, PMC9170690). In PMID:22581228 (MAGIC) BSN is again a tabled cohort (MOESM22, Supplementary Table 1, whose country column includes Australia and no other Australian cohort) and the Supplementary Note acknowledges 'BUSSELTON The Busselton Health Study acknowledges the generous support for the 1994/5 follow-up study from Healthway, Western Australia and the numerous Busselton community volunteers who assisted with data collection and the study participants from the Shire of Busselton.' (MOESM21). So BSN is one more acronym of the existing term. The identification is by elimination within the supplement (no text writes 'BSN = Busselton'), but it is unambiguous: BSN is the only tabled study without its own acknowledgement, BHS/Busselton the only acknowledged study without a table row, and the Illumina 610-Quad array and the Australian country entry both fit. label: Beijing Type 2 Diabetes Studies
example quote: The stage 2 samples for replication testing of 96 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) consisted of 13,517 unrelated Chinese Hans (6,570 T2D case and 6,947 nondiabetic control subjects) from the Guizhou-Bijie Type 2 Diabetes Study (GBTDS), the Beijing Type 2 Diabetes Studies (BTDS), and the Hubei Type 2 Diabetes Studies (HTDS).
definition: A type 2 diabetes case-control sample of unrelated Han Chinese from Beijing, China, made up of people with type 2 diabetes and nondiabetic controls, used in genetic association studies of type 2 diabetes and glycaemic traits.
location quote: The stage 2 samples for replication testing of 96 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) consisted of 13,517 unrelated Chinese Hans (6,570 T2D case and 6,947 nondiabetic control subjects) from the Guizhou-Bijie Type 2 Diabetes Study (GBTDS), the Beijing Type 2 Diabetes Studies (BTDS), and the Hubei Type 2 Diabetes Studies (HTDS).
note: Tier E (E137), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because the evidence file held nothing (the PGS Catalog lists BTDS in no score). A Europe PMC search finds two papers that name it. In the GWAS of type 2 diabetes in Chinese Hans (PMID:22961080, PMC3526061) it is one of the three independent stage-2 replication populations of T2D cases and nondiabetic controls: 'The stage 2 samples for replication testing of 96 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) consisted of 13,517 unrelated Chinese Hans (6,570 T2D case and 6,947 nondiabetic control subjects) from the Guizhou-Bijie Type 2 Diabetes Study (GBTDS), the Beijing Type 2 Diabetes Studies (BTDS), and the Hubei Type 2 Diabetes Studies (HTDS).' The same paper says 'There was no overlap of participants among stage 1, 2, and 3 samples.' A 2015 study of FOXO3 and fasting glycaemia from Beijing Hospital (PMID:25993007, PMC4439071) drew its northern Chinese middle-aged panel from it: 'The project is a cross-sectional study within the framework of the “Longevity and Health of Aging Population in Guangxi China (LHAPGC)” and “Beijing Type 2 Diabetes Studies (BTDS)”', citing the 2013 GWAS for it. So BTDS is a named Beijing T2D case-control sample of Han Chinese, and the term can be minted. Its recruitment sites, dates and design are described only in the 2013 paper's Supplementary Materials and Methods and Supplementary Table 1, which could not be read (see needs), so the definition says only what the two papers show. Type: the plural 'Studies' (like 'Hubei Type 2 Diabetes Studies') may mean BTDS pools several Beijing case-control collections, in which case it would be an aggregation; the 2013 paper treats it as one of 'three independent Chinese Han populations' with a single call rate and duplicate check, so it is drafted as a cohort; the supplement would settle this. The 2013 paper's Beijing authors include the Key Laboratory of Geriatrics of Beijing Hospital, which ran the 2015 study, but no text read says who assembled BTDS, so the definition names no institution. Related review names from the same GWAS: the other stage-2 populations E376 (GBTDS, Guizhou-Bijie Type 2 Diabetes Study) and E495 (HTDS, Hubei Type 2 Diabetes Studies); stage-1 samples NHAPC (COHO:0000789) and GMOS (E434). E113 (BGWAS, 'Beijing genome-wide association studies') is probably the stage-1 Beijing GWAS sample (the Beijing Diabetes Survey), which by the paper's own statement does not overlap BTDS; whoever checks E113 should confirm. No COHO term matches; COHO:0000808 (HapMap Han Chinese in Beijing) and COHO:0000896 (Beijing Atherosclerosis Study) are unrelated.

label: Brisbane Twin Nevus Study
other synonyms: Brisbane Twin Naevus Study|TWin Mole study
example title: Multiple common susceptibility variants near BMP pathway loci GREM1, BMP4, and BMP2 explain part of the missing heritability of colorectal cancer.
example quote: The 2,353 controls were derived from Queensland or Melbourne: for the former, the controls came from the Brisbane Twin Nevus Study [16]; for the latter, individuals were participants in the Genes in Myopia study [17].
definition: A study of the Queensland Institute of Medical Research (QIMR) in Brisbane, Australia, that from 1992 to 2016 examined annual new samples of 12-year-old twins from south-east Queensland, with their siblings nearest in age, counting their naevi and recording their sun behaviour, and re-examined them two years later; set up to investigate genetic factors in naevus development and other risk factors for melanoma, it also includes the twins' parents and is the twin mole study of the Brisbane Longitudinal Twin Study.
location quote: The BTNS cohort has measurements for iris nevi in addition to the skin nevi used in the nevus GWAS meta-analysis. The cohort comprises a sample of predominantly adolescent twins (age 9–23 years) and their parents from Southeastern Queensland, Australia.
parent quote: SPHERE-34 was administered as part of three main projects that make up the Brisbane Longitudinal Twin Study (BLTS; also known as the Brisbane Adolescent Twin Study (BATS)) [8]. The first two waves of data were collected in the clinic, following an assessment of Melanocyte Naevi (moles) around the twelfth (TWin Mole study visit 1: TW1) and fourteenth birthday of the twins (TWin Mole study visit 2: TW2)
note: Tier E (E138), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: BTNS as the Queensland control source in a colorectal-cancer GWAS (paired with a separate Melbourne cohort). P3-P4: co-cited abstracts about different, unrelated cohorts, not usable for BTNS itself. P5-P7: BTNS as an ongoing Queensland twin study of nevus count and melanoma/pigmentation genetics. P4 ('Genes in Myopia') is co-cited alongside BTNS in P1's sentence but is a separate Melbourne cohort, not a synonym; not used here. Country given as Australia via Queensland (E138.1); 'Brisbane' in the name confirms this independently. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, country and example were right. The definition was built from a 2025 abstract plus an appreciation article ('expanded into genetic discoveries in melanoma, eye colour and pigmentation' is narrative, not design) and did not say who ran it, that participants were re-examined two years later, or that parents were enrolled. The 2026 nevus GWAS meta-analysis (PMID:41807453, PMC13106845) calls it 'the QIMR Brisbane Twin Nevus Study (BTNS) cohort' and gives its population and purpose ('The cohort comprises a sample of predominantly adolescent twins (age 9–23 years) and their parents from Southeastern Queensland, Australia. The cohort was initially established to investigate the genetic factors influencing nevus development and other risk factors for melanoma'); parents of its twins were also the controls of PMID:24949998 (PMC4065098). The parent was missing: the nevus study is one of the three projects that make up the Brisbane Longitudinal Twin Study (COHO:0000744); PMID:28764680 (PMC5540428) says the first two BLTS waves were the twin mole study visits around the twelfth and fourteenth birthdays, which matches BTNS's examination at 12 and re-examination two years later ('The Brisbane Twin Nevus Study recorded sun behaviours and counted naevi on annual new samples of 12-year-old twins (and siblings nearest in age) from 1992 to 2016. Participants were re-examined 2 years later, and a subset was seen 20 years after the initial exam.', PMID:40576277). The draft's country quote names only Queensland; it is replaced by one that names Australia next to the cohort. 'Brisbane Twin Naevus Study' (PMID:24949998, PMID:29040338) and the BLTS papers' 'TWin Mole study' are added as synonyms. BTNS is a sub-study, not the whole of COHO:0000744: BLTS also comprises the twin cognition project at about 16 and later waves (19Up), which recruited twins who were not in the nevus study, while BTNS also enrolled parents, whom the BLTS term does not mention. If the curator prefers, BTNS could instead be added to COHO:0000744 as a synonym, but the PGS id and the nevus papers use it for this specific sample. The 'TWin Mole study' synonym keeps the capitalisation of PMC5540428, which marks the wave labels TW1 and TW2. Not a duplicate of COHO:0001226 (Queensland Twin Registry, established 2006) or COHO:0000015 (Australian Twin Registry). The draft's P4 (Genes in Myopia) is a separate Melbourne sample, rightly not used.

label: Bus Santé
other synonyms: Bus Santé study|Bus santé|Bus Sante
example quote: We replicated findings using de novo genotyping in the Bus Santé Study and in silico data in all other cohorts.
definition: A repeated cross-sectional population-based health examination survey of adults living in the canton of Geneva, Switzerland, which since 1992 has examined in a mobile unit, each year, a new random sample of residents drawn from the cantonal residents list and stratified by age and sex, collecting questionnaires, physical measurements and blood samples on risk factors for cardiovascular and other lifestyle-related chronic diseases.
location quote: We used data from the Bus Santé study, an ongoing yearly population-based cross-sectional study of adults living in the state of Geneva, Switzerland.
note: Tier E (E139), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because the evidence file held nothing (the PGS Catalog lists BusSante in no score). Europe PMC finds over a hundred papers on the study. It is a named, well-defined population sample: 'an ongoing yearly population-based cross-sectional study of adults living in the state of Geneva, Switzerland' (PMID:37250185, PMC10209490), in which 'Since 1992, on a yearly basis except during the 2020–2022 COVID-19 pandemic, a representative random sample of 1000 participants is recruited from the general population in Geneva, stratified according to age and sex.' (PMID:40235578, PMC11999646); 'Participant selection was based on a residents list provided by the local government, including individuals aged 35–74 years until 2017.', participants are invited to 'the mobile unit', and 'Each participant was assessed only once, as each year a new random sample is selected.' (PMC10209490). Its questionnaires cover 'a series of risk factors for major lifestyle–related chronic conditions' (PMID:39081844, PMC11286997). It has been used genetically: the serum calcium GWAS meta-analysis replicated its loci by genotyping Bus Santé participants (PMID:24068962), which is the example. Label: the study writes 'Bus Santé'; the PGS Catalog's 'Bus santé' and the unaccented 'Bus Sante' (PMC11999646 figure titles) are kept as synonyms, and the PGS id BusSante as the acronym. Start year: two papers say 'since 1992' (and the ethics approval is dated 1992), one says 'launched in 1993'; the definition follows the majority. The study is a series of independent yearly samples, not a followed cohort, like other repeated surveys in COHO; later studies such as the SEROCoV-POP serosurveys drew on its participants but are not in COHO. Not related to E135 (BSN, which is the Busselton Health Study), E402 (GENEVA Study) or COHO:0000522 (CoLaus, Lausanne). The study is associated with the Unit of Population Epidemiology of the Geneva University Hospitals (acknowledged in PMC13038253), but no text read says in so many words that the unit runs it, so the definition names no institution.

Tier E (E140), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft minted the Basque Biobank as a cohort from a single acknowledgement, and its own definition ('a biobank ... that provides participant samples and data for research studies') describes a service, not a sample. The Biobanco Vasco is a biobanking platform, not a defined group of people: 'El Biobanco Vasco es una plataforma del ámbito hospitalario, orientada a fomentar la investigación básico-clínica para facilitar la generación de herramientas para la prevención, diagnóstico y descubrimiento de dianas terapéuticas.' It belongs to the Basque health research foundation and is organised as a network ('La Fundación Vasca de Innovación e Investigación Sanitarias-BIOEF es el titular del Biobanco Vasco, que tiene una estructura en red en el que participan los centros de salud de Osakidetza, Departamento de Salud del Gobierno vasco y Onkologikoa.'), and it holds many separate collections ('El Biobanco recoge muestras poblacionales, caso-control y cohortes procedentes de:'; its collections page lists a Basque-ancestry population collection, a sleep-apnoea group and a colon cancer screening group), all at https://www.biobancovasco.bioef.eus/es/PD5-quienes-somos.html and .../Para-profesionales/PD114-cohortes.html. In the only paper the PGS Catalog records it in (PMID:35232999), the PGS Catalog put the whole evaluation sample (PSS009588, 498 IBD cases and 935 controls) under BV, but the paper says the cases came from two hospitals ('IBD cases were diagnosed using standard criteria; and the samples used in this study were obtained in the standard clinical practice, after informed consenting, in Hospital Universitario Donostia (San Sebastian, Spain) and Hospital Universitario de Cruces (Barakaldo, Spain).') and only the controls came through the biobank ('The samples of non-IBD controls were obtained through the Basque Biobank.'), with the Basque Centre of Transfusion and Human Tissues thanked for access to them. So BV names a sample repository, like the review's institution tags (MSKCC, RUNMC, UCSF), and gets no term. The IBD case-control sample of PMID:35232999 has no name of its own (the paper calls it 'the Basque cohort analysed in the present study'), so no extra record is proposed; if the curator wants it, it would be IBD patients from Hospital Universitario Donostia and Hospital Universitario de Cruces with non-IBD controls from the Basque Biobank, Basque Country, Spain. One of the biobank's collections, a population sample of people with at least three generations resident in the Basque Country, could be a cohort in its own right, but nothing tags it. Not related to COHO:0000183 (Basquecolon cohort) or COHO:0000702 (Basque Center on Cognition, Brain and Language cohort).

Tier E (E141), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P2/P3: BWH = MS cases from Partners MS Center at Brigham & Women's Hospital plus BWH-based controls. P4: enriched further and renamed 'BWH/TT' with an added cohort. Composition changes each paper; not a single defined sample. BWH is institutional shorthand, not one fixed sample: MS cases from Partners MS Center at Brigham & Women's Hospital (E141.13), pooled with controls assembled from three separately named collections (MS Genetics spouses, BWH PhenoGenetic Project, HPCGG; E141.9), later merged with 'TT' into 'BWH/TT' (E141.27). Distinct from COHO:0000383 Mass General Brigham Biobank. Checked 2026-09-23: None in the verdict: BWH is the hospital's name for a hospital-based multiple sclerosis case series with borrowed controls whose make-up changes from paper to paper, and no source read gives it a study name. Two details of the draft's reasoning were off. In the meta-analysis stratum that PGS000809 uses (PMID:19525953, 860 cases and 1,720 controls), the controls were 'MIGen study–healthy control subjects and subjects with a history of early myocardial infarction & BWH healthy control subjects'; the three named control collections the draft cites (MS Genetics spouses, BWH PhenoGenetic Project, HPCGG) were the controls of the separate replication stratum, which the PGS sample (2,624 cases and 7,220 controls) does not include. In PMID:21654844 BWH is the cases only ('BWH, Partners MS Center in Boston, MA'), used for a severity analysis. The cases may be participants of the Partners MS Center's CLIMB study (Comprehensive Longitudinal Investigation of MS at the Brigham and Women's Hospital), but no text read says so: PMID:19525953 and PMID:22190364 name CLIMB only as the source of their RNA expression data. The controls come in part from MIGen, which is tier-E row E702. Not the Mass General Brigham Biobank (COHO:0000383) and not the Brigham and Women's Rheumatoid Arthritis Sequential Study (COHO:0001292).

label: Camargo Cohort Study
other synonyms: Cantabria-Camargo|Cantabria-Camargo study|Camargo Cohort|Camargo cohort|Camargo cohort study
example quote: Cantabria-Camargo study (Cabrio-C), Cantabria osteoporosis case-control study (Cabrio-CC): Instituto de Salud Carlos III-Fondo de Investigaciones Sanitarias Grants PI 06/34,PI09/539, PI12/615 and PI15/521 (that could be cofunded by European Union-FEDER funds).
definition: A prospective community-based cohort of postmenopausal women and men aged 50 years and older who attended a primary care centre in Camargo, Cantabria, in northern Spain, for a regular health examination or for medical reasons, enrolled between February 2006 and February 2011 and re-evaluated in later waves to study the prevalence and incidence of metabolic bone diseases and the risk factors for osteoporosis and fragility fractures.
location quote: The Camargo cohort was set up with postmenopausal women and men aged 50 years or older who attended a primary care centre in northern Spain for medical reasons or for their regular health examination, whichever occurred first.
note: Tier E (E142), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft found nothing and deferred. The id comes from the GEFOS bone-density and fracture papers, whose replication tables settle it: CABRIO-C, 'Cantabria-Camargo', is the Camargo Cohort Study. Supplementary Table 20A of the 2012 GEFOS meta-analysis (PMID:22504420) describes it as a 'Community‐based study designed to evaluate the prevalence of metabolic bone diseases in postmenopausal women and men older than 50 attended at a primary care center in Northern Spain' and cites two Camargo Cohort Study papers (PMID:20594548, PMID:19737549). The 2018 GEFOS fracture GWAS (PMID:30158200, open access) repeats that row and names it 'Cantabria-Camargo study (Cabrio-C)' in its funding list. The cohort's own name, used in its papers, is the Camargo Cohort Study; 'Cantabria-Camargo' is the consortium's name for it and is kept as a synonym. The draft's country 'from the name' does not hold, because the label does not name Spain; a quote now supports it. Sibling of E143 (CABRIO-CC), a different sample from the same Santander group: a clinic-based osteoporosis case-control study, not this community cohort. No parent: both papers are GEFOS/GENOMOS meta-analyses in which the cohort took part in replication genotyping, but no text read names it a member of GEFOS (COHO:0000826). The GWAS Catalog studies of these papers (GCST001482 and GCST007691 for PMID:22504420; GCST006422 for PMID:30158200) include it only in their replication samples and carry no cohort tags, so the example is the paper; a GCST example could be given if the curator wants the cohort in the GWAS subset. 'Camargo' as the town of the primary care centre comes from the cohort's name; the texts read say only 'a primary care centre in northern Spain' and title the cohort 'the Camargo cohort (Cantabria, Spain)'.

The id comes from the GEFOS replication tables: Supplementary Table 20A of the 2012 GEFOS meta-analysis (PMID:22504420) lists 'CABRIO‐CC Cantabria Osteoporosis Case‐control', design 'Case‐control, cross‐sectional', base 'Clinic‐based plus volunteers', Spain, Santander, described as a 'Clinic‐based study of control individuals and patients with osteoporosis living in Cantabria, a region in Northern Spain', with two reference papers of the Santander bone-metabolism group (PMID:17118999, a case-control study of women with vertebral fractures due to postmenopausal osteoporosis and controls; PMID:17218734, anthropometric, hormonal and genetic determinants of BMD in people over 50). No parent: no text read names it a member of GEFOS (COHO:0000826); it took part only in GEFOS/GENOMOS replication genotyping. As for E142, the GWAS Catalog studies of these papers (GCST001482, GCST007691, GCST006422) include it only in replication and carry no cohort tags. The recruitment period is not given in any text read.

label: Coronary Artery Disease and Genomics

definition: A German case-control study of coronary artery disease that pools patients with angiographically documented coronary artery disease from the hospital catheter-laboratory-based AtheroGene Registry, enrolled in 1999–2004 at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and the German Federal Armed Forces Central Hospital in Koblenz, with controls without a history of myocardial infarction from the population-based Gutenberg Heart Study of the city of Mainz and the Mainz-Bingen district, assembled for genome-wide association studies of coronary artery disease.
location quote: CADomics (Coronary Artery Disease and genomics) is a German-based case-control study of CAD.
parent quote: CARDIoGRAM combines data from all published and several unpublished GWAS in individuals with European ancestry; includes >22 000 cases with CAD, MI, or both and >60 000 controls; and unifies samples from the Atherosclerotic Disease VAscular functioN and genetiC Epidemiology study, CADomics, Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology, deCODE, the German Myocardial Infarction Family Studies I, II, and III, Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Heath Study/AtheroRemo, MedStar, Myocardial Infarction Genetics Consortium, Ottawa Heart Genomics Study, PennCath, and the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium.
note: Tier E (E144), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred because it saw only the CARDIoGRAM table row. The cohort's own GWAS paper and a CARDIoGRAM-era supplement settle it. CADomics is a German case-control study of coronary artery disease from Mainz: 'CADomics is a case-control study including the hospital-based catheter-lab AtheroGene Registry and the population-based Gutenberg-Heart Study (GHS)' (PMID:21606135), with angiographically proven CAD cases and controls without a history of myocardial infarction; the Lancet ADAMTS7 webappendix (PMID:21239051) calls it 'a German-based case-control study of CAD' and gives the AtheroGene enrolment (June 1999 to February 2004, Department of Medicine II of Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and the German Federal Armed Forces Central Hospital, Koblenz) and the GHS sampling (city of Mainz and the Mainz-Bingen district). The country is Germany: the French funders in the funding statement go with the INSERM partners in Paris, and no text read places any recruitment in France. The name is spelled out as 'Coronary Artery Disease and Genomics' in the cohort's own paper (the PGS Catalog's 'genomics' and CARDIoGRAM's 'and Omics' are kept as synonyms). It is a named member of CARDIoGRAM (COHO:0000745), which the draft missed. The draft's example quote was a 700-character dump of a supplement table; the example is now the cohort's own GWAS, GCST001079, whose whole discovery sample (2,078 cases, 2,953 controls) is CADomics. Composition: its cases come from the AtheroGene Registry (tier-E row E067, 'Atherogene Registry') and its controls from the Gutenberg Health Study (COHO:0000263); PMID:22144573 calls it 'the Gutenberg Heart Study/Atherogene Study (CADomics)'. It is typed cohort, as one case-control sample analysed as a single study, rather than as an aggregation of those two. GCST001079 carries no GWAS Catalog cohort tag; if the curator prefers the tier-E practice of a paper-only example, keep PMID:21606135 and the quote and drop the GCST. The name CADomics was also used for a German–French BMBF/ANR research project (grant 01KU0908A), which is a funding line, not a sample; PMID:21378990 spells it 'CARDomics' there. The check's GWAS Catalog study (GCST001079), dropped when this row was assembled, was restored on 2026-09-24.

label: Caerphilly Prospective Study

example title: Trans-ethnic and Ancestry-Specific Blood-Cell Genetics in 746,667 Individuals from 5 Global Populations.
example quote: The Caerphilly Prospective Study was undertaken by the former MRC Epidemiology Unit (South Wales) and was funded by the Medical Research Council of the United Kingdom.
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of men aged 45–59 years from the town of Caerphilly and its surrounding villages in South Wales, United Kingdom, identified from electoral rolls and general practice lists and first examined in 1979–1983 by the MRC Epidemiology Unit (South Wales) to study risk factors for coronary heart disease, then re-examined in later phases that added cognitive testing and follow-up for dementia and other chronic diseases.
location quote: Population-based, South Wales, UK.
parent quote: United Kingdom UNK-BEL: Belfast/PRIME Study UNK-CAE: Caerphilly UNK-EDI/GLA/SHH/SHE: Scottish Heart Health Extended Cohort (SHHEC)
note: Tier E (E145), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P6 (all found by name): each refers to the same Caerphilly Prospective Study cohort (also 'CaPS'/'CaPs' in some papers, and in P5's title only, the '35-Year Caerphilly Cohort Study'); no PGS Catalog citation paper was listed for this id. Population, design and South Wales, UK location (E145.15) are directly stated across six independent papers (1993-2023). Acronym case varies (CaePS/CaPS/CaPs); all kept. Distinct from the separately tracked Barry Caerphilly Growth Study (BCG), another South Wales cohort not evidenced here. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label and country were right. The definition left out the town, the dates, who ran it and its original purpose: CaPS was set up 'to study the influence of CVD risk factors in the development of coronary heart disease' in men aged 45 to 59 'living in the town of Caerphilly and five adjacent villages, South Wales, UK' (PMID:28106791), identified 'from electoral rolls and general practice lists' and first seen in 1979–1983 (PMID:37844990), and 'was undertaken by the former MRC Epidemiology Unit (South Wales)' (PMID:32888493 supplement). The draft missed a parent: Caerphilly (UNK-CAE) is one of the MORGAM cohorts (COHO:0000117), with a full description on the MORGAM site. The draft also missed that a GWAS Catalog tag denotes this cohort: 'CaPS' is on 30 studies of the blood-cell trait GWAS PMID:32888493, whose Table S1B row reads 'CaPS | Caerphilly Prospective Study', so the example is now one of those studies (GCST90002292, basophil count), not a 1993 abstract whose quote says only 'the Caerphilly study'. 'CAPS' is added as an acronym because the BiomarCaRE design paper (PMID:25238720) writes 'CAPS, Caerphilly Prospective Study'; 'Caerphilly Prospective Heart Disease study' is the MORGAM description's name for it. GWAS subset: the tag CaPS was earlier matched without regard to case to COHO:0000025 (Cancer Prostate in Sweden, acronym CAPS); the note on COHO:0000025 in example_studies_curated.tsv already says 'Original CaPS match refers to the Caerphilly Prospective Study'. That is why the triage counted no GWAS study for this name. Map the tag to this term and put it in the GWAS subset. Because the overlapping-synonyms check ignores case, CaPS, CaPs and CAPS here clash with CAPS on COHO:0000025, so both terms need editor notes: here 'The acronym CAPS also denotes Cancer Prostate in Sweden (COHO:0000025); this term is the Caerphilly Prospective Study.', and on COHO:0000025 the converse. Tier-E row E159 (CAPS_b, Carotid Atherosclerosis Progression Study) will need the same if it is minted with CAPS. Not the Barry Caerphilly Growth Study (tier-E row E098), a separate cohort. The MORGAM description gives Population Health Sciences, University of Bristol, as the cohort's administrative centre since 2017 (formerly Queen's University Belfast). The check's GWAS Catalog study (GCST90002292), dropped when this row was assembled, was restored on 2026-09-24.

location quote: A replication study of the previously identified variants at 22 candidate lipid loci was performed in the general Japanese population; from 5745 individuals consecutively enrolled in the population-based setting, which is known as Amagasaki Study [26], 4990 individuals without receiving current treatment for dyslipidemia were included in the present study (Table 1).
parent quote: in the 3 population- based studies of Japanese (Amagasaki, Fukuoka, and KING Studies of CAGE Network, N = 21,875 in total)
note: Tier E (E146), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred, having seen only the two PGS papers' supplement rows. The cohort is the Amagasaki Study: 'an ongoing population-based cohort study of 5,743 individuals (3,435 males and 2,310 females), aged >18 years and recruited for a baseline examination between September 2002 to August 2003' (PMID:26648100, which places Amagasaki in Hyogo Prefecture); 'individuals consecutively enrolled in the population-based setting, which is known as Amagasaki Study' (PMID:23050023). Its own name is the Amagasaki Study; 'Cardio-metabolic Genome Epidemiology Network, Amagasaki' is the consortium tables' name and is kept as a synonym. The draft left the parent empty because it did not find the CAGE Network in COHO, but it is COHO:0000027 (acronym CAGE, whose location quote already describes the Network), and the 2011 AGEN blood-pressure GWAS names 'Amagasaki, Fukuoka, and KING Studies of CAGE Network'. Both PGS papers' supplement rows cite the Amagasaki Study's own paper (PMID:19262484). The draft's example quote was the bare tag; it is replaced by the full supplement row. Parent: COHO:0000027 is typed cohort and defined as a type 2 diabetes case-control collection, but it is in fact the CAGE Network, an umbrella of member studies (the Amagasaki Study, the Kyushu University Fukuoka Cohort Study (E147), the NCGM Hospital-based Cohort Study (E148), the KING Study (COHO:0001065) and others such as CAGE-Vietnam). isSubCohortOf is given to fit its current type; if the curator retypes COHO:0000027 as a cohort aggregation (the Cardio-metabolic Genome Epidemiology Network), the relation for all four should become membership. KING, minted in tier D without a parent, has the same evidence: the quote above, and the height GWAS supplement's 'CAGE-KING-Quad Kita-Nagoya Genomic Epidemiology Study of the CAGE Network'. The Amagasaki samples also appear in the GWAS Catalog studies of PMID:21572416 (GCST001072, GCST001074) as replication samples, without a cohort tag. 'CAGE-Amagasaki_EAS' in PMID:36224396 is an ancestry-suffixed file label and is not added.

label: Kyushu University Fukuoka Cohort Study
other synonyms: Fukuoka Cohort Study|Fukuoka Study|Fukuoka Cohort
example title: Relation of coffee consumption and serum liver enzymes in Japanese men and women with reference to effect modification of alcohol use and body mass index.

definition: A community-based prospective cohort of middle-aged and older Japanese men and women in Fukuoka, Japan, run by Kyushu University, who took part in a baseline survey with a questionnaire and DNA collection between February 2004 and August 2007 and are followed up to investigate lifestyle factors and genetic susceptibility to lifestyle-related diseases such as cardiovascular diseases, cancer and diabetes mellitus.
location quote: For study of lifestyle-related diseases, the Fukuoka Cohort was constructed from 2003 to 2009 in Kyushu area in Japan, which contains a total of 12,949 persons.
parent quote: for Fukuoka Study and Kita-Nagoya Genomic Epidemiology [KING]Study of the CAGE Network
note: Tier E (E147), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1 (CRC GWAS, PGS Catalog source-GWAS paper): its 'Fukuoka'/'Fukuoka Colorectal Cancer Study' (E147.7/.10/.13) is a separate CRC case-control set tracked elsewhere in this review (FCCS), not this row. P2: no quotable unit. P3/P4/P6 (found by name): describe this cohort directly, matching PGS Catalog's own name. PGS Catalog's own source-GWAS paper (P1) actually names a different cohort (Fukuoka Colorectal Cancer Study); its CRC case/control subset is excluded. Definition and example instead drawn from P3/P4/P6, which consistently describe this cohort's own baseline survey and purpose. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label and example are right. The definition called the participants 'affiliated with Kyushu University' (the university runs the study; the participants are residents) and did not say what the cohort is for: it collected questionnaires and DNA 'to investigate lifestyle factors and genetic susceptibility of the so-called lifestyle-related diseases such as cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and diabetes mellitus' (PMID:24647736 supplement). The draft missed the parent: the study is the 'Fukuoka Study ... of the CAGE Network' (PMID:21572416), i.e. a member study of the Cardio-metabolic Genome Epidemiology Network (COHO:0000027). The draft's country quote gave only 'Japanese men and women'; it is replaced by one that places the cohort in Japan. The PGS id's tag meaning in the draft was right: in the id's only PGS papers it denotes a different sample (see note). The PGS id CAGE-Fukuoka, named 'Kyushu University Fukuoka Cohort Study' by the PGS Catalog, denotes in its only scored use (PGS002252, source GWAS PMID:25105248) the Fukuoka Colorectal Cancer Study, which is tier-E row E335 (FCCS). Under the acronym rule E335's term should also carry CAGE-Fukuoka, with editor notes on both terms ('The acronym CAGE-Fukuoka also denotes the Fukuoka Colorectal Cancer Study (…); this term is the Kyushu University Fukuoka Cohort Study.' and the converse). Both are Kyushu University studies (each paper cites the Kyushu University Faculty of Medical Sciences ethics committee) but they are different samples: a colorectal cancer case-control study versus a community cohort surveyed in 2004–2007. Parent: see E146's note; COHO:0000027 should be retyped as the CAGE Network aggregation, after which the relation becomes membership. The baseline dates of 2003–2009 in PMID:21297916 differ from the February 2004–August 2007 given by the study's own investigators, which the definition follows.

example quote: National Center for Global health and Medicine hospital-based cohort study (CAGE-NCGM) aims to prospectively investigate the relationship between genetic and non-genetic factors.

The PGS Catalog's name is copied from the supplement of the East Asian HbA1c GWAS (PMID:24647736, open access), which describes it: 'National Center for Global health and Medicine hospital-based cohort study (CAGE-NCGM) aims to prospectively investigate the relationship between genetic and non-genetic factors. The participants were enrolled for the detailed examination of lifestyle and lifestyle-related diseases such as cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and diabetes mellitus. The NCGM investigators themselves call it 'the Hospital-based Cohort Study at the National Center for Global Health and Medicine' (PMID:26648100 and PMID:23050023), which is used as the label; its hospital is in Tokyo (PMID:26648100). Probably the same study as the 'Hospital-Based Cohort Study in IMCJ' thanked in the 2009 Japanese type 2 diabetes GWAS (PMID:19401414), since the International Medical Center of Japan (IMCJ) is the former name of the NCGM, but no text read states the rename, so that name is not added as a synonym. Not the NCGM Biobank or the NCGM BIO-CVD study, which PMID:41708081 describes as separate NCGM projects; that paper's 'NCGM hospital cohort (N = 351) previously reported' is probably this cohort. example quote: We genotyped 59 tagged SNPs in 2278 RCC cases and 3719 controls from two nested case–control studies [the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial and the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention (ATBC) study in Finland], a hospital-based Central and Eastern European RCC (CEERCC) case–control study and Caucasians from the United States Kidney Cancer (USKC) population-based case–control study (see Materials and Methods and Fig. 1).
