Participants were interviewed with standardised questionnaires on lifestyle, diet and medical, residential and occupational history and gave blood for DNA, to study the causes of the region's high kidney cancer rates.
location quote: This hospital-based case–control study was conducted in seven centres (Moscow (Russia), Bucharest (Romania), Lodz (Poland), and Prague, Olomouc, Ceske Budejovice, and Brno (Czech Republic)).
note: Tier E (E181), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CEERCC as one of several case-control studies genotyped/pooled for RCC susceptibility SNPs, with its own design given (E181.13-17); P2: PGS score-development paper for the same PGS000722 signal, no evidence extracted. Source marked 'free, not open access' for full text, but rule allows free (not just open access) for country quotes. Controls were hospital patients admitted for unrelated diagnoses (E181.7,E181.9), not general-population controls. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, acronym, countries and example were right. The label was a paraphrase from the example paper that keeps the abbreviation RCC; the study's own papers spell the acronym out as 'Central and Eastern European Renal Cell Carcinoma (CEERCC) study' (PMC2737618, PMC3111161, whose abbreviation list reads 'CEERCC=Central and Eastern European Renal Cell Carcinoma.'), and also use 'Renal Cell Cancer', 'Renal Cancer' and 'Kidney Cancer' forms, now synonyms beside the draft's label and the PGS Catalog name. The definition omitted who ran the study (IARC with the US National Cancer Institute), the case age range and the control source, the controls shared with IARC's parallel lung and head and neck cancer studies, and what was collected. The country quotes came from a free but not open-access PDF; they are replaced by the same four countries quoted from the open-access (CC BY) first report of the study, PMID:19034282. The example is unchanged except that its quote is taken from the PMC page, where the PDF's broken 'Alpha- Tocopherol' reads 'Alpha-Tocopherol'. Not in COHO. It is the kidney cancer member of IARC's central European multicentre case–control studies, whose lung (COHO:0000870, IARC Multicenter Case-Control Study) and upper aerodigestive tract (COHO:0001087, International Agency for Research on Cancer Central Europe Study) studies are already terms; it shared part of its controls with them ('Some controls also were recruited in parallel for studies of lung and head and neck cancers (Scelo et al, 2004; Hashibe et al, 2007).', https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC3111161/fullTextXML). COHO has no term for the umbrella, so there is no parent; they are siblings, not the same people. Tier-E E1183 (USKC, US Kidney Cancer Study) is a different study used beside it in the example paper. The spelling Ceske Budejovice follows the sources.

input name: Population based case-control study of brain tumors in children and adolescents aged 7–19 years conducted in Sweden, Denmark, Norway, and Switzerland
label: CEFALO
other synonyms: Cefalo|CEFALO study
example title: A Weighted Genetic Risk Score of Adult Glioma Susceptibility Loci Associated with Pediatric Brain Tumor Risk.
example quote: The GRS was calculated in CEFALO, a population-based case-control study of brain tumors in children and adolescents including saliva DNA of 245 cases and 489 controls.
definition: An international population-based case–control study of primary intracranial brain tumours in children and adolescents aged 7–19 in Denmark, Norway, Sweden and Switzerland, whose cases were diagnosed between 2004 and 2008 and identified through hospitals and national cancer registries, and whose controls were drawn at random from population registries and matched by age, sex and region. The children and their parents were interviewed in person, mainly to find out whether mobile phone use and other exposures raise the risk of brain tumours; saliva DNA from part of the participants was genotyped in candidate-gene studies.
location quote: CEFALO is a population-based case-control study of brain tumors in children and adolescents aged 7–19 years conducted in Sweden, Denmark, Norway, and Switzerland.
note: Tier E (E182), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CEFALO as the target sample for a pediatric brain-tumor genetic-risk-score evaluation; P2-P3: CEFALO's own earlier candidate-gene analyses, cited for the cohort by P1. PGS Catalog 'name' field is a description ('Population based case-control study...'), not a real name; left out of synonyms per instructions. PGS id 'CEFALO' equals the label, so omitted from acronyms as a duplicate. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, countries and example were right. The definition only restated the PGS Catalog's description of the sample: it lacked when cases were diagnosed (2004–2008), how cases and controls were found (hospitals and national cancer registries; controls drawn at random from population registries and matched by age, sex and region), the in-person interviews, the study's primary aim (mobile phone use and brain tumour risk) and the saliva DNA used in its genetic studies. 'CEFALO study' is added as a synonym beside 'Cefalo'. Not in COHO and no other name in the review matches; the adult INTERPHONE study (tier-E E552) is a different study. The sources give no expansion of CEFALO, so the PGS id equals the label and is not repeated as an acronym (no acronym clash). No parent.

label: Color Genomics
other synonyms: Color Genomics participants|Color genomics study
example title: Polygenic background modifies penetrance of monogenic variants for tier 1 genomic conditions.
example quote: Second, a breast cancer case-control study consisted of 19,264 women (1920 cases and 17,344 controls) who underwent clinical grade genetic testing for hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome at a commercial testing laboratory (Color Genomics; Burlingame, CA).
definition: A research cohort of people whose healthcare provider ordered clinical-grade multi-gene panel testing for inherited disease risk, such as hereditary breast and ovarian cancer, from Color Genomics, a commercial genetic testing laboratory in Burlingame, California, and who gave electronic informed consent, under a Western Institutional Review Board protocol, for their de-identified samples, sequence data and health histories, self-reported through an online tool, to be used in research.
note: Tier E (E183), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft read the sources right (Color Genomics is a commercial testing laboratory) but drew the wrong verdict. In both papers the id denotes one defined group of people: those whose healthcare provider ordered a Color multi-gene panel test and who consented electronically to research use of their de-identified data and samples. PMID:31771638: 'The clinical cohort included DNA samples from 11,502 individuals whose healthcare provider had ordered a Color multi-gene panel test (Fig. 1b).' and 'All individuals in the technical concordance cohort and clinical cohort gave electronic informed consent to have their de-identified information and sample used in anonymized studies (Western Institutional Review Board, #20150716).' PMID:32820175 draws a breast cancer case–control set of 19,264 tested women from the same population and calls them 'Color Genomics participants'. The PGS Catalog's own sample descriptions (PSS000217–PSS000219) say the samples 'are individuals whose healthcare provider had ordered a Color Genomics multi-gene panel test'. COHO mints such research pools of genetic-testing companies as cohorts: 23andMe research cohort (COHO:0000449), AncestryDNA Human Diversity Project (COHO:0000742), Genotek COVID-19 study (COHO:0001083), 23Mofang cohort (COHO:0001138), WeGene cohort (COHO:0001250). The samples have no name of their own: 'Color Genomics' is the PGS Catalog's name and what both papers call the source ('Color Genomics participants' in PMID:32820175, 'the Color genomics study' in its supplement); a curator may prefer 'Color Genomics research cohort', parallel to COHO:0000449. Unlocated: the laboratory is in Burlingame, California, but neither paper says where the tested people live. No COHO term or other review name matches, and the acronym CG is unused in COHO. If the curator would rather not mint a clinical laboratory's tested population (unlike 23andMe or AncestryDNA it is not a direct-to-consumer research programme but patients whose providers ordered a clinical test), the alternative is 'not a cohort'.

label: Candidate Gene Association Resource
other synonyms: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Candidate Gene Association Resource|NHLBI Candidate Gene Association Resource|Candidate gene Association Resource|Candidate-gene Association Resource|Candidate Gene Association Resource Consortium|CARe Consortium|NHLBI CARe Project
example title: Candidate gene association resource (CARe): design, methods, and proof of concept.
example quote: The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute's Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe), a planned cross-cohort analysis of genetic variation in cardiovascular, pulmonary, hematologic, and sleep-related traits, comprises >40,000 participants representing 4 ethnic groups in 9 community-based cohorts.
definition: A shared genotype–phenotype resource set up by the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute in 2006, which brought DNA samples and phenotype data from nine NHLBI cohort studies (ARIC, CARDIA, the Cleveland Family Study, the Cardiovascular Health Study, the Cooperative Study of Sickle Cell Disease, the Framingham Heart Study, the Jackson Heart Study, MESA and the Sleep Heart Health Study) to the Broad Institute, genotyped their European American, African American, Hispanic and Chinese American participants on a candidate-gene array (the ITMAT-Broad-CARe array) and the African American participants of five of the cohorts genome-wide, and makes the data available to approved researchers, to find genetic variants associated with cardiovascular, pulmonary, haematological and sleep-related traits.
location quote: Participants were recruited from six field centers across the United States: Wake Forest University, Columbia University, Johns Hopkins University, University of Minnesota, Northwestern University and University of California - Los Angeles.
note: Tier E (E184), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CARe's own design/methods paper, defining it as a 9-cohort, 4-ethnic-group cross-cohort analysis; P2-P3, P6: CARe/CARe-Plus consortium analyses of fibrinogen, blood pressure and T2D loci in African-American participants; P4-P5: later reuse of CARe study data via dbGaP. PGS id 'CGARe' does not appear verbatim in evidence; papers use 'CARe'. Both kept as acronyms. 'Candidate Gene Association Resource Plus Study' (P6) may be a related extension, not conflated here. Possible duplicate of tier-E key E776 'NHLBI_CARe' in a different batch; not linked (same-as targets only tier-D). Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronyms and example were right. The definition said CARe pooled 'several community-based cohorts', but it assembled nine named NHLBI cohorts, one of them patient-based (the Cooperative Study of Sickle Cell Disease) and one family-based (the Cleveland Family Study); it lacked the start (2006), the Broad Institute's role, the two genotyping arms (a candidate-gene array for all participants, genome-wide arrays for African Americans from ARIC, JHS, CARDIA, CFS and MESA) and the sharing of the data. No country was given, although all nine member cohorts are in the United States; the quote is from CARe's dbGaP page for its MESA substudy, which describes where those CARe participants were recruited. The PGS id NHLBI_CARe of tier-E E776 (same resource) is added to the acronyms and its name to the synonyms. Not in COHO. Tier-E E776 (PGS id NHLBI_CARe, 'National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Candidate Gene Association Resource', also unused by any score) is the same resource and should be 'same as E184'. Members, for hasCohort from this aggregation, all in one sentence of the design paper ('The nine cohorts include the Atherosclerosis Risk In Communities (ARIC) study, the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study, the Cleveland Family Study (CFS), the Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS), the Cooperative Study of Sickle Cell Disease (CSSCD), the Framingham Heart Study (FHS), the Jackson Heart Study (JHS), the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), and the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) (Table 1).', https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/bionlp/RESTful/pmcoa.cgi/BioC_xml/PMC3048024/unicode): COHO:0000011 (ARIC), COHO:0000425 (CARDIA), COHO:0000427 (Cleveland Family Study), COHO:0000384 (CHS), COHO:0001308 (CSSCD), COHO:0000385 (Framingham Heart Study), COHO:0000381 (Jackson Heart Study), COHO:0000119 (MESA) and tier-E E1023 (SHHS, not yet in COHO). Acronym clash: the overlapping-synonyms check ignores case, so CARe collides with CARE on COHO:0000110 (Los Angeles component of the Women's CARE Study) and COHO:0000229 (Canadian Airways Research Group), which already carry notes about each other; this term needs a note such as 'The acronym CARE also denotes the Los Angeles component of the Women's Contraceptive and Reproductive Experiences Study (COHO:0000110) and the Canadian Airways Research Group (COHO:0000229); this term is the NHLBI Candidate Gene Association Resource.', and both of those notes need a sentence naming this term.

label: Copenhagen General Population Study
other synonyms: Herlev/Østerbroundersøgelsen
example title: Fifteen new risk loci for coronary artery disease highlight arterial-wall-specific mechanisms.
example quote: In brief, the European (EUR) studies comprised 16,093 CAD cases and 16,616 controls from EPIC-CVD (a case-cohort study embedded in the pan-European EPIC prospective study), the Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS), the Copenhagen Ischemic Heart Disease Study (CIHDS) and the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) all recruited within Copenhagen, Denmark.
definition: A prospective general-population cohort run from Herlev and Gentofte Hospital, Copenhagen University Hospital, and modelled on the Copenhagen City Heart Study, which from 2003 to 2015 invited adults aged 20–100 living in the greater Copenhagen area, identified through the Danish Civil Registration System (all those aged 40 or over and a quarter of those aged 20–39), and examined them with a questionnaire, a physical examination, lung function tests and blood sampling with DNA extraction. Participants are re-examined in a second round that began in 2014 and are followed through the national Danish health registries for cardiovascular, pulmonary and other diseases and death.
location quote: Three studies of white individuals from Copenhagen, Denmark, were used: the Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS), a 31-year prospective general population study (n = 9022; 28 heterozygotes); the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS), a cross-sectional general population study (n = 31,241; 76 heterozygotes); and the Copenhagen Ischemic Heart Disease Study (CIHDS), a case-control study (n = 16,623; 44 heterozygotes).
note: Tier E (E185), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P6: PGS Catalog score-development papers whose author affiliations include CGPS, with no cohort-specific description extracted; P7-P9: CGPS's own design, alongside the separate sibling studies Copenhagen City Heart Study and Copenhagen Ischemic Heart Disease Study; P10-P12: recent CGPS-specific analyses giving its 2003-2015 recruitment and registry follow-up. P7 (2008) calls CGPS 'cross-sectional' (n=31,241, superseded); P12 (2025) instead gives enrollment '2003 through 2015' with registry follow-up to 2021; used the later, fuller description and did not assert 'cross-sectional'. Sibling studies CCHS and CIHDS (E185.19) are separate cohorts. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type and country were right. The definition was thin: it lacked the host (Herlev and Gentofte Hospital), the design model (the Copenhagen City Heart Study), the sampling frame (residents of the greater Copenhagen area aged 20–100 invited through the Civil Registration System), the end of enrolment (2015), the baseline examination and the second examination round. The example quote was an author affiliation, which does not show that the paper used the cohort; it is replaced by a PGS Catalog paper (source GWAS of PGS000818 and PGS000899) whose methods name CGPS among its samples. The study's Danish name was missing as a synonym. Not in COHO. The other Copenhagen studies are separate cohorts, not parents: COHO:0001296 (Copenhagen City Heart Study, on which CGPS was modelled), tier-E E193 (CIHDS) and E204 (COGEN). The 2008 description of CGPS as 'cross-sectional' refers to early analyses of baseline data only. The draft's country quote (PMID:18523221 abstract) is kept.

Tier E (E186), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred for want of evidence. Research settles it as not a cohort: the Cancer Genomics Research Laboratory (CGR) is the genotyping and sequencing laboratory of the US National Cancer Institute's Division of Cancer Epidemiology and Genetics at Frederick, Maryland (affiliation line in PMC6218483: 'Cancer Genomics Research Laboratory (CGR), Division of Cancer Epidemiology and Genetics, FNLCR Leidos Biomedical Research, National Cancer Institute, Frederick, MD 21701 USA'). It genotypes samples of many studies but recruits no participants of its own, and no source uses CGR as the name of a sample. No COHO term or other review name matches. If a later PGS Catalog release attaches CGR to a score, it will most likely label cases or controls genotyped at the laboratory for a consortium, which belong to their own studies; the review treated such institution labels the same way for MSKCC and UPENN.

Tier E (E187), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred. Research settles what the id denotes. Every PGS Catalog use of 'Chicago' goes back to one sample: the male BRCA1/2 mutation carriers genotyped by CIMBA for PMID:28448241 (sample sets PSS000074–PSS000077, where 'Chicago' is one of 37 cohort entries: CIMBA and its member studies, among them UPENN, UPITT and MSKCC); the nine prostate cancer scores of the drafter's P1–P6 (PGS000084, PGS000160, PGS000348, PGS000795, PGS000881, PGS002791–PGS002793, PGS002796) list that same 1,525-man CIMBA sample among their variant sources, and name no other Chicago sample. In PMID:28448241 the Chicago contributor is the University of Chicago (author affiliation 'University of Chicago Medical Center, Chicago, IL'; funding note 'University of Chicago was supported by National Cancer Institute Specialized Program of Research Excellence (SPORE) in Breast Cancer (CA125183)'), the CIMBA site that CIMBA's later male-carrier paper calls 'University of Chicago (UCHICAGO)' (PMC8755508). The id is thus an institution label for one site's mutation carriers within CIMBA (COHO:0000901); the site sample has no name of its own. The review decided the same kind of label, UPENN and MSKCC, as not a cohort. No COHO term or other review name matches. If the curator prefers to mint CIMBA site samples, this would be 'University of Chicago CIMBA study' (BRCA1/2 mutation carriers ascertained through the University of Chicago's cancer genetics clinic), memberOf CIMBA (COHO:0000901), with PMID:28448241 as its example; the other institution-named CIMBA ids in tier E (for example E133 BRICOH, E333 FCCC, E465 HCSC, E522 ICO, E535 ILUH, E734 MUV, E859 OUH) raise the same question and should be decided the same way.

input name: China Multi-Center Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Epidemiology
label: China Multi-Center Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Epidemiology 1998
other synonyms: China Multi-Center Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Epidemiology
example title: A polygenic risk score improves risk stratification of coronary artery disease: a large-scale prospective Chinese cohort study.
example quote: The validation cohorts were derived from three cohorts in the China-PAR project, including the International Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Disease in Asia (InterASIA), the China Multi-Center Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Epidemiology (ChinaMUCA-1998), and Community Intervention of Metabolic Syndrome in China and Chinese Family Health Study (CIMIC).
definition: A population-based cohort of Chinese men and women aged 35–59, selected in 1998 by cluster random sampling in several provinces of China for the 1998 survey of the China Multi-Center Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Epidemiology (a separate sample from that study's 1992–1994 cohort), whose participants were followed up in 2007–2008, 2012–2015 and 2018–2020 under the uniform protocol of the China-PAR project to study cardiovascular risk factors and incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
location quote: These cohorts together covered 15 provinces and provided a good representation of residents across a wide range of geographical areas in China.
note: Tier E (E188), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ChinaMUCA-1998 as one of the China-PAR project's three founding cohorts (established 1998); P2-P3: PGS000262 evaluated in ChinaMUCA-derived validation cohorts; P4: China-PAR project's own risk-equation paper; P5-P6: earlier 'MUCA' papers describing the same-named study. P5 (2007) says the cohort 'MUCA' was established 'in early 1990's', conflicting with P1's 1998 date for 'ChinaMUCA-1998' specifically; used P1's date as it matches the exact tag. Child of the China-PAR project (E188.1-3), not resolvable to a COHO ID or tier-D key here, so parent left null. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type and example were right. The China Multi-Center Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Epidemiology recruited two separate cohorts, China MUCA (1992–1994) and China MUCA (1998) ('The China MUCA (1992–1994) and the China MUCA (1998) selected 14,392 (9 clusters) and 11,480 participants (11 clusters) aged 35–59 years using cluster random sampling method in 1992–1994 and 1998, respectively.', PMC8315380). The PGS id is the 1998 one, but the draft's label (the PGS Catalog name) and its acronym MUCA name the whole study, and its country quote (PMID:18712046, participants 'reexamined 6 years later') and the 2007 'MUCA' paper (PMID:17963640, a cohort 'established in early 1990's') are about the 1992–1994 cohort, which is where the draft's date conflict came from. The label now carries the year, as COHO labels of survey rounds do; MUCA is dropped and the forms the papers use for this cohort are added; the country quote is replaced by one about China MUCA (1998) and its sister China-PAR cohorts. The definition described the cohort only through China-PAR; it now says who was sampled, how and when. Not in COHO. It is a sub-cohort of the China-PAR project (Prediction for ASCVD Risk in China), which also comprises China MUCA (1992–1994), InterASIA (tier-E E550) and CIMIC (tier-E E194); China-PAR is neither in COHO nor a name of this review, so there is no parent. If China-PAR is minted as an aggregation, this term is a member ('The validation cohorts were derived from three cohorts in the China-PAR project, including the International Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Disease in Asia (InterASIA), the China Multi-Center Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Epidemiology (ChinaMUCA-1998), and Community Intervention of Metabolic Syndrome in China and Chinese Family Health Study (CIMIC).', https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC9076396/fullTextXML). Sources disagree on the number of 1998 clusters (11 in PMC8315380 and PMC10249193, 15 in PMC7249710), so the definition gives none. The PGS Catalog name is kept as a synonym because the Catalog uses it for this id, but it also names the whole MUCA study; if the 1992–1994 cohort is ever minted, it must not share this term.

label: Chingford 1000 Women Study
other synonyms: Chingford Study|Chingford study|Chingford 1,000 Women Study|Chingford general population survey|Chingford cohort|Chingford general population cohort
example title: The incidence and characteristics of accelerated knee osteoarthritis among women: the Chingford cohort.
example quote: Hence, we determined the incidence and characteristics of AKOA among women in the Chingford Study, which is a prospective community-based cohort.
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of women aged 45–64 registered with a large general practice in Chingford, North-East London, United Kingdom, recruited in 1988–1989 to study osteoarthritis, osteoporosis and other musculoskeletal disease and assessed annually for over 20 years (to 2010) with clinical examinations, nurse-administered questionnaires, hand and knee radiographs and bone density measurements; deaths are traced through the Office for National Statistics.
location quote: The Chingford 1,000 women study is a prospective population-based cohort of women 45-64 years old at the study set up (1989), registered in the large general practice in Chingford (North East London, United Kingdom) [12].
note: Tier E (E189), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P6: all denote the same Chingford women's general-population cohort (called 'Chingford Study', 'Chingford general population survey', 'Chingford cohort' or 'Chingford 1000 Women Study') across research on obesity, smoking, accelerated OA, BMI trajectories and footwear, 1981-2022. Country from the cohort's own name (Chingford, a place in England); no unit separately states a country. Later evidence (E189.21) gives women aged 50+; earlier papers (E189.2,7) give 45-64; treated as the same cohort over time, age not asserted in definition. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, acronym, country and example were right. The study's own name is the Chingford 1000 Women Study (its papers write 'Chingford 1000 Women Study (Chingford Study)', PMC8449034, and thank 'all the participants of the Chingford 1,000 Women Study', PMC8982643), so that is the label and 'Chingford Study' becomes a synonym. The definition lacked the sampling frame (women on the register of one large general practice), the age range, the start (1988–1989), the aims (osteoarthritis and osteoporosis), the annual assessments and the length of follow-up (1989 to 2010). The country was asserted from the name, which gives only a London district; it is now quoted. The draft's tag_meaning dated the evidence '1981-2022', but the 1981 paper titled 'The Chingford Study' (PMID:7335847, no abstract) predates the 1988–1989 start and cannot be this cohort. Not in COHO and no other review name matches. The cohort is one of the prospective cohorts pooled by the World COACH hip osteoarthritis consortium (PMID:38637130), which is not in COHO, so no parent. The PGS Catalog name 'Chingford study' differs from 'Chingford Study' only in capitalisation and is kept as a synonym.

label: Chinese Prostate Cancer Genetic and Environmental Correlation Study
example title: A genetic study and meta-analysis of the genetic predisposition of prostate cancer in a Chinese population.
example quote: These male Han Chinese subjects were recruited from several regions of China (south, southeast, southwest, middle and northeast) by members of the Chinese Prostate Cancer Genetic and Environmental Correlation Study (CHIPGECS) collaborative group.
definition: A case–control study of prostate cancer in Han Chinese men run by the CHIPGECS collaborative group of Chinese hospitals and universities with Barts Cancer Institute, Queen Mary University of London, which recruited hospital patients with a pathological diagnosis of primary prostate cancer and cancer-free men of comparable age from the community or from hospital attendees having routine physical examinations, in several regions of China (south, southeast, southwest, central and northeast), and whose samples were genotyped with the PRACTICAL consortium on the iCOGS and OncoArray arrays.
location quote: These male Han Chinese subjects were recruited from several regions of China (south, southeast, southwest, middle and northeast) by members of the Chinese Prostate Cancer Genetic and Environmental Correlation Study (CHIPGECS) collaborative group.
parent quote: CHIPGECS (n=1070) Chinese Prostate Cancer Genetic and Environmental Correlation Study China Population- based, case- control, observational
note: Tier E (E190), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: PGS Catalog source-GWAS link is erroneous (an unrelated 1989 paper on Franz Schubert's illnesses); P2: CHIPGECS's own design paper (source GWAS of PGS000795); P3-P4: cite CHIPGECS-derived PGS000795 in pan-cancer PRS evaluations; P5: lists CHIPGECS (n=1070) as a PRACTICAL-associated collaborating group. P1 (PMID:2688139) is unrelated, an apparent PGS Catalog metadata error, ignored. E190.13 lists CHIPGECS in PRACTICAL's 'Supplementary Consortia' table alongside PRACTICAL-member cohorts (CeRePP, COH, HPFS, IMPACT), but no unit states CHIPGECS is a member; parent left null for a checker to verify. The definition did not say who ran the study (a Chinese collaborative group formed with Barts Cancer Institute, London) or that its samples were genotyped with the PRACTICAL consortium (iCOGS in PMID:26881390, OncoArray in PMID:33623038). The parent was left open, but CHIPGECS is one of the PRACTICAL consortium's studies: PMID:33623038, whose 'present analyses used de-identified data from the PRACTICAL consortium', lists it in its study table (the quote) and under 'Additional funding and acknowledgments from studies in PRACTICAL:', so it is a member of COHO:0000611. Membership evidence beyond the quoted table row: in the same paper, the main text says 'The present analyses used de-identified data from the PRACTICAL consortium.' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC7902617/fullTextXML), and CHIPGECS's own paper says its genotyping was done 'In association with the Prostate Cancer Association Group to Investigate Cancer Associated Alterations in the Genome (PRACTICAL) consortium' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC5008293/fullTextXML). The PHS table calls the design population-based, while the design paper says the cases were hospital-based; the definition follows the design paper. The misattributed PMID:2688139 could be reported to the PGS Catalog. No COHO term or other review name matches; CHIPGECS is unused as an acronym in COHO.

label: ChooseWell 365
other synonyms: ChooseWell 365 Study
example title: Genetic predisposition to macronutrient preference and workplace food choices.
example quote: Here we examined the associations of polygenic scores for carbohydrate, fat, and protein preference with 12 months' workplace food purchases among 397 hospital employees from the ChooseWell 365 study.
definition: A randomized clinical trial among employees of Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, Massachusetts, aged 20 to 75, who regularly paid for food at the hospital's traffic-light-labelled cafeterias with their employee ID, enrolled between September 2016 and February 2018 and followed for 24 months to test whether a 12-month automated, personalized intervention (feedback on their cafeteria purchases, health and lifestyle tips, social norm comparisons and financial incentives) prevented weight gain and improved diet.
location quote: This randomized clinical trial was conducted on the main campus of Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH), a large academic teaching hospital in Boston, Massachusetts.
note: Tier E (E191), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: ChooseWell 365 as the trial population whose 397 genotyped participants were evaluated for macronutrient-preference polygenic scores; P2: the trial's own design paper; P3-P4: secondary analyses of chronotype and gut-microbial metabolites within the same trial. PGS id 'ChooseWell 365' duplicates the label, omitted from acronyms. PGS name 'ChooseWell 365 Study' (capital S) is not attested verbatim; evidence consistently uses lowercase 'study' as a descriptor, so left out of synonyms. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type and example were right. The definition was taken from a secondary genetic analysis (a free, not open-access author manuscript); it left out the place (Boston), who was eligible (employees aged 20 to 75 who bought food at the cafeterias with their ID at least four times a week), the 24-month participation (12-month intervention plus 12 months of follow-up) and what the intervention consisted of; it is now written from the trial's own open-access results paper (PMID:34097048, JAMA Netw Open) and the design paper's abstract (PMID:30414448). The country quote only named the hospital; it is replaced by the results paper's setting sentence, which names Boston, Massachusetts. The PGS Catalog name 'ChooseWell 365 Study' is a real name of the trial (papers write 'the ChooseWell 365 study') and differs from that usage only in capitalisation, so it is added as a synonym. Not in COHO or elsewhere in the review (searched ChooseWell, worksite, workplace, cafeteria). It is a single-site trial population, not a sample of the Mass General Brigham Biobank (COHO:0000383), so no parent. The registration's official title 'Promoting Employee Health Through The Worksite Food Environment' is a project title rather than a name the trial is known by, so it is not proposed as a synonym. The registration gives a minimum age of 21, the results paper 20; the definition follows the paper.

label: Children's Health Study
other synonyms: Southern California Children's Health Study|USC Children's Health Study|Childrens Health Study
example title: Multiancestry association study identifies new asthma risk loci that colocalize with immune-cell enhancer marks.
example quote: The Children's Health Study (CHS) is an ongoing cohort study in southern California investigating both genetic and environmental factors related to childhood asthma and lung function growth.
definition: A prospective study of schoolchildren in southern California, run by the University of Southern California, that from 1993 recruited successive cohorts from school classrooms in 16 communities chosen to differ in regional air pollution (fourth, seventh and tenth graders in 1993, fourth graders in 1996, and kindergarten and first-grade children in 2002–2003) and followed them through school with yearly questionnaires and lung function tests, to study the chronic effects of air pollution and other environmental and genetic factors on children's respiratory health, asthma and lung function growth.
location quote: To assess these hypotheses, we conducted a case-control study of risk factors for early-life asthma that was nested in the Children's Health Study (CHS), a population-based study of children's respiratory health in 12 southern California communities.
parent quote: Children'Health Study (CHS) Hispanic White CHS-LAT
note: Tier E (E192), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred with no evidence; research settles it. CHS_b is the Southern California Children's Health Study of the University of Southern California. Its only source in the PGS Catalog is the Trans-National Asthma Genetic Consortium GWAS (PMID:29273806, source of PGS000799), whose supplement describes it under the EVE consortium: 'The Children's Health Study (CHS) is an ongoing cohort study in southern California investigating both genetic and environmental factors related to childhood asthma and lung function growth.' The GWAS used a nested case-control sample of Hispanic white and non-Hispanic white children, which the definition does not describe. The definition is written from the study's own website (healthstudy.usc.edu: 'The USC Children's Health Study begins' in 1992; 4th, 7th and 10th graders from 12 communities in 1993; new 4th graders in 1996; four more towns and kindergarten and 1st graders in 2002) and its review (PMID:25694817: 'a continuing series of longitudinal studies that first began in 1993'; children 'selected from classrooms in 16 communities in multiple waves of subject recruitment starting in 1993 to maximize the differences in regional air pollution concentrations and mixtures'; yearly questionnaires until high school graduation; lung function measured annually), with the 2002–2003 cohort dated by PMID:20371422. Not in COHO. It is different from the Kaiser Permanente 'KPSC Children's Health Study' (PMID:21257603) and from the Hispanic Community Children's Health Study/Study of Latino Youth (COHO:0001411). The acronym CHS is also that of the Cardiovascular Health Study (COHO:0000384), so both terms need the editor note, for example 'The acronym CHS also denotes Cardiovascular Health Study (COHO:0000384); this term is the Children's Health Study.' 'Childrens Health Study' is the PGS Catalog's spelling without the apostrophe, kept as a synonym for matching. The parent follows COHO's existing TAGC membership of GRAAD (COHO:0001344), taken from the same supplementary table, where the CHS is one of the TAGC studies listed under the EVE consortium; EVE itself is not in COHO. The 2002–2003 kindergarten and first-grade cohort is called the USC AIR Study on the website; it is an arm of this study, not a synonym.

label: Copenhagen Ischemic Heart Disease Study
other synonyms: Copenhagen Ischaemic Heart Disease Study|Copenhagen ischaemic Heart Disease Study
example title: Fifteen new risk loci for coronary artery disease highlight arterial-wall-specific mechanisms.
example quote: In brief, the European (EUR) studies comprised 16,093 CAD cases and 16,616 controls from EPIC-CVD (a case-cohort study embedded in the pan-European EPIC prospective study), the Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS), the Copenhagen Ischemic Heart Disease Study (CIHDS) and the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) all recruited within Copenhagen, Denmark.
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of ischaemic heart disease in Denmark whose cases are patients from the greater Copenhagen area referred for coronary angiography to Copenhagen University Hospital from 1991 onwards, with ischaemic heart disease documented by coronary stenosis or atherosclerosis on angiography, a positive exercise electrocardiogram or myocardial infarction, and whose controls without ischaemic heart disease are sampled from the Copenhagen General Population Study; with the Copenhagen City Heart Study and the Copenhagen General Population Study it is used in genetic and Mendelian randomization studies of cardiovascular disease.
location quote: In brief, the European (EUR) studies comprised 16,093 CAD cases and 16,616 controls from EPIC-CVD (a case-cohort study embedded in the pan-European EPIC prospective study), the Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS), the Copenhagen Ischemic Heart Disease Study (CIHDS) and the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) all recruited within Copenhagen, Denmark.
note: Tier E (E193), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CIHDS as one of four European CAD studies (with EPIC-CVD, CCHS, CGPS) recruited in Copenhagen and pooled/genotyped for a CAD GWAS meta-analysis; P2: CIHDS only via a 'CGPS-CIHDS' combined table row, not quotable; P3-P5: PGS score-development papers, no CIHDS-specific text extracted; P6: names CIHDS as one of three Copenhagen cohorts in a vitamin D Mendelian-randomization study. No dedicated design/recruitment-date paper found; identity rests on its co-listing with CCHS and CGPS as a Copenhagen study contributing CAD cases/controls. American ('Ischemic') and British ('Ischaemic') spellings both attested; used the more frequent American spelling as label. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, country and example were right. The definition described the study only through one GWAS (its cases and controls 'pooled into an international genome-wide association meta-analysis') and called it one of several Copenhagen 'population studies', which it is not: its own descriptions make it a case-control study of patients referred for coronary angiography ('This case-control study comprises 5,270 patients from the greater Copenhagen area referred for coronary angiography to Copenhagen University Hospital during the period 1991–2009 and 5,270 unmatched controls without IHD randomly sampled from the CGPS.', PMC3341326; 'In addition to a diagnosis of IHD, these patients also had stenosis/atherosclerosis on coronary angiography and/or a positive exercise electrocardiography test, and/or MI.', PMC4606982). The end of recruitment grows with each paper (1991–2009, 1991 to 2010, 1991-2011), so the definition says 'from 1991 onwards'. The PGS Catalog name, with its lower-case 'ischaemic', is added as a synonym beside the British spelling. Not in COHO. No parent: its controls are sampled from the Copenhagen General Population Study (tier-E E185), but its cases are hospital patients, so it is not a sub-cohort of that study; COGEN (E204, Copenhagen Cardiovascular Genetic study, 2010–2017 cardiology admissions) and the Copenhagen City Heart Study (COHO:0001296) are separate studies. The American spelling is kept as the label, as in most of the study's papers; 'Copenhagen ischaemic Heart Disease Study' is the PGS Catalog's form, kept for matching.

input name: Community Intervention of Metabolic Syndrome in China and Chinese Family Health Study
label: Community Intervention of Metabolic Syndrome in China and Chinese Family Health Study
other synonyms: Community Intervention of Metabolic Syndrome in China & Chinese Family Health Study
example title: A polygenic risk score improves risk stratification of coronary artery disease: a large-scale prospective Chinese cohort study.
example quote: The validation cohorts were derived from three cohorts in the China-PAR project, including the International Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Disease in Asia (InterASIA), the China Multi-Center Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Epidemiology (ChinaMUCA-1998), and Community Intervention of Metabolic Syndrome in China and Chinese Family Health Study (CIMIC).
definition: A community-based cohort of Chinese adults aged 18 or over recruited in 2007–2008 by three-stage cluster random sampling at four survey sites, in Shandong, Henan and Jiangsu provinces, chosen for their different levels of economic development; it is one of the sub-cohorts of the Prediction for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk in China (China-PAR) project, followed up with the other sub-cohorts under a uniform protocol in 2012–2015 and 2018–2020 to study cardiovascular risk factors and incident cardiovascular disease.
location quote: The CIMIC was a large, community-based cohort that was established from 2007 to 2008 and selected four survey sites from three provinces (Shandong, Henan, and Jiangsu) with different economic development levels in China.
note: Tier E (E194), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CIMIC as one of the China-PAR project's three cohorts, giving its 2007-08 establishment and follow-up waves; P2-P3: further evaluations of PGS002262 in China-PAR-derived cohorts, no additional CIMIC-specific text; P4: the China-PAR project's own risk-equation paper (whole abstract, does not name CIMIC directly). Sibling of ChinaMUCA-1998 (drafted as E188 in a prior batch) and InterASIA within the China-PAR project. Parent (China-PAR project) is not a COHO ID or a tier-D key in this batch, so left null, matching E188's treatment. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, parent (none) and example were right. The definition said only that CIMIC is a Chinese cohort established in 2007-08 and followed up with China-PAR; it left out who was recruited and how ('The CIMIC is a large community-based study, which recruited 86,428 participants aged ≥18 years by a 3-stage cluster random sampling method in 2007–2008.', PMC8315380) and where (four survey sites in Shandong, Henan and Jiangsu, PMC7249710), and it called CIMIC one of three China-PAR cohorts, whereas the project has four sub-cohorts (China MUCA (1992-94), China MUCA (1998), InterASIA and CIMIC, PMC7190010); PMID:35195259 used three of them. Like ChinaMUCA-1998 (tier-E E188, whose check left the parent null for the same reason) and InterASIA (tier-E E550), it is a sub-cohort of the China-PAR project, which is neither in COHO nor a name of this review; if China-PAR is minted as an aggregation, this term is a member ('Briefly, the China-PAR project was carried out in 15 Chinese provinces and included four subcohorts: China MUCA (1992-94) (China Multi-Center Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Epidemiology),14 China MUCA (1998),15 InterASIA (International Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Disease in Asia),16 and CIMIC (Community Intervention of Metabolic Syndrome in China and Chinese Family Health Study).12', https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC7190010/fullTextXML). The China-PAR design paper (PMID:27682885, Circulation) is not in PMC and its publisher page answered with a bot check; the open papers above were enough.

input name: Mayo Clinic Center for Individualized Treatment of Addiction
label: Mayo Clinic Center for the Individualized Treatment of Alcoholism Study
other synonyms: Mayo Clinic Center for the Individualized Treatment of Alcoholism study|Mayo Clinic Center for Individualized Treatment of Alcoholism study|Mayo Clinic Center for Individualized Treatment of Addiction|Mayo Clinic Center for the Individual Treatment of Alcohol Dependence|Mayo Clinic Center for Individualized Treatment of Alcohol Dependence|A Probe Study of Acamprosate: Genes Associated With Response
example title: Transancestral GWAS of alcohol dependence reveals common genetic underpinnings with psychiatric disorders.
example quote: The alcohol dependent patients in this sample were recruited as part of the Mayo Clinic Center for Individualized Treatment of Addiction (CITA) pharmacogenomics study of acamprosate response.
definition: A pharmacogenomic study of acamprosate response in alcohol dependence, conducted from 2008 to 2013 by the Mayo Clinic Center for the Individualized Treatment of Alcoholism, which enrolled men and women aged 18–80 with a primary diagnosis of current alcohol dependence (DSM-IV-TR) whose last drink was at least 5 days before enrolment, from community-based residential and outpatient treatment programmes affiliated with Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota, and Mayo Clinic Health System sites in Austin and Albert Lea, Minnesota, and La Crosse, Wisconsin, treated them with acamprosate for 3 months in an open-label, naturalistic prospective design and collected DNA and plasma to identify biomarkers of treatment response.
location quote: Participants were recruited from community-based residential and outpatient treatment programs affiliated with Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota, and the Mayo Clinic Health System sites in Austin, Minnesota, Albert Lea, Minnesota, and La Crosse, Wisconsin.
note: Tier E (E195), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CITA as an alcohol-dependence case cohort contributing to a transancestral alcohol-dependence GWAS, with its own Mayo Clinic Biobank-sourced controls; P2: score-development paper for an unrelated sudden-cardiac-death score, CITA mentioned only via PGS metadata, no text extracted. Mayo Clinic Biobank (COHO:0000401) supplied CITA's controls (E195.3,7) but is not asserted as a parent, only a control source. A table row (not quotable) gives an alternate name 'Individual Treatment of Alcohol Dependence', not used as a synonym. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, acronym, country and the example paper were right. The label was the PGS Catalog name, which comes from the acknowledgements of the PGC alcohol dependence GWAS; the study's own investigators call it 'the Mayo Clinic Center for the Individualized Treatment of Alcoholism Study' (PMC9270258; also without 'the' in PMC11269006, and the NIH grant P20 AA017830 is titled 'The Mayo Clinic Center for Individualized Treatment of Alcohol Dependence'), and cite ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00662571 for it, registered as 'A Probe Study of Acamprosate: Genes Associated With Response' (acronym ACAM, May 2008 to February 2013). The draft's name, the PGC table's 'Mayo Clinic Center for the Individual Treatment of Alcohol Dependence' and the registry title and acronym are now synonyms. The definition omitted that participants were treated with acamprosate for 3 months in an open-label naturalistic design, where they were recruited (Mayo-affiliated treatment programmes in Rochester, Austin, Albert Lea and La Crosse) and when; its place came from an ethics-approval sentence, and 'case series' undersold the design. The country quote (the same ethics-approval sentence) is replaced by the recruitment sentence of the GWAS's own CITA sample description, and the example quote (a funding acknowledgement) by that description's first sentence. Not in COHO. The Mayo Clinic Biobank (COHO:0000401) supplied the PGC GWAS's controls for these cases; it is not a parent. ACAM is the ClinicalTrials.gov acronym of the registered study; no paper uses it. The registry calls the design observational and case-control, while the study's papers describe an open-label, naturalistic, prospective acamprosate treatment study; the definition follows the papers.

input name: ChiLdhood Arthritis Risk factor Identification sTudY
label: ChiLdhood Arthritis Risk factor Identification sTudY
other synonyms: Childhood Arthritis Risk Factor Identification Study|CLARITY JIA Biobank
example title: Genomic risk scores for juvenile idiopathic arthritis and its subtypes.
example quote: Finally, in the Australian cohort, from the ChiLdhood Arthritis Risk factor Identification sTudY (CLARITY),28 29 all the cases were JIA diagnosed by a paediatric rheumatologist.
definition: A case-control study and biobank of juvenile idiopathic arthritis at the Royal Children's Hospital in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, begun in February 2008, whose cases are children aged 18 or under with juvenile idiopathic arthritis diagnosed by age 16, recruited at hospital clinic visits within six months of diagnosis (incident) or later (prevalent, diagnosed since 1997), and whose controls are healthy Victorian-born children undergoing minor elective surgery at the hospital's Day Surgery Unit; families complete questionnaires on clinical, epidemiological and environmental factors and the children give a blood sample, to identify genomic and environmental risk factors for the disease.
location quote: We have established a JIA biobank in Melbourne, Australia called CLARITY - ChiLdhood Arthritis Risk factor Identification sTudY, with the broad aim of identifying genomic and environmental disease risk factors.
note: Tier E (E196), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CLARITY as the Australian JIA case-control validation cohort for a genomic risk score, with its case/control ascertainment described; P2-P7: whole abstracts of papers cited for the cohort's genetic findings, none naming CLARITY; P8: CLARITY's own founding/protocol paper; P9-P10: CLARITY's own replication and sibling-exposure analyses. CHOP (COHO:0000489) is a separate validation cohort analysed alongside CLARITY, not a parent. Case-variant synonym 'Childhood Arthritis Risk Factor Identification Study' (normal capitalisation) from E196.122, kept per the capitalisation rule. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, synonym, type, country, parent (none) and example were right. The definition mixed the design paper's abstract with the case definition used by the genomic risk score paper ('all the cases were JIA diagnosed by a paediatric rheumatologist'); it lacked the start of recruitment (February 2008), the hospital where cases are recruited, the age limits, who the controls are (healthy children born in Victoria having minor elective surgery) and what is collected (questionnaires and a blood sample). It is now written from the study's own design paper (PMID:23153063, PMC3551677, open access), which also calls it 'The CLARITY JIA Biobank', added as a synonym. Not in COHO. The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia sample (COHO:0000489) and the UK cohort are separate validation and training cohorts in PMID:32887683, not parents; COHO:0000236 (CLUSTER, childhood arthritis and uveitis) is an unrelated UK consortium.

label: California Men's Health Study
other synonyms: California Mens Health Study
example quote: The CMHS is a prospective cohort study of KP California men.
definition: A prospective multiethnic cohort of men aged 45 to 69 who were members of the northern and southern California regions of the Kaiser Permanente health plan, recruited in 2002–2003 through a two-stage mailed or online questionnaire with mailing strategies to enrich the cohort with non-white men, and followed through linkage with the health plan's electronic clinical, laboratory, hospitalisation, cancer registry and mortality data, mainly to study the causes of prostate cancer and also of other cancers and non-cancerous conditions in men.
location quote: In 2002 – 2003, we established the California Men's Health Study (CMHS), a multiethnic cohort of 84 170 men ages 45 to 69 years who are members of the northern and southern California regions of Kaiser Permanente, the largest managed care organization in California.
parent quote: Our primary analyses used cases and controls from three KP studies: RPGEH, ProHealth, and CMHS.
note: Tier E (E197), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred with no evidence; research settles it. CMHS is the California Men's Health Study of Kaiser Permanente, one of the three Kaiser Permanente studies whose prostate cancer cases were combined in the multiethnic prostate cancer GWAS (PMID:26034056, GCST002944), the source GWAS of every PGS Catalog score that records the id ('The CMHS is a prospective cohort study of KP California men.'); the GWAS cites the cohort's design paper, 'California Men's Health Study (CMHS): a multiethnic cohort in a managed care setting' (PMID:16813653, open access), from which the definition is written. Not in COHO. It is a member of COHO:0000945 (ProHealth Kaiser GWAS), whose members RPGEH (COHO:0000473) and ProHealth (COHO:0000879) carry the same quote and URL, so the parent follows them. The GWAS Catalog study of that paper, GCST002944, does not tag CMHS, so the example is the paper. 'California Mens Health Study' is the PGS Catalog's spelling without the apostrophe, kept for matching. It is unrelated to the Nashville Men's Health Study (tier-E E804) and to the Shanghai Men's Health Study (COHO:0000578).

Tier E (E198), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CNG as the Paris genotyping laboratory that processed French melanoma-study controls (distinct from WTCCC's UK 1958-cohort controls); P2: CNG as the genotyping site for IARC's ARCAGE and Central-Europe upper-aerodigestive-tract case-control studies' French/Norwegian samples; P5-P7: background lung-cancer GWAS papers cited for context, no CNG mention. CNG (Centre National de Génotypage, Evry/Paris) is consistently a genotyping facility, not a named cohort: it 'held'/genotyped 'French controls' (E198.1,5,17) and processed ARCAGE/Central-Europe samples (table rows, not quotable). No unit calls it 'CNG cohort' or 'CNG study'; the actual samples are generic controls or the named ARCAGE/Central-Europe studies. Checked 2026-09-23: None in the verdict: in every paper the PGS Catalog records the id in, CNG is the Centre National de Génotypage (Evry, France) as the source of generic population controls that it genotyped or held, not a named study. The draft's reading of PMID:21437268 is slightly off: there the PGS Catalog lists ARCAGE and IARCCES separately, and CNG stands for the 'generic controls' genotyped by the centre ('1,823 French and 433 Norwegian controls genotyped by the Centre National Genotypage (CNG Evry France)'), not for the IARC studies it also genotyped. No term. The French controls are probably participants of SU.VI.MAX (review key E1070): the GenoMEL fine-mapping paper that reused the same 'population-based controls obtained from the Center National de Génotypage in France' thanks the SU.VI.MAX study for data access (PMID:25077817, PMC4328144), and a French leukaemia GWAS used 'healthy French adults of European descent from the SU.VI.MAX study' genotyped by the CNG on the same HumanHap300 array (PMID:26868379, PMC4754340). None of the three source GWAS says so, and in PMID:21437268 the id also covers Norwegian controls, so CNG should not be mapped to E1070.

input name: Spanish National Cancer Centre Breast Cancer Study

parent quote: BCAC DACC approval is required to access data from the 2SISTER, ABCS, ABCS-F, ABCTB, BBCC, BCEES, BCFR-NY, BCFR-PA, BCINIS, BIGGS, BREOGAN, BSUCH, CECILE, CGPS, CNIO-BCS, CPSII, CTS, DIETCOMPLYF, ESTHER, FHRISK, FHRISK, GENICA, GEPARSIXTO, HABCS, HCSC, HEBCS, HMBCS, HUBCS, KARBAC, KARMA, KBCP, KCONFAB/AOCS, LMBC, MABCS, MBCSG, MCBCS, MISS, MMHS, MTLGEBCS, NBCS, NCBCS, OBCS, ORIGO, PKARMA, PREFACE, PROCAS, RBCS, SEARCH, SKKDKFZS, SUCCESSB, SUCCESSC, SZBCS, TNBCC, UCIBCS, UKBGS, UKOPS and USRT studies (Supplementary Table 1).
note: Tier E (E199), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: CNIO-BCS as one contributing GWAS study in a large breast-cancer PRS paper, author affiliation tying it to CNIO, Madrid; P2: BCAC's own GWAS paper listing CNIO-BCS among DACC-governed member studies, plus its Spanish-agency funding acknowledgment; P3-P6: further PGS score-development papers reusing BCAC data, no CNIO-BCS-specific text extracted. Distinct from bare 'CNIO' (COHO:0000902's acronym, the unrelated UROMOL bladder-cancer study); no relation asserted between them. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, country (from the name) and parent were right. The definition had no design, recruitment, place or dates ('a breast cancer study based at' CNIO, from an author affiliation and a funding statement); BCAC's description of its studies (Table S2 of PMID:25390939, 'A description of each BCAC study with subjects of European origin in iCOGS', open access) gives them: cases, 2000-2005, 'consecutive breast cancer patients from three public hospitals, two in Madrid and one in Oviedo' plus familial cases 'recruited through the CNIO family cancer clinic in Madrid'; controls, 'Women attending the Menopause Research Centre, Madrid and female members of the College of Lawyers attending a free, targeted medical check-up in Madrid'. The example's quote was the bare acronym from a supplementary table of PMID:30554720; it is replaced by a sentence of a PGS Catalog source GWAS (PMID:32424353, open supplement) that names the study as one of its contributors. The draft's parent quote comes from the subscription publisher page of that paper; the author manuscript in Europe PMC (PMC7808397) prints a shorter DACC list without CNIO-BCS, so if an open quote is needed, Table S2 of PMID:25390939 lists CNIO-BCS among the BCAC studies. The BCAC papers' author affiliations for the study's clinicians are Hospital Universitario La Paz (Madrid) and Hospital Monte Naranco (Oviedo), probably two of the three hospitals, and the ethics committee in the BCAC table is that of Hospital Universitario La Paz; the definition does not name the hospitals because no source says which they are.

input name: Nutrition, Metabolism and Atherosclerosis Clinic (CNMA) of Institut de recherches cliniques de Montréal
label: Nutrition, Metabolism and Atherosclerosis Clinic cohort

example quote: In the UK Biobank cohort, cases of monogenic FH were identified from the general population based on genotype, whereas individuals from the BCFH and CNMA cohorts were identified from lipid clinics based on a clinical diagnosis of FH.

note: Tier E (E200), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: PGS000019 evaluation paper mentioning CNMA, no evidence extracted; P2: CNMA as one of three familial-hypercholesterolemia cohorts (with BCFH and UK Biobank) compared for an LDL-C polygenic score, giving its clinic identity and ethics approval; P3-P7: papers cited for context (monogenic/polygenic FH risk, UK Biobank), not about CNMA itself. CNMA's general recruitment/dates are only 'described previously' (reference not given here). The one described subset, 552 individuals carrying a French-Canadian LDLR variant (E200.39), is this paper's own selection and is not asserted as the whole clinic cohort. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, verdict, type, acronym, country and example paper were right. The label was the clinic's name; the sample is the clinic's cohort of patients with familial hypercholesterolaemia, which the source GWAS paper calls 'the Nutrition, Metabolism and Atherosclerosis Clinic (CNMA) cohort' and 'Nutrition, Metabolism and Atherosclerosis Clinic cohort (CNMA cohort)', so the label now says cohort and the clinic's name, the PGS Catalog name and the French name behind the acronym are synonyms.
