The country quote was an ethics-approval sentence that also named two other studies; it is replaced by a sentence placing the clinic in Montreal, and the example quote by one that describes the CNMA cohort. Not in COHO. Its sibling in PMID:33079599, the British Columbia Familial Hypercholesterolemia cohort, is tier-E E088; neither is part of the other. The same clinic's FH patients appear in the Montreal-FH-SCORE papers (PMID:28391914, PMID:28801029) without the CNMA name.

input name: Centre National de Recherche et de Formation sur le Paludisme
note: Tier E (E201), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. CNRFP (Centre National de Recherche et de Formation sur le Paludisme) is a Burkina Faso malaria research institute: a WANECAM trial funding/partner body (E201.1/.2/.5/.8/.9) and the local ethics IRB for a Burkina Faso trial (E201.12), not a named sample of participants. Checked 2026-09-23: None: the verdict is right. CNRFP is the Burkina Faso national malaria research and training institute in Ouagadougou; no source uses the name or the abbreviation for a defined sample of people. The PGS Catalog cohort list carries the id without any released score or sample set using it, so no paper shows what sample the curators meant. Burkina Faso participants CNRFP collected for genetic studies (for example MalariaGEN's severe-malaria case-control data) are named after the country or the consortium, not after CNRFP.

input name: Chonnam National University Lung Cancer Study
label: Chonnam National University Lung Cancer Study
example quote: Internal sets (HKS, SNU, CNULCS, SWHS, YLCS and components of samples from Japan and GELAC) were genotyped at the NCI Cancer Genomic Research (CGR) Laboratory using the Illumina 660W SNP microarray.
definition: A case–control study of lung cancer based at Chonnam National University Hwasun Hospital in Jeollanam-do, South Korea. From 2000 it enrolled consecutive patients, all ethnic Koreans, with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed incident lung cancer, excluding secondary or recurrent tumours, and compared them with population-based controls to study genetic susceptibility to lung cancer. Its never-smoking women were genotyped genome-wide as one of the studies of the Female Lung Cancer Consortium in Asia.
location quote: The CNULCS was conducted in the Chonnam National University Hwasun Hospital in Jeollanam-do, South Korea and has been previously described
parent quote: Additional studies included in this GWAS are the Guangdong Study (GDS), the Hong Kong Study (HKS), the Japanese Female Lung Cancer Collaborative Study (JLCS)14 , the Chonnam National University Lung Cancer Study (CNULCS) Study15 , and the Yunnan Lung Cancer Study (YLCS).
note: Tier E (E202), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft had no evidence and deferred. Research shows CNULCS is a defined sample, not just the university: a hospital-based lung cancer case–control study at Chonnam National University Hwasun Hospital, and one of the 14 studies in the genome-wide association study of the Female Lung Cancer Consortium in Asia (FLCCA, COHO:0000864). Neither COHO nor the review has a duplicate. The South Korea Multi-Center Lung Cancer Study (E1036, SKLCS: the Seoul National University, Korea University Medical Center and Kyungpook National University Hospital studies) is a different FLCCA study. The link between the name CNULCS and the Piao/Cui case–control study is Lan 2012's citation of Piao 2011 as CNULCS's description; the two papers share the case definition and the exclusion of secondary or recurrent tumours. The controls were taken from the thyroid survey in the Piao/Cui analyses. Lan 2012's table marks CNULCS as 'included with SNU', and Machiela 2015 lists 451 CNULCS controls, so which controls were used in the FLCCA scans is not stated; the definition says only 'population-based controls'. The parent quote comes from Lan 2012's Supplementary Note, which lists the studies of 'this GWAS'; the main text says the authors 'formed the Female Lung Cancer Consortium in Asia (FLCCA)' for it.

label: An Epidemiological Study of Periodontal Disease and Diabetes: Cytokine Genes and Inflammation Factors
other synonyms: COBRE for Oral Health Study|COBRE for Oral Health|Center of Biomedical Research Excellence for Oral Health pilot project
example quote: Participants from three SIFP projects were included in our study: the Sea Island Genetic African American Registry (Project SuGAR) (Divers et al., 2010); the Center of Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE) for Oral Health pilot project, “An Epidemiological Study of Periodontal Disease and Diabetes: Cytokine Genes and Inflammation Factors” (Fernandes et al., 2009); and the Systemic Lupus Erythematosus in Gullah Health (SLEIGH) Study (Kamen et al., 2008).
definition: A cross-sectional genetic and epidemiological study of periodontal disease and caries in Gullah African Americans with type 2 diabetes from the Sea Islands and coastal low country of South Carolina. The Medical University of South Carolina ran it as the first project funded through its NIH Center of Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE) for Oral Health. Participants were recruited in 2004–2006 from Project SuGAR, community health fairs and churches, were examined at MUSC in Charleston or at four off-site centres and gave blood for DNA, so that periodontal disease could be related to diabetes control, cytokine genes and inflammation. Their data form one of the studies of the Sea Islands Genetics Network.
location quote: Recruitment was restricted to residents of South Carolina living along the coastal border and 30 miles inland.
note: Tier E (E203), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft had no evidence and deferred. The PGS id names the Medical University of South Carolina's COBRE for Oral Health project: a defined sample of Gullah African Americans with type 2 diabetes, recruited in 2004–2006, examined for periodontal disease and caries, and bled for DNA. It is one of the four studies whose data make up the Sea Islands Genetics Network (SIGNET). Neither COHO nor the review has a duplicate. The Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia (COHO:0001000, 0001440, 0001444) is unrelated. Parent: SIGNET, the network whose data include this study, is not in COHO as an aggregation. Tier D minted the tags SIGNET and SIGNET-REGARDS as COHO:0001132, which is REGARDS's genotyped African American subset, so it is not a parent of this study. If the curator mints a Sea Islands Genetics Network aggregation, it would have hasCohort links to this study, Project SuGAR (E930), SLEIGH (E1040) and COHO:0001132, quoting Liu 2013. The study screened some participants from Project SuGAR but is its own study, not a sub-cohort of it. Label: COBRE for Oral Health is the funding programme (MUSC's NIH COBRE grant, whose Center for Oral Health Research ran several projects), and the sample is its first, pilot project. The label is therefore that project's own title, 'An Epidemiological Study of Periodontal Disease and Diabetes: Cytokine Genes and Inflammation Factors'. The PGS Catalog name and the investigators' usual short forms, 'COBRE for Oral Health' and 'the Center of Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE) for Oral Health pilot project', are kept as synonyms. A curator who prefers the name used in genetic papers can make 'COBRE for Oral Health Study' the label instead. COBRE is also the generic name of the NIH funding mechanism and of an unrelated schizophrenia imaging dataset in New Mexico, but no COHO term carries it, so no clash note is needed.

label: Copenhagen Cardiovascular Genetic study
other synonyms: The Copenhagen Cardiovascular Genetic study
example title: Insulin resistance genetic risk score and burden of coronary artery disease in patients referred for coronary angiography.
example quote: The Copenhagen Cardiovascular Genetic study (COGEN) is comprised of approximately 80,000 patients admitted to six cardiology departments in the capital region of Copenhagen, Denmark, from 2010–2017.
definition: A biobank of whole blood left over from the clinical care of patients admitted in 2010–2017 to six cardiology departments in the Capital Region of Denmark, around Copenhagen. The samples are linked to Danish clinical registries such as the Eastern Danish Heart Registry, and genotyped subsets of the patients, for example those who underwent coronary angiography in 2010–2014, are used to study the genetics of coronary artery disease, heart failure and other cardiovascular disease.
location quote: The Copenhagen Cardiovascular Genetic study (COGEN) is comprised of approximately 80,000 patients admitted to six cardiology departments in the capital region of Copenhagen, Denmark, from 2010–2017.
parent quote: Of the nine case collections, seven were primarily focused on HF while two identified HF cases from an at‐risk population (COGEN and LURIC).
note: Tier E (E204), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Inter99 is a separate Danish cohort analysed alongside COGEN for a genetic risk score comparison (E204.8/.9), not a parent; 'Cogen' lowercase kept as case-variant acronym from the supplement. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, acronyms (COGEN plus the paper's own 'Cogen'), country and example were right. The label carried the PGS Catalog's leading article; the article is dropped and the PGS form kept as a synonym. The definition said 'a cohort of patients' and gave only admission place and years. COGEN is a biobank of superfluous (left-over) whole blood from those admissions, linked to the Eastern Danish Heart Registry, and only subsets have been genotyped (first the patients who had coronary angiography in 2010–2014). The parent was missing: COGEN is one of the heart failure case collections of the HERMES consortium (COHO:0000915). Neither COHO nor the review has a duplicate; COGENT (COHO:0000999) and COGEND (COHO:0000727) are unrelated. COGEN is not the Copenhagen Hospital Biobank (COHO:0000046) or its Cardiovascular Disease Cohort (CHB-CVDC, PMID:36070241). The CHB takes left-over blood-bank samples (blood typing and antibody screening) from all hospitalised patients and is genotyped by deCODE. COGEN is a separate collection from six cardiology departments, genotyped on the Illumina CoreExome chip, and the CHB-CVDC profile does not mention it. All COGEN papers give ethics approval from the Region North Jutland committee (N-20140048), reflecting the Aalborg-based investigators, but recruitment was in the Capital Region only.

label: Collaborative Oncological Gene-environment Study
other synonyms: Collaborative Oncological Gene-Environment Study|Collaborative Oncology Gene-Environment Study|Collaborative Oncology Gene-environment Study|International Collaborative Oncology Gene-environment Study
note: Tier E (E205), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred with no evidence. 'Collaborative Oncology Gene-Environment Study' is a common variant of the name of the Collaborative Oncological Gene-environment Study (COGS/iCOGS), which COHO already has as COHO:0000731. No study called COGES exists in the literature. COGES is the PGS Catalog's own abbreviation, probably coined because the Catalog's id COGS was already taken by a colorectal cancer study (E206). Add COGES as an acronym and the 'Collaborative Oncology…' name forms as synonyms of COHO:0000731. The PGS Catalog form 'Collaborative Oncology Gene-Environment Study' and the papers' 'Collaborative Oncology Gene-environment Study' differ only in capitalisation, and both are kept. The full acronym and synonym lists above include the term's existing ones. No new clash: COGES is used by no other term. The acronym COGS that COHO:0000731 already carries is also the PGS id of E206 (a colorectal cancer study); see E206.

label: Colorectal Cancer Genetic Susceptibility Study
other synonyms: Colorectal Cancer Genetics Study|Colorectal Cancer Susceptibility Study
example title: Multiple common susceptibility variants near BMP pathway loci GREM1, BMP4, and BMP2 explain part of the missing heritability of colorectal cancer.
example quote: Scotland1 (COGS) [1] included 980 CRC cases (51% male; mean age at diagnosis 49.6 years, SD±6.1) and 1,002 cancer-free population controls (51% male; mean age 51.0 years; SD±5.9).
definition: A Scotland-wide study run from Edinburgh from 1999 that approached patients newly diagnosed with colorectal cancer at age 55 or younger. Research nurses visited them at home to take a family pedigree, give genetic counselling and take blood for genetic testing, to evaluate a strategy for finding families with hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer and to study inherited susceptibility to colorectal cancer. Population controls matched by age, sex and area of residence were recruited through the Scottish NHS. Its early-onset cases and controls formed the Scotland1 genome-wide association study of colorectal cancer.
location quote: The Colorectal Cancer Genetic Susceptibility (COGS) study aims to evaluate a new Scottish-wide research strategy for identifying individuals at high risk of developing HNPCC.
note: Tier E (E206), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred without evidence. In every paper the PGS Catalog records for COGS, the id means the Scottish early-onset colorectal cancer case–control study of the Edinburgh group, the 'Scotland1' GWAS series listed beside CoRGI, SOCCS, NSCCG and VICTOR. Its own name is the Colorectal Cancer Genetic Susceptibility (COGS) study. The PGS name 'Colorectal Cancer Genetics Study' is a garbled expansion. The id is neither COHO:0000585 (CRCGEN, a Spanish study) nor COHO:0000731 (the Collaborative Oncological Gene-environment Study, which shares the acronym). Not in COHO or the review under this name. Its sister study, the Study of Colorectal Cancer in Scotland (SOCCS, COHO:0000421; 'Scotland2', cases aged under 80), was run by the same Edinburgh group in parallel. Papers keep COGS and SOCCS apart (for example 'Cases were obtained from the Colorectal Cancer Susceptibility Study (COGS) (n = 1012), Scottish Colorectal Cancer Study I and III', PMC12356881), so COGS is not modelled as a sub-cohort of SOCCS. A curator who prefers one umbrella could instead make COGS isSubCohortOf COHO:0000421, citing Tenesa 2008's single 'prospective population-based study in Scotland (1999-2006)'. Clashes, each needing editor notes on both terms: (1) the acronym COGS is carried by COHO:0000731 (Collaborative Oncological Gene-environment Study); (2) the PGS Catalog's name 'Colorectal Cancer Genetics Study', kept here because the Catalog tags this id with it, is already a synonym of COHO:0000585 (CRCGEN, from PMID:38664626). If the curator treats the PGS name as simply wrong rather than a database tag, dropping it from this term removes clash (2). The GWAS series name 'Scotland1' is not proposed as a synonym: it names the genotyped sample set in the meta-analyses, not the study. COGS is also listed as a member study of the colorectal COGENT (COlorectal cancer GENeTics) consortium (PMID:19920828, PMC2816642). COHO lacks that consortium, and its acronym COGENT is already carried by COHO:0000999, the Continental Origins and Genetic Epidemiology Network.

label: ColoCare Study
other synonyms: ColoCare study|International ColoCare Study
example title: Suitability of circulating miRNAs as potential prognostic markers in colorectal cancer.
example quote: This pilot study is based on the ColoCare Study, a cohort study of newly diagnosed patients with stage I-IV colorectal cancer.
definition: An international, multicentre prospective cohort of adults newly diagnosed with invasive colorectal cancer of any stage. It began at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center in Seattle in 2007 and from 2009 added sites in Tampa, Heidelberg (Germany), Salt Lake City, Los Angeles, St. Louis and Memphis. Patients are enrolled before surgery. They complete questionnaires and give blood, urine and stool at enrolment and repeatedly during five years of follow-up, tumour and adipose tissue are collected at surgery, and treatment and outcome data are abstracted from medical records, so that biomarkers and modifiable lifestyle factors that predict recurrence, survival, treatment toxicity and quality of life can be found.
location quote: ColoCare is recruiting newly diagnosed patients with colorectal cancer across six sites in the United States and one site in Germany.
parent quote: ColoCare Study (ColoCare)
note: Tier E (E207), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. No design/profile paper in evidence: stage range, US sites, Germany site and 'since 2010' each rest on a different paper found by name. No unit states an overall study purpose beyond 'cohort study of newly diagnosed' CRC patients. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronym and example were right. The definition was stitched from single papers. 'Recruited since 2010' is wrong: the study began at Fred Hutchinson in Seattle in 2007, and 2010 is when the Heidelberg site joined. It named only the sites of one analysis, missing Tampa (Moffitt, 2009) and Memphis. It left out enrolment before surgery, the repeated questionnaires and biospecimens over five years, and the study's purpose (biomarkers and lifestyle factors predicting recurrence, survival, toxicity and quality of life). The design paper (PMID:30523039) was not in the evidence and gives all of this. The United States quote did not name the country; one abstract sentence of the design paper now covers both countries. The parent was missing: ColoCare is one of the studies of GECCO (COHO:0000610), which is how it entered the PGS Catalog's colorectal cancer scores. Neither COHO nor the review has a duplicate. The design paper also calls the collaboration the 'international ColoCare Consortium', but it is one prospective cohort with harmonised protocols at all sites, so the type 'cohort' is right. Heidelberg's German arm is part of the same study, not a separate cohort.

input name: Colorectal Cancer: Longitudinal Observational study on Nutritional and lifestyle factors that influence colorectal tumor recurrence, survival and quality of life
label: Colorectal cancer: Longitudinal, Observational study on Nutritional and lifestyle factors that influence colorectal tumour recurrence, survival and quality of life
other synonyms: Colorectal Cancer: Longitudinal Observational study on Nutritional and lifestyle factors that influence colorectal tumor recurrence, survival and quality of life|COlorectal cancer: Longitudinal, Observational study on Nutritional and lifestyle factors that may influence colorectal tumour recurrence, survival and quality of life|Colorectal cancer: Longitudinal, Observational study on Nutritional and lifestyle factors that may influence colorectal tumour recurrence, survival and quality of life|COLON study|Longitudinal, observational study on nutritional and lifestyle factors for colorectal cancer and related outcomes
example title: Novel Common Genetic Susceptibility Loci for Colorectal Cancer.
example quote: Colorectal Cancer: Longitudinal Observational study on Nutritional and lifestyle factors that influence colorectal tumor recur- rence, survival and quality of life (COLON): The COLON study is sponsored by Wereld Kanker Onderzoek Fonds, in- cluding funds from grant 2014/1179 as part of the World Cancer Research Fund International Regular Grant Programme, by Alpe d’Huzes and the Dutch Cancer Society (UM 2012–5653, UW 2013-5927, UW2015-7946), and by TRANSCAN (JTC2012-MetaboCCC, JTC2013-FOCUS).
definition: A multicentre prospective cohort of patients newly diagnosed with colorectal cancer of any stage, recruited in 2010–2020 at 11 hospitals in the Netherlands by investigators at Wageningen University. Participants complete questionnaires on diet, dietary supplements, physical activity, body weight and quality of life and give blood at diagnosis and 6 months, 2 years and 5 years later, while clinical data come from the Netherlands Cancer Registry and hospital records. The aim is to learn how diet and other lifestyle factors influence recurrence, survival and quality of life after colorectal cancer.
location quote: The COLON study is a multi-centre prospective cohort study among at least 1,000 incident colorectal cancer patients recruited from 11 hospitals in the Netherlands.
parent quote: Longitudinal, observational study on nutritional and lifestyle factors for colorectal cancer and related outcomes (COLON)
note: Tier E (E208), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: COLON itself (real); P2-P4 matched only on the word 'colon' (colon cancer disease/anatomy, or the GECCO/CORECT/CCFR consortia), not this study. No unit gives recruitment place or dates directly; Wageningen is investigator affiliation, not asserted as country. No membership of GECCO stated for COLON specifically, only a shared acknowledgments page. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, acronym and example were right. The label was the PGS Catalog's re-spelled form (US 'tumor', no comma); the design paper's own form is now the label, with the PGS form, the design paper's title and abstract forms, 'COLON study' and GECCO's wording as synonyms. The definition only restated the name. It lacked the design: adults newly diagnosed with any stage, 11 Dutch hospitals, recruitment 2010–2020, questionnaires and blood at diagnosis, 6 months, 2 and 5 years, and linkage to the Netherlands Cancer Registry. The design paper (PMID:24886284, open access) was not in the evidence, so the Netherlands was missing although the sources state it. The parent was missing: COLON is a GECCO study (COHO:0000610), which is how it reached the PGS Catalog's colorectal cancer scores. Neither COHO nor the review has a duplicate. The NQplus study (Wageningen population cohort), which supplied COLON's GWAS controls, is a separate study and not part of COLON. The acronym COLON is also an ordinary word; no COHO term carries it, so no clash note.

input name: Post-Columbian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer
label: Post-Columbian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer
other synonyms: Colombian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer|Post Columbian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer|COLUMBUS Consortium
example title: A Polygenic Risk Score for Breast Cancer in US Latinas and Latin American Women.
example quote: The Post-Columbian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer (COLUMBUS) is a case-control study of breast cancer with individuals recruited throughout large cancer hospitals in central and 3 southern Colombia and Mexico City.
definition: A case–control study of breast cancer in Latin American women, led by investigators at the Universidad del Tolima in Ibagué, Colombia, and the University of California, Davis. From 2011 it recruited women with incident invasive breast cancer, through population cancer registries and large cancer hospitals in Bogotá, Ibagué and Neiva in central Colombia and Pasto in the south, together with cancer-free controls from the same institutions matched on education, socioeconomic status and local origin. A Mexican arm comprises cases diagnosed from 2010 at the Social Security hospital in Mexico City, with blood-donor controls from the same hospital. The study investigates inherited and environmental causes of breast cancer, and its Colombian and Mexican arms, genotyped on different arrays, are analysed as separate datasets.
location quote: The Post-Columbian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer (COLUMBUS) is a case–control study of breast cancer with individuals recruited throughout large cancer hospitals in central and southern Colombia and Mexico City.
note: Tier E (E209), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: COLUMBUS as a whole (Colombia + Mexico case-control study); the same paper also uses 'COLUMBUS-Colombia' and 'COLUMBUS-Mexico' for its two analysed sub-datasets. Name varies in the source: supplement says 'Post-Columbian' (E209.24), figure/table legends say 'Colombian Study...' (E209.5/.36). A checker should confirm whether Colombia and Mexico arms ought to be split into separate cohort terms instead. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, acronym, countries, parent (none) and example were right. The definition mixed a study description with one paper's analysis choice. It lacked when recruitment began (2011, Colombia; Mexican cases from 2010), the cities and recruiting channels (registries and cancer hospitals in Bogotá, Ibagué, Neiva and Pasto; the Social Security hospital in Mexico City), how controls were chosen, who runs it and its purpose. COLUMBUS began as the 'Colombian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer' (PMID:25327703: Colombia only, recruitment started 2011). With the Mexican arm it became the 'Post-Columbian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer' (2020 onward), which explains the two names the draft saw. The country quote is replaced by the same sentence from an open 2025 paper, without the page-number artefact ('central and 3 southern') of the supplement quote. Neither COHO nor the review has a duplicate. The Mexican CAMA study (Cancer de Mama) is a different study that is analysed beside COLUMBUS. Separate terms for COLUMBUS-Colombia and COLUMBUS-Mexico are not needed: no database tag names an arm on its own, and the PGS Catalog's sample sets use COLUMBUS for both. 'COLUMBUS Consortium' is the investigators' group name, which papers also use for the study's samples ('the COLUMBUS consortium samples from Mexico and Colombia'), so it is kept as a synonym; the study is one case–control study, not an aggregation.

label: Consortium for the Investigation of Renal Malignancies
other synonyms: Consortium For the Investigation of Renal Malignancies|CONFIRM Kidney Study
example title: Genome-wide association study identifies multiple risk loci for renal cell carcinoma.
example quote: ConFIRM/MCCS The ConFIRM study, also known as CARES, was supported by the Victorian Cancer Agency (PTCB08_05), the Australian National Health and Medical Research Council (Project Grant 1011626).
definition: A kidney cancer study run by Cancer Council Victoria with QIMR Berghofer, the Victorian and Queensland cancer registries and hospitals and familial cancer clinics across Australia; its Queensland arm is called the CARE Study. Its population-based case–control family component recruited, through the Victorian and Queensland cancer registries, people diagnosed in 2009–2015, at age 18–74, with histologically confirmed renal cell carcinoma, with siblings and partners of cases as controls. The study also enrolled people with a strong family history of kidney cancer or a hereditary kidney cancer syndrome. Participants completed questionnaires on health, lifestyle and family and medical history and gave blood, so that lifestyle, environmental and genetic causes of kidney cancer could be investigated.
location quote: The study included Australian residents diagnosed between 2009 and 2015 with a histologically confirmed RCC (ICD-10 C64) at age 18–74 years.
note: Tier E (E210), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Full name and 'CARES' synonym come from a garbled OCR table in the supplement (E210.6/.9/.12); the reading is fairly confident (ConFIRM's letters match Consortium For Investigation Renal Malignancies) but a checker should verify against the source PDF. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, country, parent (none) and example were right, and the draft read the garbled supplement table correctly: ConFIRM is the Consortium for the Investigation of Renal Malignancies. The study writes the name with a lower-case 'for'; the table's 'For' is kept as a case-variant synonym. The definition described the GWAS sample of one paper, not the study. In Scelo 2017 the ConFIRM cases diagnosed in 2011–2014 were paired with controls from the Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study, but the study itself is a case–control family study. It recruited cases diagnosed in 2009–2015 through the Victorian and Queensland registries, took siblings and partners as controls, also enrolled high-risk families, and was run by Cancer Council Victoria. The study's own capitalisation CONFIRM and the name 'CONFIRM Kidney Study' are added. 'CARES' is kept: Scelo 2017 says ConFIRM is 'also known as CARES', and Cancer Council Victoria calls its Queensland arm the CARE Study, short for Collaborative Australian Renal Cell Carcinoma Epidemiology. Neither COHO nor the review has a duplicate. The acronym CARE (the Queensland arm) is not added, because COHO:0000110 and COHO:0000229 already carry it and it names only one arm. CONFIRM is not the Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study (COHO:0000523), which supplied only the GWAS controls and some cases ('ConFIRM/MCCS'), so no parent. It is also not I-ConFIRM, the International Consortium for the Investigation of Renal Malignancies formed in 2013 and listed by the NCI Epidemiology and Genomics Research Program: a pooling consortium that is not in COHO and is not what these tags mean.

label: Danish National Patient Register
other synonyms: Danish National Patient Registry|Landspatientregisteret|Danish National Registry of Patients|Danish National Hospital Register
example title: Cerebral thromboembolism among young women and men in Denmark 1977-1982.
example quote: In the period 1977-1982, the Danish National Patient Register recorded 1000 cases of cerebral thromboembolic attacks among women 15-44 years of age, and 971 cases among men of the same age.
definition: A nationwide Danish hospital register, established in 1977 from the hospital discharge records that Denmark's counties were asked to submit and now kept by the Danish Health Data Authority, that records every patient discharged from Danish non-psychiatric hospitals since 1977 and psychiatric inpatients and emergency-department and outpatient specialty-clinic contacts since 1995, with diagnoses, examinations, treatments and surgical procedures. Kept primarily to monitor hospital use for health-care planning, it is also used, through linkage by personal identification number, for disease monitoring, quality assurance and research.
location quote: The Danish National Patient Register (DNPR) is an important data source for register-based health-related research, providing detailed information on all hospital contacts in Denmark.
note: Tier E (E271), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P3: early Danish epidemiological studies using DNPR data (arterial disease admissions, cerebral thromboembolism, general admissions); P4: DNPR diagnosis-quality validation (cataract); P6: DNPR's own profile/methods paper (nationwide hospital-contact register, DNPR2/DNPR3). Modelled like existing COHO registers (e.g. Hospital Discharge Register Sweden, COHO:0000093). No founding year stated; E271.1 shows register data from 1976. DNPR2/DNPR3 are versions of the same register, not separate acronyms. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, country and the absence of a parent are right; a national register typed as a cohort follows Hospital Discharge Register Sweden (COHO:0000093). The definition leaned on one 2026 perspective: 'maintained as a data source for register-based epidemiological research' inverts the register's purpose, whose primary aim is monitoring hospital use for health-care planning, with research a secondary use, and the DNPR2-to-DNPR3 switch in 2019 is a technical detail. It left out what the register covers and since when (all discharges from non-psychiatric hospitals since 1977; psychiatric inpatients, emergency and outpatient specialty-clinic contacts since 1995), which the register's profile (PMID:26604824, open access) states. The example was that perspective, a narrative synthesis of classification methods rather than a study that used the register's data; replaced by the 1986 Stroke study of cerebral thromboembolism, which analysed DNPR records for 1977-1982. Acronyms missed LPR, the register's Danish abbreviation (Landspatientregisteret). Synonyms added: the official English name given in the profile ('The official English name, as it appears in the registry declaration by the Danish Health and Medicines Authority, is the Danish National Patient Registry, DNPR'), the Danish name, and two English names the profile lists as common in the literature. Label kept as the PGS Catalog name: the Danish Health Data Authority's English list calls it 'The National Patient Register' and the 2011 profile is titled 'The Danish National Patient Register', while the 2015 profile gives 'Danish National Patient Registry' as the official English name (added as a synonym). 'National Patient Register' alone was not added, as Sweden, Norway and Finland have registers of that name. The Danish Psychiatric Central Research Register (E277) has been fed through the DNPR since 1995 but is a separate, older register, so neither is a sub-cohort of the other. E264 (Danish Health Service Register) is a different register. No COHO term or other review name is the DNPR.

label: Duke Neurogenetics Study
other synonyms: Duke Neurogenetics study
example title: Neural responses to threat and reward interact to predict stress-related problem drinking: A novel protective role of the amygdala.
example quote: We used well-established neuroimaging paradigms to probe threat-related amygdala and reward-related ventral striatum reactivity in a sample of 200 young adult students from the ongoing Duke Neurogenetics Study.
definition: A study of young adult university students aged 18–22, most of them Duke University undergraduates recruited on campus in Durham, North Carolina, United States, who between 2010 and 2016 completed self-report and behavioural measures, functional and structural brain MRI and genotyping in Duke University's Laboratory of NeuroGenetics. People with psychiatric diagnoses were not excluded, as the study set out to relate variation in behaviour, brain and genes to risk for psychopathology.
location quote: The Duke Neurogenetics Study (DNS) data were collected from high-functioning young adult university students in the United States, so that it would be premature to assume that the same findings would be replicated in samples drawn from the general population.
parent quote: DNS Duke Neurogenetics Study USA
note: Tier E (E272), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P6: all denote the same ongoing Duke Neurogenetics Study of young adult students, used across separate neuroimaging-genetics analyses of threat/reward reactivity and drinking, a galanin haplotype, sleep and amygdala reactivity, resting-state brain-state dynamics, borderline personality traits, and reward learning. No dedicated design/profile paper; definition drawn from repeated descriptions across 6 independent analyses. COHO:0000584 (CATHGEN, acronym 'Duke') is a different Duke cohort (cardiac catheterisation patients), matched only by the shared word 'Duke', not used. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, synonym, acronym, type and example are right. The definition restated the 2012 abstract: 'ongoing' is out of date (participants completed the study between January 2010 and November 2016, PMID:38711811), 'supported by Duke University' is a funding line (NIH grants R01DA033369 and R01DA031579 also funded it), and it left out who took part and where (18–22-year-old university students, mostly Duke University students recruited through flyers on the Duke campus and a Duke listserv, PMID:31629936), that psychiatric diagnoses were not an exclusion criterion (PMID:31677585), and the study's stated aim of linking behavioural, neural and genetic variation to psychopathology (PMID:28887539). The draft gave no country, though open-access text places the study in the United States. It gave no parent, but the Cognitive Genomics Consortium (COGENT, COHO:0000999) lists the DNS among its cohorts in Table 1 of its GWAS report (PMID:28093568). Not the Duke Cognition Cohort (COHO:0000055), CATHGEN (COHO:0000584) or any other Duke term; no other review name is the DNS. The Laboratory of NeuroGenetics is in Duke's Department of Psychology and Neuroscience. A case variant 'Duke neurogenetics study' also occurs (PMID:31358859) if wanted as a synonym.

label: Dubbo Osteoporosis Epidemiology Study
other synonyms: Dubbo Osteoporosis Epidemiology study
example title: Prediction of Bone Mineral Density and Fragility Fracture by Genetic Profiling.
example quote: Sixty-two bone mineral density (BMD)-associated single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were genotyped in 557 men and 902 women who had participated in the Dubbo Osteoporosis Epidemiology Study.
definition: A prospective population-based study of osteoporosis and fracture that in 1989 invited all men and women aged 60 or over living in Dubbo, New South Wales, Australia, a city chosen because its age and sex structure resembled Australia's and its isolation allowed near-complete ascertainment of fractures, and recruited further participants from 2000. Run by investigators of the Garvan Institute of Medical Research, Sydney, it reassessed participants every two to three years with interviews and bone densitometry and recorded fractures from the area's radiology services until 2020.
location quote: This longitudinal population-based study documents the incidence of all symptomatic fractures from 1989 to 1992 in an elderly, predominantly Caucasian population of males and females (> or = 60 years as at 1 January 1989) living in the geographically isolated region of the city of Dubbo, NSW, Australia.
note: Tier E (E273), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: DOES as the target sample for a BMD/fragility-fracture genetic-risk evaluation (PGS Catalog evaluation paper); P2-P4, P7: DOES's own studies of postural stability, lifestyle/BMD, fracture incidence and diabetes/bone parameters; P5: COLIA1 polymorphism study in DOES; P6: DOES combined with the Canadian Multicentre Osteoporosis Study for a fracture/mortality analysis. Combined with Canadian Multicentre Osteoporosis Study (COHO:0000973) in one paper (E273.19) but not stated as a member/sub-cohort relationship, so left without a parent; distinct Australian vs Canadian cohorts. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, synonym, acronym, type, country, example and the absence of a parent are right. The definition stitched two 1994 abstracts and left out how and when participants were recruited and by whom: all Dubbo residents aged 60 or over were invited in 1989 (PMID:15727686), a second group was recruited from 2000 (the 'DOES2' participants of PMID:37701154), participants were reassessed every 2–3 years with a DXA scan (PMID:37701154), fractures were ascertained from the radiology centres serving Dubbo, and the study ran from 1989 to 2020 (PMID:38485241); its investigators are at the Garvan Institute of Medical Research, Sydney. 'Predominantly Caucasian' described the 1989–1992 fracture-incidence sample, not an eligibility criterion, and is dropped. No COHO term or other review name is DOES. The draft's example quote from PMID:27649491 is the right choice, since that is the paper in which the PGS Catalog records the id.

input name: Department of Neurosurgery, University of Bonn Medical Center
note: Tier E (E274), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1: DoNBONN as the Bonn hospital department where the 'German GWAS' case series (880 glioma-surgery patients, 1996-2008) was operated on, and as the authors' institutional affiliation; P2-P3: PGS Catalog score papers reusing the same glioma GWAS, with no DoNBONN-specific description. PGS id 'DoNBONN' names the hospital department (Department of Neurosurgery, University of Bonn Medical Center) where glioma-surgery patients were operated on (E274.1) and the authors' affiliation (E274.4); the case series itself is called 'the German GWAS', not DoNBONN. Checked 2026-09-23: None: the verdict is right. The id is a hospital department. In its source GWAS (PMID:28346443) the PGS Catalog labels each case series by the institution that supplied it (SdNM for the French cases, DoNBONN for the German ones), and the German series is only described, never named: 'The German GWAS comprised 880 patients who had undergone surgery for a glioma at the Department of Neurosurgery, University of Bonn Medical Center, between 1996 and 2008', with controls from KORA (COHO:0000045), POPGEN (COHO:0000406) and the Heinz Nixdorf Recall Study (COHO:0000756). An unnamed clinical case series with borrowed controls is treated in this review as not a cohort (compare E010 and the review's 'Bonn' row, Department of Psychiatry, University of Bonn). E1150 (UKBonn, 'Universitäts Klinikum Bonn') is a different sample: in its only PGS Catalog paper (PMID:37321833) it is Lynch syndrome carriers from the University Hospital Bonn. If the curator prefers to mint the German glioma GWAS case series, its first publication is the German GWAS cited as reference 10 of PMID:28346443; it would need a constructed label, which the review avoids.

label: Danish Osteoporosis Prevention Study
example title: The Danish Osteoporosis Prevention Study (DOPS): project design and inclusion of 2000 normal perimenopausal women.
example quote: In 1990 we initiated a 20 year, partly randomised study (Danish Osteoporosis Prevention Study, DOPS) in order to (a) evaluate clinical, biochemical and osteodensitometric variables as predictors of low bone mass and future osteoporotic fractures, and (b) test the hypothesis, that hormone replacement therapy (HRT) initiated shortly after menopause reduces the risk of later osteoporotic fractures.
definition: An investigator-initiated, partly randomised multicentre trial in Denmark that in 1990–1993 enrolled healthy white women aged 45–58 in early menopause, recruited by direct mailing to a random sample of women from the general population, and allocated them, open label, to hormone replacement therapy or no treatment either at random or by their own choice. Planned to run for 20 years, with its randomised treatment stopped in 2002, it was set up to test whether hormone replacement therapy started soon after menopause prevents osteoporotic fractures and to find clinical, biochemical and densitometric predictors of low bone mass and fracture.
note: Tier E (E275), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P6: all denote the same Danish Osteoporosis Prevention Study (DOPS); P2 is its own design paper; P1, P3, P5-P6 report follow-up, substudies and genetic analyses using DOPS participants. P2's title states a target enrollment of '2000...perimenopausal women'; omitted from the definition per the no-participant-numbers rule. No unit ties a specific Danish region/city to recruitment beyond 'four hospitals'. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, acronym, type, country (from the name), example and the absence of a parent are right. The definition's aims and start year are right, but 'perimenopausal women across four participating hospitals' misstates who took part and how they were found: participants were healthy women aged 45–58 in early menopause (last menstrual bleeding 3–24 months before entry, or perimenopausal symptoms with postmenopausal FSH), recruited by direct mailing to a random sample of women from the general population and enrolled between 1990 and 1993 (design abstract PMID:10340280; BMJ trial report PMID:23048011, open access). 'Four hospitals' comes from a compliance substudy's methods line; the trial is described as an investigator-initiated multicentre trial. The '20-year' span was the plan: the randomisation phase was stopped in 2002 after the Women's Health Initiative results (PMID:23048011). The four study centres are not named in open text; the BMJ report's authors are at Hvidovre, Aarhus, Svendborg and Hillerød hospitals and it says the authors implemented the study at different sites. Setting 'Denmark, 1990-93' is in the BMJ abstract if a quoted country is preferred to the name. The Odense Androgen Study analysed alongside DOPS in PMID:23370486 is a separate study. No COHO term or other review name is DOPS.

input name: Diseases of the Ovary and their Evaluation Study
label: Diseases of the Ovary and their Evaluation Study
other synonyms: Diseases of the Ovary and their Evaluation|Diseases of the Ovary and Their Evaluation Study
example quote: This analysis included women with epithelial ovarian cancer from six studies: African American Cancer Epidemiology Study (AACES), Diseases of the Ovary and their Evaluation Study (DOVE), Hormones and Ovarian Cancer Prediction Study (HOPE), New England Case Control Study (NECC), Nurses’ Health Study (NHS), and NHSII.
definition: A population-based case–control study of epithelial ovarian cancer in western Washington State, United States, run from Seattle with funding from the US National Cancer Institute, that enrolled women aged 35–74 diagnosed in 2002–2009 in a 13-county area, identified through the region's SEER cancer registry, together with controls from the same area identified by random-digit dialling, and collected in-person interviews and, from cases, tumour tissue.
location quote: DOV Diseases of the Ovary and their Evaluation USA: 13 counties in western Washington state
parent quote: Included in this report are data from 16 OCAC studies. Ten of these are from the USA: the Diseases of the Ovary and their Evaluation (DOVE)
note: Tier E (E276), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft deferred with no evidence. Research settles it: DOVE is an Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium study, a population-based case–control study of epithelial ovarian cancer in 13 counties of western Washington State (cases aged 35–74 diagnosed 2002–2009 through the SEER registry, random-digit-dial controls), which OCAC papers code DOV. Its OCAC membership is also already recorded as 'new' in src/curation/aggregation_members_evidence.tsv (OCAC row from PMID:20570913), which can now point to this term. Not COHO:0000350 (University of Washington ovarian carcinoma cohort, an EGA tumour RNA-seq cohort of 56 patients). 'DOV' is the OCAC study code and is not used by any COHO term. OCAC papers write the name both with and without 'Study' and with 'their' or 'Their'.

label: Danish Psychiatric Central Research Register
other synonyms: Danish Psychiatric Central Register|Psychiatric Central Research Register
example title: Excess mortality of bipolar and unipolar manic-depressive patients.
example quote: To compare mortality in bipolar and unipolar manic-depressive patients, 2168 manic-depressive first admissions reported to the Danish Psychiatric Central Register were divided into a bipolar group (19%), i.e., patients with at least one admission for mania during an average observation period of six years, and a unipolar group.
definition: A nationwide Danish register of patients treated in psychiatric departments, with records collected systematically from 1938 and computerised from 1969, covering all admissions to psychiatric hospitals and psychiatric wards of general hospitals in Denmark, the Faroe Islands and Greenland and, since 1995, all psychiatric outpatient contacts, with dates of treatment, diagnoses, referral, place and mode of admission and municipality of residence. Kept within a psychiatric epidemiology research unit and fed since 1995 through the Danish National Patient Register, it is used for national health planning and psychiatric epidemiological research.
note: Tier E (E277), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P2: DPCR as the source register for identifying manic-depressive/bipolar admissions in mortality studies; P3: DPCR's own profile/methods paper (nationwide, electronic, about 25 years old in 1993); P4-P6: DPCR used for case ascertainment in lithium-exposure, OCD-validity and schizophrenia quality-of-life studies. Analogous to Hospital Discharge Register Sweden (COHO:0000093), a national administrative register modelled as a cohort. No explicit founding year stated; P3 (1993) says the register is 'almost 25 years old' at that point. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, type, country (from the name), example and the absence of a parent are right. The label is the register's former name: its 1997 profile is titled 'The Danish Psychiatric Central Register' (PMID:9062767), but its keepers' 2011 profile is 'The Danish Psychiatric Central Research Register' (PMID:21775352), the name current papers use (often as DPCRR, e.g. PMID:40611629); the old name, which the PGS Catalog uses, is kept as a synonym. Acronyms missed PCRR (the 2011 profile's) and DPCRR. The definition's 'with an electronic component' misreads the 1993 abstract, and it left out what the register holds and since when: systematic records from 1938, computerised from 1969 for all psychiatric admissions, outpatient contacts from 1995 (PMID:9062767), and the content listed in PMID:21775352. The 1997 profile says the computerised register includes admissions in the Faroe Islands and Greenland as well as Denmark; neither has a DBpedia name in src/templates/gaz_xrefs.tsv, so only Denmark (from the name) is asserted. The register is not a sub-cohort of the Danish National Patient Register (E271): it is older and only its data since 1995 come through the DNPR. 'Kept within a psychiatric epidemiology research unit' reflects the 1997 profile ('its organization within the psychiatric epidemiological and social psychiatric research unit, Department of Psychiatric Demography'); the current keeper is not stated in the open abstracts read. The draft's example (PMID:2951410) is kept.

label: Danish Pelvic Mass Study
other synonyms: Pelvic Mass Study|Danish Pelvic Mass study
example title: High-risk HPV is not associated with epithelial ovarian cancer in a Caucasian population.
example quote: Formalin-fixed, paraffin-imbedded tumor tissue samples from 198 cases consecutively included in the Danish Pelvic Mass Study were analyzed.
definition: A prospective Danish study that from September 2004 enrolled consecutive women aged 18 or older admitted for surgery because of a suspected pelvic mass to the Gynaecologic Clinic of Copenhagen University Hospital, Rigshospitalet, collecting their blood and tumour tissue with clinical data to identify factors that distinguish benign from malignant pelvic masses and predict the prognosis of ovarian cancer.
parent quote: PVD Danish Pelvic Mass Study Denmark
note: Tier E (E278), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P5: PGS Catalog source-GWAS/score-development papers for ovarian and pan-cancer PRS, likely drawing on DPMS as part of pooled ovarian-cancer GWAS data, but no DPMS-specific text was extracted; P6-P7: DPMS's own tissue-sample studies of HPV and EBV/CMV in the same case series. P1-P5 are marked as PGS Catalog papers but no evidence text was extracted for them; definition rests only on P6-P7's tissue-sample sub-studies. No dates or recruiting institution are given. Checked 2026-09-23: Identity, label, type, country (from the name) and example are right. The definition described the 198 tumours of two tissue substudies (HPV, EBV/CMV) rather than the study: the Pelvic Mass Study enrols consecutive women aged 18 or older admitted for surgery of a suspected pelvic mass at Rigshospitalet's gynaecological clinic, from September 2004, benign as well as malignant, and banks blood and tissue to find diagnostic and prognostic markers (PMID:22363532, PMID:29696206, PMID:27418945). The draft said no dates or institution were given; open-access text gives both. It missed the parent and an acronym: the study is an Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium study under the code PVD ('The Danish Pelvic Mass Study (PVD)' in PMID:29029385; row 'PVD Danish Pelvic Mass Study Denmark' in the OCAC outcome study table of PMID:23513043, whose abstract describes its 28 studies as from the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium). E909 (PGS id PMS, 'Pelvic Mass Study', no scores or papers in the PGS Catalog) is very probably this same study, which OCAC tables also call 'Pelvic Mass Study'; if its check agrees it should be 'same as E278', otherwise the shared synonym 'Pelvic Mass Study' needs editor notes on both terms. MALOVA (E661, the Danish Malignant Ovarian Tumor Study) is a different Danish OCAC study. One 2019 paper says the patients it used were recruited from the Pelvic Mass study 'initiated in September 2004 and finalized in August 2007', while 2016–2017 papers call it ongoing and PMID:30858874 a 'continuing and national sampling', so no end date is given.

Tier E (E279), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. Checked 2026-09-23: The draft matched the PGS name to the Netherlands Twin Registry (COHO:0000125) through a 2020 dermatology paper that a Europe PMC search for the phrase returned, but nothing links the PGS Catalog id DTWC to that paper or to any sample. The id is only in the Catalog's cohort list: REST cohort/DTWC returns no record, cohort_papers.json has no entry, and no score, sample set or performance record in the Catalog dumps mentions a Dutch twin cohort. The Catalog lists the Netherlands Twin Registry separately under NTR, with scores. 'Dutch Twin Cohort' is a description rather than a study's name: in Europe PMC it occurs in 7 papers, as a phrase for NTR samples (PMID:33052394, PMID:42457938, and an NTR survey title in PMID:39080443), for a twin sample described elsewhere (PMID:18270580) and for a clinical cohort of twin pregnancies (cited in PMID:26557247). Adding DTWC to COHO:0000125 would be a guess. If the curator wants to place the id anyway, the only plausible referent is the Netherlands Twin Registry (COHO:0000125): most uses of the phrase are NTR samples, and the Catalog has created duplicate ids for one cohort before (Duke and DUKE_2 for CATHGEN). Since the id labels no score or sample, leaving it unmapped loses nothing.

label: Catheterization Genetics
note: Tier E (E280), drafted from gathered evidence and checked by an independent review before minting. P1-P6: 'Duke' tags a coronary/CAD genetic-risk-score cohort across six coronary-heart-disease PRS papers; no quotable unit was extracted for any of them. PGS id 'Duke' and PGS name 'Duke Clinic' exactly match the acronym 'Duke' and synonym 'Duke Clinic' already recorded on COHO:0000584 (CATHGEN); topic (CHD/CAD risk) matches CATHGEN's ischaemic-heart-disease profile. Nothing to add; no unit here confirms it independently. Checked 2026-09-23: None: the verdict is right, and the draft's reasoning is now confirmed from the sources rather than by name matching alone. In both GWAS the PGS Catalog took the id from, 'Duke' is the Duke CATHGEN biorepository (COHO:0000584): the CARDIoGRAMplusC4D supplement (PMID:23202125) lists 'DUKE The Duke Cathgen Study' and describes it as 'The Duke CATHGEN biorepository consists of subjects recruited sequentially through the cardiac catheterization laboratories at Duke University Medical Center (Durham, NC, USA).', and the pleiotropy CAD analysis (PMID:28209224) cites its Duke case-control sample to a GWAS (PMID:22319020) whose discovery set includes 'the Duke CATHGEN study (DUKE)'. COHO:0000584 already carries 'Duke' and 'Duke Clinic', so nothing is added. 'Duke Clinic' is the PGS Catalog's name, not one the study uses; it was put on COHO:0000584 by the tier-B check along with DUKE_2 ('Duke Cathgen Study', E281), which is the same biorepository in the 1000 Genomes CARDIoGRAMplusC4D GWAS (PMID:26343387). Not the Duke Neurogenetics Study (E272) or other Duke terms.
